“Without Your grace, I can’t stand to live another moment. And Vṛndāvan, which is even dearer to me than my life itself—I am disgusted with it. It is painful; it is always pinching me. What to speak of anything else, I am even disgusted with Kṛṣṇa. It is shameful to utter such words, but I can have no love even for Kṛṣṇa, until and unless You take me up within Your confidential camp of service. Such charm I have come for. I have seen the clue of such charm within the service of Your camp. Without that, everything is tasteless to me. And I can’t maintain my existence even in Vṛndāvan. And even Kṛṣṇa, what to speak of others, has no charm for me.” This is the prayer of Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī.
Service of Rādhārāṇī
So, Rādhā-dāsyam, the servitorship of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, is said to be the highest attainment of the living being by the school established by Mahāprabhu. It is the gist of the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span>. It is Kṛṣṇa’s own version. He says in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (11.14.15):
na tathā me priyatama ātma-yonir na śaṅkaraḥ<br />na cha saṅkarṣano na śrīr naivātmā cha yathā bhavān
“O Uddhava! Neither Brahmā, nor Śiva, nor Baladev, nor Lakṣmī, nor even My own self are as dear to Me as you are.” And that Uddhava glorifies Vṛndāvan, the Vraja-gopīs, and Rādhārāṇī in this way in the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (10.47.61):
āsām aho charaṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṁ syāṁ<br />vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām<br />yā dustyajaṁ sva-janam ārya-pathaṁ cha hitvā<br />bhejur mukunda-padavīṁ śrutibhir vimṛgyām
“The gopīs of Vṛndāvan have given up the association of their husbands, sons, and other family members, who are very difficult to renounce, and they have sacrificed even their religious principles to take shelter of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, which are sought after even by the Vedas. Oh! Grant me the fortune to be born as a blade of grass in Vṛndāvan, so that I may take the dust of those great souls upon my head.
The search for Śrī Rādhā
Uddhava has shown us the high position of the gopīs. And between all the gopīs and Rādhārāṇī there is also a categorical difference. That was proved in the Rāsa-līlā. When Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs openly displayed their transaction of heart, with that divine rasa flowing and inundating all directions, Rādhārāṇī was also there. She gave the highest contribution to the common rasa-vilās display of the parakīya-madhura-rasa, paramour mellow. Then, suddenly, dissatisfaction came in Rādhārāṇī’s heart. She began to think, “Am I also counted in the common flow of rasa?” Some reaction came within Her mind and suddenly She left. After displaying Her peculiar type of superexcellent dancing and singing, introducing a flow of a new type there, suddenly She departed. She left the circle of the Rāsa dance. And Kṛṣṇa suddenly found, “Rādhārāṇī is not here. It is tasteless.” The flow of rasa was there, but the gist, the quality, is a little down. He felt, “Why is it not so satisfactory to My inner heart?” He felt some ebb in the tide. And then by inspection He found that Rādhārāṇī was absent. Disappointed, He left the circle of the Rāsa dance and went to search after Her.
Although the parakīya-madhura-rasa, the highest mellow of conjugal love, Vṛndāvan, and the gopīs were all there, still there is a categorical difference in quality between the other gopīs and the particular camp of Rādhārāṇī. In every way there is a categorical difference, both in quality and quantity. Jayadev Goswāmī, in his <span class="e3">Gītā-govinda</span> (3.1) has described how Kṛṣṇa left the circle of the Rāsa dance:
kaṁsārir api saṁsāra-vāsanābaddha-śṛṅkhalām<br />rādhām ādhāya hṛdaye tatyāja vraja-sundarīḥ
“Lord Kṛṣṇa took Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī within His heart, for He wanted to dance with Her. In this way, He left the arena of the Rāsa dance and the company of all the other beautiful damsels of Vraja.” Jayadev has described in this way that Kṛṣṇa left the circle of the Rāsa dance, taking Rādhā within His heart. Kṛṣṇa departed in search of Rādhārāṇī. Her position is so exalted. It is said, “Lord Kṛṣṇa’s transcendental desires for loving exchanges could not be satisfied even in the midst of billions of gopīs. Thus He went searching after Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Just imagine how transcendentally qualified She is! (<span class="e3">Śata-koṭi-gopīte nahe kāma-nirvāpaṇa</span>).”
The other gopīs numbered so many, but in quality they were a little less. Their total combination could not satisfy Kṛṣṇa. The qualitative difference was there. That is found.
The Rūpānuga sampradāya, the followers of the line of Śrī Rūpa, are those who have the unique taste of service in the camp of Rādhārāṇī. In that plane, there is no entrance of any mundane exploitation or renunciation, and not even legalised śāstric devotion. The highest kind of devotion is not controlled by any law. It is spontaneous and automatic. Sacrifice to the highest degree is only possible in that camp. The highest kind of divine sentiment is distributed from the camp of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and that can never be compared with any attainment hitherto known even in the eternal factor of time and space.
Then, there is another stage for which we should be prepared. Why should we try to enter into the camp of Rādhārāṇī? Should we think that there, in that better atmosphere, we shall have Kṛṣṇa’s presence more confidentially? Should we think, “I will have contact with Kṛṣṇa very intimately?” Should we want to enter into that camp? No—we want to avoid the connection of Kṛṣṇa, but concentrate on the service of Rādhārāṇī. Why? What more benefit is possible there in the service of Rādhārāṇī? If we approach Kṛṣṇa directly to give service to Him, we shall be losers. Rādhārāṇī’s service to Kṛṣṇa is of the highest order in every way. If we devote our energy to help Rādhārāṇī, our energy will be utilised in Her service. In this way She will serve Kṛṣṇa with Her service more enhanced. Then the reciprocation will pass to us through Her as our reward. That will be devotion of the highest type, mahābhāva.
So, the general inclination of the sakhīs, the confidential maidservants of Rādhārāṇī, is not to come in direct connection with Kṛṣṇa. They avoid that. But still, it is the benevolent and generous nature of Rādhārāṇī to connect them with Kṛṣṇa on some plea at some time or other. But their innate nature is always to avoid Kṛṣṇa and concentrate on the service of Rādhārāṇī. This is confirmed in the <span class="e3">Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> (Madhya-līlā, 8.208):
rādhāra svarūpa—kṛṣṇa-prema kalpa-latā<br />sakhī-gaṇa haya tāra pallava-puṣpa-pātā
“By nature, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is just like a creeper of love of Godhead, and the gopīs are the twigs, flowers, and leaves of that creeper.” Eternally the twigs, flowers, and leaves sprout from the creeper of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. She is the trunk, and they are the branches. This is their relationship.
Yet still, there is another, higher thing. We are known as Rūpānugas, or the followers of Śrī Rūpa. Why? The service of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī eliminates everything, even Nārāyaṇ, to go to Kṛṣṇa. There is the Kṛṣṇa of Dvārakā, the Kṛṣṇa of Mathurā, and the Kṛṣṇa of Vṛndāvan. Then again in Vṛndāvan, where there is free mixing without hesitation in other camps, Rādhārāṇī’s camp is the highest. Eliminating all other camps, direct service to Rādhārāṇī is considered to be the highest. Still, there is another point.
Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī—Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī
Who is Rūpa? Rūpa Mañjarī. Generally the hierarchy in the spiritual world is eternal. New recruits can occupy a particular rank of mañjarī, assistant, in madhura-rasa. And the leader of the mañjarīs is Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī. What is the special feature in the mañjarī camp which is not found among the sakhīs, girlfriends of Kṛṣṇa? First there is Rādhārāṇī, then the camp of Her right-hand personal attendant, Lalitā. Then, under Lalitā, there is Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī. What is the unique position of the followers of Śrī Rūpa? The new recruits can attain to that status. Now, the privilege of this mañjarī class we are to conceive most respectfully and attentively.
When Rādhā and Govinda are in secrecy, in a private place, the sakhīs, who are well-versed in the art of that kind of play because they are a little grown-up, do not like to approach there to disturb Their confidential mixing. If the more grown-up sakhīs enter there, both Rādhā and Govinda will feel shy. So their presence may create some disturbance. But the younger girls can enter there, and then Rādhā and Govinda have no hesitation in free mixing. So in that highest stage of the mixing of Rādhā-Govinda, the free play of Rādhā-Govinda, these mañjarīs, the younger girls, can have admission. But the grown-up sakhīs cannot have admission there.
New recruits may come up to the mañjarī class. And the mañjarīs have that sort of special advantage under the leadership of Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī. So, they get the best advantage there; the most sacred type of pure service, which is not open even to the sakhīs, is open to the mañjarīs. That is found in Rādhārāṇī’s camp. So, the position of the Rūpānugas, the followers of Śrī Rūpa, is the most profitable position. That has been given out by Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu. That has been shown by Him, and that is fixed as the highest limit of our fortune in Kṛṣṇa’s concern. This is unexpectable, undesignable, and beyond hope, but our prospect lies there in that subtle camp of Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, Rūpa Goswāmī.
So, the camp, the sampradāya of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, is known as the Rūpānuga sampradāya. There our fate and our fortune are located. Now we have to conduct ourselves in such a way that naturally we can connect with that highest, purest spiritual conception from here. We must not allow ourselves to be satisfied with anything less than this highest ideal. That should be the highest goal of our life. And we must adjust our approach from our present position.
Spiritual inheritance
We are minors. Our father has left us with so many important documents about the properties we are to inherit. As minors, we should try to find out what properties belong to us in those documents. When we come of age, then we shall take possession of our rightful inheritance. The rāgānuga-śāstra, the scriptures of spontaneous devotional love, has been given to us, left to us, by our Guru, our guardian, our father. And as we grow more and more in the spiritual line, we will have to detect what is our prospect, what is our real wealth. We must recover that. We must have that. It is there in the document. It is ours. This is our position. We are minors, but we must become majors and demand the service meant for us by our Guardians.
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> We are putting in our claim with you. We think that in the absence of our father, the court has appointed a guardian, in order to keep us out of mischief and also to regulate our inheritance.
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> This is not mine. This is the property of my Gurudev. And Bhaktivedānta Swāmī Prabhupād gave you a clue. He has distributed the key widely and given a clue: “With the key come and open the iron chest and find out what valuable ornaments and gems are within the chest.” Of course, no one will understand us when we say such things. Who will come to appreciate? They’ll say, “Oh, this is all the product of a disorganised brain. These people are trying to take electricity from the sky, leaving aside this concrete earth. They are like the chātak bird.” Rūpa Goswāmī says that there is a class of bird known as chātak, who never take a drop of water from the earth. Their nature is that whenever they want a drop of water, they always cast their eyes to the clouds. “One drop of pure water!”—that is their cry. And so they wait, with their beaks towards the sky, towards the clouds. And they never use any water from the earth. So, our line is like that. The spirit of that bird is described in the following way by Rūpa Goswāmī:
A drop of Your grace
virachaya mayi daṇḍaṁ dīnabandho dayāṁ vā<br />gatir iha na bhavattaḥ kāchid anyā mamāsti<br />nipatatu śata-koṭir nirbharaṁ vā navāmbhas<br />tad api kila payodaḥ stūyate chātakena
“You may punish me, O cloud, You may punish me. If a thunderbolt comes, I’ll be nowhere. You can throw down thunder, or You can give me water. But how much can I drink with my small beak? A flood of rain may come. O Lord of the poor, Lord of the helpless, You can give me a drop of Your devotion, or You may punish me like anything.”
He is always praying for water. The cloud may satisfy him immediately or, by sending a thunderbolt, it may finish him and efface him from the earth. The bird has no other alternative by nature. So he says, “My position is also like that bird. O Kṛṣṇa, You may finish me, destroy me, efface me from the world, or You may save me by only a drop of Your grace. I won’t search after my satisfaction in the mud. That is finished. I will never go back to search for my fortune in the earth, in the mundane. I am already fixed to do or die. Either I must receive a drop of Your grace, or You may finish me.” In this way, Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī prays that Kṛṣṇa’s mercy will descend like rain from the clouds, and not only quench his thirst, but bathe him, satisfy his utmost hankering, and fulfil his innermost necessity.
So, we should never search for our fortune in the mud. We must always look to the high sky and pray for Śrī Guru and his grace.

Explanation of the Logo of <br />Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh
by His Divine Grace
Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
Om is the very gist of gāyatrī, and from that Om comes merciful rays, like the rays of the sun. Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh, where saṅkīrtan is always going on, is inside the flute of Kṛṣṇa, and from there comes this sound Om. Om, the meaning of gāyatrī, is coming from Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh, and from there the explanation of gāyatrī has been given by Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj:
gāyatrī muralīṣṭa-kīrtana-dhanaṁ rādhā-padaṁ dhīmahi
The position of the Guru is like water; the servitors of Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh are like lotuses; and the position of the worshippable Supreme Personality of Godhead is the Divine Form of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Om. Everything is within Om. Om is coming from the flute of Kṛṣṇa, and the meaning of Om, of gāyatrī, is: <span class="e3">gāyatrī muralīṣṭa-kīrtana-dhanaṁ Rādhā-padaṁ dhīmahi</span>. Kṛṣṇa’s flute does not make any other sound except the glorification of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and that is the real meaning and gist of the gāyatrī mantram.
The sun’s merciful rays give nourishment to the lotus, but if there is no water—if one cannot take shelter of Śrī Guru and His Grace—then the lotus will become burnt by the rays of the sun.

॥ अथ मङ्गलाचरणम् ॥
Maṅgalācharaṇam <br /><span class="e7">Auspicious Invocation</span>
ॐ पार्थाय प्रतिबोधितां भगवता नारायणेन स्वयं<br />व्यासेन ग्रथितां पुराणमुनिना मध्ये महाभारते ।<br />अद्वैतामृतवर्षिणीं भगवतीमष्टाशाध्यायिनी-<br />मम्ब त्वामनुसन्दधामि भगवद्गीते भवद्वेषिणीम् ॥१॥
oṁ pārthāya pratibodhitāṁ bhagavatā nārāyaṇena svayaṁ<br />vyāsena grathitāṁ purāṇa-muninā madhye mahā-bhārate<br />advaitāmṛta-varṣiṇīṁ bhagavatīm aṣṭādaśādhyāyiṇīm<br />amba tvām anusandadhāmi bhagavad-gīte bhavad-veṣiṇīm [1]
Meditation on <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>—
O <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span>, song of the Supreme Lord Himself, you are the bestower of Arjuna’s enlightenment. You have been woven into the scripture <span class="e3">Mahābhārata</span> by the ancient sage Śrīla Vedavyās. In eighteen chapters, you are the rain of ever-flowing nectar, non-different from the Lord. O Mother, I meditate upon you; may you graciously enter my heart.
नमोऽस्तुते व्यासविशालबुद्धे फुल्लारविन्दायतपत्रनेत्र ।<br />येन त्वया भारततैलपूर्णः प्रज्वालितो ज्ञानमयः प्रदीपः ॥२॥
namo ’stu te vyāsa-viśāla-buddhe<br />phullāravindāyata-patra-netra<br />yena tvayā bhārata-taila-pūrṇaḥ<br />prajvālito jñāna-mayaḥ pradīpaḥ [2]
Obeisances unto Śrīla Vyāsadev—
O Śrīla Vyāsadev of formidable intelligence, whose eyes resemble the long petals of the blooming lotus flower, and who ignited the lamp of knowledge, filled with the oil of the <span class="e3">Mahābhārata</span>—I offer my obeisances unto you.
प्रपन्नपारिजाताय तोत्रवेत्रैकपाणये ।<br />ज्ञानमुद्राय कृष्णाय गीतामृतदुहे नमः ॥३॥
prapanna-pārijātāya totra-vetraika-pāṇaye<br />jñāna-mudrāya kṛṣṇāya gītāmṛta-duhe namaḥ [3]
Obeisances unto the Lord as the chariot-driver of Arjuna—
I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who fulfills the wishes of His surrendered devotees. He holds a driving-rod in one hand while the other is poised in the expression of instruction, and He is the milker of the nectar of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>.
सर्व्वोपनिषदो गावो दोग्धा गोपालनन्दनः ।<br />पार्थो वत्सः सुधीरभोक्ता दुग्धं गीतामृतं महत् ॥४॥
sarvopaniṣado gāvo dogdhā gopāla-nandanaḥ<br />pārtho vatsaḥ sudhīr bhoktā dugdhaṁ gītāmṛtaṁ mahat [4]
The Glories of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>—
The crest-jewels of the Vedas, all the Upaniṣads, are as the cow, and the milker of the cow is Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāj. Arjuna is the calf, the nectar of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is the milk, and the fortunate devotees are the enjoyers of that milk.
वसुदेवसुतं देवं कंसचाणूरमर्द्दनम् ।<br />देवकीपरमानन्दं कृष्णं वन्दे जगद्गुरुम् ॥५॥
vasudeva-sutaṁ devaṁ kaṁsa-chāṇūra-mardanam<br />devakī-paramānandaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ vande jagad-gurum [5]
Obeisances unto Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa—
I bow unto the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vasudev, the vanquisher of the demons Kaṁsa and Chāṇūra, the joy of mother Devakī, and the universal teacher.
भीष्मद्रोणतटा जयद्रथजला गान्धारनीलोत्पला<br />शल्यग्राहवती कृपेण वहनी कर्णेन वेलाकुला ।<br />अश्वत्थामविकर्णघोरमकरा दुर्य्योधनावर्त्तिनी<br />सोत्तीर्ण खलु पाण्डवै रणनदी कैवर्त्तकः केशवः ॥६॥
bhīṣma-droṇa-taṭā jayadratha-jalā gāndhāra-nīlotpalā<br />śalya-grāhavatī kṛpeṇa vahanī karṇena velā-kulā<br />aśvatthāma-vikarṇa-ghora-makarā duryodhanāvartinī<br />sottīrṇā khalu pāṇḍavai raṇa-nadī kaivartakaḥ keśavaḥ [6]
The river of the battle of Kurukṣetra—
One bank is Bhīṣma, the other Droṇāchārya; Jayadratha is the water; the sons of Gāndhārī, the blue lotus flower; Śalya, the crocodile; Kṛpa, the waves; Karṇa, the shore; Aśvatthāmā, Vikarṇa and company, the fearful sharks; Duryodhan, the whirlpool; and Keśava is the boatman of this river of the battle that was crossed by the Pāṇḍavas.
पाराशर्य्यवचः सरोजममलं गीतार्थगन्धोत्कटं<br />नानाख्यानककेसरं हरिकथासम्बोधनाबोधितम् ।<br />लोके सज्जनषट्पदैरहरहःपेपीयमानं मुदा<br />भूयाद्भारतपङ्कजं कलिमलप्रध्वंसि नः श्रेयसे ॥७॥
pārāśarya-vachaḥ sarojam-amalaṁ gītārtha-gandhotkaṭaṁ<br />nānākhyānaka-kesaraṁ hari-kathā-sambodhanābodhitam<br />loke sajjana-ṣaṭ-padair ahar-ahaḥ pepīyamānaṁ mudā<br />bhūyād bhārata-paṅkajaṁ kali-mala-pradhvaṁsi naḥ śreyase [7]
The <span class="e3">Mahābhārata</span> as a lotus flower—
These words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyan Vyāsadev, the son of Parāśar Muni, are a perfect lotus flower. The meaning of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is the beautiful fragrance of this lotus, the various episodes are its stamens, and the enlightening narrations about the Supreme Lord are its nectar. In this world, the pure devotees are the bees who day after day delight in drinking the nectar of the lotus flower. May this <span class="e3">Mahābhārata</span> lotus, the vanquisher of all evils in this Age of Kali, graciously bestow auspiciousness upon us.
यं ब्रह्मा वरुणेन्द्ररुद्रमरुतस्तुन्वन्ति दिव्यैः स्तवैर्<br />वेदैः साङ्गपदक्रमोपनिषदैर्गायन्ति यं सामगाः ।<br />ध्यानावस्थिततद्गतेन मनसा पश्यन्ति यं योगिनो<br />यस्यान्तं न विदुः सुरासुरगणा देवाय तस्मै नमः ॥८॥
yaṁ brahmā varuṇendra-rudra-maruta-stunvanti divyaiḥ stavair<br />vedaiḥ sāṅga-pada-kramopaniṣadair gāyanti yaḥ sāmagāḥ<br />dhyānāvasthita-tad-gatena manasā paśyanti yaṁ yogino<br />yasyāntaṁ na viduḥ surāsura-gaṇā devāya tasmai namaḥ [8]
Obeisances unto the Supreme Lord—
I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord whose glories are sung with celestial prayers by the gods Brahmā, Varuṇ, Indra, Rudra, and the Maruts; whose glories are sung by the verses of the Vedas along with their six auxiliary books and the Upaniṣads; whose glories are sung by the brāhmaṇs that sing the <span class="e3">Sāma-veda</span>; who the yogīs see within their hearts absorbed in meditation; and whose infinite glories are inconceivable to all beings, whether gods or demons.
नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरञ्चैव नरोत्तमम् ।<br />देवीं सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत् ॥९॥
nārāyaṇaṁ namskṛtya narañ chaiva narottamam<br />devīṁ sarasvatīṁ vyāsaṁ tato jayam udīrayet [9]
Before reciting the scriptures that can conquer material existence, we offer obeisances unto the Supreme Lord who is known as ‘Nārāyaṇ’, ‘Nara’, and ‘Narottam’; the goddess of learning Saraswatī; and the great sage empowered by the Lord to reveal the scriptures, Śrīla Vyāsadev.

All glory to Śrī Guru and Śrī Gaurāṅga
Preface
[Publisher’s Note, first Bengali edition,<br />appearance day of Lord Kṛṣṇa, 1961]
Unique in its wide publication and extensive circulation, the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span> appears in various languages, both in India and other countries, along with the commentaries of former great saints as well as modern scholars. The commentaries of the prominent Vaiṣṇava Āchāryas such as Śrī Rāmānuja, Śrīmat Madhva Muni, and Śrī Śrīdhar Swāmīpād are most notable, whilst among the proponents of jñāna-mārg, or the monistic path, the commentaries of Śrīmat Śaṅkar Āchārya and Śrī Madhusūdan Saraswatī are well-known. The commentaries of Śrīyuta Bāla Gaṅgādhar Tilak and Śrī Aurobindo favour the school of karma-yoga, or the path of action, and are also familiar to modern scholars. Great thinkers of both East and West have ardently sung the glories of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>, being inspired by the ideals of its teachings.
However, the achintya-bhedābheda-siddhānta, theology of inconceivable oneness and difference, as revealed by the proponents of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu—Gauḍīya Āchāryas Śrīla Viśvanāth Chakravartī and Śrīla Baladev Vidyābhūṣaṇ—is concluded by the learned devotees to be most favorable to exclusive devotion. The devotees also embrace Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s Bengali commentary on <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> as a harmonious, spiritual mine of the treasure of divine love for Śrī Kṛṣṇa (Kṛṣṇa-prema), the fifth and transcendental goal of life, beyond the four general human objectives of religion, wealth, sense enjoyment, and liberation.
In his introduction my worshipful Divine Master, Śrī Guru Pāda-padma Om Viṣṇupād Paramahaṁsa Parivrājakāchārya Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj, has revealed to the readers glimpses of his own deep devotional realisations. Although numerous editions of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> are presently available, few commentaries can be said to nurture pure devotion according to the teachings of bona fide divine succession, which has given us the opportunity of service in producing this edition. We shall consider ourselves blessed if the fortunate readers take the all-auspicious essence of this sincere attempt to heart.
Śrī Bhakti Sundar Govinda
Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh,
Nabadwīp

All glory to Śrī Guru and Śrī Gaurāṅga
Introduction
[of the first Bengali edition]
वन्दे श्रीगुरुगौराङ्गौ राधागोविन्दसुन्दरौ ।<br />सगुणौ गीयते चाथ गीतागूढार्थगौरवम् ॥
vande śrī-guru-gaurāṅgau rādhā-govinda-sundarau<br />sa-guṇau gīyate chātha gītā-gūḍhārtha-gauravam
Bowing down to the holy feet of Śrī Guru, Śrī Gaurāṅga, and Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Govindasundar, all accompanied by Their associates, I sing the glories of the hidden treasure of <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span>.
Since <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span> is very familiar to the learned society, an acquaintance of the conceptions of this edition may be given here. We are followers of the school of thought descending from Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, so this edition is based on the <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> commentaries of the pre-eminent, exalted Śrī Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Āchāryas—Śrī Viśvanāth, Śrī Baladev, and Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur.
By the grace of our worshipful Spiritual Master, Om Viṣṇupād Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Goswāmī Prabhupād, and from indications in the commentaries given by the aforementioned great pure devotees, in places some new light has been shed, revealing deeper meanings. The devoted reader will appreciate this particularly with regard to the four verses (10.<span class="e2">8</span>–11) which were described by Śrī Viśvanāthpād as the four essential verses (chatuḥ-ślokī) of the book.
Generally, <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> is known as an excellent study of the science of religion. The language of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> is simple and sweet; its mood is grave, extensive, and radical; its thought is succinct, lucid, and impartial; and its logic is sound and natural. The eloquence of the prologue, epilogue, exposition, review, analysis, synthesis, and delivery of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> is unprecedented and charming in the extreme. <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> is activation for the lazy, courage for the fearful, hope for the hopeless, and new life for the dying. <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> unifies and sustains all ranks, whether revolutionary, occultist, optimist, renunciationist, liberationist, or full-fledged theist. From the atheist of grossly crude vision to the most elevated saint, the essential conceptions of all classes of philosophers are illustrated with clear and powerful logic. The devotees of the Lord (bhagavad-bhaktas) and persons on the paths of action, knowledge, and yoga (karmīs, jñānīs, and yogīs) will each find the essence of their paths dealt with in a comprehensive and illuminating manner, and thus the book is highly esteemed by all.
The essential and inner purport of the Vedas and Upaniṣads of the Āryans is directly explained, and the essence of various non-Āryan doctrines can also be found. <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> teaches us enlightenment through the selfless execution of scripturally ordained actions. When the consciousness is thus purified, self-realisation or spiritual realisation is attained. In its maturity, this pure realisation blossoms into loving service in the joyful, divine plane.
From the standpoint of sambandha-jñān or ‘knowledge of relationship’, <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> gives us the conception that the Absolute Reality is a transcendental personality; from the standpoint of prayojan or ‘the objective’, spiritual love for the Absolute Reality is given as the highest attainment; and from the standpoint of abhidheya or ‘the means’, we are taught that one must initially offer all his actions to the Supreme Lord, followed by the cultivation of self-realisation favourable to realisation of the Lord, and finally surrender to the Lord, to the exclusion of all other endeavours. Ultimately, the means will culminate in the objective when, in one’s perfected spiritual form, one whole-heartedly engages in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.
<span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> has clearly shown the distinctions between the various paths, such as the path of action, including worship of the gods for worldly fulfillment, and the path of knowledge, for the attainment of liberation. The thoughtful reader can note that <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>, by its comparative study, refutes the misconception that the many paths and goals are ‘all one’. Rather, it is stated, “<span class="e3">Yo yach chhradhaḥ sa eva saḥ</span>: a man is known by his faith.”
These verses would warrant deep consideration in this respect:
“The yogī is superior to persons engaged in austerities, superior to the person of knowledge, and superior to the person of action. Therefore, O Arjuna, be a yogī. And best of all yogīs is My faithful devotee for whom I am the only goal, and who serves Me whole-heartedly. This is My opinion.” (6.46–47)
Showing the inferiority and meaninglessness of dry renunciation, the gift of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> is most substantial and positive. Rather then merely renouncing action, one should selflessly offer one’s actions to the Supreme Lord (karma-yoga). Ultimately, based on one’s surrender, one will be inspired to act in devotion (bhakti) for the Lord alone. This is the conclusive and sublime teaching of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>. In the finest conception, the overall excellence of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> is found in its gift of devotion. In its full manifestation, such devotion is prema-bhakti, loving devotion to the all-attractive Supreme Personality—Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Reality the Beautiful.
Secret, more secret, and the most secret of all teachings have been given, as the congregational chanting of the Holy Names of the Lord (saṅkīrtan), and service in spontaneity (bhāva-sevā), with exclusive surrender and dedication to the transcendental pleasure of Kṛṣṇa as the ultimate goal of life, as sung by the vibrant clarion call of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>—<span class="e3">sarva-dharmān parityajya Mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja</span>—and as deeply contemplated by the followers of the lotus footsteps of the Supreme Lord who mercifully appears as the saviour in this Age of Kali—Śrī Chaitanyachandra, and as corroborated by the divine succession of saintly teachers.
May Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa accept the offering of this edition.
Swāmī B.R. Śrīdhar
Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh
Nabadwīp
Janmāṣṭamī
Bengali year 1368

प्रथमोऽध्यायः
Chapter One
Sainya-darśana <br /><span class="e7">Observing the Armies</span>
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ।
धर्म्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।<br />मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्व्वत सञ्जय ॥१॥
dhṛtarāṣṭra uvācha
dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ<br />māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś chaiva kim akurvata sañjaya [1]
<span class="e2">dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvācha</span>–Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> sañjaya</span>–O Sañjaya;<span class="e2"> dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre</span>–at the holy land of Kurukṣetra;<span class="e2"> māmakāḥ</span>–Duryodhan and party;<span class="e2"> pāṇḍavāḥ cha</span>–and Yudhiṣṭhir and party;<span class="e2"> samavetāḥ</span>–who assembled;<span class="e2"> yuyutsavaḥ</span>–desirous of battle;<span class="e2"> eva</span>–thereafter;<span class="e2"> akurvata kim</span>–did what? [1]
1 Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: O Sañjaya, what happened when my sons and the sons of Pāṇḍu assembled for battle at the holy place of Kurukṣetra?
सञ्जय उवाच ।
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्य्योधनस्तदा ।<br />आचार्य्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥२॥
sañjaya uvācha
dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṁ vyūḍhaṁ duryodhanas tadā<br />āchāryam upasaṅgamya rājā vachanam abravīt [2]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said:<span class="e2"> tadā tu</span>–Then;<span class="e2"> rājā duryodhanaḥ</span>–King Duryodhan;<span class="e2"> dṛṣṭvā</span>–having seen;<span class="e2"> pāṇḍava-anīkam</span>–the soldiers of the Pāṇḍavas;<span class="e2"> vyūḍham</span>–arrayed in military formation;<span class="e2"> abravīt</span>–spoke;<span class="e2"> vachanam</span>–the following words;<span class="e2"> upasaṅgamya</span>–approaching;<span class="e2"> āchāryam</span>–Droṇāchārya. [2]
2 Sañjaya said: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas’ soldiers and armies arrayed for battle, King Duryodhan approached Droṇāchārya and said:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य्य महतीं चमूम् ।<br />व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥३॥
paśyaitāṁ pāṇḍu-putrāṇām āchārya mahatīṁ chamūm<br />vyūḍhāṁ drupada-putreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> āchārya</span>–O respected teacher;<span class="e2"> paśya</span>–please observe;<span class="e2"> etām mahatīm</span>–this great;<span class="e2"> chamūm</span>–army of seven akṣauhiṇīs (one akṣauhiṇī is 21,870 chariots, 21,870 elephants, 65,610 horses, and 109,350 foot-soldiers);<span class="e2"> pāṇḍu-putrāṇām</span>–of the Pāṇḍavas;<span class="e2"> vyūḍhām</span>–arranged in military formation;<span class="e2"> tava dhīmatā śiṣyeṇa</span>–by your intelligent disciple;<span class="e2"> drupada-putreṇa</span>–Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the son of Drupada. [3]
3 O my teacher, please observe the great armies of the Pāṇḍavas, arranged in military formation by your brilliant disciple, Dhṛṣṭadyumna.
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्ज्जुनसमा युधि ।<br />युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥४॥
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्य्यवान् ।<br />पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥५॥
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्य्यवान् ।<br />सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व्व एव महारथाः ॥६॥
atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjuna-samā yudhi<br />yuyudhāno virāṭaś cha drupadaś cha mahā-rathaḥ [4]
dhṛṣṭaketuś chekitānaḥ kāśīrājaś cha vīryavān<br />purujit kuntibhojaś cha śaibyaś cha nara-puṅgavaḥ [5]
yudhāmanyuś cha vikrānta uttamaujāś cha vīryavān<br />saubhadro draupadeyāś cha sarva eva mahā-rathāḥ [6]
<span class="e2">atra</span>–In this phalanx; (<span class="e2">santi</span>)–are;<span class="e2"> śūrāḥ</span>–warriors;<span class="e2"> maheṣvāsāḥ</span>–great archers;<span class="e2"> bhīma-arjuna-samāḥ</span>–comparable to Bhīma and Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yudhi</span>–in battle; (<span class="e2">yathā</span>)–such as;<span class="e2"> yuyudhānaḥ</span>–Sātyaki;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> virāṭaḥ</span>–King Virāṭa;<span class="e2"> mahā-rathaḥ drupadaḥ cha</span>–and the great warrior Drupada;<span class="e2"> dhṛṣtaketuḥ</span>–Dhṛṣtaketu;<span class="e2"> chekitānaḥ</span>–King Chekitāna;<span class="e2"> vīryavān kāśīrājaḥ cha</span>–and the powerful King of Kāśī;<span class="e2"> purujit</span>–Purujit;<span class="e2"> kuntibhojaḥ cha</span>–and Kuntibhoja;<span class="e2"> nara-puṅgavaḥ śaibyaḥ cha</span>–and the noble King Śaibya;<span class="e2"> vikrāntaḥ yudhāmanyuḥ cha</span>–and valiant Yudhāmanyu;<span class="e2"> vīryavān uttamaujāḥ cha</span>–heroic Uttamaujā;<span class="e2"> saubhadraḥ</span>–Abhimanyu;<span class="e2"> draupadeyāḥ cha</span>–and the sons of Draupadī;<span class="e2"> eva</span>–indeed;<span class="e2"> sarva mahā-rathāḥ</span>–all great warriors. [4–6]
4–6 Among these soldiers are the expert archers Bhīma, Arjuna, and others equally skilled in battle, like Sātyaki, King Virāṭa, the great fighter Drupada, Dhṛṣṭaketu, Chekitāna, the mighty hero Kāśīrāj, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, the noble King Śaibya, the valiant Yudhāmanyu, the heroic Uttamaujā, Abhimanyu, and the sons of Draupadī. They are all great warriors, indeed.
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।<br />नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥७॥
asmākaṁ tu viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha dvijottama<br />nāyakā mama sainyasya saṁjñārthaṁ tān bravīmi te [7]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dvija-uttama</span>–O Droṇāchārya, best of the twice-born;<span class="e2"> nibodha</span>–kindly consider;<span class="e2"> tān</span>–those;<span class="e2"> asmākam</span>–of us;<span class="e2"> tu ye viśiṣṭāḥ</span>–who are the prominent;<span class="e2"> nāyakāḥ</span>–commanders;<span class="e2"> mama sainyasya</span>–of my armies.<span class="e2"> bravīmi</span>–I speak;<span class="e2"> te</span>–to you;<span class="e2"> tān</span>–of them;<span class="e2"> saṁjñā-artham</span>–by name. [7]
7 O best of the twice-born, please consider, too, the foremost amongst us, the commanders of my armies. I submit their names before you:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः ।<br />अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिर्जयद्रथः ॥८॥
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।<br />नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्व्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥९॥
bhavān bhīṣmaś cha karṇaś cha kṛpaś cha samitiñjayaḥ<br />aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś cha saumadattir jayadrathaḥ [8]
anye cha bahavaḥ śūrā mad-arthe tyakta-jīvitāḥ<br />nānā-śastra-praharaṇāḥ sarve yuddha-viśāradāḥ [9]
<span class="e2">bhavān</span>–Your respected self;<span class="e2"> bhīṣmaḥ cha</span>–Bhīṣma;<span class="e2"> karṇaḥ cha</span>–and Karṇa;<span class="e2"> samitiñjayaḥ kṛpaḥ cha</span>–Kṛpa, who is victorious in battle;<span class="e2"> aśvatthāmā</span>–Aśvatthāmā;<span class="e2"> vikarṇaḥ cha</span>–Vikarṇa;<span class="e2"> saumadattiḥ</span>–Bhūriśravā;<span class="e2"> jayadrathaḥ</span>–Jayadratha;<span class="e2"> anye cha bahavaḥ śūrāḥ</span>–and many other warriors; (<span class="e2">santi</span>)–are present;<span class="e2"> nānā-śastra-praharaṇāḥ</span>–armed with various weapons;<span class="e2"> sarve</span>–all;<span class="e2"> yuddha-viśāradāḥ</span>–skilled in battle;<span class="e2"> tyakta-jīvitāḥ</span>–and prepared to sacrifice their lives;<span class="e2"> mad-arthe</span>–for my sake. [<span class="e2">8</span>–9]
8–9 Firstly there is your respected self, then Bhīṣma, Karṇa, the ever victorious Kṛpāchārya, Aśvatthāmā, Vikarṇa, Bhūriśravā, Jayadratha, and many other heroes skilled in the art of warfare, all armed with various weapons and prepared to lay down their very lives for me.
अपर्य्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् ।<br />पर्य्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥१०॥
aparyāptaṁ tad asmākaṁ balaṁ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam<br />paryāptaṁ tv idam eteṣāṁ balaṁ bhīmābhirakṣitam [10]
<span class="e2">asmākam tat balam</span>–That strength of our army;<span class="e2"> bhīṣma-abhirakṣitam</span>–protected by Bhīṣma; (<span class="e2">bhāti</span>)–appears;<span class="e2"> aparyāptam</span>–unlimited (or insufficient);<span class="e2"> tu</span>–but;<span class="e2"> idam balam</span>–the strength of this army;<span class="e2"> eteṣām</span>–of theirs;<span class="e2"> bhīma-abhirakṣitam</span>–protected by Bhīma; (<span class="e2">bhāti</span>)–appears;<span class="e2"> paryāptam</span>–limited (or sufficient) [both interpretations are possible]. [10]
10 The strength of our army, headed by Bhīṣma, seems inestimable, yet the strength of the Pāṇḍavas’ army, protected by Bhīma, is estimable.
अयनेषु च सर्व्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः ।<br />भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व्व एव हि ॥११॥
ayaneṣu cha sarveṣu yathā-bhāgam avasthitāḥ<br />bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi [11]
<span class="e2">bhavantaḥ</span>–You;<span class="e2"> sarve eva hi</span>–all indeed;<span class="e2"> abhirakṣantu</span>–may support;<span class="e2"> bhīṣmam eva</span>–Bhīṣma;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu ayaneṣu cha</span>–at all points of entrance into the formation; <span class="e2">avasthitāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–being situated;<span class="e2"> yathā-bhāgam</span>–at your posts. [11]
11 Now take up your posts at the strategic points of the formation in support of Bhīṣma.
तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः ।<br />सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥१२॥
tasya sañjanayan harṣaṁ kuru-vṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ<br />siṁha-nādaṁ vinadyochchaiḥ śaṅkhaṁ dadhmau pratāpavān [12]
<span class="e2">pratāpavān</span>–The hero;<span class="e2"> kuru-vṛddhaḥ-pitāmahaḥ</span>–the venerable ‘grandfather’ Bhīṣma;<span class="e2"> siṁha-nādam vinadya</span>–roaring like the lion;<span class="e2"> śaṅkham dadhmau</span>–then blew his conchshell;<span class="e2"> uchchaiḥ</span>–very loudly;<span class="e2"> tasya harṣam sañjanayan</span>–for the pleasure of Duryodhan. [12]
12 Then, with a war-cry like the roar of a lion, the venerable elder, Bhīṣma, loudly blew his conchshell to encourage Duryodhan.
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्य्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः ।<br />सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥१३॥
tataḥ śaṅkhāś cha bheryaś cha paṇavānaka-gomukhāḥ<br />sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo ’bhavat [13]
<span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–Thereafter;<span class="e2"> śaṅkhāḥ cha bheryaḥ cha paṇava-ānaka gomukhāḥ</span>–conchshells, kettledrums, hand-drums, bugles, and other instruments;<span class="e2"> sahasā eva abhyahanyanta</span>–were immediately sounded.<span class="e2"> saḥ śabdaḥ</span>–That sound;<span class="e2"> tumulaḥ abhavat</span>–was tumultuous. [13]
13 At once there arose a tumultuous vibration of conchshells, kettledrums, hand-drums, bugles, and the resounding of many instruments.
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ ।<br />माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥१४॥
tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau<br />mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś chaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ [14]
<span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–Thereafter;<span class="e2"> mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ cha eva</span>–both Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna;<span class="e2"> sthitau</span>–situated;<span class="e2"> mahati syandane</span>–in a magnificent chariot;<span class="e2"> śvetaiḥ hayaiḥ yukte</span>–yoked with white horses;<span class="e2"> pradadhmatuḥ</span>–sounded;<span class="e2"> divyau śaṅkhau</span>–divine conchshells. [14]
14 Then Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, in a magnificent chariot drawn by white horses, blew their divine conchshells.
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः ।<br />पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्म्मा वृकोदरः ॥१५॥
pāñchajanyaṁ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṁ dhanañjayaḥ<br />pauṇḍraṁ dadhmau mahā-śaṅkhaṁ bhīma-karmā vṛkodaraḥ [15]
<span class="e2">hṛṣīkeśaḥ</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> dadhmau</span>–sounded;<span class="e2"> pāñchajanyam</span>–the Pāñchajanya;<span class="e2"> dhanañjayaḥ</span>–Arjuna (sounded);<span class="e2"> devadattam</span>–the Devadatta; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and;<span class="e2"> bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ</span>–the performer of mighty tasks, Bhīmasen (sounded);<span class="e2"> mahā-śaṅkham</span>–the great conchshell;<span class="e2"> pauṇḍram</span>–named Pauṇḍra. [15]
15 Hṛṣīkeś blew His conchshell Pāñchajanya; Dhanañjaya sounded his, the Devadatta; and Bhīmasen, the performer of mighty tasks, blew the conchshell Pauṇḍra.
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।<br />नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥१६॥
anantavijayaṁ rājā kuntī-putro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ<br />nakulaḥ sahadevaś cha sughoṣa-maṇipuṣpakau [16]
<span class="e2">kuntī-putraḥ rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ</span>–King Yudhiṣṭhir, the son of Kuntī; (<span class="e2">dadhmau</span>)–sounded;<span class="e2"> anantavijayam</span>–the Anantavijay;<span class="e2"> nakulaḥ sahadevaḥ cha</span>–and Nakula and Sahadeva (sounded);<span class="e2"> sughoṣa-maṇipuṣpakau</span>–the conchshells named Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka. [16]
16 King Yudhiṣṭhir, the son of Kuntī, blew the Anantavijay, while Nakul and Sahadev blew the conchshells Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka.
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः ।<br />धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥१७॥
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व्वशः पृथिवीपते ।<br />सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥१८॥
kāśyaś cha parameṣv-āsaḥ śikhaṇḍī cha mahā-rathaḥ<br />dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś cha sātyakiś chāparājitaḥ [17]
drupado draupadeyāś cha sarvaśaḥ pṛthivī-pate<br />saubhadraś cha mahā-bāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak [18]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pṛthivī-pate</span>–O lord of the earth, Dhṛtarāṣṭra;<span class="e2"> kāśyaḥ cha</span>–the King of Kāśī;<span class="e2"> parama-iṣu-āsaḥ</span>–skilled in bowmanship;<span class="e2"> mahā-rathaḥ śikhaṇḍī cha</span>–and the great warrior, Śikhaṇḍī;<span class="e2"> dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ virāṭaḥ cha</span>–Dhṛṣṭadyumna and King Virāṭa;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> aparājitaḥ</span>–the unconquerable;<span class="e2"> sātyakiḥ</span>–Sātyaki;<span class="e2"> drupadaḥ</span>–King Drupada;<span class="e2"> draupadeyāḥ cha</span>–the sons of Draupadī;<span class="e2"> mahā-bāhuḥ saubhadraḥ cha</span>–and the mighty Abhimanyu;<span class="e2"> sarvaśaḥ</span>–all;<span class="e2"> dadhmuḥ</span>–sounded;<span class="e2"> pṛthak pṛthak śaṅkhān</span>–their respective conchshells. [17–18]
17–18 O lord of the earth, the skilled archer Kāśīrāj, the great warrior Śikhaṇḍī, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, King Virāṭa, the unconquerable Sātyaki, King Drupada, the sons of Draupadī, and the mighty son of Subhadrā, Abhimanyu—all blew their conchshells.
स घोषो धार्त्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् ।<br />नभश्च पृथिवीञ्चैव तुमुलोऽभ्यनुनादयन् ॥१९॥
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṁ hṛdayāni vyadārayat<br />nabhaś cha pṛthivīñ chaiva tumulo ’bhyanunādayan [19]
<span class="e2">saḥ tumulaḥ ghoṣaḥ</span>–That tumultuous sound;<span class="e2"> abhyanunādayan</span>–echoing;<span class="e2"> pṛthivīm cha nabhaḥ cha eva</span>–throughout the land and heavens;<span class="e2"> vyadārayat</span>–rent, pierced;<span class="e2"> hṛdayāni</span>–the hearts;<span class="e2"> dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām</span>–of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. [19]
19 Resounding throughout the land and heavens, the tremendous vibration of those conchshells pierced the hearts of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्त्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः ।<br />प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ।<br />हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ॥२०॥
atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapi-dhvajaḥ<br />pravṛtte śastra-sampāte dhanur udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ<br />hṛṣīkeśaṁ tadā vākyam idam āha mahī-pate [20]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahī-pate</span>–O King;<span class="e2"> atha</span>–thereafter; <span class="e2">pravṛtte </span>(<span class="e2">sati</span>)–at the time for commencing;<span class="e2"> śastra-sampāte</span>–the casting of weapons;<span class="e2"> kapi-dhvajaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ</span>–Arjuna of the Hanumān flag;<span class="e2"> dhārtarāṣṭrān vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā</span>–having seen the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra arrayed before him ready for battle;<span class="e2"> tadā</span>–at that time;<span class="e2"> dhanuḥ udyamya</span>–taking up his bow;<span class="e2"> āha</span>–spoke;<span class="e2"> idam vākyam</span>–these words;<span class="e2"> hṛṣīkeśam</span>–to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. [20]
20 O King, as the battle was about to commence, Arjuna, whose chariot was adorned with the flag of Hanumān, seeing Duryodhan and his army poised for battle, took up his bow and said to Śrī Kṛṣṇa:
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥२१॥
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान् ।<br />कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥२२॥
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः ।<br />धार्त्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥२३॥
arjuna uvācha
senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṁ sthāpaya me ’chyuta [21]
yāvad etān nirīkṣe ’haṁ yoddhu-kāmān avasthitān<br />kair mayā saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇa-samudyame [22]
yotsyamānān avekṣe ’haṁ ya ete ’tra samāgatāḥ<br />dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priya-chikīrṣavaḥ [23]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> achyuta</span>–O Achyuta;<span class="e2"> sthāpaya</span>–please place;<span class="e2"> me ratham</span>–my chariot;<span class="e2"> madhye</span>–between;<span class="e2"> ubhayoḥ senayoḥ</span>–both armies;<span class="e2"> yāvat</span>–so that;<span class="e2"> aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> nirīkṣe</span>–can observe;<span class="e2"> yoddhu-kāmān avasthitān etān</span>–these warriors desirous of battle;<span class="e2"> kaiḥ saha</span>–with whom;<span class="e2"> mayā yoddhavyam</span>–I have to fight;<span class="e2"> asmin raṇa-samudyame</span>–on this battlefield;<span class="e2"> aham</span>–and I;<span class="e2"> avekṣe</span>–may see; (<span class="e2">tān</span>)<span class="e2"> yotsyamānān</span>–the warriors;<span class="e2"> atra yuddhe</span>–in this battle;<span class="e2"> ete ye samāgatāḥ</span>–who have come;<span class="e2"> priya-chikīrṣavaḥ</span>–as well-wishers;<span class="e2"> durbuddheḥ dhārtarāṣṭrasya</span>–of wicked Duryodhan. [21–23]
21–23 O Kṛṣṇa, please place my chariot between the two armies so I may observe the warriors with whom I must contend on this battlefield, and who have come to fight for the satisfaction of the wicked Duryodhan.
सञ्जय उवाच ।
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत ।<br />सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥२४॥
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्व्वेषाञ्च महीक्षिताम् ।<br />उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥२५।
sañjaya uvācha
evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata<br />senayor ubhayor madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam [24]
bhīṣma-droṇa-pramukhataḥ sarveṣāñ cha mahīkṣitām<br />uvācha pārtha paśyaitān samavetān kurūn iti [25]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Dhṛtarāṣṭra; <span class="e2">evam uktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–this being spoken;<span class="e2"> guḍākeśena</span>–by Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep;<span class="e2"> hṛṣīkeśaḥ</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> sthāpayitvā</span>–placing;<span class="e2"> ratha-uttamam</span>–the grand chariot;<span class="e2"> ubhayoḥ senayoḥ madhye</span>–between both armies; (<span class="e2">purataḥ</span>)–before;<span class="e2"> bhīṣma-droṇa-pramukhataḥ</span>–Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and company;<span class="e2"> sarveṣām cha mahī-kṣitām</span>–and all the chieftains;<span class="e2"> uvācha iti</span>–spoke thus: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> paśya</span>–behold;<span class="e2"> samavetān etān kurūn</span>–these assembled Kurus. [24–25]
24–25 Sañjaya said: O descendant of Bharat, after the vigilant Arjuna spoke these words, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the perceptions of all living beings, drew the grand chariot between both armies, before Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and all the chieftains of the earth. The Lord then said: O Pārtha, behold the Kauravas assembled here for battle!
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान् ।<br />आचार्य्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ।<br />श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि ॥२६॥
tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝn atha pitāmahān<br />āchāryān mātulān bhrātṝn putrān pautrān sakhīṁs tathā<br />śvaśurān suhṛdaś chaiva senayor ubhayor api [26]
<span class="e2">atha</span>–Thereafter;<span class="e2"> eva</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> pārthaḥ</span>–Arjuna;<span class="e2"> api apaśyat</span>–could also see;<span class="e2"> sthitān</span>–situated;<span class="e2"> tatra</span>–there; (<span class="e2">madhye</span>)–within;<span class="e2"> ubhayoḥ senayoḥ</span>–both armies;<span class="e2"> pitṝn</span>–paternal elders;<span class="e2"> pitāmahān</span>–grandfathers;<span class="e2"> āchāryān</span>–teachers;<span class="e2"> mātulān</span>–maternal elders;<span class="e2"> bhrātṝn</span>–brothers;<span class="e2"> putrān</span>–sons;<span class="e2"> pautrān</span>–grandsons;<span class="e2"> sakhīn</span>–friends;<span class="e2"> tathā śvaśurān</span>–fathers-in-law;<span class="e2"> suhṛdaḥ cha</span>–and well-wishers. [26]
26 There, within both armies, Arjuna saw paternal and maternal elders, grandfathers, teachers, brothers, sons, grandsons, fathers-in-law, friends, and other well-wishers.
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्व्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ।<br />कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्नदमब्रवीत् ॥२७॥
tān samīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān<br />kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdann idam abravīt [27]
<span class="e2">samīkṣya</span>–Seeing;<span class="e2"> tān sarvān bandhūn</span>–all these kinsmen;<span class="e2"> avasthitān</span>–present; (<span class="e2">tatra</span>)–on the battlefield;<span class="e2"> saḥ kaunteyaḥ</span>–that son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> parayā kṛpayā āviṣṭaḥ</span>–overwhelmed with great compassion; <span class="e2">viṣīdan </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–and being grief-stricken;<span class="e2"> idam abravīt</span>–spoke thus. [27]
27 Seeing his kinsmen present on the battlefield, Arjuna, the son of Kuntī, was grief-stricken and overcome with pity. He said:
अर्ज्जुन उवाच
दृष्ट्वेमान्स्वजनान्कृष्ण युयुत्सून्समवस्थितान् ।<br />सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखञ्च परिशुष्यति ॥२८॥
arjuna uvācha
dṛṣṭvemān svajanān kṛṣṇa yuyutsūn samavasthitān<br />sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhañ cha pariśuṣyati [28]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> dṛṣṭvā</span>–seeing;<span class="e2"> imān svajanān</span>–all these friends and relatives;<span class="e2"> samavasthitān</span>–assembled;<span class="e2"> yuyutsūn</span>–and desirous of battle;<span class="e2"> mama gātrāṇi</span>–my body;<span class="e2"> sīdanti</span>–feels exhausted;<span class="e2"> mukham cha pariśuṣyati</span>–and my mouth is becoming dry. [28]
28 O Kṛṣṇa, seeing all these relatives and friends assembled and eager for battle, the strength is draining from my limbs and my mouth feels parched.
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ।<br />गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते ॥२९॥
vepathuś cha śarīre me roma-harṣaś cha jāyate<br />gāṇḍīvaṁ sraṁsate hastāt tvak chaiva paridahyate [29]
<span class="e2">me śarīre</span>–In my body;<span class="e2"> vepathuḥ</span>–are tremors;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> romaharṣaḥ</span>–bodily hairs standing on end;<span class="e2"> cha jāyate</span>–is also occurring.<span class="e2"> gāṇḍīvam</span>–The bow Gāṇḍīva;<span class="e2"> sraṁsate</span>–is slipping;<span class="e2"> hastāt</span>–from my hand;<span class="e2"> tvak cha</span>–and my skin;<span class="e2"> paridahyate eva</span>–burns too. [29]
29 I am trembling and the hairs on my body are standing on end, my skin is burning, and I am losing grip of my Gāṇḍīva bow.
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ।<br />निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव ॥३०॥
na cha śaknomy avasthātuṁ bhramatīva cha me manaḥ<br />nimittāni cha paśyāmi viparītāni keśava [30]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> keśava</span>–O Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> na śaknomi</span>–am unable to;<span class="e2"> avasthātum cha</span>–compose myself any longer;<span class="e2"> iva</span>–as;<span class="e2"> me manaḥ</span>–my mind;<span class="e2"> bhramati</span>–is flickering;<span class="e2"> paśyāmi cha</span>–and I see;<span class="e2"> viparītāni nimittāni</span>–bad omens. [30]
30 O Keśava, I cannot maintain my composure any longer. My mind is disturbed, and I see bad omens.
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ।<br />न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ॥३१॥
na cha śreyo ’nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanam āhave<br />na kāṅkṣe vijayaṁ kṛṣṇa na cha rājyaṁ sukhāni cha [31]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> na anupaśyāmi cha</span>–nor do I see;<span class="e2"> śreyaḥ</span>–any good;<span class="e2"> svajanam hatvā</span>–in killing my kinsmen;<span class="e2"> āhave</span>–in battle. (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> vijayam na kāṅkṣe</span>–desire neither victory;<span class="e2"> na cha rājyam cha sukhāni</span>–nor the enjoyment of a kingdom. [31]
31 I do not see any good in killing my kinsmen in this battle. O Kṛṣṇa, I have no wish for victory or to enjoy a kingdom.
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ।<br />येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ॥३२॥
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ।<br />आचार्य्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः ॥३३॥
मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः संबन्धिनस्तथा ।<br />एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन ॥३४॥
kiṁ no rājyena govinda kiṁ bhogair jīvitena vā<br />yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitaṁ no rājyaṁ bhogāḥ sukhāni cha [32]
ta ime ’vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṁs tyaktvā dhanāni cha<br />āchāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva cha pitāmahāḥ [33]
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ sambandhinas tathā<br />etān na hantum ichchhāmi ghnato ’pi madhusūdana [34]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> govinda</span>–O Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> kim naḥ rājyena</span>–of what value is our kingdom;<span class="e2"> kim vā bhogaiḥ jīvitena</span>–and what is the need of its royal pleasures, or life itself;<span class="e2"> yeṣām arthe</span>–if those for whom;<span class="e2"> naḥ</span>–our;<span class="e2"> rājyam bhogāḥ sukhāni cha</span>–kingdom with its pleasures and enjoyable objects;<span class="e2"> kāṅkṣitam</span>–is desirable;<span class="e2"> te ime</span>–all these;<span class="e2"> āchāryaḥ</span>–teachers;<span class="e2"> pitaraḥ</span>–fatherly elders;<span class="e2"> putrāḥ</span>–sons;<span class="e2"> tathā eva cha</span>–and also even;<span class="e2"> pitāmahāḥ</span>–grandfathers;<span class="e2"> mātulāḥ</span>–maternal uncles;<span class="e2"> śvaśurāḥ</span>–fathers-in-law;<span class="e2"> pautrāḥ</span>–grandsons;<span class="e2"> śyālāḥ</span>–brothers-in-law;<span class="e2"> tathā sambandhinaḥ</span>–and other relatives;<span class="e2"> yuddhe avasthitāḥ</span>–are present on the battlefield;<span class="e2"> tyaktvā</span>–risking;<span class="e2"> dhanāni prāṇān cha</span>–their wealth and lives? (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> madhusūdana</span>–(Therefore,) O Madhusūdan;<span class="e2"> ghnataḥ api</span>–though I may be killed by them;<span class="e2"> na ichchhāmi</span>–I do not wish;<span class="e2"> etān hantum</span>–to kill them. [32–34]
32–34 O Govinda, if those for whom we desire all this—teachers, paternal and maternal elders, sons, grandfathers, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives—are about to risk their wealth and lives in battle, of what value is our kingdom and its royal pleasures, or even life itself? O Madhusūdan, I do not wish to kill them even though I, myself, may be killed.
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ।<br />निहत्य धार्त्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्द्दन ॥३५॥
api trailokya-rājyasya hetoḥ kiṁ nu mahī-kṛte<br />nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana [35]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> janārdana</span>–O Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> kā prītiḥ syāt</span>–what happiness can be possible;<span class="e2"> naḥ</span>–for us;<span class="e2"> nihatya</span>–by killing;<span class="e2"> dhārtarāṣṭrān</span>–the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra;<span class="e2"> trailokya rājyasya hetoḥ api</span>–for the sovereignty of even the three worlds;<span class="e2"> mahī-kṛte kim nu</span>–not to speak of ruling the earth? [35]
35 O Janārdan, even if we gain sovereignty over the three worlds, not to speak of ruling the earth, how can we be happy if we kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra?
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ।<br />तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्त्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् ।<br />स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥३६॥
pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ<br />tasmān nārhā vayaṁ hantuṁ dhārtarāṣṭrān svabāndhavān<br />svajanaṁ hi kathaṁ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava [36]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mādhava</span>–O Mādhava;<span class="e2"> pāpam eva</span>–only sin;<span class="e2"> āśrayet</span>–will enter;<span class="e2"> asmān</span>–us;<span class="e2"> hatvā</span>–by killing;<span class="e2"> etān ātatāyinaḥ</span>–these adversaries.<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> vayam</span>–we;<span class="e2"> na arhāḥ</span>–are wrong;<span class="e2"> hantum</span>–to kill;<span class="e2"> svabāndhavān</span>–our own family members;<span class="e2"> dhārtarāṣṭrān</span>–the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.<span class="e2"> svajanam hatvā hi</span>–By killing our kinsmen;<span class="e2"> katham</span>–how; (<span class="e2">vayam</span>)<span class="e2"> syāma</span>–can we be;<span class="e2"> sukhinaḥ</span>–happy? [36]
36 Only sin will befall us if we slay our teachers and guardians, though they be our adversaries. We cannot take the lives of our own relatives, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. O Mādhava, how can we be happy by killing our kinsmen?
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः ।<br />कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥३७॥
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्त्तितुम् ।<br />कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्द्दन ॥३८॥
yadyapy ete na paśyanti lobhopahata-chetasaḥ<br />kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṁ doṣaṁ mitra-drohe cha pātakam [37]
kathaṁ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum<br />kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṁ doṣaṁ prapaśyadbhir janārdana [38]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> janārdana</span>–O Janārdan, Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> yadyapi ete</span>–although these persons; <span class="e2">lobha-upahata-chetasaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–their hearts being afflicted with greed;<span class="e2"> pātakam na paśyanti</span>–do not see the sin;<span class="e2"> mitra-drohe</span>–of betraying one’s friends;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> kula-kṣaya-kṛtam doṣam</span>–the sin of destroying the dynasty; (<span class="e2">tathāpi</span>)–nonetheless;<span class="e2"> katham</span>–how;<span class="e2"> na jñeyam</span>–should it not be known;<span class="e2"> asmābhiḥ</span>–by us;<span class="e2"> nivartitum</span>–to refrain;<span class="e2"> asmāt pāpāt</span>–from this sinful act;<span class="e2"> prapaśyadbhiḥ</span>–clearly seeing;<span class="e2"> kula-kṣaya-kṛtam doṣam</span>–the evil of destroying the dynasty? [37–38]
37–38 Although they, overwhelmed with greed, cannot see the sin of betraying one’s friends and destroying the dynasty, O Janārdan, how can we not refrain from this heinous act, being in full knowledge of the consequences?
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्म्माः सनातनाः ।<br />धर्म्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्म्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥३९॥
kula-kṣaye praṇaśyanti kula-dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ<br />dharme naṣṭe kulaṁ kṛtsnam adharmo ’bhibhavaty uta [39]
<span class="e2">kula-kṣaye</span>–With the decline of the dynasty;<span class="e2"> sanātanāḥ</span>–the traditional;<span class="e2"> kula-dharmāḥ</span>–religious practices of the dynasty;<span class="e2"> praṇaśyanti</span>–are destroyed. <span class="e2">dharme naṣṭe </span>(<span class="e2">sati</span>)–When religious practices are lost;<span class="e2"> adharmaḥ</span>–irreligion;<span class="e2"> abhibhavati</span>–overcomes;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam uta kulam</span>–the entire dynasty. [39]
39 With the decline of the dynasty, its religious traditions are lost. When religious practices are lost, irreligion overcomes the entire dynasty.
अधर्म्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः ।<br />स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥४०॥
adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kula-striyaḥ<br />strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇa-saṅkaraḥ [40]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> adharma-abhibhavāt</span>–when the family is overcome by irreligion;<span class="e2"> kula-striyaḥ</span>–the women of the family;<span class="e2"> praduṣyanti</span>–are polluted. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> vārṣṇeya</span>–O descendant of the Vṛṣṇi dynasty; <span class="e2">strīṣu duṣṭāsu </span>(<span class="e2">satsu</span>)–when the women of the family become corrupt;<span class="e2"> jāyate</span>–the result is;<span class="e2"> varṇa-saṅkaraḥ</span>–adulterated progeny. [40]
40 O Kṛṣṇa, descendant of the Vṛṣṇi dynasty, when the dynasty is thus overcome by irreligion, the women of the family become corrupt and adulterated progeny is the result.
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च ।<br />पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥४१॥
saṅkaro narakāyaiva kula-ghnānāṁ kulasya cha<br />patanti pitaro hy eṣāṁ lupta-piṇḍodaka-kriyāḥ [41]
<span class="e2">saṅkaraḥ</span>–Adulterated progeny; <span class="e2">narakāya eva </span>(<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–causes a hellish condition;<span class="e2"> kulasya kula-ghnānām cha</span>–for both the dynasty and its destroyers.<span class="e2"> eṣām</span>–Their;<span class="e2"> pitaraḥ</span>–forefathers;<span class="e2"> patanti hi</span>–surely fall;<span class="e2"> lupta-piṇḍa-udaka-kriyāḥ</span>–due to the cessation of obsequial offerings of food and water. [41]
41 Adulterated progeny forces both the family and its aggressors into a hellish existence. The same fate befalls their ancestors, because regular offerings of food and water to them cease.
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः ।<br />उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्म्माः कुलधर्म्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥४२॥
doṣair etaiḥ kula-ghnānāṁ varṇa-saṅkara-kārakaiḥ<br />utsādyante jāti-dharmāḥ kula-dharmāś cha śāśvatāḥ [42]
<span class="e2">etaiḥ doṣaiḥ</span>–By such heinous acts;<span class="e2"> kula-ghnānām</span>–of the destroyers of the dynasty;<span class="e2"> varṇa-saṅkara-kārakaiḥ</span>–causing varṇa-saṅkara, adulterated progeny;<span class="e2"> śāśvatāḥ</span>–traditional;<span class="e2"> kula-dharmāḥ jāti-dharmāḥ cha</span>–familial and socio-religious functions;<span class="e2"> utsādyante</span>–are ruined. [42]
42 Such heinous acts by the destroyers of the dynasty are the cause of adulterated progeny, ruining the culture of a civilized society and noble lineage.
उत्सन्नकुलधर्म्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्द्दन ।<br />नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥४३॥
utsanna-kula-dharmāṇāṁ manuṣyāṇāṁ janārdana<br />narake niyataṁ vāso bhavatīty anuśuśruma [43]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> janārdana</span>–O Janārdan; (<span class="e2">vayam</span>)<span class="e2"> anuśuśruma</span>–We have heard;<span class="e2"> iti</span>–that;<span class="e2"> manuṣyāṇām</span>–for those persons;<span class="e2"> utsanna-kula-dharmāṇām</span>–whose family traditions have been destroyed;<span class="e2"> niyatam</span>–constant;<span class="e2"> narake vāsaḥ</span>–residence in hell;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–occurs. [43]
43 O Janārdan, we have heard that persons whose familial, social and religious traditions are disrupted dwell always in hell.
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्त्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् ।<br />यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥४४॥
aho bata mahat-pāpaṁ kartuṁ vyavasitā vayam<br />yad rājya-sukha-lobhena hantuṁ svajanam udyatāḥ [44]
<span class="e2">aho bata</span>–Alas, what a tragedy! <span class="e2">vayam</span>–We;<span class="e2"> vyavasitāḥ</span>–have resolved;<span class="e2"> kartum</span>–to commit;<span class="e2"> mahat-pāpam</span>–a most heinous sin.<span class="e2"> yat rājya-sukha-lobhena</span>–Out of greed for royal pleasures;<span class="e2"> udyatāḥ</span>–we are prepared;<span class="e2"> svajanam hantum</span>–to slay our relatives. [44]
44 Alas, what a grave sin we have resolved to commit! Driven by greed for trifling royal happiness, we are about to slay our own kinsmen.
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः ।<br />धार्त्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥४५॥
yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṁ śastra-pāṇayaḥ<br />dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṁ bhavet [45]
<span class="e2">yadi</span>–If;<span class="e2"> dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ</span>–the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra;<span class="e2"> śastra-pāṇayaḥ</span>–equipped with weapons;<span class="e2"> hanyuḥ</span>–kill;<span class="e2"> mām</span>–me;<span class="e2"> aśastram</span>–unarmed;<span class="e2"> apratīkāram</span>–and unresisting;<span class="e2"> raṇe</span>–in battle;<span class="e2"> tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> bhavet</span>–will be;<span class="e2"> kṣemataram</span>–more auspicious;<span class="e2"> me</span>–for me. [45]
45 If, unarmed and unresisting, I am killed on this battlefield by the armed sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that will be more auspicious for me.
सञ्जय उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वार्ज्जुनः सङ्ख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् ।<br />विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥४६॥
sañjaya uvācha
evam uktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat<br />visṛjya sa-śaraṁ chāpaṁ śoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ [46]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said:<span class="e2"> arjunaḥ</span>–Arjuna;<span class="e2"> evam uktvā</span>–having thus spoken;<span class="e2"> saṅkhye</span>–on the battlefield;<span class="e2"> visṛjya</span>–casting aside;<span class="e2"> chāpam</span>–bow;<span class="e2"> sa-śaram</span>–and arrows;<span class="e2"> upāviśat</span>–sat down;<span class="e2"> ratha-upasthaḥ</span>–on the chariot;<span class="e2"> śoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ</span>–his heart heavy with sorrow. [46]
46 Sañjaya said: There, on the battlefield, speaking these words, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, his heart filled with sadness.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्यां<br />भीष्मपर्व्वणि श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे<br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे सैन्यदर्शनं नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः ॥१॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma-<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde sainya-<br />darśanaṁ nāma prathamo ’dhyāyaḥ [1]
End of Chapter One<br />Observing the Armies<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

द्वितीयोऽध्यायः
Chapter Two
Sāṅkhya-yoga <br /><span class="e7">The Constitution of the Soul</span>
सञ्जय उवाच ।
तं तथा कृपयाविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् ।<br />विषीदन्तमदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥१॥
sañjaya uvācha
taṁ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśru-pūrṇākulekṣaṇam<br />viṣīdantam idaṁ vākyam uvācha madhusūdanaḥ [1]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said:<span class="e2"> madhusūdanaḥ</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> tathā</span>–then;<span class="e2"> uvācha</span>–spoke;<span class="e2"> idam vākyam</span>–these words;<span class="e2"> viṣīdantam tam</span>–to the saddened Arjuna;<span class="e2"> kṛpayā-āviṣṭam</span>–whose heart was filled with pity;<span class="e2"> aśru-pūrṇa-ākula-īkṣaṇam</span>–his eyes brimming with tears, showing his distress. [1]
1 Sañjaya said: The Supreme Lord, Madhusūdan, then spoke to the saddened Arjuna whose heart was filled with pity, his eyes brimming with tears.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ।<br />अनार्य्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्त्तिकरमर्ज्जुन ॥२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṁ viṣame samupasthitam<br />anārya-juṣṭam asvargyam akīrti-karam arjuna [2]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> viṣame</span>–in this crisis;<span class="e2"> kutaḥ</span>–how;<span class="e2"> idam kaśmalam</span>–has this illusion;<span class="e2"> tvā</span>–of yours;<span class="e2"> samupasthitam</span>–occurred?<span class="e2"> anārya-juṣṭam</span>–This does not befit an Āryan (noble person);<span class="e2"> asvargyam</span>–it is an obstacle to the attainment of heaven;<span class="e2"> akīrti-karam</span>–and the cause of infamy. [2]
2 The Supreme Lord said: O Arjuna, how has such illusion overcome you at this crucial moment? This does not befit an Āryan, and it leads not to heaven but to infamy.
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्यपपद्यते ।<br />क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥३॥
klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate<br />kṣudraṁ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṁ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> klaibyam mā sma gamaḥ</span>–do not be overcome by cowardice.<span class="e2"> etat</span>–This;<span class="e2"> na upapadyate</span>–does not befit;<span class="e2"> tvayi</span>–you. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> parantapa</span>–O subduer of the enemy;<span class="e2"> tyaktvā</span>–giving up;<span class="e2"> kṣudram hṛdaya-daurbalyam</span>–petty weakheartedness;<span class="e2"> uttiṣṭha</span>–arise for battle. [3]
3 O son of Kuntī, give up this cowardice, for it does not befit you. O great hero, cast off this petty weakness of heart and arise for battle!
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणञ्च मधुसूदन ।<br />इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥४॥
arjuna uvācha
kathaṁ bhīṣmam ahaṁ saṅkhye droṇañ cha madhusūdana<br />iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv arisūdana [4]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> madhusūdana arisūdana</span>–O Madhusūdan, slayer of the enemy;<span class="e2"> katham aham</span>–how can I;<span class="e2"> pratiyotsyāmi</span>–counterattack;<span class="e2"> iṣubhiḥ</span>–with arrows;<span class="e2"> saṅkhye</span>–in battle; (<span class="e2">lakṣī-kṛtya</span>)–aiming at;<span class="e2"> pūjā-arhau</span>–worshippable;<span class="e2"> bhīṣmam droṇam cha</span>–Bhīṣma and Droṇa? [4]
4 Arjuna said: O Madhusūdan, slayer of the enemy, how can I counterattack, shooting arrows at venerable Bhīṣma and my teacher Droṇa, who are worthy of my worship?
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावाञ्<br />श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।<br />हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनहैव<br />भुञ्जीय भोगान्रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥५॥
gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvāñ<br />śreyo bhoktuṁ bhaikṣyam apīha loke<br />hatvārtha-kāmāṁs tu gurūn ihaiva<br />bhuñjīya bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān [5]
<span class="e2">śreyaḥ</span>–Better;<span class="e2"> bhaikṣyam api bhoktum</span>–to live on food obtained by begging;<span class="e2"> iha loke</span>–in this world;<span class="e2"> ahatvā hi</span>–without killing;<span class="e2"> mahā-anubhāvān gurūn</span>–noble elders and teachers.<span class="e2"> tu</span>–Otherwise;<span class="e2"> gurūn hatvā</span>–by killing our teachers and superiors;<span class="e2"> bhuñjīya</span>–we shall enjoy;<span class="e2"> rudhira-pradigdhān</span>–their blood-tainted;<span class="e2"> artha-kāmān bhogān</span>–wealth and coveted enjoyable objects;<span class="e2"> iha eva</span>–here. [5]
5 It is better to live in this world and beg, without taking the lives of our noble elders and teachers. Otherwise, by killing them we shall remain in this world only to enjoy their wealth and possessions tainted with their blood.
न चैतद्वद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो<br />यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।<br />यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्<br />तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्त्तराष्ट्राः ॥६॥
na chaitad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo<br />yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ<br />yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas<br />te ’vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ [6]
<span class="e2">yat vā</span>–If indeed; (<span class="e2">vayam</span>)–we;<span class="e2"> jayema</span>–win;<span class="e2"> yadi vā</span>–or if; (<span class="e2">ete</span>)–these men;<span class="e2"> naḥ jayeyuḥ</span>–happen to conquer us;<span class="e2"> na cha vidmaḥ</span>–we do not understand;<span class="e2"> etat katarat</span>–which of these;<span class="e2"> garīyaḥ</span>–is more beneficial;<span class="e2"> naḥ</span>–for us.<span class="e2"> te dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ</span>–Those very sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra;<span class="e2"> yān hatvā</span>–by killing whom;<span class="e2"> na jijīviṣāmaḥ eva</span>–we do not wish to even live;<span class="e2"> avasthitāḥ</span>–are present;<span class="e2"> pramukhe</span>–before us for battle. [6]
6 I cannot understand which will be better—victory or defeat; for if we kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who now stand before us on the battlefront, we shall not wish to live.
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः<br />पृच्छामि त्वां धर्म्मसम्मूढचेताः ।<br />यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चतं ब्रूहि तन्मे<br />शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥७॥
kārpaṇya-doṣopahata-svabhāvaḥ<br />pṛchchhāmi tvāṁ dharma-sammūḍha-chetāḥ<br />yach chhreyaḥ syān niśchitaṁ brūhi tan me<br />śiṣyas te ’haṁ śādhi māṁ tvāṁ prapannam [7]
<span class="e2">kārpaṇya-doṣa upahata-svabhāvaḥ</span>–Losing heart, thus losing the courage of the warrior by apprehending the fall of the dynasty; (<span class="e2">tathā</span>)–and;<span class="e2"> dharma-sammūḍha-chetāḥ</span>–bewildered in determining my duty and non-duty; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> pṛchchhāmi</span>–I am asking;<span class="e2"> tvām</span>–You; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)<span class="e2"> brūhi</span>–You please say;<span class="e2"> tat</span>–that (course of action);<span class="e2"> yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> syāt</span>–may;<span class="e2"> niśchitam</span>–be ascertained;<span class="e2"> śreyaḥ</span>–as best;<span class="e2"> me</span>–for me.<span class="e2"> aham</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> te śiṣyaḥ</span>–ready for Your counsel and direction; (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–therefore;<span class="e2"> śādhi</span>–please instruct;<span class="e2"> mām</span>–me;<span class="e2"> tvām prapannam</span>–Your surrendered soul. [7]
7 Now I am bewildered. What is my real duty? I am losing heart and distraught. So please tell me clearly what is the best course of action to take. I am Your surrendered disciple; please instruct me.
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्<br />यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् ।<br />अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं<br />राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥८॥
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād<br />yach chhokam uchchhoṣaṇam indriyāṇām<br />avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṁ <br />rājyaṁ surāṇām api chādhipatyam [8]
<span class="e2">avāpya</span>–After gaining; <span class="e2">asapatnam</span>–an unrivalled; <span class="e2">ṛddham</span>–expansive; <span class="e2">rājyam</span>–kingdom; <span class="e2">bhūmau</span>–on earth; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">ādhipatyam</span>–sovereignty; <span class="e2">surāṇām api</span>–over even the demigods; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I; <span class="e2">na hi prapaśyāmi</span>–do not see; <span class="e2">yat</span>–that which; <span class="e2">apanudyāt</span>–will dispel; <span class="e2">mama</span>–my; <span class="e2">śokam</span>–grief; <span class="e2">uchchhoṣaṇam</span>–that saps; <span class="e2">indriyāṇām</span>–my senses. [8]
8 Even if we gain an unrivalled, flourishing kingdom on earth and sovereignty over heaven, I see nothing to dispel my debilitating grief.
सञ्जय उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तपः ।<br />न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥९॥
sañjaya uvācha
evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṁ guḍākeśaḥ parantapaḥ<br />na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṁ babhūva ha [9]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said:<span class="e2"> evam uktvā</span>–Having spoken thus;<span class="e2"> hṛṣīkeśam</span>–unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> guḍākeśaḥ</span>–sense-controlled Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep;<span class="e2"> parantapaḥ</span>–the chastiser of the enemy;<span class="e2"> uktvā iti</span>–then said;<span class="e2"> govindam</span>–to Govinda: (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> na yotsye</span>–“I shall not fight”;<span class="e2"> babhūva ha</span>–and then was;<span class="e2"> tūṣṇīm</span>–silent. [9]
9 Sañjaya said: Thus the valiant, vigilant Arjuna spoke to Kṛṣṇa, who is Hṛṣīkeś, the Lord of the senses of all beings. Then he declared, “Govinda, I will not fight”, and fell silent.
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत ।<br />सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥१०॥
tam uvācha hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata<br />senayor ubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṁ vachaḥ [10]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Dhṛtarāṣṭra;<span class="e2"> ubhayoḥ senayoḥ madhye</span>–situated between both armies;<span class="e2"> hṛṣīkeśaḥ</span>–Hṛṣīkeś, Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> prahasan iva</span>–smilingly;<span class="e2"> uvācha</span>–spoke;<span class="e2"> idam vachaḥ</span>–these words;<span class="e2"> viṣīdantam</span>–to the grief-stricken;<span class="e2"> tam</span>–Arjuna. [10]
10 O Bhārat, there amidst the armies, Śrī Hṛṣīkeś, smiling, spoke thus to the grief-stricken Arjuna:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे ।<br />गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥११॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
aśochyān anvaśochas tvaṁ prajñā-vādāṁś cha bhāṣase<br />gatāsūn agatāsūṁś cha nānuśochanti paṇḍitāḥ [11]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said:<span class="e2"> tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> anvaśochaḥ</span>–are lamenting;<span class="e2"> aśochyān</span>–for those unworthy of grief;<span class="e2"> prajñā-vādān cha bhāṣase</span>–and speaking like a wise man.<span class="e2"> paṇḍitāḥ</span>–The wise;<span class="e2"> na anuśochanti</span>–do not lament;<span class="e2"> gatāsūn</span>–for the dead;<span class="e2"> agatāsūn cha</span>–or the living. [11]
11 The Lord said: O Arjuna, you are lamenting for that which is unworthy of grief, yet speaking words of wisdom. The wise lament neither for the living nor the dead.
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।<br />न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्व्वे वयमतः परम् ॥१२॥
na tv evāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ<br />na chaiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param [12]
