(<span class="e2">iti</span>)<span class="e2"> tu na eva</span>–It is not a fact that;<span class="e2"> aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> na āsam</span>–did not exist;<span class="e2"> jātu</span>–ever before; (<span class="e2">iti</span>)<span class="e2"> na</span>–nor is it that;<span class="e2"> tvam na</span>–you did not exist; (<span class="e2">iti na</span>)–nor is it that;<span class="e2"> ime janādhipāḥ</span>–all these kings;<span class="e2"> na</span>–did not exist;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">iti na</span>)<span class="e2"> eva</span>–nor is it that;<span class="e2"> sarve vayam na bhaviṣyāmaḥ</span>–we will all no longer exist;<span class="e2"> ataḥ param</span>–hereafter. [12]
12 Never was there a time when you, I, or all these kings did not exist. Just as we exist in the present, so have we existed in the past, and shall continue to exist in the future.
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।<br />तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥१३॥
dehino ’smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā<br />tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati [13]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–As;<span class="e2"> asmin dehe</span>–in this body;<span class="e2"> dehinaḥ</span>–of the embodied living being;<span class="e2"> kaumāram</span>–childhood;<span class="e2"> yauvanam</span>–youth;<span class="e2"> jarā</span>–and old age; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–occur;<span class="e2"> tathā</span>–so also;<span class="e2"> deha-antara prāptiḥ</span>–the attainment of yet another body; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–occurs.<span class="e2"> dhīraḥ</span>–The wise;<span class="e2"> na muhyati</span>–are not deluded;<span class="e2"> tatra</span>–by that. [13]
13 As the living being passes through the bodily changes of childhood, youth, and old age, it similarly attains another body at death. The wise are not deluded by this.
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।<br />आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥१४॥
mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ<br />āgamāpāyino ’nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata [14]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna, son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> mātrā-sparśāḥ tu</span>–material contact—the engagement of the senses with their objects;<span class="e2"> śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ</span>–produces cold and heat, pleasure and pain sensations. (<span class="e2">te</span>)<span class="e2"> āgama-apāyinaḥ</span>–These come and go;<span class="e2"> anityāḥ</span>–and are temporary. (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–Therefore; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> titikṣasva</span>–endure;<span class="e2"> tān</span>–them. [14]
14 O son of Kuntī, the engagement of the senses with their objects produces the sensations of cold, heat, pleasure, and pain. But these effects are temporary—they come and go. Therefore, O Bhārat, you must endure them.
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।<br />समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥१५॥
yaṁ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṁ puruṣarṣabha<br />sama-duḥkha-sukhaṁ dhīraṁ so ’mṛtatvāya kalpate [15]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> puruṣa-ṛṣabha</span>–O noblest of men;<span class="e2"> saḥ dhīram puruṣam</span>–the wise man;<span class="e2"> sama-duḥkha-sukham</span>–equipoised in happiness and unhappiness;<span class="e2"> yam</span>–who;<span class="e2"> ete</span>–these; (<span class="e2">mātrā-sparśāḥ</span>)–actions of the senses engaging with material sense objects;<span class="e2"> na vyathayanti</span>–cannot disturb;<span class="e2"> kalpate hi</span>–is alone qualified;<span class="e2"> amṛtatvāya</span>–for immortality. [15]
15 O noblest of men, the wise man who is equipoised in pleasure and pain, and undisturbed by sense-experiences, is alone qualified for immortality.
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।<br />उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥१६॥
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ<br />ubhayor api dṛṣṭo ’ntas tv anayos tattva-darśibhiḥ [16]
<span class="e2">asataḥ</span>–Of a destructible object;<span class="e2"> na vidyate</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> bhāvaḥ</span>–eternal existence;<span class="e2"> tu</span>–and;<span class="e2"> sataḥ</span>–of an eternal object;<span class="e2"> na vidyate</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> abhāvaḥ</span>–destruction.<span class="e2"> antaḥ</span>–Such a conclusion, i.e., of the nature;<span class="e2"> anayoḥ ubhayoḥ api</span>–of each;<span class="e2"> dṛṣṭaḥ</span>–has been realised;<span class="e2"> tattva-darśibhiḥ</span>–by the seers of the truth.
16 Of the asat (destructible object, such as the mutable body and associated phenomena) there is no eternal existence; of the sat (eternal object, the soul) there is no destruction or change. The nature of each has been realised by the seers of the truth.
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्व्वमिदं ततम् ।<br />विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्त्तुमर्हति ॥१७॥
avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṁ tatam<br />vināśam avyayasyāsya na kaśchit kartum arhati [17]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But;<span class="e2"> viddhi</span>–know that;<span class="e2"> tat</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> yena</span>–by which;<span class="e2"> idam sarvam</span>–this entire body;<span class="e2"> tatam</span>–is pervaded;<span class="e2"> avināśi</span>–is indestructible.<span class="e2"> na kaśchit</span>–No one;<span class="e2"> arhati</span>–is able;<span class="e2"> vināśam kartum</span>–to bring about the destruction;<span class="e2"> avyayasya asya</span>–of this imperishable soul. [17]
17 Know that the soul, by which the entire body is pervaded, is indestructible. No one can destroy the imperishable soul.
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।<br />अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥१८॥
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ<br />anāśino ’prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata [18]
<span class="e2">śarīriṇaḥ</span>–Of the living being;<span class="e2"> nityasya</span>–who is always the same;<span class="e2"> anāśinaḥ</span>–indestructible;<span class="e2"> aprameyasya</span>–and immeasurable, due to his extremely subtle nature;<span class="e2"> ime dehāḥ</span>–all these bodies;<span class="e2"> uktāḥ</span>–are said to be;<span class="e2"> antavantaḥ</span>–subject to destruction;<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–therefore; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yudhyasva</span>–fight. [18]
18 The soul is said to be eternal, indestructible and immeasurable. Only these physical bodies are subject to destruction. Therefore fight, O Bhārat.
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।<br />उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥१९॥
ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ yaś chainaṁ manyate hatam<br />ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate [19]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–Those persons who;<span class="e2"> vetti</span>–think;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–this soul to be;<span class="e2"> hantāram</span>–a killer;<span class="e2"> yaḥ cha enam manyate</span>–and those who think it;<span class="e2"> hatam</span>–killed;<span class="e2"> tau ubhau</span>–both of them;<span class="e2"> na vijānītaḥ</span>–are ignorant; (<span class="e2">yasmāt</span>)–since;<span class="e2"> ayam</span>–this soul;<span class="e2"> na hanti</span>–neither kills anyone;<span class="e2"> na hanyate</span>–nor is killed by anyone. [19]
19 Those who think the living being slays, and those who think it is slain, are ignorant of the true nature of the soul; for the soul neither slays nor is slain.
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्<br />नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।<br />अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥२०॥
na jāyate mriyate vā kadāchin<br />nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ<br />ajo nityaḥ śāśvato ’yaṁ purāṇo<br />na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre [20]
<span class="e2">ayam</span>–This soul;<span class="e2"> na jāyate</span>–is neither born;<span class="e2"> vā na mriyate</span>–nor dies;<span class="e2"> kadāchit</span>–at any time;<span class="e2"> bhūtvā na vā</span>–nor being;<span class="e2"> bhavitā</span>–will it be created;<span class="e2"> bhūyaḥ</span>–again.<span class="e2"> ayam ajaḥ</span>–This soul is birthless;<span class="e2"> nityaḥ</span>–eternal;<span class="e2"> śāśvataḥ</span>–free from decay;<span class="e2"> purāṇaḥ</span>–ancient, changeless; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and; (<span class="e2">ayam</span>)–the soul;<span class="e2"> na hanyate</span>–is never destroyed; <span class="e2">śarīre hanyamāne </span>(<span class="e2">api</span>)–even if the body is destroyed. [20]
20 The soul is neither born nor dies; it has neither been nor will it be created, because it is unborn and eternal. It is ever-youthful, yet ancient. It is not destroyed when the body is destroyed.
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् ।<br />कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥२१॥
vedāvināśinaṁ nityaṁ ya enam ajam avyayam<br />kathaṁ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṁ ghātayati hanti kam [21]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yaḥ</span>–that person who;<span class="e2"> veda</span>–knows;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–this soul as;<span class="e2"> nityam</span>–eternal;<span class="e2"> ajam</span>–birthless;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–immutable;<span class="e2"> avināśinam</span>–and indestructible;<span class="e2"> katham</span>–how can;<span class="e2"> saḥ puruṣaḥ ghātayati</span>–that person cause the death;<span class="e2"> kam</span>–of anyone; (<span class="e2">vā</span>)–or; (<span class="e2">katham</span>)–how can;<span class="e2"> hanti</span>–he kill;<span class="e2"> kam</span>–anyone? [21]
21 O Pārtha, knowing the soul to be indestructible, eternal, birthless and immutable, how can a person kill or cause anyone to be killed?
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय<br />नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।<br />तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्य्<br />अन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥२२॥
vāsāṁsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya<br />navāni gṛhṇāti naro ’parāṇi<br />tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny<br />anyāni saṁyāti navāni dehī [22]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–As;<span class="e2"> naraḥ</span>–a man;<span class="e2"> vihāya</span>–rejecting;<span class="e2"> jīrṇāni vāsāṁsi</span>–torn clothes;<span class="e2"> gṛhṇāti</span>–accepts;<span class="e2"> aparāṇi navāni</span>–new garments;<span class="e2"> tathā</span>–similarly;<span class="e2"> dehī</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> vihāya</span>–rejecting;<span class="e2"> jīrṇāni</span>–old and decrepit;<span class="e2"> śarīrāṇi</span>–bodies;<span class="e2"> saṁyāti</span>–accepts;<span class="e2"> anyāni navāni</span>–new bodies. [22]
22 As a person adopts new garments, discarding those that are old and worn, similarly, the soul continues to adopt new bodies, leaving those that are old and useless.
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।<br />न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥२३॥
nainaṁ chhindanti śastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ<br />na chainaṁ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ [23]
<span class="e2">śastrāṇi</span>–Weapons;<span class="e2"> na chhindanti</span>–cannot pierce;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> pāvakaḥ</span>–fire;<span class="e2"> na dahati</span>–cannot burn;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> āpaḥ</span>–water;<span class="e2"> na kledayanti</span>–cannot dampen;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> mārutah</span>–the air;<span class="e2"> na śoṣayati</span>–cannot dry; (<span class="e2">enam</span>)–the soul. [23]
23 Weapons cannot pierce the soul, and fire cannot burn it. Water cannot wet it, and air cannot dry it.
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च ।<br />नित्यः सर्व्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥२४॥
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्य्योऽयमुच्यते ।<br />तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥२५॥
achchhedyo ’yam adāhyo ’yam akledyo ’śoṣya eva cha<br />nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur achalo ’yaṁ sanātanaḥ [24]
avyakto ’yam achintyo ’yam avikāryo ’yam uchyate<br />tasmād evaṁ viditvainaṁ nānuśochitum arhasi [25]
<span class="e2">ayam achchhedyaḥ</span>–The soul is indivisible;<span class="e2"> ayam adāhyaḥ</span>–it cannot be burned; (<span class="e2">ayam</span>)<span class="e2"> akledyaḥ</span>–it cannot be moistened; (<span class="e2">ayam</span>)<span class="e2"> aśoṣyaḥ eva cha</span>–and it cannot be dried.<span class="e2"> ayam nityaḥ</span>–It is everlasting;<span class="e2"> sarva-gataḥ</span>–reaching all planes, migratory through all species of life according to its actions;<span class="e2"> sthāṇuḥ</span>–still;<span class="e2"> achalaḥ</span>–immovable;<span class="e2"> sanātanaḥ</span>–beginningless, changeless, ever-present.<span class="e2"> ayam uchyate</span>–It is said to be;<span class="e2"> avyaktaḥ</span>–imperceptible due to its extremely subtle nature;<span class="e2"> ayam achintyaḥ</span>–inconceivable;<span class="e2"> ayam avikāryaḥ</span>–and untransformable.<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> viditvā</span>–knowing;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> evam</span>–as such;<span class="e2"> anuśochitum na arhasi</span>–it is inappropriate to grieve for it. [24–25]
24–25 It is said that the soul is indivisible and cannot be burned, moistened, or dried. It is eternal, it reaches all planes yet remains still, immovable, and ever-present. It is imperceptible, inconceivable, and untransformable (by the sixfold transformations*). Therefore, knowing the nature of the soul as such, there is no reason to lament for it.
*Birth, existence, growth, maturity, diminution, and destruction.
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।<br />तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैनं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥२६॥<br />जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।<br />तस्मादपरिहार्य्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥२७॥
atha chainaṁ nitya-jātaṁ nityaṁ vā manyase mṛtam<br />tathāpi tvaṁ mahā-bāho nainaṁ śochitum arhasi [26]
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṁ janma mṛtasya cha<br />tasmād aparihārye ’rthe na tvaṁ śochitum arhasi [27]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O best of warriors, Arjuna;<span class="e2"> atha cha</span>–and even if;<span class="e2"> manyase</span>–you think;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> nitya-jātam</span>–to be always born;<span class="e2"> vā</span>–or;<span class="e2"> nityam mṛtam</span>–always subject to death;<span class="e2"> tathā api</span>–even then;<span class="e2"> tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> sochitum na arhasi</span>–ought not grieve;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–for it;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–since;<span class="e2"> jātasya</span>–for one who has taken birth;<span class="e2"> mṛtyuḥ</span>–death;<span class="e2"> dhruvaḥ</span>–is certain;<span class="e2"> mṛtasya cha</span>–and for one who is dead;<span class="e2"> janma</span>–birth, for undergoing the reactions to his past actions;<span class="e2"> dhruvam</span>–is certain.<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> na arhasi</span>–ought not;<span class="e2"> śochitum</span>–grieve;<span class="e2"> aparihārye arthe</span>–for the inevitable. [26–27]
26–27 And, O best of warriors, even if you think that the soul is perpetually subject to birth and death, you still have no reason to lament. For one who is born, death is certain, and for one who dies, he must be reborn to undergo the reactions of his past actions. Therefore, you should not lament over the inevitable.
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत ।<br />अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥२८॥
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyakta-madhyāni bhārata<br />avyakta-nidhanāny eva tatra kā paridevanā [28]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–of the living beings;<span class="e2"> avyaktādīni</span>–the situation before birth is unknown;<span class="e2"> vyakta-madhyāni</span>–the period between birth and death is known;<span class="e2"> avyakta-nidhanāny eva</span>–and the situation after death is again unknown;<span class="e2"> kā paridevanā</span>–so what cause is there for grief;<span class="e2"> tatra</span>–in that matter?
28 O Bhārat, when all living beings are unmanifest before birth, manifest between birth and death, and again unmanifest at death, why lament for them?
आश्चर्य्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनम्<br />आश्चर्य्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः ।<br />आश्चर्य्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति<br />श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥२९॥
āścharyavat paśyati kaśchid enam<br />āścharyavad vadati tathaiva chānyaḥ<br />āścharyavach chainam anyaḥ śṛṇoti<br />śrutvāpy enaṁ veda na chaiva kaśchit [29]
<span class="e2">kaśchit</span>–Some persons;<span class="e2"> paśyati</span>–see;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–the soul;<span class="e2"> āścharyavat</span>–as astonishing.<span class="e2"> tathā eva</span>–Similarly;<span class="e2"> anyaḥ cha</span>–others, too;<span class="e2"> vadati</span>–describe; (<span class="e2">enam</span>)–the soul;<span class="e2"> āścharyavat</span>–as astonishing;<span class="e2"> anyaḥ cha</span>–and others;<span class="e2"> śṛṇoti</span>–hear;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–of the soul;<span class="e2"> āścharyavat</span>–as astonishing;<span class="e2"> kaśchit cha eva</span>–and some;<span class="e2"> śrutvā api</span>–though hearing about it;<span class="e2"> na veda</span>–do not know;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–the soul. [29]
29 Some see the soul as astonishing, some describe it as astonishing, some hear of it as astonishing, while others, though hearing about it, know nothing of it.
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्व्वस्य भारत ।<br />तस्मात्सर्व्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥३०॥
dehī nityam avadhyo ’yaṁ dehe sarvasya bhārata<br />tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṁ śochitum arhasi [30]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> dehe</span>–in the bodies;<span class="e2"> sarvasya</span>–of all living beings;<span class="e2"> ayam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> dehī</span>–soul;<span class="e2"> nityam</span>–is eternal;<span class="e2"> avadhyaḥ</span>–unslayable.<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> śochitum na arhasi</span>–should not lament;<span class="e2"> sarvāṇi bhūtāni</span>–for any living beings. [30]
30 O Bhārat, the soul dwelling within the bodies of all living beings is eternal and cannot be slain. Therefore, you need lament for no one.
स्वधर्म्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि ।<br />धर्म्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥३१॥
svadharmam api chāvekṣya na vikampitum arhasi<br />dharmyāddhi yuddhāch chhreyo ’nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate [31]
<span class="e2">api</span>–Moreover;<span class="e2"> na arhasi</span>–you should not;<span class="e2"> vikampitum</span>–fear;<span class="e2"> cha avekṣya</span>–considering, too;<span class="e2"> svadharmam</span>–your natural duty as a warrior;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–since;<span class="e2"> kṣatriyasya</span>–for a kṣatriya, or one who upholds the law;<span class="e2"> na vidyate</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> anyat śreyaḥ</span>–better course of action;<span class="e2"> dharmyāt yudhāt</span>–than a battle for justice.
31 Moreover, considering your natural duty, you have no reason to waver, since there is no action more auspicious for a warrior than a battle for justice.
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।<br />सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥३२॥
yadṛchchhayā chopapannaṁ svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam<br />sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam [32]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> sukhinaḥ</span>–the fortunate;<span class="e2"> kṣatriyāḥ</span>–warriors;<span class="e2"> labhante</span>–attain;<span class="e2"> yuddham</span>–a battle;<span class="e2"> īdṛśam</span>–like this;<span class="e2"> upapannam</span>–present;<span class="e2"> yadṛchchhayā</span>–of its own accord;<span class="e2"> apāvṛtam svarga-dvāram cha</span>–as an open door to heaven. [32]
32 O Pārtha, only the most fortunate warriors are blessed with the opportunity of such a battle, which has come to you like an open door to heaven.
Commentary
One’s natural duty or ‘svadharma’ is of two types—relative or absolute—according to the soul’s state of either material bondage or liberation respectively. In the liberated state, the natural function of the soul is purely spiritual devotional service, for the transcendental pleasure of the Supreme Lord alone. But in the state of material bondage, a person’s natural duty possesses mundane attributes. The conditioned soul accepts various births throughout the 8,400,000 species of life according to his actions, until by the influence of piety he obtains a human birth. Then, according to his nature, he may adopt a position and prescribed duty in the God-centred socio-religious system (Daiva-varṇāśram), which helps one attain the natural duty of the liberated state.
In this respect, the natural duty of the liberated soul is somewhat covered by the relativity of the material world; yet, within the God-centred socio-religious system, it is nonetheless considered a person’s natural duty, as, for example, smoke-covered fire is still considered fire, despite its covering.
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्म्यं सङ्ग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।<br />ततः स्वधर्म्मं कीर्त्तिञ्च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥३३॥
atha chet tvam imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṅgrāmaṁ na kariṣyasi<br />tataḥ svadharmaṁ kīrtiñ cha hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi [33]
<span class="e2">atha</span>–Otherwise;<span class="e2"> chet</span>–if;<span class="e2"> tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> na kariṣyasi</span>–do not engage;<span class="e2"> imam dharmyam saṅgrāmam</span>–in this battle for justice;<span class="e2"> tataḥ</span>–then;<span class="e2"> hitvā</span>–leaving;<span class="e2"> svadharmam kīrtim cha</span>–the kṣatriya’s duty and glory;<span class="e2"> avāpsyasi</span>–you will incur;<span class="e2"> pāpam</span>–sin. [33]
33 But if you choose not to fight this battle for justice, your religious principles will be lost, fame will desert you, and sin will overcome you.
अकीर्त्तिञ्चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् ।<br />सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्त्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥३४॥
akīrtiñ chāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te ’vyayām<br />sambhāvitasya chākīrtir maraṇād atirichyate [34]
<span class="e2">cha</span>–Also;<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–the people;<span class="e2"> kathayiṣyanti</span>–will speak;<span class="e2"> avyayām</span>–for all time;<span class="e2"> te</span>–of your;<span class="e2"> akīrtim api</span>–infamy;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> akīrtiḥ</span>–infamy;<span class="e2"> atirichyate</span>–is worse;<span class="e2"> maraṇāt</span>–than death;<span class="e2"> sambhāvitasya</span>–for the respected. [34]
34 People will speak of your infamy for all time to come; and for the renowned, infamy is worse than death.
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः ।<br />येषाञ्च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥३५॥
bhayād raṇād uparataṁ maṁsyante tvāṁ mahā-rathāḥ<br />yeṣāñ cha tvaṁ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam [35]
<span class="e2">mahā-rathāḥ</span>–Great warriors like Duryodhan and others;<span class="e2"> maṁsyante</span>–will consider that;<span class="e2"> tvām</span>–you;<span class="e2"> uparatam</span>–desisted;<span class="e2"> raṇāt</span>–from battle;<span class="e2"> bhayāt</span>–out of fear;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> yeṣāṁ</span>–of those for whom;<span class="e2"> tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> bahu-mataḥ bhūtvā</span>–have been the object of great honour;<span class="e2"> lāghavam yāsyasi</span>–you will be held the object of ridicule. [35]
35 The great warriors who highly honour you will ridicule you, considering that you were afraid to fight.
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।<br />निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥३६॥
avāchya-vādāṁś cha bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ<br />nindantas tava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim [36]
<span class="e2">tava ahitāḥ</span>–Your enemies;<span class="e2"> vadiṣyanti</span>–will speak;<span class="e2"> bahūn avāchya-vādān cha</span>–many unworthy words;<span class="e2"> nindantaḥ</span>–condemning;<span class="e2"> tava sāmarthyam</span>–your capabilities.<span class="e2"> nu</span>–Alas, Arjuna;<span class="e2"> kim</span>–what could be;<span class="e2"> duḥkhataram</span>–more painful;<span class="e2"> tataḥ</span>–than that? [36]
36 Your enemies will mock you. What could be more painful?
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।<br />तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥३७॥
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm<br />tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niśchayaḥ [37]
<span class="e2">hataḥ vā</span>–If killed in battle;<span class="e2"> svargam prāpsyasi</span>–you will attain heaven;<span class="e2"> jitvā vā</span>–or by gaining victory;<span class="e2"> bhokṣyase</span>–you will enjoy;<span class="e2"> mahīm</span>–the earth.<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–Therefore; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">kṛta-niśchayaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being confident of success;<span class="e2"> uttiṣṭha</span>–arise;<span class="e2"> yuddhāya</span>–for battle. [37]
37 O son of Kuntī, if you are killed, you will attain heaven, and if you are victorious, you will enjoy your life on earth. Therefore, being confident of your success, arise for battle!
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।<br />ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥३८॥
sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau<br />tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi [38]
<span class="e2">same kṛtvā</span>–By seeing with an attitude of equanimity;<span class="e2"> sukha-duḥkhe</span>–pleasure and pain;<span class="e2"> lābha-alābhau</span>–gain and loss; <span class="e2">jaya-ajayau </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and victory and defeat;<span class="e2"> tataḥ</span>–thereafter;<span class="e2"> yujyasva</span>–engage;<span class="e2"> yuddhāya</span>–in battle.<span class="e2"> evam</span>–In this way;<span class="e2"> na avāpsyasi</span>–you will not incur;<span class="e2"> pāpam</span>–sin. [38]
38 Considering pleasure and pain, gain and loss, and victory and defeat to be one and the same—fight. No sin will be incurred by you.
एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृनु ॥<br />बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्म्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥३९॥
eṣā te ’bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṁ śṛnu<br />buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karma-bandhaṁ prahāsyasi [39]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> abhihitā te</span>–I have revealed to you;<span class="e2"> eṣā buddhiḥ sāṅkhye</span>–this knowledge of the soul.<span class="e2"> tu</span>–Further;<span class="e2"> śṛṇu</span>–hear of;<span class="e2"> imām</span>–this knowledge;<span class="e2"> yoge</span>–in (bhakti-) yoga, in practice;<span class="e2"> yayā buddhyā yuktaḥ</span>–attaining which wisdom;<span class="e2"> prahāsyasi</span>–you will be completely freed;<span class="e2"> karma-bandham</span>–from the bondage of action. [39]
39 I have revealed to you this knowledge (buddhi) of the soul. Now hear from Me how to act in this knowledge (bhakti-yoga), through which you will be able to free yourself from the bondage of action.
Commentary
“It will be revealed that buddhi-yoga (yoga of wisdom) is a singular path. When buddhi-yoga is seen to be limited by the ideal of action, it is known as karma-yoga; when it extends beyond action up to the peak of knowledge, it is known as jñāna-yoga or sāṅkhya-yoga; and when, transcending the limitations of both action and knowledge it touches bhakti or devotion, it is then known as bhakti-yoga, or perfectly pure and complete buddhi-yoga.”
—Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।<br />स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्म्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥४०॥
nehābhikrama-nāśo ’sti pratyavāyo na vidyate<br />svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt [40]
<span class="e2">iha</span>–In this (bhakti-) yoga;<span class="e2"> na asti</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> abhikrama-nāśaḥ</span>–failure in the beginning;<span class="e2"> na vidyate</span>–and there is no;<span class="e2"> pratyavāyaḥ</span>–diminution of results.<span class="e2"> svalpam api</span>–Even the slightest practice;<span class="e2"> asya dharmasya</span>–of this bhakti-yoga;<span class="e2"> trāyate</span>–saves one;<span class="e2"> mahataḥ bhayāt</span>–from the great fear of birth and death in the material world. [40]
40 On this path there can be no loss and no harm. The slightest practice of such a spiritual ideal saves one from the greatest fear.
Commentary
Mahābhay, the greatest fear, is generally considered to be the fear of repeated birth and death in this world. But mahābhay also refers to sāyujya-mukti, the liberation of merging into the impersonal non-differentiated consciousness of Brahmaloka, Virajā, or a kind of impersonal samādhi. Renunciation alone leads to sāyujya-mukti, the cessation of birth and death, but not to a life in the positive plane. It takes one to a permanent ‘burial’ in Brahmaloka. The demon of mukti will devour one wholesale, and therefore it is even more dangerous than this ordinary life of action and reaction. Mukti means a strike in the organic system, so it must be avoided. For example, to either ignore duties in a factory or to declare a strike by cessation of duties are both abnormal.
Bhukti, exploitation, and mukti, renunciation, are both fearsome ghosts. Therefore, here, mahābhay means the great apprehension of falling prey to both the ghost of exploitation leading to birth and death, as well as the ghost of committing suicide by merging into the impersonalism of incarceration in Brahmaloka—fear of both bhoga-bhūmi, the land of exploitation, and tyāga-bhūmi, the plane of renunciation. It is stated in the <span class="e3">Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</span> (1.2.22, 1.1.9):
भुक्तिमुक्तिस्पृहा यावत् पिशाची हृदि वर्त्तते ।<br />तावद्भक्तिसुखस्यात्र कथमभ्युदयो भवेत् ॥
bhukti-mukti-spṛhā yāvat piśāchī hṛdi vartate<br />tāvad bhakti-sukhasyātra katham abhyudayo bhavet
“The ecstasy of devotion to Kṛṣṇa will never appear in a heart that is haunted by the ghosts of exploitation and renunciation.”
अन्याभिलाषिता शून्यं ज्ञानकर्म्माद्यनावृतम् ।<br />आनुकूल्येन कृष्णनुशीलनं भक्तरुत्तमा ॥
anyābhilāṣitā śūnyaṁ jñāna-karmādy anāvṛtam<br />ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānuśīlanaṁ bhaktir uttamā
“The highest devotion is that which is cultivated for the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, with no desire except to serve Him, and divested of all external attempts such as worldly action, knowledge in search of the impersonal Absolute, or the meditational attempt to become one with God.”
Only the Supreme Lord is abhay, beyond apprehension. Therefore nothing but participation in His service can free one from the ghosts of exploitation and renunciation, bhukti and mukti. If we subtract bhukti and mukti, then only positive bhakti, devotion, is the remainder. Therefore, without devotion, everything is mahābhay, great danger.
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन ।<br />बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥४१॥
vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana<br />bahu-śākhā hy anantāś cha buddhayo ’vyavasāyinām [41]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kuru-nandana</span>–O Arjuna, descendant of the Kuru dynasty;<span class="e2"> vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ</span>–the resolute intelligence;<span class="e2"> iha</span>–to practise this (bhakti-) yoga; <span class="e2">eka </span>(<span class="e2">eva</span>)–is onepointed; (<span class="e2">tu</span>)–but;<span class="e2"> buddhayaḥ</span>–the intelligence;<span class="e2"> avyavasāyinām</span>–of the irresolute—those who nurture mundane desires;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–is certainly;<span class="e2"> anantāḥ</span>–endlessly;<span class="e2"> bahu-śākhāḥ cha</span>–many-branched, splayed. [41]
41 O descendant of the Kuru dynasty, resolute intelligence dedicated to Me is one-pointed—I am its only objective. But irresolute intelligence is splayed by endless desires for mundane enjoyment.
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाच प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।<br />वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥४२॥
yām imāṁ puṣpitāṁ vāchaṁ pravadanty avipaśchitaḥ<br />veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ [42]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> avipaśchitaḥ</span>–the unwise;<span class="e2"> veda-vāda-ratāḥ</span>–who are fond of interpreting the Vedas, not knowing the true directive of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> vādinaḥ iti</span>–say that;<span class="e2"> na asti</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> anyat</span>–other (divine or controlling) principle beyond beasts, food, offspring, heaven, etc.;<span class="e2"> pravadanti</span>–and they glorify as supreme;<span class="e2"> yām imām vācham</span>–those statements which;<span class="e2"> puṣpitām</span>–momentarily please the ear (which, thus taken out of context, are effectively poisonous as they do not help the spiritual progress of the soul). [42]
42 O Pārtha, unwise persons, not knowing that the chief directive of the Vedas is the attainment of the Supreme Truth, are fond of interpreting the fleetingly enchanting words of the karma-kāṇḍa section of the Vedas as ultimate.
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपराः जन्मकर्म्मफलप्रदाम् ।<br />क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्य्यगतिं प्रति ॥४३॥
kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parāḥ janma-karma-phala-pradām<br />kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṁ bhogaiśvarya-gatiṁ prati [43]
<span class="e2">kāma-ātmānaḥ</span>–Their hearts filled with selfish desires;<span class="e2"> svarga-parāḥ</span>–heaven is their goal;<span class="e2"> kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulām</span>–and they advocate the various ceremonies and rituals;<span class="e2"> janmakarma-phala-pradām</span>–which yield high birth;<span class="e2"> bhoga-aiśvarya-gatim prati</span>–and lead to enjoyment and opulence. [43]
43 Their hearts are filled with desires and their goal is heaven. They advocate the many sacrifices and rituals that yield wealth, worldly pleasures, and high birth.
भोगैश्वर्य्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।<br />व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥४४॥
bhogaiśvarya-prasaktānāṁ tayāpahṛta-chetasām<br />vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate [44]
<span class="e2">bhoga-aiśvarya-prasaktānām</span>–Of those persons attached to enjoyment and opulence;<span class="e2"> apahṛta-chetasām</span>–whose minds are deluded;<span class="e2"> tayā</span>–by those flowery words of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ</span>–the resolve;<span class="e2"> samādhau</span>–in dedication to the Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> na vidhīyate</span>–is not accomplished. [44]
44 Thus attached to enjoyment and opulence, deluded by these flowery words of the Vedas, they do not attain the resolve to dedicate themselves to the Supreme Lord.
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्ज्जुन ।<br />निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥४५॥
traiguṇya-viṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna<br />nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣema ātmavān [45]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> vedāḥ</span>–the Vedas;<span class="e2"> trai-guṇya-viṣayāḥ</span>–deal with the modes of material nature—worldly subjects.<span class="e2"> nirdvandvaḥ</span>–Give up duality (honour and dishonour, etc., in the purview of these modes);<span class="e2"> nitya-sattva-sthaḥ</span>–be always situated in the truth (or remain with the true devotees);<span class="e2"> niryoga-kṣemaḥ</span>–free from acquisition and preservation; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and; <span class="e2">ātmavān </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–engaging in this buddhi-yoga, yoga of wisdom that I teach you;<span class="e2"> bhava</span>–become;<span class="e2"> nistraiguṇyaḥ</span>–transcendental to the three modes of material nature. [45]
45 O Arjuna, the Vedas deal with the three modes of material nature (by accommodating fruitive action and liberation as an allowance and incentive for persons who are ignorant of the true objective of the Vedas). But you, Arjuna, give up duality and all pursuits for gain and preservation, stand ever in the plane of truth, and by the yoga of wisdom, transcend the modes of nature.
(The objective of the Vedas is transcendental. Without fruitive action or liberation, O Arjuna, follow the transcendental path of devotion to the Lord as taught by the Vedas.)
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्व्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके ।<br />तावान्सर्व्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥४६॥
yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake<br />tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ [46]
<span class="e2">yāvān arthaḥ</span>–Of various purposes; (<span class="e2">sidhyati</span>)–achieved;<span class="e2"> udapāne</span>–by a well or pond; <span class="e2">tāvān </span>(<span class="e2">eva arthaḥ</span>)–all the purposes;<span class="e2"> sarvataḥ</span>–of all these wells; (<span class="e2">sidhyati</span>)–are achieved; (<span class="e2">tato ’pi vaiśiṣṭyena</span>)–better than that;<span class="e2"> sampluta-udake</span>–by a large expanse of water, a lake. (<span class="e2">evam</span>)–Similarly; (<span class="e2">yāvān arthaḥ sidhyati</span>)–of the various purposes fulfilled;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu vedeṣu</span>–by the prayers described in all the Vedas for worshipping the various demigods; (<span class="e2">tāvān arthaḥ sidhyati</span>)–those purposes are all fulfilled; (<span class="e2">bhagavad ārādhane eva</span>)–by worshipping the Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ</span>–for the brāhmaṇ who is in full knowledge that devotion to the Lord is the sole purport of the Vedas. [46]
46 As all the purposes served by several ponds can be served better by a large lake, similarly, the fruits of worshipping the various gods by their respective Vedic prayers are surpassed by serving Me. The knower of Brahma who thus knows the purport of the Vedas fulfils all life’s objectives.
कर्म्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।<br />मा कर्म्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्म्मणि ॥४७॥
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadāchana<br />mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stv akarmaṇi [47]
<span class="e2">te</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> adhikāraḥ</span>–right;<span class="e2"> eva karmaṇi</span>–is to perform your prescribed duties; <span class="e2">mā kadāchana </span>(<span class="e2">bhūḥ</span>)–but never;<span class="e2"> phaleṣu</span>–to the results.<span class="e2"> mā bhūḥ</span>–Be neither;<span class="e2"> karma-phala-hetuḥ</span>–motivated by the fruits of action;<span class="e2"> mā</span>–nor;<span class="e2"> astu</span>–may;<span class="e2"> akarmaṇi</span>–non-performance of your prescribed duties; (<span class="e2">bhūḥ</span>)–be;<span class="e2"> te</span>–your;<span class="e2"> saṅgaḥ</span>–inclination. [47]
47 Your right is to your work, never to the fruits. Be neither motivated by the fruit of action nor inclined to give up action.
योगस्थः कुरु कर्म्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।<br />सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥४८॥
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya<br />siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate [48]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dhanañjaya</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yoga-sthaḥ</span>–stand in yoga;<span class="e2"> tyaktvā</span>–giving up;<span class="e2"> saṅgam</span>–ego;<span class="e2"> samaḥ bhūtvā</span>–and being equipoised;<span class="e2"> siddhi-asiddhyoḥ</span>–in success and failure;<span class="e2"> kuru</span>–do;<span class="e2"> karmāṇi</span>–your duties; (<span class="e2">yataḥ</span>)–as;<span class="e2"> samatvam</span>–such equanimity;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> yogaḥ</span>–yoga. [48]
48 O Dhanañjaya, give up the ego that you are the doer, and be equipoised in success and failure. Thus stand firm in the plane of yoga and do your prescribed duties. Such a state of balance is indeed known as yoga.
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय ।<br />बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥४९॥
dūreṇa hy avaraṁ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañjaya<br />buddhau śaraṇam anvichchha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ [49]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dhanañjaya</span>–O Dhanañjaya;<span class="e2"> karma hi</span>–action alone;<span class="e2"> dūreṇa avaram</span>–is far inferior;<span class="e2"> buddhi-yogāt</span>–to the yoga of wisdom; (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–therefore;<span class="e2"> anvichchha</span>–seek;<span class="e2"> śaraṇam</span>–refuge;<span class="e2"> buddhau</span>–in the wisdom of equanimity.<span class="e2"> phala-hetavaḥ</span>–Those motivated by the fruits of their actions;<span class="e2"> kṛpaṇāḥ</span>–are misers. [49]
49 O Dhanañjaya, (fruitive) action is far inferior to this yoga of wisdom; those motivated by the fruits of their actions are misers. Therefore, seek refuge in the selfless wisdom of equanimity.
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते ।<br />तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्म्मसु कौशलम् ॥५०॥
buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte<br />tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam [50]
<span class="e2">buddhi-yuktaḥ</span>–The wise person;<span class="e2"> jahāti</span>–abstains;<span class="e2"> ubhe</span>–from both;<span class="e2"> sukṛta-duṣkṛte</span>–pious and sinful actions;<span class="e2"> iha</span>–in this world.<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> yujyasva</span>–engage;<span class="e2"> yogāya</span>–in yoga.<span class="e2"> yogaḥ</span>–Yoga;<span class="e2"> kauśalam</span>–is the expertise;<span class="e2"> karmasu</span>–of action. [50]
50 The wise person abstains from both good and bad actions in this world. Engage thus in yoga, as yoga is the art of all works.
कर्म्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।<br />जन्मबन्धविनिर्म्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥५१॥
karma-jaṁ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ<br />janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padaṁ gachchhanty anāmayam [51]
<span class="e2">hi</span>–Since;<span class="e2"> tyaktvā</span>–by giving up;<span class="e2"> phalam</span>–the fruits;<span class="e2"> karma-jam</span>–born of work;<span class="e2"> buddhi-yuktāḥ</span>–the wise; <span class="e2">manīṣiṇaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–are enlightened; <span class="e2">janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–and attaining liberation from the bondage of birth;<span class="e2"> gachchhanti</span>–attain;<span class="e2"> padam</span>–the plane;<span class="e2"> anāmayam</span>–beyond suffering. [51]
51 The wise are enlightened by giving up the fruits of their actions, and thus attaining liberation from the bondage of birth, they reach the plane beyond all suffering.
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।<br />तदा गन्तासि निर्व्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥५२॥
yadā te moha-kalilaṁ buddhir vyatitariṣyati<br />tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śrotavyasya śrutasya cha [52]
<span class="e2">yadā</span>–When;<span class="e2"> te</span>–your;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–intelligence;<span class="e2"> vyatitariṣyati</span>–overcomes;<span class="e2"> moha-kalilam</span>–the strong illusion (of bodily identification);<span class="e2"> tadā</span>–then; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)<span class="e2"> gantāsi</span>–you will attain;<span class="e2"> nirvedam</span>–indifference;<span class="e2"> śrotavyasya</span>–of all to be heard;<span class="e2"> śrutasya cha</span>–and already heard. [52]
52 When your intelligence fully emerges from the dense forest of illusion, you will be indifferent to all that has been heard or is yet to be heard.
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।<br />समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥५३॥
śruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niśchalā<br />samādhāv achalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi [53]
<span class="e2">yadā</span>–When;<span class="e2"> te buddhiḥ</span>–your intelligence;<span class="e2"> achalā</span>–unmoved;<span class="e2"> śruti-vipratipannā</span>–by the apparent contradictions of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> sthāsyati</span>–remains;<span class="e2"> niśchalā samādhau</span>–steadily absorbed in consciousness of the Supreme;<span class="e2"> tadā</span>–then;<span class="e2"> avāpsyasi</span>–you will attain;<span class="e2"> yogam</span>–yoga. [53]
53 You shall attain perfect yoga or pure devotion when your intelligence, undisturbed by the apparent contradictions of the Vedas, abides in the Lord.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।<br />स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥५४॥
arjuna uvācha
sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhi-sthasya keśava<br />sthita-dhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣeta kim āsīta vrajeta kim [54]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> keśava</span>–O Keśava;<span class="e2"> kā bhāṣā</span>–what is the description;<span class="e2"> sthita-prajñasya</span>–of a person of firmly established wisdom;<span class="e2"> samādhi-sthasya</span>–one in samādhi, absorbed in thought of the Supreme?<span class="e2"> sthita-dhīḥ kim prabhāṣeta</span>–How does such a person of steady mind speak?<span class="e2"> kim āsīta kim vrajeta</span>–How does he be and act? [54]
54 Arjuna said: O Keśava, what are the characteristics of the person of firmly established wisdom, who is fully absorbed in consciousness of the Supreme (samādhi)? How does such a man of steady mind speak, be, and act in this world?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्व्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।<br />आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥५५॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān<br />ātmany evātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthita-prajñas tadochyate [55]
<span class="e2">śri bhagavān uvācha</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> yadā</span>–when; (<span class="e2">jīvaḥ</span>)–the living being;<span class="e2"> prajahāti</span>–gives up;<span class="e2"> sarvān</span>–all;<span class="e2"> kāmān</span>–desires;<span class="e2"> manaḥ-gatān</span>–entering the mind; <span class="e2">tuṣṭaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–and is content;<span class="e2"> ātmanā eva</span>–by the self;<span class="e2"> ātmani</span>–within the self;<span class="e2"> tadā</span>–then; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–that person;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is said to be;<span class="e2"> sthita-prajñaḥ</span>–of steady intelligence. [55]
55 The Supreme Lord said: O Pārtha, one who rejects all desires that enter the mind and remains self-satisfied within is known as a person whose wisdom is firmly established.
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।<br />वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥५६॥
duḥkheṣv anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ<br />vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir uchyate [56]
<span class="e2">anudvigna-manāḥ</span>–One whose mind is undisturbed;<span class="e2"> duḥkheṣu</span>–by sorrow;<span class="e2"> vigata-spṛhaḥ sukheṣu</span>–and whose hankering for pleasure has gone; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and;<span class="e2"> vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ</span>–who is free from attachment, fear, and anger; (<span class="e2">saḥ eva</span>)–such a person;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is said to be;<span class="e2"> muniḥ</span>–a silent sage;<span class="e2"> sthita-dhīḥ</span>–of steady intelligence. [56]
56 One who is undisturbed by sorrow, whose hankering for pleasure has gone, and who is free from attachment, fear, and anger, is known as a silent sage of steady mind.
यः सर्व्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।<br />नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥५७॥
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śubhāśubham<br />nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā [57]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who;<span class="e2"> anabhisnehaḥ</span>–is without attachment;<span class="e2"> sarvatra</span>–for anything in this world;<span class="e2"> na abhinandati</span>–neither joyful;<span class="e2"> na dveṣṭi</span>–nor resentful;<span class="e2"> prāpya</span>–in the event of;<span class="e2"> śubha-aśubham</span>–auspiciousness or inauspiciousness;<span class="e2"> tat tat</span>–respectively;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–his;<span class="e2"> prajñā</span>–wisdom;<span class="e2"> pratiṣṭhitā</span>–is firmly established. [57]
57 One who is not attached to anything in this world, who neither enjoys nor resents auspiciousness or inauspiciousness—his wisdom is firmly established.
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्म्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्व्वशः ।<br />इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥५८॥
yadā saṁharate chāyaṁ kūrmo ’ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ<br />indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā [58]
<span class="e2">yadā cha</span>–When;<span class="e2"> ayam</span>–this person;<span class="e2"> sarvaśaḥ</span>–completely;<span class="e2"> saṁharate</span>–withdraws;<span class="e2"> kūrmaḥ aṅgāni iva</span>–like the limbs of a tortoise;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi</span>–the perceptual senses;<span class="e2"> indriya-arthebhyaḥ</span>–from their objects (sound, touch, form, taste, and smell); (<span class="e2">tadā</span>)–then;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–his;<span class="e2"> prajñā</span>–wisdom;<span class="e2"> pratiṣṭhitā</span>–is firmly established. [58]
58 When one’s senses are controlled and totally withdrawn from their objects, like the limbs of the tortoise withdrawn in its shell, his wisdom is firmly established.
विषया विनिवर्त्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।<br />रसवर्ज्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्त्तते ॥५९॥
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ<br />rasa-varjaṁ raso ’py asya paraṁ dṛṣṭvā nivartate [59]
<span class="e2">dehinaḥ</span>–For the embodied;<span class="e2"> nirāhārasya</span>–who restricts the senses;<span class="e2"> viṣayāḥ</span>–the objects of the senses;<span class="e2"> vinivartante</span>–recede;<span class="e2"> rasa-varjam</span>–but not the taste to enjoy them.<span class="e2"> rasaḥ api</span>–But even the taste;<span class="e2"> nivartate</span>–disappears;<span class="e2"> asya</span>–for the man of wisdom;<span class="e2"> dṛṣṭvā</span>–by the vision;<span class="e2"> param</span>–of the Supreme. [59]
59 The embodied being may renounce the sense objects, but the taste for them remains. But that, too, vanishes for the man of wisdom, by his vision of the Supreme.
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।<br />इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥६०॥
yatato hy api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaśchitaḥ<br />indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṁ manaḥ [60]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–yet;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi pramāthīni</span>–the turbulent senses;<span class="e2"> prasabham</span>–forcibly;<span class="e2"> haranti</span>–snatch away;<span class="e2"> manaḥ</span>–the mind;<span class="e2"> vipaśchitaḥ puruṣasya api</span>–of even the wise person;<span class="e2"> yatataḥ</span>–striving for liberation. [60]
60 And yet, O son of Kuntī, the turbulent senses can forcibly plunder the mind of even the wise person striving for liberation.
तानि सर्व्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।<br />वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥६१॥
tāni sarvāṇi saṁyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ<br />vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā [61]
<span class="e2">saṁyamya</span>–Controlling;<span class="e2"> tāni sarvāṇi</span>–all these senses;<span class="e2"> mat-paraḥ</span>–the person absorbed in consciousness of Me, devoted to Me;<span class="e2"> yuktaḥ āsīta</span>–should remain one-pointed in concentration;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–for;<span class="e2"> yasya</span>–he whose;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi</span>–senses;<span class="e2"> vaśe</span>–have been brought under control;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–his;<span class="e2"> prajñā</span>–intelligence;<span class="e2"> pratiṣṭhitā</span>–is steady. [61]
61 Devoted to Me, the bhakti-yogī brings his senses under proper control. Firmly established is the wisdom of one whose senses are controlled.
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।<br />सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥६२॥
dhyāyato viṣayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate<br />saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho ’bhijāyate [62]
<span class="e2">dhyāyataḥ</span>–(Otherwise, without devotion, renunciation alone fails:) By thinking of;<span class="e2"> viṣayān</span>–the objects of the senses;<span class="e2"> puṁsaḥ</span>–a person’s;<span class="e2"> saṅgaḥ</span>–attachment;<span class="e2"> teṣu</span>–to them;<span class="e2"> upajāyate</span>–is born.<span class="e2"> saṅgāt</span>–From attachment;<span class="e2"> kāmaḥ</span>–desire;<span class="e2"> sañjāyate</span>–is born. <span class="e2">kāmāt</span>–From desire;<span class="e2"> krodhaḥ</span>–anger;<span class="e2"> abhijāyate</span>–arises. [62]
62 But one whose thoughts dwell on the objects of the senses becomes attached to them. From attachment, desire is born, and from desire, anger arises.
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।<br />स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥६३॥
krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ<br />smṛti-bhraṁśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati [63]
<span class="e2">krodhāt</span>–From anger;<span class="e2"> saṁmohaḥ</span>–delusion;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–occurs.<span class="e2"> saṁmohāt</span>–From delusion;<span class="e2"> smṛti-vibhramaḥ</span>–forgetfulness of scriptural morality; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–occurs.<span class="e2"> smṛti-bhraṁ śāt</span>–From forgetfulness;<span class="e2"> buddhi-nāśaḥ</span>–loss of truth-seeking intelligence; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–occurs.<span class="e2"> buddhi-nāśāt</span>–From loss of intelligence; (<span class="e2">pumān</span>)–a person;<span class="e2"> praṇaśyati</span>–falls into saṁsāra, the cycle of birth and death in the material world. [63]
63 Anger gives rise to delusion, and the power of delusion causes forgetfulness; forgetfulness destroys the intelligence, and when the intelligence is lost, one loses all.
रागद्वेषविमुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।<br />आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥६४॥
rāga-dveṣa-vimuktais tu viṣayān indriyaiś charan<br />ātma-vaśyair vidheyātmā prasādam adhigachchhati [64]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But;<span class="e2"> vidheya-ātmā</span>–the person who can control his mind at will—whose mind is obedient to him; <span class="e2">rāga-dveṣa-vimuktaiḥ </span>(or <span class="e2">-viyuktaiḥ</span> in another reading)–free from attraction and repulsion, adopting yukta-vairāgya or devotionally integrated detachment;<span class="e2"> charan</span>–actively accepting;<span class="e2"> viṣayān</span>–objects;<span class="e2"> ātma-vaśyaiḥ indriyaiḥ</span>–through senses under his own control;<span class="e2"> adhigachchhati</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> prasādam</span>–tranquillity. [64]
64 But the integrated person who can control his mind at will, and who, free from attraction and repulsion, accepts his worldly necessities through his controlled senses, attains tranquillity.
प्रसादे सर्व्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।<br />प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्यशु बुद्धिः पर्य्यवतिष्ठते ॥६५॥
prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṁ hānir asyopajāyate<br />prasanna-chetaso hy āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate [65]
<span class="e2">prasāde </span>(<span class="e2">sati</span>)–When the heart is tranquil;<span class="e2"> asya</span>–for such a person;<span class="e2"> hāniḥ</span>–the end;<span class="e2"> sarva-duḥkhānām</span>–of all sorrows;<span class="e2"> upajāyate</span>–occurs;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–since;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–the wisdom; <span class="e2">prasanna-chetasaḥ</span>–of the peaceful-hearted person;<span class="e2"> āśu</span>–swiftly becomes;<span class="e2"> pari-avatiṣṭhate</span>–steadfast. [65]
65 When one attains a peaceful heart, all his sorrows are dispelled. The tranquil person’s wisdom swiftly becomes steadfast.
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।<br />न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥६६॥
nāsti buddhir ayuktasya na chāyuktasya bhāvanā<br />na chābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham [66]
<span class="e2">ayuktasya</span>–For a person without self-control;<span class="e2"> na asti</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–wisdom, self-knowledge.<span class="e2"> ayuktasya</span>–For such a person devoid of this intelligence; <span class="e2">na cha </span>(<span class="e2">asti</span>)–there is no;<span class="e2"> bhāvanā</span>–meditation on the Lord, purity of thought.<span class="e2"> abhāvayataḥ</span>–For one without meditation; <span class="e2">na cha </span>(<span class="e2">asti</span>)–there is no;<span class="e2"> śāntiḥ</span>–peace.<span class="e2"> aśāntasya</span>–For a person who has no peace;<span class="e2"> kutaḥ</span>–where is;<span class="e2"> sukham</span>–happiness? [66]
66 A person bereft of self-control can have neither wisdom nor meditation. Without meditation there is no peace, and without peace, where is the hope for happiness?
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते ।<br />तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥६७॥
indriyāṇāṁ hi charatāṁ yan mano ’nuvidhīyate<br />tad asya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi [67]
<span class="e2">hi</span>–Because;<span class="e2"> iva</span>–as;<span class="e2"> vāyuḥ</span>–an unfavourable wind; (<span class="e2">harati</span>)–carries away;<span class="e2"> nāvam</span>–a boat;<span class="e2"> ambhasi</span>–on the ocean; (<span class="e2">tadvat</span>)–similarly;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇām</span>–of the senses;<span class="e2"> charatāṁ</span>–that wander about their objects;<span class="e2"> yat</span>–whichever sense;<span class="e2"> manaḥ</span>–the mind;<span class="e2"> anuvidhīyate</span>–follows;<span class="e2"> tat</span>–that sense;<span class="e2"> harati</span>–carries away, lures towards its object;<span class="e2"> prajñām</span>–the wisdom, intelligence;<span class="e2"> asya</span>–of that person bereft of self-control. [67]
67 As a boat on the ocean is thrown off course by an unfavourable wind, similarly, the wisdom of a person lacking self-control is carried away by even one of the roaming senses that the mind might follow.
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्व्वशः ।<br />इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥६८॥
tasmād yasya mahā-bāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ<br />indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā [68]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O subduer of the enemy;<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–therefore;<span class="e2"> yasya</span>–he whose;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi</span>–senses;<span class="e2"> nigṛhītāni</span>–are withdrawn;<span class="e2"> sarvaśaḥ</span>–fully;<span class="e2"> indriya-arthebhyaḥ</span>–from the sense objects;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–his;<span class="e2"> prajñā</span>–wisdom;<span class="e2"> pratiṣṭhitā</span>–is firmly established. [68]
68 Therefore, O subduer of the enemy, one whose senses are fully withdrawn from their objects is a person of firmly established wisdom.
या निशा सर्व्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्त्ति संयमी ।<br />यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥६९॥
yā niśā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti saṁyamī<br />yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ [69]
<span class="e2">sarva-bhūtānām yā niśā</span>–That which is night for all living beings (who, immersed in ignorance, remain asleep to spiritual knowledge);<span class="e2"> tasyām</span>–in that night;<span class="e2"> saṁyamī</span>–the self-disciplined person;<span class="e2"> jāgarti</span>–remains awake (joyful in his spiritual intelligence).<span class="e2"> yasyām</span>–That (mundane intelligence) in which;<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–all living beings;<span class="e2"> jāgrati</span>–remain awake (experience the pleasures and pains, sorrows and delusions of worldly life);<span class="e2"> sā</span>–such (mundane intelligence) is;<span class="e2"> niśā</span>–night;<span class="e2"> muneḥ</span>–for the sage;<span class="e2"> paśyataḥ</span>–who sees (the futility of mundane endeavours and remains indifferent to the dualities). [69]
69 That which is day for the self-controlled sage is night for all beings, and that which is day for all beings is night for the sage who sees. (The living beings absorbed in mundane life are asleep to the spiritual joy of the realised soul, who remains indifferent to their quest for the pleasures of the senses, devoid of spiritual joy.)
आपूर्य्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं<br />समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।<br />तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्व्वे<br />स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥७०॥
āpūryamāṇam achala-pratiṣṭhaṁ<br />samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat<br />tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśanti sarve<br />sa śāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī [70]
<span class="e2">yadvat</span>–As;<span class="e2"> āpaḥ</span>–water;<span class="e2"> praviśanti</span>–enters;<span class="e2"> samudram</span>–the ocean;<span class="e2"> āpūryamāṇam</span>–which is always full;<span class="e2"> achala-pratiṣṭham</span>–it remains steady, its water never crossing the shore;<span class="e2"> tadvat</span>–similar is;<span class="e2"> yam</span>–that sage who;<span class="e2"> sarve kāmāḥ</span>–all desires;<span class="e2"> praviśanti</span>–enter to be enjoyed (for they cannot disturb his mind).<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–He alone;<span class="e2"> āpnoti</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> śāntim</span>–peace; (<span class="e2">tu</span>)–but;<span class="e2"> kāma-kāmī</span>–a person who nurtures desires; na (<span class="e2">tad āpnoti</span>)–cannot achieve that. [70]
70 As the ocean remains full and unchanged though many rivers and streams enter into it, the person of firmly established wisdom attains peace despite all desires entering him. But a person who nurtures desires cannot know peace.
विहाय कामान्यः सर्व्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।<br />निर्म्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥७१॥
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṁś charati niḥspṛhaḥ<br />nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigachchhati [71]
<span class="e2">yaḥ pumān</span>–That person who;<span class="e2"> vihāya</span>–giving up;<span class="e2"> sarvān kāmān</span>–all desires;<span class="e2"> charati</span>–moves through the world;<span class="e2"> nispṛhaḥ</span>–free from hankering;<span class="e2"> nirahaṅkāraḥ nirmamaḥ</span>–free from the false ego of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ in relation to the body and its attachments (having a divine relationship with the Supreme);<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–he;<span class="e2"> adhigachchhati</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> śāntim</span>–peace. [71]
71 Only a person who lives his life abandoning all desires, hankering, ego and possessiveness, can know real peace.
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।<br />स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्व्वाणमृच्छति ॥७२॥
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati<br />sthitvāsyām anta-kāle ’pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛchchhati [72]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> eṣā brahmī sthitiḥ</span>–this is the state of realising Brahma, the Absolute.<span class="e2"> enām prāpya</span>–Having reached this; (<span class="e2">naraḥ</span>)–a person;<span class="e2"> na vimuhyati</span>–is freed from the delusion of mundane existence.<span class="e2"> ṛchchhati</span>–He attains;<span class="e2"> brahma-nirvāṇam</span>–liberation from matter and entrance into the divine plane;<span class="e2"> sthitvā</span>–being situated;<span class="e2"> asyām</span>–in this state;<span class="e2"> anta-kāle api</span>–even at the time of death. [72]
72 O Pārtha, this is realisation of the Absolute, attaining which a person is freed from the delusion of mundane existence. Even at the time of death, only a momentary attainment of this state leads one to the divine abode.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे साङ्ख्य योगो नाम द्वितोयोऽध्यायः ॥२॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma-<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde<br />sāṅkhya-yogo nāma dvitīyo ’dhyāyaḥ [2]
End of Chapter Two<br />The Constitution Of The Soul<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

तृतीयोऽध्यायः
Chapter Three
Karma-yoga <br />The Path of Action
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्म्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्द्दन ।<br />तत्किं कर्म्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥१॥
arjuna uvācha
jyāyasī chet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana<br />tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśava [1]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> janārdana</span>–O Janārdan; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> keśava</span>–O Keśava;<span class="e2"> chet</span>–if;<span class="e2"> te matā</span>–it is Your opinion that;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–wisdom;<span class="e2"> jyāyasī</span>–is superior;<span class="e2"> karmaṇaḥ</span>–to action;<span class="e2"> tat kim</span>–why, then;<span class="e2"> niyojayasi mām</span>–do You urge me to engage;<span class="e2"> ghore karmaṇi</span>–in the terrible action of warfare? [1]
1 Arjuna said: O Janārdan, O Keśava, if You consider wisdom superior to action, why, then, do you urge me to engage in the violence of warfare?
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे ।<br />तदेकं वद निश्चत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥२॥
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṁ mohayasīva me<br />tad ekaṁ vada niśchitya yena śreyo ’ham āpnuyām [2]
<span class="e2">mohayasi iva</span>–You are bewildering;<span class="e2"> me</span>–my;<span class="e2"> buddhim</span>–intelligence;<span class="e2"> vākyena</span>–by Your words;<span class="e2"> vyāmiśreṇa iva</span>–by their ambiguous meanings, sometimes praising action and sometimes praising wisdom.<span class="e2"> tat</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> niśchitya</span>–ascertaining;<span class="e2"> ekam</span>–one;<span class="e2"> vada</span>–please say;<span class="e2"> yena</span>–that by which;<span class="e2"> aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> āpnuyām</span>–can obtain;<span class="e2"> śreyaḥ</span>–the highest benefit. [2]
2 I am confused by Your words. They appear to be ambiguous, sometimes supporting action and sometimes supporting wisdom. So please tell me, which is the most beneficial path for me to take?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ ।<br />ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्म्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥३॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
loke ’smin dvi-vidhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha<br />jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānāṁ karma-yogena yoginām [3]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> anagha</span>–O sinless Arjuna;<span class="e2"> asmin loke</span>–in this world;<span class="e2"> dvi-vidhā niṣṭhā</span>–two ways;<span class="e2"> proktā</span>–have been spoken of;<span class="e2"> mayā</span>–by Me;<span class="e2"> purā</span>–in the previous chapter: (<span class="e2">niṣṭhā sthāpitā</span>)–the established practice;<span class="e2"> sāṅkhyānām</span>–of the realised;<span class="e2"> jñāna-yogena</span>–by the yoga of knowledge; (<span class="e2">niṣṭhā sthāpitā</span>)–and the established practice;<span class="e2"> yoginām</span>–of those engaged in action in the world;<span class="e2"> karma-yogena</span>–by the yoga of selfless action. [3]
3 The Supreme Lord replied: O sinless one, I have described the two paths to be found in this world—the yoga of wisdom practised by the realised and the yoga of selfless action practised by those active in the world. (Both paths touch the beginnings of devotional practice since the ladder to the plane of devotion is one, while the practice is twofold according to the stage attained.)
न कर्म्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते ।<br />न च सन्न्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥४॥
na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṁ puruṣo ’śnute<br />na cha sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigachchhati [4]
<span class="e2">puruṣaḥ</span>–A person;<span class="e2"> na aśnute</span>–cannot attain;<span class="e2"> naiṣkarmyam</span>–to the state of spiritual consciousness beyond material activity;<span class="e2"> anārambhāt</span>–by refraining from;<span class="e2"> karmaṇām</span>–(scripturally prescribed) actions;<span class="e2"> na samadhigachchhati</span>–and he cannot attain;<span class="e2"> siddhim</span>–fulfillment, perfection;<span class="e2"> sannyasanāt eva cha</span>–by renunciation alone. [4]
4 One cannot attain freedom from action by refraining from action. Nor can one attain fulfillment by renunciation alone.
न हि कश्चत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्म्मकृत् ।<br />कार्य्यते ह्यवशः कर्म्म सर्व्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥५॥
na hi kaśchit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarmakṛt<br />kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jair guṇaiḥ [5]
<span class="e2">kaśchit</span>–One;<span class="e2"> na hi tiṣṭhati</span>–cannot remain;<span class="e2"> jātu</span>–at any time;<span class="e2"> akarma-kṛt</span>–without engaging in activity;<span class="e2"> kṣaṇam api</span>–even for a moment.<span class="e2"> sarvaḥ hi</span>–Indeed, all living beings;<span class="e2"> avaśaḥ</span>–are helplessly;<span class="e2"> karma kāryate</span>–engaged in activity;<span class="e2"> prakṛti-jaiḥ guṇaiḥ</span>–by the modes or qualities born of material nature. [5]
5 No one can refrain from activity for even a moment. Everyone is impelled to act by the modes of material nature. (Thus the person of impure consciousness should not disregard scripturally prescribed purificatory works.)
कर्म्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।<br />इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥६॥
karmendriyāṇi saṁyamya ya āste manasā smaran<br />indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyāchāraḥ sa uchyate [6]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–That person who;<span class="e2"> saṁyamya</span>–having controlled;<span class="e2"> karma-indriyāṇi</span>–the senses of action—the hands, legs, etc. (see 13.6);<span class="e2"> smaran āste</span>–remembers, dwells on;<span class="e2"> indriya-arthān</span>–the sense objects;<span class="e2"> manasā</span>–within his mind;<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–that person;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is known as;<span class="e2"> vimūḍha-ātmā</span>–a fool;<span class="e2"> mithyā-āchāraḥ</span>–and a hypocrite. [6]
6 One who externally restrains his hands, legs, and other senses of action, but whose mind dwells on sense objects, is a fool. Know him to be a hypocrite.
यस्त्वन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />कर्म्मेन्द्रियैः कर्म्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥७॥
yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate ’rjuna<br />karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate [7]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> arjuna</span>–O Dhanañjaya;<span class="e2"> yaḥ tu</span>–but he, who;<span class="e2"> niyamya</span>–having stabilised;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi</span>–the senses;<span class="e2"> manasā</span>–by the mind;<span class="e2"> ārabhate</span>–engages in;<span class="e2"> karma-yogam</span>–the yoga of action as directed by the scriptures;<span class="e2"> karma-indriyaiḥ</span>–utilising the senses of action;<span class="e2"> asaktaḥ</span>–without any desire for the results;<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–that person;<span class="e2"> viśiṣyate</span>–is superior to such a hypocrite. [7]
7 O Arjuna, superior is one who (though married) has stabilised his senses by the mind and engaged in the yoga of selfless action.
नियतं कुरु कर्म्म त्वं कर्म्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्म्मणः ।<br />शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्म्मणः ॥८॥
niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ<br />śarīra-yātrāpi cha te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ [8]
<span class="e2">tvam</span>–You;<span class="e2"> kuru</span>–perform;<span class="e2"> niyatam karma</span>–prescribed duties;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–since;<span class="e2"> karma</span>–the performance of duty;<span class="e2"> jyāyaḥ</span>–is superior;<span class="e2"> akarmaṇaḥ</span>–to renouncing duty.<span class="e2"> akarmaṇaḥ cha</span>–By becoming inactive;<span class="e2"> te śarīra yātrā api</span>–even your bodily sustenance;<span class="e2"> na prasiddhyet</span>–will not be accomplished. [8]
8 Perform your prescribed duties, since to be active is better than idleness. Inactive persons cannot even maintain their existence. (By giving up fruitive action and performing your obligatory duties, your heart will be purified. Surpassing the plane of renunciation, you will attain pure devotion, transcendental to the mundane plane.)
यज्ञार्थात्कर्म्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्म्मबन्धनः ।<br />तदर्थं कर्म्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥९॥
yajñārthāt karmaṇo ’nyatra loko ’yaṁ karma-bandhanaḥ<br />tad-arthaṁ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samāchara [9]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> ayam lokaḥ</span>–all the living beings of this world; <span class="e2">karma-bandhanaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–come into bondage by their action;<span class="e2"> karmaṇaḥ anyatra</span>–other than action;<span class="e2"> yajña-arthāt</span>–as selfless duty offered to Lord Viṣṇu. (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–Therefore; <span class="e2">mukta-saṅgaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being free from attachment;<span class="e2"> karma samāchara</span>–be fully active;<span class="e2"> tat-artham</span>–for the purpose of such sacrifice, for Him. [9]
9 Selfless duty performed as an offering to the Supreme Lord is called yajña, or sacrifice. O Arjuna, all action performed for any other purpose is the cause of bondage in this world of repeated birth and death. Therefore, remaining unattached to the fruits of action, perform all your duties in the spirit of such sacrifice. (Such selfless action is the way to begin devotional practice, gradually realise the presence of the Lord, and ultimately attain pure devotion transcendental to the modes of material nature [nirguṇa bhakti]).
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः ।<br />अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥१०॥
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovācha prajāpatiḥ<br />anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo ’stv iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk [10]
<span class="e2">purā</span>–At the universal manifestation;<span class="e2"> sṛṣṭvā</span>–after manifesting;<span class="e2"> saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ</span>–the progeny of the world, with sacrifices for Lord Viṣṇu;<span class="e2"> prajāpatiḥ</span>–Lord Brahmā;<span class="e2"> uvācha</span>–said:<span class="e2"> prasaviṣyadhvam</span>–“May your prosperity flourish;<span class="e2"> anena</span>–by this religious practice.<span class="e2"> eṣaḥ astu</span>–May this sacrifice be;<span class="e2"> vaḥ</span>–your;<span class="e2"> iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk</span>–bestower of desired objects.” [10]
10 In the beginning, Lord Brahmā manifested the progeny of the world, along with sacrifices. He instructed them thus: “Take shelter of this religious principle of sacrifice; prosper and flourish. May such sacrifice be the bestower of the things you desire.”
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः ।<br />परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥११॥
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ<br />parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha [11]
<span class="e2">anena</span>–“By this yajña; (<span class="e2">yūjam</span>)–you all;<span class="e2"> bhāvayata</span>–propitiate;<span class="e2"> devān</span>–the demigods; <span class="e2">te devāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">api</span>)–and the demigods being thus pleased;<span class="e2"> bhāvayantu vaḥ</span>–may bestow upon you your desired fruits. (<span class="e2">evam</span>)–In this way;<span class="e2"> parasparam</span>–mutually;<span class="e2"> bhāvayantaḥ</span>–nourished;<span class="e2"> avāpsyatha</span>–you will obtain;<span class="e2"> param śreyaḥ</span>–the ultimate auspiciousness.” [11]
11 “Propitiate the gods by sacrifices, and may they satisfy you by bestowing your desired fruits. In this way, through mutual nourishment, you will be the gainers of great auspiciousness.”
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः ।<br />तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥१२॥
iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ<br />tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ [12]
<span class="e2">devāḥ</span>–The demigods (as limbs of My universal form); <span class="e2">yajña-bhāvitāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–being pleased by sacrifices;<span class="e2"> dāsyante</span>–will bestow;<span class="e2"> vaḥ</span>–upon you;<span class="e2"> iṣṭān bhogān</span>–desired enjoyable objects.<span class="e2"> hi</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> yaḥ</span>–he who;<span class="e2"> bhuṅkte</span>–enjoys;<span class="e2"> taiḥ dattān</span>–food provided by the demigods; (<span class="e2">vṛṣṭyādi dvāreṇa</span>)–via the rain, etc.;<span class="e2"> apradāya</span>–without making any offerings (of that food); (<span class="e2">pañcha-yajña-ādhibhiḥ</span>)–by means of the five kinds of sacrifices, etc.;<span class="e2"> ebhyaḥ</span>–to those demigods, who are all under My shelter;<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–that person;<span class="e2"> stenaḥ eva</span>–is but a thief. [12]
12 Propitiated by sacrifices, the gods (My worldly representatives) will bestow upon you all your desired enjoyable things. But one who enjoys what is given by the gods without offering it to them, is a thief.
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्व्वकिल्बिषैः ।<br />भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥१३॥
yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ santo muchyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ<br />bhuñjate te tv aghaṁ pāpā ye pachanty ātma-kāraṇāt [13]
<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>–Virtuous persons;<span class="e2"> yajña-śiṣṭa-aśinaḥ</span>–who partake of the remnants of sacrifice to the demigods (universal administrators subordinate to the Lord);<span class="e2"> muchyante</span>–are liberated;<span class="e2"> sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ</span>–from all sin (pañcha-sūnā, five types of sin due to five kinds of violence to other living beings).<span class="e2"> ye tu</span>–But those who;<span class="e2"> pachanti</span>–cook;<span class="e2"> ātma-kāraṇāt</span>–for their own pleasure;<span class="e2"> te</span>–those;<span class="e2"> pāpāḥ</span>–sinful persons;<span class="e2"> bhuñjate</span>–eat; (<span class="e2">eva</span>)–only;<span class="e2"> agham</span>–sin. [13]
13 By accepting sacrificial remnants of the universal gods*, virtuous persons are liberated from all sins arising from violence towards other living entities. But those who prepare food for their own pleasure partake only of sin.
* The remnants referred to here are not the same as the Kṛṣṇa-prasād (food that has been offered to the Supreme Lord by His devotees). See 9.20–26.
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्ज्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ।<br />यज्ञाद्भवति पर्ज्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्म्मसमुद्भवः ॥१४॥
annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-sambhavaḥ<br />yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ [14]
<span class="e2">annāt</span>–From food (transformed into semen and blood);<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–(the physical bodies of) all living entities;<span class="e2"> bhavanti</span>–are manifest.<span class="e2"> anna-sambhavaḥ</span>–Food is manifest;<span class="e2"> parjanyāt</span>–due to rainfall.<span class="e2"> parjanyaḥ</span>–Rainfall;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–occurs;<span class="e2"> yajñāt</span>–due to yajña, sacrifice.<span class="e2"> yajñaḥ</span>–Sacrifice;<span class="e2"> karma-samudbhavaḥ</span>–is born of action. [14]
14 The living beings’ bodies are manifest from food, food is manifest due to rain, rainfall ensues from the performance of sacrifice, and action is the cause of sacrifice.
कर्म्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।<br />तस्मात्सर्व्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥१५॥
karma brahmodbhavaṁ viddhi brahmākṣara-samudbhavam<br />tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam [15]
