<span class="e2">viddhi</span>–Know that;<span class="e2"> karma</span>–action;<span class="e2"> brahma-udbhavam</span>–is born of the Vedas.<span class="e2"> brahma</span>–The Vedas;<span class="e2"> akṣara-samudbhavam</span>–are born of Akṣara, the Imperishable.<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> sarva-gatam</span>–the all-pervading;<span class="e2"> brahma</span>–Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> nityam pratiṣthitam</span>–is always situated;<span class="e2"> yajñe</span>–within sacrifice. [15]
15 Action is prescribed in the Vedas, and the Vedas originate in Akṣara, the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading, imperishable Lord is ever present within the acts of sacrifice offered to Him.
एवं प्रवर्त्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्त्तयतीह यः ।<br />अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥१६॥
evaṁ pravartitaṁ chakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ<br />aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati [16]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yaḥ</span>–one who;<span class="e2"> iha</span>–in this life;<span class="e2"> na anuvartayati</span>–does not follow;<span class="e2"> chakram</span>–the cycle;<span class="e2"> evam pravartitam</span>–thus established in the nature of cause and effect; (<span class="e2">parama-puruṣeṇa</span>)–by the Supreme Personality;<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–he;<span class="e2"> jīvati</span>–lives;<span class="e2"> agha-āyuḥ</span>–a life of sin;<span class="e2"> indriya-ārāmaḥ</span>–enjoying the senses;<span class="e2"> mogham</span>–in vain. [16]
16 O Arjuna, one who does not respect this natural causal cycle leads a life of sin, enjoying the senses in vain.
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः ।<br />आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्य्यं न विद्यते ॥१७॥
yas tv ātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛptaś cha mānavaḥ<br />ātmany eva cha santuṣṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate [17]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But;<span class="e2"> yah mānavaḥ</span>–that man who;<span class="e2"> syāt</span>–is;<span class="e2"> ātma-ratiḥ</span>–internally ecstatic;<span class="e2"> ātma-tṛptaḥ eva cha</span>–internally satiated;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> santuṣṭaḥ</span>–fully satisfied;<span class="e2"> ātmani eva</span>–in the self alone;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–his;<span class="e2"> kāryam</span>–duties;<span class="e2"> na vidyate</span>–are none. [17]
17 Yet there is no duty to fulfill for the realised person who delights within the self, being fully satisfied within. (His only worldly action or karma is as required for his subsistence.)
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन ।<br />न चास्य सर्व्वभूतेषु कश्चदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥१८॥
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaśchana<br />na chāsya sarva-bhūteṣu kaśchid artha-vyapāśrayaḥ [18]
<span class="e2">iha</span>–In this world;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–for that ātmārāma, one who delights in the self;<span class="e2"> arthaḥ na eva</span>–no piety is gained;<span class="e2"> kṛtena</span>–by action; <span class="e2">kaśchana </span>(<span class="e2">anārthaḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> na</span>–nor is any sin committed;<span class="e2"> akṛtena</span>–by inaction;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūteṣu cha</span>–and of all beings; <span class="e2">kaśchit na </span>(<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–no one is;<span class="e2"> asya artha-vyapāśrayaḥ</span>–depended on by him for any purpose. [18]
18 In the world, he neither gains by action, nor loses by inaction. He does not depend on any other being (from Lord Brahmā down to the simplest life-form) for any purpose.
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्य्यं कर्म्म समाचर ।<br />असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥१९॥
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samāchara<br />asakto hy ācharan karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ [19]
<span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore; <span class="e2">asaktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being unattached to the fruits of your actions;<span class="e2"> satatam</span>–always;<span class="e2"> samāchara</span>–perfectly perform;<span class="e2"> kāryam karma</span>–prescribed duties;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–since;<span class="e2"> karma ācharan</span>–by performing these duties;<span class="e2"> asaktaḥ</span>–without attachment;<span class="e2"> pūruṣaḥ</span>–a person;<span class="e2"> āpnoti</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> param</span>–liberation, param-bhakti—pure devotion. [19]
19 So perform your prescribed duties without attachment. By selflessly executing one’s duties a person attains liberation. (True liberation is the state of pure devotion, attained in the maturity of selfless action.)
कर्म्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः ।<br />लोकसङ्ग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्यन्कर्त्तुमर्हसि ॥२०॥
karmaṇaiva hi saṁsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ<br />loka-saṅgraham evāpi sampaśyan kartum arhasi [20]
<span class="e2">janaka-ādayaḥ</span>–The learned, such as King Janaka and others;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> āsthitāḥ</span>–obtained;<span class="e2"> saṁsiddhim</span>–success—devotion;<span class="e2"> karmaṇā eva</span>–by fulfilling their duties.<span class="e2"> arhasi</span>–Be prepared;<span class="e2"> kartum</span>–to do; (<span class="e2">karma</span>)–work;<span class="e2"> api</span>–also;<span class="e2"> loka-saṅgraham sampaśyan eva</span>–in the consideration of the welfare of the people. [20]
20 King Janaka and other learned personalities succeeded in attaining devotion through the execution of their prescribed duties. So it is fitting that you fulfill your duty in consideration of the welfare of the people.
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।<br />स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्त्तते ॥२१॥
yad yad ācharati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ<br />sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate [21]
<span class="e2">yat yat</span>–However;<span class="e2"> śreṣṭaḥ</span>–the great personality;<span class="e2"> ācharati</span>–conducts himself;<span class="e2"> itaraḥ janaḥ</span>–other lesser men; (<span class="e2">ācharati</span>)–will conduct themselves;<span class="e2"> tat tat eva</span>–accordingly.<span class="e2"> yat</span>–Whatever;<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–the great personality;<span class="e2"> kurute</span>–accepts;<span class="e2"> pramāṇam</span>–as the standard;<span class="e2"> lokaḥ</span>–ordinary men;<span class="e2"> tat anuvartate</span>–follow that. [21]
21 The masses follow the ways of great men, following the standards they set.
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्त्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन ।<br />नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त्त एव च कर्म्मणि ॥२२॥
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣu lokeṣu kiñchana<br />nānavāptam avāptavyaṁ varta eva cha karmaṇi [22]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> triṣu lokeṣu</span>–in the three worlds;<span class="e2"> na asti</span>–there is not;<span class="e2"> kiñchana</span>–any;<span class="e2"> kartavyam</span>–duty to be done;<span class="e2"> me</span>–for Me; (<span class="e2">yataḥ</span>)–since; <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">asti kiñchana</span>)–there is nothing;<span class="e2"> anavāptam</span>–unobtained;<span class="e2"> avāptavyam</span>–or to be obtained; (<span class="e2">mama</span>)–for Me; (<span class="e2">tathāpi</span>)–and yet;<span class="e2"> varte eva cha</span>–I am engaged;<span class="e2"> karmaṇi</span>–in activity. [22]
22 O Arjuna, I have no duty in the three worlds. I lack nothing, and there is nothing to be attained by Me; and yet, I, Myself, am active.
यदि ह्यहं न वर्त्तेयं जातु कर्म्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।<br />मम वर्त्त्मानुवर्त्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्व्वशः ॥२३॥
yadi hy ahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ<br />mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ [23]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yadi jātu</span>–if ever;<span class="e2"> aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> na varteyam</span>–do not engage;<span class="e2"> atandritaḥ</span>–attentively;<span class="e2"> karmaṇi</span>–in duties; (<span class="e2">tarhi</span>)–then;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> manuṣyāḥ</span>–all men;<span class="e2"> anuvartante</span>–will follow;<span class="e2"> mama</span>–My;<span class="e2"> vartma</span>–path;<span class="e2"> sarvaśaḥ</span>–in all respects. [23]
23 O Arjuna, if ever I do not engage attentively in duties, then all men, following My example, will give up their duties.
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्य्यां कर्म्म चेदहम् ।<br />सङ्करस्य च कर्त्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥२४॥
utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ched aham<br />saṅkarasya cha kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ [24]
<span class="e2">chet</span>–If;<span class="e2"> aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> na kuryān</span>–do not engage in;<span class="e2"> karma</span>–duty; (<span class="e2">tarhi</span>)–then;<span class="e2"> ime lokāḥ</span>–the inhabitants of these worlds;<span class="e2"> utsīdeyuḥ</span>–will be ruined; (<span class="e2">karma tyaktvā</span>)–by renouncing their duty;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> syām</span>–will be;<span class="e2"> kartā</span>–the maker;<span class="e2"> saṅkarasya</span>–of varṇa-saṅkara, or adulterated progeny; (<span class="e2">evam aham eva</span>)–and in this way, I alone;<span class="e2"> upahanyām</span>–will cause the downfall;<span class="e2"> imāḥ prajāḥ</span>–of these people. [24]
24 If I do not engage in duty, the people of these worlds will renounce their duties and fall to ruination. Thus I will be responsible for their downfall, caused by adulterated progeny.
सक्ताः कर्म्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्व्वन्ति भारत ।<br />कुर्य्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसङ्ग्रहम् ॥२५॥
saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṁso yathā kurvanti bhārata<br />kuryād vidvāṁs tathāsaktaś chikīrṣur loka-saṅgraham [25]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yathā</span>–just as;<span class="e2"> avidvāṁsaḥ</span>–the ignorant;<span class="e2"> karmaṇi saktāḥ</span>–attached to work;<span class="e2"> kurvanti</span>–perform; (<span class="e2">karmaṇi</span>)–work;<span class="e2"> tathā</span>–similarly;<span class="e2"> vidvān</span>–the wise; <span class="e2">asaktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being unattached;<span class="e2"> kuryāt</span>–should work;<span class="e2"> chikīrṣuḥ</span>–wishing;<span class="e2"> loka-saṅgraham</span>–to guide the people. [25]
25 O Arjuna, as ignorant persons work with attachment, the wise, too, must work, but without attachment, in order to guide the general people who exist in the plane of worldly action. (They differ not in their work but in their attitudes of attachment and detachment.)
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्म्मसङ्गिनाम् ।<br />योजयेत्सर्व्वकर्म्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥२६॥
na buddhi-bhedaṁ janayed ajñānāṁ karma-saṅginām<br />yojayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācharan [26]
<span class="e2">vidvān</span>–The learned, the teacher of jñāna-yoga;<span class="e2"> na janayet</span>–must not create;<span class="e2"> ajñānām</span>–among ignorant men;<span class="e2"> karma-saṅginām</span>–who are attached to work;<span class="e2"> buddhi-bhedam</span>–the confusion to neglect duties and cultivate knowledge. (<span class="e2">api tu</span>)–Rather; <span class="e2">yuktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–remaining unattached;<span class="e2"> samācharan</span>–fully executing;<span class="e2"> sarva-karmāṇi</span>–all duties; (<span class="e2">ajñān</span>)<span class="e2"> yojayet</span>–they should encourage the ignorant in their duties. [26]
26 The scripturally learned teacher should not create confusion in the minds of ignorant, attached men by apparently advocating the neglect of duty for the cultivation of knowledge. Rather, he should set the example of selflessness in fulfilling duties, thus encouraging the ignorant in the performance of their prescribed duties.
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्म्माणि सर्व्वशः ।<br />अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्त्ताहमिति मन्यते ॥२७॥
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ<br />ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate [27]
<span class="e2">karmāṇi</span>–Actions;<span class="e2"> kriyamāṇāni</span>–are effected;<span class="e2"> sarvaśaḥ</span>–in all ways;<span class="e2"> guṇaiḥ</span>–(by the senses, impelled) by the modes;<span class="e2"> prakṛteḥ</span>–of material nature; (<span class="e2">tu</span>)–but;<span class="e2"> ahaṅkāra-vimūḍha-ātmā</span>–one deluded by bodily ego;<span class="e2"> manyate iti</span>–thinks thus;<span class="e2"> aham kartā</span>–“I am the doer.” [27]
27 All actions in the world are in every respect effected by the modes of material nature (which impel the senses). But a man deluded by bodily identification thinks, “I alone am accomplishing this work.”
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्म्मविभागयोः ।<br />गुणा गुणेषु वर्त्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥२८॥
tattvavit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ<br />guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate [28]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O Arjuna, best of heroes;<span class="e2"> tattva-vit</span>–one who is in knowledge;<span class="e2"> guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ</span>–of the division of the modes of material nature (the three modes of goodness, passion, and ignorance), and action (the functional demigods, the senses, and the sense objects); (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–he;<span class="e2"> matvā</span>–considering;<span class="e2"> iti</span>–that;<span class="e2"> guṇāḥ</span>–the modes (in the form of the senses of perception—ear, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose, activated by the demigods);<span class="e2"> vartante</span>–are engaged;<span class="e2"> guṇeṣu</span>–within the modes (in the form of the sense objects of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell);<span class="e2"> na sajjate</span>–is not attached to them, not absorbed in them. [28]
28 However, O mighty-armed Arjuna, one who is in knowledge of the division of the modes of material nature and action, knows that the modes are engaging within the modes, and he is detached from them. (One who knows that the three modes activated by the demigods impel the engagement of the senses with their objects, knows himself to be independent of these elements, therefore he does not consider himself a doer.)
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्म्मसु ।<br />तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥२९॥
prakṛter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu<br />tān akṛtsna-vido mandān kṛtsna-vin na vichālayet [29]
<span class="e2">prakṛteḥ-guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ</span>–Persons bewildered by the modes;<span class="e2"> sajjante</span>–are absorbed;<span class="e2"> guṇa-karmasu</span>–in the functions of the modes (the engagement of the senses with their objects).<span class="e2"> kṛtsna-vit</span>–Those possessing knowledge;<span class="e2"> na vichālayet</span>–should not agitate (by trying to induce them to accept knowledge of self and non-self);<span class="e2"> tān</span>–those;<span class="e2"> akṛtsna-vidaḥ</span>–ignorant;<span class="e2"> mandān</span>–unfortunate persons; (<span class="e2">kintu guṇāveśa-nivartakaṁ niṣkāma karmaiva kārayet</span>)–but should rather engage them in selfless action which frees them from absorption in the modes of nature. [29]
29 Persons bewildered by the modes of nature are absorbed in the functions of the modes (the engagement of the senses with their objects). Enlightened persons should not agitate such ignorant, unfortunate persons by trying to convince them of higher philosophical truths. (Rather, they should advise the conditioned souls to practise selfless action, which liberates them from absorption in the modes.)
मयि सर्व्वाणि कर्म्माणि सन्न्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा ।<br />निराशीर्निर्म्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥३०॥
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi sannyasyādhyātma-chetasā<br />nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ [30]
<span class="e2">sannyasya</span>–Completely surrendering;<span class="e2"> sarvāṇī karmāṇi</span>–all activities;<span class="e2"> mayi</span>–unto Me;<span class="e2"> adhyātma-chetasā</span>–always conscious of the Spiritual Being;<span class="e2"> bhūtvā</span>–being;<span class="e2"> nirāśīḥ</span>–without fruitive desire;<span class="e2"> nirmamaḥ</span>–without possessiveness; <span class="e2">vigata-jvaraḥ </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and without anguish;<span class="e2"> yudhyasva</span>–fight. [30]
30 Surrender all your activities to Me with this understanding: “All my actions are under the control of the indwelling Lord.” In such consciousness, free from possessiveness and anguish, take recourse to battle (as your natural duty).
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः ।<br />श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्म्मभिः ॥३१॥
ye me matam idaṁ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ<br />śraddhāvanto ’nasūyanto muchyante te ’pi karmabhiḥ [31]
<span class="e2">ye mānavāḥ</span>–Those men who;<span class="e2"> śraddhāvantaḥ</span>–faithfully;<span class="e2"> anasūyantaḥ</span>–and unbegrudgingly;<span class="e2"> nityam</span>–always;<span class="e2"> anutiṣṭhanti</span>–execute;<span class="e2"> idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> me matam</span>–teaching of Mine, of selfless action;<span class="e2"> te api</span>–they too;<span class="e2"> muchyante</span>–are liberated;<span class="e2"> karmabhiḥ</span>–from the bondage of karma, or action and reaction in the mundane plane. [31]
31 Faithful, unbegrudging men who always practise My teaching, this yoga of selfless action, are liberated from the bondage of action, even though they engage in action.
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।<br />सर्व्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥३२॥
ye tv etad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam<br />sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāṁs tān viddhi naṣṭān achetasaḥ [32]
<span class="e2">ye tu</span>–But those who;<span class="e2"> abhyasūyantaḥ</span>–out of resentment;<span class="e2"> na anutiṣṭhanti</span>–do not follow;<span class="e2"> etat me matam</span>–that teaching of Mine;<span class="e2"> tān viddhi</span>–know them to be;<span class="e2"> sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhān</span>–deprived of all knowledge;<span class="e2"> naṣṭān</span>–completely deviated from the goal of human life;<span class="e2"> achetasaḥ</span>–and bereft of good intelligence. [32]
32 But the arrogant who resent My teaching are bereft of all knowledge. Know them to be lost in ignorance.
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि ।<br />प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥३३॥
sadṛśaṁ cheṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api<br />prakṛtiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣyati [33]
<span class="e2">jñānavān api</span>–Even a knowledgable person;<span class="e2"> cheṣṭate</span>–acts;<span class="e2"> sadṛśam</span>–according to;<span class="e2"> svasyāḥ prakṛteḥ</span>–his nature.<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–Living beings;<span class="e2"> prakṛtim yānti</span>–follow their natures.<span class="e2"> kim kariṣyati</span>–What will be the use of;<span class="e2"> nigrahaḥ</span>–repression; (<span class="e2">teṣām</span>)–of them? [33]
33 For even a knowledgable person tends to act according to his nature (mundane inclinations). The living beings’ endeavours are dictated by their natures. What, then, can repression accomplish?
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ ।<br />तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥३४॥
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāga-dveṣau vyavasthitau<br />tayor na vaśam āgachchhet tau hy asya paripanthinau [34]
<span class="e2">rāga-dveṣau</span>–Attraction and aversion;<span class="e2"> indriyasya</span>–of all the senses;<span class="e2"> vyavasthitau</span>–exist;<span class="e2"> indriyasya-arthe</span>–for their objects. (<span class="e2">tathāpi</span>)–However;<span class="e2"> vaśam na āgachchhet</span>–One must not be controlled;<span class="e2"> tayoḥ</span>–by such attraction and aversion;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–since;<span class="e2"> tau pari-panthinau</span>–they are an obstacle;<span class="e2"> asya</span>–to the spiritual practitioner. [34]
34 Although the senses are attracted to and repelled by the sense objects, one must not be controlled by these urges, for they are the greatest enemy of the candidate for self-realisation.
श्रेयान्स्वधर्म्मो विगुणः परधर्म्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।<br />स्वधर्म्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्म्मो भयावहः ॥३५॥
śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt<br />svadharme nidhanaṁ śreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ [35]
<span class="e2">svadharmaḥ</span>–One’s own function;<span class="e2"> viguṇaḥ</span>–tinged with faults;<span class="e2"> śreyān</span>–is better;<span class="e2"> para-dharmāt</span>–than another’s function;<span class="e2"> su-anuṣṭhitāt</span>–done well.<span class="e2"> nidhanam</span>–Even death;<span class="e2"> svadharme</span>–on one’s own path of duty (according to one’s appropriate position in the varṇāśram or God-centred socio-religious system);<span class="e2"> śreyaḥ</span>–is better.<span class="e2"> para-dharmaḥ</span>–Another’s path of duty;<span class="e2"> bhaya-āvahaḥ</span>–is dangerous. [35]
35 Even if it is imperfect, it is better to do one’s duty according to one’s own nature, than to do another’s well. Even death in the discharge of one’s own duty is better, for to perform another’s is dangerous.
Commentary
The eternal, superexcellent, natural function (dharma) of the soul is pure devotion to Adhokṣaja, the transcendental Lord. Therefore, even if this function is somewhat imperfectly attempted by one with external malpractices, such an attempt will be superior to the ‘good’ practices within the material modes of nature and worldly chain of actions and habits foreign to the soul’s nature. Even if death occurs during the cultivation of such pure devotion in proper saintly association, it is the bestower of the ultimate good; but in the name of good practices to ignorantly follow ‘another’s path’—anything other than devotion to the Lord (dvitīyābhiniveś)—is <span class="e3">bhayāvaḥ</span>, endangering to the spiritual progress of the soul.*
* भयं द्वितीयाभिनिवेशतः स्याद्<br />ईशादपेतस्य विपर्य्ययोऽस्मृतिः ।<br />तन्माययातो बुध आभजेत्तं<br />भक्त्यैकयेशं गुरुदेवतात्मा ॥
bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād<br />īśād apetasya viparyayo ’smṛtiḥ<br />tan māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ<br />bhaktyaikayeśaṁ guru-devatātmā
(SB: 11.2.37)
“A person of fine intelligence will serve with single-minded devotion his Lord who is his teacher and dearmost friend. But those who have turned away from the Lord adopt the illusory ego of considering the perishable body to be the self, forgetting their true identities. Their consciousness absorbed in ‘secondary pursuits’, i.e., mundane objectives, they are always fearful on account of the body and its attachments.”
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापञ्चरति पूरुषः ।<br />अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥३६॥
arjuna uvācha
atha kena prayukto ’yaṁ pāpañ charati pūruṣaḥ<br />anichchhann api vārṣṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ [36]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said:<span class="e2"> atha</span>–Now; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> vārṣṇeya</span>–O descendant of the Vṛṣṇi dynasty; <span class="e2">kena prayuktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being incited by what;<span class="e2"> ayam pūruṣaḥ charati</span>–does this living being commit;<span class="e2"> pāpam</span>–sinful activities;<span class="e2"> anichchhan api</span>–even unwillingly;<span class="e2"> niyojitaḥ iva</span>–as if engaged;<span class="e2"> balāt</span>–by force? [36]
36 Arjuna inquired: O descendant of the Vṛṣṇis, by what is the living being compelled to commit sinful activities, even unwillingly, as if by force?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।<br />महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥३७॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇa-samudbhavaḥ<br />mahāśano mahā-pāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam [37]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said:<span class="e2"> eṣaḥ kāmaḥ</span>–It is this desire to enjoy the mundane;<span class="e2"> eṣaḥ krodhaḥ</span>–transformed into anger.<span class="e2"> rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ</span>–It arises from the mode of passion, and from that desire, blind anger is born.<span class="e2"> viddhi enam</span>–Know such desire to be;<span class="e2"> mahā-aśanaḥ</span>–never satisfied;<span class="e2"> mahā-pāpmā</span>–greatly wrathful;<span class="e2"> vairiṇam</span>–and the worst enemy of the living being;<span class="e2"> iha</span>–in this world. [37]
37 The Supreme Lord replied: It is the desire to enjoy the mundane that induces a person to commit sin, and in different situations it produces anger. It is utterly insatiable, extremely malicious, and the worst enemy of the living being in this world.
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च ।<br />यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥३८॥
dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśo malena cha<br />yatholbenāvṛto garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛtam [38]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–As;<span class="e2"> vahniḥ</span>–fire;<span class="e2"> āvriyate</span>–is covered;<span class="e2"> dhūmena</span>–by smoke;<span class="e2"> yathā</span>–as;<span class="e2"> ādarśaḥ</span>–a mirror; (<span class="e2">āvriyate</span>)–is covered;<span class="e2"> malena</span>–by dust; (<span class="e2">yathā</span>)<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and as;<span class="e2"> garbhaḥ</span>–the embryo;<span class="e2"> āvṛtaḥ</span>–is covered;<span class="e2"> ulbena</span>–by the womb;<span class="e2"> tathā</span>–similarly;<span class="e2"> idam</span>–one’s consciousness;<span class="e2"> āvṛtam</span>–is covered;<span class="e2"> tena</span>–by that desire. [38]
38 As fire is thinly veiled by smoke, as a mirror is thickly covered with dust, and as the embryo remains completely enclosed within the womb, similarly, this desire covers the consciousness of the living being (in these three degrees of intensity, according to the modes of material nature—goodness, passion, and ignorance respectively).
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा ।<br />कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥३९॥
āvṛtaṁ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā<br />kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena cha [39]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna, son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> jñānam</span>–discriminatory knowledge;<span class="e2"> āvṛtam</span>–is covered;<span class="e2"> etena</span>–by this;<span class="e2"> nitya-vairiṇā</span>–perpetual enemy;<span class="e2"> jñāninaḥ</span>–of even knowledgable persons;<span class="e2"> kāma-rūpeṇa</span>–in the form of desire;<span class="e2"> duṣpūreṇa analena cha</span>–which is like insatiable fire. [39]
39 Knowledge is covered by desire, the constant enemy of the wise. It burns like an insatiable fire (never satisfied by offerings of butter).
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते ।<br />एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥४०॥
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam uchyate<br />etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam [40]
<span class="e2">uchyate</span>–It is said that;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi</span>–the senses;<span class="e2"> manaḥ buddhiḥ</span>–mind and intelligence;<span class="e2"> adhiṣṭhānam</span>–are the seats;<span class="e2"> asya</span>–of this enemy, desire.<span class="e2"> āvṛtya</span>–Covering;<span class="e2"> jñānam</span>–one’s knowledge;<span class="e2"> etaiḥ</span>–via these seats;<span class="e2"> eṣaḥ</span>–this desire;<span class="e2"> vimohayati</span>–deludes;<span class="e2"> dehinam</span>–the embodied living being. [40]
40 It is said that this enemy, desire, dwelling within the senses, mind, and intelligence, covers the perception of the embodied living being and deludes him.
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ ।<br />पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥४१॥
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau niyamya bharatarṣabha<br />pāpmānaṁ prajahi hy enaṁ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam [41]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharatarṣabha</span>–O Arjuna, noblest of the Bhāratas;<span class="e2"> tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> tasmāt</span>–therefore;<span class="e2"> ādau</span>–first;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi niyamya</span>–bring the senses under control;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–and completely;<span class="e2"> prajahi</span>–destroy;<span class="e2"> enam</span>–this desire;<span class="e2"> pāpmānam</span>–which is the embodiment of sin;<span class="e2"> jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam</span>–and the destroyer of both jñān, knowledge of the self and non-self as delineated in the scriptures, and vijñān, realisation of such knowledge. [41]
41 Therefore, O noblest of the Bhāratas, control your senses and destroy this desire, the embodiment of sin, which destroys both knowledge and realisation.
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः ।<br />मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेर्यः परतस्तु सः ॥४२॥
indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṁ manaḥ<br />manasas tu parā buddhir buddher yaḥ paratas tu saḥ [42]
(<span class="e2">paṇḍitāḥ</span>)–The wise;<span class="e2"> āhuḥ</span>–say that;<span class="e2"> indriyāṇi parāṇi</span>–the senses are superior; (<span class="e2">viṣayebhyaḥ</span>)–to matter;<span class="e2"> manaḥ</span>–the mind;<span class="e2"> param</span>–is superior;<span class="e2"> indriyebhyaḥ</span>–to the senses;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–the intelligence or faculty of decision;<span class="e2"> parā</span>–is superior;<span class="e2"> manasaḥ tu</span>–to the mind, too;<span class="e2"> yaḥ</span>–and that which;<span class="e2"> parataḥ</span>–is superior;<span class="e2"> buddheḥ tu</span>–to even the intelligence;<span class="e2"> saḥ</span>–is he—the jīva—the soul. [42]
42 It is said by the wise that the senses are superior to matter, the mind is superior to the senses, and the intelligence is superior to the mind; and the soul is superior to even the intelligence.
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना ।<br />जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥४३॥
evaṁ buddheḥ paraṁ buddhvā saṁstabhyātmānam ātmanā<br />jahi śatruṁ mahā-bāho kāma-rūpaṁ durāsadam [43]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty Arjuna;<span class="e2"> evam</span>–in this way;<span class="e2"> buddhvā</span>–discerning;<span class="e2"> buddheḥ param</span>–the soul to be superior to the intelligence;<span class="e2"> saṁstabhya</span>–by steadying;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–the mind;<span class="e2"> ātmanā</span>–by resolute intelligence—conviction;<span class="e2"> jahi</span>–destroy;<span class="e2"> durāsadam</span>–the formidable;<span class="e2"> śatrum</span>–enemy;<span class="e2"> kāma-rūpam</span>–in the form of desire. [43]
43 O mighty Arjuna, knowing the soul to be superior to the intelligence, steady the mind with resolute intelligence and destroy the formidable enemy, desire.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे<br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे कर्म्मयोगो नाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः ॥३॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde<br />karma-yogo nāma tṛtīyo ’dhyāyaḥ [3]
End of Chapter Three<br />The Path of Action<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

चतुर्थोऽध्यायः
Chapter Four
Jñāna-yoga <br />The Path of Knowledge
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् ।<br />विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥१॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
imaṁ vivasvate yogaṁ proktavān aham avyayam<br />vivasvān manave prāha manur ikṣvākave ’bravīt [1]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Lord said: <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">proktavān</span>–imparted; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this; <span class="e2">avyayam</span>–imperishable; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–yoga of knowledge (jñāna-yoga) achieved by selfless action; <span class="e2">vivasvate</span>–to Sūrya, the sun-god. <span class="e2">vivasvān</span>–Sūrya; <span class="e2">prāha</span>–taught; <span class="e2">manave</span>–his son, Vaivasvata Manu; <span class="e2">manuḥ</span>–and Manu; <span class="e2">abravīt</span>–related it; <span class="e2">ikṣvākave</span>–to his son, Ikṣvāku. [1]
1 The Supreme Lord said: I imparted this imperishable yoga of knowledge, achieved by selfless action, to Sūrya, the presiding deity of the sun. Sūrya taught it to his son Vaivasvata Manu, who passed it on to his son Ikṣvāku.
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः ।<br />स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥२॥
evaṁ paramparā-prāptam imaṁ rājarṣayo viduḥ<br />sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa [2]
<span class="e2">evam</span>–In this way; <span class="e2">paramparā-prāptam</span>–attained through disciplic succession; <span class="e2">rājarṣayaḥ</span>–the saintly kings; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–came to know; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this path. (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">parantapa</span>–O Arjuna, subduer of the enemy; <span class="e2">saḥ yogaḥ</span>–that yoga; <span class="e2">naṣṭaḥ</span>–has been lost; <span class="e2">iha</span>–at present; <span class="e2">mahatā kālena</span>–after the passage of a long time. [2]
2 O conqueror of the enemy, thus the saintly kings such as Nimi, Janaka, and others learned this yoga, which was passed down to them by disciplic succession. But in the course of time, this teaching has been lost.
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः ।<br />भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥३॥
sa evāyaṁ mayā te ’dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ<br />bhakto ’si me sakhā cheti rahasyaṁ hy etad uttamam [3]
(<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You; <span class="e2">asi</span>–are;<span class="e2"> me</span>–My; <span class="e2">bhaktaḥ sakhā cha</span>–devotee and friend. <span class="e2">iti </span>(<span class="e2">hetoḥ</span>)–For this reason; <span class="e2">ayam saḥ eva</span>–this very same; <span class="e2">purātanaḥ</span>–ancient; <span class="e2">yogaḥ</span>–yoga; <span class="e2">proktaḥ</span>–is described; <span class="e2">adya</span>–today; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you; <span class="e2">hi</span>–although; <span class="e2">etat</span>–this; <span class="e2">uttamam rahasyam</span>–is a great secret. [3]
3 As you are my devotee and friend, I now reveal to you this supreme secret—the eternal yoga.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः ।<br />कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥४॥
arjuna uvācha
aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ<br />katham etad vijānīyāṁ tvam ādau proktavān iti [4]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: <span class="e2">bhavataḥ</span>–Your; <span class="e2">janma</span>–birth; <span class="e2">aparam</span>–is in these times. <span class="e2">vivasvataḥ</span>–The sun-god’s; <span class="e2">janma</span>–birth; <span class="e2">param</span>–was long ago. (<span class="e2">tasmāt</span>)–So; <span class="e2">katham</span>–how; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> vijānīyām</span>–am I to understand; <span class="e2">etat</span>–that; <span class="e2">ādau</span>–in ancient times; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–You; <span class="e2">proktavān iti</span>–had thus taught; (<span class="e2">imam yogam</span>)–this yoga? [4]
4 Arjuna said: Vivasvān, the sun-god, was born in ancient times, long before You were. Therefore, how am I to consider that You previously gave these teachings to him?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चर्ज्जुन ।<br />तान्यहं वेद सर्व्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥५॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava chārjuna<br />tāny ahaṁ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṁ vettha parantapa [5]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">parantapa arjuna</span>–O Arjuna, subduer of the enemy; <span class="e2">bahūni</span>–many; <span class="e2">janmāni</span>–births; <span class="e2">me tava cha</span>–of Mine and yours; <span class="e2">vyatītāni</span>–have passed. <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">veda</span>–know; <span class="e2">tāni sarvāṇi</span>–all of them; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–(but) you; <span class="e2">na vettha</span>–do not know; (<span class="e2">tāni</span>)–them. [5]
5 The Supreme Lord said: O chastiser of the enemy, both you and I have passed through many births. I can remember all of them, whereas you, O Arjuna, cannot.
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् ।<br />प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥६॥
ajo ’pi sann avyayātmā bhūtānām īśvaro ’pi san<br />prakṛtiṁ svām adhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmy ātma-māyayā [6]
<span class="e2">api</span>–Although; <span class="e2">san</span>–being; <span class="e2">ajaḥ</span>–birthless; <span class="e2">avyaya-ātmā</span>–of imperishable form; <span class="e2">api</span>–and although; <span class="e2">san</span>–being; <span class="e2">īśvaraḥ</span>–the Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">bhūtānām</span>–of all beings; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I; <span class="e2">adhiṣṭhāya</span>–remaining; <span class="e2">svām prakṛtim</span>–in My own divine nature of truth, auspiciousness, and beauty; <span class="e2">sambhavāmi</span>–appear in the world; <span class="e2">ātma-māyayā</span>–by My potency, yogamāyā. [6]
6 Although My eternal form is transcendental to birth and death, and I am the Lord of all beings, I appear within the world in My divine nature, by My sweet will, extending My internal potency.
यदा यदा हि धर्म्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।<br />अभ्युत्थानमधर्म्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥७॥
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata<br />abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham [7]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">bhārata</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">yadā yadā hi</span>–whenever; <span class="e2">glāniḥ</span>–a decline; <span class="e2">dharmasya</span>–of religion; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and; <span class="e2">abhyutthānam</span>–an uprising; <span class="e2">adharmasya</span>–of irreligion; <span class="e2">bhavati</span>–occurs; <span class="e2">tadā</span>–then; <span class="e2">aham sṛjāmi</span>–I appear, seemingly like a being born in this world—I make My advent; <span class="e2">ātmānam</span>–Myself. [7]
7 O Bhārata, whenever there is a decline of religion and an uprising of irreligion, I personally make My advent.
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।<br />धर्म्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥८॥
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya cha duṣkṛtām<br />dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge [8]
<span class="e2">paritrāṇāya</span>–For the deliverance; <span class="e2">sādhūnām</span>–of saintly devotees; (<span class="e2">tathā</span>)–and; <span class="e2">vināśāya</span>–for the vanquishing; <span class="e2">duṣkṛtām</span>–of miscreants; <span class="e2">saṁsthāpana-arthāya cha</span>–and for firmly establishing; <span class="e2">dharma</span>–dhyān (meditation), yajana (performance of sacrifice), paricharyā (worship), and saṅkīrtan (congregational chanting of the Holy Names) all centred on Me; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I; <span class="e2">sambhavāmi</span>–appear; <span class="e2">yuge yuge</span>–age after age. [8]
8 I appear age after age to deliver the saintly devotees, vanquish the miscreants, and firmly establish true religion.
जन्म कर्म्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।<br />त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्ज्जुन ॥९॥
janma karma cha me divyam evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ<br />tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so ’rjuna [9]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who; <span class="e2">vetti</span>–knows; <span class="e2">evam</span>–thus; <span class="e2">tattvataḥ</span>–the reality; <span class="e2">me</span>–of My; <span class="e2">divyam</span>–spontaneous, divine; <span class="e2">janma karma cha</span>–birth and activities; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">tyaktvā</span>–upon giving up; <span class="e2">deham</span>–the body; <span class="e2">na eti</span>–does not accept; <span class="e2">punaḥ janma</span>–rebirth. <span class="e2">mam eti</span>–He attains Me. [9]
9 O Arjuna, one who comes to know thus the truth of My Pastimes of divine birth and activities, does not undergo rebirth. After giving up this body, he attains Me. (My grace is revealed to him as My personal transcendental joyful potency, hlādinī-śakti. His heart is melted in divine love, and he attains My eternal devotional service.)
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः ।<br />बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥१०॥
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhā man-mayā mām upāśritāḥ<br />bahavo jñāna-tapasā pūtā mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ [10]
<span class="e2">vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhāḥ</span>–Free from mundane attachment, fear, and anger; <span class="e2">mat-mayāḥ</span>–wholeheartedly absorbed in services to Me; <span class="e2">bahavaḥ</span>–many persons; <span class="e2">mām upāśritāḥ</span>–in My refuge; <span class="e2">pūtāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–being purified; <span class="e2">jñāna-tapasā</span>–by knowledge and austerities in relation to My service; <span class="e2">āgatāḥ</span>–attained; <span class="e2">mat-bhāvam</span>–My bhāva—devotion to Me. [10]
10 Free from attachment, fear, and anger, many persons have taken shelter in Me, absorbing their hearts in My services (hearing, chanting, and remembering). Purified by knowledge and the fire of ordeal in My service, they attained divine love for Me.
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।<br />मम वर्त्त्मानुवर्त्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्व्वशः ॥११॥
ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham<br />mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ [11]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–Howsoever; <span class="e2">ye</span>–those who; <span class="e2">prapadyante</span>–surrender; <span class="e2">mām</span>–to Me; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">tathā eva</span>–accordingly; <span class="e2">bhajāmi</span>–reward; <span class="e2">tān</span>–them. (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">sarvaśaḥ manuṣyāḥ</span>–all types of men (on all paths); <span class="e2">anuvartante</span>–follow; <span class="e2">mama vartma</span>–My path. [11]
11 Howsoever people surrender to Me, I accordingly reward them. Being the ultimate goal of all paths, I am the objective to be attained by all. O Pārtha, all men follow My various paths.
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्म्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।<br />क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्म्मजा ॥१२॥
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṁ siddhiṁ yajanta iha devatāḥ<br />kṣipraṁ hi mānuṣe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā [12]
<span class="e2">iha</span>–In this world; <span class="e2">kāṅkṣantaḥ</span>–persons who desire; <span class="e2">siddhim</span>–the fruition; <span class="e2">karmaṇām</span>–of worldly actions; <span class="e2">yajante</span>–worship; <span class="e2">devatāḥ</span>–the demigods; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; <span class="e2">mānuṣe loke</span>–in the human plane; <span class="e2">siddhiḥ</span>–the fruit (attainment of heaven, etc.); <span class="e2">karma-jā</span>–born of action; <span class="e2">bhavati</span>–appears; <span class="e2">kṣipram</span>–very quickly. [12]
12 Persons who desire the fruit of their actions worship the gods, since in the human plane, actions swiftly bear fruit.
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्म्मविभागशः ।<br />तस्य कर्त्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्त्तारमव्ययम् ॥१३॥
chātur-varṇyaṁ mayā sṛṣṭaṁ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ<br />tasya kartāram api māṁ viddhy akartāram avyayam [13]
<span class="e2">chātuḥ-varṇyam</span>–The four social divisions or varṇas—brāhmaṇ, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra; <span class="e2">sṛṣṭam</span>–are manifest; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me; <span class="e2">guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ</span>–classified according to the modes of nature and corresponding activities (vide 18.41–44). <span class="e2">kartāram api</span>–Although I am the accomplisher; <span class="e2">tasya</span>–of that; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me; <span class="e2">akartāram</span>–to be the non-doer; <span class="e2">avyayam</span>–and unchangeable. [13]
13 The four social divisions, classified according to the material modes of nature and corresponding activities, are made manifest by Me. Although I am the doer of this, know Me to be the non-doer and unchangable.
न मां कर्म्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्म्मफले स्पृहा ।<br />इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्म्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥१४॥
na māṁ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛhā<br />iti māṁ yo ’bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate [14]
<span class="e2">karmāṇi</span>–Actions; <span class="e2">na limpanti</span>–do not implicate or taint; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me; (<span class="e2">jīvam iva</span>)–like the living beings. <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">asti</span>)–There is no; <span class="e2">spṛhā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">me</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">karma-phale</span>–for the fruits of action. <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus; <span class="e2">mām abhijānāti</span>–knows Me in truth (as the Supreme Lord); <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">na badhyate</span>–is not bound; <span class="e2">karmabhiḥ</span>–by karma. [14]
14 I am never implicated by action nor do I desire the fruits of action. One who knows Me thus (as the Supreme Lord, transcendental to worldly action) is never bound by action.
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म्म पूर्व्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः ।<br />कुरु कर्म्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्व्वैः पूर्व्वतरं कृतम् ॥१५॥
evaṁ jñātvā kṛtaṁ karma pūrvair api mumukṣubhiḥ<br />kuru karmaiva tasmāt tvaṁ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṁ kṛtam [15]
<span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–Knowing; <span class="e2">evam</span>–this; <span class="e2">mumukṣubhiḥ api</span>–the seekers of liberation; <span class="e2">pūrvaiḥ</span>–of previous times; <span class="e2">kṛtam</span>–performed; <span class="e2">karma</span>–selfless action. <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–you; <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">kuru</span>–must adopt; <span class="e2">karma</span>–the path of selfless action; <span class="e2">pūrvataram kṛtam</span>–as done in the past; <span class="e2">pūrvaiḥ</span>–by the ancient mahājans, great saintly persons, like Janaka and others. [15]
15 Knowing this basic principle, seekers of liberation in previous times renounced all fruitive work and performed their duties as a selfless offering to Me. Likewise, you should adopt this yoga of selfless action as did the great saintly persons of yore.
किं कर्म्म किमकर्म्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः ।<br />तत्ते कर्म्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥१६॥
kiṁ karma kim akarmeti kavayo ’py atra mohitāḥ<br />tat te karma pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣyase ’śubhāt [16]
<span class="e2">kim karma</span>–What is action? <span class="e2">kim akarma</span>–what is inaction? <span class="e2">iti atra</span>–In this subject; <span class="e2">kavayaḥ api</span>–even the learned; <span class="e2">mohitāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">bhavanti</span>)–are baffled. (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–Therefore; <span class="e2">pravakṣyāmi</span>–I shall describe; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you; <span class="e2">tat karma</span>–what is karma and akarma, action and inaction; <span class="e2">yat jñātvā</span>–knowing which; <span class="e2">mokṣyase</span>–you will be liberated; <span class="e2">aśubhāt</span>–from inauspiciousness. [16]
16 What is action? What is inaction? Even the learned have difficulty understanding this. Hence, I shall enlighten you in this matter, knowing which you will liberated from inauspiciousness.
कर्म्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यञ्च विकर्म्मणः ।<br />अकर्म्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्म्मणो गतिः ॥१७॥
karmaṇo hy api boddhavyaṁ boddhavyañ cha vikarmaṇaḥ<br />akarmaṇaś cha boddhavyaṁ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ [17]
<span class="e2">karmaṇaḥ api boddhavyam</span>–Action prescribed (by the Vedas) should be understood; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">vikarmaṇaḥ boddhavyam</span>–action prohibited (by the Vedas) should be understood; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">akarmaṇaḥ boddhavyam</span>–renunciation of action should be understood; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; <span class="e2">gatiḥ</span>–the true nature; <span class="e2">karmaṇaḥ</span>–of action; <span class="e2">gahanā</span>–is very difficult to comprehend. [17]
17 The true nature of action is difficult to comprehend. One should understand prescribed action, prohibited action, and inaction.
कर्म्मण्यकर्म्म यः पश्येदकर्म्मणि च कर्म्म यः ।<br />स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्म्मकृत् ॥१८॥
karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed akarmaṇi cha karma yaḥ<br />sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsna-karma-kṛt [18]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; <span class="e2">paśyet</span>–sees; <span class="e2">akarma</span>–inaction; <span class="e2">karmaṇi</span>–in action; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–who; (<span class="e2">paśyet</span>)–sees; <span class="e2">karma</span>–action; <span class="e2">akarmaṇi</span>–in inaction; <span class="e2">saḥ buddhimān</span>–he is wise; <span class="e2">manuṣyeṣu</span>–among men. <span class="e2">saḥ yuktaḥ</span>–He is a yogī; <span class="e2">kṛtsna-karma-kṛt</span>–a performer of all actions. [18]
18 One who sees action within inaction, and inaction within action, is wise among men. He is a yogī and a performer of all actions.
यस्य सर्व्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्ज्जिताः ।<br />ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्म्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥१९॥
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṅkalpa-varjitāḥ<br />jñānāgni-dagdha-karmāṇaṁ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṁ budhāḥ [19]
<span class="e2">yasya</span>–One whose; <span class="e2">sarve</span>–every; <span class="e2">samārambhāḥ</span>–undertaking; <span class="e2">kāma-saṅkalpa-varjitāḥ</span>–is without fruitive desire; <span class="e2">jñāna-agni-dagdha-karmāṇam</span>–and who has burnt all actions in the fire of knowledge; <span class="e2">budhāḥ</span>–the wise; <span class="e2">āhuḥ tam</span>–describe him as; <span class="e2">paṇḍitam</span>–learned. [19]
19 One whose every action is without fruitive desire, and who burns all actions in the fire of knowledge, is described by the wise as learned.
त्यक्त्वा कर्म्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।<br />कर्म्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥२०॥
tyaktvā karma-phalāsaṅgaṁ nitya-tṛpto nirāśrayaḥ<br />karmaṇy abhipravṛtto ’pi naiva kiñchit karoti saḥ [20]
(<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>)–One who; <span class="e2">tyaktvā</span>–giving up; <span class="e2">karma-phala-āsaṅgam</span>–attachment to the fruits of action; <span class="e2">nirāśrayaḥ</span>–is free from mundane dependence; <span class="e2">nitya-tṛptaḥ</span>–and content in the eternal bliss within; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">abhipravṛttaḥ api</span>–although fully engaged; <span class="e2">karmaṇi</span>–in all kinds of activities; <span class="e2">na karoti</span>–does not do; <span class="e2">kiñchit eva</span>–anything at all. [20]
20 Such a person, giving up attachment to the fruits of action, fully content in the eternal bliss within, and free from mundane dependence, though fully active, does nothing at all.
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्व्वपरिग्रहः ।<br />शारीरं केवलं कर्म्म कुर्व्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥२१॥
nirāśīr yata-chittātmā tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ<br />śārīraṁ kevalaṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam [21]
<span class="e2">nirāśīḥ</span>–Desireless; <span class="e2">yata-chitta-ātmā</span>–of controlled mind and body; <span class="e2">tyakta-sarva-pari-grahaḥ</span>–and a renouncer of all possessiveness and acquisition; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–that person; <span class="e2">na āpnoti</span>–does not incur; <span class="e2">kilbiṣam</span>–sin; <span class="e2">kurvan </span>(<span class="e2">api</span>)–although he performs; <span class="e2">śārīram karma</span>–action for bodily sustenance; <span class="e2">kevalam</span>–only. [21]
21 Desireless, controlling mind and body by the intelligence, and renouncing all possessiveness and acquisition, no sinful or pious reaction is incurred by such a person who may act to acquire mundane objects merely for his bodily sustenance.
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।<br />समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥२२॥
yadṛchchhā-lābha-santuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ<br />samaḥ siddhāv asiddhau cha kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate [22]
(<span class="e2">janaḥ</span>)–A person; <span class="e2">yadṛchchhā-lābha-santuṣṭaḥ</span>–satisfied with whatever is readily available; <span class="e2">dvandva-atītaḥ</span>–beyond dualities such as heat and cold, pleasure and pain, attraction and aversion; <span class="e2">vimatsaraḥ</span>–devoid of envy; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">samaḥ</span>–equipoised; <span class="e2">siddhau-asiddhau</span>–in the event of either success or failure of action; <span class="e2">kṛtvā api</span>–though performing; (<span class="e2">karma</span>)–action; <span class="e2">na nibadhyate</span>–is not bound. [22]
22 Content with whatever is readily available and unaffected by dualities (of pleasure and pain, attraction and aversion), such a person has no envy. He is equipoised, neither elated nor dejected in success or failure. Though active, he is not bound by any action.
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः।<br />यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥२३॥
gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthita-chetasaḥ<br />yajñāyācharataḥ karma samagraṁ pravilīyate [23]
<span class="e2">gata-saṅgasya</span>–For one who is free from attachment; <span class="e2">muktasya</span>–who is liberated; <span class="e2">jñāna-avasthita-chetasaḥ</span>–who is realised; <span class="e2">karma ācharataḥ</span>–who performs action; <span class="e2">yajñāya</span>–for yajña, i.e. for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">samagram</span>–all; (<span class="e2">karma</span>)– action; <span class="e2">pravilīyate</span>–is dissipated, i.e. it does not produce any reaction.
23 For one who is detached, enlightened, and liberated, all his actions, performed in the spirit of sacrifice, are perfectly dissipated.
Commentary
The actions of one practising the yoga of selfless action do not lead to apūrva as considered by the philosophers known as karma-mīmāṁsaka. According to their ethical yet atheistic ideology, the karma-mīmāṁsakas or mundane rationalists claim that pious actions produce an unseen, subtle potency known as apūrva, which must fructify at the appropriate time after death. Their conception that this fruit can later be shared by others is meant to show the eternality of karma, or action, but it ignores the presence of the Supreme Autocrat.
So the statement of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, “<span class="e3">Samagraṁ pravilīyate</span>: all actions are dissipated,” ought not be misinterpreted to mean that the actions of liberated souls cause some such remote worldly consequence, or apūrva. Rather, the Lord indicates that the actions offered to Him by the selfless karma-yogī do not cause any subsequent reaction to be either enjoyed or suffered by others in this mundane plane.
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।<br />ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्म्मसमधिना ॥२४॥
brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam<br />brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahma-karma-samadhinā [24]
<span class="e2">arpaṇam </span>(<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–The sacrificial utensils such as sruk, sruvā, or spoon, ladle, etc., are; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–Brahma; (<span class="e2">arpyamāṇam</span>)<span class="e2"> haviḥ</span>–the oblation of ghee, etc.; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–is; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–Brahma; <span class="e2">hutam</span>–offered; <span class="e2">brahma-agnau</span>–into the sacrificial fire of Brahma; <span class="e2">brahmaṇā </span>(<span class="e2">havana kartā</span>)–by the brāhmaṇ offerer who is Brahma. <span class="e2">brahma eva</span>–Brahma, the Absolute; <span class="e2">gantavyam</span>–is attainable; <span class="e2">tena brahma-karma-samādhinā</span>–by a person whose consciousness is absorbed in Brahma action. [24]
24 The ladle is Brahma, the oblation is Brahma offered by Brahma into the fire of Brahma. One whose consciousness is fully absorbed in Brahma action certainly attains to Brahma, the Absolute.
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्य्युपासते ।<br />ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥२५॥
daivam evāpare yajñaṁ yoginaḥ paryupāsate<br />brahmāgnāv apare yajñaṁ yajñenaivopajuhvati [25]
<span class="e2">apare</span>–Other; <span class="e2">yoginaḥ</span>–(karma-) yogīs; <span class="e2">paryupāsate</span>–worship; <span class="e2">daivam yajñam eva</span>–the demigods with sacrifice. <span class="e2">apare</span>–Other (jñāna-) yogīs; <span class="e2">upajuhvati</span>–offer; <span class="e2">yajñam</span>–the self (jīvātmā, as the element tvam, representing the ghee of sacrifice); <span class="e2">brahma-agnau</span>–to the fire of Brahma (or to the Supersoul, Paramātmā, as the element tat, representing the sacrificial fire); <span class="e2">yajñena eva</span>–by vibrating the praṇava mantra, Om. [25]
25 Some yogīs offer sacrifices to the demigods, and others offer the self into the fire of Brahma by vibrating the praṇava mantra, Om.
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति ।<br />शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥२६॥
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye saṁyamāgniṣu juhvati<br />śabdādīn viṣayān anya indriyāgniṣu juhvati [26]
<span class="e2">anye</span>–Others (naiṣṭika or lifelong celibates); <span class="e2">juhvati</span>–offer; <span class="e2">indriyāṇi</span>–the senses; <span class="e2">śrotra-ādīni</span>–of hearing, etc.; <span class="e2">saṁyama-agniṣu</span>–into the fires of self (mental) control. <span class="e2">anye</span>–Others (persons in sacred marriage); <span class="e2">juhvati</span>–offer; <span class="e2">viṣayān</span>–the sense objects; <span class="e2">śabda-ādīn</span>–sound, etc.; <span class="e2">indriya-agniṣu</span>–into the fires of the senses. [26]
26 Some offer their senses of hearing, touching, seeing, tasting, and smelling into the fires of self-control; yet others offer the sense objects of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell into the fire of the senses.
सर्व्वाणीन्द्रियकर्म्माणि प्राणकर्म्माणि चापरे ।<br />आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥२७॥
sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi chāpare<br />ātma-saṁyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite [27]
<span class="e2">apare</span>–Others (meditating mystic yogīs in realisation of the pure self [tvam]); <span class="e2">juhvati</span>–offer; <span class="e2">sarvāṇi</span>–all; <span class="e2">indriya-karmāṇi</span>–the functions of the senses; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">prāṇa-karmāṇi</span>–the functions of the ten vital life-airs; <span class="e2">ātma-saṁyama-yoga-agnau</span>–into the yogic fire of self-purification; <span class="e2">jñāna-dīpite</span>–ignited by knowledge. [27]
27 Again, there are the yogīs who offer all the functions of the senses and the life forces into the yogic fire of self-purification ignited by knowledge.
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे ।<br />स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥२८॥
dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tathāpare<br />svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāś cha yatayaḥ saṁśita-vratāḥ [28]
(<span class="e2">kechit</span>)–Some; <span class="e2">dravya-yajñāḥ</span>–sacrifice material possessions or wealth; (<span class="e2">kechit</span>)–some; <span class="e2">tapaḥ-yajñāḥ</span>–perform sacrifice in the form of penance (such as Chāndrāyaṇ, etc.); <span class="e2">tathā-apare</span>–and others; <span class="e2">yoga-yajñāḥ</span>–perform sacrifice in the form of the eightfold mystic yoga practice; (<span class="e2">kechana</span>)–and again some; <span class="e2">svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāḥ cha</span>–perform ‘knowledge-sacrifice’ in the form of singing and introspectively studying the Vedas. (<span class="e2">ete sarve</span>)–All these persons; <span class="e2">yatayaḥ</span>–are diligent; <span class="e2">saṁśita-vratāḥ</span>–performers of unshakeable vows. [28]
28 Sincere in their practices and faithful to their vows, some persons sacrifice their possessions, some undergo strict penances as a sacrifice, some practise the eightfold mystic yoga as a sacrifice, and yet others perform ‘knowledge-sacrifice’ by singing and introspectively studying the Vedas.
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे ।<br />प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ।<br />अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति ॥२९॥
apāne juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe ’pānaṁ tathāpare<br />prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ<br />apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati [29]
<span class="e2">apare</span>–Others; <span class="e2">juhvati apāne prāṇam</span>–bring the ascending air into union with the descending air while inhaling (pūraka). <span class="e2">tathā</span>–Likewise; (<span class="e2">juhvati</span>)–they offer; <span class="e2">prāṇe apānam</span>–the descending air into the ascending air while exhaling (rechaka); (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and; <span class="e2">ruddhvā</span>–stopping; <span class="e2">prāṇa-apāna-gatī</span>–the flow of both prāṇa and apāna while retaining the breath (kumbhaka); <span class="e2">prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">bhavanti</span>)–they arduously practise breath-control (prāṇāyām). <span class="e2">apare</span>–Others; <span class="e2">juhvati</span>–offer; <span class="e2">prāṇān</span>–the senses; <span class="e2">prāṇeṣu</span>–into the life-airs, the prāṇa-vāyu; <span class="e2">niyata-āhārāḥ</span>–by reducing their intake of food. [29]
29 Others practise breath-control. Closing the right nostril and inhaling through the left, they bring the ascending air into union with the descending; closing the left nostril and exhaling through the right, they similarly offer the descending air into the ascending; then closing both nostrils, they check both ascending and descending airs. Yet other practitioners of sense-control offer all the senses into the life-airs by reducing their food intake.
सर्व्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षयितकल्मषाः ।<br />यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥३०॥
sarve ’py ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣayita-kalmaṣāḥ<br />yajña-śiṣṭāmṛta-bhujo yānti brahma sanātanam [30]
<span class="e2">ete sarve api</span>–All these persons; <span class="e2">yajñā-vidaḥ</span>–are knowers of sacrifice. <span class="e2">yajñā-kṣayitakalmaṣāḥ</span>–Purified of sin by the performance of sacrifice; <span class="e2">yajñā-śiṣṭa-amṛta-bhujaḥ</span>–they enjoy the nectarean remnants of sacrifice; <span class="e2">yānti sanātanam</span>–and reach the eternal; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–Brahma, Absolute Truth. [30]
30 All these persons are knowers of sacrifice, purified by sacrifice. Enjoying the nectarean remnants of sacrifice, they attain to the eternal plane of the Absolute.
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥३१॥
nāyaṁ loko ’sty ayajñasya kuto ’nyaḥ kuru-sattama [31]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kuru-sattama</span>–O Arjuna, best of the Kurus; <span class="e2">ayam lokaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">api</span>)–even this world (or human plane of meagre pleasures); <span class="e2">na asti</span>–is denied; <span class="e2">ayajñasya</span>–a person who does not perform sacrifice. <span class="e2">kutaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">prāptavyaḥ</span>)–How, then, will it be possible for him to attain; <span class="e2">anyaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">lokaḥ</span>)–the next world (or heaven)? [31]
31 O Arjuna, foremost of the Kurus, without sacrifice one cannot attain fulfillment in this world, to say nothing of the next.
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।<br />कर्म्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्व्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥३२॥
evaṁ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe<br />karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evaṁ jñātvā vimokṣyase [32]
<span class="e2">evam</span>–In this way; <span class="e2">bahu-vidhāḥ</span>–many varieties of; <span class="e2">yajñāḥ</span>–sacrifices; <span class="e2">vitatāḥ</span>–have been elucidated; <span class="e2">brahmaṇaḥ mukhe</span>–by the mouthpiece of the Vedas. (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–should know; <span class="e2">tān sarvān</span>–all those sacrifices; <span class="e2">karma-jān</span>–to be born of action, in thought, word, and deed. <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–Knowing; <span class="e2">evam</span>–this; <span class="e2">vimokṣyase</span>–you will be liberated from the bondage of action. [32]
32 Thus many types of sacrifice are described in the Vedas and allied scriptures. Know that they are all accomplished through action (of thought, word, and deed). Knowing this, you will be liberated from the bondage of action.
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप ।<br />सर्व्वं कर्म्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥३३॥
śreyān dravyamayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa<br />sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate [33]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">parantapa pārtha</span>–O Arjuna, subduer of the enemy; <span class="e2">jñāna-yajñaḥ</span>–‘knowledge-sacrifice’; <span class="e2">śreyān</span>–is better; <span class="e2">yajñāt</span>–than sacrifice; <span class="e2">dravya-mayāt</span>–of materials; (<span class="e2">yataḥ</span>)–since; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–all; <span class="e2">karma</span>–action; <span class="e2">akhilam</span>–in its entirety, including its fruit; <span class="e2">pari-samāpyate</span>–has its consummation; <span class="e2">jñāne</span>–in knowledge. [33]
33 O Arjuna, subduer of the enemy, ‘knowledge-sacrifice’ is superior to the sacrifice of material objects, because the perfection of all action, including its fruit, is its culmination in knowledge.
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया ।<br />उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥३४॥
tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā<br />upadekṣyanti te jñānaṁ jñāninas tattva-darśinaḥ [34]
<span class="e2">tat</span>–Such knowledge; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–should be known; <span class="e2">praṇipātena</span>–by submission, obeisances; <span class="e2">paripraśnena</span>–by relevant inquiry; <span class="e2">sevayā</span>–and by sincere service. <span class="e2">jñāninaḥ</span>–Those learned in the scriptures; <span class="e2">tattva-darśinaḥ</span>–endowed with divine revelation of the Supreme Absolute Truth; <span class="e2">upadekṣyanti</span>–will impart; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you. [34]
34 You will be able to attain knowledge by satisfying the divine master with submission, relevant inquiry, and sincere service. The enlightened souls who are learned in scriptural knowledge and endowed with direct realisation of the Supreme Absolute Truth will impart divine knowledge to you.
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव ।<br />येन भूतान्यशेषाणि द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥३५॥
yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṁ yāsyasi pāṇḍava<br />yena bhūtāny aśeṣāṇi drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi [35]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pāṇḍava</span>–O Arjuna, son of Pāṇḍu; <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">yat </span>(<span class="e2">jñānam</span>)–that knowledge; <span class="e2">na yāsyasi</span>–you will not be subject to; <span class="e2">evam</span>–such; <span class="e2">moham</span>–illusion; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–again. <span class="e2">yena</span>–By that knowledge; <span class="e2">drakṣyasi</span>–you will see; <span class="e2">aśeṣāṇi bhūtāni</span>–all species from highest to lowest; <span class="e2">ātmani</span>–<span class="e2">in the ātmā</span>–in their spiritual nature; (<span class="e2">pṛthak upādhitvena</span>)–though appearing in the forms of their various material designations; <span class="e2">atha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">drakṣyasi</span>)–you will see them; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–in Me. [35]
35 O Pāṇḍava, when you are enlightened by this knowledge of the reality, you will no longer be subject to your present illusion. You will see the one spiritual nature in all species of life, from highest to lowest, and that all are situated within Me.
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्व्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः ।<br />सर्व्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥३६॥
api ched asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamaḥ<br />sarvaṁ jñāna-plavenaiva vṛjinaṁ santariṣyasi [36]
<span class="e2">api chet</span>–Even if; <span class="e2">asi</span>–you are; <span class="e2">pāpa-kṛttamaḥ</span>–the most sinful; <span class="e2">sarvebhyaḥ papebhyaḥ</span>–of all sinners; (<span class="e2">tathāpi</span>)–nonetheless; <span class="e2">santariṣyasi eva</span>–you will cross; <span class="e2">sarvam vṛjinam</span>–all sins; <span class="e2">jñāna-plavena</span>–by the boat of knowledge. [36]
36 Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross the ocean of sins by the boat of knowledge.
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />ज्ञानाग्निः सर्व्वकर्म्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥३७॥
yathaidhāṁsi samiddho ’gnir bhasmasāt kurute ’rjuna<br />jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā [37]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna, <span class="e2">yathā</span>–as; <span class="e2">samiddhaḥ</span>–blazing; <span class="e2">agniḥ</span>–fire; <span class="e2">kurute</span>–renders; <span class="e2">edhāṁsi</span>–firewood; <span class="e2">bhasmasāt</span>–to ashes; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–similarly; <span class="e2">jñāna-agniḥ</span>–the fire of knowledge; <span class="e2">kurute</span>–renders; <span class="e2">sarva-karmāṇi</span>–all karma (worldly actions and reactions in this life); <span class="e2">bhasmasāt</span>–to ashes. [37]
37 As a blazing fire renders wood to ashes, O Arjuna, the fire of knowledge burns up all worldly actions.
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।<br />तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥३८॥
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṁ pavitram iha vidyate<br />tat svayaṁ yoga-saṁsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati [38]
<span class="e2">iha</span>–In this world, or, of the aforementioned practices of austerity, etc.; (<span class="e2">kim api</span>)<span class="e2"> na hi vidyate</span>–there is nothing; <span class="e2">pavitram</span>–(as) pure; <span class="e2">jñānena sadṛśam</span>–as knowledge. <span class="e2">yoga-saṁsiddhaḥ</span>–A person successful in (niṣkām karma) yoga; <span class="e2">vindati</span>–realises; <span class="e2">svayam</span>–for himself; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that knowledge; <span class="e2">ātmani</span>–within the heart; <span class="e2">kālena</span>–after (a long) time. [38]
38 In this world, there is nothing as pure as knowledge. Eventually, a person who has achieved perfection in the yoga of selfless action naturally realises this knowledge within his heart.
श्रद्धावान्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।<br />ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥३९॥
śraddhāvān labhate jñānaṁ tat-paraḥ saṁyatendriyaḥ<br />jñānaṁ labdhvā parāṁ śāntim achireṇādhigachchati [39]
<span class="e2">śraddhāvān</span>–The faithful (having faith in the Lord’s words or the scriptures); <span class="e2">tat-paraḥ</span>–devoted; <span class="e2">saṁyata-indriyaḥ</span>–sense-controlled person; <span class="e2">labhate</span>–attains; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge. <span class="e2">labdhvā</span>–Having attained; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–enlightenment; <span class="e2">achireṇa</span>–quickly; <span class="e2">adhi-gachhati</span>–he attains; <span class="e2">parām śāntim</span>–supreme peace (beyond the mundane). [39]
39 It is the devoted, faithful, and sense-controlled person who attains knowledge. Achieving enlightenment, such a person soon attains the supreme peace.
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।<br />नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥४०॥
ajñaś chāśraddadhānaś cha saṁśayātmā vinaśyati<br />nāyaṁ loko ’sti na paro na sukhaṁ saṁśayātmanaḥ [40]
<span class="e2">ajñaḥ</span>–The ignorant (like an animal); <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">aśraddadhānaḥ</span>–faithless (confused by many interpretations despite scriptural knowledge); <span class="e2">saṁśaya-ātmā cha</span>–and doubting person (who doubts he will succeed despite having some faith); <span class="e2">vinaśyati</span>–is ruined by misfortune. <span class="e2">saṁśaya-ātmanaḥ</span>–For the doubting person; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–there is no; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">na ayam lokaḥ</span>–either in this world; <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)<span class="e2"> paraḥ</span>–or the next. [40]
40 The ignorant, faithless, and doubting person is doomed to misfortune. For the doubting soul there can be happiness neither in this life nor the next.
योगसन्न्यस्तकर्म्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् ।<br />आत्मवन्तं न कर्म्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥४१॥
yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇaṁ jñāna-sañchhinna-saṁśayam<br />ātmavantaṁ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya [41]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">dhanañjaya</span>–O Dhanañjaya; <span class="e2">karmāṇi</span>–actions; <span class="e2">na nibadhnanti</span>–cannot bind; <span class="e2">yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇam</span>–one who has ceased all action in accordance with the path of sannyās, abnegation, by practising niṣkām karma-yoga, the path of selfless action; <span class="e2">jñāna-sañchhinna-saṁśayam</span>–and overcome all his doubts by the cultivation of divine knowledge (sambandha-jñān, knowledge of the eternal serving relationship of the individual soul with the Lord); <span class="e2">ātma-vantam</span>–and who has realised the nature of the soul. [41]
41 O Dhanañjaya, renouncing all worldly actions by following the path of selfless action, one who severs all his doubts by knowledge and realises his internal divine nature, can never be bound by action.
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः <br />छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥४२॥
tasmād ajñāna-sambhūtaṁ hṛt-sthaṁ jñānāsinātmanaḥ<br />chhittvainaṁ saṁśayaṁ yogam ātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata [42]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">bhārata</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–therefore; <span class="e2">chhittvā</span>–slashing; <span class="e2">jñāna-asinā</span>–by the sword of knowledge, sambandha-jñān; <span class="e2">enam</span>–these; <span class="e2">saṁśayam</span>–doubts; <span class="e2">ātmanaḥ</span>–of yours; <span class="e2">hṛt-stham</span>–in your heart; <span class="e2">ajñāna-sambhūtam</span>–which are born of ignorance; <span class="e2">ātiṣṭha</span>–take refuge in; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–niṣkām karma-yoga—the yoga of selfless action; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and; <span class="e2">uttisṭha</span>–arise for battle. [42]
42 Therefore, O Bhārat, with the sword of knowledge slash to shreds all these doubts in your heart, which are born of ignorance. Take refuge in selfless action and arise for battle!
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे<br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे ज्ञानयोगो नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ॥४॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma-<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde<br />jñāna-yogo nāma chaturtho ’dhyāyaḥ [4]
End of Chapter Four<br />The Path of Knowledge<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

पञ्चमोऽध्यायः
Chapter Five
Karma-sannyāsa-yoga <br />The Path of Renunciation of Action
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
सन्न्यासं कर्म्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगञ्च शंससि ।<br />यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम् ॥१॥
arjuna uvācha
sannyāsaṁ karmaṇāṁ kṛṣṇa punar yogañ cha śaṁsasi<br />yach chhreya etayor ekaṁ tan me brūhi suniśchitam [1]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You; <span class="e2">śaṁsasi</span>–speak of; <span class="e2">sannyāsam</span>–renunciation; <span class="e2">karmaṇām</span>–of actions; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–then again; <span class="e2">yogam cha</span>–application, yoga (of selfless action, niṣkām karma-yoga). <span class="e2">me brūhi</span>–Please tell me; <span class="e2">suniśchitam</span>–clearly; <span class="e2">yat tat ekam</span>–which one; <span class="e2">etayoḥ</span>–of the two; <span class="e2">śreyaḥ</span>–is superior. [1]
1 Arjuna said: O Kṛṣṇa, you speak of renunciation of actions, and then again, You speak of the path of selfless action. Therefore, please tell me clearly which is superior.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
सन्न्यासः कर्म्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ ।<br />तयोस्तु कर्म्मसन्न्यासात्कर्म्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
sannyāsaḥ karma-yogaś cha niḥśreyasa-karāv ubhau<br />tayos tu karma-sannyāsāt karma-yogo viśiṣyate [2]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: <span class="e2">ubhau</span>–both; sannyāsaḥ <span class="e2">karma-yogaḥ cha</span>–renunciation of action and the path of selfless action; <span class="e2">niḥśreyasa-karau</span>–bring great benefit; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">tayoḥ</span>–of these two; <span class="e2">karma-yoga</span>–the path of selfless action; <span class="e2">viśiṣyate</span>–is superior; <span class="e2">karma-sannyāsāt</span>–to renunciation of action. [2]
2 The Supreme Lord said: Both renunciation of action and the path of selfless action bring great benefit. Yet, of the two, know that the way of selfless action is superior.
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसन्न्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति ।<br />निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥३॥
jñeyaḥ sa nitya-sannyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati<br />nirdvandvo hi mahā-bāho sukhaṁ bandhāt pramuchyate [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty-armed one; <span class="e2">jñeyaḥ</span>–it is to be known that; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who; <span class="e2">na dveṣṭi</span>–neither resents; <span class="e2">na kāṅkṣati</span>–nor desires; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that person; <span class="e2">nitya-sannyāsī</span>–is renounced, though performing action; <span class="e2">hi</span>–because; <span class="e2">nirdvandvaḥ</span>–one who is free from duality; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–is easily; <span class="e2">pramuchyate</span>–liberated; <span class="e2">bandhāt</span>–from bondage. [3]
3 O mighty-armed Arjuna, know that one who is free from attraction and aversion is truly renounced, though performing action; for one who is free from duality easily attains liberation from bondage.
साङ्ख्य योगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः ।<br />एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥४॥
sāṅkhya-yogau pṛthag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ<br />ekam apy āsthitaḥ samyag ubhayor vindate phalam [4]
<span class="e2">bālāḥ</span>–The childish, the unwise; <span class="e2">pravadanti</span>–say that; <span class="e2">sāṅkhya-yogau</span>–the paths of renunciation and (karma-) yoga; <span class="e2">pṛthak</span>–are separate; (<span class="e2">tu</span>)–but; <span class="e2">paṇḍitāḥ</span>–the learned; <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">vadanti</span>)–do not say this. <span class="e2">samyak āsthitaḥ</span>–A person who adopts perfectly; <span class="e2">ekam api</span>–only one; <span class="e2">vindate</span>–attains; <span class="e2">phalam</span>–the result; <span class="e2">ubhayoḥ</span>–of both. [4]
4 The path of renunciation (sāṅkhya-yoga) and the path of selfless action (karma-yoga) are considered separate paths by the unwise, but not by the learned. One who perfectly follows either of these paths will achieve the result of both.
