यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते ।<br />एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगञ्च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥५॥
yat sāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṁ tad yogair api gamyate<br />ekaṁ sāṅkhyañ cha yogañ cha yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati [5]
<span class="e2">yat sthānam</span>–That state which; <span class="e2">prāpyate</span>–is obtained; <span class="e2">sāṅkhyaiḥ</span>–by renunciation (sannyās); <span class="e2">tat </span>(<span class="e2">sthānam</span>)–that state; <span class="e2">gamyate</span>–is reached; <span class="e2">yogaiḥ api</span>–by niṣkām karma-yoga, too. <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; (<span class="e2">vivekena</span>)–by proper consideration; <span class="e2">ekam paśyati</span>–sees as one; <span class="e2">sāṅkhyam cha yogam cha</span>–both sannyās and karma-yoga; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">paśyati</span>–sees. [5]
5 The state achieved by the renunciation of action is also achieved by the performance of selfless action. One who sees these two paths to be one and the same, actually sees.
सन्न्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः ।<br />योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म न चिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥६॥
sannyāsas tu mahā-bāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ<br />yoga-yukto munir brahma na chireṇādhigachchhati [6]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">mahā-bāho</span>–O best of the valiant; <span class="e2">ayogataḥ</span>–without niṣkām karma-yoga; <span class="e2">sannyāsaḥ</span>–renunciation; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–is; <span class="e2">duḥkham āptum</span>–the cause of sorrow; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">yoga-yuktaḥ</span>–one who performs niṣkām karma-yoga; <span class="e2">muniḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being a man of knowledge; <span class="e2">na chireṇa</span>–very soon; <span class="e2">adhigachchhati</span>–is able to attain to; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–the Absolute. [6]
6 O mighty hero, without selfless action, mere renunciation of action is the cause of sorrow. But the wise man who engages in selfless action swiftly attains to the Absolute.
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः ।<br />सर्व्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्व्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥७॥
yoga-yukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ<br />sarva-bhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvann api na lipyate [7]
<span class="e2">yoga-yuktaḥ</span>–Engaged in such a yoga process; <span class="e2">viśuddha-ātmā</span>–the clean-hearted person; <span class="e2">vijita-ātmā</span>–of controlled mind; <span class="e2">jita-indriyaḥ</span>–who has mastery over the senses; <span class="e2">na lipyate</span>–is not implicated; <span class="e2">kurvan api</span>–although performing action; <span class="e2">sarva-bhūta-ātmabhūta-ātmā </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–having reached the state in which his whole being is pervaded with affection and compassion for all beings. [7]
7 The clean-hearted person thus engaged in yoga controls his mind and senses. Becoming filled with affection and compassion for all beings, although fully active, he is never implicated by any action.
नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् ।<br />पश्यञ्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपञ्श्वसन् ॥८॥
प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि ।<br />इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्त्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥९॥
naiva kiñchit karomīti yukto manyeta tattva-vit<br />paśyañ śṛṇvan spṛśañ jighrann aśnan gachchhan svapañ śvasan [8]
pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇann unmiṣan nimiṣann api<br />indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan [9]
<span class="e2">yuktaḥ tattva-vit</span>–The realised karma-yogī; <span class="e2">api</span>–although engaged in the functions of; <span class="e2">paśyan</span>–seeing; <span class="e2">śṛṇvan</span>–hearing; <span class="e2">spṛśan</span>–touching; <span class="e2">jighṛan</span>–smelling; <span class="e2">aśnan</span>–eating; <span class="e2">gachchhan</span>–moving; <span class="e2">svapan</span>–sleeping; <span class="e2">śvasan</span>–breathing; <span class="e2">pralapan</span>–speaking; <span class="e2">visṛjan</span>–evacuating; <span class="e2">gṛhṇan</span>–grasping objects in the hands; <span class="e2">unmiṣan</span>–and opening; <span class="e2">nimiṣan</span>–and closing the eyes, or blinking; <span class="e2">dhārayan</span>–understanding; <span class="e2">iti</span>–that; <span class="e2">indriyāṇi</span>–the senses, viz., eyes, etc.; <span class="e2">vartante</span>–function; <span class="e2">indriya-artheṣu</span>–in relation to their respective sense objects of form, etc.; <span class="e2">iti manyeta</span>–thus considers: (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–“I; <span class="e2">na karomi</span>–do not do; <span class="e2">kiñchit eva</span>–anything”. [8–9]
8–9 The realised karma-yogī performs the activities of seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing, speaking, evacuating, grasping objects, blinking the eyes, and so on, and he understands, “My sense organs—eyes, ears, skin, nose, and tongue—function in relation to their respective objects of form, sound, touch, smell, and taste.” Thus, he considers, “I do not perform any action at all.”
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्म्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।<br />लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥१०॥
brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ<br />lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā [10]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; <span class="e2">karoti</span>–acts; <span class="e2">ādhāya</span>–by offering; <span class="e2">karmāṇi</span>–all actions; <span class="e2">brahmaṇi</span>–unto the Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">tyaktvā</span>–having given up; <span class="e2">saṅgam</span>–attachment; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">na lipyate</span>–is not affected; <span class="e2">pāpena</span>–by sin (or piety); <span class="e2">padma-patram iva</span>–as a lotus leaf; (<span class="e2">na lipyate</span>)–is not touched; <span class="e2">ambhasā</span>–by water. [10]
10 One who, though living in this world, selflessly offers all his actions to the Supreme Lord, is not polluted by sin, as a lotus leaf remains on the water yet is untouched by it.
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि ।<br />योगिनः कर्म्म कुर्व्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वात्मशुद्धये ॥११॥
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api<br />yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṁ tyaktvātma-śuddhaye [11]
<span class="e2">tyaktvā</span>–By giving up; <span class="e2">saṅgam</span>–attachment (to the fruits of action); <span class="e2">yoginaḥ</span>–the karma-yogīs; <span class="e2">karma kurvanti</span>–perform action; <span class="e2">kevalaiḥ</span>–merely; <span class="e2">kāyena</span>–by the body; <span class="e2">manasā</span>–by the mind; <span class="e2">buddhyā</span>–by the intelligence; <span class="e2">api indriyaiḥ</span>–and even by the senses; <span class="e2">ātma-śuddhaye</span>–for purification of the heart, self-purification. [11]
11 By giving up attachment, the karma-yogīs perform action merely through the body, mind, intelligence and even the senses, for self-purification.
युक्तः कर्म्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् ।<br />अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥१२॥
yuktaḥ karma-phalaṁ tyaktvā śāntim āpnoti naiṣṭhikīm<br />ayuktaḥ kāma-kāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate [12]
<span class="e2">yuktaḥ</span>–A niṣkām karma-yogī, one engaged in the yoga of selfless action; <span class="e2">tyaktvā</span>–giving up; <span class="e2">karma-phalam</span>–the fruits of action; <span class="e2">āpnoti</span>–attains; <span class="e2">naiṣṭhikīm</span>–uninterrupted; <span class="e2">śāntim</span>–peace, i.e. liberation; (<span class="e2">kintu</span>)–but; <span class="e2">ayuktaḥ</span>–a sakām karmī, fruitive worker; <span class="e2">nibadhyate</span>–becomes bound; <span class="e2">saktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being attached; <span class="e2">phale</span>–to the fruits of action; <span class="e2">kāma-kāreṇa</span>–by nurturing fruitive desires. [12]
12 Giving up attachment to the fruits of his actions, the materially unmotivated (niṣkām) karma-yogī attains constant peace, or liberation from actions and reactions. But the fruitive worker (sakām karmī) is attached to the fruits of his actions, and he becomes implicated by his endeavours.
सर्व्वकर्म्माणि मनसा सन्न्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी ।<br />नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्व्वन्न कारयन् ॥१३॥
sarva-karmāṇi manasā sannyasyāste sukhaṁ vaśī<br />nava-dvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan [13]
<span class="e2">manasā</span>–Mentally; <span class="e2">sannyasya</span>–renouncing; <span class="e2">sarva-karmāṇi</span>–all actions; <span class="e2">vaśī</span>–the sense-controlled; <span class="e2">dehī</span>–embodied being; <span class="e2">āste</span>–resides; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–happily; <span class="e2">nava-dvāre pure</span>–in the city of nine gates; <span class="e2">na eva kurvan</span>–neither acting; <span class="e2">na kārayan</span>–nor causing work for others. [13]
13 Mentally renouncing all actions, the sense-controlled embodied living being resides happily within the city of nine gates*, neither acting nor causing work for others.
* The body of nine gates—two eyes, two nostrils, two ears, mouth, anus, and genital.
न कर्त्तृत्वं न कर्म्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः ।<br />न कर्म्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्त्तते ॥१४॥
na kartṛtvaṁ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ<br />na karma-phala-saṁyogaṁ svabhāvas tu pravartate [14]
<span class="e2">prabhuḥ</span>–The Lord; <span class="e2">na sṛjati</span>–does not generate; <span class="e2">lokasya</span>–anyone’s; <span class="e2">kartṛtvam</span>–ego of considering themselves ‘the doer’; <span class="e2">na karmāni</span>–nor their actions; <span class="e2">na karma-phala-saṁyogam</span>–nor their association with the fruits of actions; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">svabhāvaḥ</span>–their nature (of ignorance since time immemorial); <span class="e2">pravartate</span>–initiates these. [14]
14 The Lord does not generate anyone’s ego of considering themselves ‘the doer’, nor their actions, nor their association with the fruits of their actions. These are all a result of their external nature of ignorance since time immemorial.
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः ।<br />अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥१५॥
nādatte kasyachit pāpaṁ na chaiva sukṛtaṁ vibhuḥ<br />ajñānenāvṛtaṁ jñānaṁ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ [15]
<span class="e2">vibhuḥ</span>–The self-satisfied Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">ādatte</span>–accepts; <span class="e2">na pāpam</span>–neither the sin; <span class="e2">sukṛtam cha na eva</span>–nor the piety; <span class="e2">kasyachit</span>–of anyone. <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–Knowledge; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–is; <span class="e2">āvṛtam</span>–covered; <span class="e2">ajñānena</span>–by ignorance—by the Lord’s external potency (avidyā-śakti), to fulfill the living being’s desire to enjoy the material world; <span class="e2">tena</span>–thus; <span class="e2">jantavaḥ</span>–the living beings (though spiritual in constitution); <span class="e2">muhyanti</span>–are deluded, thinking the body to be the self. [15]
15 The Supreme Lord accepts neither the sin nor the piety of anyone. The living beings fall into illusion because their knowledge is covered by ignorance.
ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः ।<br />तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥१६॥
jñānena tu tad ajñānaṁ yeṣāṁ nāśitam ātmanaḥ<br />teṣām ādityavaj jñānaṁ prakāśayati tat param [16]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But; <span class="e2">yeṣām</span>–of those for whom; <span class="e2">tat ajñānam</span>–that ignorance; <span class="e2">nāśitam</span>–has been destroyed; <span class="e2">ātmanaḥ jñānena</span>–by self-knowledge, by the Lord’s superior potency; <span class="e2">tat jñānam</span>–that knowledge; <span class="e2">teṣām</span>–of those persons; <span class="e2">prakāśayati</span>–reveals; <span class="e2">param</span>–the Supreme Reality; <span class="e2">ādityavat</span>–like the sun that dispels darkness. [16]
16 For persons whose divine knowledge has awakened, their ignorance is destroyed, and their wisdom, like the shining sun, reveals the Supreme Reality.
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः ।<br />गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥१७॥
tad-buddhayas tad-ātmānas tan-niṣṭhās tat-parāyaṇāḥ<br />gachchhanty apunar-āvṛttiṁ jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣāḥ [17]
<span class="e2">jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣāḥ</span>–Persons whose ignorance has been destroyed by knowledge; <span class="e2">tat-buddhayaḥ</span>–who think constantly of the Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">tat-ātmānaḥ</span>–who meditate on Him alone; <span class="e2">tat-niṣṭhāḥ</span>–who abide in Him always; <span class="e2">tat-parāyaṇāḥ</span>–and who are devoted to hearing and singing His glories; (<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–being so engaged; <span class="e2">gachchhanti</span>–they attain; <span class="e2">apunaḥ-āvṛttim</span>–liberation. [17]
17 Those whose illusion has been completely dispelled by knowledge always think of Me, the Supreme Lord; I am their meditation, and they abide in Me alone, hearing and singing My unending glories in pure devotion. Thus, they are liberated from the mundane.
विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि ।<br />शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥१८॥
vidyā-vinaya-sampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini<br />śuni chaiva śvapāke cha paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ [18]
<span class="e2">sama-darśinaḥ eva</span>–Those who see with equanimity, who see Brahma, transcendence; <span class="e2">vidyā-vinaya-sampanne</span>–in a learned and humble; <span class="e2">brāhmaṇe</span>–brāhmaṇ; <span class="e2">gavi</span>–a cow; <span class="e2">hastini</span>–an elephant; <span class="e2">śuni cha</span>–and a dog; <span class="e2">śvapake cha</span>–or a chaṇḍāl (dog-eater or outcast); (<span class="e2">kathyate</span>)–(such seers) are to be known as; <span class="e2">paṇḍitāḥ</span>–truly learned. [18]
18 The enlightened souls see transcendence within all living beings, whether the humble and learned brāhmaṇ, the cow, the elephant, the dog, or the dog-eater. Therefore, they are to be known as paṇḍit—men of true wisdom.
इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः ।<br />निर्द्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥१९॥
ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣāṁ sāmye sthitaṁ manaḥ<br />nirdoṣaṁ hi samaṁ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ [19]
<span class="e2">yeṣām</span>–For those whose; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–mind; <span class="e2">sthitam</span>–is situated; <span class="e2">sāmye</span>–equipoised in Brahma; <span class="e2">sargaḥ</span>–the cycle of birth and death; <span class="e2">jitaḥ</span>–is conquered; <span class="e2">taiḥ</span>–by them; <span class="e2">eva iha</span>–while living within this world. <span class="e2">brahma samam hi</span>–Possessing spiritual equanimity; <span class="e2">nirdoṣam</span>–and being faultless (free from attachment and hatred); <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–thus; <span class="e2">te</span>–they; <span class="e2">brahmaṇi sthitāḥ</span>–are situated in Brahma. [19]
19 Those whose minds are equipoised in Brahma have conquered the cycle of birth and death while living within this world. By their perfect spiritual equanimity, they are always situated in transcendence.
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् ।<br />स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥२०॥
na prahṛṣyet priyaṁ prāpya nodvijet prāpya chāpriyam<br />sthira-buddhir asammūḍho brahma-vid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ [20]
<span class="e2">brahmaṇi sthitāḥ</span>–Fully situated in Brahma; <span class="e2">sthira-buddhiḥ</span>–endowed with steady intelligence; <span class="e2">asammūdhaḥ</span>–devoid of the delusion of considering one’s body and its attachments as ‘me’ and ‘mine’; <span class="e2">brahma-vit</span>–one in knowledge of Brahma; <span class="e2">na prahṛṣyet</span>–is neither elated; <span class="e2">priyam prāpya</span>–by obtaining something desirable; <span class="e2">na cha udvijet</span>–nor dejected; <span class="e2">apriyam prāpya</span>–by obtaining something undesirable. [20]
20 Absorbed in transcendence, endowed with steady intelligence, and free from the delusion of thinking of the body and associated objects as ‘me’ and ‘mine,’ the knower of the Absolute is neither happy when pleasant things come his way nor sad when unpleasant things come his way.
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् ।<br />स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥२१॥
bāhya-sparśeṣv asaktātmā vindaty ātmani yat sukham<br />sa brahma-yoga-yuktātmā sukham akṣayam aśnute [21]
<span class="e2">asakta-ātmā</span>–The person with mind detached; <span class="e2">bāhya-sparśeṣu</span>–from external (sense-) enjoyment; (<span class="e2">adau</span>)–first; <span class="e2">vindati</span>–tastes; (<span class="e2">tat</span>)<span class="e2"> sukham</span>–that happiness; <span class="e2">yat ātmani </span>(<span class="e2">anubhūyamāne</span>)–which is experienced in self-realisation; (<span class="e2">tataḥ</span>)–then; <span class="e2">brahma-yoga-yukta-ātmā</span>–absorbing himself in meditation on the Absolute; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a person; <span class="e2">aśnute</span>–enjoys; <span class="e2">akṣayam</span>–inexhaustible; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–bliss. [21]
21 Detaching his mind from external pleasures, such a knower of the Absolute Truth tastes the inner joy of self-realisation. Then, absorbing himself in meditation on the Absolute, he experiences inexhaustible bliss.
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते ।<br />आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥२२॥
ye hi saṁsparśajā bhogā duḥkha-yonaya eva te<br />ādy-antavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ [22]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">ye bhogāḥ</span>–those pleasures; <span class="e2">saṁsparśa-jāḥ</span>–born of the senses contacting their objects; te <span class="e2">duḥkha-yonayaḥ eva</span>–are the origin of misery; <span class="e2">hi</span>–as; <span class="e2">ādi-antavantaḥ</span>–they begin and end. (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–Therefore; <span class="e2">budhaḥ</span>–the wise person; <span class="e2">na ramate</span>–does not delight; <span class="e2">teṣu</span>–in them. [22]
22 O son of Kuntī, the pleasures that arise from the contact of the senses with their objects are the cause of unhappiness, as they are transient. The wise never delight in such pleasures.
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् ।<br />कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥२३॥
śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṁ prāk śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt<br />kāma-krodhodbhavaṁ vegaṁ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ [23]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; <span class="e2">śaknoti</span>–is able (by the yoga of selfless action); <span class="e2">soḍhum</span>–to check; <span class="e2">kāma-krodha-udbhavam vegam</span>–the impulses of desire and anger; <span class="e2">iha eva</span>–in this life; <span class="e2">prāk</span>–before; <span class="e2">śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt</span>–leaving the body; <span class="e2">saḥ naraḥ</span>–that person; <span class="e2">yuktaḥ</span>–is a yogī; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">sukhī</span>–is happy. [23]
23 Know that one who, before leaving the body, utilises the opportunity of this life to check the impulses of desire and anger—he is a yogī who knows true happiness.
योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः ।<br />स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्व्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥२४॥
yo ’ntaḥ-sukho ’ntar-ārāmas tathāntar-jyotir eva yaḥ<br />sa yogī brahma-nirvāṇaṁ brahma-bhūto ’dhigachchhati [24]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; <span class="e2">antaḥ-sukhaḥ</span>–experiences the joy of the self within; <span class="e2">antaḥ-ārāmaḥ</span>–who delights in the self within; <span class="e2">tathā yaḥ</span>–and who; <span class="e2">eva</span>–in this way; <span class="e2">antaḥ-jyotiḥ</span>–sees the illumination within; <span class="e2">saḥ yogī</span>–such a (niṣkām karma-) yogī (follower of the yoga of selfless action); <span class="e2">brahma-bhūtaḥ</span>–attaining the transcendental state; <span class="e2">adhigachchhati</span>–achieves; <span class="e2">brahma-nirvāṇam</span>–liberation in Brahma; in the personal conception, he reaches the Supersoul, Paramātmā. [24]
24 Such a yogī sees the self within and delights in the bliss of the self within. Attaining the transcendental state, he attains liberation from matter (and entry into the abode of Brahma).
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्व्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः ।<br />छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्व्वभूतहिते रताः ॥२५॥
labhante brahma-nirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ<br />chhinna-dvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarva-bhūta-hite-ratāḥ [25]
<span class="e2">kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ</span>–Sinless; <span class="e2">yata-ātmānaḥ</span>–self-controlled; <span class="e2">ṛṣayaḥ</span>–sages; <span class="e2">chinna-dvaidhāḥ</span>–with doubts destroyed; <span class="e2">sarva-bhūta-hite-ratāḥ</span>–dedicated to the welfare of all; <span class="e2">labhante</span>–attain; <span class="e2">brahma-nirvāṇam</span>–liberation from the mundane plane. [25]
25 Sinless, free from doubt, self-controlled, and dedicated to the welfare of all living beings, the seers of truth attain such liberation.
कामक्रोधविमुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् ।<br />अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्व्वाणं वर्त्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥२६॥
kāma-krodha-vimuktānāṁ yatīnāṁ yata-chetasām<br />abhito brahma-nirvāṇaṁ vartate viditātmanām [26]
<span class="e2">yatīnām</span>–Of the sannyāsīs; <span class="e2">yata-chetasām</span>–who have controlled their thoughts (conquered the subtle body); <span class="e2">vidita-ātmanām</span>–who are knowers of the element tvam, the soul; <span class="e2">kāma-krodha-vimuktānām</span>–and free from desire and anger; <span class="e2">brahma-nirvāṇam</span>–liberation from matter; <span class="e2">vartate</span>–occurs; <span class="e2">abhitaḥ</span>–either way, whether they live or die. [26]
26 Persons of the renounced order who have controlled their thoughts, who are free from desire and anger, and who have achieved knowledge of the nature of the soul, are liberated whether they live or die.
स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः ।<br />प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥२७॥
यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः ।<br />विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥२८॥
sparśān kṛtvā bahir bāhyāṁś chakṣuś chaivāntare bhruvoḥ<br />prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantara-chāriṇau [27]
yatendriya-mano-buddhir munir mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ<br />vigatechchhā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ [28]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–That person who; <span class="e2">bahiḥ kṛtvā</span>–expelling; <span class="e2">bāhyān sparśān</span>–external sense objects of sound, etc.; (<span class="e2">manaḥ praviṣṭān</span>)–which enter the mind; <span class="e2">cha eva </span>(<span class="e2">kṛtvā</span>)–and concentrating; <span class="e2">chakṣuḥ</span>–the eyes; <span class="e2">antare</span>–between; <span class="e2">bhruvoḥ</span>–the eyebrows; <span class="e2">kṛtvā samau</span>–stabilising; <span class="e2">prāṇa-apānau</span>–inhalation and exhalation; <span class="e2">nāsā-abhyantara-chāriṇau</span>–flowing through the nostrils; (<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>)–that person who; <span class="e2">yata-indriya-manaḥ-buddhiḥ</span>–is a controller of the senses, mind, and intelligence; <span class="e2">mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ</span>–dedicated to liberation; <span class="e2">vigata-ichchhā-bhaya-krodhaḥ</span>–free from desire, fear, and anger; <span class="e2">muniḥ</span>–a contemplative seeker of the self; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–is always; <span class="e2">mukta eva</span>–actually liberated. [27–28]
27–28 Expelling from the mind all the external sense objects of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell; centering the concentration and stabilising the incoming and outgoing breath; subjugating the senses, mind, and intelligence; dedicating himself to liberation; his desire, fear, and anger gone, such a sage is ever liberated.
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्व्वलोकमहेश्वरम् ।<br />सुहृदं सर्व्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥२९॥
bhoktāraṁ yajña-tapasāṁ sarva-loka-maheśvaram<br />suhṛdaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ jñātvā māṁ śāntim ṛchchhati [29]
(<span class="e2">jīvaḥ</span>)–The living being; <span class="e2">ṛchchhati</span>–attains; <span class="e2">śāntim</span>–the joy of his original divine identity; <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–by knowing; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me; <span class="e2">bhoktāram</span>–as the maintainer, or worshippable objective; <span class="e2">yajña-tapasām</span>–of the karmīs’ sacrifices and the jñānīs’ austerities; <span class="e2">sarva-loka-mahā-īśvaram</span>–the worshippable Supreme Lord of all planes—Lord Nārāyaṇ; <span class="e2">suhṛdam sarva-bhūtānām</span>–and the benefactor of all living beings by mercifully teaching pure devotion to Me, through My devotees, since I am the adorable friend of the devotees—Lord Kṛṣṇa. [29]
29 I am the enjoyer and objective of the sacrifices performed by persons of action, and of the austerities performed by persons of knowledge. I am Nārāyaṇ, the indwelling monitor of all planes of life, the worshippable Supreme Personality who awards liberation. I am Kṛṣṇa, the well-wisher of all and the dear friend of the devotees. One who knows Me thus, attains the bliss of knowing his own original divine identity.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे<br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे कर्म्मसन्न्यासयोगो नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः ॥५॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma-<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde karma-<br />sannyāsa-yogo nāma pañchamo ’dhyāyaḥ [5]
End of Chapter Five<br />The Path of Renunciation of Action<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

षष्ठोऽध्यायः
Chapter Six
Dhyāna-yoga <br />The Path of Meditation
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
अनाश्रितः कर्म्मफलं कार्य्यं कर्म्म करोति यः ।<br />स सन्न्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥१॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṁ kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ<br />sa sannyāsī cha yogī cha na niragnir na chākriyaḥ [1]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–That person who; <span class="e2">karoti</span>–performs; <span class="e2">kāryam</span>–compulsory; <span class="e2">karma</span>–scripturally enjoined actions; <span class="e2">anāśritaḥ</span>–without expectation; <span class="e2">karma-phalam</span>–of the fruits of action; <span class="e2">saḥ cha</span>–he is; <span class="e2">sannyāsī</span>–a sannyāsī, one who has given up all for the Lord; <span class="e2">yogī cha</span>–and he is a yogī, one in union with the Lord. <span class="e2">na niragniḥ</span>–A sannyāsī is not one who merely renounces the fire sacrifice (agnihotra yajña) and other prescribed duties; <span class="e2">na cha akriyaḥ</span>–nor is a yogī one who merely renounces physical activities. [1]
1 The Supreme Lord said: Know a genuine sannyāsī and yogī as one who, without expectation of the fruits of his actions, performs his duties as prescribed by the scriptures. One is not a sannyāsī merely by renouncing the performance of the fire sacrifice and other prescribed duties, and one is not a yogī merely by becoming physically inactive.
यं सन्न्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव ।<br />न ह्यसन्न्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥२॥
yaṁ sannyāsam iti prāhur yogaṁ taṁ viddhi pāṇḍava<br />na hy asannyasta-saṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaśchana [2]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pāṇḍavaḥ</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">yam</span>–that which; (<span class="e2">sudhiyaḥ</span>)–the learned; <span class="e2">prāhuḥ</span>–call; <span class="e2">sannyāsam iti</span>–sannyās, complete renunciation; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–you should know; <span class="e2">tam </span>(<span class="e2">eva</span>)<span class="e2"> yogam</span>–as yoga; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; <span class="e2">asannyasta-saṅkalpaḥ</span>–without renunciation of fruitive attachment (the basis of niṣkām karma-yoga); <span class="e2">na kaśchana</span>–no one; <span class="e2">bhavati</span>–can be; <span class="e2">yogī</span>–a yogī. [2]
2 O Arjuna, that which is known as sannyās (complete renunciation) you should know to be yoga, since without renouncing fruitive desire no one can be a yogī.
आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म्म कारणमुच्यते ।<br />योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥३॥
ārurukṣor muner yogaṁ karma kāraṇam uchyate<br />yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇam uchyate [3]
<span class="e2">muneḥ</span>–For the yoga practitioner; <span class="e2">ārurukṣoḥ</span>–desirous of ascending; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–to steady yoga meditation; (<span class="e2">tad ārohe</span>)–in the ascent of yoga; <span class="e2">karma</span>–action; <span class="e2">uchyate</span>–is said; <span class="e2">kāraṇam</span>–to be the means. <span class="e2">tasya eva yoga-ārūḍhasya</span>–For that person accomplished in yoga, that is, when he has achieved meditation; <span class="e2">śamaḥ</span>–renunciation of all action; <span class="e2">uchyate</span>–is described; <span class="e2">kāraṇam</span>–as the means. [3]
3 For the yoga practitioner desirous of attaining steady yoga meditation, action is said to be the means. When he has achieved yoga meditation, renunciation of all action is said to be the means of remaining in meditation.
यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्म्मस्वनुषज्जते ।<br />सर्व्वसङ्कल्पसन्न्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥४॥
yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasv anuṣajjate<br />sarva-saṅkalpa-sannyāsī yogārūḍhas tadochyate [4]
<span class="e2">yadā hi</span>–When; (<span class="e2">yogī</span>)–the yoga practitioner; <span class="e2">na anuṣajjate</span>–does not become attached; <span class="e2">indriya-artheṣu</span>–to the objects of the senses—sound, touch, form, taste, and smell; <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">anuṣajjate</span>)<span class="e2"> karmasu </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and does not become attached to action in pursuit of their enjoyment; <span class="e2">sarva-saṅkalpa-sannyāsī </span>(<span class="e2">cha bhavati</span>)–and renounces all thoughts of enjoyment; <span class="e2">tadā</span>–then; <span class="e2">uchyate yoga-ārūḍhaḥ</span>–he is said to have attained to yoga. [4]
4 When the yoga practitioner does not become attached to the objects of the senses, and to any action in pursuit of their enjoyment, and renounces all thoughts of enjoyment, then he is said to have attained to yoga.
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।<br />आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥५॥
uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet<br />ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ [5]
<span class="e2">ātmānam</span>–The living being; <span class="e2">uddharet</span>–must be delivered from the bondage of the material world; <span class="e2">ātmanā</span>–by the (detached) mind; <span class="e2">ātmānam</span>–and the living being; <span class="e2">na avasādayet</span>–must not be made to fall down into the bondage of the material world; (<span class="e2">ātmanā</span>)–by the mind (enchanted by sense objects); <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; <span class="e2">ātmā eva</span>–this very mind; <span class="e2">bandhuḥ</span>–is the friend; <span class="e2">ātmānaḥ</span>–of the living being; <span class="e2">ātmā eva</span>–and this very mind; <span class="e2">ripuḥ</span>–is the enemy; <span class="e2">ātmānaḥ</span>–of the living being. [5]
5 One must elevate himself by the mind, not degrade himself by the mind; for the mind is sometimes the friend of the living being, and in another situation that very mind is his enemy.
बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनैवात्मात्मना जितः ।<br />अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्त्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥६॥
bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenaivātmātmanā jitaḥ<br />anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat [6]
<span class="e2">yena ātmanā</span>–For one by whom; <span class="e2">ātmā</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">jitaḥ</span>–has been subjugated; <span class="e2">tasya ātmānaḥ</span>–that person’s; <span class="e2">ātmā eva</span>–very mind; <span class="e2">bandhuḥ</span>–is a friend; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">anātmanaḥ</span>–for a person of uncontrolled mind; <span class="e2">ātmā eva</span>–that very mind; <span class="e2">varteta</span>–is engaged; <span class="e2">śatrutve</span>–in disservice; <span class="e2">śatruvat</span>–like an enemy. [6]
6 For one who has conquered the mind, his mind is his friend. For one unable to control the mind, his mind works against him like an enemy.
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः ।<br />शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥७॥
jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya param ātmā samāhitaḥ<br />śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ [7]
śīta-<span class="e2">uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu</span>–In cold and heat, happiness and unhappiness; <span class="e2">tathā māna-apamānayoḥ</span>–and in honour and dishonour; <span class="e2">ātmā</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">praśāntasya</span>–of the peaceful (without attraction and aversion); <span class="e2">jitātmanaḥ</span>–yogī who has conquered the mind; (<span class="e2">bhavet</span>)–is; <span class="e2">param samāhitaḥ</span>–in perfect samādhi. [7]
7 The yogī who has conquered the mind remains deeply absorbed in yogic trance, peaceful, and undisturbed by cold and heat, happiness and unhappiness, or honour and dishonour.
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः ।<br />युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्ट्राश्मकाञ्चनः ॥८॥
jñāna-vijñāna-tṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ<br />yukta ity uchyate yogī sama-loṣṭrāśma-kāñchanaḥ [8]
<span class="e2">yogī</span>–The yogī; <span class="e2">jñāna-vijñāna-tṛpta-ātmā</span>–satisfied in his heart by scriptural knowledge as well as realisation; <span class="e2">kūṭa-sthaḥ</span>–situated in the one unchanging spiritual nature; <span class="e2">vijita-indriyaḥ</span>–sense-controlled; <span class="e2">sama-loṣṭra-aśma-kāñchanaḥ</span>–and of equal vision for earth, stone, and gold; <span class="e2">uchyate</span>–is said; <span class="e2">yuktaḥ iti</span>–to have attained yoga. [8]
8 One who is always satisfied within by both knowledge and realisation, who is always fixed in his spiritual nature, who is sense-controlled, and who has the vision of equality for a clod of earth, a rock, or gold—it is said that such a person has attained yoga.
सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु ।<br />साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥९॥
suhṛn-mitrāry-udāsīna-madhyastha-dveṣya-bandhuṣu<br />sādhuṣv api cha pāpeṣu sama-buddhir viśiṣyate [9]
<span class="e2">sama-buddhiḥ</span>–One of equipoised intelligence; <span class="e2">suhṛt-mitra-ari-udāsīna-madhya-stha-dveṣya-bandhuṣu</span>–towards a well-wisher, a friend, an enemy, an indifferent person, a mediator, a hateful person, a relative; <span class="e2">sādhuṣu</span>–a saintly person; <span class="e2">pāpeṣu cha api</span>–and a sinner, too; <span class="e2">viśiṣyate</span>–such a yogī is well-qualified. [9]
9 Such an eminent yogī has the vision of equality towards a well-wisher, a friend, an enemy, an indifferent person, a mediator, a hateful person, a relative, a saint, and a sinner.
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः ।<br />एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥१०॥
yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānaṁ rahasi sthitaḥ<br />ekākī yata-chittātmā nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ [10]
<span class="e2">yogī</span>–The practising yogī; <span class="e2">sthitaḥ</span>–remaining; <span class="e2">ekākī</span>–alone; <span class="e2">rahasi</span>–in a solitary place; <span class="e2">yata-chitta-ātmā</span>–controlling mind and body; <span class="e2">nirāśīḥ</span>–desireless; <span class="e2">aparigrahaḥ</span>–without enjoyable objects or acquisition; <span class="e2">yuñjīta ātmānam</span>–must concentrate his mind; <span class="e2">satatam</span>–constantly. [10]
10 The yogī should constantly concentrate his mind by remaining alone in a solitary place, his mind and body controlled, free from desire and acquisition.
शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः ।<br />नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चेलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥११॥
तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः ।<br />उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥१२॥
śuchau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ<br />nāty-uchchhritaṁ nāti-nīchaṁ chelājina-kuśottaram [11]
tatraikāgraṁ manaḥ kṛtvā yata-chittendriya-kriyaḥ<br />upaviśyāsane yuñjyād yogam ātma-viśuddhaye [12]
<span class="e2">pratiṣṭhāpya</span>–Establishing; <span class="e2">ātmānaḥ</span>–his; <span class="e2">āsanam</span>–seat; <span class="e2">chela-ajina-kuśa-uttaram</span>–of Kuśa grass, deerskin, and cloth; <span class="e2">śuchau deśe</span>–in a clean place; <span class="e2">sthiram</span>–which is firm; <span class="e2">na ati-uchchhritam</span>–neither too high; <span class="e2">na ati-nīcham</span>–nor too low; <span class="e2">upaviśya</span>–sitting; <span class="e2">tatra āsane</span>–on that seat; <span class="e2">yata-chitta-indriya-kriyaḥ</span>–subjugating all mental and sensual activity; <span class="e2">kṛtvā</span>–making; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">eka-agram</span>–one-pointed; <span class="e2">yuñjyāt</span>–he should practise; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–samādhi; <span class="e2">ātma-viśuddhaye</span>–for self-purification, to attain spiritual realisation. [11–12]
11–12 In a clean place, not too high and not too low, the yogī should establish a firm seat of Kuśa grass, deerskin, and cloth. Then, sitting on that seat, subjugating all mental and sensual activity, with one-pointed concentration he should practise meditational trance in order to purify his heart.
समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः ।<br />सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥१३॥
प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः ।<br />मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥१४॥
samaṁ kāya-śiro-grīvaṁ dhārayann achalaṁ sthiraḥ<br />samprekṣya nāsikāgraṁ svaṁ diśaś chānavalokayan [13]
praśāntātmā vigata-bhīr brahmachāri-vrate sthitaḥ<br />manaḥ saṁyamya mach-chitto yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ [14]
<span class="e2">dhārayan</span>–Holding; <span class="e2">kāya-śiraḥ-grīvam</span>–the body, head, and neck; <span class="e2">samam</span>–straight; <span class="e2">achalam</span>–still; <span class="e2">sthiraḥ</span>–and poised; <span class="e2">samprekṣya</span>–gazing at; <span class="e2">svam nāsikā</span>–his nose; <span class="e2">agram</span>–at the top, between the eyes (centering the concentration); <span class="e2">cha anavalokayan</span>–not looking; <span class="e2">diśaḥ</span>–in all directions; <span class="e2">brahmachāri-vrate-sthitaḥ</span>–remaining fixed in spirituality (or celibacy); <span class="e2">praśānta-ātmā</span>–with a peaceful heart; <span class="e2">vigata-bhīḥ</span>–and fearless; <span class="e2">manaḥ saṁyamya</span>–subjugating the mind; <span class="e2">yuktaḥ</span>–the yogī; <span class="e2">mat-paraḥ</span>–devoted to Me; <span class="e2">āsīta</span>–should remain; <span class="e2">mat-chittaḥ</span>–absorbed in thought of Me. [13–14]
13–14 Soberly keeping his body, head, and neck straight and upright, poised, the yogī should fix his gaze at one point, as though between the eyes, without casting a glance in any direction. Tranquil, fearless, and reposed in the vow of celibacy, he should meditate on Me (as four-armed Viṣṇu), and devoting himself to Me, he should thus practise yoga.
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः ।<br />शान्तिं निर्व्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥१५॥
yuñjann evaṁ sadātmānaṁ yogī niyata-mānasaḥ<br />śāntiṁ nirvāṇa-paramāṁ mat-saṁsthām adhigachchhati [15]
<span class="e2">evam</span>–In this manner; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–constantly; <span class="e2">yuñjan ātmānam</span>–engaging the mind in yogic meditation; <span class="e2">yogī</span>–the yogī; <span class="e2">niyata-mānasaḥ</span>–of mind withdrawn from hankering for material enjoyment; <span class="e2">adhigachchhati</span>–attains to; <span class="e2">śāntim</span>–the peace; <span class="e2">nirvāṇa-paramām</span>–of emancipation by the destruction of material existence; <span class="e2">mat-saṁsthām</span>–(the peace) which abides in Me (in My non-differentiated Brahma effulgence [Śrīla Viśvanāth Chakravartī Ṭhākur.]). [15]
15 In this way, constantly absorbing his mind in meditation (dhyāna-yoga), the yogī who has ceased hankering for material enjoyment achieves the peace of liberation from mundanity, the peace which abides in Me (in my Brahma effulgence).
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः ।<br />न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्ज्जुन ॥१६॥
nāty-aśnatas tu yogo ’sti na chaikāntam anaśnataḥ<br />na chāti-svapna-śīlasya jāgrato naiva chārjuna [16]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">yogaḥ</span>–yoga, samādhi; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–is not; <span class="e2">ati-aśnataḥ tu</span>–for the overeater; <span class="e2">na cha</span>–nor; <span class="e2">ekāntam anaśnataḥ</span>–for the undereater; <span class="e2">na cha</span>–nor; <span class="e2">ati-svapna-śīlasya</span>–for one who oversleeps; <span class="e2">na cha</span>–nor; <span class="e2">eva jāgratah</span>–for one who remains awake excessively. [16]
16 O Arjuna, yoga cannot be practised by one who overeats, undereats, oversleeps, or undersleeps.
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्म्मसु ।<br />युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥१७॥
yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-cheṣṭasya karmasu<br />yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkha-hā [17]
<span class="e2">yukta-āhāra-vihārasya</span>–For the person whose eating and recreation are regulated; <span class="e2">yukta-cheṣṭasya-karmasu</span>–whose effort in works is regulated; <span class="e2">yukta-svapna-avabodhasya</span>–and whose sleeping and waking hours are in proper measure; <span class="e2">yogaḥ</span>–yoga; <span class="e2">bhavati</span>–is; <span class="e2">duḥka-hā</span>–a dispeller of suffering. [17]
17 For a person who eats, relaxes, and works in a regulated way, and who keeps regular hours in proper measure, his practice of yoga dispells all his suffering.
यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते ।<br />निःस्पृहः सर्व्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥१८॥
yadā viniyataṁ chittam ātmany evāvatiṣṭhate<br />niḥspṛhaḥ sarva-kāmebhyo yukta ity ucyate tadā [18]
<span class="e2">yadā</span>–When; <span class="e2">viniyatam</span>–the disciplined; <span class="e2">chittam</span>–heart; <span class="e2">avatiṣṭhate</span>–dwells; <span class="e2">ātmani eva</span>–in the soul alone; <span class="e2">tadā</span>–then; <span class="e2">niḥspṛhaḥ</span>–that person detached; <span class="e2">sarva-kāmebhyaḥ</span>–from all desires; <span class="e2">uchyate</span>–is described; <span class="e2">yuktaḥ iti</span>–as actually in yoga. [18]
18 When a yogī withdraws the mind from mundane thoughts and centres it unwaveringly in the self, then, free from mundane desires, he is said to be actually situated in yoga, or linked with the Absolute.
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।<br />योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥१९॥
yathā dīpo nivāta-stho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā<br />yogino yata-chittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ [19]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–As; <span class="e2">dīpaḥ</span>–a lamp-flame; <span class="e2">nivāta-sthaḥ</span>–in a windless place; <span class="e2">na iṅgate</span>–does not waver; <span class="e2">sā</span>–such; <span class="e2">upamā</span>–an analogy; <span class="e2">smṛtā</span>–is cited; <span class="e2">yoginaḥ</span>–of the yogī; <span class="e2">ātmanaḥ</span>–the soul-centred; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–yoga; <span class="e2">yuñjataḥ</span>–practitioner; <span class="e2">yata-chittasya</span>–of unwavering one-pointed mind. [19]
19 It is said, as a lamp-flame situated in a windless place does not waver, similarly, the mind of the yogī absorbed in the self never flickers in its concentration.
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया ।<br />यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥२०॥
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ।<br />वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥२१॥
यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः ।<br />यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥२२॥
तं विद्याद्दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् ।<br />स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्व्विण्ण चेतसा ॥२३॥
yatroparamate chittaṁ niruddhaṁ yoga-sevayā<br />yatra chaivātmanātmānaṁ paśyann ātmani tuṣyati [20]
sukham ātyantikaṁ yat tad buddhi-grāhyam atīndriyam<br />vetti yatra na chaivāyaṁ sthitaś chalati tattvataḥ [21]
yaṁ labdhvā chāparaṁ lābhaṁ manyate nādhikaṁ tataḥ<br />yasmin sthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vichālyate [22]
taṁ vidyād duḥkha-saṁyoga-viyogaṁ yoga-saṁjñitam<br />sa niśchayena yoktavyo yogo ’nirviṇṇa-chetasā [23]
<span class="e2">yatra</span>–That (samādhi) within which; <span class="e2">chittam</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">niruddham</span>–disciplined; <span class="e2">yoga-sevayā</span>–by yoga practice; <span class="e2">uparamate</span>–is tranquil (relieved from mundane association); <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yatra</span>–within which; <span class="e2">paśyan</span>–having observed; <span class="e2">ātmānam</span>–the Supersoul, Paramātmā; <span class="e2">ātmanā</span>–by the pure self of the same nature as the Supersoul; <span class="e2">tuṣyati</span>–one is satisfied; <span class="e2">ātmani eva</span>–only in Him; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and; <span class="e2">yatra</span>–by which; <span class="e2">ayam</span>–this yogī; <span class="e2">vetti tat</span>–experiences that; <span class="e2">ātyantikam</span>–constant; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–bliss; <span class="e2">ati-indriyam</span>–transcendental to the senses; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which is; <span class="e2">buddhi-grāhyam</span>–known by spiritual enlightenment; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">yatra</span>)<span class="e2"> sthitaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being situated within which; <span class="e2">na eva chalati</span>–one never deviates; <span class="e2">tattvataḥ</span>–from reality; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and; <span class="e2">yam labdhvā</span>–gaining which; <span class="e2">na manyate</span>–one does not consider; <span class="e2">aparam lābham</span>–any other attainment; <span class="e2">adhikam</span>–greater; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–than that; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yasmin sthitaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being situated within which; <span class="e2">na vichālyate</span>–one is not disturbed; <span class="e2">guruṇā duḥkhena api</span>–even by intense suffering; <span class="e2">vidyāt</span>–know; <span class="e2">tam</span>–that; <span class="e2">duḥkha-saṁyoga-viyogam</span>–state within which all association with unhappiness is severed; <span class="e2">yoga-saṁjñitam</span>–to be defined as yoga. <span class="e2">yoktavyah</span>–One should practise; <span class="e2">saḥ yogaḥ</span>–this yoga; <span class="e2">niśchayena</span>–with perseverance; <span class="e2">anirviṇṇa-chetasā</span>–and a heart that is never discouraged. [20–23]
20–23 The mind controlled by yoga practice is tranquil, pacified by detachment from mundane association. The yogī remains satisfied in the Lord alone, directly seeing the Supersoul through his purified consciousness. In his spiritual enlightenment, he tastes transcendental, eternal bliss. He never deviates from the reality. He considers that there is no greater gain in this world. He is undisturbed by even the worst suffering. Know that the attainment of such a state, in which all association with unhappiness is severed, is called yoga. Yoga must be practised with perseverance and a heart that is never discouraged.
सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्व्वानशेषतः ।<br />मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥२४॥
saṅkalpa-prabhavān kāmāṁs tyaktvā sarvān aśeṣataḥ<br />manasaivendriya-grāmaṁ viniyamya samantataḥ [24]
(<span class="e2">yoktavyaḥ</span>)–Such yoga must be practised; <span class="e2">tyaktvā</span>–giving up; <span class="e2">sarvān kāmān</span>–all desires; <span class="e2">saṅkalpa-prabhavān</span>–born of the thoughts; <span class="e2">aśeṣataḥ</span>–completely (including all impressions); <span class="e2">manasā eva</span>–and by the mind (with the vision of the futility of mundane enjoyment); <span class="e2">viniyamya</span>–withdrawing; <span class="e2">indriya-grāmam</span>–the group of senses; <span class="e2">samantataḥ</span>–from all material objects. [24]
24 To practise yoga one must abandon all thoughts that give rise to desires, and using the mind, withdraw the senses from all material objects.
शनैः शनैरुपरमेद्बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया ।<br />आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥२५॥
śanaiḥ śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛti-gṛhītayā<br />ātma-saṁsthaṁ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñchid api chintayet [25]
<span class="e2">buddhyā</span>–By means of the intelligence; <span class="e2">dhṛti-gṛhītayā</span>–controlled by the yogic practice of dhāraṇā; <span class="e2">manaḥ ātma-saṁstham kṛtvā</span>–completely steadying the mind within the self; <span class="e2">śanaiḥ śanaiḥ</span>–and gradually; <span class="e2">uparamet</span>–as the mind becomes tranquil; <span class="e2">na chintayet</span>–one should not think; <span class="e2">kiñchit api</span>–of anything else. [25]
25 By steadying the intelligence, one should gradually still the mind and focus it within the self alone.
यतो यतो निश्चलति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् ।<br />ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥२६॥
yato yato niśchalati manaś chañchalam asthiram<br />tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṁ nayet [26]
<span class="e2">yataḥ yataḥ</span>–Whatever objects; <span class="e2">chañchalam</span>–the fickle; <span class="e2">asthiram</span>–unsteady; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–mind; <span class="e2">niśchalati</span>–pursues; <span class="e2">etat</span>–this mind; <span class="e2">niyamya</span>–should be withdrawn; <span class="e2">tataḥ tataḥ</span>–from those objects; <span class="e2">vaśam nayet</span>–and should be subjugated; <span class="e2">ātmani eva</span>–within the self alone. [26]
26 The wavering and unsteady mind should be brought back from whatever mundane objects it pursues, and be held within the self alone.
प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् ।<br />उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥२७॥
praśānta-manasaṁ hy enaṁ yoginaṁ sukham uttamam<br />upaiti śānta-rajasaṁ brahma-bhūtam akalmaṣam [27]
<span class="e2">uttamam sukham</span>–The joy of self-realisation; <span class="e2">upaiti</span>–comes; <span class="e2">enam yoginam hi</span>–to such a yogī; <span class="e2">śānta-rajasam</span>–who is free from the action of the mode of passion; <span class="e2">praśānta-manasam</span>–of pacified heart; <span class="e2">akalmaṣam</span>–free from the defects of attachment, fear, and anger; <span class="e2">brahma-bhūtam</span>–and situated in the spiritual nature. [27]
27 The transcendental joy of self-realisation comes to the yogī whose passions are quieted, who is peacefulhearted, free from the defects of attachment, fear, and anger, and always situated in the spiritual nature.
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः ।<br />सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥२८॥
yuñjann evaṁ sadātmānaṁ yogī vigata-kalmaṣaḥ<br />sukhena brahma-saṁsparśam atyantaṁ sukham aśnute [28]
<span class="e2">evam</span>–In this way; <span class="e2">sadā yuñjan</span>–having constantly experienced by yoga; <span class="e2">ātmānam</span>–his own internal nature; <span class="e2">vigata-kalmaṣaḥ</span>–the clean-hearted; <span class="e2">yogī</span>–yogī; <span class="e2">sukhena</span>–easily; <span class="e2">aśnute</span>–attains; <span class="e2">atyantam sukham</span>–boundless, profound ecstasy; <span class="e2">brahma-saṁsparśam</span>–by contact with the divine; realisation of the Supersoul. [28]
28 Thus absorbed in self-realisation, the clean-hearted yogī easily attains the boundless ecstasy of contacting the divine. He realises the Supersoul. (Such yoga is of a devotional nature).
सर्व्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्व्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।<br />ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्व्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥२९॥
sarva-bhūta-stham ātmānaṁ sarva-bhūtāni chātmani<br />īkṣate yoga-yuktātmā sarvatra sama-darśanaḥ [29]
<span class="e2">yoga-yukta-ātmā</span>–The yogī who is united with Brahma, the Absolute, who realises himself as qualitatively identical with Brahma; <span class="e2">sarvatra sama-darśanaḥ</span>–and is a seer of the same spirituality everywhere; <span class="e2">īkṣate</span>–sees; <span class="e2">ātmānam</span>–the Supersoul; <span class="e2">sarva-bhūta-stham</span>–situated in all beings; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">sarva-bhūtāni</span>–all beings; (<span class="e2">sthitaḥ</span>)–situated; <span class="e2">ātmani</span>–in the Supersoul. [29]
29 His consciousness united with the Infinite, the master of yoga sees the universal spirituality. He sees the Supreme Soul within all beings, and all beings within the Supreme.
यो मां पश्यति सर्व्वत्र सर्व्वञ्च मयि पश्यति ।<br />तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥३०॥
yo māṁ paśyati sarvatra sarvañ cha mayi paśyati<br />tasyāhaṁ na praṇaśyāmi sa cha me na praṇaśyati [30]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–For one who; <span class="e2">paśyati</span>–sees; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me; <span class="e2">sarvatra</span>–everywhere, in all elements; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">paśyati</span>–sees; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–everything; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–in Me; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">na</span>–am never; <span class="e2">praṇaśyāmi</span>–unseen, lost; <span class="e2">tasya</span>–to him; <span class="e2">saḥ cha</span>–and he; <span class="e2">na</span>–is never; <span class="e2">praṇaśyati</span>–unseen, lost; <span class="e2">me</span>–to Me—he never fails to be conscious of Me. [30]
30 For one who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, I am never lost to him, and he is never lost to Me.
सर्व्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः ।<br />सर्व्वथा वर्त्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्त्तते ॥३१॥
sarva-bhūta-sthitaṁ yo māṁ bhajaty ekatvam āsthitaḥ<br />sarvathā vartamāno ’pi sa yogī mayi vartate [31]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–That yogī who; <span class="e2">āsthitaḥ</span>–taking shelter; <span class="e2">mām</span>–in Me; <span class="e2">ekatvam</span>–in My nondifferent form; <span class="e2">sarva-bhūta-sthitam</span>–situated in the heart of every being (as the Supersoul, My four-armed form measuring one prādeś, the distance between the thumb and forefinger); <span class="e2">bhajati </span>(<span class="e2">mām</span>)–worships Me with devotion (based on hearing, chanting, and remembering); <span class="e2">saḥ yogī</span>–such a yogī; <span class="e2">vartate</span>–abides; <span class="e2">mayi </span>(<span class="e2">eva</span>)–in Me alone; <span class="e2">varta-mānaḥ api</span>–although present; <span class="e2">sarvathā</span>–in all circumstances (whether engaged in the execution of scripturally prescribed duties or not). [31]
31 The yogī who takes shelter of Me and adores Me in My non-different form as the Supersoul situated within the heart of every living being, abides in Me in all circumstances.
आत्मौपम्येन सर्व्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥३२॥
ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṁ paśyati yo ’rjuna<br />sukhaṁ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṁ sa yogī paramo mataḥ [32]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who; <span class="e2">ātmā-aupamyena</span>–in comparison to himself; <span class="e2">paśyati</span>–sees; <span class="e2">sukham vā yadi vā duḥkham</span>–the happiness or unhappiness; <span class="e2">sarvatra</span>–of all living beings; <span class="e2">samam</span>–equal (to his own); <span class="e2">saḥ yogī</span>–such a yogī; <span class="e2">mataḥ</span>–in My opinion; <span class="e2">paramaḥ</span>–is the best. [32]
32 I consider the best of all yogīs to be the one who knows the happiness and unhappiness of all beings as his own.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन ।<br />एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥३३॥
arjuna uvācha
yo ’yaṁ yogas tvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana<br />etasyāhaṁ na paśyāmi chañchalatvāt sthitiṁ sthirām [33]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">madhusūdana</span>–O Madhusūdan; <span class="e2">ayam</span>–this; <span class="e2">yogaḥ</span>–yoga; <span class="e2">yaḥ proktaḥ</span>–that has been described; <span class="e2">tvayā</span>–by You; <span class="e2">sāmyena</span>–as equanimity: <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">na paśyāmi</span>–cannot conceive; <span class="e2">etasya</span>–its; <span class="e2">sthirām</span>–stable; <span class="e2">sthitim</span>–state; <span class="e2">chañchalatvāt</span>–due to the fickle nature; (<span class="e2">manasaḥ</span>)–of the mind. [33]
33 Arjuna said: O Madhusūdan, because of the fickle nature of the mind, I cannot conceive how one can maintain the equilibrium in yoga that You have described.
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् ।<br />तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥३४॥
chañchalaṁ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham<br />tasyāhaṁ nigrahaṁ manye vāyor iva suduṣkaram [34]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">hi</span>–for; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">chañchalam</span>–is naturally fickle; <span class="e2">pramāthi</span>–turbulent—disturbing the intelligence, body, and senses; <span class="e2">balavat</span>–powerful—uncontrollable by even the intelligence; <span class="e2">dṛḍham</span>–and obstinate. (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–Therefore; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">manye</span>–consider; <span class="e2">nigraham</span>–the control; <span class="e2">tasya</span>–of the mind; <span class="e2">suduṣkaram</span>–more difficult; <span class="e2">vayoḥ iva</span>–than (controlling) the wind. [34]
34 O Kṛṣṇa, the mind is fickle, turbulent, obstinate and very powerful. I consider controlling it to be more difficult than controlling the wind.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् ।<br />अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥३५॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
asaṁśayaṁ mahā-bāho mano durnigrahaṁ chalam<br />abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa cha gṛhyate [35]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">mahā-bāho</span>–O heroic Arjuna; <span class="e2">asaṁśayam</span>–undoubtedly; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">chalam</span>–is fickle; <span class="e2">durnigraham</span>–and extremely difficult to control; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">gṛhyate</span>–it is controlled; <span class="e2">abhyāsena</span>–by, under the guidance of a bona fide spiritual master, practice (of meditation on the Supreme Lord); <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">vairāgyena</span>–by detachment. [35]
35 The Supreme Lord said: O heroic Arjuna, undoubtedly the mind is fickle and extremely difficult to control. However, O son of Kuntī, it is possible by practice and detachment.
असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः ।<br />वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥३६॥
asaṁyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ<br />vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo ’vāptum upāyataḥ [36]
<span class="e2">yogaḥ</span>–Yoga; <span class="e2">duṣprāpaḥ</span>–is difficult to attain; <span class="e2">asaṁyata-ātmanā</span>–by a person of uncontrolled mind; <span class="e2">iti</span>–this is; <span class="e2">me</span>–My; <span class="e2">matiḥ</span>–opinion; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">yatatā</span>–one who strives; <span class="e2">vaśya-ātmanā</span>–to control the mind; <span class="e2">upāyataḥ</span>–by the appropriate method of arduous practice (sādhana); <span class="e2">avāptum śakyaḥ</span>–can attain to yoga. [36]
36 I consider that yoga is difficult to attain for the person of unrestrained mind. But one who strives to restrain the mind by the appropriate practice can succeed in yoga.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः ।<br />अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥३७॥
arjuna uvācha
ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāch chalita-mānasaḥ<br />aprāpya yoga-saṁsiddhiṁ kāṁ gatiṁ kṛṣṇa gachchhati [37]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">kām gatim gachchhati</span>–what is the fate of; <span class="e2">śraddhayā upetaḥ</span>–a person who engages in yoga practice due to his faith in yoga scriptures; <span class="e2">ayatiḥ</span>–yet is not diligent; <span class="e2">yogāt chalita-mānasaḥ</span>–and whose mind deviates from yoga (due to a lack of practice and abnegation); <span class="e2">aprāpya</span>–without achieving; <span class="e2">yoga-saṁsiddhim</span>–success in yoga? [37]
37 Arjuna said: O Kṛṣṇa, what is the destination of a person who, due to his faith in the scriptures, engages in yoga practice, but lacking perseverance, proper practice, and abnegation, is distracted by mundane inclinations and fails to succeed in yoga practice?
कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति ।<br />अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥३८॥
kachchin nobhaya-vibhraṣṭaś chhinnābhram iva naśyati<br />apratiṣṭho mahā-bāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi [38]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty hero; <span class="e2">kachchit na</span>–is it not that; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–such a person; <span class="e2">vimūḍhaḥ</span>–bewildered; <span class="e2">brahmaṇaḥ pathi</span>–on the path of attaining the Absolute; <span class="e2">apratiṣṭhaḥ</span>–shelterless; <span class="e2">ubhaya-vibhraṣṭaḥ</span>–and deviated from the paths of both karma and yoga; <span class="e2">naśyati</span>–is lost; <span class="e2">iva</span>–like; <span class="e2">chhinna-abhram</span>–a scattered cloud? [38]
38 O mighty hero, O Kṛṣṇa, having deviated from the yoga of attaining the Absolute, shelterless and fallen from the paths of both action and meditation, is not such a person utterly lost, like a scattered cloud?
एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः ।<br />त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥३९॥
etan me saṁśayaṁ kṛṣṇa chhettum arhasy aśeṣataḥ<br />tvad-anyaḥ saṁśayasyāsya chhettā na hy upapadyate [39]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You; <span class="e2">arhasi</span>–are able; <span class="e2">aśeṣataḥ chhettum</span>–to completely slash; <span class="e2">etat saṁśayam</span>–this doubt; <span class="e2">me</span>–of mine. <span class="e2">tvat anyaḥ</span>–Other than You; <span class="e2">chhettā</span>–a destroyer; <span class="e2">asya saṁśayasya</span>–of this doubt; <span class="e2">na hi upapadyate</span>–is not to be found. [39]
39 O Kṛṣṇa! No one but You can dispel this doubt of mine. Please mercifully slash it at the root.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते ।<br />न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥४०॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśas tasya vidyate<br />na hi kalyāṇa-kṛt kaśchid durgatiṁ tāta gachchhati [40]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">na vidyate</span>–there is no; <span class="e2">tasya vināśaḥ</span>–loss for him, he is not denied the happiness of the heavenly plane; <span class="e2">iha eva</span>–in this world; <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">vidyate</span>)–and there is no; (<span class="e2">tasya vināśaḥ</span>)–loss for him, he is not denied the chance of the fortune to see the Supersoul; <span class="e2">amutra</span>–in the next life, i.e. in the supramundane plane; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">tata</span>–O dear one; <span class="e2">kaśchit</span>–any; <span class="e2">kalyāṇa-kṛt</span>–person engaged in virtuous actions; <span class="e2">na gachchhati durgatim</span>–does not suffer an ill fate. [40]
40 The Supreme Lord said: O Arjuna, son of Kuntī, there is no loss for the unsuccessful yoga practitioner as he is not denied the happiness of the heavenly plane in this world, nor is he denied the chance of the fortune to see the Supersoul in the transcendental realm. This is so, O dear one, because a person who performs virtuous actions never suffers an ill fate.
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः ।<br />शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥४१॥
prāpya puṇya-kṛtāṁ lokān uṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ<br />śuchīnāṁ śrīmatāṁ gehe yoga-bhraṣṭo ’bhijāyate [41]
<span class="e2">prāpya</span>–Attaining to; <span class="e2">lokān</span>–the planes; <span class="e2">puṇya-kṛtam</span>–of the pious; <span class="e2">yoga-bhraṣṭaḥ</span>–the person fallen from (comparatively short) yoga practice; <span class="e2">uṣitvā</span>–residing; (<span class="e2">tatra</span>)–there; <span class="e2">śāśvatīḥ samāḥ</span>–for many years; <span class="e2">abhijāyate</span>–takes birth; <span class="e2">gehe</span>–in the home; <span class="e2">śrīmatām</span>–of noble, prosperous persons; <span class="e2">śuchīnām</span>–given to pure and honest practices. [41]
41 After residing for many years in all those heavenly planes that are attainable by the performers of great sacrifices such as the Aśvamedha, the unsuccessful yoga practitioner takes birth in the home of honourable, prosperous persons given to pure and honest practices.
अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् ।<br />एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥४२॥
athavā yoginām eva kule bhavati dhīmatām<br />etaddhi durlabhataraṁ loke janma yad īdṛśam [42]
<span class="e2">athavā eva</span>–Otherwise (after relatively longer yoga practice); <span class="e2">bhavati</span>–he is born; <span class="e2">kule</span>–in a lineage; <span class="e2">dhīmatām</span>–of teachers of yoga; <span class="e2">yoginām</span>–dedicated to yoga practice. <span class="e2">hi</span>–Certainly; <span class="e2">yat īdṛśam</span>–such; <span class="e2">janma</span>–a birth; <span class="e2">etat</span>–as this; <span class="e2">durlabhataram</span>–is more rarely attained; <span class="e2">loke</span>–in this world. [42]
42 Or he takes birth in the home or family of teachers of yoga, who are dedicated to yoga practice. Such a birth is more rarely attained in this world.
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्व्वदैहिकम् ।<br />यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥४३॥
tatra taṁ buddhi-saṁyogaṁ labhate paurva-daihikam<br />yatate cha tato bhūyaḥ saṁsiddhau kuru-nandana [43]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kuru-nandana</span>–O Arjuna, son of Kuru; <span class="e2">tatra</span>–in one of these situations; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–he; <span class="e2">labhate</span>–attains; <span class="e2">tam buddhi-saṁyogam</span>–that consciousness of the Supersoul; <span class="e2">paurva-daihikam</span>–of his previous life. <span class="e2">tataḥ cha</span>–Thereby; <span class="e2">yatate</span>–he strives; <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–again; <span class="e2">saṁsiddhau</span>–for spiritual success—to attain the darśan or transcendental vision of the Supersoul. [43]
43 O son of Kuru, within one of these situations, the wisdom he had attained in his previous life is revived, and he again strives for success.
पूर्व्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः ।<br />जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्त्तते ॥४४॥
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hy avaśo ’pi saḥ<br />jijñāsur api yogasya śabda-brahmātivartate [44]
<span class="e2">hi</span>–Since; <span class="e2">avaśaḥ api</span>–despite himself; <span class="e2">saḥ eva</span>–he; <span class="e2">hriyate</span>–is carried; <span class="e2">tena pūrva-abhyāsena</span>–by his practice of the previous life. <span class="e2">jijñāsuḥ api</span>–As a seeker; <span class="e2">yogasya</span>–of yoga; <span class="e2">ativartate</span>–he surpasses; <span class="e2">śabda-brahma</span>–(the fruitive rituals of) the Vedas. [44]
44 Despite himself, he is carried by the yoga practice of his previous life. In his search, he surpasses the fruitive rituals of the Vedas.
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः ।<br />अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥४५॥
prayatnād yatamānas tu yogī saṁśuddha-kilbiṣaḥ<br />aneka-janma-saṁsiddhas tato yāti parāṁ gatim [45]
<span class="e2">yogī tu</span>–The yogī; <span class="e2">yatamānaḥ</span>–striving harder; <span class="e2">prayatnāt</span>–than the previous attempt; <span class="e2">saṁśuddha-kilbiṣaḥ</span>–his consciousness cleansed of all worldly attachment; <span class="e2">aneka-janma-saṁsiddhaḥ</span>–gains the perfection of many lifetimes’ endeavours; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–and thereby; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–gains; <span class="e2">parām gatim</span>–liberation in the form of both self-realisation and Supersoul-realisation. [45]
45 Striving harder than before, the yogī’s consciousness is cleansed of all worldly attachment, and he achieves the fruit of many lifetimes of yoga practice—he attains the supreme destination.
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः ।<br />कर्म्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्ज्जुन ॥४६॥
tapasvibhyo ’dhiko yogī jñānibhyo ’pi mato ’dhikaḥ<br />karmibhyaś chādhiko yogī tasmād yogī bhavārjuna [46]
<span class="e2">yogī</span>–The yogī; <span class="e2">adhikaḥ</span>–is superior; <span class="e2">tapasvibhyaḥ</span>–to the performer of severe austerities (such as Chāndrāyaṇ); <span class="e2">adhikaḥ api</span>–and is also superior; <span class="e2">jñānibhyaḥ</span>–to the jñānī, the person of knowledge. <span class="e2">yogī</span>–The yogī; <span class="e2">adhikaḥ cha</span>–is also superior; <span class="e2">karmibhyaḥ</span>–to the karmī, person of action; (<span class="e2">iti me</span>)–this is My; <span class="e2">mataḥ</span>–consideration. <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–be; <span class="e2">yogī</span>–a yogī. [46]
46 The yogī is superior to persons engaged in severe austerities (such as the Chāndrāyaṇ vow), superior to the person of knowledge who worships Brahma, and superior to the person of action. Know this to be My conclusion. Therefore, O Arjuna, be a yogī.
योगिनामपि सर्व्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना ।<br />श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥४७॥
yoginām api sarveṣāṁ mad-gatenāntar-ātmanā<br />śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ [47]
<span class="e2">sarveṣām yoginām api</span>–Of all types of yogīs on the paths of karma, jñān, tapasyā, aṣṭāṅga-yoga, bhakti, etc.; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who; <span class="e2">śraddhāvān</span>–with firm faith in the holy scriptures which corroborate the superexcellence of devotion for Me; <span class="e2">antaḥ-ātmanā</span>–and with heart; <span class="e2">mat-gatena</span>–fully dedicated to Me; <span class="e2">bhajate mām</span>–renders service to Me by engaging in the devotional practices based on hearing and chanting My glories; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a devotee; <span class="e2">yuktatamaḥ</span>–is foremost. (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–This is; <span class="e2">me</span>–My; <span class="e2">mataḥ</span>–opinion. [47]
47 The best of all yogīs is the devotee who has full faith in the authoritative pure devotional scriptures, and who adores Me with all his heart, hearing and singing My divine glories, rendering all services unto Me. This is My opinion.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे ध्यानयोगो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः ॥६॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde<br />dhyāna-yogo nāma ṣaṣṭho ’dhyāyaḥ [6]
End of Chapter Six<br />The Path of Meditation<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

सप्तमोऽध्यायः
Chapter Seven
Jñāna-vijñāna-yoga <br />Knowledge and Realisation <br />of the Supreme
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः ।<br />असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥१॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
mayy āsakta-manāḥ pārtha yogaṁ yuñjan mad-āśrayaḥ<br />asaṁśayaṁ samagraṁ māṁ yathā jñāsyasi tach chhṛṇu [1]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">śṛṇu tat</span>–hear; <span class="e2">yathā</span>–how; <span class="e2">āsakta-manāḥ</span>–with mind attached; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–to Me, the Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">yuñjan yogam</span>–linking your consciousness with Me; <span class="e2">mat-āśrayaḥ</span>–taking refuge in Me alone (without any attempts of karma, etc.); <span class="e2">asaṁśayam</span>–without doubt; <span class="e2">jñāsyasi</span>–you will be able to know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me; <span class="e2">samagram</span>–in full—along with My abode, My opulences, and My associates. [1]
1 The Lord said: O Pārtha, hear from Me how, with mind attached to Me, the Supreme Lord, linking your consciousness with Me and taking refuge in Me alone, you will without doubt be able to know Me, My holy abode, My opulences, and My associates.
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ।<br />यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥२॥
jñānaṁ te ’haṁ sa-vijñānam idaṁ vakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ<br />yaj jñātvā neha bhūyo ’nyaj jñātavyam avaśiṣyate [2]
<span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">vakṣyāmi</span>–shall now describe; <span class="e2">aśeṣataḥ</span>–completely; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you; <span class="e2">idam jñānam</span>–this knowledge of My absolute power (aiśvaryamaya-jñān); <span class="e2">sa-vijñānam</span>–with the knowledge to be realised of My sweetness (mādhurya-anubhav); <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–again; <span class="e2">anyat</span>–any other; (<span class="e2">tava</span>)<span class="e2"> jñātavyam</span>–thing to be known by you; <span class="e2">na avaśiṣyate</span>–will not remain; <span class="e2">iha</span>–on this supreme path. [2]
2 Now I shall reveal to you this knowledge of My absolute power as well as the realisation of My sweetness, knowing which, nothing will remain to be known, here on this supreme path.
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये ।<br />यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥३॥
manuṣyāṇāṁ sahasreṣu kaśchid yatati siddhaye<br />yatatām api siddhānāṁ kaśchin māṁ vetti tattvataḥ [3]
<span class="e2">manuṣyāṇām sahasreṣu</span>–Of thousands of men; <span class="e2">kaśchit</span>–a rare one; <span class="e2">yatati</span>–endeavours; <span class="e2">siddhaye</span>–for self-realisation and Supersoul-realisation; <span class="e2">yatatām siddhānām api</span>–and of thousands who have attained such realisation; <span class="e2">kaśchit</span>–a rare one; <span class="e2">tattvataḥ</span>–truly; <span class="e2">vetti</span>–knows; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me, Śyāmasundar. [3]
3 Of countless souls, few reach the human form; of thousands of human beings, very few may try to realise the soul and the Supersoul; and of thousands who have attained such realisation, hardly one can actually know Me, Śyāmasundar.
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च ।<br />अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥४॥
bhūmir āpo ’nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhir eva cha<br />ahaṅkāra itīyaṁ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā [4]
<span class="e2">bhūmiḥ</span>–Earth; <span class="e2">āpaḥ</span>–water; <span class="e2">analaḥ</span>–fire; <span class="e2">vāyuḥ</span>–air; <span class="e2">kham</span>–ether; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–mind; <span class="e2">buddhiḥ</span>–intelligence; <span class="e2">ahaṅkāraḥ eva cha</span>–and ego; <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus; <span class="e2">iyam</span>–this; <span class="e2">prakṛtiḥ</span>–nature, māyā-śakti, illusory potency; <span class="e2">me</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">bhinnā</span>–is divided; <span class="e2">aṣṭa-dhā</span>–eightfold. [4]
4 Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intelligence, and ego are the eight divisions of My illusory potency in this world.
Commentary
In this verse, it is expressed that jñān, or knowledge, in the true sense of the word and in accordance with the precepts of devotion, is actually Bhagavad-aiśvarya-jñān, or knowledge of the supremacy of the Lord. The general seekers of knowledge may consider realisation of the soul—as distinct from the body and material elements—to be enlightenment, but this does not constitute ultimate knowledge.
Thus, to explain the conception of His Lordship, the Lord reveals His forms, His potencies, and their characteristics: “My different aspects are Brahma, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān. Brahma is a non-differentiated, formless aspect of My potency. Paramātmā, the Supersoul, is also an appearance of My potency (in relation to the cosmic manifestation), and this aspect of Mine is not eternally manifest. Only My form of Bhagavān, the Supreme Lord, is My eternal Self, and in this form My three eternal potencies exist as antaraṅgā- or chit-śhakti—the internal, divine potency; bahiraṅgā- or māyā-śakti—the external, illusory potency; and taṭasthā- or jīva-śakti—the marginal potency comprising the innumerable living beings.”
In this verse, the Lord has described His external, illusory potency.
—Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् ।<br />जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्य्यते जगत् ॥५॥
apareyam itas tv anyāṁ prakṛtiṁ viddhi me parām<br />jīva-bhūtāṁ mahā-bāho yayedaṁ dhāryate jagat [5]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty hero; <span class="e2">iyam</span>–this external nature, external potency; <span class="e2">aparā</span>–is inferior; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">parām</span>–superior; <span class="e2">itaḥ</span>–to this; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–you should know; <span class="e2">anyām</span>–another; <span class="e2">prakṛtim</span>–nature, the marginal potency; <span class="e2">me</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">jīva-bhūtām</span>–in the form of the individual souls; <span class="e2">yayā</span>–the conscious potency by which; <span class="e2">idam jagat</span>–this world;<span class="e2"> dhāryate</span>–is adopted for enjoyment through fruitive actions. [5]
5 O mighty hero, Arjuna, this external, worldly nature is inferior. But know that superior to this nature is My marginal potency, comprised of the individual souls. Worldly existence is adopted by the souls for enjoyment through fruitive actions. (The divine world emanates from My internal potency and the mundane world from My external potency. The potency of the living beings is known as marginal as they are constitutionally situated midway between these planes. They may choose to reside either in the mundane plane or the divine.)
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्व्वाणीत्युपधारय ।<br />अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥६॥
etad yonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇīty upadhāraya<br />ahaṁ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā [6]
