<span class="e2">upadhāraya</span>–Understand; <span class="e2">iti</span>–that;<span class="e2"> sarvāṇi bhūtāni</span>–all living species, moving and stationary;<span class="e2"> etat yonīni</span>–are manifest from these two types of prakṛti, or natures, as kṣetra and kṣetrajña (vide 13.12).<span class="e2"> aham prabhavaḥ</span>–I am the source of manifestation;<span class="e2"> tathā pralayaḥ</span>–and dissolution;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnasya</span>–of the entire;<span class="e2"> jagataḥ</span>–universe. [6]
6 Know that all species, either moving or stationary, are manifest from these two natures as the field of action and the knower of the field; and I alone am the cause of the manifestation and dissolution of the entire universe.
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय ।<br />मयि सर्व्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥७॥
mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñchid asti dhanañjaya<br />mayi sarvam idaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva [7]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dhanañjaya</span>–O Dhanañjaya, conqueror of riches;<span class="e2"> na anyat kiñchit</span>–nothing else; <span class="e2">asti</span>–is;<span class="e2"> parataram</span>–superior; <span class="e2">mattaḥ</span>–to Me.<span class="e2"> idam sarvam</span>–This whole world; <span class="e2">protam</span>–is threaded; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–in Me; <span class="e2">iva</span>–like;<span class="e2"> maṇi-gaṇāḥ</span>–gems; <span class="e2">sūtre</span>–strung on a thread. [7]
7 O Arjuna, there is nothing superior to Me. All existence depends on Me, like gems strung on a thread.
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्य्ययोः ।<br />प्रणवः सर्व्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥८॥
raso ’ham apsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśi-sūryayoḥ<br />praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṁ nṛṣu [8]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am present; <span class="e2">rasaḥ</span>–by My power as the essential taste; <span class="e2">apsu</span>–of water. (<span class="e2">aham asmi</span>)–I am present; <span class="e2">prabhā</span>–by My power of radiance;<span class="e2"> śaśi-sūryayoḥ</span>–in the moon and sun. (<span class="e2">aham asmi</span>)–I am present;<span class="e2"> sarva-vedeṣu</span>–in all the Vedas;<span class="e2"> praṇavaḥ</span>–as the origin of the Vedas, Oṁkār. (<span class="e2">aham asmi</span>)–I am present; <span class="e2">śabdaḥ</span>–as the element of sound; <span class="e2">khe</span>–in the ether. (<span class="e2">aham asmi</span>)–I am present;<span class="e2"> pauruṣaṁ</span>–as masculinity; <span class="e2">nṛṣu</span>–in men. [8]
8 O son of Kuntī, I am the taste of water, I am the radiance of the sun and the moon. I am Om, the fundamental vibration in all the Vedas, I am the sound in the ether, and I am the masculinity in men.
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्याञ्च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ ।<br />जीवनं सर्व्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥९॥
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāñ cha tejaś chāsmi vibhāvasau<br />jīvanaṁ sarva-bhūteṣu tapaś chāsmi tapasviṣu [9]
(<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I; <span class="e2">asmi</span>–am present;<span class="e2"> puṇyaḥ gandhaḥ</span>–as the unmixed fragrance;<span class="e2"> pṛthivyām cha</span>–in the earth;<span class="e2"> tejaḥ vibhāvasau cha</span>–and as the force of radiance and heat in fire; <span class="e2">asmi</span>–(I) am present;<span class="e2"> jīvanam</span>–as the life-span;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūteṣu</span>–of all beings; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–the power to endure duality, etc.;<span class="e2"> tapasviṣu</span>–in the performers of austerities. [9]
9 I am the pure fragrance of the earth, and I am the radiance of fire. I am the life-span of all beings, and in ascetics, I am the power to endure duality such as cold and heat.
बीजं मां सर्व्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् ।<br />बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥१०॥
bījaṁ māṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ viddhi pārtha sanātanam<br />buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham [10]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> sanātanam bījam</span>–as the eternal cause, known as pradhān;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtānām</span>–of all life-forms.<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am present;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–as the intelligence;<span class="e2"> buddhi-matām</span>–of the intelligent; <span class="e2">tejaḥ</span>–and as the prowess;<span class="e2"> tejasvinām</span>–of the bold. [10]
10 O Pārtha, know Me as the eternal, original cause of all life-forms. I am the intelligence of the intelligent, the power of the powerful.
बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्ज्जितम् ।<br />धर्म्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥११॥
balaṁ balavatāṁ chāhaṁ kāma-rāga-vivarjitam<br />dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo ’smi bharatarṣabha [11]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharatarṣabha</span>–O best of the dynasty of Bharat;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am present;<span class="e2"> bala-vatām</span>–for the strong; <span class="e2">balam</span>–as strength of sāttvika quality, or goodness, which enables one to execute his religious duties;<span class="e2"> kāma-rāga-vivarjitam</span>–without selfishness and attachment; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">aham asmi</span>)–I am present;<span class="e2"> bhūteṣu</span>–in the living beings; <span class="e2">kāmaḥ</span>–as the desire to procreate;<span class="e2"> dharma-aviruddhaḥ</span>–without crossing the universal principles of religion, i.e. to beget offspring only in one’s wife. [11]
11 O Arjuna, I am the strength of the strong, without selfishness and attachment; and I am the desire for procreation in the living beings which does not contravene the universal principles of religion.
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये ।<br />मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥१२॥
ye chaiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś cha ye<br />matta eveti tān viddhi na tv ahaṁ teṣu te mayi [12]
<span class="e2">ye ye bhāvāḥ eva</span>–Whatever exists;<span class="e2"> sāttvikāḥ</span>–of the nature of goodness;<span class="e2"> rājasāḥ cha</span>–and of the nature of passion;<span class="e2"> tāmasāḥ cha</span>–and of the nature of ignorance; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know; <span class="e2">tān </span>(<span class="e2">sarvān</span>)–all these; <span class="e2">iti</span>–as;<span class="e2"> mattaḥ eva</span>–manifest from Me alone. <span class="e2">aham na </span>(<span class="e2">varte</span>)–I do not reside; <span class="e2">teṣu</span>–within them; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">te </span>(<span class="e2">vartante</span>)<span class="e2"> mayi</span>–they are in Me. [12]
12 Furthermore, know that all things, of the nature of goodness, passion, and ignorance, are manifest from Me alone. Nevertheless, I am not in them. They, subordinate to Me, are in Me.
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्व्वमिदं जगत् ।<br />मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥१३॥
tribhir guṇamayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṁ jagat<br />mohitaṁ nābhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam [13]
<span class="e2">idam</span>–This; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–whole; <span class="e2">jagat</span>–living world;<span class="e2"> mohitam</span>–is deluded;<span class="e2"> ebhiḥ bhāvaiḥ tribhiḥ guṇamayaiḥ</span>–by this manifestation of the three modes of material nature. (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–Therefore;<span class="e2"> na abhijānāti</span>–no one knows; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me, Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> ebhyaḥ param</span>–who am transcendental to these modes;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–and immutable. [13]
13 The entire world of living beings is deluded by the three modes of material nature. Therefore, no one can know Me, the Supreme Lord, who am transcendental to these modes and immutable.
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया ।<br />मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥१४॥
daivī hy eṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā<br />mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te [14]
<span class="e2">eṣā</span>–This; <span class="e2">daivī</span>–supramundane (alluring); <span class="e2">māyā</span>–external potency; <span class="e2">mama</span>–of Mine;<span class="e2"> guṇa-mayī</span>–composed of the three modes of material nature; <span class="e2">hi</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> duratyayā</span>–is difficult to cross. (<span class="e2">tathāpi</span>)–However; <span class="e2">ye</span>–those who;<span class="e2"> prapadyante</span>–take shelter; <span class="e2">mām eva</span>–in Me alone; <span class="e2">te</span>–they;<span class="e2"> taranti</span>–are able to cross; <span class="e2">etām</span>–this almost insurmountable; <span class="e2">māyām</span>–māyā, illusion. [14]
14 My alluring, ‘trimodal’, illusory potency is practically insurmountable. However, those who take shelter in Me can overcome this powerful obstacle.
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाःप्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः ।<br />माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥१५॥
na māṁ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ<br />māyayāpahṛta-jñānā āsuraṁ-bhāvam-āśritāḥ [15]
<span class="e2">duṣkṛtinaḥ</span>–These four kinds of wrongdoers or unfortunate persons;<span class="e2"> na prapadyante</span>–do not surrender; <span class="e2">mām</span>–to Me; <span class="e2">mūdhāḥ</span>–(1) the karmīs, or fruitive workers;<span class="e2"> nara-adhamāḥ</span>–(2) fallen persons, or those who take the path of devotion but later reject it, considering it inadequate or worthless;<span class="e2"> apahṛta-jñānāḥ</span>–(3) those whose knowledge is covered; <span class="e2">māyayā</span>–by māyā, illusion (despite their study of the scriptures, they consider that only the form of Lord Nārāyaṇ is worshippable, and that Lord Kṛṣṇa, Lord Rāma, and other factual forms of the Supreme are merely mortal);<span class="e2"> āsuram-bhāvam-āśritāḥ</span>–and (4) the demoniac (māyāvādīs, the impersonalists, who dismember My form by their arrows of false logic, resembling demons like Jarāsandha). [15]
15 These four kinds of wrongdoers do not surrender unto Me: fruitive workers, comparable to animals; fallen persons who take the highest path, devotion, but later reject it, considering it inadequate or worthless; those whose knowledge covered by illusion, Māyā (despite their scriptural study, they consider that only the form of Lord Nārāyaṇ is worshippable, and they think that Lord Kṛṣṇa, Lord Rāma and other factual forms are merely mortal); and the demoniac (impersonalists who dismember My form by their arrows of false logic, resembling demons like Jarāsandha).
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />आर्त्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥१६॥
chatur-vidhā bhajante māṁ janāḥ sukṛtino ’rjuna<br />ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī cha bharatarṣbha [16]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharatarṣabha</span>–O great scion of Bharat; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">ārtaḥ</span>–one suffering from disease or other afflictions;<span class="e2"> jijñāsuḥ</span>–one seeking scriptural knowledge or knowledge of the soul;<span class="e2"> artha-arthī</span>–one desiring earthly or heavenly happiness; cha and; <span class="e2">jñānī</span>–the purified knower of the soul; (<span class="e2">iti</span>)<span class="e2"> chatuḥ-vidhāḥ janāḥ</span>–these four kinds of persons; <span class="e2">sukṛtinaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–being fortunate—influenced by devotion for Me;<span class="e2"> bhajante mām</span>–worship Me (though their motives may be mixed with action or knowledge). [16]
16 O Arjuna, best of the Bhāratas, four kinds of persons have the fortune to worship Me: the afflicted, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of happiness, and the self-realised.
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते ।<br />प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥१७॥
teṣāṁ jñānī nitya-yukta eka-bhaktir viśiṣyate<br />priyo hi jñānino ’ty-artham ahaṁ sa cha mama priyaḥ [17]
<span class="e2">teṣām</span>–Among them; <span class="e2">jñānī</span>–the self-realised person;<span class="e2"> eka-bhaktiḥ</span>–My pure devotee;<span class="e2"> nityaḥ-yuktaḥ</span>–whose consciousness is completely absorbed in Me;<span class="e2"> viśiṣyate</span>–is the best. <span class="e2">hi</span>–For; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I, Śyāmasundar;<span class="e2"> ati-artham</span>–am very; <span class="e2">priyaḥ</span>–dear;<span class="e2"> jñāninaḥ</span>–to that enlightened soul;<span class="e2"> saḥ cha priyaḥ</span>–and he, too, is dear; <span class="e2">mama</span>–to Me. [17]
17 Of these four types of devotees, best is the self-realised person who is My pure devotee, and whose consciousness is fully absorbed in Me. For I, Śyāmasundar, am very dear to him, and he is dear to Me.
उदाराः सर्व्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् ।<br />आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥१८॥
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam<br />āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā mām evānuttamāṁ gatim [18]
<span class="e2">eva</span>–Certainly; <span class="e2">sarve</span>–all; <span class="e2">ete</span>–these persons are; <span class="e2">udārāḥ</span>–noble, unselfish souls dear to Me; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">jñānī</span>–the spiritually self-realised soul;<span class="e2"> ātmā eva</span>–is as dear to Me as My own self. (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–This is; <span class="e2">me</span>–My; <span class="e2">matam</span>–opinion; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; <span class="e2">yukta-ātmā eva </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–having fully dedicated his heart unto Me; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that jñānī;<span class="e2"> eva āsthitaḥ</span>–has fully determined; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me, Śyāmasundar;<span class="e2"> anuttamām</span>–as the supreme; <span class="e2">gatim</span>–goal.[18]
18 Certainly they are all noble souls, dear to Me, yet the spiritually self-realised soul is as beloved to Me as My own self, for he has given his heart to Me as his only shelter and ultimate goal of life.
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते ।<br />वासुदेवः सर्व्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥१९॥
bahūnāṁ janmanām ante jñānavān māṁ prapadyate<br />vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ [19]
<span class="e2">ante</span>–After;<span class="e2"> bahūnām</span>–many;<span class="e2"> janmanām</span>–births;<span class="e2"> jñānavān</span>–the enlightened person (by the fortune of sādhu-saṅga, devotional association); <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus realising; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–everything, the entire world of moving and stationary beings;<span class="e2"> vāsudevaḥ</span>–is of the nature of Vāsudev, Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> prapadyate</span>–he surrenders; <span class="e2">mām</span>–unto Me. <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–Such;<span class="e2"> mahātmā</span>–a great soul;<span class="e2"> su-durlabhaḥ</span>–is very rare. [19]
19 After many births, the enlightened soul (blessed with devotional association) realises that everything is of the nature of (subordinate to) Vāsudev, and thus he surrenders unto Me. Such a great soul is very rare.
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः ।<br />तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥२०॥
kāmais tais tair hṛta-jñānāḥ prapadyante ’nya-devatāḥ<br />taṁ taṁ niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā [20]
<span class="e2">hṛta-jñānāḥ</span>–Persons whose intelligence is misled;<span class="e2"> taiḥ taiḥ kāmaiḥ</span>–by particular worldly desires based on likes and dislikes; <span class="e2">niyatāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–being governed;<span class="e2"> svayā prakṛtyā</span>–by their own natures;<span class="e2"> prapadyante</span>–worship;<span class="e2"> anya-devatāḥ</span>–other godly personalities—the demigods—the sun-god, etc.;<span class="e2"> āsthāya</span>–after adopting; <span class="e2">tam tam</span>–the corresponding;<span class="e2"> niyamam</span>–rituals of fasting, etc. [20]
20 Persons misled by worldly desires, being governed by their own natures, worship other godly personalities like the sun-god and the many demigods, adopting the corresponding rituals to attain their objectives.
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्च्चितुमिच्छति ।<br />तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥२१॥
yo yo yāṁ yāṁ tanuṁ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārchitum ichchhati<br />tasya tasyāchalāṁ śraddhāṁ tām eva vidadhāmy aham [21]
<span class="e2">yām yām</span>–According to whichever; <span class="e2">tanum</span>–demigod, representing a form of Me; <span class="e2">yaḥ yaḥ</span>–a particular;<span class="e2"> bhaktaḥ</span>–devotee;<span class="e2"> ichchhati</span>–desires;<span class="e2"> architum śraddhayā</span>–to worship with faith; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I, as the Supersoul dwelling within his heart; <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> vidadhāmi</span>–ordain;<span class="e2"> achalām</span>–firm;<span class="e2"> śraddhām</span>–faith;<span class="e2"> tasya tasya</span>–in that particular devotee; <span class="e2">tām</span>–for that form. [21]
21 According to a person’s desire, as his faith grows to worship a particular demigod, I, as the Supersoul in his heart, make his faith strong in that demigod (representing a form of Me).
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते ।<br />लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् ॥२२॥
sa tayā śraddhayā yuktas tasyārādhanam īhate<br />labhate cha tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān hi tān [22]
<span class="e2">yuktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–Being linked;<span class="e2"> tayā śraddhayā</span>–with that firm faith; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that devotee; <span class="e2">īhate</span>–performs;<span class="e2"> ārādhanam</span>–worship; <span class="e2">tasyāḥ</span>–of that demigod’s deity; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">hi</span>– actually;<span class="e2"> vihitān</span>–arranged;<span class="e2"> mayā eva</span>–by Me alone, as the Supersoul of the demigod;<span class="e2"> labhate</span>–(the devotee) attains;<span class="e2"> tān kāmān</span>–his desired results; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–from that deity. [22]
22 His faith nourished by Me, such a devotee continues worshipping the deity of that demigod and attains all his desired objects from that deity. Again, this happens by My sanction alone, since I am the Supersoul, situated within the heart of the demigod, too.
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् ।<br />देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥२३॥
antavat tu phalaṁ teṣāṁ tad bhavaty alpa-medhasām<br />devān deva-yajo yānti mad-bhaktā yānti mām api [23]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But;<span class="e2"> tat phalam</span>–that fruit;<span class="e2"> teṣām alpa-medhasām</span>–of those unwise worshippers of the demigods;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–is;<span class="e2"> antavat</span>–temporary.<span class="e2"> deva-yajaḥ</span>–The worshippers of the demigods; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–reach; <span class="e2">devān</span>–the respective demigods;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktāḥ api</span>–and My devotees; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–reach; <span class="e2">māṁ</span>–Me. [23]
23 But the fruit obtained by those unwise worshippers of the demigods is temporary. They reach the gods they worship, but My devotees come to Me.
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः ।<br />परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥२४॥
avyaktaṁ vyaktim āpannaṁ manyante mām abuddhayaḥ<br />paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto mamāvyayam anuttamam [24]
<span class="e2">ajānantaḥ</span>–Not knowing; <span class="e2">mama</span>–My;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–eternal;<span class="e2"> anuttamam</span>–superexcellent; <span class="e2">param</span>–transcendental; <span class="e2">bhāvam</span>–<span class="e2">nature</span>–form, birth, qualities, activities, and Pastimes, etc.;<span class="e2"> abuddhayaḥ</span>–unwise persons;<span class="e2"> manyante</span>–think; <span class="e2">mām</span>–of Me;<span class="e2"> avyaktam</span>–as the impersonal or formless Brahma;<span class="e2"> āpannam</span>–which has accepted;<span class="e2"> vyaktim</span>–birth in Vasudev’s cell as an ordinary human being. [24]
24 My eternal superexcellent nature—My form, qualities, activities, and Pastimes—are all transcendental, but unwise persons cannot know the truth, and they think, “The formless Brahma took birth in Vasudev’s cell as an ordinary human being.”
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्व्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः ।<br />मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥२५॥
nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ<br />mūḍho ’yaṁ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam [25]
<span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">bhavāmi</span>)–am not;<span class="e2"> prakāśaḥ</span>–manifest;<span class="e2"> sarvasya</span>–to all;<span class="e2"> yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ</span>–being concealed by My yogamāyā potency; (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–therefore; <span class="e2">ayam</span>–these;<span class="e2"> mūḍhaḥ lokaḥ</span>–foolish persons;<span class="e2"> na abhijānāti</span>–cannot know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me, Śyāmasundar, the son of Vasudev; <span class="e2">ajam</span>–birthless;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–and immutable. [25]
25 By My sweet will, remaining concealed by My own potency, I am not manifest to anyone and everyone. So the foolish cannot know Me, the son of Vasudev, unborn and ever-existent in My divine Śyāmasundar form of beautiful feature like a blackish rain-cloud.
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्त्तमानानि चार्ज्जुन ।<br />भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥२६॥
vedāhaṁ samatītāni vartamānāni chārjuna<br />bhaviṣyāṇi cha bhūtāni māṁ tu veda na kaśchana [26]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">veda</span>–know;<span class="e2"> samatītāni</span>–all past;<span class="e2"> vartamānāni</span>–present;<span class="e2"> bhaviṣyāṇi cha</span>–and future;<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–mobile and immobile beings; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but;<span class="e2"> kaśchana</span>–anyone (either in this world or beyond it);<span class="e2"> na cha veda</span>–cannot know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me (due to their knowledge being covered by māyā and yogamāyā, My external illusory potency and the internal potency of My will). [26]
26 O Arjuna, I know all living beings of the past, present and future, but no one can know Me in truth.
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत ।<br />सर्व्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥२७॥
ichchhā-dveṣa-samutthena dvandva-mohena bhārata<br />sarva-bhūtāni sammohaṁ sarge yānti parantapa [27]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">bhārata </span>(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> parantapa</span>–O Arjuna, chastiser of the enemy; <span class="e2">sarge</span>–at the manifestation of the universe;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtāni</span>–all beings; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–become;<span class="e2"> sammoham</span>–deluded;<span class="e2"> dvandva-mohena</span>–by the illusion of duality;<span class="e2"> ichchhā-dveṣa-samutthena</span>–arising from likes and dislikes. [27]
27 O Arjuna, chastiser of the enemy, at the manifestation of the universe, all beings become deluded by duality based on likes and dislikes.
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्म्मणाम् ।<br />ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्म्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥२८॥
yeṣāṁ tv anta-gataṁ pāpaṁ janānāṁ puṇya-karmaṇām<br />te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā bhajante māṁ dṛḍha-vratāḥ [28]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But;<span class="e2"> janānām</span>–persons;<span class="e2"> puṇya-karmaṇām</span>–who are performers of virtuous deeds; <span class="e2">yeṣām</span>–whose; <span class="e2">pāpam</span>–sins;<span class="e2"> anta-gatam</span>–have been eradicated (by the fortune of association with My pure devotee); <span class="e2">te</span>–all such persons;<span class="e2"> dvandva-moha-nirmuktāḥ</span>–free from the illusion of duality;<span class="e2"> dṛḍha-vratāḥ</span>–and fixed in consciousness of Me;<span class="e2"> bhajante</span>–worship, serve; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me. [28]
28 But the performers of virtuous deeds are purified of all sin (by the fortune of association with My pure devotee). Thus freed from the illusion of duality, they worship Me with firm resolve.
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये ।<br />ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म्म चाखिलम् ॥२९॥
jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye<br />te brahma tad viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmaṁ karma chākhilam [29]
<span class="e2">ye</span>–Those who;<span class="e2"> yatanti</span>–strive;<span class="e2"> jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya</span>–for freedom from disease and death;<span class="e2"> āśritya</span>–taking shelter, placing their trust and devotion; <span class="e2">mām</span>–in Me; <span class="e2">te</span>–they; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–know;<span class="e2"> tat brahma</span>–that Brahma;<span class="e2"> adhyātmam</span>–the individual soul;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam</span>–in full; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> akhilam</span>–all; <span class="e2">karma</span>–the action by which the souls are bound to worldly existence. [29]
29 Those who strive for freedom from the world of disease and death, placing their trust and devotion in Me—they know Brahma, they know the soul, and they know karma, the action that binds the soul again and again to this mundane plane of suffering.
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञञ्च ये विदुः ।<br />प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥३०॥
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṁ māṁ sādhiyajñañ cha ye viduḥ<br />prayāṇa-kāle ’pi cha māṁ te vidur yukta-chetasaḥ [30]
<span class="e2">cha</span>–And; <span class="e2">ye</span>–those who; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> sa-adhibhūta-adhidaivam</span>–in relation to the worldly plane and to the celestial plane;<span class="e2"> sa-adhiyajñam cha</span>–and in relation to sacrifice; <span class="e2">te</span>–those persons;<span class="e2"> yukta-chetasaḥ</span>–of consciousness absorbed in Me; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> prayāṇa-kāle api</span>–even at the time of death. [30]
30 And those who know Me in relation to the worldly plane, the celestial plane, and the plane of sacrifice—such persons, their consciousness absorbed in Me, know Me even at the time of death. (Afflicted in the face of fearful death, they do not forget Me.)
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे<br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे ज्ञानविज्ञानयोगो नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः ॥७॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde jñāna-<br />vijñāna-yogo nāma saptamo ’dhyāyaḥ [7]
End of Chapter Seven<br />Knowledge and Realisation of the Supreme<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

अष्टमोऽध्यायः
Chapter Eight
Tāraka-brahma-yoga <br />The Merciful Absolute
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म्म पुरुषोत्तम ।<br />अधिभूतञ्च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥१॥
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन ।<br />प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥२॥
arjuna uvācha
kiṁ tad-brahma kim adhyātmaṁ kiṁ karma puruṣottama<br />adhibhūtañ cha kiṁ proktam adhidaivaṁ kim uchyate [1]
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṁ ko ’tra dehe ’smin madhusūdana<br />prayāṇa-kāle cha kathaṁ jñeyo ’si niyatātmabhiḥ [2]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> puruṣottama</span>–O Puruṣottam, Supreme Person; <span class="e2">kim</span>–what is; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–Brahma?<span class="e2"> adhyātmam kim</span>–What is adhyātma, the soul?<span class="e2"> karma kim</span>–What is karma, action? <span class="e2">cha</span>–And;<span class="e2"> kim proktam</span>–what is;<span class="e2"> adhibhūtam</span>–adhibhūta, the worldly plane? <span class="e2">kim </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–and what is;<span class="e2"> adhidaivam</span>–adhidaiva, the celestial plane? (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> madhusūdana</span>–O Madhusūdan;<span class="e2"> atra dehe</span>–within the body;<span class="e2"> kaḥ adhiyajñaḥ</span>–who or what is Adhiyajña, the agent of sacrifice? <span class="e2">katham</span>–How; (<span class="e2">sthitaḥ</span>)–is He present; <span class="e2">asmin </span>(<span class="e2">dehe</span>)–in this body?<span class="e2"> katham cha</span>–And how; (tvam)<span class="e2"> jñeyaḥ asi</span>–are You to be known;<span class="e2"> prayāṇa-kāle</span>–at the time of death;<span class="e2"> niyata-ātmabhiḥ</span>–by persons of controlled mind? [1–2]
1–2 Arjuna inquired: O Supreme Person, what is Brahma, and what is the soul? What is action, and what is the worldly plane? What is the celestial plane? O Madhusūdan: within the body, who is the agent of sacrifice, and how is He present? And how are You to be known by the self-controlled at the time of death?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
अक्षरं परमं ब्रह्म स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते ।<br />भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्म्मसंज्ञितः ॥३॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
akṣaraṁ paramaṁ brahma svabhāvo ’dhyātmam uchyate<br />bhūta-bhāvodbhava-karo visargaḥ karma-saṁjñitaḥ [3]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: <span class="e2">brahma</span>–Brahma;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–means;<span class="e2"> akṣaram paramam</span>–the imperishable Absolute.<span class="e2"> adhyātmam</span>–The individual soul; (<span class="e2">uchyate</span>)–refers to;<span class="e2"> svabhāvaḥ</span>–the pure spiritual nature. <span class="e2">karma</span>–Action;<span class="e2"> saṁjñitaḥ</span>–means;<span class="e2"> visargaḥ</span>–the creative force (or offerings to a demigod);<span class="e2"> bhūta-bhāva-udbhava-karaḥ</span>–which manifests the bodies of the human and other species of life through the agency of gross and subtle material elements. [3]
3 The Supreme Lord spoke thus: It is said that Brahma is the imperishable Absolute, and the soul is the living being’s own pure spiritual nature. By action is meant the creative force (or offerings by charity, sacrifice, and austerity, etc., to a demigod), manifesting, through the gross and subtle elements, the bodies of the human and other species of life.
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् ।<br />अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥४॥
adhibhūtaṁ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaś chādhidaivatam<br />adhiyajño ’ham evātra dehe deha-bhṛtāṁ vara [4]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> deha-bhṛtām vara</span>–O best of embodied beings, Arjuna;<span class="e2"> adhibhūtam</span>–worldly existence; <span class="e2">kṣaraḥ</span>–is the perishable; <span class="e2">bhāvaḥ</span>–existence.<span class="e2"> adhidaivatam</span>–Celestial existence;<span class="e2"> puruṣaḥ</span>–is the collective universal form, in which are contained the demigods, headed by the solar gods; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> aham eva</span>–I, indeed;<span class="e2"> atra dehe</span>–within this body;<span class="e2"> adhiyajñaḥ</span>–am the Lord of sacrifice in the form of the Supersoul, the sanctioner and rewarder of the (sacrificial etc.) actions of the living beings. [4]
4 O Arjuna, best of beings, the worldly plane means that which is perishable (such as the body). The celestial plane is the collective universal form which encompasses and governs the demigods; and I am the Lord of sacrifice, present as the Supersoul within the bodies of all living beings, as the sanctioner and rewarder of their actions (of sacrifices, etc.).
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् ।<br />यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥५॥
anta-kāle cha mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram<br />yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṁ yāti nāsty atra saṁśayaḥ [5]
<span class="e2">anta-kāle cha</span>–At the time of death; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who; <span class="e2">smaran</span>–thinks; <span class="e2">mām eva</span>–only of Me; <span class="e2">muktvā</span>–when leaving;<span class="e2"> kalevaram</span>–the body;<span class="e2"> prayāti</span>–departing this world; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–attains to;<span class="e2"> mat-bhāvam</span>–My nature. <span class="e2">na asti</span>–There is no;<span class="e2"> saṁśayaḥ</span>–doubt; <span class="e2">atra</span>–in this respect. [5]
5 One who thinks of Me at the time of death attains to My nature on departing this world. Of this there is no doubt.
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।<br />तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥६॥
yaṁ yaṁ vāpi smaran bhāvaṁ tyajaty ante kalevaram<br />taṁ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ [6]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī; (<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>)–one who;<span class="e2"> tyajati</span>–leaves;<span class="e2"> kalevaram</span>–the body; <span class="e2">smaran</span>–remembering;<span class="e2"> yam yam vā api</span>–whatever; <span class="e2">bhāvam</span>–object; <span class="e2">ante</span>–at the time of death; <span class="e2">eti</span>–he attains;<span class="e2"> tam tam eva</span>–to that very object;<span class="e2"> tat-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ</span>–having absorbed his mind in thought of it; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–constantly. [6]
6 O son of Kuntī, one who has always thought of a particular object will remember it and attain to it after leaving the body.
तस्मात्सर्व्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च ।<br />मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयः ॥७॥
tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya cha<br />mayy arpita-mano-buddhir mām evaiṣyasy asaṁśayaḥ [7]
<span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> anusmara</span>–remember; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu kāleṣu</span>–at all times; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yudhya</span>–fight, execute your natural duty.<span class="e2"> arpita-manaḥ-buddhiḥ</span>–Offering mind and intelligence; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–unto Me; <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">eṣyasi</span>–you will reach; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me.<span class="e2"> asaṁśayaḥ</span>–There is no doubt; (<span class="e2">atra</span>)–in this. [7]
7 Therefore always remembering Me, fight, as it is your natural duty. Thus dedicating your mind and intelligence to Me, you will reach Me. Of this there is no doubt.
अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना ।<br />परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥८॥
abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena chetasā nānya-gāminā<br />paramaṁ puruṣaṁ divyaṁ yāti pārthānuchintayan [8]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Pṛthā;<span class="e2"> anuchintayan</span>–thinking at every moment; <span class="e2">divyam</span>–of the effulgent;<span class="e2"> paramam puruṣam</span>–Supreme Person;<span class="e2"> na anya-gāminā chetasā</span>–by an undeviating mind;<span class="e2"> abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena</span>–engaged in yoga practice; (<span class="e2">yogī</span>)–the yogī; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–reaches; (<span class="e2">tam eva</span>)–that Supreme Person. [8]
8 O Pārtha, the yogī who practises meditation with an undeviating mind, always thinking of the effulgent Supreme Person, reaches Him.
कविं पुराणमनुशासितारम्<br />अणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः ।<br />सर्व्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपम्<br />आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥९।
प्रयाणकाले मनसाचले<br /> भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव ।<br />भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्<br />स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥१०॥
kaviṁ purāṇam anuśāsitāram<br />aṇor aṇīyāṁsam anusmared yaḥ<br />sarvasya dhātāram achintya-rūpam<br />āditya-varṇaṁ tamasaḥ parastāt [9]
prayāṇa-kāle manasāchalena<br />bhaktyā yukto yoga-balena chaiva<br />bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak<br />sa taṁ paraṁ puruṣam upaiti divyam [10]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who;<span class="e2"> prayāṇa-kāle</span>–at the time of death;<span class="e2"> achalena manasā</span>–with an unflickering mind;<span class="e2"> yoga-balena</span>–by strength of yoga practice;<span class="e2"> bhaktyā yuktaḥ</span>–being constantly engaged in smaraṇam, devotional remembrance;<span class="e2"> samyak āveśya cha</span>–and fully concentrating; <span class="e2">prāṇam</span>–the life-force;<span class="e2"> bhruvoḥ madhye</span>–between the eyebrows;<span class="e2"> anusmaret</span>–meditates on; (<span class="e2">param puruṣam</span>)–the Supreme Person; <span class="e2">kavim</span>–the all-knowing;<span class="e2"> purāṇam</span>–beginningless;<span class="e2"> anuśāsitāram</span>–merciful teacher of devotion unto Himself;<span class="e2"> aṇoḥ aṇīyāṁsam</span>–who is more subtle than the atom;<span class="e2"> sarvasya dhātāram</span>–(yet) the support of all existence;<span class="e2"> achintya-rūpam</span>–and of aprākṛta or supramundane form—medium-sized—of human feature;<span class="e2"> āditya-varṇam</span>–possessing a radiant form, which, like the sun, illuminates both Himself and others;<span class="e2"> tamasaḥ parastāt</span>–and is transcendental to material nature; <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that person; <span class="e2">upaiti</span>–reaches; <span class="e2">tam</span>–that; <span class="e2">divyam</span>–effulgent; <span class="e2">param</span>–Supreme;<span class="e2"> puruṣam</span>–Person. [9–10]
9–10 He, the Supreme Person, is the all-knowing, beginningless, merciful teacher of devotion unto Himself. Although more subtle that the atom, He is the infinite support of all existence. His form is supramundane, that is, of a humanlike feature, yet He is self-illuminating and all-illuminating like the sun. He is transcendental to illusion. One whose mind is fully focused by strength of yoga practice, who continuously remembers Him with devotion, and who at the time of death establishes the life-force between the eyebrows (at the ājñā-chakra) with full concentration, thinking of Him, reaches the effulgent Supreme Person.
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति<br />विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः ।<br />यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्य्यं चरन्ति<br />तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥११॥
yad akṣaraṁ veda-vido vadanti<br />viśanti yad yatayo vīta-rāgāḥ<br />yad ichchhanto brahmacharyaṁ charanti<br />tat te padaṁ saṅgraheṇa pravakṣye [11]
<span class="e2">saṅgraheṇa</span>–Along with the method of attaining it; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> pravakṣye</span>–shall describe; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you;<span class="e2"> tat padam</span>–that objective; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> veda-vidaḥ</span>–the learned knowers of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> vadanti</span>–call;<span class="e2"> akṣaram</span>–the imperishable, Oṁkār, denoting Brahma; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> vīta-rāgāḥ</span>–the desireless;<span class="e2"> yatayaḥ</span>–ascetics;<span class="e2"> viśanti</span>–enter;<span class="e2"> ichchhantaḥ</span>–and aspiring to reach; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; (<span class="e2">brahmachāriṇaḥ</span>)–the brahmachārīs, celibate seekers of the Absolute;<span class="e2"> charanti</span>–maintain;<span class="e2"> brahmacharyam</span>–the vow of celibacy. [11]
11 Along with the method of attaining it, I shall describe to you that objective which the learned knowers of the Vedas call Om, the Imperishable, within which the desireless ascetics enter, and which the devout seekers aspire to reach by practising the vow of celibacy.
सर्व्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।<br />मूर्ध्न्यधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् [१२]
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् ।<br />यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥१३॥
sarva-dvārāṇi saṁyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya cha<br />mūrdhny ādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yoga-dhāraṇām [12]
om ity ekākṣaraṁ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran<br />yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṁ sa yāti paramāṁ gatim [13]
<span class="e2">saṁyamya</span>–Controlling;<span class="e2"> sarva-dvārāṇi</span>–all the gateways of the senses—stopping them from accepting the objects of the senses;<span class="e2"> nirudhya</span>–steadying; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">hṛdi</span>–within the heart;<span class="e2"> ādhāya cha</span>–and establishing; <span class="e2">prāṇam</span>–the vital life-air;<span class="e2"> mūrdhni</span>–between the eyebrows;<span class="e2"> āsthitaḥ</span>–remaining;<span class="e2"> yoga-dhāraṇām</span>–in samādhi through the practice of dhāraṇā, yogic concentration;<span class="e2"> ātmanaḥ</span>–on the spiritual self;<span class="e2"> vyāharan</span>–and uttering; <span class="e2">oṁ iti</span>–thus, Om;<span class="e2"> eka-akṣaram</span>–the monosyllable; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–sound vibration of Brahma;<span class="e2"> anusmaran mām</span>–in full remembrance of Me; <span class="e2">saḥ yaḥ</span>–he who;<span class="e2"> deham tyajan</span>–leaving the body;<span class="e2"> prayāti</span>–thus departs; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> paramām gatim</span>–the supreme goal—the spiritual plane or sālokya-mukti. [12, 13]
12 , 13 Controlling all the gateways of the senses, holding the mind steady within the heart, establishing the life-force between the eyebrows, and fully absorbing the thoughts in the spiritual self, one who at the time of leaving the body vibrates the monosyllable Om and departs the world in consciousness of Me, reaches the transcendental world.
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः ।<br />तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥१४॥
ananya-chetāḥ satataṁ yo māṁ smarati nityaśaḥ<br />tasyāhaṁ sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ [14]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who;<span class="e2"> ananya-chetāḥ</span>–one-pointedly (without the practices of karma, jñān, etc., or without desiring their objectives of heaven, liberation, etc.);<span class="e2"> satatam</span>–in all circumstances;<span class="e2"> nityaśaḥ</span>–always;<span class="e2"> smarati</span>–remembers; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> tasya yoginaḥ</span>–for such a person in a relationship of dāsya, sakhya, etc.;<span class="e2"> nitya-yuktasya</span>–who constantly aspires for My divine association; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> sulabhaḥ</span>–am easily reached. [14]
14 O Pārtha, a person who one-pointedly remembers Me always, in all circumstances, and who, in his relationship with Me (in servitude, friendship, etc.) constantly aspires for My divine association—I am easily reached by such a devotee.
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् ।<br />नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥१५॥
mām upetya punar janma duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam<br />nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṁsiddhiṁ paramāṁ gatāḥ [15]
<span class="e2">mahātmānaḥ</span>–The great souls; <span class="e2">gatāḥ</span>–who have attained;<span class="e2"> paramām saṁsiddhim</span>–the highest perfection, My association in My Pastimes; <span class="e2">upetya</span>–having reached; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> na āpnuvanti</span>–do not take; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–again; <span class="e2">janma</span>–a birth;<span class="e2"> aśāśvatam</span>–of impermanence;<span class="e2"> duḥkhālayam</span>–which is the abode of suffering. [15]
15 The great souls who become My associates in My divine Pastimes, having reached Me, are never again born into transitory existence, which is the abode of suffering.
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्त्तिनोऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥१६॥
ābrahma-bhuvanāl lokāḥ punar āvartino ’rjuna<br />mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate [16]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> ābrahma-bhuvanāt</span>–from Brahmaloka, the highest plane in the universe, downwards; <span class="e2">lokāḥ</span>–all planes or their residents;<span class="e2"> punaḥ āvartinaḥ</span>–by nature repeatedly return; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> mām upetya</span>–reaching Me, attaining My shelter;<span class="e2"> na vidyate</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> punaḥ janma</span>–rebirth. [16]
16 O Arjuna, from the plane of Lord Brahmā downwards, all planes or their residents are subject to return. But, O Kaunteya, there is no rebirth after reaching Me.
सहस्रयुगपर्य्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः ।<br />रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥१७॥
sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ<br />rātriṁ yuga-sahasrāntāṁ te ’ho-rātra-vido janāḥ [17]
<span class="e2">te janāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">ye</span>)–Those who; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–know;<span class="e2"> brahmanaḥ</span>–Lord Brahmā’s; <span class="e2">ahaḥ</span>–day; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> sahasra-yuga-paryantam</span>–comprises the duration of one thousand chatur-yugas; <span class="e2">rātrim</span>–and (his) night;<span class="e2"> yuga-sahasra-antām</span>–of the duration of one thousand chatur-yugas;<span class="e2"> ahaḥ-rātra-vidaḥ</span>–are knowers of day and night. [17]
17 A day of Lord Brahmā lasts for one thousand chatur-yugas*, and his night is of the same duration. Persons who know this have the true conception of day and night.
* One yuga (age) in the time calculation of the demigods equals the four yugas or one chatur-yuga in the time calculation of man, or 4,320,000 years.
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्व्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे ।<br />रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥१८॥
avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanty ahar-āgame<br />rātry-āgame pralīyante tatraivāvyakta-saṁjñake [18]
<span class="e2">ahaḥ-āgame</span>–With the coming of (Lord Brahmā’s) day;<span class="e2"> sarvāḥ vyaktayaḥ</span>–universal progeny with their bodies, senses, enjoyable objects, and abodes;<span class="e2"> prabhavanti</span>–are born;<span class="e2"> avyaktāt</span>–of Lord Brahmā in his waking state; (<span class="e2">punaḥ</span>)–and again;<span class="e2"> rātri-āgame</span>–with the coming of night;<span class="e2"> pralīyante</span>–they are absorbed;<span class="e2"> tatra eva</span>–within Lord Brahmā;<span class="e2"> avyakta-saṁjñake</span>–who is known as avyakta, ‘the unmanifest.’ [18]
18 With the coming of day, the universal progeny with their bodies, senses, enjoyable objects, and abodes are born of Lord Brahmā in his waking state; and at nightfall, they are again absorbed into Lord Brahmā, who is known as ‘the unmanifest.’
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।<br />रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥१९।
bhūta-grāmaḥ sa evāyaṁ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate<br />rātry-āgame ’vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavaty ahar-āgame [19]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha; <span class="e2">avaśaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–helplessly; being subject to the law of karma;<span class="e2"> ayam saḥ eva bhūta-grāmaḥ</span>–the multitude of beings;<span class="e2"> bhūtvā bhūtvā</span>–being repeatedly born;<span class="e2"> ahaḥ-āgame</span>–with the coming of the day of Lord Brahmā;<span class="e2"> pralīyate</span>–disappear;<span class="e2"> rātri-āgame</span>–at nightfall;<span class="e2"> prabhavati</span>–and are born; (<span class="e2">punaḥ ahaḥ-āgame</span>)–with a new day. [19]
19 O Pārtha, the multitude of beings are helplessly (subject to the law of karma) born again and again. With the coming of Lord Brahmā’s night they are absorbed, and with the coming of his day they are again born.
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः ।<br />यः स सर्व्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥२०॥
paras tasmāt tu bhāvo ’nyo ’vyakto ’vyaktāt sanātanaḥ<br />yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati [20]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But; <span class="e2">paraḥ</span>–beyond, superior;<span class="e2"> tasmāt avyaktāt</span>–to this unmanifest Hiraṇyagarbha (‘born within the golden egg, the universe’), Lord Brahmā; (<span class="e2">asti</span>)–is; <span class="e2">anyaḥ</span>–another;<span class="e2"> avyaktaḥ</span>–unmanifest, imperceptible, transcendental;<span class="e2"> sanātanaḥ</span>–beginningless; <span class="e2">bhāvaḥ</span>–existence: <span class="e2">saḥ yaḥ</span>–He who;<span class="e2"> na vinaśyati</span>–is not destroyed;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu</span>–when all beings are destroyed. [20]
20 But superior to this unmanifest (Lord Brahmā) there is another unmanifest, and that existence is beginningless and transcendental to the perception of the living beings. He is not destroyed when all beings are destroyed.
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् ।<br />यं प्राप्य न निवर्त्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥२१॥
avyakto ’kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṁ gatim<br />yaṁ prāpya na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama [21]
(<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–He; <span class="e2">uktaḥ iti</span>–is said to be; <span class="e2">avyaktaḥ akṣaraḥ </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–the Unmanifest and the Invincible. (<span class="e2">vedāntāḥ</span>)–The Upaniṣads; <span class="e2">āhuḥ</span>–proclaim; <span class="e2">tam</span>–Him;<span class="e2"> paramām gatim</span>–the supreme destination;<span class="e2"> yam prāpya</span>–reaching whom; (<span class="e2">jīvāḥ</span>)–the living beings;<span class="e2"> na nivartate</span>–do not return. (<span class="e2">viddhi</span>)–Know; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that as; <span class="e2">mama</span>–My;<span class="e2"> paramam dhāma</span>–supreme abode. [21]
21 He is said to be the Unmanifest and the Invincible, proclaimed (by the Upaniṣads) to be the supreme goal, reaching whom one does not return to this world. Know that destination to be My supreme abode.
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया ।<br />यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्व्वमिदं ततम् ॥२२॥
puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyas tv ananyayā<br />yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṁ tatam [22]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> saḥ paraḥ puruṣaḥ</span>–the Supreme Person; <span class="e2">antaḥ</span>–within; <span class="e2">yasya</span>–whom;<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–all beings; <span class="e2">sthāni</span>–are situated; <span class="e2">yena</span>–and by whom; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–whole universe; <span class="e2">tatam</span>–is pervaded; <span class="e2">labhyaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">bhavāmi</span>)–am attainable;<span class="e2"> ananyayā bhaktyā tu</span>–only by exclusive devotion. [22]
22 O Pārtha, I, the Supreme Person, within whom all beings are situated and by whom this whole universe is pervaded, am attainable only by exclusive devotion.
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिञ्चैव योगिनः ।<br />प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥२३॥
yatra kāle tv anāvṛttim āvṛttiñ chaiva yoginaḥ<br />prayātā yānti taṁ kālaṁ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha [23]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharatarṣabha</span>–O Arjuna, best of the Bhāratas; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> vakṣyāmi</span>–shall now describe;<span class="e2"> tam kālam eva</span>–that moment;<span class="e2"> yatra kāle tu</span>–when;<span class="e2"> prayātāḥ</span>–death occurs;<span class="e2"> yoginaḥ</span>–the yogīs; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–attain;<span class="e2"> anāvṛttim</span>–liberation;<span class="e2"> āvṛttim cha</span>–or rebirth. [23]
23 O Bharatarṣabha, now I shall describe to you the circumstances in which the yogīs attain either liberation or rebirth at the moment of death.
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् ।<br />तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥२४॥
agnir jyotir ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā uttarāyaṇam<br />tatra prayātā gachchhanti brahma brahma-vido janāḥ [24]
(<span class="e2">yatra</span>)–The path on which;<span class="e2"> agniḥ jyotiḥ</span>–the deities of fire and light; <span class="e2">ahaḥ</span>–the deity of day; <span class="e2">suklaḥ</span>–the deity of the waxing moon;<span class="e2"> uttarāyaṇam ṣaṭ-māsāḥ</span>–and the deity of the sun’s six-monthly northern ascent; (<span class="e2">avasthitaḥ</span>)–preside;<span class="e2"> brahma-vidaḥ janāḥ</span>–the knowers of Brahma;<span class="e2"> prayātāḥ</span>–going, i.e. leaving the body; <span class="e2">tatra</span>–on that path;<span class="e2"> gachchhanti</span>–attain; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–Brahma. [24]
24 Upon leaving the body, the knowers of Brahma attain Brahma via the path of fire, light, day, the waxing moon, and the sun’s northern ascent.
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् ।<br />तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्त्तते ॥२५॥
dhūmo rātris tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā dakṣiṇāyanam<br />tatra chāndramasaṁ jyotir yogī prāpya nivartate [25]
(<span class="e2">yatra</span>)–The path on which; <span class="e2">dhūmaḥ</span>–the deity of smoke; <span class="e2">rātriḥ</span>–the deity of night; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇaḥ</span>–the deity of the waning moon;<span class="e2"> tathā ṣaṭ-māsāḥ dakṣiṇāyanam</span>–and the deity of the sun’s six-monthly southern ascent; (<span class="e2">avasthitaḥ</span>)–preside; <span class="e2">yogī</span>–the (karma-) yogī; (<span class="e2">prayātaḥ</span>)–who goes; <span class="e2">tatra</span>–on that path; <span class="e2">prāpya</span>–reaching;<span class="e2"> chāndramasam jyotiḥ</span>–Svarga-loka, the heavenly plane;<span class="e2"> nivartate</span>–<span class="e2">returns</span>–undergoes rebirth. [25]
25 Upon leaving the body, the karma-yogī reaches the heavenly plane via the path of smoke, night, the waning moon, and the sun’s southern ascent, but returns to undergo rebirth.
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।<br />एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्त्तते पुनः ॥२६॥
śukla-kṛṣṇe gatī hy ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate<br />ekayā yāty anāvṛttim anyayāvartate punaḥ [26]
<span class="e2">ete</span>–These;<span class="e2"> gatī śukla-kṛṣṇe</span>–two paths, bright and dark;<span class="e2"> jagataḥ</span>–of the world (where persons are apt to follow the paths of jñān and karma); <span class="e2">mate</span>–are considered;<span class="e2"> śāśvate hi</span>–perpetual. <span class="e2">ekayā</span>–By one;<span class="e2"> anāvṛttim</span>–liberation; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–is attained; <span class="e2">anyayā</span>–by the other;<span class="e2"> punaḥ āvartate</span>–one returns, is reborn. [26]
26 These two paths of the world, the bright and the dark, are accepted as being perpetual. By the bright path liberation is attained, and by the dark path one is reborn.
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन ।<br />तस्मात्सर्व्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्ज्जुन ॥२७॥
naite sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaśchana<br />tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yoga-yukto bhavārjuna [27]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha (Arjuna); <span class="e2">jānan</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">ete</span>–this; <span class="e2">sṛtī</span>–pair of paths;<span class="e2"> kaśchana yogī</span>–any (bhakti-) yogī (one engaged in the devotional service of the Lord);<span class="e2"> na muhyati</span>–is not deluded. <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu kāleṣu</span>–always; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–be;<span class="e2"> yoga-yuktaḥ</span>–engaged in yoga. [27]
27 O Pārtha, the devotee (bhakti-yogī) who knows these bright and dark paths is not deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, be ever fixed in transcendental, exclusive devotion.
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव<br />दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् ।<br />अत्येति तत्सर्व्वमिदं विदित्वा<br />योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥२८॥
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu chaiva<br />dāneṣu yat puṇya-phalaṁ pradiṣṭam<br />atyeti tat sarvam idaṁ viditvā<br />yogī paraṁ sthānam upaiti chādyam [28]
<span class="e2">viditvā</span>–Knowing; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this—My supremacy and the supremacy of My devotion; <span class="e2">yogī</span>–the yogī, the devoted soul; <span class="e2">atyeti</span>–transcends;<span class="e2"> tat sarvam puṇya-phalam</span>–all those fruits of piety; <span class="e2">vedeṣu</span>–achieved by chanting the Vedas;<span class="e2"> yajñeṣu</span>–performing sacrifice;<span class="e2"> tapaḥsu</span>–performing austerity;<span class="e2"> dāneṣu eva cha</span>–and performing charity; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> pradiṣṭam</span>–have been mentioned in the scriptures; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">upaiti</span>–attains; <span class="e2">param</span>–the supreme; <span class="e2">ādyam</span>–original;<span class="e2"> sthānam</span>–place. [28]
28 Thus knowing of My glories and the glories of devotion to Me, the devoted soul, surpassing the scripturally cited fruits of piety achieved by chanting the Vedas and performing sacrifice, austerity, and charity, attains My supreme, holy abode.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे तारकब्रह्मयोगो नामाष्टमोऽध्यायः ॥८॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde tāraka-<br />brahma-yogo nāmāṣṭamo ’dhyāyaḥ [8]
End of Chapter Eight<br />The Merciful Absolute<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

नवमोऽध्यायः
Chapter Nine
Rāja-guhya-yoga <br />The Hidden Treasure of Devotion
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे ।<br />ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥१॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
idaṁ tu te guhyatamaṁ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave<br />jñānaṁ vijñāna-sahitaṁ yaj jñātvā mokṣyase ’śubhāt [1]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> pravakṣyāmi</span>–I now tell; <span class="e2">te</span>–you;<span class="e2"> anasūyave</span>–who are without envy; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> guhyatamam</span>–most hidden; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge of pure devotion for Me (singing My glories which expands into unlimited services);<span class="e2"> vijñāna-sahitam tu</span>–up to direct realisation of Me; <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you;<span class="e2"> mokṣyase</span>–will be liberated;<span class="e2"> aśubhāt</span>–from inauspiciousness, or, from all that is opposed to devotion. [1]
1 The Supreme Lord said: I now reveal to you, who are without envy, this most hidden treasure of knowledge of pure devotion, with direct realisation of Me, knowing which you will be liberated from inauspiciousness—from all that is opposed to devotion.
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् ।<br />प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्म्यं सुसुखं कर्त्तुमव्ययम् ॥२॥
rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyaṁ pavitram idam uttamam<br />pratyakṣāvagamaṁ dharmyaṁ susukhaṁ kartum avyayam [2]
(<span class="e2">viddhi</span>)–Know; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> rāja-vidyā</span>–as the king of knowledge;<span class="e2"> rāja-guhyam</span>–the most secret of secrets;<span class="e2"> uttamam</span>–supreme;<span class="e2"> pavitram</span>–pure;<span class="e2"> pratyakṣa-avagamam</span>–attained by direct realisation;<span class="e2"> dharmyam</span>–the perfection of religion;<span class="e2"> kartum susukham</span>–very easy to practise; <span class="e2">avyayam </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and imperishable. [2]
2 Know this to be the king of secrets, the king of knowledge, supreme, pure, and imperishable. It is known by direct realisation (by one eager to serve Me), it is the perfection of religion, and very easy to practise.
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्म्मस्यास्य परन्तप ।<br />अप्राप्य मां निवर्त्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्त्मनि ॥३॥
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa<br />aprāpya māṁ nivartante mṛtyu-saṁsāra-vartmani [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> parantapa</span>–O conqueror of the enemy;<span class="e2"> puruṣāḥ</span>–persons;<span class="e2"> aśraddadhānāḥ</span>–lacking faith;<span class="e2"> asya dharmasya</span>–in this pure life of devotion for Me;<span class="e2"> aprāpya</span>–unable to reach; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> nivartante</span>–ever revolve;<span class="e2"> mṛtyu-saṁsāra-vartmani</span>–on the path of death in the material world. [3]
3 O conqueror of the enemy, men who have no faith in this hidden treasure of devotion to Me are unable to reach Me, and so they remain wandering on the path of death in the material world.
मया ततमिदं सर्व्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्त्तिना ।<br />मत्स्थानि सर्व्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥४॥
mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā<br />mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na chāhaṁ teṣv avasthitaḥ [4]
<span class="e2">idam</span>–This;<span class="e2"> sarvam jagat</span>–whole world; <span class="e2">tatam</span>–is pervaded; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me;<span class="e2"> avyakta-mūrtinā</span>–by My unmanifest form.<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtāni</span>–All beings;<span class="e2"> mat-sthāni</span>–are situated in Me, the infinite;<span class="e2"> aham cha</span>–but I;<span class="e2"> na avasthitaḥ</span>–am not situated; <span class="e2">teṣu</span>–in them. [4]
4 This entire universe is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest form, and all beings are situated in Me; yet I am not in them.
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ।<br />भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥५॥
na cha mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram<br />bhūta-bhṛn na cha bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ [5]
<span class="e2">bhūtāni na cha mat-sthāni</span>–Yet all beings are not situated in Me. <span class="e2">paśya</span>–Behold; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> aiśvaram yogam</span>–supreme mystical power. <span class="e2">mama</span>–My; <span class="e2">ātmā</span>–self;<span class="e2"> bhūta-bhṛt</span>–is the mainstay;<span class="e2"> bhūta-bhāvanaḥ cha</span>–and origin of all beings; (<span class="e2">kintu</span>)–yet;<span class="e2"> na bhūta-sthaḥ</span>–is not in them. [5]
5 Again, they are not in Me. Behold My supreme mystical power of inconceivable oneness and difference (achintya-bhedābheda). I, Myself, am the mainstay and origin of all beings, but I am not in them.
यथाकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्व्वत्रगो महान्<br />तथा सर्व्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥६॥
yathākāśa-sthito nityaṁ vāyuḥ sarvatra-go mahān<br />tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthānīty upadhāraya [6]
<span class="e2">upadhāraya</span>–Conceive; <span class="e2">iti</span>–in this way: <span class="e2">yathā</span>–as; <span class="e2">mahān</span>–the mighty; <span class="e2">vāyuḥ</span>–air or wind;<span class="e2"> sarvatra-gaḥ</span>–going everywhere; <span class="e2">nityam</span>–always;<span class="e2"> ākāśa-sthitaḥ</span>–rests in the sky; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–similarly;<span class="e2"> sarvāṇi bhūtāni</span>–all beings;<span class="e2"> mat-sthāni</span>–rest in Me. [6]
6 Know that as the mighty wind blowing everywhere rests always in the sky, similarly, all beings rest in Me.
सर्व्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् ।<br />कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥७॥
sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṁ yānti māmikām<br />kalpa-kṣaye punas tāni kalpādau visṛjāmy aham [7]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Kaunteya;<span class="e2"> kalpa-kṣaye</span>–at the millennium’s end;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtāni</span>–all beings; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–merge;<span class="e2"> māmikām prakṛtim</span>–in My trimodal material nature.<span class="e2"> kalpa-adau</span>–With a new day of Brahmā; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> visṛjāmi</span>–manifest; <span class="e2">tāni</span>–them; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–again. [7]
7 O son of Kuntī, at the end of the millennium, all beings are merged in the material nature of three modes, which is My external potency; and at the beginning of a new millennium, I make them manifest again.
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः ।<br />भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥८॥
prakṛtiṁ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ<br />bhūta-grāmam imaṁ kṛtsnam avaśaṁ prakṛter vaśāt [8]
<span class="e2">avaṣṭabhya</span>–Controlling;<span class="e2"> svām prakṛtim</span>–My trimodal nature; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> punaḥ punaḥ</span>–repeatedly;<span class="e2"> visṛjāmi</span>–manifest; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam</span>–entire;<span class="e2"> bhūta-grāmam</span>–multitude of beings; <span class="e2">avaśam</span>–who are helplessly;<span class="e2"> prakṛteḥ vaśāt</span>–controlled by their natures acquired through their previous actions. [8]
8 I control My potency of material nature, to repeatedly manifest the multitude of beings, who are helplessly controlled by their natures.
न च मां तानि कर्म्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ।<br />उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्म्मसु ॥९॥
na cha māṁ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya<br />udāsīnavad āsīnam asaktaṁ teṣu karmasu [9]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dhanañjaya</span>–O Dhanañjaya;<span class="e2"> tāni karmāṇi</span>–those actions of manifestation, sustenance, and withdrawal;<span class="e2"> na nibadhnanti</span>–cannot bind; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> asaktam</span>–who am detached;<span class="e2"> udāsīnavat āsīnam cha</span>–remaining as neutral;<span class="e2"> teṣu karmasu</span>–in those actions. [9]
9 O conqueror of wealth, I remain detached and situated as neutral in the cosmic manifestation, sustenance, and withdrawal, and these functions cannot bind Me.
मयाध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् ।<br />हेतुनानेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्त्तते ॥१०॥
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sa-charācharam<br />hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate [10]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> mayā adhyakṣeṇa</span>–ordained by Me;<span class="e2"> prakṛtiḥ</span>–My māyā potency; <span class="e2">sūyate</span>–produces; (<span class="e2">jagat</span>)–the universe;<span class="e2"> sa-chara-acharam</span>–with moving and stationary beings.<span class="e2"> anena hetunā</span>–By this cause; <span class="e2">jagat</span>–the universe;<span class="e2"> viparivartate</span>–is repeatedly manifest. [10]
10 O Kaunteya, ordained by Me, My illusory potency produces this universe of moving and stationary beings. Thus it is manifest over and over again.
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् ।<br />परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् ॥११॥
avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam<br />paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto mama bhūta-maheśvaram [11]
<span class="e2">ajānantaḥ</span>–Not knowing; <span class="e2">param</span>–the transcendental; <span class="e2">bhāvam</span>–nature, reality;<span class="e2"> mama āśritam mānuṣīm tanum</span>–of My form of human features; <span class="e2">mūḍhāḥ</span>–ignorant persons;<span class="e2"> avajānanti</span>–considering Me a mere mortal, blaspheme; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> bhūta-mahā-īśvaram</span>–the Supreme Lord of all beings. [11]
11 Not knowing the transcendental nature of My form of human features, ignorant persons blaspheme Me, the Supreme Lord of all beings, considering Me a mere mortal.
मोघाशा मोघकर्म्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः ।<br />राक्षसीमासुरीञ्चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥१२॥
moghāśā mogha-karmāṇo mogha-jñānā vichetasaḥ<br />rākṣasīm āsurīñ chaiva prakṛtiṁ mohinīṁ śritāḥ [12]
(<span class="e2">te</span>)–They; (<span class="e2">bhavanti</span>)–remain;<span class="e2"> mogha-āśāḥ</span>–with vain hopes;<span class="e2"> mogha-karmāṇaḥ</span>–vain actions;<span class="e2"> mogha-jñānāḥ</span>–vain knowledge; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and;<span class="e2"> vichetasaḥ</span>–vain thoughts; <span class="e2">śritāḥ</span>–adopting;<span class="e2"> rākṣasīm</span>–the ignorant;<span class="e2"> āsurīm cha</span>–and passionate, demoniac;<span class="e2"> prakṛtim eva</span>–nature;<span class="e2"> mohinīm</span>–causing their delusion, their downfall. [12]
12 Their hopes, acts, knowledge, and thoughts all in vain, such persons acquire the ignorant and demoniac nature, which leads to their downfall.
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः ।<br />भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् ॥१३॥
mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ<br />bhajanty ananya-manaso jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam [13]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Pṛthā, Arjuna;<span class="e2"> āśritāḥ</span>–taking refuge in;<span class="e2"> daivīm prakṛtim</span>–the godly nature;<span class="e2"> mahā-ātmānaḥ</span>–the great-hearted, the devoted souls; <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> bhūta-ādim</span>–as the origin of all that be; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–imperishable;<span class="e2"> bhajanti</span>–worship, adore; (<span class="e2">mām</span>)–Me;<span class="e2"> ananya-manasaḥ</span>–whole-heartedly. [13]
13 But, O Pārtha, the great-hearted souls take refuge in the divine nature, and they whole-heartedly worship and adore Me, knowing Me as the eternal origin of all.
सततं कीर्त्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः ।<br />नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ॥१४॥
satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ yatantaś cha dṛḍha-vratāḥ<br />namasyantaś cha māṁ bhaktyā nitya-yuktā upāsate [14]
<span class="e2">satatam</span>–At all times, in all places and circumstances;<span class="e2"> mām kīrtayantaḥ</span>–singing the glories of My divine Name, form, etc.;<span class="e2"> yatantaḥ</span>–striving to learn spiritual truths of My transcendental nature, personality, etc.;<span class="e2"> dṛḍha-vratāḥ cha</span>–and unfailingly following the devotional observances such as Ekādaśī and regular chanting of the Holy Name;<span class="e2"> namasyantaḥ cha</span>–offering obeisances unto Me and following all the practices of devotion; (<span class="e2">te</span>)–they;<span class="e2"> upāsate</span>–worship; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> bhaktyā</span>–with devotion;<span class="e2"> nitya-yuktāḥ</span>–earnestly aspiring for their eternal relationship with Me. [14]
14 They continually chant My glories, strive to learn spiritual truths about Me, and faithfully follow the devotional practices. Bowing to Me and worshipping Me with devotion, they aspire for their eternal relationship with Me.
ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते ।<br />एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् ॥१५॥
jñāna-yajñena chāpy anye yajanto mām upāsate<br />ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvato-mukham [15]
<span class="e2">api cha</span>–Also;<span class="e2"> jñāna-yajñena</span>–by performing the ‘knowledge-sacrifice’; <span class="e2">anye</span>–others, self-worshippers;<span class="e2"> yajantaḥ</span>–who offer oblations;<span class="e2"> mām upāsate</span>–worship Me;<span class="e2"> ekatvena</span>–conscious of oneness; (<span class="e2">anye cha</span>)–and others, external form-worshippers; (<span class="e2">mām upāsate</span>)–worship Me;<span class="e2"> pṛthaktvena</span>–Viṣṇu, but in the form of demigods, conscious of differentiation; (<span class="e2">anye cha</span>)–and yet others; (<span class="e2">mām upāsate</span>)–worship Me;<span class="e2"> bahudhā</span>–in many ways;<span class="e2"> viśvataḥ-mukham</span>–as the cosmic or universal form. [15]
15 Others perform the ‘knowledge-sacrifice’ and worship Me in oneness, others worship Me in differentiation, and yet others worship Me in a multitude of ways as the universal form.
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाहमहमौषधम् ।<br />मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥१६॥
ahaṁ kratur ahaṁ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣadham<br />mantro ’ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṁ hutam [16]
<span class="e2">aham kratuḥ</span>–I am the fire sacrifices Agniṣṭoma, Atyāgniṣṭoma, Uktha, Ṣoḍaśi, Atirātra, Aptoryāma and Vājapeya, collectively known as Jyotiṣṭoma;<span class="e2"> aham yajñaḥ</span>–I am the five types of sacrifices to demigod deities such as the Viśvadevas and others according to the smṛti scriptures;<span class="e2"> aham svadhā</span>–I am the obsequial oblation offered to the ancestors;<span class="e2"> aham auṣadham</span>–I am the food;<span class="e2"> aham mantraḥ</span>–I am the sacred incantation;<span class="e2"> aham ājyam</span>–I am the ghee (clarified butter) and other sacrificial ingredients;<span class="e2"> aham agniḥ</span>–I am the fire;<span class="e2"> aham hutam eva</span>–I am the act of offering. [16]
16 I am the Vedic Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice and the five sacrifices to the Viśvadeva demigods and others as enjoined in the smṛti scriptures. I am the oblation to the ancestors, the food, and the mantra. I am the sacrificial ingredients such as ghee, I am the consecrated fire, and I am the act of offering.
पिताहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः ।<br />वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक्साम यजुरेव च ॥१७॥
pitāham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ<br />vedyaṁ pavitram oṁkāra ṛk sāma yajur eva cha [17]
<span class="e2">aham pitā</span>–I am the father;<span class="e2"> asya jagataḥ</span>–of this universe; <span class="e2">mātā</span>–the mother; <span class="e2">dhātā</span>–the ordainer of the living beings’ fruits of actions;<span class="e2"> pitāmahaḥ</span>–the grandfather; <span class="e2">vedyam</span>–the object of all knowledge;<span class="e2"> pavitram oṁkāraḥ</span>–the purifying praṇava monosyllable; <span class="e2">ṛk</span>–the <span class="e3">Ṛg-veda</span>; <span class="e2">sāma</span>–<span class="e3">Sāma-veda</span>;<span class="e2"> yajuḥ eva cha</span>–and <span class="e3">Yajur-veda</span>. [17]
17 I am the father and the mother of the universe, the ordainer of the living beings’ fruits of actions, the forefather, and the object of all knowledge. I am the purifying Om, the <span class="e3">Ṛg-</span>, <span class="e3">Sāma-</span>, and <span class="e3">Yajur-vedas</span>.
गतिर्भर्त्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् ।<br />प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥१८॥
gatir bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṁ suhṛt<br />prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṁ nidhānaṁ bījam avyayam [18]
(<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">gatiḥ</span>–I am the fruit of action; <span class="e2">bhartā</span>–the maintainer;<span class="e2"> prabhuḥ</span>–the Lord; <span class="e2">sākṣī</span>–the witness;<span class="e2"> nivāsaḥ</span>–the refuge;<span class="e2"> śaraṇam</span>–the guardian; <span class="e2">suhṛt</span>–the true friend;<span class="e2"> prabhavaḥ</span>–the universal manifestation;<span class="e2"> pralayaḥ</span>–withdrawal;<span class="e2"> sthānam</span>–and sustenance;<span class="e2"> nidhānam</span>–the reservoir;<span class="e2"> avyayam bījam</span>–the imperishable seed. [18]
18 And I am the goal, the maintainer, master, witness, refuge, guardian, and true friend. I am the universal manifestation, sustenance, and withdrawal. I am the reservoir, I am the original seed, I am the imperishable Supreme Lord.
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च ।<br />अमृतञ्चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्ज्जुन ॥१९॥
tapāmy aham ahaṁ varṣaṁ nigṛhṇāmy utsṛjāmi cha<br />amṛtañ chaiva mṛtyuś cha sad asach chāham arjuna [19]
<span class="e2">cha</span>–And; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> aham tapāmi</span>–I give heat;<span class="e2"> aham utsṛjāmi</span>–I bring forth; <span class="e2">varṣam</span>–rain;<span class="e2"> nigṛhṇāmi cha</span>–and I withdraw it.<span class="e2"> aham eva amṛtam</span>–I am immortality;<span class="e2"> mṛtyuḥ cha</span>–and death; <span class="e2">sat</span>–truth;<span class="e2"> asat cha</span>–and untruth. [19]
19 O Arjuna, I give heat, and the rain comes and goes by My will. I am immortality and death. I am truth and untruth.
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा<br />यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते ।<br />ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोकम्<br />अश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥२०॥
trai-vidyā māṁ soma-pāḥ pūta-pāpā<br />yajñair iṣṭvā svar-gatiṁ prārthayante<br />te puṇyam āsādya surendra-lokam<br />aśnanti divyān divi deva-bhogān [20]
<span class="e2">trai-vidyāḥ</span>–Performers of the fruitive rituals of the <span class="e3">Ṛg-</span>, <span class="e3">Yajur-</span> and <span class="e3">Sāma-vedas</span>;<span class="e2"> soma-pāḥ</span>–who take the remnants of soma-rasa, a beverage made from the soma creeper, dear to the demigods;<span class="e2"> pūta-pāpāḥ</span>–and are purified of sin; <span class="e2">iṣṭvā</span>–having worshipped; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> yajñaiḥ</span>–by sacrifice, but indirectly through the demigods;<span class="e2"> prārthayante</span>–pray;<span class="e2"> svar-gatim</span>–to attain the heavenly plane, the abode of the demigods. <span class="e2">āsādya</span>–Reaching; <span class="e2">puṇyam</span>–in reward for their piety;<span class="e2"> sura-indra-lokam</span>–the plane of Indra, heaven;<span class="e2"> te aśnanti</span>–they enjoy; <span class="e2">divyān</span>–the exalted;<span class="e2"> deva-bhogān</span>–happiness of the demigods; <span class="e2">divi</span>–in heaven. [20]
20 Persons who perform the fruitive ritualistic sacrifices prescribed in three of the Vedas worship Indra and other demigods. In fact, they worship Me, but in an indirect way. They drink the sacrificial remnants of the soma beverage, purify themselves of sin, and pray to attain the heavenly plane. As the result of their piety, they reach heaven and enjoy celestial pleasures.
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं<br />क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्त्यलोकं विशन्ति ।<br />एवं त्रयीधर्म्ममनुप्रपन्न<br />गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥२१॥
te taṁ bhuktvā svarga-lokaṁ viśālaṁ<br />kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṁ viśanti<br />evaṁ trayī-dharmam anuprapannā<br />gatāgataṁ kāma-kāmā labhante [21]
<span class="e2">bhuktvā</span>–After enjoying; <span class="e2">tam</span>–that;<span class="e2"> viśālam</span>–vast;<span class="e2"> svarga-lokam</span>–heavenly plane;<span class="e2"> puṇye kṣīṇe</span>–with the exhaustion of their piety; <span class="e2">te</span>–they;<span class="e2"> viśanti</span>–enter;<span class="e2"> martya-lokam</span>–the human plane. <span class="e2">evam</span>–In this way;<span class="e2"> kāma-kāmāḥ</span>–those desiring enjoyment;<span class="e2"> anuprapannāḥ</span>–given to;<span class="e2"> trayī-dharmam</span>–the worship prescribed in three of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> labhante</span>–attain;<span class="e2"> gata-agatam</span>–coming and going in this world. [21]
21 After enjoying the vast heavenly plane, upon the exhaustion of their pious merits they return to the human plane. In this way, persons desiring enjoyment who follow the Vedic rituals for demigod worship come and go—they undergo repeated birth and death in this material world.
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्य्युपासते ।<br />तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥२२॥
ananyāś chintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate<br />teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham [22]
