<span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">vahāmi</span>–bear;<span class="e2"> yoga-kṣemam</span>–the responsibility of providing and protecting the necessities; <span class="e2">teṣām</span>–of those;<span class="e2"> nitya-abhiyuktānām</span>–who are exclusively devoted to Me;<span class="e2"> ye janāḥ</span>–and who;<span class="e2"> ananyāḥ</span>–exclusively;<span class="e2"> mām chintyantaḥ</span>–always think of Me;<span class="e2"> pari-upāsate</span>–and worship Me in all respects, every relationship. [22]
22 I bear the responsibility of acquiring and protecting the necessities of My fully dependent devotees who are always absorbed in thought of Me, and who worship Me in every way.
येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः ।<br />तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्व्वकम् ॥२३॥
ye ’py anya-devatā-bhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ<br />te ’pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhi-pūrvakam [23]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">ye</span>–those persons who;<span class="e2"> anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ api</span>–although devotees of ‘other gods’;<span class="e2"> yajante</span>–worship the demigods;<span class="e2"> śraddhayā-anvitāḥ</span>–with faith; <span class="e2">te api</span>–they too;<span class="e2"> yajanti</span>–worship; <span class="e2">mām eva</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> avidhi-pūrvakam</span>–but not in a way appropriate to attaining Me. [23]
23 O Kaunteya, the devotees of the demigods who have faith in worshipping them, are actually worshipping Me, but incorrectly.
अहं हि सर्व्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च ।<br />न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते ॥२४॥
ahaṁ hi sarva-yajñānāṁ bhoktā cha prabhur eva cha<br />na tu mām abhijānanti tattvenātaś chyavanti te [24]
<span class="e2">aham hi</span>–I alone am;<span class="e2"> bhoktā eva cha</span>–the enjoyer;<span class="e2"> prabhuḥ cha</span>–and the rewarder;<span class="e2"> sarva-yajñānām</span>–of all sacrifices; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but;<span class="e2"> na abhijānanti</span>–being ignorant; <span class="e2">mām</span>–of Me;<span class="e2"> tattvena</span>–in truth; <span class="e2">te</span>–they; <span class="e2">ataḥ</span>–therefore;<span class="e2"> chyavanti</span>–fall to take birth; (<span class="e2">punaḥ</span>)–again. [24]
24 I alone am the enjoyer and rewarder of all sacrifices, but being ignorant of My position, the demigod worshippers fall to take birth again.
यान्ति देवव्रता देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रताः ।<br />भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥२५॥
yānti deva-vratā devān pitṝn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ<br />bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti mad-yājino ’pi mām [25]
<span class="e2">deva-vratāḥ</span>–The demigod worshippers; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–reach; <span class="e2">devān</span>–the demigods;<span class="e2"> pitṛ-vratāḥ</span>–the ancestral worshippers; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–reach; <span class="e2">pitṝṇ</span>–their ancestors;<span class="e2"> bhūta-ijyāḥ</span>–the spirit worshippers; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–reach;<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–the spirits;<span class="e2"> mat-yājinaḥ</span>–My worshippers; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–reach; <span class="e2">mām api</span>–Me. [25]
25 The demigod worshippers reach the demigods, the forefather worshippers go to the plane of their ancestors, and the worshippers of the spirits go to the spirits. But those who worship Me come to Me.
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।<br />तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥२६॥
patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayachchhati<br />tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ [26]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–For one who;<span class="e2"> bhaktyā</span>–with devotion;<span class="e2"> prayachchhati</span>–offers; <span class="e2">me</span>–Me; <span class="e2">patram</span>–a leaf; <span class="e2">puṣpam</span>–a flower; <span class="e2">phalam</span>–fruit; <span class="e2">toyam</span>–water; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">aśnāmi</span>–partake of that—I affectionately accept; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> bhakti-upahṛtam</span>–devotional offering; (<span class="e2">tasya</span>)–of that person;<span class="e2"> prayata-ātmanaḥ</span>–of clean heart. [26]
26 If one offers Me with devotion a leaf, flower, fruit, or water, I affectionately accept that offering of the clean hearted devotee.
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् ।<br />यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥२७॥
yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi yaj juhoṣi dadāsi yat<br />yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam [27]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Arjuna, son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">yat </span>(<span class="e2">tvam</span>)<span class="e2"> karoṣi</span>–whatever you do, general or scripturally prescribed actions;<span class="e2"> yat aśnāsi</span>–whatever you eat;<span class="e2"> yat juhoṣi</span>–whatever you offer in sacrifice;<span class="e2"> yat dadāsi</span>–whatever you give in charity;<span class="e2"> yat tapasyasi</span>–and whichever austerity you perform or vow you keep;<span class="e2"> tat kuruṣva</span>–do that;<span class="e2"> mat-arpaṇam</span>–as an offering unto Me. [27]
27 O Kaunteya, whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give, and whatever vow you may keep—do everything as an offering unto Me.
शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्म्मबन्धनैः ।<br />सन्न्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि ॥२८॥
śubhāśubha-phalair evaṁ mokṣyase karma-bandhanaiḥ<br />sannyāsa-yoga-yuktātmā vimukto mām upaiṣyasi [28]
(<span class="e2">karma-kurvan</span>)–Acting; <span class="e2">evam</span>–in this way;<span class="e2"> mokṣyase</span>–you will be liberated;<span class="e2"> karma-bandhanaiḥ</span>–from bondage to action;<span class="e2"> śubha-aśubha-phalaiḥ</span>–and its auspicious or inauspicious results.<span class="e2"> sannyāsa-yoga-yukta-ātmā</span>–With mind linked to Me by renouncing the fruits of your actions; <span class="e2">vimuktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being perfectly liberated;<span class="e2"> mām upaiṣyasi</span>–you will reach Me. [28]
28 Acting thus, you will be freed from bondage to action and its auspicious or inauspicious results. With mind selflessly linked to Me, you will be perfectly liberated, and you will come to Me.
समोऽहं सर्व्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः ।<br />ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥२९॥
samo ’haṁ sarva-bhūteṣu na me dveṣyo ’sti na priyaḥ<br />ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu chāpy aham [29]
<span class="e2">aham samaḥ</span>–I am equal;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūteṣu</span>–to all beings; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–there is neither;<span class="e2"> dveṣyaḥ</span>–an enemy; <span class="e2">priyaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)<span class="e2"> na</span>–nor a friend; <span class="e2">me</span>–for Me;. <span class="e2">tu</span>–but;<span class="e2"> ye bhajanti</span>–whoever serves; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> bhaktyā</span>–with love; (<span class="e2">yathā</span>)–as; <span class="e2">te</span>–they; (<span class="e2">āsaktāḥ</span>)–are attached; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–to Me;<span class="e2"> aham api cha</span>–I, too; (<span class="e2">tathā āsaktiḥ</span>)–am similarly attached; <span class="e2">teṣu</span>–to them. [29]
29 I am equal to all, so no one is My enemy or My friend. Yet, for those who serve Me with love, as they are bound by affection for Me, I am similarly bound by the tie of affection for them.
अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् ।<br />साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥३०॥
api chet sudurāchāro bhajate mām ananya-bhāk<br />sādhur eva sa mantavyaḥ samyag vyavasito hi saḥ [30]
<span class="e2">chet</span>–If; <span class="e2">api</span>–even;<span class="e2"> sudurāchāraḥ</span>–a person of sinful practices;<span class="e2"> bhajate</span>–serves; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> ananya-bhāk</span>–with exclusive devotion (giving up all other endeavours such as karma and jñān); <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> saḥ mantavyaḥ</span>–he should be regarded; <span class="e2">sādhuḥ</span>–as a saintly person; <span class="e2">hi</span>–because;<span class="e2"> saḥ samyak vyavasitaḥ</span>–his resolve is perfect. [30]
30 If even a very sinful person serves Me exclusively with devotion, he should be regarded as saintly, for his resolve is perfect.
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्म्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति ।<br />कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥३१॥
kṣipraṁ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvach-chhāntiṁ nigachchhati<br />kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati [31]
[1] (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–He (who dedicates himself to Me);<span class="e2"> kṣipram</span>–swiftly;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–becomes;<span class="e2"> dharma-ātmā</span>–a person of virtuous practices;<span class="e2"> nigachchhati</span>–and attains; <span class="e2">śaśvat</span>–constant; <span class="e2">śāntim</span>–peace, relief from obstacles. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> pratijānīhi</span>–declare; (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–thus; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> bhaktaḥ</span>–devotee;<span class="e2"> na praṇaśyati</span>–is never vanquished. [31]
[2] (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> pratijānīhi</span>–promise and declare it; (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–that;<span class="e2"> me bhaktaḥ</span>–My devotee;<span class="e2"> na praṇaśyati</span>–is never vanquished. (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–That person who proclaims this;<span class="e2"> kṣipram</span>–swiftly;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–becomes;<span class="e2"> dharma-ātmā</span>–virtuous, religious;<span class="e2"> nigachchhati</span>–and attains; <span class="e2">śaśvat</span>–constant; <span class="e2">śāntim</span>–peace, joy. [31]
31 He swiftly becomes a person of virtuous practices and attains constant peace. O son of Kuntī, declare to the world that My devotee is never vanquished!
or
31 O son of Kuntī, declare to the world that My devotee is never vanquished. One who declares this swiftly becomes virtuous and attains eternal joy.
Commentary
The second interpretation of this verse was revealed to Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur in a dream.
In the <span class="e2">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (11.11.32) Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa says:
आज्ञायैवं गुणान्दोषान्मयादिष्टानपि स्वकान् ।<br />धर्म्मान्सन्त्यज्य यः सर्व्वान्मां भजेत्स च सत्तमः ॥
ājñāyaivaṁ guṇān doṣān mayādiṣṭān api svakān<br />dharmān santyajya yaḥ sarvān māṁ bhajet sa cha sattamaḥ
“The best of the saintly persons are those who have surpassed the forms of duties that I, Myself, have recommended in the scriptures for the people in general. Although it is My directive, they cross it and render loving service to Me.”
In society, one must obey the law, but there is also the situation of crossing the law to show fidelity to the king. If one risks his life and reputation, and crossing the general law enters the royal chamber to combat an assassin, then he will be considered the most loyal servitor. Similarly, the Lord is saying, “I have already given some direction for the people in general. Do this, don’t do that, don’t cross these laws, etc. But if for My interest anyone takes the risk of committing sin, then he should be considered the best of My devotees.
“So, Arjuna, go and declare it, promise to the public that the <span class="e3">ananya-bhāk</span> (verse 30), the exclusively devoted persons, will never come to ruin. Then you will get the benefit. You will become <span class="e3">dharmātmā</span>, religious, and attain eternal divine happiness. The <span class="e3">ananya-bhāk</span>, the exclusive devotees, have already crossed the threshold of dharma, the standard of dutifulness, and taken the risk to throw themselves fully into My service. <span class="e3">Sarva dharmān parityajya Mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja</span> (18.66). There is no question of them ‘becoming’ virtuous or religious as they long before surpassed dharma and took the risk and entered into prema-dharma, My loving service, transcending both piety and sinfulness.”
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः ।<br />स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥३२॥
māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye ’pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ<br />striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās te ’pi yānti parāṁ gatim [32]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">ye api</span>–even those who; <span class="e2">syuḥ</span>–may be considered ;<span class="e2"> pāpa-yonayaḥ</span>–low-born persons;<span class="e2"> striyaḥ</span>–women;<span class="e2"> vaiśyāḥ</span>–merchants;<span class="e2"> tathā śūdrāḥ</span>–and labourers;<span class="e2"> vyapāśritya hi</span>–if they take full shelter; <span class="e2">mām</span>–in Me;<span class="e2"> te api yānti</span>–they, too, attain;<span class="e2"> parām gatim</span>–the supreme destination. [32]
32 O son of Pṛthā, persons of low birth, women, merchants or labourers—they, too, attain the supreme destination by taking full refuge in Me.
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा ।<br />अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥३३॥
kiṁ punar brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayas tathā<br />anityam asukhaṁ lokam imaṁ prāpya bhajasva mām [33]
<span class="e2">kim punaḥ</span>–Not to mention that; <span class="e2">bhaktāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–having become devoted to Me; <span class="e2">puṇyāḥ</span>–the pure;<span class="e2"> brāhmaṇāḥ</span>–brāhmaṇs; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–and;<span class="e2"> rājarṣayaḥ</span>–saintly kings; (<span class="e2">parāṁ gatiṁ yānti</span>)–will surely attain the supreme destination. <span class="e2">prāpya</span>–(Therefore) having achieved; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> anityam</span>–temporary;<span class="e2"> asukham</span>–miserable; <span class="e2">lokam</span>–human body;<span class="e2"> bhajasva</span>–serve; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me. [33]
33 So can there be any doubt that those brāhmaṇs and saintly kings who are pure devotees will achieve the supreme goal? Therefore, worship Me, since although this human body is temporary and a place of suffering, it is attained only after many births and it affords the best opportunity to render devotional service to Me.
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।<br />मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥३४॥
man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru<br />mām evaiṣyasi yuktvaivam ātmānaṁ mat-parāyaṇaḥ [34]
<span class="e2">bhava</span>–Be;<span class="e2"> mat-manāḥ</span>–always conscious of Me;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktaḥ</span>–My devoted servitor; <span class="e2">mat-yājī </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and My worshipper.<span class="e2"> namaskuru</span>–Offer obeisances; <span class="e2">mām</span>–to Me. <span class="e2">evam</span>–In this way;<span class="e2"> yuktvā ātmānam</span>–having dedicated yourself to Me;<span class="e2"> mat-parāyaṇaḥ</span>–taking refuge in Me; <span class="e2">eṣyasi</span>–you will reach; <span class="e2">mām eva</span>–Me. [34]
34 Always think of Me, be my devotee, always worship Me and offer obeisances to Me. Thus offering yourself to Me and taking refuge in Me, you will come to Me.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे राजगुह्ययोगो नाम नवमोऽध्यायः ॥९॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde rāja-<br />guhya-yogo nāma navamo ’dhyāyaḥ [9]
End of Chapter Nine<br />The Hidden Treasure of Devotion<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

दशमोऽध्यायः
Chapter Ten
Vibhūti-yoga <br />The Divine Glories of the Lord
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।<br />यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥१॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
bhūya eva mahā-bāho śṛṇu me paramaṁ vachaḥ<br />yat te ’haṁ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hita-kāmyayā [1]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty-armed Arjuna; <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–hear;<span class="e2"> bhūyaḥ eva</span>–once again; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> paramam</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">vachaḥ</span>–word; <span class="e2">yat</span>–since; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> vakṣyāmi</span>–will speak;<span class="e2"> te prīyamāṇāya</span>–to you, who are very dear to Me;<span class="e2"> hita-kāmyayā</span>–desiring your welfare. [1]
1 The Supreme Lord said: O heroic Arjuna, listen to My supreme word once again. Desiring your welfare, I shall speak to you, who are very dear to Me.
न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः ।<br />अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणाञ्च सर्व्वशः ॥२॥
na me viduḥ sura-gaṇāḥ prabhavaṁ na maharṣayaḥ<br />aham ādir hi devānāṁ maharṣīṇāñ cha sarvaśaḥ [2]
<span class="e2">na</span>–Neither;<span class="e2"> sura-gaṇāḥ</span>–the demigods; <span class="e2">na</span>–nor;<span class="e2"> mahā-ṛṣayaḥ</span>–the great sages; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–understand; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> prabhavam</span>–transcendental birth; <span class="e2">hi</span>–because;<span class="e2"> sarvaśaḥ</span>–in all respects;<span class="e2"> aham ādiḥ</span>–I am the origin;<span class="e2"> devānām</span>–of the demigods;<span class="e2"> mahā-ṛṣīṇām cha</span>–and of the great sages, too. [2]
2 Neither the demigods nor the great sages can understand My transcendental appearance in this world, as I alone am the origin of those celestial beings and sages.
यो मामजमनादिञ्च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् ।<br />असम्मूढः स मर्त्त्येषु सर्व्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥३॥
yo mām ajam anādiñ cha vetti loka-maheśvaram<br />asammūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarva-pāpaiḥ pramuchyate [3]
<span class="e2">yah</span>–One who; <span class="e2">vetti</span>–knows; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me, the son of Devakī; <span class="e2">ajam</span>–as the birthless; <span class="e2">anādim</span>–the beginningless;<span class="e2"> loka-mahā-īśvaram cha</span>–and the Supreme Lord of all beings; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he;<span class="e2"> asammūḍhaḥ</span>–undeluded;<span class="e2"> martyeṣu</span>–among men;<span class="e2"> pramuchyate</span>–is liberated;<span class="e2"> sarva-pāpaiḥ</span>–from all sins or obstacles to devotion. [3]
3 One who knows Me, the son of Devakī, as the birthless, beginningless, Supreme Lord of all beings, is undeluded among men and completely liberated from sin.
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसम्मोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः ।<br />सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयञ्चाभयमेव च ॥४॥
अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः ।<br />भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥५॥
buddhir jñānam asammohaḥ kṣamā satyaṁ damaḥ śamaḥ<br />sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ bhavo ’bhāvo bhayañ chābhayam eva cha [4]
ahiṁsā samatā tuṣṭis tapo dānaṁ yaśo ’yaśaḥ<br />bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṁ matta eva pṛthag-vidhāḥ [5]
(<span class="e2">ete</span>)–All these;<span class="e2"> pṛthak-vidhāḥ bhāvāḥ</span>–various qualities;<span class="e2"> bhūtānām</span>–of the living beings;<span class="e2"> bhavanti</span>–are born;<span class="e2"> mattaḥ eva</span>–of Me alone:<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–ability to determine subtle meanings; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–ability to discriminate between spirit and matter;<span class="e2"> asammohaḥ</span>–freedom from delusion; <span class="e2">kṣamā</span>–tolerance; <span class="e2">satyam</span>–truthfulness; <span class="e2">damaḥ</span>–control of the external senses; <span class="e2">śamaḥ</span>–control of the internal senses; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–happiness;<span class="e2"> duḥkham</span>–unhappiness; <span class="e2">bhavaḥ</span>–birth;<span class="e2"> abhāvaḥ</span>–death;<span class="e2"> bhayam cha</span>–fear;<span class="e2"> abhayam eva cha</span>–and fearlessness; <span class="e2">ahiṁsā</span>–nonviolence; <span class="e2">samatā</span>–equanimity, seeing the happiness and unhappiness of all beings as one’s own; <span class="e2">tuṣṭiḥ</span>–satisfaction; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity as directed in the Vedas; <span class="e2">dānam</span>–charity; <span class="e2">yaśaḥ</span>–fame; <span class="e2">ayaśaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and infamy. [4–5]
4–5 Intelligence, knowledge, freedom from delusion, forbearance, truthfulness, mental control, sense control, happiness, unhappiness, birth, death, fear, courage, nonviolence, equanimity, satisfaction, austerity, charity, fame, and infamy—all these various attributes of the living beings are born of Me alone.
महर्षयः सप्त पूर्व्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा ।<br />मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥६॥
maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve chatvāro manavas tathā<br />mad-bhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṁ loka imāḥ prajāḥ [6]
(ete)<span class="e2"> mat-bhāvāḥ</span>–All these personalities, empowered by Me;<span class="e2"> mānasāḥ jātāḥ</span>–are born of My mind, which is manifest as Hiraṇyagarbha, Lord Brahmā:<span class="e2"> sapta mahāṛṣayaḥ</span>–the seven great sages—Marīchi, Atri, Aṅgirā, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vaśiṣṭha; <span class="e2">pūrve</span>–and their predecessors;<span class="e2"> chatvārah</span>–the four sages Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanat Kumār, and Sanātan, all known as brahmarṣis;<span class="e2"> tathā manavaḥ</span>–and the fourteen Manus headed by Svayambhuva.<span class="e2"> imāḥ prajāḥ loke</span>–Mankind—brāhmaṇ, etc., and all progeny; <span class="e2">yeṣām</span>–descends from these patriarchs. [6]
6 The seven great sages headed by Marīchi, and preceding them, the four brāhmaṇ sages headed by Sanaka, and also the fourteen Manus or progenitors headed by Svayambhuva—all are empowered by Me and are born of Lord Brahmā, who is a manifestation of My mind. Mankind and all progeny descends from these patriarchs.
एतां विभूतिं योगञ्च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।<br />सोऽविकल्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥७॥
etāṁ vibhūtiṁ yogañ cha mama yo vetti tattvataḥ<br />so ’vikalpena yogena yujyate nātra saṁśayaḥ [7]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; <span class="e2">vetti</span>–knows;<span class="e2"> tattvataḥ</span>–in truth; <span class="e2">etām</span>–this;<span class="e2"> vibhūtim</span>–supremacy; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–(bhakti-) yoga; <span class="e2">mama</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a person;<span class="e2"> yujyate</span>–is linked;<span class="e2"> avikalpena</span>–by undeviating; <span class="e2">yogena</span>–knowledge of essential truth. <span class="e2">atra</span>–In this matter; <span class="e2">na saṁśayaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">asti</span>)–there is no doubt. [7]
7 One who thus knows in truth My supremacy and devotional service serves Me in unwavering realisation. Of this there is no doubt.
अहं सर्व्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्व्वं प्रवर्त्तते ।<br />इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥८॥
ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate<br />iti matvā bhajante māṁ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ [8]
<span class="e2">aham prabhavaḥ</span>–I am the Supreme Absolute Truth, Svayam Bhagavān or the original Supreme Lord, the cause;<span class="e2"> sarvasya</span>–of all causes, including Brahma, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān. <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–All activity in the universe of matter and spirit, and the Vedas and allied scriptures;<span class="e2"> pravartate</span>–arise; <span class="e2">mattaḥ</span>–from Me. <span class="e2">matvā</span>–Realising; <span class="e2">iti</span>–this deep truth; <span class="e2">budhāḥ</span>–persons of fine theistic intelligence;<span class="e2"> bhāva-samanvitāḥ</span>–in their divine relationship of servitude, friendship, etc.;<span class="e2"> bhajante</span>–worship, adore; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me. [8]
8 I am Kṛṣṇa, the Sweet Absolute, the origin of all. The entire universe of material and transcendental play, activity, purpose, and the Vedas and allied scriptures which give guidance—all evolve from Me alone. Realising this hidden treasure, persons of fine theistic intelligence surpass the mundane and embrace the path of love divine, rāga-marg, and adore Me forever.
Commentary
Verses 8–11 are the four principal verses of <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span>. The ontological substance of the book is contained within these four essential verses beginning, “<span class="e3">Ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo</span>: everything evolves from Me.”
In the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (1.2.11), the three main conceptions of the Absolute are given as Brahma, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān. Brahma is the all-comprehensive aspect of the Absolute, Paramātmā is the all-permeating aspect of the Absolute, and Bhagavān is the personal conception of the Absolute. The word <span class="e3">Bhagavān</span> is generally defined as stated in the <span class="e3">Viṣṇu-purāṇa</span> (6.5.47):
ऐश्वर्य्यस्य समग्रस्य वीर्य्यस्य यशसः श्रियः<br />ज्ञानवैराग्ययोश्चैव षण्णां भग इतीङ्गना
aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ<br />jñāna-vairāgyayoś chaiva ṣaṇṇāṁ bhaga itīṅganā
“He who is full with all the six opulences of wealth, power, fame, beauty, knowledge, and renunciation is known as <span class="e3">Bhagavān</span>, the Supreme Lord.”
The characteristic of Bhagavān, as Lord Nārāyaṇ, is that all kinds of potencies are personally controlled by Him. However, Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī has given a special and particularly fine interpretation: <span class="e3">Bhagavān</span> means <span class="e3">bhajanīya guṇa-viśiṣṭa</span>. His nature is such that whoever comes into contact with Him cannot resist serving Him. No one can resist feeling moved to worship and adore His charming personality. As Lord Kṛṣṇa, He attracts the love of everyone.
Therefore, by the word <span class="e3">sarvasya</span>, Lord Kṛṣṇa indicates, “I am Svayam Bhagavān, the Supreme Lord Himself. I am the origin of not only Brahma and Paramātmā. I am also the origin of the Master of all potencies who commands the respect of everyone, Lord Nārāyaṇ of Vaikuṇṭha.
“<span class="e3">Mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate</span>: every attempt and movement begins from Me, including the methods by which everyone worships and serves Me in devotion.”
नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो<br />न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन ।<br />यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्<br />तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम् ॥
(कठोपनिषद् १.२.२३)
nāyam ātmā pravachanena labhyo<br />na medhayā na bahunā śrutena<br />yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas<br />tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṁ svām
(Kaṭhopaniṣad: 1.2.23)
“The Lord cannot by known by logic, intelligence, or extensive study of the scriptures. But He reveals Himself to one who is eager to serve Him and prays to Him for His grace.”
In this way, “<span class="e3">Mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate</span>: I am the first to reveal to the people, ‘Worship Me in this way.’ I appear as Guru, and through him, I worship Myself.”
In the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (11.17.27), the Guru is described by the Lord as His own direct manifestation:
आचार्य्यं मां विजानीयान्नावमन्येत कर्हिचित् ।<br />न मर्त्त्य बुद्ध्यासूयेत सर्व्व देवमयो गुरुः ॥
āchāryaṁ māṁ vijānīyān nāvamanyeta karhichit<br />na martya buddhyāsūyeta sarva deva-mayo guruḥ
(Śrī Kṛṣṇa said to His devotee, Uddhava:) “You should know the bona fide spiritual master as My very Self. Gurudev is the embodiment of all the gods. Never dishonour him or find fault in him by ascribing any mundane conception of place, time, and circumstances to him.”
Furthermore, the Lord’s finest potency is Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Of course, there are many other eternal associates, but the highest order of devotional service is represented in Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. The Lord is therefore saying, “My worship is shown by Me. I, as My finest potency, worship Myself. <span class="e3">Iti matvā bhajante Māṁ</span>: understanding this conception, the devotee will come to worship Me, always under the direction of My best worshipper—My finest potency and representation—Rādhārāṇī, or Gurudev. Crossing Her, the highest and most desirable form of service to Me is not possible.”
Rādhā-dāsyam, the servitorship of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, is indicated here. Only those who are blessed with divine intelligence will be able to appreciate this, and not persons with self-acquired intelligence from this māyika quarter, the world of misconception. In this verse, the word <span class="e3">budhāḥ</span> refers to sumedhasaḥ as described in the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (11.5.32), or persons of fine theistic intelligence arising from direct connection with the transcendental plane. The inner guidance and direction they receive is the outcome of sukṛti, divine merit acquired by the association of pure devotees. <span class="e3">Bhāva-samanvitāḥ</span> means rāga-samanvitāḥ—anurāga—love and attraction which is affinity, not by strictly following scriptural rules or drawn from any plane of loss and gain, but from bhāva, inner divine inspiration. Devotion of this high type is completely noncalculative (jñāna-śūnyā-bhakti), as described by Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī in his <span class="e3">Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</span> (1.1.11):
अन्याभिलाषिता शून्यं ज्ञानकर्म्माद्यनावृतम् ।<br />आनुकूल्येन कृष्णानुशीलनं भक्तिरुत्तमा ॥
anyābhilāṣitā śūnyaṁ jñāna-karmādy anāvṛtam<br />ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānuśīlanaṁ bhaktir uttamā
“The highest devotion is that which satisfies Lord Kṛṣṇa, free from the coverings of any pursuits such as action and knowledge.”
The most rare and elevated stage of devotion is in the line of spontaneous devotion, known as rāga-mārg. In that line, guided by the qualified Guru, an elevated pure devotee may attain service to a leader of one of the groups of Kṛṣṇa’s personal associates who serve the Lord in His Pastimes in a relationship of friendship (sakhya-rasa), parenthood (vātsalya-rasa), or consorthood (madhura-rasa). In Vṛndāvan the Lord is served in spontaneous devotion by His friends headed by Subal Sakhā, and by His parental devotees headed by Nanda Mahārāj and mother Yaśodā. The gopīs headed by Lalitā and Viśākhā serve Him in consorthood. But amongst all His associates, and amongst all the gopīs, the highest order of divine loving service is rendered to the Lord by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Therefore, the acme of rāga-mārg is the service of Rādhārāṇī (Rādhā-dāsyam). This is the highest objective of the Rūpānuga Gauḍīya sampradāya, the followers of pure devotion as taught by Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhupād, in the line of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् ।<br />कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥९॥
mach-chittā mad-gata-prāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam<br />kathayantaś cha māṁ nityaṁ tuṣyanti cha ramanti cha [9]
<span class="e2">mat-gata-prāṇāḥ</span>–Those who have dedicated their lives to Me;<span class="e2"> mat-chittāḥ</span>–who always think of Me;<span class="e2"> mām kathayantaḥ cha</span>–and talk about Me; <span class="e2">bodhayantaḥ parasparam </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–enlightening one another with the nectar of their devotional realisations; <span class="e2">nityam</span>–are ever;<span class="e2"> tuṣyanti cha</span>–satisfied;<span class="e2"> ramanti cha</span>–and ecstatic. [9]
9 Always thinking of Me, those surrendered souls converse about Me, enlightening one another with the nectar of their devotional realisations, ever content and ecstatic in their divine natures.
Commentary
The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa is speaking about His pure devotees. “I am in the heart of their hearts, in their every thought. Their entire energy—their whole life—is dedicated to My satisfaction. They converse with one another about Me and experience mutual enlightenment. They always love to talk about Me with whoever they meet, and nothing else. For every time, place, and circumstance, I am the only subject of their discussion. They find very much satisfaction in this (<span class="e3">tuṣyanti cha</span>).” Up to the divine relationship of parenthood, there is the feeling of satisfaction.
Furthermore, “<span class="e3">Ramanti cha</span>: just as a wife enjoys a conjugal relationship with her husband, the devotees similarly feel such ecstasy in My intimate company when speaking about Me.” This has also been mentioned by the previous Āchāryas.
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्व्वकम् ।<br />ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥१०॥
teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam<br />dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ yena mām upayānti te [10]
<span class="e2">teṣām prīti-pūrvakam bhajatām</span>–To those loving devotees;<span class="e2"> satata-yuktānām</span>–who are always engaged in My service; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I; <span class="e2">dadāmi</span>–give; <span class="e2">tam</span>–that;<span class="e2"> buddhi-yogam</span>–inspiration; <span class="e2">yena</span>–by which; <span class="e2">te</span>–they;<span class="e2"> upayānti</span>–can come; <span class="e2">mām</span>–to Me. [10]
10 To those devotees who are always lovingly engaged in My service, I give the divine inspiration by which they can come to Me.
Commentary
The Lord says, “The highest group of My servitors (whose devotion was described in the previous verse by the word <span class="e3">ramanti</span>) are those who are constantly engaged (<span class="e3">satata-yukta</span>) in My service in consorthood (madhura-rasa) with heartfelt love (<span class="e3">bhajatām prīti-pūrvakam</span>).” Then He says that He will give them further inspiration or inner instruction ‘by which they can come to Him’ (<span class="e3">yena Mām upayānti te</span>). When already in this and the previous verse the devotees’ service to the Lord has been described as eternal (by the words <span class="e3">nityam</span> and <span class="e3">satata-yukta</span>), now the statement that He will give them further inspiration ‘by which they can come to Him’ may appear to be redundant. Therefore, in the expression <span class="e3">Mām upayānti te</span> (“They will come to Me”), the word <span class="e3">upayānti</span> must be defined as <span class="e3">parakīya-bhāvena—upapati</span>. <span class="e3">Pati</span> means husband, and <span class="e3">upapati</span> means paramour.
In Vṛndāvan, Lord Kṛṣṇa is not considered a lawful husband, but He is the Lord of the heart, transcendental to even the husband (parakīya-rasa). Deceiving their husbands, the gopīs of Vṛndāvan unite with Kṛṣṇa. they do not allow a second party to come between them and Kṛṣṇa. They cannot allow the interception of social law or even scriptural regulation, because Kṛṣṇa’s position is absolute, and such a relationship is more relishable to Him. This is Vṛndāvan-bhajan*, and this is the meaning of <span class="e3">upapati</span>.
* विक्रीडितं व्रजवधूभिरिदञ्च विष्णोः<br />श्रद्धान्वितोऽनुशृणुयादय वर्णयेद्यः ।<br />भक्तिं परां भगवति प्रतिलभ्य कामं<br />हृद्रोगमाश्वपहिनोत्यचिरेण धीरः ॥
(भाः १०/३३/३९)
vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idañ cha viṣṇoḥ<br />śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ<br />bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ<br />hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty achireṇa dhīraḥ
(SB: 10.33.39)
“A self-controlled person who possesses sincere faith in the divine Pastimes transcendentally enjoyed by Lord Kṛṣṇa with the gopīs (Rāsa-līlā), and who, having heard those divine Pastimes from the lotus mouth of the bona fide Guru constantly sings or narrates their glories—such a person swiftly achieves the most elevated form of pure devotion for the Lord, and is promptly able to ward off the heart disease of lust.”
In his writings, Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī has laid stress on the word <span class="e3">dhīra</span>, meaning ‘self-controlled.’ To hear these elevated subjects, one must enter into the culture of sense-control, otherwise he will be lost.
नैतत्समाचरेज्जातु मनसापि ह्यनीश्वरः ।<br />विनश्यत्याचरन्मौढ्याद्यथारुद्रोऽब्धिजं विषम् ॥
(भाः १०/३३/३०)
naitat samācharej jātu manasāpi hy anīśvaraḥ<br />vinaśyaty ācharan mauḍhyād yathārudro ’bdhi-jaṁ viṣam
(SB: 10.33.30)
“No one should ever even think of imitating this behaviour of the Supreme Lord and the gopīs. If out of gross foolishness anyone tries to imitate the Pastimes of the Lord, he will be destroyed, as though imitating Lord Śiva by drinking the poison which arose from the ocean.” (It is described in the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> that once the demigods and the demons jointly engaged in churning the ocean to produce nectar. Both nectar and poison were produced, and Lord Śiva, by his power, could hold the poison within his throat.)
“My relationship with them is independent of everything conceivable, including law, society, and the scriptures. It is most innate and natural, and it does not require any social or scriptural sanction. I say to them, ‘You may show formal respect to all these restrictions and live in the society. But from the heart of your heart, you are Mine.’ This is the special inspiration and insight I give those devotees (<span class="e3">buddhi-yogam yena Mām upayānti te</span>).
“Externally there are social and scriptural demands, but My position is over and above them. Veda is My instruction for the benefit of the masses who have deviated from Me, and society is also under the jurisdiction of those general instructions given to the people by Me. But My divine relationship with everything is intrinsic and independent. It does not require recognition from anyone. Such a relationship is the highest. It is the constant. It supersedes all law and society which are guided by the Vedas; rather, all the Vedas are searching for such a thing.”
<span class="e3">Śrutibhir vimṛgyām</span> (SB: 10.47.61): <span class="e3">viśeṣa-mṛgya</span>—the Vedas are searching after this ideal divine position. In the section of the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> which deals with Rāsa-līlā, the Vedas are begging forgiveness.
“We are generally supposed to give tidings of You, but we could not describe You as we now experience You here. Now we understand that we have committed an offence, because we could not distribute this Rāsa-līlā to the world.”
Like signposts, all the revealed scriptures are only showing the direction; but where, how? “We don’t know.” Only, “He may be available in this direction.”
Anywhere and everywhere, everything belongs to Him. For one who knows this, all possibilities of sense pleasure and exploitation are uprooted. For example, an unmarried woman may have the possibility of being approached by many, but there is less possibility for those who are married, because they are possessed by someone. Similarly, when we are able to know that everything is only for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa, then we shall realise that all our exploiting tendencies have vanished forever. Nothing will remain to be utilised for the pleasure of our sense-experience. It will be very deeply felt in our hearts that everything has its existence only for His satisfaction, and there is no room for any other exploitation.
We, too, are included there—our existence is also only for His satisfaction. Everything is meant for His divine Pastimes (līlā), and there is no possibility for any others’ pastimes. All are included in that one līlā. Encroachment will disappear when we learn the proper utility of everything. He is the owner, and His ownership is absolute. The scriptures, society, and law designate, “This is yours, that is another’s, or that belongs to a third party.” This is something like a temporary lease, but the permanent ownership is in all respects with Him. All others—possessor and property, master and servant—are relative, and only sanctioned by Him for the time being. He alone is the absolute owner, possessor, and enjoyer. Complete purification of our hearts is possible only when we arrive at such a conclusion. Everyone is thinking of themselves as many masters of many things, but this is all ‘heart disease’ (<span class="e3">hṛd-rogam</span>). This is all conceived in a diseased state of consciousness. In a healthy state, when the heart is quite wholesome, we can see the Supreme Whole, and we can see that everything is meant only for His satisfaction.
तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः ।<br />नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥११॥
teṣām evānukampārtham aham ajñāna-jaṁ tamaḥ<br />nāśayāmy ātma-bhāva-stho jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā [11]
<span class="e2">anukampa-artham</span>–Out of compassion;<span class="e2"> teṣām eva</span>–for them; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ</span>–appearing within their hearts;<span class="e2"> nāśayāmi</span>–destroy;<span class="e2"> bhāsvatā jñāna-dīpena</span>–with the shining lamp of knowledge; <span class="e2">tamaḥ</span>–the darkness;<span class="e2"> ajñāna-jam</span>–born of ignorance. [11]
11 Out of compassion for them, I, situated within the hearts of all living beings, dispel the darkness of ignorance with the radiance of knowledge.
or
11 Being conquered by the love of those devotees who in their unalloyed loving devotion become afflicted by the all-devouring darkness born of their pangs of separation from Me, I illuminate their hearts with My presence, destroying the darkness of their pain of separation.
Commentary
Of the two translations given above, the first is the most general interpretation of this verse. But if we appreciate pure, noncalculative devotion (jñāna-śūnyā-bhakti), the Lord’s statement here may again appear redundant and inconsistent.
When those high devotees are already admitted to be performing continuous and unadulterated service, and even above that, they are situated in the plane of pure love, spontaneous and automatic (rāga-mārg), how can it be harmonised that the Lord will now in the last stage destroy their ignorance (<span class="e3">tamaḥ</span>) born of misunderstanding (<span class="e3">ajñāna-jam</span>), by giving them knowledge (<span class="e3">jñāna</span>)? Jñān is only a cover—a futile, finite conception of the infinite Absolute (<span class="e3">jñāna-karmādy anāvṛtam … bhaktir uttamā</span>). When they have achieved devotion devoid of the covering of knowledge (jñāna-śūnyā-bhakti), how will they again have to return to that knowledge (<span class="e3">jñāna</span>)? In his commentary, Śrīla Viśvanāth Chakravartī Ṭhākur has mentioned that this knowledge is extraordinary (vilakṣaṇam), though he did not enter into specific detail. To clarify this point, we have given the following explanation:
Lamentation and delusion are generally known to be symptoms of the mode of ignorance (tamo-guṇa). In jñāna-śūnyā-bhakti, the elevated devotees who take Kṛṣṇa not as the Supreme God, but as a friend, son, husband, or lover, will come to experience lamentation and delusion, but this is only an outward appearance of ignorance. In fact, it is the pain of divine separation. They lament. “Where have You gone?”
In this verse, the Lord’s statement, <span class="e3">teṣām evānukampārtham</span> generally means “Fortunately for them,” or, “To favour them (I dispel their darkness, etc.).” But it may also be interpreted, “I want their favour. I aspire for the favour of those devotees of the highest order.”
The Lord also says to the Gopīs in the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (10.82.44):
मयि भक्तिर्हि भूतानाममृतत्वाय कल्पते ।<br />दिष्ट्या यदासीन्मत्स्नेहो भवतीनां मदापनः ॥
mayi bhaktir hi bhūtānām amṛtatvāya kalpate<br />diṣṭyā yad āsīn mat-sneho bhavatīnāṁ mad-āpanaḥ
“In general, people want devotion to Me to achieve eternal life. To cross the limit of mortality and to have eternal life, they come to Me and worship Me. For these reasons they want My service, but fortunately for you, O gopīs, you have some natural affection towards Me. That will ultimately bring you to Me.”
This is the general meaning. However, in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span>, Śrīla Kṛṣṇadās Kavirāj Goswāmī has drawn out the inner meaning of what Kṛṣṇa is saying to the gopīs, which is just the opposite:
“Through devotion, everyone wants Me to help them attain the highest position of eternal benefit, and if they have a connection with Me, they consider themselves fortunate. But I consider Myself fortunate because I have come in touch with the valuable affection that I found in your hearts. By My fortune, I have got your association.”
Therefore, here in <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>, the Lord is saying, “<span class="e3">Teṣām evānukampārtham</span>: being conquered by the love of those unalloyed devotees, when I cannot tolerate their pain of separation, I at once come running to satisfy them, and I reveal to them with special light, special consciousness, ‘I have returned to you—see Me now.’ With powerful brilliance (<span class="e3">jñāna-dīpena</span>) I show them My presence when they are very much in need of Me, and I relieve their pain of separation.”
<span class="e3">Ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ</span>: He reveals Himself according to His devotee’s divine relationship with Him (rasa): to a friend, as a friend; to a mother, as a child; to a wife, as a husband; and to the sweethearts, as a paramour.
After Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu left home and accepted the renounced order of life, sannyās, Mother Śachī could not tolerate the deep separation, and she began to cry. Śachī Devī was preparing excellent dishes, offering them to the Deity, and weeping. “Where is my Nimāi? He’s very fond of these curries—His favourite dishes, and Nimāi is not here.” Suddenly, Lord Chaitanya came and began to eat. Śachī Devī exclaimed, “Oh, Nimāi is eating!” and for the time being her separation was relieved. Moments later, she reconsidered, “Did I see Nimāi eating? But He is now a sannyāsī in Jagannāth Purī, so how could He have come here? Did I serve Him? There must be a mistake.” Then she examined the pots again to see if there was food there. Finding them empty, she began to conjecture whether even a dog or some other animal had come and eaten it. But during that moment, Nimāi had actually come, and Mother Śachī saw Him in broad daylight. That illumination is transcendental, and not the ‘knowledge’ (jñān) that is generally known in our vocabulary.
The acme of theism is parakīya-rasa. <span class="e3">Parakīya</span> means ‘another’s.’ In every divine relationship, the Lord captures all. In the whole of Vṛndāvan where everyone follows the path of love (rāga-mārg), this parakīya-rasa is infused. The friends of Kṛṣṇa sometimes say, “Some people say that Kṛṣṇa is a resident of Mathurā. They say He’s the son of Vasudev, and He will soon go to Mathurā. They say He is not our friend! Will we really lose His company? Then how will we be able to live in this jungle and herd the cows?” They experience this apprehension—“We may lose Him at any time.” This intensifies their friendly service to Him.
Similarly, Mother Yaśodā thinks, “Some say that Kṛṣṇa is not my son, He’s Devakī’s son. What is this? I won’t admit this. He’s my child!” This idea enhances Yaśodā’s affection for Kṛṣṇa: “I may lose Him? Then how shall I live?” Therefore, the parakīya-rasa stresses the rarity of Kṛṣṇa’s relationship, because the possibility of losing His company is always in the background. But the highest intensity of service is to be found in the madhura-rasa (consorthood) group. In the other rasas, there is the idea of suspense that He may ‘go away,’ but in the consorthood relationship in the divine abode of Vṛndāvan, the consorts cross the direction of the scriptures and the society, which guide everyone to remain as husband and wife (svakīya). Parakīya (‘another’s’) has been accepted in the science of devotion as the highest conception, above the socially and scripturally sanctioned svakīya (‘one’s own’).
Parakīya or paramour relationship nourishes the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa by deceiving one who claims ownership over another, such as a husband over a wife, or a parent over a child. The normally accepted relationship of svakīya is commonplace, but to cross the jurisdiction of the scriptures and society, as a paramour, means a greater risk as if to commit sin. Thus, this relationship is very rare, and rarity enhances its intensity and value. The idea of deceiving the ‘possessor’ to favour the ‘non-possessor’ (in the spiritual sense) is a beautiful, ornamental conception. Actually, in Kṛṣṇa’s case there cannot be any state of paramourship, because in truth He is the owner of everything. However, the divine arrangement is fashioned in this way to enhance the devotee’s internal devotion for the Lord, just as food appears more tasteful when hunger is present.
In Vaikuṇṭha, the nature of the worship of Lord Viṣṇu is gorgeous, majestic, reverential, and awe-inspiring. But above that, in the highest conception, Godhead is humanlike in form and nature. It is stated in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> in the teachings to Sanātana Goswāmī:
কৃষ্ণের যতেক খেলা,<span class="e22">	সর্ব্বোত্তম নরলীলা,<br /></span><span class="e23">	নরবপু তাহার স্বরূপ ।</span><span class="e23"><br /></span>গোপবেশ, বেণুকর,<span class="e22">	নবকিশোর, নটবর,<br /></span><span class="e23">	নরলীলা হয় অনুরূপ॥</span>
<span class="e23">	কৃষ্ণের মধুর </span><span class="e23">রূপ শুন সনাতন ।<br /></span>যে রূপের এক কণ,<span class="e22">	ডুবায় সব </span><span class="e22">ত্রিভুবন,<br /></span><span class="e23">	সর্ব্বপ্রাণী করে আকর্ষণ ॥</span>
kṛṣṇera yateka khelā,<span class="e5">	sarvvottama nara-līlā,<br /></span><span class="e6">	nara-vapu tāhāra svarūpa<br /></span>gopa-veśa, veṇu-kara,<span class="e5">	nava-kiśora, naṭavara,<br /></span><span class="e6">	nara-līlā haya anurūpa</span>
<span class="e6">	kṛṣṇera madhura-rūpa śuna sanātana<br /></span>ye rūpera eka kaṇa,<span class="e5">	ḍubāya saba tribhuvana,<br /></span><span class="e6">	sarvva-prāṇī kare ākarṣaṇa</span>
“The highest form of Godhead is Kṛṣṇa, who plays in His eternal divine Pastimes like a human being. An ever-youthful cowherd boy of Vṛndāvan, the best of dancers, He enjoys His Pastimes, always playing His flute. His beauty is so charming and sweet that the whole universe is flooded by even the tiniest atom of it, and all beings are attracted irresistibly to Him.”
He is approachable by all. We can find God nearest of all—in a human feature. It has been explained how Kṛṣṇa’s form of human feature is the highest form of the Absolute, according to the calculation of ecstasy (rasa), which is the common standard of measurement of the whole scope of the Infinite. By the development of śānta-, dāsya-, sakhya-, vātsalya-, and madhura-, and then parakīya-rasa (tranquillity, servitude, friendship, parenthood, consorthood, and then paramour relationship), this is scientifically proven, without whimsical or blind faith. If we follow the line of Rūpānuga-bhajan (devotion following the line of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī) which originates from Śrī Chaitanyadev, this scientific basis can be appreciated. The previous Āchāryas have left comprehensive teachings for us on how to follow, conceive, and attain all these things.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् ।<br />पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥१२॥
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्व्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा ।<br />असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयञ्चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥१३॥
arjuna uvācha
paraṁ brahma paraṁ dhāma pavitraṁ paramaṁ bhavān<br />puruṣaṁ śāśvataṁ divyam ādi-devam ajaṁ vibhum [12]
āhus tvām ṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣir nāradas tathā<br />asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayañ chaiva bravīṣi me [13]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">ahaṁ manye</span>)–I accept; <span class="e2">bhavān</span>–Your grace;<span class="e2"> param brahma</span>–as the Supreme Brahma, directly the Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> param dhāma</span>–the supreme Śyāmasundar form, the supreme refuge;<span class="e2"> paramam</span>–the supreme;<span class="e2"> pavitram</span>–sanctifier, saviour. <span class="e2">sarve</span>–All; <span class="e2">ṛṣayaḥ</span>–the sages;<span class="e2"> deva-ṛṣiḥ nāradaḥ</span>–Nārad Muni, the saint among the gods; <span class="e2">asitaḥ</span>–Asita;<span class="e2"> devalaḥ</span>–Devala;<span class="e2"> tathā vyāsaḥ</span>–and the great sage Vyās; <span class="e2">āhuḥ</span>–call; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You;<span class="e2"> śāśvatam puruṣam</span>–the eternal personality; <span class="e2">divyam</span>–the self-manifest;<span class="e2"> ādi-devam</span>–the original Lord; <span class="e2">ajam</span>–the birthless; <span class="e2">vibhum</span>–the all-pervading Lord, the fountain-head of all opulences;<span class="e2"> cha svayam eva</span>–and You, Yourself;<span class="e2"> bravīṣi me</span>–are now declaring this to me. [12–13]
12–13 Arjuna said: O Lord, You are the supreme Brahma, the supreme shelter, and the supreme saviour. All the prominent sages such as Devarṣi Nārad, Asita, Devala, and Vyās have described You as the self-manifest, eternal Supreme Person, the fountainhead of all opulences and the root of all existence from whose divine play everything emanates. And now You are personally declaring this to be the truth.
सर्व्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव ।<br />न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥१४॥
sarvam etad ṛtaṁ manye yan māṁ vadasi keśava<br />na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṁ vidur devā na dānavāḥ [14]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">keśava</span>–O Keśava; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">manye</span>–I accept; <span class="e2">ṛtam</span>–as factual;<span class="e2"> sarvam etat</span>–all;<span class="e2"> yat vadasi</span>–You have told; <span class="e2">mām</span>–me. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhagavan</span>–O Lord; <span class="e2">hi</span>–indeed;<span class="e2"> na devāḥ na dānavāḥ</span>–neither the demigods nor the demons; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–know; <span class="e2">te</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> vyaktim</span>–personality in full. [14]
14 O Keśava, I fully accept all that You have said. O Lord, indeed neither demigods nor demons know Your personality in full.
स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम ।<br />भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥१५॥
svayam evātmanātmānaṁ vettha tvaṁ puruṣottama<br />bhūta-bhāvana bhūteśa deva-deva jagat-pate [15]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> puruṣottama</span>–O Supreme Person; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhūta-bhāvana</span>–O universal father; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhūta-īśa</span>–O Lord of all beings; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> deva-deva</span>–O God of the gods; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> jagat-pate</span>–O Jagannāth, Lord of the universe; <span class="e2">eva</span>–only; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–You; <span class="e2">svayam</span>–Yourself; <span class="e2">vettha</span>–know;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–Yourself; <span class="e2">ātmanā</span>–by Yourself—by Your own potency. [15]
15 O Supreme Person, universal father, Lord of all beings, God of the gods, Lord of the universe! Only You can know Yourself, by Your own divine potency.
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।<br />याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥१६॥
vaktum arhasy aśeṣeṇa divyā hy ātma-vibhūtayaḥ<br />yābhir vibhūtibhir lokān imāṁs tvaṁ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi [16]
<span class="e2">hi </span>(<span class="e2">tvam</span>)<span class="e2"> vaktum arhasi</span>–You may kindly describe;<span class="e2"> aśeṣeṇa</span>–elaborately; (<span class="e2">tāḥ</span>)–those; <span class="e2">divyāḥ</span>–divine;<span class="e2"> ātma-vibhūtayaḥ</span>–personal opulences;<span class="e2"> yābhiḥ vibhūtibhiḥ</span>–by which opulences; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–You;<span class="e2"> tiṣṭhasi</span>–are present; <span class="e2">vyāpya</span>–pervading;<span class="e2"> imān lokān</span>–all these worlds. [16]
16 Please describe to me in full Your personal opulences by which You pervade all these worlds.
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् ।<br />केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥१७॥
kathaṁ vidyām ahaṁ yogiṁs tvāṁ sadā parichintayan<br />keṣu keṣu cha bhāveṣu chintyo ’si bhagavan mayā [17]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">yogin</span>–O Lord of yogamāyā, Lord of divine potency; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhagavan</span>–O Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">katham</span>–how can; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–be constantly;<span class="e2"> parichintayan</span>–absorbed in thought; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–of You; <span class="e2">vidyām</span>–know; (<span class="e2">tvām</span>)–You; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> keṣu keṣu bhāveṣu</span>–in which forms; <span class="e2">asi</span>–are; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You;<span class="e2"> chintyaḥ</span>–to be thought of; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by me? [17]
17 O Lord of divine potency, how can I be constantly absorbed in thought of You, how can I know You, and in which forms should I think of You?
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिञ्च जनार्द्दन ।<br />भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥१८॥
vistareṇātmano yogaṁ vibhūtiñ cha janārdana<br />bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptir hi śṛṇvato nāsti me ’mṛtam [18]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> janārdana</span>–O Janārdan;<span class="e2"> kathaya</span>–please describe; <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–again;<span class="e2"> vistareṇa</span>–in detail;<span class="e2"> ātmanaḥ yogam</span>–the process of devotional union with You (bhakti-yoga);<span class="e2"> vibhūtim cha</span>–and Your opulences; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since;<span class="e2"> śṛṇvataḥ</span>–hearing; <span class="e2">amṛtam</span>–Your ambrosial words; <span class="e2">me</span>–my; <span class="e2">tṛptiḥ</span>–satiation; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–does not occur. [18]
18 O Janārdan, please again describe in detail Your opulences and the path of devotion to You, for I never tire of hearing Your ambrosial words.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।<br />प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥१९॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hy ātma-vibhūtayaḥ<br />prādhānyataḥ kuru-śreṣṭha nāsty anto vistarasya me [19]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said:<span class="e2"> hanta kuru-śreṣṭha</span>–O best of the Kurus;<span class="e2"> kathayiṣyāmi</span>–I will tell; <span class="e2">te</span>–you;<span class="e2"> prādhānyataḥ</span>–the principal; <span class="e2">divyāḥ</span>–transcendental;<span class="e2"> ātma-vibhūtayaḥ</span>–personal opulences, manifest by My divine potency; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–there is no; <span class="e2">antaḥ</span>–end;<span class="e2"> vistarasya me</span>–to the expanse of My glories. [19]
19 The Supreme Lord said: O Arjuna, best of the Kurus, My glories are unlimited, so I shall tell you of My principal transcendental opulences, manifest in this world by My divine potency.
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्व्वभूताशयस्थितः ।<br />अहमादिश्च मध्यञ्च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥२०॥
aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūtāśaya-sthitaḥ<br />aham ādiś cha madhyañ cha bhūtānām anta eva cha [20]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> guḍākeśa</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> aham ātmā</span>–I am the Supersoul;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ</span>–situated within the heart of all beings; <span class="e2">cha eva</span>–and;<span class="e2"> aham ādiḥ</span>–I am the beginning;<span class="e2"> madhyam cha</span>–middle;<span class="e2"> antaḥ cha</span>–and end;<span class="e2"> bhūtānām</span>–of all beings. [20]
20 O conqueror of sleep, I am the Supersoul within the hearts of all beings, and I am their beginning, middle, and end.
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् ।<br />मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥२१॥
ādityānām ahaṁ viṣṇur jyotiṣāṁ ravir aṁśumān<br />marīchir marutām asmi nakṣatrāṇām ahaṁ śaśī [21]
<span class="e2">ādityānām</span>–Of the twelve Ādityas;<span class="e2"> aham asmi viṣṇuḥ</span>–I am the Āditya known as Viṣṇu.<span class="e2"> jyotiṣām</span>–Of the luminaries; <span class="e2">aham </span>(<span class="e2">asmi</span>)–I am;<span class="e2"> aṁśumān</span>–the blazing; <span class="e2">raviḥ</span>–sun;<span class="e2"> marutām</span>–Of the Vāyu demigods;<span class="e2"> marīchiḥ</span>–(I am) the Vāyu known as Marīchi;<span class="e2"> nakṣatrāṇām</span>–and of the stars; <span class="e2">śaśī</span>–(I am) the moon. [21]
21 Of the twelve Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; of the luminaries I am the radiant sun; of the Vāyus I am Marīchi, of stars I am the moon.
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः ।<br />इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥२२॥
vedānāṁ sāma-vedo ’smi devānām asmi vāsavaḥ<br />indriyāṇāṁ manaś chāsmi bhūtānām asmi chetanā [22]
<span class="e2">vedānām</span>–Of the Vedas; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> sāma-vedaḥ</span>–the <span class="e3">Sāma-veda</span>.<span class="e2"> devānām</span>–Of the demigods; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> vāsavaḥ</span>–Indra.<span class="e2"> indriyāṇām</span>–Of the senses; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> chetanā</span>–the life;<span class="e2"> bhūtānām</span>–of all that lives. [22]
22 Of the Vedas, I am <span class="e3">Sāma-veda</span>; of the demigods I am Indra; of the senses I am the mind, and I am the life of all that lives.
रुद्राणां शंकरश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् ।<br />वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥२३॥
rudrāṇāṁ śaṅkaraś chāsmi vitteśo yakṣa-rakṣasām<br />vasūnāṁ pāvakaś chāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇām aham [23]
<span class="e2">rudrāṇām</span>–Of the eleven Rudras;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> śaṅkaraḥ</span>–Śiva; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> yakṣa-rakṣasām</span>–of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> vitta-īśaḥ</span>–Kubera.<span class="e2"> vasūnām</span>–Of the eight Vasus;<span class="e2"> pāvakaḥ</span>–(I am) Agni; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> śikhariṇām</span>–of the mountains; <span class="e2">meruḥ</span>–(I am) Sumeru. [23]
23 Of the eleven Rudras I am Śaṅkar, and of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas I am Kubera. Of the eight Vasus I am Agni, and of mountains I am Sumeru.
पुरोधसाञ्च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।<br />सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥२४॥
purodhasāñ cha mukhyaṁ māṁ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim<br />senānīnām ahaṁ skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ [24]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> bṛhaspatim</span>–as Bṛhaspati;<span class="e2"> mukhyam purodhasām</span>–the chief among priests engaged in sacrifice.<span class="e2"> senānīnām</span>–Of generals;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> skandaḥ</span>–Kārtikeya; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> sarasām</span>–among reservoirs;<span class="e2"> sāgaraḥ</span>–(I am) the ocean. [24]
24 O Pārtha, you should know Me as the chief of priests, Bṛhaspati; of generals I am Kārtikeya, and of reservoirs I am the ocean.
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् ।<br />यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥२५॥
maharṣīṇāṁ bhṛgur ahaṁ girām asmy ekam akṣaram<br />yajñānāṁ japa-yajño ’smi sthāvarāṇāṁ himālayaḥ [25]
<span class="e2">mahā-ṛṣīnām</span>–Of great sages;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">bhṛguḥ</span>–Bhṛgu. <span class="e2">girām</span>–Of sound vibrations; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> ekam akṣaram</span>–the praṇava monosyllable, Oṁkār.<span class="e2"> yajñānām</span>–Of all types of sacrifices; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> japa-yajñaḥ</span>–sacrifice in the form of meditative chanting of the holy names; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and;<span class="e2"> sthāvarāṇām</span>–of the immovable;<span class="e2"> himālayaḥ</span>–(I am) the Himālayas. [25]
25 Of great sages, I am Bhṛgu; of sound vibrations, I am Om; of all sacrifices, I am the chanting of the Holy Names; and of the immovable, I am the Himālayas.
अश्वत्थः सर्व्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणाञ्च नारदः ।<br />गन्धर्व्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥२६॥
aśvatthaḥ sarva-vṛkṣāṇāṁ devarṣīṇāñ cha nāradaḥ<br />gandharvāṇāṁ chitrarathaḥ siddhānāṁ kapilo muniḥ [26]
<span class="e2">sarva-vṛkṣāṇām</span>–Of all trees;<span class="e2"> aśvatthaḥ</span>–(I am) the Aśvattha tree;<span class="e2"> deva-ṛṣīṇām</span>–of godly sages;<span class="e2"> nāradaḥ</span>–(I am) Nārad Muni.<span class="e2"> gandharvāṇām</span>–Of Gandharvas;<span class="e2"> chitrarathaḥ</span>–(I am) Chitraratha; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> siddhānām</span>–of perfected beings;<span class="e2"> kapilaḥ muniḥ</span>–(I am) the sage Kapila. [26]
26 I am the Aśvattha among trees, Nārad of godly sages, Chitraratha of heavenly singers, and Kapila Muni of perfected beings.
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् ।<br />ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणाञ्च नराधिपम् ॥२७॥
uchchaiḥśravasam aśvānāṁ viddhi mām amṛtodbhavam<br />airāvataṁ gajendrāṇāṁ narāṇāñ cha narādhipam [27]
<span class="e2">aśvānām</span>–Of horses; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know;<span class="e2"> mām uchchaiḥ-śravasam</span>–Me as Uchchaiḥśravā;<span class="e2"> amṛta-udbhavam</span>–who was born of the churning of nectar;<span class="e2"> gaja-indrāṇām</span>–Of elephants;<span class="e2"> airāvatam</span>–(I am) Airāvata; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> narāṇām</span>–among men;<span class="e2"> nara-adhipam</span>–(I am) the king. [27]
27 Among horses know Me as Uchchaiḥśravā, who was born of nectar; know Me as Airāvata among elephants, and king among men.
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् ।<br />प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥२८॥
āyudhānām ahaṁ vajraṁ dhenūnām asmi kāmadhuk<br />prajanaś chāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ [28]
<span class="e2">āyudhānām</span>–Of weapons;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">vajram</span>–the thunderbolt, the weapon of Lord Indra.<span class="e2"> dhenūnām</span>–Of cows; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> kāma-dhuk</span>–the desire-fulfilling cow. (<span class="e2">kandarpāṇām</span>)–Of cupids; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> prajanaḥ</span>–the progenitor;<span class="e2"> kandarpaḥ</span>–Cupid; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> sarpāṇām</span>–of single-headed venomous snakes;<span class="e2"> vāsukiḥ</span>–(I am) Vāsuki, the king of snakes. [28]
28 Of weapons I am the thunderbolt, and of cows I am the heavenly desire-fulfilling cow. Of cupids I am the progenitor, and of one-headed venomous snakes I am Vāsuki, the king of snakes.
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् ।<br />पितॄणामर्य्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥२९॥
anantaś chāsmi nāgānāṁ varuṇo yādasām aham<br />pitṝṇām aryamā chāsmi yamaḥ saṁyamatām aham [29]
<span class="e2">nāgānām</span>–Of the multi-headed non-poisonous serpents;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> anantaḥ</span>–the divine serpent Ananta; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> yādasām</span>–of aquatics;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> varuṇaḥ</span>–Varuṇadev.<span class="e2"> pitṝṇām</span>–Of the deified ancestors; <span class="e2">aryamā</span>–(I am) Aryamā; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> saṁyamatām</span>–among chastisers; <span class="e2">yamaḥ</span>–Yamarāja. [29]
29 Of the multi-headed non-poisonous serpents I am the Ananta Nāga, and of aquatics I am Varuṇadev. Of the deified ancestors I am Aryamā, and of ministers I am Yamarāj, the lord of punishment.
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् ।<br />मृगाणाञ्च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥३०॥
prahlādaś chāsmi daityānāṁ kālaḥ kalayatām aham<br />mṛgāṇāñ cha mṛgendro ’haṁ vainateyaś cha pakṣiṇām [30]
<span class="e2">daityānām</span>–Of the descendents of Diti;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> prahlādaḥ</span>–Prahlād;<span class="e2"> kalayatām cha</span>–and of subduers; <span class="e2">aham </span>(<span class="e2">asmi</span>)–I am; <span class="e2">kālaḥ</span>–time; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> mṛgāṇām</span>–of animals;<span class="e2"> mṛga-indraḥ</span>–the lion; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> pakṣiṇām</span>–of birds;<span class="e2"> vainateyaḥ</span>–Garuḍa. [30]
30 Of the Daityas I am Prahlād, and of subjugators I am time. Of animals I am the lion, and of birds I am Garuḍa.
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् ।<br />झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥३१॥
pavanaḥ pavatām asmi rāmaḥ śastra-bhṛtām aham<br />jhaṣāṇāṁ makaraś chāsmi srotasām asmi jāhnavī [31]
<span class="e2">pavatām</span>–Of sanctifiers or of the rapid;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> pavanaḥ</span>–wind.<span class="e2"> śastra-bhṛtām</span>–Of weapon-wielding heroes; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">rāmaḥ</span>–Lord Paraśurām.<span class="e2"> jhaṣāṇām</span>–Among fish; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> makaraḥ</span>–the shark; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> srotasām</span>–of rivers;<span class="e2"> jāhnavī</span>–(I am) the Jāhnavī, the Ganges. [31]
31 Of sanctifiers I am the wind; of weapon-wielding heroes I am Lord Paraśurām; among fish I am the shark, and of rivers I am the Ganges.
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यञ्चैवाहमर्ज्जुन ।<br />अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥३२॥
sargāṇām ādir antaś cha madhyañ chaivāham arjuna<br />adhyātma-vidyā vidyānāṁ vādaḥ pravadatām aham [32]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> sargāṇām</span>–of the manifest;<span class="e2"> aham eva ādiḥ</span>–I am the beginning; <span class="e2">antaḥ</span>–end;<span class="e2"> madhyam cha</span>–and middle.<span class="e2"> vidyānām</span>–Of knowledge;<span class="e2"> adhyātma-vidyā</span>–(I am) self-knowledge; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> aham vādaḥ</span>–I am the philosophy;<span class="e2"> pravadatām</span>–of philosophers. [32]
32 O Arjuna, of all that is manifest I am the beginning, middle, and end. Of all wisdom I am self-knowledge, and I am the philosophy of philosophers.
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च ।<br />अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥३३॥
akṣarāṇām akāro ’smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya cha<br />aham evākṣayaḥ kālo dhātāhaṁ viśvato-mukhaḥ [33]
<span class="e2">akṣarāṇām</span>–Of letters;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">a-kāraḥ</span>–the letter ‘a’; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> sāmāsikasya</span>–of compound words;<span class="e2"> dvandvaḥ</span>–(I am) the dual compound word.<span class="e2"> aham eva akṣayaḥ kālaḥ</span>–I alone am the eternal time flow; (<span class="e2">sraṣṭṛām cha</span>)–and of creators;<span class="e2"> viśvataḥ mukhaḥ</span>–four-headed; <span class="e2">dhātā</span>–Lord Brahmā. [33]
33 Of the primary letters of the alphabet I am the letter ‘a’, and of compound words I am the dual. I alone am the endless flow of time, and of universal creators I am the four-headed Lord Brahmā.
मृत्युः सर्व्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् ।<br />कीर्त्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥३४॥
mṛtyuḥ sarva-haraś chāham udbhavaś cha bhaviṣyatām<br />kīrtiḥ śrīr vāk cha nārīṇāṁ smṛtir medhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā [34]
(<span class="e2">haraṇa-kāriṇām</span>)–Of plunderers;<span class="e2"> aham mṛtyuḥ</span>–I am death;<span class="e2"> sarva-haraḥ</span>–the vanquisher of all; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> bhaviṣyatām</span>–of the predestined six transformations of the living beings;<span class="e2"> udbhavaḥ</span>–(I am) the first, as birth; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> nārīṇām</span>–of feminine qualities; <span class="e2">kīrtiḥ</span>–fame; <span class="e2">śrīḥ</span>–beauty; <span class="e2">vāk</span>–perfect speech; <span class="e2">smṛtiḥ</span>–remembrance; <span class="e2">medhā</span>–intelligence (regarding scriptural wisdom); <span class="e2">dhṛtiḥ</span>–patience; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">kṣamā</span>–forgiveness (or the seven wives of Dharma). [34]
34 Of plunderers I am all-devouring death, and of the predestined six transformations I am birth, the foremost. Of the feminine qualities I am fame, beauty, perfect speech, remembrance, intelligence, patience, and forgiveness—the seven wives of Dharma.
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् ।<br />मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥३५॥
bṛhat-sāma tathā sāmnāṁ gāyatrī chhandasām aham<br />māsānāṁ mārga-śīrṣo ’ham ṛtūnāṁ kusumākaraḥ [35]
<span class="e2">sāmnām</span>–Of all the mantras in the <span class="e3">Sāma-veda</span>;<span class="e2"> bṛhat-sāma</span>–(I am) the mantra prayer to Lord Indra; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–and;<span class="e2"> chhandasām</span>–of metrical mantras;<span class="e2"> aham gāyatrī</span>–I am the gāyatrī mantra.<span class="e2"> māsānām</span>–Of the months;<span class="e2"> aham mārga-śīrṣaḥ</span>–I am the month Agrahāyaṇ, the month of harvest (mid-November to mid-December). (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–And; <span class="e2">ṛtūnām</span>–of the seasons;<span class="e2"> kusuma-ākaraḥ</span>–(I am) spring. [35]
35 Of all the mantras in the <span class="e3">Sāma-veda</span> I am the Bṛhatsāma prayer to Lord Indra, and of metrical mantras I am the holy gāyatrī mantra. Of the months I am the foremost, Agrahāyaṇ, and of the seasons I am flowerbearing spring.
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ।<br />जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥३६॥
dyūtaṁ chhalayatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham<br />jayo ’smi vyavasāyo ’smi sattvaṁ sattvavatām aham [36]
<span class="e2">chhalayatām</span>–Of cheats;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">dyūtam</span>–gambling.<span class="e2"> tejasvinām</span>–Of the splendid;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">tejaḥ</span>–splendour. <span class="e2">asmi</span>–(I) am; <span class="e2">jayaḥ</span>–victory;<span class="e2"> vyavasāyaḥ</span>–perseverance; (<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–the power of truth;<span class="e2"> sattva-vatām</span>–of the truthful. [36]
36 I am the gambling of cheats, and the glory of the glorious. I am victory, I am perseverance, and I am the power of truth of the honest.
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः ।<br />मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशनाः कविः ॥३७॥
vṛṣṇīnāṁ vāsudevo ’smi pāṇḍavānāṁ dhanañjayaḥ<br />munīnām apy ahaṁ vyāsaḥ kavīnām uśanāḥ kaviḥ [37]
<span class="e2">vṛṣṇīnām</span>–Of the Yādavas;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> vāsudevaḥ</span>–Vāsudev;<span class="e2"> pāṇḍavānām</span>–of the Pāṇḍavas;<span class="e2"> dhanañjayaḥ</span>–Arjuna;<span class="e2"> munīnām</span>–of the sages; <span class="e2">vyāsaḥ</span>–Vyāsadev; <span class="e2">api</span>–and;<span class="e2"> kavīnām</span>–of knowers of the scriptures;<span class="e2"> uśanāḥ kaviḥ</span>–Paṇḍit Śukrāchārya. [37]
37 Of the Yādavas I am Vāsudev, of the Pāṇḍavas I am Arjuna, of the sages I am Vyāsadev, and of knowers of the scriptures I am Śukrāchārya.
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् ।<br />मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥३८॥
daṇḍo damayatām asmi nītir asmi jigīṣatām<br />maunaṁ chaivāsmi guhyānāṁ jñānaṁ jñānavatām aham [38]
<span class="e2">damayatām</span>–Of law enforcers;<span class="e2"> aham asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">daṇḍaḥ</span>–punishment.<span class="e2"> jigīṣatām</span>–Of those desiring to conquer; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">nītiḥ</span>–political wisdom.<span class="e2"> guhyānām</span>–Of all secrets; (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">maunam</span>–silence; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> jñāna-vatām</span>–of the learned;<span class="e2"> jñānam eva</span>–(I am) knowledge. [38]
38 I am the punishment meted out by the enforcers of the law, I am the political wisdom of those desiring to conquer. I am the silence of all secrets, I am the wisdom of the wise.
यच्चापि सर्व्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्ज्जुन ।<br />न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥३९॥
yach chāpi sarva-bhūtānāṁ bījaṁ tad aham arjuna<br />na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṁ charācharam [39]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yat</span>–whatever is; <span class="e2">bījam</span>–the seed;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtānām</span>–of all beings;<span class="e2"> aham tat api</span>–I am that.<span class="e2"> yat tat syāt</span>–Whatever may exist;<span class="e2"> chara-acharam</span>–moving and stationary; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–there is no; <span class="e2">bhūtam</span>–existence;<span class="e2"> mayā vinā</span>–without Me. [39]
39 O Arjuna, whatever is considered the origin of all beings, I am that. Nothing, whether stationary or moving, can exist without Me.
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप ।<br />एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥४०॥
nānto ’sti mama divyānāṁ vibhūtīnāṁ parantapa<br />eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūter vistaro mayā [40]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> parantapa</span>–O chastiser of the enemy; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–there is no; <span class="e2">antaḥ</span>–end;<span class="e2"> mama divyānām vibhūtīnām</span>–of My divine opulences; <span class="e2">eṣaḥ tu</span>–so;<span class="e2"> uddeśataḥ</span>–an indication;<span class="e2"> vistaraḥ</span>–of the expanse;<span class="e2"> vibhūteḥ</span>–of these opulences;<span class="e2"> proktaḥ</span>–has been mentioned; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me. [40]
40 O conqueror of the enemy, My divine glories have no end. I have given you but an indication of them.
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्ज्जितमेव वा ।<br />तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम् ॥४१॥
yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ śrīmad ūrjitam eva vā<br />tat tad evāvagachchha tvaṁ mama tejo ’ṁśa-sambhavam [41]
<span class="e2">yat yat eva</span>–Of each and every;<span class="e2"> vibhūtimat</span>–magnificent; <span class="e2">śrīmat</span>–beautiful; <span class="e2">vā</span>–or;<span class="e2"> ūrjitam</span>–glorious;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–existence; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> ava-gachchha eva</span>–should know; <span class="e2">tat tat</span>–each of them;<span class="e2"> aṁśa-sambhavam</span>–as born of a portion;<span class="e2"> mama tejaḥ</span>–of My power. [41]
41 Know for certain that whatever is magnificent, beautiful or glorious is born of but a fraction of My power.
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्ज्जुन ।<br />विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् ॥४२॥
athavā bahunaitena kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna<br />viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam ekāṁśena sthito jagat [42]
