(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">athavā</span>–however;<span class="e2"> tava kim</span>–what is your need;<span class="e2"> jñātena</span>–of knowing; <span class="e2">etena</span>–this; <span class="e2">bahunā</span>–elaborately?<span class="e2"> viṣṭabhya</span>–Supporting; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam</span>–entire; <span class="e2">jagat</span>–universe;<span class="e2"> aham sthitaḥ</span>–I am situated;<span class="e2"> eka-aṁśena</span>–in My fractional expansion as the Supersoul of material nature—Mahāviṣṇu or Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī Viṣṇu. [42]
42 But, O Arjuna, what is the need of elaborating further on My opulences? I support this entire universe in My fractional expansion as the Supersoul of material nature.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे विभूतियोगो नाम दशमोऽध्यायः ॥१०॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde<br />vibhūti-yogo nāma daśamo ’dhyāyaḥ [10]
End of Chapter Ten<br />The Divine Glories of the Lord<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

एकादशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Eleven
Viśva-rūpa-darśana-yoga <br />The Vision of the Universal Form
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् ।<br />यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥१॥
arjuna uvācha
mad-anugrahāya paramaṁ guhyam adhyātma-saṁjñitam<br />yat tvayoktaṁ vachas tena moho ’yaṁ vigato mama [1]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: <span class="e2">ayam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> mama mohaḥ</span>–ignorance of mine, about You;<span class="e2"> vigataḥ</span>–has been dispelled; <span class="e2">tena</span>–by that;<span class="e2"> paramam</span>–most; <span class="e2">guhyam</span>–secret; <span class="e2">vachaḥ</span>–revelation;<span class="e2"> adhyātma-saṁjñitam</span>–pertaining to the divine glories of Your Supreme Self; <span class="e2">yat</span>–as; <span class="e2">uktam</span>–described; <span class="e2">tvayā</span>–by You;<span class="e2"> mat-anugrahāya</span>–out of Your mercy for me.[1]
1 Arjuna said: By Your grace, You have revealed Your hidden treasure to me, and my ignorance of Your Supreme Self has been dispelled.
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया ।<br />त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥२॥
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṁ śrutau vistaraśo mayā<br />tvattaḥ kamala-patrākṣa māhātmyam api chāvyayam [2]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kamala-patra-akṣa</span>–O Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus flower; <span class="e2">hi</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> vistaraśaḥ</span>–elaborately;<span class="e2"> bhava-apyayau</span>–the manifestation and withdrawal;<span class="e2"> bhūtānām</span>–of all beings; <span class="e2">śrutau</span>–has been heard; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by me;<span class="e2"> tvattaḥ</span>–from You; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">tava</span>)–Your;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–inexhaustible;<span class="e2"> māhātmyam</span>–glories; <span class="e2">api</span>–too; (<span class="e2">śrutam</span>)–have been heard. [2]
2 O beautiful lotus-eyed Lord, I have heard Your elaborate description of the manifestation and dissolution of the living beings, and I have also heard Your description of Your inexhaustible glories.
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर ।<br />द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥३॥
evam etad yathāttha tvam ātmānaṁ parameśvara<br />draṣṭum ichchhāmi te rūpam aiśvaraṁ puruṣottama [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> parama-īśvara</span>–O Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">yathā</span>–as; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–You; <span class="e2">āttha</span>–have spoken;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–of the glories pertaining to Yourself; <span class="e2">evam</span>–such; <span class="e2">etat</span>–is so; (<span class="e2">tathāpi</span>)–yet; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> puruṣa-uttama</span>–O Supreme Person; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> ichchhāmi</span>–I wish;<span class="e2"> draṣṭum</span>–to see; <span class="e2">te</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> aiśvaram</span>–glorious; <span class="e2">rūpam</span>–form. [3]
3 O Lord, You have perfectly described Your Supreme Self. Yet, O Puruṣottam, I wish to see this glorious form of Yours.
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो ।<br />योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् ॥४॥
manyase yadi tach chhakyaṁ mayā draṣṭum iti prabho<br />yogeśvara tato me tvaṁ darśayātmānam avyayam [4]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">prabho</span>–O Lord; <span class="e2">yadi</span>–if;<span class="e2"> manyase iti</span>–You consider; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> śakyam draṣṭum</span>–is possible to be seen; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by me; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–then; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> yoga-īśvara</span>–O all-powerful one; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–You;<span class="e2"> darśaya</span>–please reveal;<span class="e2"> avyayam ātmānam</span>–Your imperishable Self; <span class="e2">me</span>–to me. [4]
4 O Yogeśvar, I implore Thee, if You consider it possible for me to see it, please reveal Your imperishable form to me.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।<br />नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥५॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo ’tha sahasraśaḥ<br />nānā-vidhāni divyāni nānā-varṇākṛtīni cha [5]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha; <span class="e2">paśya</span>–see; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> śataśaḥ</span>–hundreds;<span class="e2"> atha sahasraśaḥ</span>–of thousands of;<span class="e2"> divyāni</span>–divine; <span class="e2">rūpāṇi</span>–forms;<span class="e2"> nānā-vidhāni</span>–of many kinds;<span class="e2"> nānā-varṇa-ākṛtīni cha</span>–and many colours and shapes. [5]
5 The Supreme Lord said: O Pārtha, behold My innumerable divine forms of many kinds, colours, and shapes.
पश्यादित्यान्वसून् रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा ।<br />बहून्यदृष्टपूर्व्वाणि पश्याश्चर्य्याणि भारत ॥६॥
paśyādityān vasūn rudrān aśvinau marutas tathā<br />bahūny adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi paśyāścharyāṇi bhārata [6]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O descendant of Bharat; <span class="e2">paśya</span>–see;<span class="e2"> ādityān</span>–the twelve Ādityas; <span class="e2">vasūn</span>–the eight Vasus; <span class="e2">rudrān</span>–the eleven Rudras;<span class="e2"> aśvinau</span>–the Aśvinī twins;<span class="e2"> tathā marutaḥ</span>–and the forty-nine Vāyus. <span class="e2">paśya</span>–See; <span class="e2">bahūni</span>–many;<span class="e2"> āścharyāṇi</span>–wondrous forms;<span class="e2"> adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi</span>–hitherto unseen. [6]
6 O Bhārat, behold the gods—Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Aśvinī Kumāras, and Vāyus. Behold many wondrous forms, hitherto unseen.
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् ।<br />मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥७॥
ihaikasthaṁ jagat kṛtsnaṁ paśyādya sa-charācharam<br />mama dehe guḍākeśa yach chānyad draṣṭum ichchhasi [7]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> guḍākeśa</span>–O conqueror of sleep;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam</span>–the whole; <span class="e2">jagat</span>–universe;<span class="e2"> sa-chara-acharam</span>–including moving and stationary beings;<span class="e2"> eka-stham</span>–is situated in one place;<span class="e2"> iha dehe</span>–in this form; <span class="e2">mama</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yat</span>–whatever; <span class="e2">anyat</span>–else; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you;<span class="e2"> ichchhasi</span>–wish;<span class="e2"> draṣṭum</span>–to see; <span class="e2">paśya</span>–see; (<span class="e2">tadapi</span>)–that too; <span class="e2">adya</span>–today. [7]
7 O vigilant Arjuna, behold in one place, in this form of Mine, the whole universe of moving and stationary beings, or anything else you desire to see.
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा ।<br />दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥८॥
na tu māṁ śakyase draṣṭum anenaiva svachakṣuṣā<br />divyaṁ dadāmi te chakṣuḥ paśya me yogam aiśvaram [8]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But; <span class="e2">anena</span>–with these;<span class="e2"> svachakṣuṣā eva</span>–present eyes of yours; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you;<span class="e2"> na śakyase</span>–cannot;<span class="e2"> draṣṭum</span>–see; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me. <span class="e2">dadāmi</span>–(So) I give; <span class="e2">te</span>–you; <span class="e2">divyam</span>–divine;<span class="e2"> chakṣuḥ</span>–eyes. <span class="e2">paśya</span>–Behold; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> aiśvaram</span>–opulences; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–of divine potency. [8]
8 But you cannot see Me with these eyes, so I give you divine vision. Behold My divine opulences.
सञ्जय उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः ।<br />दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् ॥९॥
sañjaya uvācha
evam uktvā tato rājan mahā-yogeśvaro hariḥ<br />darśayāmāsa pārthāya paramaṁ rūpam aiśvaram [9]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">rājan</span>–O King Dhṛtarāṣṭra; <span class="e2">uktvā</span>–speaking; <span class="e2">evam</span>–in this way;<span class="e2"> mahā-yoga-īśvaraḥ</span>–the omnipotent Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">hariḥ</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–then;<span class="e2"> darśayāmāsa</span>–revealed;<span class="e2"> paramam</span>–His almighty;<span class="e2"> aiśvaram</span>–magnificent; <span class="e2">rūpam</span>–form;<span class="e2"> pārthāya</span>–to Arjuna. [9]
9 Sañjaya said: O King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, speaking thus to Arjuna, the omnipotent Supreme Lord Śrī Hari revealed His magnificent, almighty form.
अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् ।<br />अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम् ॥१०॥
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् ।<br />सर्व्वाश्चर्य्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् ॥११॥
aneka-vaktra-nayanam anekādbhuta-darśanam<br />aneka-divyābharaṇaṁ divyānekodyatāyudham [10]
divya-mālyāmbara-dharaṁ divya-gandhānulepanam<br />sarvāścharyamayaṁ devam anantaṁ viśvato-mukham [11]
(<span class="e2">hariḥ</span>)–The Supreme Lord; (<span class="e2">rūpaṁ darśayāmāsa</span>)–revealed His form;<span class="e2"> aneka-vaktra-nayanam</span>–of many mouths and eyes;<span class="e2"> aneka-adbhuta-darśanam</span>–many wonders;<span class="e2"> aneka-divya-ābharaṇam</span>–many effulgent ornaments;<span class="e2"> divya-aneka-udyata-āyudham</span>–and many raised gleaming weapons;<span class="e2"> divya-mālya-ambara-dharam</span>–resplendently garlanded and dressed;<span class="e2"> divya-gandha-anulepanam</span>–anointed with celestial fragrances;<span class="e2"> sarva-āścharya-mayam</span>–all-wonderful;<span class="e2"> anantam</span>–unlimited; <span class="e2">devam</span>–effulgent;<span class="e2"> viśvataḥ-mukham</span>–and facing all directions of the universe. [10–11]
10–11 The Lord revealed His effulgent, omnipresent, all-wonderful universal form of many mouths and eyes, many marvels, effulgent dress and garlands, anointed with celestial fragrances, many dazzling ornaments, and gleaming upraised weapons.
दिवि सूर्य्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता ।<br />यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥१२॥
divi sūrya-sahasrasya bhaved yugapad utthitā<br />yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syād bhāsas tasya mahātmanaḥ [12]
<span class="e2">yadi</span>–If;<span class="e2"> yugapat</span>–simultaneously; <span class="e2">bhāḥ</span>–the effulgence;<span class="e2"> sūrya-sahasrasya</span>–of a thousand suns;<span class="e2"> utthitā bhavet</span>–appeared; <span class="e2">divi</span>–in the sky; (<span class="e2">tarhi</span>)–then; <span class="e2">syāt</span>–perhaps; <span class="e2">sā</span>–that; <span class="e2">sadṛśī</span>–might resemble; <span class="e2">bhāsaḥ</span>–the effulgence;<span class="e2"> tasya mahā-ātmanaḥ</span>–of this supreme universal form. [12]
12 The brilliance of a thousand suns appearing simultaneously in the sky might resemble the effulgence of this great universal form of the Lord.
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा ।<br />अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥१३॥
tatraika-sthaṁ jagat kṛtsnaṁ pravibhaktam anekadhā<br />apaśyad deva-devasya śarīre pāṇḍavas tadā [13]
<span class="e2">tadā</span>–Then; <span class="e2">tatra</span>–there on the battlefield;<span class="e2"> pāṇḍavaḥ</span>–Arjuna;<span class="e2"> apaśyat</span>–saw; <span class="e2">śarīre</span>–in the body;<span class="e2"> deva-devasya</span>–of the God of gods;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam</span>–the entire; <span class="e2">jagat</span>–universe;<span class="e2"> eka-stham</span>–situated in one;<span class="e2"> aneka-dhā</span>–variously;<span class="e2"> pravibhaktam</span>–divided. [13]
13 In that moment, there on the battlefield, Arjuna saw the entire multi-faceted universe in one, within the body of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme God of gods.
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः ।<br />प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥१४॥
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭa-romā dhanañjayaḥ<br />praṇamya śirasā devaṁ kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata [14]
<span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–After that; (<span class="e2">san</span>)–being;<span class="e2"> vismaya-āviṣṭaḥ</span>–astonished;<span class="e2"> hṛṣṭa-romāḥ</span>–with body hairs standing on end;<span class="e2"> saḥ dhanañjayaḥ</span>–Arjuna;<span class="e2"> praṇamya</span>–offering obeisances; <span class="e2">śirasā</span>–with bowed head; <span class="e2">devam</span>–unto Lord Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> abhāṣata</span>–spoke;<span class="e2"> kṛta-añjaliḥ</span>–placing his palms together in prayer. [14]
14 Astonished, the hairs of his body standing on end, Arjuna bowed his head in obeisance to Lord Kṛṣṇa. Placing his palms together, he prayed.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे<br /> सर्व्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् ।<br />ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थम्<br />ऋषींश्च सर्व्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥१५॥
arjuna uvācha
paśyāmi devāṁs tava deva dehe<br />sarvāṁs tathā bhūta-viśeṣa-saṅghān<br />brahmāṇam īśaṁ kamalāsana-stham<br />ṛṣīṁś cha sarvān uragāṁś cha divyān [15]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">deva</span>–O Lord; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> paśyāmi</span>–I see;<span class="e2"> tava dehe</span>–within Your body; <span class="e2">sarvān</span>–all; <span class="e2">devān</span>–the demigods; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–and;<span class="e2"> bhūta-viśeṣa-saṅghān</span>–all species of life; <span class="e2">sarvān</span>–all;<span class="e2"> divyān ṛṣīn</span>–the celestial sages; <span class="e2">uragān</span>–and serpents;<span class="e2"> īśam cha</span>–and Mahādev, Lord Śiva;<span class="e2"> brahmāṇam cha</span>–and Lord Brahmā, too;<span class="e2"> kamala-āsana-stham</span>–seated on the lotus flower. [15]
15 Arjuna said: O Lord, I see within Your body the demigods, all species of life, the celestial sages and serpents, Mahādev, and Lord Brahmā seated on the lotus flower.
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं<br />पश्यामि त्वां सर्व्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् ।<br />नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं<br />पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥१॥
aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netraṁ<br />paśyāmi tvāṁ sarvato ’nanta-rūpam<br />nāntaṁ na madhyaṁ na punas tavādiṁ<br />paśyāmi viśveśvara viśva-rūpa [16]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> viśva-īśvara</span>–O Lord of the universe; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> viśva-rūpa</span>–O universal form; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> paśyāmi</span>–I see; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You;<span class="e2"> ananta-rūpam</span>–of infinite form;<span class="e2"> sarvataḥ</span>–in all directions;<span class="e2"> aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netram</span>–with Your many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes. <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–Yet; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> paśyāmi</span>–I see; <span class="e2">na ādim</span>–no beginning;<span class="e2"> na madhyam</span>–no middle;<span class="e2"> na antam</span>–and no end; <span class="e2">tava</span>–of You. [16]
16 O Lord of the universe, O universal form, in all directions I see Your infinite form of many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes. I see no beginning, middle, or end of You.
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणञ्च<br />तेजोराशिं सर्व्वतो दीप्तिमन्तम् ।<br />पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ताद्<br />दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥१७॥
kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ chakriṇañ cha<br />tejorāśiṁ sarvato dīptimantam<br />paśyāmi tvāṁ durnirīkṣyaṁ samantād<br />dīptānalārka-dyutim aprameyam [17]
(<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> paśyāmi</span>–I see; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You;<span class="e2"> samantāt</span>–everywhere;<span class="e2"> kirīṭinam</span>–with crown;<span class="e2"> gadinam</span>–club; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> chakriṇam</span>–disc;<span class="e2"> tejaḥ-rāśim</span>–a mass of effulgence;<span class="e2"> sarvataḥ dīptimantam</span>–illuminating all;<span class="e2"> dipta-anala-arka-dyutim</span>–like the blazing fire of the sun;<span class="e2"> durnirīkṣyam</span>–difficult to behold;<span class="e2"> aprameyam</span>–and incomprehensible. [17]
17 I see You everywhere with crown, club, and disc, a mass of effulgence illuminating all like the blazing light of the sun, difficult to behold and incomprehensible.
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं<br />त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् ।<br />त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्म्मगोप्त<br /> सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ॥१८॥
tvam akṣaraṁ paramaṁ veditavyaṁ<br />tvam asya viśvasya paraṁ nidhānam<br />tvam avyayaḥ śāśvata-dharma-goptā<br />sanātanas tvaṁ puruṣo mato me [18]
<span class="e2">tvam paramam akṣaram</span>–You are Parabrahma;<span class="e2"> veditavyam</span>–knowable by the Vedas.<span class="e2"> tvam param</span>–You are the supreme;<span class="e2"> nidhānam</span>–reservoir;<span class="e2"> asya viśvasya</span>–of this universe.<span class="e2"> tvam avyayaḥ</span>–You are the imperishable;<span class="e2"> śāśvata-dharma-goptā</span>–preserver of Vedic sanātan-dharma, the eternal religion.<span class="e2"> tvam sanātanaḥ</span>–You are the eternal;<span class="e2"> puruṣaḥ</span>–Supreme Personality; (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–this is; <span class="e2">me</span>–my; <span class="e2">mataḥ</span>–understanding. [18]
18 You are the Supreme Absolute Truth knowable by the Vedas. You are the supreme reservoir of the universe and the imperishable preserver of the eternal religion described in the Vedas. I now understand You to be the eternal Supreme Personality.
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य्यम्<br />अन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्य्यनेत्रम् ।<br />पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्र<br />स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ॥१९॥
anādi-madhyāntam ananta-vīryam<br />ananta-bāhuṁ śaśi-sūrya-netram<br />paśyāmi tvāṁ dīpta-hutāśa-vaktraṁ<br />svatejasā viśvam idaṁ tapantam [19]
(<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> paśyāmi</span>–I see; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You;<span class="e2"> anādi-madhya-antam</span>–without beginning, middle, and end;<span class="e2"> ananta-vīryam</span>–infinitely powerful;<span class="e2"> ananta-bāhum</span>–with infinite arms;<span class="e2"> śaśi-sūrya-netram</span>–and Your eyes are the sun and moon;<span class="e2"> dīpta-hutāśa-vaktram</span>–Your mouth of blazing fire;<span class="e2"> idam viśvam</span>–this universe;<span class="e2"> tapantam</span>–is seared;<span class="e2"> svatejasā</span>–by Your radiance. [19]
19 I see You without beginning, middle, or end, infinitely powerful with countless arms. Your eyes are the sun and the moon, Your mouth is blazing fire, and the entire universe is seared by Your radiance.
द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि<br />व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्व्वाः ।<br />दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं रूपमिदं तवोग्रं<br />लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ॥२०॥
dyāv āpṛthivyor idam antaraṁ hi<br />vyāptaṁ tvayaikena diśaś cha sarvāḥ<br />dṛṣṭvādbhutaṁ rūpam idaṁ tavograṁ<br />loka-trayaṁ pravyathitaṁ mahātman [20]
<span class="e2">hi</span>–Certainly; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> antaram</span>–space between;<span class="e2"> dyau āpṛthivyoḥ</span>–heaven and earth;<span class="e2"> sarvāḥ diśaḥ cha</span>–and all directions;<span class="e2"> vyāptam</span>–are pervaded; <span class="e2">tvayā</span>–by You; <span class="e2">ekena</span>–alone. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-ātman</span>–O gracious one; <span class="e2">dṛṣṭvā</span>–seeing; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> adbhutam</span>–wondrous; <span class="e2">ugram</span>–fearsome; <span class="e2">rūpam</span>–form; <span class="e2">tava</span>–of Yours;<span class="e2"> loka-trayam</span>–all the three worlds;<span class="e2"> pravyathitam</span>–are terrified. [20]
20 You alone pervade all directions and all space between heaven and earth. O gracious one, seeing this wondrous and fearsome form of Yours, all the inhabitants of the three worlds are terrified.
अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति<br />केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति ।<br />स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः<br />स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः ॥२१॥
amī hi tvāṁ sura-saṅghā viśanti<br />kechid bhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti<br />svastīty uktvā maharṣi-siddha-saṅghāḥ<br />stuvanti tvāṁ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ [21]
<span class="e2">amī</span>–All these;<span class="e2"> sura-saṅghāḥ</span>–demigods;<span class="e2"> viśanti</span>–are entering; <span class="e2">tvām hi</span>–into You; <span class="e2">kechit</span>–some; <span class="e2">bhītāḥ</span>–fearfully;<span class="e2"> gṛṇanti</span>–offering prayers;<span class="e2"> prāñjalayaḥ</span>–with cupped hands.<span class="e2"> su-asti iti uktvā</span>–“May auspiciousness come to the world”<span class="e2">—</span>saying this;<span class="e2"> mahā-ṛṣi-siddha-saṅghāḥ</span>–the great sages and perfected beings;<span class="e2"> stuvanti</span>–are offering prayers; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–to You;<span class="e2"> puṣkalābhiḥ</span>–by excellent;<span class="e2"> stutibhiḥ</span>–verses singing Your glories. [21]
21 All the demigods are entering into You, some fearfully offering You prayers with cupped hands. The great sages and perfected beings are singing Your glories in beautiful verses, saying, “May all auspiciousness come to the world.”
रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या<br />विश्वेऽश्विनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च ।<br />गन्धर्व्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा<br />वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्व्वे ॥२२॥
rudrādityā vasavo ye cha sādhyā<br />viśve ’śvinau marutaś choṣmapāś cha<br />gandharva-yakṣāsura-siddha-saṅghā<br />vīkṣante tvāṁ vismitāś chaiva sarve [22]
<span class="e2">rudra-ādityāḥ</span>–The Rudras and the Ādityas;<span class="e2"> vasavaḥ</span>–the Vasus; <span class="e2">ye cha </span>(<span class="e2">nāma</span>)–and those called;<span class="e2"> sādhyāḥ</span>–the Sādhyas; <span class="e2">viśve</span>–the Viśvadevas;<span class="e2"> aśvinau</span>–the Aśvinī Kumāras;<span class="e2"> marutaḥ cha</span>–and the Vāyus;<span class="e2"> uṣma-pāḥ cha</span>–and the forefather-demigods;<span class="e2"> gandharva-yakṣa-asura-siddha-saṅghāḥ cha</span>–and also the Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and perfected beings; (<span class="e2">te</span>)<span class="e2"> sarve eva</span>–indeed, they all;<span class="e2"> vismitāḥ</span>–marvel;<span class="e2"> vīkṣante tvām</span>–to behold You. [22]
22 The Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Viśvadevas, Aśvinī Kumāras, Vāyus, deities of the forefathers, the Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and Siddhas—indeed, they all marvel to behold You.
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं<br />महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् ।<br />बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं<br />दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाहम् ॥२३॥
rūpaṁ mahat te bahu-vaktra-netraṁ<br />mahā-bāho bahu-bāhūru-pādam<br />bahūdaraṁ bahu-daṁṣṭrā-karālaṁ<br />dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitās tathāham [23]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">lokāḥ</span>–all;<span class="e2"> tathā aham</span>–including myself;<span class="e2"> pravyathitāḥ</span>–are afflicted with fear; <span class="e2">dṛṣṭvā</span>–seeing; <span class="e2">te</span>–Your; <span class="e2">mahat</span>–vast; <span class="e2">rūpam</span>–form;<span class="e2"> bahu-vaktra-netram</span>–of many mouths and eyes;<span class="e2"> bahu-bāhu-uru-pādam</span>–many arms, thighs, and feet;<span class="e2"> bahu-udaram</span>–many bellies;<span class="e2"> bahu-daṁṣṭrā-karālam</span>–and fearful with many teeth. [23]
23 O mighty-armed one, seeing Your vast form of many mouths, eyes, arms, legs, feet, and bellies, fearful with its many teeth, all beings, including myself, are afflicted with fear.
नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं<br />व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् ।<br />दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा<br />धृतिं न विन्दामि शमञ्च विष्णो ॥२४॥
nabhaḥ-spṛśaṁ dīptam aneka-varṇaṁ<br />vyāttānanaṁ dīpta-viśāla-netram<br />dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṁ pravyathitāntar-ātmā<br />dhṛtiṁ na vindāmi śamañ cha viṣṇo [24]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">viṣṇo</span>–O pervader of the universe; <span class="e2">dṛṣṭvā</span>–seeing; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You;<span class="e2"> nabhaḥ-spṛśam</span>–sky-touching; <span class="e2">dīptam</span>–dazzling;<span class="e2"> aneka-varṇam</span>–multi-coloured;<span class="e2"> vyātta-ānanam</span>–of gaping mouth;<span class="e2"> dīpta-viśāla-netram</span>–and huge fiery eye; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> pravyathita-antaḥ-ātmā</span>–with extremely fearful heart;<span class="e2"> na hi vindāmi dhṛtim śamam cha</span>––cannot find equilibrium or peace. [24]
24 O Viṣṇu, seeing Your sky-touching, dazzling form of myriad colours, with gaping mouth and huge fiery eye, my heart trembles with fear, and I cannot find equilibrium or peace.
दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि<br />दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि ।<br />दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म्म<br />प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥२५॥
daṁṣṭrā-karālāni cha te mukhāni<br />dṛṣṭvaiva kālānala-sannibhāni<br />diśo na jāne na labhe cha śarma<br />prasīda deveśa jagan-nivāsa [25]
<span class="e2">dṛṣṭvā eva</span>–Seeing; <span class="e2">te</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> mukhāni</span>–mouths;<span class="e2"> daṁṣṭrā-karālāni</span>–ghastly with their teeth;<span class="e2"> kāla-anala sannibhāni cha</span>–and resembling the fire of the universal annihilation; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I; <span class="e2">na jāne</span>–cannot know; <span class="e2">diśaḥ</span>–the directions;<span class="e2"> na labhe</span>–nor can I find;<span class="e2"> śarma cha</span>–composure. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> deva-īśa</span>–O God of gods; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> jagat-nivāsa</span>–O abode of the universe; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)<span class="e2"> prasīda</span>–be gracious. [25]
25 Seeing Your mouths resembling the fire of the universal annihilation, ghastly with their terrible teeth, I am distraught and have lost my bearings. Be gracious, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe.
अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः<br />सर्व्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः ।<br />भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथासौ<br />सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः ॥२६॥
वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्त<br />दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि ।<br />केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु<br />सन्दृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः ॥२७॥
amī cha tvāṁ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ<br />sarve sahaivāvanipāla-saṅghaiḥ<br />bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūta-putras tathāsau<br />sahāsmadīyair api yodha-mukhyaiḥ [26]
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti<br />daṁṣṭrā-karālāni bhayānakāni<br />kechid vilagnā daśanāntareṣu<br />sandṛśyante chūrṇitair uttamāṅgaiḥ [27]
<span class="e2">amī cha sarve</span>–All these; <span class="e2">putrāḥ</span>–sons;<span class="e2"> dhṛtarāṣṭrasya</span>–of Dhṛtarāṣṭra;<span class="e2"> avani-pāla-saṅghaiḥ saha eva</span>–along with their allied kings; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–as well as;<span class="e2"> bhīṣmaḥ</span>–Bhīṣma; <span class="e2">droṇaḥ</span>–Droṇa;<span class="e2"> asau sūta-putraḥ</span>–and that Karṇa;<span class="e2"> saha api</span>–along with;<span class="e2"> yodha-mukhyaiḥ</span>–the chief warriors;<span class="e2"> asmadīyaiḥ</span>–of our party;<span class="e2"> tvaramāṇāḥ</span>–are swiftly; (<span class="e2">viśanti</span>)–entering; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You;<span class="e2"> viśanti</span>–entering; <span class="e2">te</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> bhayānakāni</span>–terrible;<span class="e2"> vaktrāṇi</span>–mouths;<span class="e2"> daṁṣṭrā-karālāni</span>–of terrible teeth. <span class="e2">kechit</span>–Some;<span class="e2"> saṁdṛśyante</span>–are seen;<span class="e2"> chūrṇitaiḥ-uttama-aṅgaiḥ</span>–with crushed heads;<span class="e2"> vilagnāḥ</span>–caught;<span class="e2"> daśana-antareṣu</span>–between the teeth. [26–27]
26–27 The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, their allied kings, and Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Karṇa, along with our chief warriors, are all rushing into Your dreadful mouths of terrible teeth. Some can be seen with their heads caught and crushed by Your teeth.
यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः<br />समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति ।<br />तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा<br />विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभितो ज्वलन्ति ॥२८॥
yathā nadīnāṁ bahavo ’mbu-vegāḥ<br />samudram evābhimukhā dravanti<br />tathā tavāmī nara-loka-vīrā<br />viśanti vaktrāṇy abhito jvalanti [28]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–As;<span class="e2"> bahavaḥ</span>–many;<span class="e2"> ambu-vegāḥ</span>–currents of water;<span class="e2"> nadīnām</span>–of rivers; <span class="e2">abhimukhāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–flowing towards the ocean;<span class="e2"> dravanti eva</span>–enter;<span class="e2"> samudram</span>–the ocean; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–similarly; <span class="e2">amī</span>–all these;<span class="e2"> nara-loka-vīrāḥ</span>–heroic men;<span class="e2"> viśanti</span>–are entering; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> vaktrāṇi</span>–mouths;<span class="e2"> jvalanti</span>–which are fiery, illuminating;<span class="e2"> abhitaḥ</span>–all around. [28]
28 As many rivers flow towards the ocean to finally enter into it, so these heroes of the world are entering Your flaming mouths that illuminate all around.
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्ग<br /> विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः ।<br />तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोकास्<br />तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः ॥२९॥
yathā pradīptaṁ jvalanaṁ pataṅgā<br />viśanti nāśāya samṛddha-vegāḥ<br />tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokās<br />tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddha-vegāḥ [29]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–As;<span class="e2"> pataṅgāḥ</span>–insects;<span class="e2"> samṛddha-vegāḥ</span>–are impelled; <span class="e2">nāśāya</span>–to their destruction;<span class="e2"> viśanti</span>–entering into;<span class="e2"> pradīptam</span>–blazing;<span class="e2"> jvalanam</span>–fire; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–similarly;<span class="e2"> lokāḥ api</span>–all the worlds; <span class="e2">samṛddha-vegāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–are helplessly rushing;<span class="e2"> viśanti</span>–entering into;<span class="e2"> tava vaktrāṇi</span>–Your mouths;<span class="e2"> nāśāya eva</span>–to certain death. [29]
29 As moths are impelled to their death in blazing fire, similarly, all the worlds are helplessly rushing to certain death, entering into Your mouths.
लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ताल्<br />लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः ।<br />तेजोभिरापूर्य्य जगत्समग्रं<br />भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो ॥३०॥
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantāl<br />lokān samagrān vadanair jvaladbhiḥ<br />tejobhir āpūrya jagat samagraṁ<br />bhāsas tavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo [30]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">viṣṇo</span>–O pervader of the universe; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You;<span class="e2"> lelihyase</span>–are relishing;<span class="e2"> grasamānaḥ</span>–devouring;<span class="e2"> samagrān</span>–all these; <span class="e2">lokān</span>–persons, worlds;<span class="e2"> samantāt</span>–in all directions;<span class="e2"> jvaladbhiḥ vadanaiḥ</span>–with Your flaming mouths. <span class="e2">āpūrya</span>–Filled;<span class="e2"> tava tejobhiḥ</span>–with Your effulgence; <span class="e2">ugrāḥ</span>–of severe; <span class="e2">bhāsaḥ</span>–glare;<span class="e2"> samagram jagat</span>–the whole universe;<span class="e2"> pratapanti</span>–is being seared. [30]
30 O Viṣṇu, with Your flaming mouths, You are relishing devouring all the worlds, Your all-pervading, glaring effulgence searing the entire universe.
आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो<br />नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद ।<br />विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं<br />न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् ॥३१॥
ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugra-rūpo<br />namo ’stu te deva-vara prasīda<br />vijñātum ichchhāmi bhavantam ādyaṁ<br />na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim [31]
<span class="e2">ākhyāhi me</span>–Please tell me;<span class="e2"> kaḥ bhavān</span>–who are You;<span class="e2"> ugra-rūpaḥ</span>–of fearsome form.<span class="e2"> namaḥ astu</span>–I offer obeisance; <span class="e2">te</span>–unto You. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> deva-vara</span>–O Lord of lords; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)<span class="e2"> prasīda</span>–be gracious. (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> ichchhāmi</span>–I wish;<span class="e2"> vijñātum</span>–to fully know;<span class="e2"> bhavantam</span>–You; <span class="e2">ādyam</span>–the Origin; <span class="e2">hi</span>–as; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> na prajānāmi</span>–cannot understand; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> pravṛttim</span>–intention. [31]
31 O fearsome one, please tell me who You are. O Lord of the gods, I offer obeisance unto You; please be gracious. I wish to fully know You, the Origin, as I cannot understand your actions.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो<br />लोकान्समाहर्त्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः ।<br />ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्व्वे<br />येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः ॥३२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
kālo ’smi loka-kṣaya-kṛt pravṛddho<br />lokān samāhartum iha pravṛttaḥ<br />ṛte ’pi tvāṁ na bhaviṣyanti sarve<br />ye ’vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ [32]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–I am;<span class="e2"> pravṛddhaḥ</span>–mighty; <span class="e2">kālaḥ</span>–time;<span class="e2"> loka-kṣaya-kṛt</span>–the destroyer of all beings;<span class="e2"> pravṛttaḥ</span>–engaged;<span class="e2"> samāhartum</span>–to annihilate; <span class="e2">lokān</span>–all beings; <span class="e2">iha</span>–in this plane.<span class="e2"> ye yodhāḥ</span>–Of those warriors;<span class="e2"> avasthitāḥ</span>–present;<span class="e2"> pratyanīkeṣu</span>–in the enemy army; (<span class="e2">te</span>)<span class="e2"> sarve na bhaviṣyanti</span>–none will be spared;<span class="e2"> tvām ṛte api</span>–despite you. [32]
32 The Supreme Lord said: I am the time, the mighty vanquisher of all, and I am engaged in destroying the worlds. Even if you do not slay them, not one of the warriors in the enemy party will be spared.
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व<br />जित्वा शत्रून्भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् ।<br />मयैवैते निहताः पूर्व्वमेव<br />निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥३३॥
tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva<br />jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṁ samṛddham<br />mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva<br />nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savyasāchin [33]
<span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> uttiṣṭha</span>–arise for battle;<span class="e2"> labhasva</span>–take; <span class="e2">yaśaḥ</span>–the credit; <span class="e2">jitvā</span>–and conquering; <span class="e2">śatrūn</span>–the enemies;<span class="e2"> bhuṅkṣva</span>–enjoy;<span class="e2"> samṛddham rājyam</span>–a flourishing kingdom. <span class="e2">ete</span>–All these warriors;<span class="e2"> nihatāḥ</span>–have been slain;<span class="e2"> mayā eva</span>–by Me;<span class="e2"> pūrvam eva</span>–long before. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> savyasāchin</span>–O Arjuna, who can skilfully shoot arrows even with his left hand; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–be;<span class="e2"> nimitta-mātram</span>–but an instrument. [33]
33 So arise! Be glorious! Conquer the enemies and enjoy a flourishing kingdom. All these warriors have already been killed by Me. O Savyasāchin, you be but an instrument.
द्रोणञ्च भीष्मञ्च जयद्रथञ्च<br />कर्णं तथान्यानपि योधवीरान् ।<br />मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा<br />युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् ॥३४॥
droṇañ cha bhīṣmañ cha jayadrathañ cha<br />karṇaṁ tathānyān api yodha-vīrān<br />mayā hatāṁs tvaṁ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā<br />yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān [34]
<span class="e2">tvam</span>–You; <span class="e2">jahi</span>–slay;<span class="e2"> droṇam cha</span>–Droṇa;<span class="e2"> bhīṣmam cha</span>–Bhīṣma;<span class="e2"> jayadratham</span>–Jayadratha;<span class="e2"> karṇam cha</span>–and Karṇa; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–as;<span class="e2"> anyān api</span>–any other;<span class="e2"> yodha-vīrān</span>–warriors desiring battle; <span class="e2">hatān</span>–(but already) killed; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me.<span class="e2"> mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ</span>–Fear not;<span class="e2"> yudhyasva</span>–fight!<span class="e2"> jetā asi</span>–You shall conquer;<span class="e2"> sapatnān</span>–the enemy; <span class="e2">raṇe</span>–in battle. [34]
34 Slay Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa, and the many warriors who are as good as slain by Me. Fear not, fight! You will be victorious over the enemy.
सञ्जय उवाच ।
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य<br />कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी ।<br />नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं<br />सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य ॥३५॥
sañjaya uvācha
etach chhrutvā vachanaṁ keśavasya<br />kṛtāñjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī<br />namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṁ<br />sagadgadaṁ bhīta-bhītaḥ praṇamya [35]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said: <span class="e2">śrutvā</span>–Hearing;<span class="e2"> etat vachanam</span>–these words;<span class="e2"> keśavasya</span>–of Lord Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">kirīṭī</span>–Arjuna;<span class="e2"> vepamānaḥ</span>–trembling; kṛta-<span class="e2">añjaliḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–placing the palms of his hands together in prayer;<span class="e2"> namaḥ-kṛtvā</span>–bowing;<span class="e2"> bhīta-bhītaḥ eva</span>–with a very fearful heart; <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–again;<span class="e2"> praṇamya</span>–offering obeisances; <span class="e2">āha</span>–spoke; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇam</span>–to Lord Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> sa-gad-gadam</span>–falteringly. [35]
35 Sañjaya said: Hearing these words of the Lord, the trembling Arjuna bowed his head, placing the palms of his hands together in prayer. With a fearful heart, bowing again, he spoke falteringly.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्त्या<br />जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च ।<br />रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति<br />सर्व्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः ॥३६॥
arjuna uvācha
sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā<br />jagat prahṛṣyaty anurajyate cha<br />rakṣāṁsi bhītāni diśo dravanti<br />sarve namasyanti cha siddha-saṅghāḥ [36]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> hṛṣīkeśa</span>–O Lord of the senses of all beings; <span class="e2">sthāne</span>–rightfully; <span class="e2">jagat</span>–the whole world;<span class="e2"> prahṛṣyati</span>–is joyful;<span class="e2"> tava prakīrtyā</span>–by singing Your glories;<span class="e2"> cha anurajyate</span>–with love;<span class="e2"> rakṣāmsi</span>–the demons; <span class="e2">bhītāni </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–being afraid;<span class="e2"> dravanti</span>–run; <span class="e2">diśaḥ</span>–in all four directions; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">sarve</span>–all;<span class="e2"> siddha-saṅghāḥ</span>–the perfected beings;<span class="e2"> namasyanti</span>–offer respects, obeisance. [36]
36 Arjuna said: O Hṛṣīkeś, it is fitting that the whole world joyfully sings Your glories with love, the demons flee, scattering in all directions, and the perfected beings offer obeisance to You.
कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्<br />गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्त्रे ।<br />अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास<br />त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत् ॥३७॥
kasmāch cha te na nameran mahātman<br />garīyase brahmaṇo ’py ādi-kartre<br />ananta deveśa jagan-nivāsa<br />tvam akṣaraṁ sad-asat tat paraṁ yat [37]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-ātman</span>–O gracious personality; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">ananta</span>–O infinite, embodiment of all; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> deva-īśa</span>–O God of gods; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> jagat-nivāsa</span>–O abode of the universe;<span class="e2"> garīyase</span>–the worshippable;<span class="e2"> ādi-kartre cha</span>–and the creator;<span class="e2"> brahmaṇaḥ api</span>–of even Lord Brahmā; <span class="e2">kasmāt </span>(<span class="e2">sarve</span>)<span class="e2"> na nameran</span>–how would they all not bow; <span class="e2">te</span>–to You?<span class="e2"> tvam sat asat</span>–You are the manifest and the unmanifest, the material effect and cause;<span class="e2"> akṣaram</span>–the Imperishable, Brahma;<span class="e2"> tat param yat</span>–that which is transcendental, the Supreme. [37]
37 And, O gracious one, how would they not bow to You, the worshippable creator of even the creator Lord Brahmā? O infinite God of gods, O abode of the universe, You are the manifest, the unmanifest, the Supreme Imperishable.
त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराणस्<br />त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् ।<br />वेत्तासि वेद्यञ्च परञ्च धाम<br />त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥३८॥
tvam ādi-devaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇas<br />tvam asya viśvasya paraṁ nidhānam<br />vettāsi vedyañ cha parañ cha dhāma<br />tvayā tataṁ viśvam ananta-rūpa [38]
<span class="e2">tvam </span>(<span class="e2">asi</span>)–You are;<span class="e2"> ādi-devaḥ</span>–the original Lord;<span class="e2"> purāṇaḥ puruṣaḥ</span>–the eternal personality;<span class="e2"> tvam asi</span>–You are; <span class="e2">param</span>–the only;<span class="e2"> nidhānam</span>–refuge, resting place;<span class="e2"> asya viśvasya</span>–of this universe; <span class="e2">vettā</span>–the knower;<span class="e2"> vedyam cha</span>–and the knowable;<span class="e2"> param dhāma cha</span>–and the supreme abode. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> ananta-rūpa</span>–O Lord of infinite forms; <span class="e2">viśvam</span>–the universe; <span class="e2">tatam</span>–is pervaded; <span class="e2">tvayā</span>–by You. [38]
38 You are the eternal origin of all the demigods, and the only refuge of this universe. You alone are the knower and the knowable, and the supreme abode. O Lord of infinite forms, the entire universe is pervaded by You.
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः<br />प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च ।<br />नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः<br />पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ॥३९॥
vāyur yamo ’gnir varuṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ<br />prajāpatis tvaṁ prapitāmahaś cha<br />namo namas te ’stu sahasra-kṛtvaḥ<br />punaś cha bhūyo ’pi namo namas te [39]
<span class="e2">tvam vāyuḥ</span>–You are the god of air; <span class="e2">yamaḥ</span>–the god of death; <span class="e2">agniḥ</span>–the god of fire;<span class="e2"> varuṇaḥ</span>–the god of the ocean;<span class="e2"> śaśāṅkaḥ</span>–the god of the moon;<span class="e2"> prajāpatiḥ</span>–the universal father, Lord Brahmā;<span class="e2"> prapitāmahaḥ cha</span>–and the grandfather, too.<span class="e2"> namaḥ astu</span>–My obeisances; <span class="e2">te</span>–unto You;<span class="e2"> sahasra-kṛtvaḥ</span>–thousands of times;<span class="e2"> puṇaḥ cha namaḥ</span>–and again obeisances;<span class="e2"> bhūyaḥ api</span>–and yet again;<span class="e2"> namaḥ namaḥ</span>–obeisances, obeisances; <span class="e2">te</span>–unto You. [39]
39 You are the father and grandfather of all beings, You are air, death, fire, the ocean, and the moon. Obeisances unto You thousands of times, again and yet again.
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते<br />नमोऽस्तु ते सर्व्वत एव सर्व्व ।<br />अनन्तवीर्य्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं<br />सर्व्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्व्वः ॥४०॥
namaḥ purastād atha pṛṣṭhatas te<br />namo ’stu te sarvata eva sarva<br />ananta-vīryāmita-vikramas tvaṁ<br />sarvaṁ samāpnoṣi tato ’si sarvaḥ [40]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">sarva</span>–O embodiment of all existences; <span class="e2">namaḥ</span>–my obeisances; <span class="e2">te</span>–unto You;<span class="e2"> purastāt</span>–from the front; <span class="e2">atha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> pṛṣṭhataḥ</span>–from the rear.<span class="e2"> namaḥ astu</span>–I offer obeisances; <span class="e2">te</span>–unto You; <span class="e2">eva</span>–indeed;<span class="e2"> sarvataḥ</span>–from all directions. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> ananta-vīrya</span>–O Lord of infinite potency;<span class="e2"> amita-vikramaḥ</span>–of immeasurable prowess; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–You;<span class="e2"> samāpnoṣi</span>–pervade; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–all; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–therefore; <span class="e2">asi</span>–You are; <span class="e2">sarvaḥ</span>–all. [40]
40 O embodiment of all existences, my obeisances unto You from the front, behind, and all directions. O Lord of unlimited potency and immeasurable prowess, You pervade all, therefore You are all.
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं<br />हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति ।<br />अजानता महिमानं तवेदं<br />मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥४१॥
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि<br />विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु ।<br />एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं<br />तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥४२॥
sakheti matvā prasabhaṁ yad uktaṁ<br />he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti<br />ajānatā mahimānaṁ tavedaṁ<br />mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi [41]
yach chāvahāsārtham asatkṛto ’si<br />vihāra-śayyāsana-bhojaneṣu<br />eko ’thavāpy achyuta tat-samakṣaṁ<br />tat kṣāmaye tvām aham aprameyam [42]
<span class="e2">ajānatā</span>–Not knowing; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> mahimānam</span>–greatness;<span class="e2"> idam cha</span>–and this (universal form);<span class="e2"> pramādāt</span>–inadvertently;<span class="e2"> praṇayena vā api</span>–and due to intimacy;<span class="e2"> sakhā iti matvā</span>–thinking of You as a friend;<span class="e2"> yat uktam</span>–whatever has been said;<span class="e2"> prasabham</span>–rashly; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by me; <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus:<span class="e2"> he kṛṣṇa</span>–“O Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> he yādava</span>–Yādava;<span class="e2"> he sakhe</span>–my friend”; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> achyuta</span>–O infallible one;<span class="e2"> yat asat-kṛtaḥ asi</span>–whatever disrespect I have shown You;<span class="e2"> avahāsa-artham</span>–in jest;<span class="e2"> vihāra-śayyā-āsana-bhojaneṣu</span>–in recreation, resting, sitting, eating; <span class="e2">ekaḥ</span>–alone; <span class="e2">athavā</span>–or; <span class="e2">api</span>–even;<span class="e2"> tat-samakṣam</span>–in the presence of others; <span class="e2">tat</span>–for all this; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> tvām aprameyam kṣāmaye</span>–beg You, the inconceivable, to please forgive me. [41–42]
41–42 Due to the familiarity of affection I have rashly addressed You, “Kṛṣṇa,” “Yādava,” or “my friend,” ignorant of this Your greatness. O infallible Lord, whatever disrespect I have shown You—in jest, while relaxing, resting, sitting or eating, either alone with You or in company—I beg You, the inconceivable, to please forgive me for that.
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य<br />त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् ।<br />न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो<br />लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव ॥४३॥
pitāsi lokasya charācharasya<br />tvam asya pūjyaś cha gurur garīyān<br />na tvat-samo ’sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto ’nyo<br />loka-traye ’py apratima-prabhāva [43]
<span class="e2">tvam asi</span>–You are; <span class="e2">pitā</span>–the father;<span class="e2"> asya lokasya</span>–of this universe;<span class="e2"> chara-acharasya</span>–of moving and stationary beings; <span class="e2">pūjyaḥ</span>–the worshippable;<span class="e2"> garīyān</span>–most glorious; <span class="e2">guruḥ</span>–teacher; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">api</span>–indeed; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–there is no one;<span class="e2"> tvat-samaḥ</span>–equal to You;<span class="e2"> loka-traye</span>–within the three worlds; <span class="e2">kutaḥ</span>–so how can; <span class="e2">anyaḥ</span>–another;<span class="e2"> abhyadhikaḥ</span>–be superior; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> apratima-prabhāva</span>–O Lord of unrivalled power! [43]
43 You are the father of all living beings, the worshippable and most glorious teacher. You have no equal within these three worlds. How can there be anyone greater than You, O Lord of unrivalled power!
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं<br />प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् ।<br />पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः<br />प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥४४॥
tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṁ<br />prasādaye tvām aham īśam īḍyam<br />piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ<br />priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum [44]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">deva</span>–O Lord; <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–therefore;<span class="e2"> kāyam praṇidhāya</span>–prostrating my body;<span class="e2"> praṇamya</span>–in obeisance;<span class="e2"> aham prasādaye</span>–I am propitiating; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You; <span class="e2">īḍyam</span>–the worshippable; <span class="e2">īśam</span>–Lord. <span class="e2">iva</span>–As;<span class="e2"> pitā sakhā priyaḥ</span>–a father, friend or lover (forgive);<span class="e2"> putrasya sakhyuḥ priyāyāḥ</span>–(the mistakes) of a son, friend or beloved; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You; (<span class="e2">tathā</span>)<span class="e2"> iva</span>–similarly; <span class="e2">arhasi</span>–please; <span class="e2">soḍhum</span>–forgive (me). [44]
44 So I offer my prostrate obeisance unto You, my Lord and worshippable master, praying for Your mercy. Please excuse me as a father, friend, or lover overlooks the mistakes of his son, companion, or beloved.
अदृष्टपूर्व्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा<br />भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे ।<br />तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं<br />प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥४५॥
adṛṣṭa-pūrvaṁ hṛṣito ’smi dṛṣṭvā<br />bhayena cha pravyathitaṁ mano me<br />tad eva me darśaya deva rūpaṁ<br />prasīda deveśa jagan-nivāsa [45]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">deva</span>–O Lord; <span class="e2">dṛṣṭvā</span>–seeing; (<span class="e2">idam</span>)<span class="e2"> adṛṣṭa-pūrvam</span>–this previously unseen universal form of Yours;<span class="e2"> hṛṣitaḥ asmi</span>–I am joyful; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and then again; <span class="e2">me</span>–my; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–mind;<span class="e2"> bhayena pravyathitam</span>–is distraught with fear. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> deva-īśa</span>–O God of gods; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> jagat-nivāsa</span>–O refuge of the universe;<span class="e2"> prasīda</span>–may You be gracious;<span class="e2"> darśaya</span>–to show; <span class="e2">me</span>–me;<span class="e2"> tat eva rūpam</span>–that form You showed before. [45]
45 O Lord, my heart is joyful to see Your hitherto unseen universal form. Yet, I am afraid. O God of gods, shelter of the universe, be gracious upon me and appear in the form I saw before.
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्तम्<br />इच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव ।<br />तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन<br />सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्त्ते ॥४६॥
kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ chakra-hastam<br />ichchhāmi tvāṁ draṣṭum ahaṁ tathaiva<br />tenaiva rūpeṇa chatur-bhujena<br />sahasra-bāho bhava viśva-mūrte [46]
<span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> ichchhāmi</span>–wish;<span class="e2"> draṣṭum</span>–to see; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You;<span class="e2"> tathā eva</span>–as previously;<span class="e2"> kirīṭinam</span>–with crown;<span class="e2"> gadinam</span>–club;<span class="e2"> chakra-hastam</span>–and holding the disc. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> sahasra-bāho</span>–O Lord with a thousand arms; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> viśva-mūrte</span>–O universal form; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–may You appear;<span class="e2"> tena chatuḥ-bhujena rūpeṇa eva</span>–in that form of four arms. [46]
46 I wish to see You again wearing a crown and holding a club and disc. O thousand-armed Lord, O universal form, please appear in that four-armed form.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्ज्जुनेदं<br />रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् ।<br />तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं<br />यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्व्वम् ॥४७॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṁ<br />rūpaṁ paraṁ darśitam ātma-yogāt<br />tejomayaṁ viśvam anantam ādyaṁ<br />yan me tvad-anyena na dṛṣṭa-pūrvam [47]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> prasannena</span>–being satisfied; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> tejaḥ-mayam</span>–effulgent;<span class="e2"> anantam</span>–infinite; <span class="e2">ādyam</span>–and primeval; <span class="e2">param</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">viśvam</span>–universal; <span class="e2">rūpam</span>–form; <span class="e2">me</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> na dṛṣṭa-pūrvam</span>–was not seen previously;<span class="e2"> tvat-anyena</span>–by anyone else;<span class="e2"> darśītam</span>–has been shown; <span class="e2">tava</span>–to you; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me;<span class="e2"> ātma-yogāt</span>–by My divine potency, yogamāya. [47]
47 The Supreme Lord said: O Arjuna, to grant you My special favour I have today revealed this effulgent, universal, infinite, and primeval form, by My divine potency. This supreme universal form has never been seen by anyone before.
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानैर्<br />न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः ।<br />एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके<br />द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥४८॥
na veda-yajñādhyayanair na dānair<br />na cha kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ<br />evaṁ-rūpaḥ śakya ahaṁ nṛloke<br />draṣṭuṁ tvad-anyena kuru-pravīra [48]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kuru-pravīra</span>–O most valiant of the Kauravas; <span class="e2">nṛ-loke</span>–in this human plane;<span class="e2"> na veda-yajña-adhyayanaiḥ</span>–neither by study of the Vedas or Vedic sacrifices;<span class="e2"> na dānaiḥ</span>–nor by giving land, etc. in charity;<span class="e2"> na kriyābhiḥ</span>–nor by rituals;<span class="e2"> na cha tapobhiḥ ugraiḥ</span>–nor by severe austerity; <span class="e2">śakyaḥ</span>–can; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> draṣṭum</span>–be seen;<span class="e2"> evam-rūpaḥ</span>–in such a (universal) form;<span class="e2"> tvat-anyena</span>–by persons other than you. [48]
48 O Arjuna, most valiant of the Kauravas, no one in this human plane can see this form of Mine that you have seen, neither by study of the Vedas, nor Vedic sacrifices, nor charity, nor rituals, nor severe austerity.
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो<br />दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् ।<br />व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं<br />तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥४९॥
mā te vyathā mā cha vimūḍha-bhāvo<br />dṛṣṭvā rūpaṁ ghoram īdṛṅ mamedam<br />vyapeta-bhīḥ prīta-manāḥ punas tvaṁ<br />tad eva me rūpam idaṁ prapaśya [49]
<span class="e2">te vyathā mā </span>(<span class="e2">astu</span>)–Be not bewildered; <span class="e2">dṛṣṭvā</span>–seeing;<span class="e2"> mama rūpam</span>–My form;<span class="e2"> īdṛk idam ghoram</span>–of such terrible feature; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">mā </span>(<span class="e2">astu</span>)–be not;<span class="e2"> vimūḍha-bhāvaḥ</span>–bewildered. <span class="e2">vyapeta-bhīḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–Being free of fear;<span class="e2"> prīta-manāḥ</span>–and contented;<span class="e2"> tvam prapaśya</span>–behold; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> tat rūpam eva</span>–four-armed form; <span class="e2">me</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–again. [49]
49 Be not bewildered by seeing this terrible aspect of Mine. Do not fear. Now, with a peaceful heart, behold My four-armed form once again.
सञ्जय उवाच ।
इत्यर्ज्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा<br />स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः।<br />आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं<br />भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥५०॥
sañjaya uvācha
ity arjunaṁ vāsudevas tathoktvā<br />svakaṁ rūpaṁ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ<br />āśvāsayāmāsa cha bhītam enaṁ<br />bhūtvā punaḥ saumya-vapur mahātmā [50]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said: <span class="e2">uktvā</span>–speaking; <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus;<span class="e2"> arjunam</span>–to Arjuna;<span class="e2"> vāsudevaḥ</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–again;<span class="e2"> darśayāmāsa</span>–revealed;<span class="e2"> tathā svakam rūpam</span>–His own form;<span class="e2"> punaḥ cha</span>–and once again; <span class="e2">bhūtvā</span>–appearing;<span class="e2"> mahā-ātmā</span>–as the most merciful Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> saumya-vapuḥ</span>–of charming (human) feature, dressed in yellow as familiar to Arjuna;<span class="e2"> āśvāsayāmāsa</span>–He pacified;<span class="e2"> enam bhītam</span>–the fearful Arjuna. [50]
50 Sañjaya said: Speaking thus to Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa again revealed His own form. And once again, He revealed His charming personality—the most merciful Śrī Kṛṣṇa (of human feature, adorned with yellow cloth, Kaustubha jewel, and Vaijayantī garland), thus reassuring the fearful Arjuna.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्द्दन<br />इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥५१॥
arjuna uvācha
dṛṣṭvedaṁ mānuṣaṁ rūpaṁ tava saumyaṁ janārdana<br />idānīm asmi saṁvṛttaḥ sa-chetāḥ prakṛtiṁ gataḥ [51]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> janārdana</span>–O Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">dṛṣṭvā</span>–seeing; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> saumyam</span>–charming;<span class="e2"> mānuṣam</span>–human-featured; <span class="e2">rūpam</span>–form; <span class="e2">tava</span>–of Yours; <span class="e2">idānīm</span>–now;<span class="e2"> sa-chetāḥ saṁvṛttaḥ</span>–I am pacified;<span class="e2"> prakṛtim gataḥ asmi</span>–and composed again. [51]
51 Arjuna said: O Janārdan, seeing Your beautiful form of human feature I am calm and composed once again.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
सुदुर्द्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम ।<br />देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ॥५२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
sudurdarśam idaṁ rūpaṁ dṛṣṭavān asi yan mama<br />devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṁ darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ [52]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said:<span class="e2"> idam rūpam</span>–this sach-chid-ānanda form; <span class="e2">mama</span>–of Mine; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you;<span class="e2"> dṛṣṭavān asi</span>–are seeing before you;<span class="e2"> sudurdarśam</span>–is very rarely seen.<span class="e2"> devāḥ api</span>–Even the demigods;<span class="e2"> nityam darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ</span>–ever aspire for a glimpse;<span class="e2"> asya rūpasya</span>–of this form. [52]
52 The Supreme Lord said: O Arjuna, it is very rare that anyone sees this My form which you now behold. Even the gods constantly aspire for a glimpse of this humanlike divine form.
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया ।<br />शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम ॥५३॥
nāhaṁ vedair na tapasā na dānena na chejyayā<br />śakya evaṁ-vidho draṣṭuṁ dṛṣṭavān asi yan mama [53]
<span class="e2">na vedaiḥ</span>–Neither by study of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> na tapasā</span>–nor by severe austerities such as the Chāndrāyaṇ vow;<span class="e2"> na dānena</span>–nor by giving land, etc. in charity;<span class="e2"> na ijyayā cha</span>–nor by great sacrifices such as Agniṣṭoma; (<span class="e2">kaśchit</span>)<span class="e2"> śakyaḥ</span>–is anyone able;<span class="e2"> draṣṭum aham</span>–to see Me;<span class="e2"> evam-vidhaḥ mama</span>–in this eternal form of Mine, of human features; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you;<span class="e2"> dṛṣṭavān asi</span>–are seeing. [53]
53 Neither by study of the Vedas, nor by austerity, charity, and sacrifice can anyone see My eternal humanlike form of the Sweet Absolute as you see Me.
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुञ्च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुञ्च परन्तप ॥५४॥
bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakya aham evaṁ-vidho ’rjuna<br />jñātuṁ draṣṭuñ cha tattvena praveṣṭuñ cha parantapa [54]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> parantapa</span>–O conqueror of the enemy; (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">tu</span>–yet;<span class="e2"> evam-vidhaḥ</span>–in this form; <span class="e2">aham śakyaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">asmi</span>)–can I; <span class="e2">jñātum</span>–be known;<span class="e2"> tattvena</span>–in truth;<span class="e2"> draṣṭum cha</span>–and be seen;<span class="e2"> praveṣṭum cha</span>–and My Pastimes be entered into;<span class="e2"> ananyayā</span>–by exclusive;<span class="e2"> bhaktyā</span>–devotion; (<span class="e2">bhaktena</span>)–by the pure devotee. [54]
54 O Arjuna, conqueror of the enemy, only by pure devotion is it possible to know Me, see Me, and enter My divine Pastimes.
मत्कर्म्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्ज्जितः ।<br />निर्व्वैरः सर्व्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥५५॥
mat-karma-kṛn mat-paramo mad-bhaktaḥ saṅga-varjitaḥ<br />nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava [55]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pāṇḍava</span>–O son of Pāṇḍu;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktaḥ</span>–My devotee; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–who;<span class="e2"> mat-karma-kṛt</span>–serves Me;<span class="e2"> mat-paramaḥ</span>–knowing Me as the supreme; (<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> saṅga-varjitaḥ</span>–giving up all attachment to material objects;<span class="e2"> nirvairaḥ</span>–and free from enmity;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūteṣu</span>–towards all beings; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a person; <span class="e2">eti</span>–attains; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me. [55]
55 O Arjuna, My devotee who gives up all attachments and whose heart is totally free from enmity to all beings, who serves Me wholeheartedly, knowing Me as the Supreme, reaches Me.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे विश्वरूपदर्शनयोगो नामैकादशोऽध्यायः ॥११॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde viśva-rūpa<br />darśana-yogo nāmaikādaśo ’dhyāyaḥ [11]
End of Chapter Eleven<br />The Vision of the Universal Form<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

द्वादशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Twelve
Bhakti-yoga <br />The Path of Devotion
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्य्युपासते ।<br />ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥१॥
arjuna uvācha
evaṁ satata-yuktā ye bhaktās tvāṁ paryupāsate<br />ye chāpy akṣaram avyaktaṁ teṣāṁ ke yoga-vittamāḥ [1]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said:<span class="e2"> ye bhaktāḥ</span>–Those devotees who; <span class="e2">evam</span>–thus;<span class="e2"> satata-yuktāḥ</span>–constantly with exclusive devotion;<span class="e2"> paryupāsate</span>–worship; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–You, Śyāmasundar; <span class="e2">cha api</span>–or; <span class="e2">ye</span>–those who; (<span class="e2">paryupāsate</span>)–worship;<span class="e2"> avyaktam</span>–the unmanifest, impersonal;<span class="e2"> akṣaram</span>–imperishable, Brahma; <span class="e2">teṣām</span>–of these two types of yogīs (jñāna-yogī and bhakti-yogī); <span class="e2">ke</span>–who;<span class="e2"> yoga-vittamāḥ</span>–is the best knower of yoga? [1]
1 Arjuna inquired: Of those devotees who are constantly engaged in worshipping You (as Śyāmasundar, Your original humanlike form) with exclusive devotion, and those who worship the impersonal Brahma, who is the best knower of yoga?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।<br />श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
mayy āveśya mano ye māṁ nitya-yuktā upāsate<br />śraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ [2]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: <span class="e2">ye</span>–Those who;<span class="e2"> śraddhayā upetāḥ</span>–with faith; <span class="e2">parayā</span>–transcendental to the mundane; <span class="e2">āveśya</span>–have absorbed; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–in thought of Me, Śyāmasundar;<span class="e2"> nitya-yuktāḥ</span>–always engaged in exclusive devotion; (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–thus;<span class="e2"> upāsate</span>–worship; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me; <span class="e2">te</span>–they;<span class="e2"> yuktatamāḥ</span>–are the best knowers of yoga. (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–This is; <span class="e2">me</span>–My; <span class="e2">matāḥ</span>–opinion. [2]
2 The Supreme Lord said: In My opinion, those who with faith in the divine are absorbed in thought of Me, Śyāmasundar, and worship Me constantly with exclusive devotion, are the superior knowers of yoga.
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्द्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्य्युपासते ।<br />सर्व्वत्रगमचिन्त्यञ्च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥३॥
सन्नियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्व्वत्र समबुद्धयः ।<br />ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्व्वभूतहिते रताः ॥४॥
ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktaṁ paryupāsate<br />sarvatra-gam achintyañ cha kūṭastham achalaṁ dhruvam [3]
sanniyamyendriya-grāmaṁ sarvatra sama-buddhayaḥ<br />te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ [4]
<span class="e2">ye tu</span>–But those who;<span class="e2"> sanniyamya</span>–fully control;<span class="e2"> indriya-grāmam</span>–all the senses;<span class="e2"> sama-buddhayaḥ</span>–with equanimity;<span class="e2"> sarvatra</span>–for everything; <span class="e2">ratāḥ</span>–(who are) dedicated;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūta-hite</span>–to the welfare of all beings; (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–and thus;<span class="e2"> paryupāsate</span>–worship; (<span class="e2">me</span>)–My;<span class="e2"> anirdeśyam</span>–indefinable;<span class="e2"> avyaktam</span>–unmanifest, impersonal;<span class="e2"> sarvatra-gam</span>–all-pervading;<span class="e2"> achintyam</span>–inconceivable;<span class="e2"> kūṭa-stham</span>–unchanging;<span class="e2"> achalam</span>–immovable;<span class="e2"> dhruvam</span>–eternal;<span class="e2"> akṣaram cha</span>–attributeless aspect of Brahma; <span class="e2">te eva</span>–they, too;<span class="e2"> prāpnuvanti</span>–attain; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me (as My Brahma effulgence). [3–4]
3–4 However, those who fully control their senses, who are equal-minded towards everything, who are dedicated to the welfare of all beings and thus worship My indefinable, impersonal, all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, immovable, eternal, attributeless aspect of Brahma—they, too, attain Me (as Brahma).
Commentary
The Lord’s statement, “The worshippers of Brahma also reach Me,” should not be misconstrued to mean that the impersonalists are on an equal footing with the devotees. The clue as to how the impersonalists can also reach Kṛṣṇa has been given in the writings of Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur.
A person may progress on the path of selfless action up to the stage of meditation, as described in the first six chapters of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>. Then he may undergo great difficulty in searching for the Lord on the path of impersonalism. But when he progresses to the stage of dedicating himself to perform welfare work for others (<span class="e3">sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ</span>), he may get the chance to render service to a pure devotee.
For example, if one engages in the general public welfare work of opening or running a hospital, if some service is even unknowingly rendered to a devotee of the Lord, a Vaiṣṇava, one’s devotional merit begins (ajñāta-sukṛti). By association with a devotee (sādhu-saṅga), one develops faith in the divine personal form of the Lord, and automatically abandons the attempt of attaining to the impersonal Brahma.
With such faith, one takes shelter of a bona fide Guru, engages in the devotional practices based on hearing and chanting the Holy Name and glories of the Lord, and progresses on the path back to home, back to Godhead. Thus Lord Kṛṣṇa indicates: “I am the ultimate goal, and Brahma is only a relative position. It is not the final absolute, because the absolute position is Mine. Only if the impersonalists serve others they may thereby come to Me—because the only way to come to Me is through a Vaiṣṇava.”
रहूगणैतत्तपसा न याति<br />न चेज्यया निर्व्वपणाद्गृहाद्वा ।<br />न च्छन्दसा नैव जलाग्निसूर्य्यैर्<br />विना महत्पादरजोऽभिषेकम् ॥
(भा: ५/१२/१२)
rahūgaṇaitat tapasā na yāti<br />na chejyayā nirvapaṇād gṛhād vā<br />na chchhandasā naiva jalāgni-sūryair<br />vinā mahat-pāda-rajo ’bhiṣekam
(SB: 5.12.12)
(The sage Jaḍ Bharat said to King Rahūgaṇ:) “O Rahūgaṇ, without bathing in the dust of the holy feet (service) of the pure devotees (Mahābhāgavat Vaiṣṇavas), one cannot know the Supreme Lord by adopting the religious life of brahmacharya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha, or sannyās, or by worshipping the gods of water, fire, and sun, etc.”
नैषां मतिस्तावदुरुक्रमाङ्घ्रिं<br />स्पृशत्यनर्थापगमो यदर्थः ।<br />महीयसां पादरजोऽभिषेकं<br />निष्किञ्चनानां न वृणीत यावत्
(भा: ७/५/३२)
naiṣāṁ matis tāvad urukramāṅghriṁ<br />spṛśaty anarthāpagamo yad arthaḥ<br />mahīyasāṁ pāda-rajo ’bhiṣekaṁ<br />niṣkiñchanānāṁ na vṛṇīta yāvat
(SB: 7.5.32)
(Prahlād Mahārāj said:) “As long as persons of mundane mentality have not been bathed by the dust of the feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s surrendered devotees who are free from mundane attachment, they cannot have a touch of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, which are the destroyer of all obstacles.”
To consider that the Lord has taken the personal and impersonal aspects to be equal is a very commonly committed mistake. In reply to Arjuna’s doubt in this respect, the Lord has clearly stated that the personalists are superior to the impersonalists—yet, the impersonalists are also given a chance to reach Him, because without Him, no ultimate goal exists. Without coming to the path of devotion, the worshippers of impersonal Brahma will reach Brahma, the dazzling effulgence of the divine form of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् ।<br />अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते ॥५॥
kleśo ’dhikataras teṣām avyaktāsakta-chetasām<br />avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṁ dehavadbhir avāpyate [5]
<span class="e2">teṣām</span>–For those;<span class="e2"> avyakta-āsakta-chetasām</span>–of minds attached to the unmanifest; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–there is;<span class="e2"> adhikataraḥ</span>–greater; <span class="e2">kleśaḥ</span>–struggle; <span class="e2">hi</span>–as;<span class="e2"> avyaktā gatiḥ</span>–the way of attaining the unmanifest, the impersonal Brahma;<span class="e2"> avāpyate</span>–is attained;<span class="e2"> duḥkham</span>–with difficulty;<span class="e2"> dehavadbhiḥ</span>–by the embodied soul. [5]
5 Persons whose minds are attached to the impersonal Brahma must undergo a greater struggle, as the path of attaining the impersonal Brahma is difficult for the embodied soul.
ये तु सर्व्वाणि कर्म्माणि मयि सन्न्यस्य मत्पराः ।<br />अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥६॥
तेषामहं समुद्धर्त्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् ।<br />भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥७॥
ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-parāḥ<br />ananyenaiva yogena māṁ dhyāyanta upāsate [6]
teṣām ahaṁ samuddhartā mṛtyu-saṁsāra-sāgarāt<br />bhavāmi na chirāt pārtha mayy āveśita-chetasām [7]
<span class="e2">ye tu</span>–But those who;<span class="e2"> sannyasya</span>–offering;<span class="e2"> sarvāṇi</span>–all;<span class="e2"> karmāṇi</span>–actions; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–to Me;<span class="e2"> mat-parāḥ</span>–taking refuge in Me;<span class="e2"> mām dhyāyantaḥ</span>–meditating on Me;<span class="e2"> ananyena yogena eva</span>–with exclusive devotion;<span class="e2"> upāsate</span>–thus worship (Me); (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> na chirāt</span>–without delay;<span class="e2"> bhavāmi</span>–become;<span class="e2"> samuddhartā</span>–the deliverer;<span class="e2"> mṛtyu-saṁsāra-sāgarāt</span>–from the deathly ocean of material suffering; <span class="e2">teṣām</span>–of those persons;<span class="e2"> āveśita-chetasām</span>–whose hearts are absorbed in thought; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–of Me. [6–7]
6–7 But those who offer all their actions to Me, take refuge in Me, their hearts absorbed in thought of Me in pure devotion and who thus worship and adore Me—O Pārtha, I swiftly deliver such dedicated souls from the deathly ocean of material suffering.
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय ।<br />निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥८॥
mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṁ niveśaya<br />nivasiṣyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṁ na saṁśayaḥ [8]
<span class="e2">ādhatsva</span>–Steady; <span class="e2">manaḥ</span>–your mind;<span class="e2"> mayi eva</span>–in Me alone.<span class="e2"> niveśaya</span>–Repose;<span class="e2"> buddhim</span>–your intelligence; <span class="e2">mayi </span>(<span class="e2">eva</span>)–in Me alone.<span class="e2"> nivasiṣyasi</span>–You will abide;<span class="e2"> mayi eva</span>–in Me;<span class="e2"> ataḥ ūrdhvam</span>–hereafter;<span class="e2"> na saṁśayaḥ</span>–there is no doubt. [8]
8 So fix your mind in Me always and repose your intelligence in Me, Śyāmasundar, and you will ultimately abide in Me. Of this there is no doubt.
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।<br />अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥९॥
atha chittaṁ samādhātuṁ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram<br />abhyāsa-yogena tato mām ichchhāptuṁ dhanañjaya [9]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dhanañjaya</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">atha</span>–if;<span class="e2"> na śaknoṣi</span>–you are unable;<span class="e2"> samādhātum</span>–to establish;<span class="e2"> chittam</span>–your mind;<span class="e2"> sthiram</span>–resolutely; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–in Me; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–then;<span class="e2"> ichchha</span>–seek; <span class="e2">āptum</span>–to attain; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> abhyāsa-yogena</span>–by the yoga of constant practice. [9]
9 O Dhanañjaya, and if you are unable to firmly fix your mind in Me, try to attain Me by the repeated practice of remembering Me.
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्म्मपरमो भव ।<br />मदर्थमपि कर्म्माणि कुर्व्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥१०॥
abhyāse ’py asamartho ’si mat-karma-paramo bhava<br />mad-artham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi [10]
(<span class="e2">yadi</span>)–If; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)<span class="e2"> asi</span>–you are;<span class="e2"> asamarthaḥ</span>–unable;<span class="e2"> abhyāse api</span>–to practise remembering Me, too; (<span class="e2">tarhi</span>)–then;<span class="e2"> mat-karma-paramaḥ bhava</span>–concentrate on offering your actions to Me.<span class="e2"> kurvan api</span>–Also by performing;<span class="e2"> karmāṇi</span>–actions;<span class="e2"> mat-artham</span>–for Me;<span class="e2"> avāpsyasi</span>–you will attain;<span class="e2"> siddhim</span>–perfection. [10]
10 If you cannot do that either, concentrate on offering your actions to Me. You will attain perfection through actions performed for Me.
अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्त्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः ।<br />सर्व्वकर्म्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥११॥
athaitad apy aśakto ’si kartuṁ mad-yogam āśritaḥ<br />sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṁ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān [11]
<span class="e2">atha</span>–And if;<span class="e2"> etat api</span>–this, too; <span class="e2">asi</span>–is;<span class="e2"> aśaktah</span>–not possible; <span class="e2">kartum</span>–to do; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–then; <span class="e2">mat-yogam āśritah </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–taking shelter in My yoga; <span class="e2">yata-ātmavān </span>(<span class="e2">bhūtvā</span>)–controlling your mind;<span class="e2"> sarva-karma-phala-tyāgam kuru</span>–give up, for Me, the fruits of all your actions. [11]
11 And if you cannot do that, then resolve to give up, for Me, the fruits of your actions.
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते ।<br />ध्यानात्कर्म्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥१२॥
śreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṁ viśiṣyate<br />dhyānāt karma-phala-tyāgas tyāgāch chhāntir anantaram [12]
<span class="e2">hi</span>–For; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–Knowledge of Me; <span class="e2">śreyaḥ</span>–is better;<span class="e2"> abhyāsāt</span>–than practice;<span class="e2"> dhyānam</span>–meditation on Me;<span class="e2"> jñānāt viśiṣyate</span>–is better than knowledge.<span class="e2"> karma-phala-tyāgaḥ</span>–Giving up, for Me, the fruits of action;<span class="e2"> dhyānāt</span>–comes from meditation. <span class="e2">tyāgāt</span>–From giving up, for Me, the fruits of action; <span class="e2">śāntiḥ</span>–peace ensues;<span class="e2"> anantaram</span>–thereafter. [12]
12 For knowledge of Me is superior to mere practice, and meditation on Me is superior to knowledge alone; from meditation comes the selflessness of giving up, for Me, the fruits of action, following which peace ensues.
अद्वेष्टा सर्व्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।<br />निर्म्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥१३॥
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।<br />मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥१४॥
adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva cha<br />nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣamī [13]
santuṣṭaḥ satataṁ yogī yatātmā dṛḍha-niśchayaḥ<br />mayy-arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ [14]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who is;<span class="e2"> adveṣṭā</span>–without hatred;<span class="e2"> maitraḥ</span>–friendly;<span class="e2"> karuṇaḥ eva cha</span>–and compassionate;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtānām</span>–towards all beings;<span class="e2"> nirmamaḥ</span>–free from possessiveness;<span class="e2"> nirahaṅkāraḥ</span>–free from ego;<span class="e2"> sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ</span>–equipoised in unhappy and happy circumstances; <span class="e2">kṣamī</span>–forgiving, tolerant;<span class="e2"> satatam santuṣṭaḥ</span>–ever content; <span class="e2">yogī</span>–a yogī;<span class="e2"> yata-ātmā</span>–self-controlled;<span class="e2"> dṛḍha-niśchayaḥ</span>–of firm resolve;<span class="e2"> arpita-mano-buddhiḥ</span>–who has given his mind and intelligence; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–to Me; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a person is;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktaḥ</span>–My devotee;<span class="e2"> me priyaḥ</span>–dear to Me. [13–14]
13–14 One who is without hatred, who is friendly and compassionate towards all, free from possessiveness and ego, equipoised in unhappy and happy circumstances, forgiving, always content, a self-controlled yogī of firm resolve who has given his mind and intelligence to Me—such a person is My devotee, and he is dear to Me.
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।<br />हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥१५॥
