yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate cha yaḥ<br />harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa cha me priyaḥ [15]
<span class="e2">yasmāt</span>–He by whom; <span class="e2">lokaḥ</span>–anyone;<span class="e2"> na udvijate</span>–is not disturbed; <span class="e2">yaḥ cha</span>–and he who;<span class="e2"> na udvijate</span>–is not disturbed; <span class="e2">lokāt</span>–by anyone; <span class="e2">yaḥ cha</span>–and who; <span class="e2">muktaḥ</span>–is free;<span class="e2"> harṣa-amarṣa-bhaya-udvegaiḥ</span>–from elation, anger, fear, and grief; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he is; <span class="e2">priyaḥ</span>–dear; <span class="e2">me</span>–to Me. [15]
15 One who causes no disturbance to anyone and who is not disturbed by anyone, who is free from elation, anger, fear, and grief—he is dear to Me.
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः ।<br />सर्व्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥१६॥
anapekṣaḥ śuchir dakṣa udāsīno gata-vyathaḥ<br />sarvārambha-parityāgī yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ [16]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who is;<span class="e2"> anapekṣaḥ</span>–without expectation; <span class="e2">śuchiḥ</span>–clean hearted; <span class="e2">dakṣaḥ</span>–able;<span class="e2"> udāsīnaḥ</span>–impartial;<span class="e2"> gata-vyathaḥ</span>–fearless;<span class="e2"> sarva-ārambha-parityāgī</span>–and a renouncer of all selfish undertakings; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he is;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktaḥ</span>–My devotee;<span class="e2"> me priyaḥ</span>–dear to Me. [16]
16 One who is without expectation, clean hearted, able, impartial, fearless, and a renouncer of all selfish undertakings—he is My devotee, he is dear to Me.
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।<br />शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥१७॥
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śochati na kāṅkṣati<br />śubhāśubha-parityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ [17]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who is;<span class="e2"> na hṛṣyati</span>–neither elated;<span class="e2"> na dveṣṭi</span>–nor resentful;<span class="e2"> na śochati</span>–neither laments any loss;<span class="e2"> na kāṅkṣati</span>–nor hankers for the unattained;<span class="e2"> śubha-aśubha-parityāgī</span>–a renouncer of both auspicious and inauspicious acts;<span class="e2"> yaḥ bhaktimān</span>–and who is endowed with devotion;<span class="e2"> saḥ me priyaḥ</span>–he is dear to Me. [17]
17 One who is neither elated nor resentful, who neither laments nor hankers as he has renounced both auspicious and inauspicious endeavours, and who is endowed with devotion—he is dear to Me.
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।<br />शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्ज्जितः ॥१८॥
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् ।<br />अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥१९॥
samaḥ śatrau cha mitre cha tathā mānāpamānayoḥ<br />śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅga-vivarjitaḥ [18]
tulya-nindā-stutir-maunī santuṣṭo yena kenachit<br />aniketaḥ sthira-matir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ [19]
(<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> naraḥ</span>–A person who; <span class="e2">samaḥ</span>–sees with equality;<span class="e2"> śatrau cha</span>–an enemy;<span class="e2"> mitre cha</span>–and a friend; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–and similarly; <span class="e2">samaḥ</span>–is equipoised;<span class="e2"> māna-apamānayoḥ</span>–in honour and dishonour;<span class="e2"> śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu</span>–and in the presence of cold, heat, pleasure, and pain;<span class="e2"> saṅga-vivarjitaḥ</span>–who has given up all attachment;<span class="e2"> tulya-nindā-stutiḥ</span>–and who considers abuse and praise equally; <span class="e2">maunī</span>–who is contemplative or of controlled speech;<span class="e2"> santuṣṭaḥ</span>–satisfied;<span class="e2"> yena kenachit</span>–in any eventuality;<span class="e2"> aniketaḥ</span>–who has no attachment to hearth and home;<span class="e2"> sthira-matiḥ</span>–whose mind is peaceful;<span class="e2"> bhaktimān</span>–and who is endowed with devotion; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> me priyaḥ</span>–he is dear to Me. [18–19]
18–19 A person who sees with equality an enemy and friend; who is equipoised in honour and dishonour, and in the presence of cold, heat, pleasure, and pain; who has given up all attachment; who considers abuse and praise equally; who is contemplative; who is satisfied in all circumstances; who has no attachment to hearth and home; whose mind is peaceful, and who is endowed with devotion—he is dear to Me.
ये तु धर्म्मामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्य्युपासते ।<br />श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥२०॥
ye tu dharmāmṛtam idaṁ yathoktaṁ paryupāsate<br />śraddadhānā mat-paramā bhaktās te ’tīva me priyāḥ [20]
<span class="e2">ye tu śraddadhānāḥ</span>–Those faithful persons who;<span class="e2"> paryupāsate</span>–adore and follow; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> dharma-amṛtam</span>–nectarean path;<span class="e2"> yathā-uktam</span>–as described;<span class="e2"> mat-paramāḥ</span>–knowing Me as the supreme goal;<span class="e2"> te bhaktāḥ</span>–such devotees; <span class="e2">atīva</span>–are very; <span class="e2">priyaḥ</span>–dear; <span class="e2">me</span>–to Me. [20]
20 Those faithful devotees who, knowing Me as the supreme goal of life, wholeheartedly follow the nectarean path I have described, are very dear to Me.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे भक्तियोगो नाम द्वादशोऽध्यायः ॥१२॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde<br />bhākti-yogo nāma dvādaśo ’dhyāyaḥ [12]
End of Chapter Twelve<br />The Path of Devotion<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Thirteen
Prakṛti-puruṣa-viveka-yoga <br />Distinction Between Matter and Spirit
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
प्रकृतिं पुरुषञ्चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च ।<br />एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयञ्च केशव ॥१॥
arjuna uvācha
prakṛtiṁ puruṣañ chaiva kṣetraṁ kṣetrajñam eva cha<br />etad veditum ichchhāmi jñānaṁ jñeyañ cha keśava [1]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">keśava</span>–O Keśava; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I;<span class="e2"> ichchhāmi</span>–wish;<span class="e2"> veditum</span>–to know; <span class="e2">etat</span>–about these subjects:<span class="e2"> prakṛtim</span>–material nature;<span class="e2"> puruṣam cha eva</span>–and the person;<span class="e2"> kṣetram</span>–the field;<span class="e2"> kṣetra-jñam eva cha</span>–and the knower of the field; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge;<span class="e2"> jñeyam cha</span>–and the object of knowledge. [1]
1 Arjuna said: O Keśava, I would like to know about material nature, the person, the field, the knower of the field, knowledge, and the object of knowledge.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते ।<br />एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
idaṁ śarīraṁ kaunteya kṣetram ity abhidhīyate<br />etad yo vetti taṁ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tad vidaḥ [2]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> idam sarīram</span>–this body;<span class="e2"> abhidhīyate iti</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> kṣetram</span>–kṣetra, or the field.<span class="e2"> yaḥ vetti</span>–One who knows; <span class="e2">etat</span>–this field;<span class="e2"> tat vidaḥ</span>–the learned; <span class="e2">prāhuḥ</span>–describe; <span class="e2">tam</span>–him;<span class="e2"> kṣetra-jñaḥ iti</span>–as kṣetrajña, the knower of the field. [2]
2 The Supreme Lord said: O Arjuna, this body is known as the field. One who knows this field is described by the learned as the knower of the field.
क्षेत्रज्ञञ्चापि मां विद्धि सर्व्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत ।<br />क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥३॥
kṣetrajñañ chāpi māṁ viddhi sarva-kṣetreṣu bhārata<br />kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor jñānaṁ yat taj jñānaṁ mataṁ mama [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O descendant of the Bharat dynasty; <span class="e2">api</span>–further; <span class="e2">cha</span>–also; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> sarva-kṣetreṣu</span>–within all bodies;<span class="e2"> kṣetra-jñam</span>–as kṣetrajña, the knower of the field.<span class="e2"> yat jñānam</span>–This knowledge;<span class="e2"> kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ</span>–of the field and the knower of the field;<span class="e2"> tat jñānam</span>–is actual knowledge;<span class="e2"> mama matam</span>–in My opinion. [3]
3 O Bhārat, you should also know Me as the knower of all fields. This knowledge, of the field and of the knower of the field, is true knowledge, in My opinion.
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।<br />स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु ॥४॥
tat kṣetraṁ yach cha yādṛk cha yad vikāri yataś cha yat<br />sa cha yo yat prabhāvaś cha tat samāsena me śṛṇu [4]
<span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–Hear; <span class="e2">me</span>–from Me;<span class="e2"> tat samāsena</span>–briefly;<span class="e2"> yat tat kṣetram</span>–what that field is; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yādṛk</span>–how is it constituted; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> yat vikāri</span>–what its transformations are; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yataḥ</span>–wherefrom; <span class="e2">yat</span>–it develops; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–who is; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that knower of the field; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> yat prabhāvaḥ</span>–what his potency is. [4]
4 Now hear from Me briefly what this field is, its constitution, transformations, causes and effects; and who the knower of the field is, and of his potency.
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् ।<br />ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः ॥५॥
ṛṣibhir bahudhā gītaṁ chhandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak<br />brahma-sūtra-padaiś chaiva hetumadbhir viniśchitaiḥ [5]
(<span class="e2">tat</span>)–That knowledge of kṣetra and kṣetrajña; <span class="e2">gītam</span>–is sung;<span class="e2"> vividhaiḥ ṛṣibhiḥ</span>–by many types of sages;<span class="e2"> bahudhā eva</span>–in many ways;<span class="e2"> pṛthak chhandobhiḥ</span>–by the different Vedas;<span class="e2"> brahma-sūtra-padaiḥ</span>–and by the aphorisms of Vedānta;<span class="e2"> viniśchitaiḥ</span>–with conclusive;<span class="e2"> hetumadbhiḥ cha</span>–logic. [5]
5 This has been taught in many ways by various sages, the different Vedas, and the aphorisms of the <span class="e3">Brahma-sūtra</span> with its conclusive logic.
महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च ।<br />इन्द्रियाणि दशैकञ्च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥६॥
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतना धृतिः ।<br />एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥७॥
mahā-bhūtāny ahaṅkāro buddhir avyaktam eva cha<br />indriyāṇi daśaikañ cha pañcha chendriya-gocharāḥ [6]
ichchhā dveṣaḥ sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṅghātaś chetanā dhṛtiḥ<br />etat kṣetraṁ samāsena sa-vikāram udāhṛtam [7]
<span class="e2">mahā-bhūtāni</span>–The five primary elements;<span class="e2"> ahaṅkāraḥ</span>–ego;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–intelligence (mahat-tattva);<span class="e2"> avyaktam eva cha</span>–the unmanifest material nature;<span class="e2"> daśa indriyāṇi</span>–the ten senses (the five senses of action—voice, hands, legs, anus, and genital; and the five senses of perception—eye, tongue, skin, nose, and ear);<span class="e2"> ekam cha</span>–and the mind;<span class="e2"> pañcha cha</span>–and the five;<span class="e2"> indriya-gocharāḥ</span>–corresponding objects of the senses (form, taste, touch, smell, and sound);<span class="e2"> ichchhā</span>–likes; <span class="e2">dveṣaḥ</span>–dislikes; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–happiness;<span class="e2"> duḥkham</span>–unhappiness;<span class="e2"> saṅghātaḥ</span>–the aggregate, the gross body;<span class="e2"> chetanā</span>–consciousness; <span class="e2">dhṛtiḥ</span>–determination; <span class="e2">etat</span>–all these;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtam</span>–are described;<span class="e2"> samāsena</span>–in brief;<span class="e2"> kṣetram</span>–as the field;<span class="e2"> sa-vikāram</span>–with its transformations. [6–7]
6–7 The five primary elements of ether, air, fire, water, and earth; ego, intelligence, and the unmanifest material nature; the ten senses, the mind, and the five objects of the senses; likes, dislikes, happiness, unhappiness, the aggregate, consciousness, and determination—all these are summarily known as the field and its transformations.
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्ज्जवम् ।<br />आचार्य्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्य्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥८॥
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च ।<br />जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥९॥
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु ।<br />नित्यञ्च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु ॥१०॥
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी ।<br />विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि ॥११॥
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् ।<br />एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा ॥१२॥
amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṁsā kṣāntir ārjavam<br />āchāryopāsanaṁ śauchaṁ sthairyam ātma-vinigrahaḥ [8]
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyam anahaṅkāra eva cha<br />janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣānudarśanam [9]
asaktir anabhiṣv-aṅgaḥ putra-dāra-gṛhādiṣu<br />nityañ cha sama-chittatvam iṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu [10]
mayi chānanya-yogena bhaktir avyabhichāriṇī<br />vivikta-deśa-sevitvam aratir jana-saṁsadi [11]
adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvaṁ tattva-jñānārtha-darśanam<br />etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṁ yad ato ’nyathā [12]
<span class="e2">etat jñānam</span>–The following qualities denote knowledge:<span class="e2"> amānitvam</span>–the quality of desirelessness for honour;<span class="e2"> adambhitvam</span>–pridelessness; <span class="e2">ahiṁsā</span>–nonviolence;<span class="e2"> kṣāntiḥ</span>–forbearance;<span class="e2"> ārjavam</span>–straightforwardness and simplicity;<span class="e2"> āchārya-upāsanam</span>–service to the spiritual master;<span class="e2"> śaucham</span>–purity;<span class="e2"> sthairyam</span>–steadiness;<span class="e2"> ātma-vinigrahaḥ</span>–self-control;<span class="e2"> indriya-artheṣu vairāgyam</span>–detachment from the objects of the senses;<span class="e2"> anahaṅkāraḥ eva cha</span>–absence of egoism;<span class="e2"> duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśanam</span>–awareness of the miseries;<span class="e2"> janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi</span>–of birth, death, infirmity, and disease;<span class="e2"> asaktiḥ</span>–worldly detachment;<span class="e2"> anabhiṣu-aṅgaḥ</span>–not to dote on;<span class="e2"> putra-dāra-gṛha-ādiṣu</span>–children, wife, home, etc.;<span class="e2"> nityam sama-chittatvam cha</span>–constant equanimity;<span class="e2"> iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-upapattiṣu</span>–in desirable or undesirable circumstances; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> ananya-yogena</span>–single-minded;<span class="e2"> avyabhichāriṇī</span>–undeviating;<span class="e2"> bhaktiḥ</span>–devotion; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–to Me;<span class="e2"> vivikta-deśa-sevitam</span>–residing in a solitary place; <span class="e2">aratiḥ</span>–indifference;<span class="e2"> jana-saṁsadi</span>–to mundane association;<span class="e2"> adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvam</span>–constancy in self-knowledge;<span class="e2"> tattva-jñāna-artha-darśanam</span>–and the vision of the goal of true knowledge; <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus;<span class="e2"> proktam</span>–has been proclaimed; (<span class="e2">ṛṣibhiḥ</span>)–by the sages. <span class="e2">yat</span>–Anything;<span class="e2"> anyathā</span>–contrary; <span class="e2">ataḥ</span>–to this;<span class="e2"> ajñānam</span>–is nescience. [8–12]
8–12 Desirelessness for honour, pridelessness, nonviolence, forbearance, honesty, service to the spiritual master, purity, stability, self-control, detachment from the objects of the senses, absence of egoism, awareness of the miseries of birth, disease, old age, and death; worldly detachment, absence of doting on children, wife, home, etc., constant equanimity in desirable or undesirable circumstances, undeviating pure devotion to Me, residing in a solitary place, indifference to mundane association, constancy in self-knowledge, and the vision of the goal of true knowledge—all these qualities have been said to denote knowledge. Anything contrary to this is to be considered ignorance.
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वामृतमश्नुते ।<br />अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥१३॥
jñeyaṁ yat tat pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvāmṛtam aśnute<br />anādi mat-paraṁ brahma na sat tan nāsad uchyate [13]
(<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> pravakṣyāmi</span>–I now describe; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; <span class="e2">jñeyam</span>–is the object of knowledge; <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–realising; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; <span class="e2">amṛtam</span>–the nectar of life; <span class="e2">aśnute</span>–is attained.<span class="e2"> tat brahma uchyate</span>–That is known as Brahma; <span class="e2">anādi</span>–beginningless, eternal;<span class="e2"> mat-param</span>–resting in Me; <span class="e2">na sat</span>–beyond being, beyond the material effect; <span class="e2">na asat</span>–and beyond non-being, beyond the material cause. [13]
13 Now I shall describe the object of knowledge, realising which one attains the nectar of life. Resting in Me, it is known as Brahma, eternal, neither being nor non-being.
सर्व्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्व्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ।<br />सर्व्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्व्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥१४॥
sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṁ tat sarvato ’kṣi-śiro-mukham<br />sarvataḥ śrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati [14]
<span class="e2">sarvataḥ</span>–Everywhere;<span class="e2"> pāṇi-pādam</span>–hands and feet;<span class="e2"> sarvataḥ</span>–everywhere;<span class="e2"> akṣi-śiraḥ-mukham</span>–eyes, heads, and mouths;<span class="e2"> sarvataḥ</span>–everywhere;<span class="e2"> śrutimat</span>–ears; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that object of knowledge;<span class="e2"> tiṣṭhati</span>–exists; <span class="e2">āvṛtya</span>–pervading; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–everything; <span class="e2">loke</span>–in the universe. [14]
14 Everywhere are His hands and feet, everywhere are His eyes, heads, mouths, and ears. He pervades the entire universe (as the Supersoul).
सर्व्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्व्वेन्द्रियविवर्ज्जितम् ।<br />असक्तं सर्व्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥१५॥
sarvendriya-guṇābhāsaṁ sarvendriya-vivarjitam<br />asaktaṁ sarva-bhṛch chaiva nirguṇaṁ guṇa-bhoktṛ cha [15]
<span class="e2">sarva-indriya-guṇa-ābhāsam</span>–(He) illuminates all the senses and their functions; (<span class="e2">tad api</span>)–yet;<span class="e2"> sarva-indriya-vivarjitam</span>–is without (material) senses.<span class="e2"> asaktam</span>–(Although) aloof;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhṛt cha</span>–(He is) the maintainer of all.<span class="e2"> nirguṇam cha</span>–(Although) transcendental to the modes of nature;<span class="e2"> guṇa-bhoktṛ eva</span>–(He is) the Lord of all qualities. [15]
15 He illuminates all the senses and their functions, yet He is without material senses; He is completely aloof to everything, yet He is the maintainer of all (Viṣṇu); He is transcendental to the three modes of material nature, yet He is the Lord of all qualities.
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च ।<br />सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥१६॥
bahir antaś cha bhūtānām acharaṁ charam eva cha<br />sūkṣmatvāt tad avijñeyaṁ dūrasthaṁ chāntike cha tat [16]
<span class="e2">tat</span>–That knowable is;<span class="e2"> bahiḥ cha</span>–outside; <span class="e2">antaḥ</span>–and inside;<span class="e2"> acharam</span>–stationary;<span class="e2"> charam eva cha</span>–and moving;<span class="e2"> bhūtānām</span>–beings.<span class="e2"> sūkṣmatvāt</span>–Due to subtlety; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> avijñeyam</span>–is difficult to comprehend;<span class="e2"> antike cha</span>–near;<span class="e2"> dūra-stham cha</span>–yet far. [16]
16 He is situated within and without all moving and stationary beings, near yet far, subtle, and therefore most difficult to comprehend.
अविभक्तञ्च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।<br />भूतभर्त्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥१७॥
avibhaktañ cha bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva cha sthitam<br />bhūta-bhartṛ cha taj jñeyaṁ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu cha [17]
<span class="e2">tat avibhaktam</span>–That indivisible;<span class="e2"> sthitam</span>–appears;<span class="e2"> vibhaktam iva cha</span>–as divided;<span class="e2"> bhūteṣu</span>–in the living beings. (<span class="e2">tat eva</span>)–He; <span class="e2">jñeyam</span>–is to be known;<span class="e2"> prabha-viṣṇu cha</span>–as the manifestor;<span class="e2"> bhūta-bhartṛ cha</span>–the maintainer;<span class="e2"> grasiṣṇu cha</span>–and the devourer. [17]
17 Although indivisible, He appears as divided in all beings. He is to be known as the one who manifests, maintains, and devours all beings.
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते ।<br />ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्व्वस्य धिष्ठितम् ॥१८॥
jyotiṣām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param uchyate<br />jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ jñāna-gamyaṁ hṛdi sarvasya dhiṣṭhitam [18]
<span class="e2">tat</span>–He;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is said to be; <span class="e2">jyotiḥ</span>–the illuminator;<span class="e2"> jyotiṣām api</span>–of the luminaries; <span class="e2">param</span>–beyond;<span class="e2"> tamasaḥ</span>–the darkness; (<span class="e2">tat eva</span>)–He is; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge; <span class="e2">jñeyam</span>–the object of knowledge;<span class="e2"> jñāna-gamyam</span>–reached by knowledge (verses 8–12);<span class="e2"> dhiṣṭhitam</span>–situated as the Supersoul; <span class="e2">hṛdi</span>–within the hearts;<span class="e2"> sarvasya</span>–of all. [18]
18 He is known as the illuminator of the luminaries, beyond darkness. Situated in the hearts of all beings, He is knowledge, the object of knowledge, reached by knowledge.
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयञ्चोक्तुं समासतः ।<br />मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥१९॥
iti kṣetraṁ tathā jñānaṁ jñeyañ choktuṁ samāsataḥ<br />mad-bhakta etad vijñāya mad-bhāvāyopapadyate [19]
<span class="e2">iti</span>–Thus;<span class="e2"> kṣetram</span>–the field; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge;<span class="e2"> jñeyam cha</span>–and the object of knowledge (the Lord in His aspects of Brahma, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān);<span class="e2"> tathā uktam</span>–are described;<span class="e2"> samāsataḥ</span>–in brief.<span class="e2"> etat vijñāya</span>–Realising this;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktaḥ</span>–My devotee;<span class="e2"> upapadyate</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> mat-bhāvāya</span>–love for Me. [19]
19 The field, knowledge, and the object of knowledge have been briefly described by Me. Realising these truths, My devotee attains love for Me.
प्रकृतिं पुरुषञ्चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि ।<br />विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसम्भवान् ॥२०॥
prakṛtiṁ puruṣañ chaiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api<br />vikārāṁś cha guṇāṁś chaiva viddhi prakṛti-sambhavān [20]
<span class="e2">viddhi</span>–Know;<span class="e2"> ubhau api</span>–both;<span class="e2"> prakṛtim</span>–nature—māyā;<span class="e2"> puruṣam cha</span>–and the jīvātma, individual soul, described as ‘knower of the field’;<span class="e2"> anādī eva</span>–to be beginningless. <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–Know;<span class="e2"> vikārān cha</span>–the transformations—body, senses, and their functions;<span class="e2"> guṇān eva cha</span>–and the transformations of the modes of nature, as happiness, unhappiness, sorrow, and delusion, etc.;<span class="e2"> prakṛti-sambhavān</span>–as born of material nature. [20]
20 Know that both material nature (māyā) and the person (individual soul) are beginningless, and know that the transformations (body, senses, and their functions) and the transformations of the modes of nature (such as pleasure, pain, sorrow, and delusion) are born of material nature.
कार्य्यकारणकर्त्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।<br />पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥२१॥
kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir uchyate<br />puruṣaḥ sukha-duḥkhānāṁ bhoktṛtve hetur uchyate [21]
<span class="e2">prakṛtiḥ</span>–Material nature (with the presence of puruṣ);<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is said to be; <span class="e2">hetuḥ</span>–the cause;<span class="e2"> kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛtve</span>–via the presiding demigods of the senses, of the production of the effect, as the body, and of the cause, as the senses.<span class="e2"> puruṣaḥ</span>–The person—jīva;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is said to be; <span class="e2">hetuḥ</span>–the cause;<span class="e2"> bhoktṛtve</span>–of the state of being an enjoyer or a sufferer;<span class="e2"> sukha-duḥkhānām</span>–of happiness and unhappiness. [21]
21 Material nature is said to be the cause of the production of effect (the body) and cause (the senses); the person (in material bondage) is said to be the cause of the condition of being an enjoyer or a sufferer of happiness and unhappiness.
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् ।<br />कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥२२॥
puruṣaḥ prakṛti-stho hi bhuṅkte prakṛti-jān guṇān<br />kāraṇaṁ guṇa-saṅgo ’sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu [22]
<span class="e2">prakṛti-sthaḥ</span>–Situated within (the body which is an effect of) material nature;<span class="e2"> puruṣaḥ hi</span>–a person;<span class="e2"> bhuṅkte</span>–enjoys; <span class="e2">guṇān</span>–the modes;<span class="e2"> prakṛti-jān</span>–born of material nature.<span class="e2"> guṇa-saṅgaḥ</span>–Attachment to the modes (as body, senses, etc.); (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–is;<span class="e2"> kāraṇam</span>–the cause; <span class="e2">asya</span>–of that person’s;<span class="e2"> sat-asat-yoni-janmasu</span>–births in higher and lower species. [22]
22 Being situated within material nature, a person enjoys the modes born of material nature. His attachment to these modes is the cause of his repeated births in higher and lower species.
उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्त्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः ।<br />परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥२३॥
upadraṣṭānumantā cha bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ<br />paramātmeti chāpy ukto dehe ’smin puruṣaḥ paraḥ [23]
<span class="e2">paraḥ puruṣaḥ</span>–The Supreme Person;<span class="e2"> upadraṣṭā</span>–witness;<span class="e2"> anumantā</span>–sanctioner; <span class="e2">bhartā</span>–support; <span class="e2">bhoktā</span>–maintainer;<span class="e2"> mahā-īśvaraḥ cha</span>–and Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> asmin dehe</span>–within this body;<span class="e2"> api uktaḥ</span>–is also described; <span class="e2">iti cha</span>–as;<span class="e2"> paramātmā</span>–Paramātmā, the Supersoul. [23]
23 The Supreme Person—the witness, sanctioner, support, guardian, and almighty Lord within this body, is known as Paramātmā, the Supersoul.
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिञ्च गुणैः सह ।<br />सर्व्वथा वर्त्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥२४॥
ya evaṁ vetti puruṣaṁ prakṛtiñ cha guṇaiḥ saha<br />sarvathā vartamāno ’pi na sa bhūyo ’bhijāyate [24]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who;<span class="e2"> evam vetti</span>–thus knows;<span class="e2"> puruṣam</span>–the Supreme Person;<span class="e2"> prakṛtim cha</span>–and material nature;<span class="e2"> guṇaiḥ saha</span>–with its modes; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he;<span class="e2"> vartamānaḥ api</span>–though present;<span class="e2"> sarvathā</span>–in any situation;<span class="e2"> na abhijāyate</span>–is not born; <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–again. [24]
24 Thus, one who truly knows the Supreme Person and material nature with its modes, will never in any circumstances have to take birth again.
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना ।<br />अन्ये साङ्ख्ये न योगेन कर्म्मयोगेन चापरे ॥२५॥
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kechid ātmānam ātmanā<br />anye sāṅkhyena yogena karma-yogena chāpare [25]
<span class="e2">kechit</span>–Some;<span class="e2"> paśyanti</span>–see;<span class="e2"> dhyānena</span>–by meditation; <span class="e2">ātmanā</span>–by the pure consciousness;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–the Supersoul; <span class="e2">ātmani</span>–within the heart; <span class="e2">anye</span>–others;<span class="e2"> sāṅkhyena yogena</span>–by sāṅkhya-yoga;<span class="e2"> apare cha</span>–and yet others;<span class="e2"> karma-yogena</span>–by karma-yoga. [25]
25 With their pure consciousness, some persons see the Supersoul within the heart, in their meditation. Others perceive Him through enlightenment, and yet others by the yoga of selfless action.
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते ।<br />तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥२६॥
anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate<br />te ’pi chātitaranty eva mṛtyuṁ śruti-parāyaṇāḥ [26]
<span class="e2">anye tu</span>–Yet others;<span class="e2"> ajānantaḥ</span>–not knowing; <span class="e2">evam</span>–of all these methods;<span class="e2"> upāsate</span>–worship; <span class="e2">śrutvā</span>–by hearing;<span class="e2"> anyebhyaḥ</span>–from others. <span class="e2">te api</span>–They too; <span class="e2">śruti-parāyaṇāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–when their faith is deepened by hearing;<span class="e2"> atitaranti eva</span>–surpass;<span class="e2"> mṛtyum cha</span>–death. [26]
26 Further, there are those who, not knowing of these methods, engage in worship by hearing the scriptures. When their faith is deepened by such hearing, they, too, surpass the mortal plane.
यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।<br />क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥२७॥
yāvat sañjāyate kiñchit sattvaṁ sthāvara-jaṅgamam<br />kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṁyogāt tad viddhi bharatarṣabha [27]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharatarṣabha</span>–O best of the Bharat dynasty;<span class="e2"> yāvat kiñchit</span>–whatever;<span class="e2"> sthāvara-jaṅgamam</span>–stationary or moving;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–being;<span class="e2"> sañjayate</span>–is born; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṁyogāt</span>–as born of the combination of the field and its knower. [27]
27 O Arjuna, best of the Bhāratas, whatever is born in the world, whether moving or stationary, know it to be manifest from the combination of the field and its knower.
समं सर्व्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।<br />विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥२८॥
samaṁ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṁ parameśvaram<br />vinaśyatsv avinaśyantaṁ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati [28]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who;<span class="e2"> paśyati</span>–sees;<span class="e2"> parama-īśvaram</span>–the Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> tiṣṭhantam</span>–situated; <span class="e2">samam</span>–equally;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu bhūteṣu</span>–in all beings;<span class="e2"> avinaśyantam</span>–as the imperishable;<span class="e2"> vinaśyatsu</span>–within the perishable; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a person;<span class="e2"> paśyati</span>–sees perfectly. [28]
28 One who sees the Supreme Lord situated equally within all beings as the imperishable within the perishable—such a person sees perfectly.
समं पश्यन्हि सर्व्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् ।<br />न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥२९॥
samaṁ paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram<br />na hinasty ātmanātmānaṁ tato yāti parāṁ gatim [29]
(<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> hi</span>–Such a person; <span class="e2">paśyan</span>–by seeing; <span class="e2">samam</span>–with equality;<span class="e2"> īśvaram</span>–the Lord;<span class="e2"> samavasthitam</span>–dwelling alike;<span class="e2"> sarvatra</span>–in every place;<span class="e2"> na hinasti</span>–does not deceive, deprive;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–himself; <span class="e2">ātmanā</span>–by himself; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–and therefore; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> parām gatim</span>–the supreme destination. [29]
29 Such a person with the vision of equality, seeing the Lord dwelling in every place alike, does not deceive himself, and thus he attains the supreme destination.
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्म्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्व्वशः ।<br />यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्त्तारं स पश्यति ॥३०॥
prakṛtyaiva cha karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ<br />yaḥ paśyati tathātmānam akartāraṁ sa paśyati [30]
<span class="e2">cha</span>–And; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–he who;<span class="e2"> paśyati</span>–sees; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–that;<span class="e2"> sarvaśaḥ</span>–all;<span class="e2"> karmāṇi</span>–actions;<span class="e2"> kriyamāṇāni</span>–are brought about; <span class="e2">eva</span>–only;<span class="e2"> prakṛtyā</span>–by material nature; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a person;<span class="e2"> paśyati</span>–sees;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–himself;<span class="e2"> akartāram</span>–as non-doer. [30]
30 He who sees that all actions are brought about only by material nature, sees himself as non-doer.
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति ।<br />तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥३१॥
yadā bhūta-pṛthag-bhāvam eka-stham anupaśyati<br />tata eva cha vistāraṁ brahma sampadyate tadā [31]
<span class="e2">yadā</span>–When; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–such a seer;<span class="e2"> anupaśyati</span>–can see;<span class="e2"> bhūta-pṛthak-bhāvam</span>–the different types of beings;<span class="e2"> eka-stham</span>–situated in the one nature; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">bhūtānām</span>)<span class="e2"> vistāram</span>–the projection of all beings;<span class="e2"> tataḥ eva</span>–from that nature; <span class="e2">tadā</span>–then;<span class="e2"> brahma sampadyate</span>–the state of Brahma is reached. [31]
31 When such an enlightened person realises that the different types of beings are situated within the one nature and that all are made manifest from that nature, he attains realisation of Brahma.
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः ।<br />शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥३२॥
anāditvān nirguṇatvāt paramātmāyam avyayaḥ<br />śarīra-stho ’pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate [32]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> anāditvāt</span>–because of eternality;<span class="e2"> nirguṇatvāt</span>–and being transcendental to the material modes;<span class="e2"> avyayaḥ</span>–and inexhaustible; <span class="e2">ayam</span>–the;<span class="e2"> paramātmā</span>–Supersoul;<span class="e2"> śarīra-sthaḥ api</span>–although present within the field;<span class="e2"> na karoti</span>–neither acts;<span class="e2"> na lipyate</span>–nor is affected by any action. [32]
32 O Arjuna, since the Supersoul is beginningless, transcendental, and inexhaustible, although also present within the field (with the individual soul), He neither acts nor is affected by any action.
यथा सर्व्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते ।<br />सर्व्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥३३॥
yathā sarva-gataṁ saukṣmyād ākāśaṁ nopalipyate<br />sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate [33]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–As;<span class="e2"> sarva-gatam</span>–the all-pervading; <span class="e2">ākāśam</span>–space;<span class="e2"> na upalipyate</span>–is not tainted by anything, is untouched;<span class="e2"> saukṣmyāt</span>–due to its subtleness; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–similarly; <span class="e2">ātmā</span>–ātma, the soul;<span class="e2"> avasthitaḥ</span>–situated;<span class="e2"> sarvatra</span>–pervading; <span class="e2">dehe</span>–the body;<span class="e2"> na upalipyate</span>–is not tainted or touched. [33]
33 As the most subtle element of space pervades everything yet is not tainted by anything, similarly, the soul, though pervading the body, is not tainted by it.
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः ।<br />क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥३४॥
yathā prakāśayaty ekaḥ kṛtsnaṁ lokam imaṁ raviḥ<br />kṣetraṁ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṁ prakāśayati bhārata [34]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">yathā</span>–as; <span class="e2">ekaḥ</span>–the one; <span class="e2">raviḥ</span>–sun;<span class="e2"> prakāśayati</span>–illuminates; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam</span>–entire; <span class="e2">lokam</span>–world; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–similarly; <span class="e2">kṣetrī</span>–the occupier of the field;<span class="e2"> prakāśayati</span>–illuminates;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnam</span>–the entire;<span class="e2"> kṣetram</span>–field. [34]
34 O Bhārat, as the one sun illuminates the entire world, the occupier of the field illuminates the entire field.
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।<br />भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षञ्च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥३५॥
kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor evam antaraṁ jñāna-chakṣuṣā<br />bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣañ cha ye vidur yānti te param [35]
<span class="e2">ye</span>–Those who;<span class="e2"> jñāna-chakṣuṣā</span>–through the eyes of knowledge;<span class="e2"> evam viduḥ</span>–can thus know;<span class="e2"> antaram</span>–the distinction;<span class="e2"> kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ</span>–between the field and its knower; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and (can thus know);<span class="e2"> bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣam</span>–the way of liberation of the living beings from material nature; <span class="e2">te</span>–they; <span class="e2">yānti</span>–attain; <span class="e2">param</span>–the Supreme. [35]
35 Those who, through the eyes of knowledge, can thus distinguish between the field and the knower of the field, and who can thus know the path of liberation of the living beings from material nature—such persons attain the Supreme.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे प्रकृतिपुरुषविवेकयोगो नाम त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः ॥१३॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde prakṛti-<br />puruṣa-viveka-yogo nāma trayodaśo ’dhyāyaḥ [13]
End of Chapter Thirteen<br />Distinction between Matter and Spirit<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

चतुर्द्दशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Fourteen
Guṇatraya-vibhāga-yoga <br />The Three Divisions of Material Nature
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।<br />यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्व्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥१॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
paraṁ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṁ jñānam uttamam<br />yaj jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṁ siddhim ito gatāḥ [1]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–Again; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> pravakṣyāmi</span>–I shall speak; <span class="e2">param</span>–the supreme; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge, teaching;<span class="e2"> uttamam</span>–the highest;<span class="e2"> jñānānām</span>–of all fields of knowledge; <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; <span class="e2">sarve</span>–all;<span class="e2"> munayaḥ</span>–the sages; <span class="e2">gatāḥ</span>–attained; <span class="e2">parām</span>–ultimate;<span class="e2"> siddhim</span>–perfection; <span class="e2">itaḥ</span>–beyond this mundane plane. [1]
1 The Supreme Lord said: Again, I shall describe to you the supreme teaching, the highest of all fields of knowledge, knowing which the sages attained the ultimate perfection beyond this mundane plane.
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्म्यमागताः ।<br />सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥२॥
idaṁ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ<br />sarge ’pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti cha [2]
<span class="e2">upāśritya</span>–Taking refuge in; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge; (<span class="e2">jīvaḥ</span>)–the living being; <span class="e2">āgatāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–attaining;<span class="e2"> sādharmyam</span>–the same (spiritual) nature; <span class="e2">mama</span>–as Mine;<span class="e2"> na upajāyante</span>–is neither born;<span class="e2"> sarge api</span>–in the universal manifestation;<span class="e2"> na vyathanti</span>–nor suffers;<span class="e2"> pralaye cha</span>–in the universal dissolution. [2]
2 By taking refuge in this knowledge, the soul attains to My nature. Then he is neither born in the cosmic manifestation, nor does he suffer (death) in the cosmic dissolution.
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन्गर्भं दधाम्यहम् ।<br />सम्भवः सर्व्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥३॥
mama yonir mahad-brahma tasmin garbhaṁ dadhāmy aham<br />sambhavaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ tato bhavati bhārata [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> mahat-brahma</span>–primordial matter;<span class="e2"> mama yoniḥ</span>–is My place of impregnation; <span class="e2">tasmin</span>–into which; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> dadhāmi</span>–cast;<span class="e2"> garbham</span>–the seed. <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–From there;<span class="e2"> sambhavaḥ</span>–the birth;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtānām</span>–of all living beings;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–occurs. [3]
3 O Bhārat, I place the seed within My womb of primordial matter from which all living beings take birth.
सर्व्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्त्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः ।<br />तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥४॥
sarva-yoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ<br />tāsāṁ brahma mahad yonir ahaṁ bīja-pradaḥ pitā [4]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> yāḥ mūrtayaḥ</span>–of all forms which;<span class="e2"> sambhavanti</span>–are born;<span class="e2"> sarva-yoniṣu</span>–of the wombs of all species; <span class="e2">tāsām</span>–their; <span class="e2">yoniḥ</span>–womb;<span class="e2"> mahat brahma</span>–is primordial matter; <span class="e2">aham</span>–and I;<span class="e2"> bīja-pradaḥ</span>–the seed-giving; <span class="e2">pitā</span>–father. [4]
4 O Kaunteya, primordial matter is the original womb of all life-forms that are born of the wombs of all species, and I am the seed-giving father.
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसम्भवाः ।<br />निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥५॥
sattvaṁ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛti-sambhavāḥ<br />nibadhnanti mahā-bāho dehe dehinam avyayam [5]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty hero; <span class="e2">guṇāḥ</span>–the qualities;<span class="e2"> sattvam rajaḥ tamaḥ iti</span>–known as goodness, passion, and ignorance;<span class="e2"> prakṛti-sambhavāḥ</span>–manifest from material nature;<span class="e2"> nibadhnanti</span>–bind;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–the immutable;<span class="e2"> dehinam</span>–resident of the body; <span class="e2">dehe</span>–within the body. [5]
5 O mighty hero, Arjuna, the three modes of goodness, passion, and ignorance, born of material nature, bind the immutable spirit soul within the body.
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्म्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् ।<br />सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥६॥
tatra sattvaṁ nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam<br />sukha-saṅgena badhnāti jñāna-saṅgena chānagha [6]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">anagha</span>–O sinless one; <span class="e2">tatra</span>–among these three;<span class="e2"> nirmalatvāt</span>–due to purity;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–the mode of goodness;<span class="e2"> prakāśakam</span>–illuminating;<span class="e2"> anāmayam</span>–and wholesome;<span class="e2"> badhnāti</span>–binds; (<span class="e2">dehinam</span>)–the embodied living being;<span class="e2"> sukha-saṅgena</span>–with happiness;<span class="e2"> jñāna-saṅgena cha</span>–and knowledge. [6]
6 O sinless one, of these three modes, due its purity, the mode of goodness is illuminating and wholesome, conditioning one to happiness and knowledge.
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् ।<br />तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्म्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥७॥
rajo rāgātmakaṁ viddhi tṛṣṇā-saṅga-samudbhavam<br />tan nibadhnāti kaunteya karma-saṅgena dehinam [7]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know; <span class="e2">rajaḥ</span>–the mode of passion;<span class="e2"> rāga-ātmakam</span>–as the embodiment of desire;<span class="e2"> tṛṣṇā-saṅga-samudbhavam</span>–born of hankering and attachment. <span class="e2">tat</span>–That rajo-guṇa mode of passion;<span class="e2"> nibadhnāti</span>–binds;<span class="e2"> dehinam</span>–the embodied;<span class="e2"> karma-saṅgena</span>–by action. [7]
7 O son of Kuntī, know the mode of passion to be the embodiment of desire. Born of hankering and attachment, it conditions one to action.
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्व्वदेहिनाम् ।<br />प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥८॥
tamas tv ajñāna-jaṁ viddhi mohanaṁ sarva-dehinām<br />pramādālasya-nidrābhis tan nibadhnāti bhārata [8]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> viddhi tu</span>–and know; <span class="e2">tamaḥ</span>–the mode of ignorance;<span class="e2"> ajñāna-jam</span>–born of darkness;<span class="e2"> mohanam</span>–the delusion;<span class="e2"> sarva-dehinām</span>–of all the embodied beings; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> nibadhnāti</span>–binds; (<span class="e2">dehinam</span>)–the living being;<span class="e2"> pramāda-ālasya-nidrābhiḥ</span>–with delusion, laziness, and sleep. [8]
8 And, O Bhārat, know the mode of ignorance, born of darkness, to be the ignorance of all the embodied beings, conditioning them to delusion, laziness, and slumber.
सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्म्मणि भारत ।<br />ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥९॥
sattvaṁ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata<br />jñānam āvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayaty uta [9]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–the mode of goodness;<span class="e2"> sañjayati</span>–dominates; (<span class="e2">dehinam</span>)–the embodied living being; <span class="e2">sukhe</span>–with happiness; <span class="e2">rajaḥ</span>–and the mode of passion;<span class="e2"> karmaṇi</span>–with action; <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">tamaḥ</span>–the mode of ignorance; <span class="e2">āvṛtya</span>–covering; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge;<span class="e2"> sañjayati uta</span>–binds one;<span class="e2"> pramāde</span>–with illusion. [9]
9 O Arjuna, the mode of goodness conditions the embodied being to happiness, and the mode of passion conditions him to action. But the mode of ignorance covers his knowledge and traps him in illusion.
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत ।<br />रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥१०॥
rajas tamaś chābhibhūya sattvaṁ bhavati bhārata<br />rajaḥ sattvaṁ tamaś chaiva tamaḥ sattvaṁ rajas tathā [10]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–the mode of goodness;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–appears;<span class="e2"> abhibhūya</span>–defeating;<span class="e2"> rajaḥ tamaḥ cha</span>–the modes of passion and ignorance. <span class="e2">rajaḥ</span>–The mode of passion; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–appears; (<span class="e2">abhibhūya</span>)–defeating;<span class="e2"> sattvam tamaḥ eva cha</span>–goodness and ignorance too. <span class="e2">tathā</span>–Similarly; <span class="e2">tamaḥ</span>–ignorance; (<span class="e2">abhibhūya bhavati</span>)–defeats;<span class="e2"> sattvam rajaḥ</span>–goodness and passion. [10]
10 O Bhārat, goodness overcomes passion and ignorance, passion overcomes goodness and ignorance, and ignorance overcomes goodness and passion. Each mode in turn defeats the others in an unending battle for supremacy.
सर्व्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते ।<br />ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥११॥
sarva-dvāreṣu dehe ’smin prakāśa upajāyate<br />jñānaṁ yadā tadā vidyād vivṛddhaṁ sattvam ity uta [11]
<span class="e2">yadā</span>–When;<span class="e2"> prakāśaḥ</span>–illumination; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–of knowledge;<span class="e2"> upajāyate</span>–appears;<span class="e2"> sarva-dvāreṣu</span>–in the gateways (the senses);<span class="e2"> asmin dehe</span>–of this body; <span class="e2">tadā</span>–then;<span class="e2"> vidyāt iti uta</span>–know by that symptom;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–the mode of goodness;<span class="e2"> vivṛddham</span>–has increased. [11]
11 When the gateways of the body are illuminated with knowledge, know this to be the manifestation of the mode of goodness.
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्म्मणामशमः स्पृहा ।<br />रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥१२॥
lobhaḥ pravṛttir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśamaḥ spṛhā<br />rajasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha [12]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharatarṣabha</span>–O most noble of the Bharat dynasty;<span class="e2"> rajasi vivṛddhe</span>–with a predominance of the mode of passion; <span class="e2">etāni</span>–all these symptoms;<span class="e2"> jāyante</span>–are manifest: <span class="e2">lobhaḥ</span>–greed;<span class="e2"> pravṛttiḥ</span>–exertion;<span class="e2"> ārambhaḥ</span>–undertaking;<span class="e2"> karmaṇām</span>–of activities; <span class="e2">aśamaḥ</span>–unrest; <span class="e2">spṛhā</span>–and hankering. [12]
12 O Arjuna, most noble of the Bharat dynasty, know that when the mode of passion predominates in a person, greed, exertion, undertaking of activities, unrest, and hankering become manifest.
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च ।<br />तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥१३॥
aprakāśo ’pravṛttiś cha pramādo moha eva cha<br />tamasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe kuru-nandana [13]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kuru-nandana</span>–O descendant of Kuru;<span class="e2"> tamasi vivṛddhe</span>–by the force of the mode of ignorance; <span class="e2">etāni</span>–all these symptoms;<span class="e2"> jāyante</span>–are manifest:<span class="e2"> aprakāśaḥ</span>–dullness;<span class="e2"> apravṛttiḥ cha</span>–inactivity;<span class="e2"> pramādaḥ</span>–delusion;<span class="e2"> mohaḥ eva cha</span>–and bewilderment. [13]
13 O Kuru Nandan, by the influence of the mode of ignorance, all the symptoms of dullness, inactivity, delusion, and bewilderment become manifest.
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।<br />तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥१४॥
yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṁ yāti deha-bhṛt<br />tadottama-vidāṁ lokān amalān pratipadyate [14]
<span class="e2">yadā</span>–When;<span class="e2"> deha-bhṛt</span>–the embodied; <span class="e2">pravṛddhe </span>(<span class="e2">sati</span>)–having developed; <span class="e2">sattve</span>–goodness; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–reaches;<span class="e2"> pralayam</span>–death; <span class="e2">tadā tu</span>–then; <span class="e2">amalān</span>–the pure; <span class="e2">lokān</span>–planes;<span class="e2"> uttama-vidām</span>–of persons of higher knowledge (worshippers of Hiraṇyagarbha [Brahmā], etc.);<span class="e2"> pratipadyate</span>–are attained. [14]
14 If a person dies in a state of the mode of goodness, he goes to the pure planes where those who have higher knowledge reside.
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्म्मसङ्गिषु जायते ।<br />तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥१५॥
rajasi pralayaṁ gatvā karma-saṅgiṣu jāyate<br />tathā pralīnas tamasi mūḍha-yoniṣu jāyate [15]
(<span class="e2">jīvaḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> pralayam gatvā</span>–When a person dies; <span class="e2">rajasi </span>(<span class="e2">pravṛddhe</span>)–with a predominance of the mode of passion; <span class="e2">jāyate</span>–he is born;<span class="e2"> karma-saṅgiṣu</span>–as a human attached to action. <span class="e2">tathā</span>–Similarly; <span class="e2">pralīnaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–dying; <span class="e2">tamasi </span>(<span class="e2">vivṛddhe</span>)–when the mode of ignorance predominates; <span class="e2">jāyate</span>–one takes birth;<span class="e2"> mūḍha-yoniṣu</span>–in the lower species. [15]
15 When a person dies in the mode of passion, he takes birth as a human attached to worldly activity. If one dies in the mode of ignorance, he takes birth in the lower species.
कर्म्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्म्मलं फलम् ।<br />रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥१६॥
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṁ nirmalaṁ phalam<br />rajasas tu phalaṁ duḥkham ajñānaṁ tamasaḥ phalam [16]
(<span class="e2">paṇḍitāḥ</span>)–The learned; <span class="e2">āhuḥ</span>–proclaim; <span class="e2">phalam</span>–the fruit;<span class="e2"> sukṛtasya karmaṇaḥ</span>–of good works;<span class="e2"> nirmalam</span>–is pure;<span class="e2"> sāttvikam</span>–and of the nature of goodness;<span class="e2"> tu phalam</span>–and the fruit;<span class="e2"> rajasaḥ</span>–of passionate action;<span class="e2"> duḥkham</span>–is sorrow; <span class="e2">phalam </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and the fruit;<span class="e2"> tamasaḥ</span>–of ignorant action;<span class="e2"> ajñānam</span>–is ignorance. [16]
16 It is said by the learned that good actions result in purity, passionate actions result in sorrow, and ignorant actions lead to darkness.
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।<br />प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥१७॥
sattvāt sañjāyate jñānaṁ rajaso lobha eva cha<br />pramāda-mohau tamaso bhavato ’jñānam eva cha [17]
<span class="e2">sattvāt</span>–From goodness; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge; <span class="e2">cha eva</span>–and;<span class="e2"> rajasaḥ</span>–from passion; <span class="e2">lobhaḥ</span>–greed;<span class="e2"> sañjayate</span>–is born; <span class="e2">tamasaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and from ignorance;<span class="e2"> pramāda-mohau</span>–delusion and bewilderment;<span class="e2"> bhavataḥ</span>–arise;<span class="e2"> ajñānam eva cha</span>–and a lack of knowledge; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–ensues. [17]
17 From the mode of goodness, knowledge arises; from the mode of passion, greed; and from the mode of ignorance, delusion, bewilderment, and a lack of knowledge ensue.
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।<br />जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥१८॥
ūrdhvaṁ gachchhanti sattva-sthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ<br />jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthā adho gachchhanti tāmasāḥ [18]
<span class="e2">sattva-sthāḥ</span>–Persons situated in the mode of goodness;<span class="e2"> gachchhanti</span>–go;<span class="e2"> ūrdhvam</span>–up (to Satyaloka).<span class="e2"> rājasāḥ</span>–Those in the mode of passion;<span class="e2"> tiṣṭhanti</span>–remain; <span class="e2">madhye</span>–in the middle (as humans).<span class="e2"> tāmasāḥ</span>–Persons in the mode of ignorance;<span class="e2"> jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthāḥ</span>–tending to lower qualities;<span class="e2"> gachchhanti</span>–go; <span class="e2">adhaḥ</span>–down (suffer). [18]
18 Persons in goodness ascend (up to Satyaloka), those in passion remain in the middle (as humans), and the unfortunate, ignorant persons fall to the lower planes (of suffering).
नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्त्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति ।<br />गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥१९॥
nānyaṁ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṁ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati<br />guṇebhyaś cha paraṁ vetti mad-bhāvaṁ so ’dhigachchhati [19]
<span class="e2">yadā</span>–When; <span class="e2">draṣṭā</span>–the living being, the witness;<span class="e2"> anupaśyati</span>–sees;<span class="e2"> na anyam</span>–nothing else;<span class="e2"> guṇebhyaḥ</span>–but the three modes of nature;<span class="e2"> kartāram</span>–as the doer; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">vetti</span>–is able to know; <span class="e2">param</span>–the Lord, transcendental;<span class="e2"> guṇebhyaḥ</span>–to the modes; (<span class="e2">tadā</span>)–then; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he;<span class="e2"> adhigachchhati</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> mat-bhāvam</span>–My nature (My bhāva-bhakti). [19]
19 When a person sees the three modes to be the only impetus of this world, and knows the Supreme Lord, transcendental to the modes, then he comes to love Me with devotion.
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् ।<br />जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥२०॥
guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān<br />janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhair vimukto ’mṛtam aśnute [20]
<span class="e2">dehī</span>–The embodied living being; <span class="e2">atītya</span>–transcending;<span class="e2"> etān trīn guṇān</span>–these three modes of nature;<span class="e2"> deha-samudbhavān</span>–that appear in the body; <span class="e2">vimuktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being liberated;<span class="e2"> janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhaiḥ</span>–from the miseries of birth, death, and old age; <span class="e2">aśnute</span>–knows the joy of; <span class="e2">amṛtam</span>–immortality, love transcendental (nirguṇa prema). [20]
20 Transcending these modes manifest in the body, he is liberated from the miseries of birth, death, and old age, and knows the joy of immortality.
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो ।<br />किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्त्तते ॥२१॥
arjuna uvācha
kair liṅgais trīn guṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho<br />kim āchāraḥ kathaṁ chaitāṁs trīn guṇān ativartate [21]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">prabho</span>–O Lord;<span class="e2"> kaiḥ liṅgaiḥ</span>–by what symptoms; <span class="e2">bhavati </span>(<span class="e2">jñeyaḥ</span>)–can be known; <span class="e2">atītaḥ</span>–a person who has transcended; <span class="e2">etān</span>–these; <span class="e2">trīn</span>–three; <span class="e2">guṇān</span>–modes?<span class="e2"> kim āchāraḥ</span>–How does he behave?<span class="e2"> katham cha</span>–and how;<span class="e2"> ativartate</span>–does he transcend; <span class="e2">etān</span>–these;<span class="e2"> trīn guṇān</span>–three modes? [21]
21 Arjuna said: O Lord, what are the symptoms of a person transcendental to these three modes of material nature? How does he behave, and how does he transcend the modes?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
प्रकाशञ्च प्रवृत्तिञ्च मोहमेव च पाण्डव ।<br />न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥२२॥
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते ।<br />गुणा वर्त्तन्त इत्येवं योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥२३॥
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्ट्राश्मकाञ्चनः ।<br />तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥२४॥
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः ।<br />सर्व्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥२५॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
prakāśañ cha pravṛttiñ cha moham eva cha pāṇḍava<br />na dveṣṭi sampravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati [22]
udāsīnavad āsīno guṇair yo na vichālyate<br />guṇā vartanta ity evaṁ yo ’vatiṣṭhati neṅgate [23]
sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ svasthaḥ sama-loṣṭrāśma-kāñchanaḥ<br />tulya-priyāpriyo dhīras tulya-nindātma-saṁstutiḥ [24]
mānāpamānayos tulyas tulyo mitrāri-pakṣayoḥ<br />sarvārambha-parityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa uchyate [25]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord replied: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pāṇḍava</span>–O son of Pāṇḍu; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who;<span class="e2"> na dveṣṭi</span>–neither resents;<span class="e2"> prakāśaṁ cha</span>–illumination (the effect of goodness);<span class="e2"> pravṛttim cha</span>–activation (the effect of passion);<span class="e2"> moham eva cha</span>–and delusion (the effect of ignorance);<span class="e2"> sampravṛttāni</span>–when they appear;<span class="e2"> na kāṅkṣati</span>–nor hankers for them;<span class="e2"> nivṛttāni</span>–when they disappear; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who; <span class="e2">āsīnaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–remaining;<span class="e2"> udāsīnavat</span>–as unconcerned;<span class="e2"> na vichālyate</span>–is not perturbed; <span class="e2">gunaiḥ</span>–by the modes;<span class="e2"> avatiṣṭhati</span>–remains poised;<span class="e2"> na iṅgate</span>–without wavering; <span class="e2">iti evam </span>(<span class="e2">jñātvā</span>)–knowing that; <span class="e2">guṇāḥ</span>–the modes;<span class="e2"> vartate</span>–are engaged in their functions; (<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>)–one who;<span class="e2"> sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ</span>–is equipoised in happiness and unhappiness;<span class="e2"> svasthaḥ</span>–is situated within the self;<span class="e2"> sama-loṣṭra-aśma-kāñchanaḥ</span>–with the vision of equality towards earth, stone, or gold;<span class="e2"> tulya-priya-apriyaḥ</span>–equipoised in desirable and undesirable circumstances; <span class="e2">dhīraḥ</span>–wise;<span class="e2"> tulya-nindā-ātma-saṁstutiḥ</span>–balanced with regard to abuse and praise;<span class="e2"> tulyaḥ māna-apamānayoḥ</span>–balanced in honour and dishonour; <span class="e2">tulyaḥ</span>–balanced;<span class="e2"> mitra-ari-pakṣayoḥ</span>–toward friend and foe;<span class="e2"> sarva-ārambha-parityāgī</span>–and is a renouncer of all mundane endeavours; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that person;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is described;<span class="e2"> guṇa-atītaḥ</span>–as transcendental to the modes of material nature. [22–25]
22–25 The Supreme Lord replied: O Pāṇḍava, it is said that a person who has transcended the three modes of material nature neither resents illumination, activation, and delusion when they appear, nor does he hanker for them when they withdraw. Poised in the knowledge that the modes are engaging, he is not distracted by them; he remains unperturbed, unconcerned. Remaining self-satisfied, he sees joy and sorrow equally; he sees earth, rock, or gold with the vision of equality; he is wise, equipoised in desirable and undesirable circumstances, abuse and praise, honour and dishonour; he behaves fairly with friend and foe alike, and he renounces all mundane endeavours.
माञ्च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते ।<br />स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥२६॥
māñ cha yo ’vyabhichāreṇa bhakti-yogena sevate<br />sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahma-bhūyāya kalpate [26]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who;<span class="e2"> bhakti-yogena</span>–by the yoga of devotion;<span class="e2"> avyabhichāreṇa</span>–without deviation; <span class="e2">sevate</span>–renders service; <span class="e2">mām cha</span>–unto Me (the Supreme Lord Śyāmasundar); <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that person;<span class="e2"> samatītya</span>–transcending; <span class="e2">etān</span>–these; <span class="e2">guṇān</span>–modes;<span class="e2"> kalpate</span>–becomes qualified;<span class="e2"> brahma-bhūyāya</span>–to know his internal divine identity (chit-svarūp-siddhi). [26]
26 A person who, without deviation, serves Me with devotion, transcends the three modes of material nature and becomes qualified to know his internal divine identity.
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च ।<br />शाश्वतस्य च धर्म्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥२७॥
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham amṛtasyāvyayasya cha<br />śāśvatasya cha dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya cha [27]
<span class="e2">hi</span>–For;<span class="e2"> aham pratiṣṭhā</span>–I am the basis;<span class="e2"> brahmaṇaḥ</span>–of the Absolute Truth;<span class="e2"> avyayasya cha</span>–and of the inexhaustible;<span class="e2"> amṛtasya</span>–nectar;<span class="e2"> śāśvatasya cha</span>–and of the eternal;<span class="e2"> dharmasya</span>–divine Pastimes;<span class="e2"> aikāntikasya sukhasya cha</span>–and of the ultimate ecstasy of divine love. [27]
27 I am the basis of the Absolute Truth, the inexhaustible nectar, the eternal Pastimes, and the ultimate ecstasy of divine love.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे गुणत्रयविभागयोगो नाम चतुर्द्दशोऽध्यायः ॥१४॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde guṇatraya<br />vibhāga-yogo nāma chaturdaśo ’dhyāyaḥ [14]
End of Chapter Fourteen<br />The Three Divisions of Material Nature<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

पञ्चदशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Fifteen
Puruṣottama-yoga <br />The Supreme Person
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् ।<br />छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥१॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
ūrdhva-mūlam adhaḥ-śākham aśvatthaṁ prāhur avyayam<br />chhandāṁsi yasya parṇāni yas taṁ veda sa veda-vit [1]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: <span class="e2">prāhuḥ</span>–It is said in the scriptures (when describing this material world):<span class="e2"> ūrdhva-mūlam</span>–“The roots are uppermost as it is rooted in aversion to the highest principle, the Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> adhaḥ-śākham</span>–the branches face downwards, representing all beings from Lord Brahmā down to the lowest species;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–and it is endless (for those who desire the independence to enjoy the fruits of their actions);<span class="e2"> aśvattham</span>–yet transient; (for a person with devotion to the Lord) it will be ‘gone tomorrow’.<span class="e2"> chhandāṁsi</span>–The ritualistic verses of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> parṇāni</span>–are represented by the protective leaves; <span class="e2">yasya</span>–of the Aśvattha or Peepul tree of this material world.” <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who; <span class="e2">veda</span>–knows; <span class="e2">tam</span>–that tree; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–he;<span class="e2"> veda-vit</span>–is a knower of the Vedas. [1]
1 The Supreme Lord said: It is said in the scriptures that this material world is like a Peepul tree, roots up, branches down, endless, yet transient. Its leaves represent the nourishing verses of the Vedas. One who knows this tree is a knower of the Vedas.
Commentary
The roots of the tree of this world are said to face upwards—its root cause is the highest plane. It is manifest by the potency of the Supreme Lord. However, it is rooted in aversion to the Lord. Its branches are said to face downwards since according to the law of karma all species of life from the highest to the lowest branch out from it. It is known as an Aśvattha tree. The word aśvattha means ‘ephemeral,’ or ‘that which does not remain in the same state for even a day.’ Yet, it is endless* in the sense that it constantly appears in the natural flow of cause and effect. The leaves of the tree represent the fruitive verses of the Vedas (karma-kāṇḍa). As the leaves of a tree nourish and beautify it, these verses similarly encourage and illuminate the world.
The external potency of the Lord, māyā, is eternal, and it manifests this world. Yet the world itself is perishable inasmuch as it again becomes unmanifest. Although the fruitive verses of the Vedas provide its nourishment, their underlying purpose is rather to enlighten the conditioned souls to take shelter of the Supreme Lord who is transcendental to the mundane. Thus, one who knows these fundamental principles is a knower of the true essence of the Vedas.
*The Peepul tree is known for its longevity.
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा<br />गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः ।<br />अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि<br />कर्म्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥२॥
adhaś chordhvaṁ prasṛtās tasya śākhā<br />guṇa-pravṛddhā viṣaya-pravālāḥ<br />adhaś cha mūlāny anusantatāni<br />karmānubandhīni manuṣya-loke [2]
<span class="e2">tasya śākhāḥ</span>–Its branches, representing the living beings;<span class="e2"> viṣaya-pravālāḥ</span>–with shoots, representing the objects of the senses;<span class="e2"> guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ</span>–nourished by the three modes of nature;<span class="e2"> adhaḥ prasṛtāḥ</span>–extend downwards as the planes of human, animal, and lower species;<span class="e2"> ūrdhvam cha</span>–and upwards, as the planes of higher celestial beings.<span class="e2"> karma-anubandhīni</span>–According to religious and irreligious actions; <span class="e2">mūlāni</span>–some roots, as aerial roots;<span class="e2"> anusantatāni</span>–as a secondary causal factor, as the search to enjoy the fruits of actions, have extended;<span class="e2"> adhaḥ cha</span>–downwards also;<span class="e2"> manuṣya-loke</span>–in the human plane. [2]
2 Some of its branches extend upwards (as the planes of the demigods and celestial beings), some of the branches extend downwards (as the planes of the humans, animals, and lower species), and nourished by three modes of nature, its shoots are the objects of the senses. Some aerial roots also extend downwards, to take root in the land of karma, within the human plane.
Commentary
Within the expansive manifestation of this ‘perishable yet endless’ world, some of the living beings are nourished by the mode of goodness, and they wander throughout the upper planes, in the ego of gods and celestial beings. Others, influenced by the modes of passion and ignorance, are wandering throughout the planes of the humans, animals, trees, and lower species, assuming the identities of those species. The shoots of the tree of this world represent the objects of the senses—sound, smell, touch, taste, and form, as transformations of the five primary subtle elements (pañcha-tanmātra) produced from the ego of the living beings.
The principal roots face upwards, inverted, indicating aversion to the Supreme Lord. Further, some aerial roots face downward, entering the land of karma in the human plane. These represent the humans’ attempt to enjoy the fruits of their actions, and these aerial roots nourish the tree as a separate, secondary cause.
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते<br />नान्तो न चादिर्न च सम्प्रतिष्ठा ।<br />अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूलम्<br />असङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥३॥
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं<br />यस्मिन्गता न निवर्त्तन्ति भूयः ।<br />तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये<br />यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥४॥
na rūpam asyeha tathopalabhyate<br />nānto na chādir na cha sampratiṣṭhā<br />aśvattham enaṁ suvirūḍha-mūlam<br />asaṅga-śastreṇa dṛḍhena chhittvā [3]
tataḥ padaṁ tat parimārgitavyaṁ<br />yasmin gatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ<br />tam eva chādyaṁ puruṣaṁ prapadye<br />yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī [4]
<span class="e2">iha</span>–Within this world;<span class="e2"> tathā rūpam</span>–that inverted form; <span class="e2">asya</span>–of the Aśvattha tree representing this world;<span class="e2"> na upalabhyate</span>–cannot be realised (through any method except Vedic knowledge); (<span class="e2">asya</span>)<span class="e2"> antaḥ na</span>–nor its end;<span class="e2"> ādiḥ cha na</span>–nor its origin;<span class="e2"> sampratiṣṭhā cha na</span>–nor its continuance.<span class="e2"> chhittvā</span>–Cutting down;<span class="e2"> enam suvirūḍha-mūlam</span>–this stubbornly rooted (in aversion to the Supreme Lord);<span class="e2"> aśvattham</span>–perishable tree of the material world;<span class="e2"> dṛḍhena</span>–with the sharp;<span class="e2"> asaṅga-śastreṇa</span>–axe of detachment acquired from sādhu-saṅga, association of saints; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–and thereafter; <span class="e2">yasmin gatāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–having reached that plane from which; (<span class="e2">kechid api</span>)–one;<span class="e2"> na nivartanti</span>–does not return; <span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–again;<span class="e2"> parimārgitavyam</span>–one should approach for shelter;<span class="e2"> tat padam</span>–the holy feet of Lord Viṣṇu; (<span class="e2">ekānta bhaktyā</span>)–with exclusive devotion; (<span class="e2">iti evam</span>)–in this way:<span class="e2"> prapadye</span>–“I surrender unto;<span class="e2"> tam eva cha</span>–Him alone; <span class="e2">ādyam</span>–the original;<span class="e2"> puruṣam</span>–Supreme Person; <span class="e2">yataḥ</span>–from whose illusory energy; (<span class="e2">eṣā</span>)–this; <span class="e2">purāṇī</span>–perpetual;<span class="e2"> pravṛttiḥ</span>–manifestation;<span class="e2"> prasṛtā</span>–has appeared.” [3–4]
3–4 In the human plane, this inverted form of the Peepul tree of this material world is inconceivable (without Vedic knowledge)—neither its beginning, nor its middle, nor its end can be perceived. From the association of devotees, one acquires the sharp axe of detachment from the mundane. Using this weapon to cut down that illusory tree of one’s mundane existence which is stubbornly rooted in aversion to the Supreme Lord, one attains to the plane of no return, which is the lotus feet of the Lord. With pure devotion, one should approach the holy lotus feet of the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu for shelter, and pray, “I surrender unto the Original Person, the Supreme Lord of all, by whose illusory potency (māyā) this perpetual tree of the material world has appeared.”
निर्म्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा<br />अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः ।<br />द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञैर्<br />गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥५॥
nirmāna-mohā jita-saṅga-doṣā<br />adhyātma-nityā vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ<br />dvandvair vimuktāḥ sukha-duḥkha-saṁjñair<br />gachchhanty amūḍhāḥ padam avyayaṁ tat [5]
<span class="e2">nirmāna-mohāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–Having become free from pride and delusion;<span class="e2"> jita-saṅga-doṣāḥ</span>–free from the defect of unholy association;<span class="e2"> adhyātma-nityāḥ</span>–dedicated to self-realisation;<span class="e2"> vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ</span>–completely free from desire;<span class="e2"> vimuktāḥ</span>–completely liberated;<span class="e2"> dvandvaiḥ</span>–from the dualities;<span class="e2"> sukha-duḥkha-saṁjñaiḥ</span>–known as joy and sorrow;<span class="e2"> amūḍhāḥ</span>–thus undeluded; (<span class="e2">te</span>)–those surrendered souls;<span class="e2"> gachchhanti</span>–reach; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">padam</span>–goal. [5]
5 Free from vanity and delusion, aloof to unholy association, dedicated to self-realisation, desireless, liberated from the duality of joy and sorrow, undeluded, those surrendered souls reach the eternal goal.
न तद्भासयते सूर्य्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।<br />यद्गत्वा न निवर्त्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥६॥
na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ<br />yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama [6]
<span class="e2">tat mama</span>–That is My;<span class="e2"> paramam</span>–all-illuminating; <span class="e2">dhāma</span>–holy abode; <span class="e2">gatvā</span>–having reached; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; (<span class="e2">prapannāḥ</span>)–the surrendered souls; <span class="e2">na nivartante </span>(<span class="e2">tataḥ</span>)–never return from there. <span class="e2">sūryaḥ</span>–The sun;<span class="e2"> na bhāsayate</span>–cannot illuminate; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> na śaśāṅkaḥ</span>–nor the moon;<span class="e2"> na pāvakaḥ</span>–nor fire. [6]
6 The surrendered souls reach My eternal abode, never to return to this world. Neither sun, nor moon, nor fire—nothing can illuminate that all-illuminating supreme abode.
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।<br />मनः षष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥७॥
mamaivāṁśo jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ<br />manaḥ ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛti-sthāni karṣati [7]
<span class="e2">eva</span>–Certainly;<span class="e2"> jīva-bhūtaḥ</span>–the spirit soul living being is; <span class="e2">mama</span>–My;<span class="e2"> sanātanaḥ</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">aṁśaḥ</span>–particle, potency.<span class="e2"> jīva-loke</span>–In this world;<span class="e2"> karṣati</span>–it attracts, adopts;<span class="e2"> prakṛti-sthāni</span>–the mundane;<span class="e2"> manaḥ ṣaṣṭhāni indriyāṇi</span>–six perceptual senses including the mind. [7]
7 The soul is a particle (potency) of Mine. Although it is eternal, for worldly existence it adopts the five mundane senses and the mind, which is the sixth.
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः ।<br />गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥८॥
śarīraṁ yad avāpnoti yach chāpy utkrāmatīśvaraḥ<br />gṛhītvaitāni saṁyāti vāyur gandhān ivāśayāt [8]
<span class="e2">yat sarīram</span>–Regarding any body which;<span class="e2"> īśvaraḥ</span>–the soul, as master of the body;<span class="e2"> avāpnoti</span>–obtains;<span class="e2"> yat cha api</span>–and from which;<span class="e2"> utkrāmati</span>–it departs; (<span class="e2">tadā</span>)–then;<span class="e2"> gṛhītvā</span>–taking; <span class="e2">etāni</span>–these six senses;<span class="e2"> vāyuḥ iva</span>–as the wind;<span class="e2"> gandhān</span>–carries fragrance; <span class="e2">āśayāt</span>–from its source, such as a flower; (<span class="e2">śarīrāntaram</span>)<span class="e2"> saṁyāti</span>–it goes to enter another body. [8]
8 The soul is the master of the body. When it departs the body, it goes to enter another, carrying these (subtle) senses, as the wind carries fragrance from its source.
श्रोत्रञ्चक्षुः स्पर्शनञ्च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।<br />अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥९॥
śrotrañ chakṣuḥ sparśanañ cha rasanaṁ ghrāṇam eva cha<br />adhiṣṭhāya manaś chāyaṁ viṣayān upasevate [9]
<span class="e2">adhiṣṭhāya</span>–Presiding over;<span class="e2"> śrotram</span>–the ear;<span class="e2"> chakṣuḥ</span>–eye;<span class="e2"> sparśanam</span>–skin;<span class="e2"> rasanam cha</span>–tongue;<span class="e2"> ghrāṇam eva cha</span>–and nose;<span class="e2"> manaḥ cha</span>–and also the mind; <span class="e2">ayam</span>–this soul;<span class="e2"> upasevate</span>–enjoys;<span class="e2"> viṣayān</span>–the objects of the senses—sound, etc. [9]
9 Presiding over the ear, eye, skin, tongue, and nose, and also the mind, the living entity enjoys the sense objects of sound, form, touch, taste, and smell.
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।<br />विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥१०॥
utkrāmantaṁ sthitaṁ vāpi bhuñjānaṁ vā guṇānvitam<br />vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñāna-chakṣuṣaḥ [10]
<span class="e2">vimūḍhāḥ</span>–Those thus deluded;<span class="e2"> na anupaśyanti</span>–cannot see; (<span class="e2">jīvam</span>)–the soul;<span class="e2"> utkrāmantam</span>–when departing the body;<span class="e2"> sthitam vā api</span>–or residing in the body;<span class="e2"> bhuñjānam vā</span>–or enjoying;<span class="e2"> guṇa-anvitam</span>–in association with the senses and their objects.<span class="e2"> jñāna-chakṣuṣaḥ</span>–Persons with the eyes of wisdom;<span class="e2"> paśyanti</span>–see. [10]
10 Those who are thus deluded cannot see the soul when it is departing the body, residing in the body, or when enjoying through the senses in the body. Those with the eyes of wisdom can see.
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् ।<br />यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥११॥
yatanto yoginaś chainaṁ paśyanty ātmany avasthitam<br />yatanto ’py akṛtātmāno nainaṁ paśyanty achetasaḥ [11]
