<span class="e2">cha</span>–And;<span class="e2"> yatantaḥ</span>–the perseverant, sincere;<span class="e2"> yoginaḥ</span>–yogīs—seekers;<span class="e2"> paśyanti</span>–see; <span class="e2">enam</span>–this soul;<span class="e2"> avasthitam</span>–situated; <span class="e2">ātmani</span>–within.<span class="e2"> yatantaḥ api</span>–But despite endeavouring;<span class="e2"> achetasaḥ</span>–those of poor understanding;<span class="e2"> akṛta-ātmānaḥ</span>–lacking self-control;<span class="e2"> na paśyanti</span>–cannot see; <span class="e2">enam</span>–this soul. [11]
11 And the sincere seekers see the soul present within. But persons of poor understanding and lacking in self-control cannot see the soul, despite their endeavours.
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् ।<br />यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥१२॥
yad āditya-gataṁ tejo jagad bhāsayate ’khilam<br />yach chandramasi yach chāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam [12]
<span class="e2">yat tejaḥ</span>–That effulgence which;<span class="e2"> āditya-gatam</span>–emanates from the sun;<span class="e2"> bhāsayate</span>–and illuminates;<span class="e2"> akhilam jagat</span>–the entire universe;<span class="e2"> yat chandramasi cha</span>–and which is in the moon; <span class="e2">yat agnau </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and which is in fire; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know;<span class="e2"> tat tejaḥ</span>–that effulgence;<span class="e2"> māmakam</span>–as Mine. [12]
12 The light of the sun that illuminates the entire universe, the light of the moon, and the radiance of fire—know that to be Mine.
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा ।<br />पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्व्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥१३॥
gām āviśya cha bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā<br />puṣṇāmi chauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ [13]
<span class="e2">āviśya cha</span>–Entering; <span class="e2">gām</span>–the earth; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> dhārayāmi</span>–maintain;<span class="e2"> bhūtāni</span>–the living beings; <span class="e2">ojasā</span>–by My potency.<span class="e2"> bhūtvā cha</span>–And becoming;<span class="e2"> rasa-ātmakaḥ</span>–the essential; <span class="e2">somaḥ</span>–moon; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> puṣṇāmi</span>–I nourish; <span class="e2">sarvāḥ</span>–all;<span class="e2"> auṣadhīḥ</span>–crops. [13]
13 Entering the earth, I maintain all beings by My potency; and in the form of the life-giving moon, I nourish the crops.
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः ।<br />प्राणापानसमायुक्तःपचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥१४॥
ahaṁ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṁ deham āśritaḥ<br />prāṇāpāna-samāyuktaḥ pachāmy annaṁ chatur-vidham [14]
<span class="e2">bhūtvā</span>–Becoming;<span class="e2"> vaiśvānaraḥ</span>–the power of digestion; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> āśritaḥ</span>–entering into;<span class="e2"> prāṇinām deham</span>–the bodies of the living beings;<span class="e2"> pachāmi</span>–digest;<span class="e2"> chatuḥ-vidham annam</span>–the four types of foodstuffs;<span class="e2"> prāṇa-apāna-samāyuktaḥ</span>–through the agency of the ascending and descending vital airs. [14]
14 Entering into the bodies of the living beings as the power of digestion, I digest the four types of eatables (chewed, sucked, licked, and drunk), through the agency of the ascending and descending vital airs.
सर्व्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्ठो<br />मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनञ्च ।<br />वेदैश्च सर्व्वैरहमेव वेद्यो<br />वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥१५॥
sarvasya chāhaṁ hṛdi sanniviṣṭho<br />mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanañ cha<br />vedaiś cha sarvair aham eva vedyo<br />vedānta-kṛd veda-vid eva chāham [15]
<span class="e2">aham cha sanniviṣṭaḥ</span>–I am situated as the indwelling monitor, the Supersoul; <span class="e2">hṛdi</span>–within the heart;<span class="e2"> sarvasya</span>–of all beings. (<span class="e2">jīvasya</span>)–The living being’s; <span class="e2">smṛtiḥ</span>–remembrance; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge;<span class="e2"> apohanam cha</span>–and the disappearance of both; <span class="e2">mattaḥ</span>–arise from Me;<span class="e2"> aham eva cha vedyaḥ</span>–and I alone am the object to be known;<span class="e2"> sarvaiḥ vedaiḥ</span>–by means of all the Vedas.<span class="e2"> aham eva vedānta-kṛt</span>–In the form of Vedavyās, I am the revealer of the Vedānta;<span class="e2"> veda-vit cha</span>–and the knower of the meaning of the Vedas. [15]
15 I am situated (as the Supersoul) within the heart of all souls, and from Me arises the soul’s remembrance, knowledge, and forgetfulness (according to his actions). I alone am the Sweet Absolute to be known through all the Vedas. I am the revealer of the Vedānta—Vedavyās, and I am the knower of the Vedas.
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च ।<br />क्षरः सर्व्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥१६॥
dvāv imau puruṣau loke kṣaraś chākṣara eva cha<br />kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho ’kṣara uchyate [16]
<span class="e2">loke</span>–In the fourteen worlds;<span class="e2"> imau dvau eva</span>–only these two types of;<span class="e2"> puruṣau</span>–conscious entities; (<span class="e2">sthaḥ</span>)–exist:<span class="e2"> kṣaraḥ cha</span>–the perishable;<span class="e2"> akṣaraḥ cha</span>–and the imperishable. (<span class="e2">tayoḥ</span>)–Of the two;<span class="e2"> sarvāṇi bhūtāni</span>–all beings, from Lord Brahmā down to the lowest stationary beings;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–are described; <span class="e2">kṣaraḥ</span>–as perishable, as they are fallen from their true nature;<span class="e2"> kūṭa-sthaḥ</span>–and the associates of the Lord, situated in their eternally perfect nature; (<span class="e2">uchyate</span>)–are described;<span class="e2"> akṣaraḥ</span>–as imperishable; (<span class="e2">vidvadbhiḥ</span>)–by the knowledgeable. [16]
16 In this world, there are two types of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All beings from Lord Brahmā down to the lowest stationary life-forms are known as perishable (as they are fallen from their true nature). But those who are situated in their eternal, spiritual nature are known as imperishable (eternal associates of the Lord).
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः ।<br />यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥१७॥
uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ<br />yo loka-trayam āviśya bibharty avyaya īśvaraḥ [17]
<span class="e2">anyaḥ tu</span>–But otherwise;<span class="e2"> uttamaḥ</span>–the Supreme;<span class="e2"> puruṣaḥ</span>–Person;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtaḥ</span>–is described; <span class="e2">iti</span>–as;<span class="e2"> paramātmā</span>–the Supersoul, Akṣara-puruṣ, or the Supreme Imperishable Personality;<span class="e2"> īśvaraḥ</span>–the Lord: <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–who; <span class="e2">āviśya</span>–entering;<span class="e2"> loka-trayam</span>–the three worlds;<span class="e2"> avyayaḥ</span>–in His eternal form;<span class="e2"> bibharti</span>–is maintaining all beings. [17]
17 But completely distinct from both these types of beings is the Supreme Person, who is known as Paramātmā, the Supersoul. He is the Supreme Lord. Entering the three worlds in His eternal form, He maintains all beings in the universe.
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः ।<br />अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥१८॥
yasmāt kṣaram atīto ’ham akṣarād api chottamaḥ<br />ato ’smi loke vede cha prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ [18]
<span class="e2">yasmāt</span>–Because;<span class="e2"> aham atītaḥ</span>–I am transcendental to; <span class="e2">kṣaram</span>–the perishable beings; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; (<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> uttamaḥ</span>–I am superior;<span class="e2"> akṣarāt api</span>–to the liberated souls, too; <span class="e2">ataḥ</span>–therefore;<span class="e2"> prathitaḥ asmi</span>–I am glorified; <span class="e2">loke</span>–in the world;<span class="e2"> vede cha</span>–and in the Vedas;<span class="e2"> puruṣottamaḥ</span>–as Puruṣottam, the Supreme Person. [18]
18 Because I am transcendental to the perishable beings and also superior to My imperishable eternal associates, My glories are sung in the world and in the scriptures as Puruṣottam, the Supreme Person.
यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् ।<br />स सर्व्वविद्भजति मां सर्व्वभावेन भारत ॥१९॥
yo mām evam asammūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam<br />sa sarva-vid bhajati māṁ sarva-bhāvena bhārata [19]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O descendant of Bharat; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–one who; <span class="e2">asammūdhaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being free from delusion; <span class="e2">jānāti</span>–knows; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> evam puruṣottamam</span>–as the Supreme Person;<span class="e2"> saḥ sarva-vit</span>–that knower of complete essential truth;<span class="e2"> bhajati</span>–worships; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhāvena</span>–in all ways (in all spiritual relationships). [19]
19 O Bhārat, one who is free from delusion and knows Me as the Supreme Person of eternal, all-conscious, ecstatic form, is the perfect knower of full-fledged theism, and he worships Me in all ways (in the spiritual relationships of tranquillity, servitorship, friendship, parenthood, and consorthood).
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ ।<br />एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥२०॥
iti guhyatamaṁ śāstram idam uktaṁ mayānagha<br />etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛta-kṛtyaś cha bhārata [20]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">anagha</span>–O sinless one; <span class="e2">iti</span>–in this way; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> guhyatamam</span>–most hidden;<span class="e2"> śāstram</span>–purport of all the scriptures; <span class="e2">uktam</span>–has been described; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Bharat;<span class="e2"> etat buddhvā</span>–taking this to heart;<span class="e2"> buddhimān</span>–the intelligent persons of fine theistic temperament;<span class="e2"> kṛta-kṛtyaḥ cha syāt</span>–attain their goal. [20]
20 O pure hearted Arjuna, I have thus explained to you this most hidden treasure of all the scriptures. O Bhārat, embracing this in their hearts, the persons of fine theistic intelligence attain the perfection of their endeavours.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे पुरुषोत्तमयोगो नाम पञ्चदशोऽध्यायः ॥१५॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde puruṣottama-<br />yogo nāma pañchadaśo ’dhyāyaḥ [15]
End of Chapter Fifteen<br />The Supreme Person<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

षोडशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Sixteen
Daivāsura-sampad-vibhāga-yoga <br />The Godly and Ungodly Natures
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः ।<br />दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्ज्जवम् ॥१॥
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् ।<br />दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्द्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥२॥
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता ।<br />भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥३॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
abhayaṁ sattva-saṁśuddhir jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ<br />dānaṁ damaś cha yajñaś cha svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam [1]
ahiṁsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śāntir apaiśunam<br />dayā bhūteṣv aloluptvaṁ mārdavaṁ hrīr achāpalam [2]
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucham adroho nātimānitā<br />bhavanti sampadaṁ daivīm abhijātasya bhārata [3]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Arjuna; (<span class="e2">ete guṇāḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> bhavanti</span>–these are the qualities;<span class="e2"> abhijātasya</span>–of a person born to a destiny;<span class="e2"> daivīm sampadam</span>–blessed with godliness:<span class="e2"> abhayam</span>–fearlessness;<span class="e2"> sattva-saṁśuddhiḥ</span>–gracious-heartedness;<span class="e2"> jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ</span>–absorption in the yoga of knowledge (13.8–12); <span class="e2">dānam</span>–generosity;<span class="e2"> damaḥ cha</span>–sense-control;<span class="e2"> yajñaḥ cha</span>–sacrifice;<span class="e2"> svādhyāyaḥ</span>–study of the Vedas; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity;<span class="e2"> ārjavam</span>–straightforwardness; <span class="e2">ahiṁsā</span>–nonviolence; <span class="e2">satyam</span>–truthfulness;<span class="e2"> akrodhaḥ</span>–freedom from anger; <span class="e2">tyāgaḥ</span>–worldly detachment; <span class="e2">śantiḥ</span>–mental control, tranquillity;<span class="e2"> apaiśunam</span>–freedom from finding fault in others; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–compassion;<span class="e2"> bhūteṣu</span>–for all beings;<span class="e2"> aloluptvam</span>–absence of greed;<span class="e2"> mārdavam</span>–gentleness; <span class="e2">hrīḥ</span>–modesty;<span class="e2"> achāpalam</span>–steadfastness; <span class="e2">tejaḥ</span>–vigour; <span class="e2">kṣamā</span>–forgiveness; <span class="e2">dhṛtiḥ</span>–patience;<span class="e2"> śaucham</span>–external and internal purity;<span class="e2"> adrohaḥ</span>–freedom from malice;<span class="e2"> na ati-mānitā</span>–and freedom from conceit. [1–3]
1–3 The Supreme Lord said: O Bhārat, these are the qualities of a person born of a godly nature: fearlessness, gracious-heartedness, absorption in self-knowledge, generosity, sense-control, sacrifice, study of the Vedas, austerity, sincerity, nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, worldly detachment, tranquillity, disinclination to see the faults of others, compassion, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, steadfastness, vigour, forgiveness, patience, purity, and freedom from malice and egoism.
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च ।<br />अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥४॥
dambho darpo ’bhimānaś cha krodhaḥ pāruṣyam eva cha<br />ajñānaṁ chābhijātasya pārtha sampadam āsurīm [4]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī; (<span class="e2">ete guṇāḥ bhavanti</span>)–these are the (impure) characteristics;<span class="e2"> abhijātasya</span>–of a person born to a destiny;<span class="e2"> āsurīm sampadam</span>–of the ungodly nature:<span class="e2"> dambhaḥ</span>–pride (of religiosity, etc.); <span class="e2">darpaḥ</span>–conceit (on account of one’s knowledge, wealth, or high birth);<span class="e2"> abhimānaḥ cha</span>–considering oneself worshippable;<span class="e2"> krodhaḥ</span>–anger;<span class="e2"> pāruṣyam eva cha</span>–mercilessness;<span class="e2"> ajñānam cha</span>–and ignorance. [4]
4 O Pārtha, these are the qualities of a person born of an ungodly nature: pride, conceit, egoism, anger, cruelty, and ignorance.
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता ।<br />मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥५॥
daivī sampad vimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā<br />mā śuchaḥ sampadaṁ daivīm abhijāto ’si pāṇḍava [5]
<span class="e2">daivī sampat</span>–The godly qualities; <span class="e2">matā</span>–are described;<span class="e2"> vimokṣāya</span>–as the cause of liberation; <span class="e2">āsurī </span>(<span class="e2">cha</span>)–and the demoniac qualities;<span class="e2"> nibandhāya</span>–as the cause of bondage. (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pāṇḍava</span>–O son of Pāṇḍu; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you;<span class="e2"> abhijātaḥ asi</span>–are born to a destiny;<span class="e2"> daivīm sampadam</span>–of the godly and virtuous qualities;<span class="e2"> mā śuchaḥ</span>–so do not fear. [5]
5 The godly qualities have been described as the cause of liberation, and the ungodly qualities have been described as the cause of bondage. O Pāṇḍava, do not fear, for you are born of a godly nature.
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च ।<br />दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु ॥६॥
dvau bhūta-sargau loke ’smin daiva āsura eva cha<br />daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṁ pārtha me śṛṇu [6]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> dvau eva bhūta-sargau</span>–these two natures of beings; (<span class="e2">dṛśyate</span>)–are seen;<span class="e2"> asmin loke</span>–in this material world: <span class="e2">daivaḥ</span>–the godly nature; <span class="e2">āsuraḥ cha</span>—and the ungodly. <span class="e2">daivaḥ</span>–The godly nature;<span class="e2"> proktaḥ</span>–has been described;<span class="e2"> vistaraśaḥ</span>–elaborately. <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–Now hear; <span class="e2">me</span>–from Me; <span class="e2">āsuram</span>–of the ungodly nature. [6]
6 O Pārtha, in this world the living beings are of two natures—the godly and the ungodly. I have elaborately described the godly nature to you, so now hear from Me about the ungodly:
प्रवृत्तिञ्च निवृत्तिञ्च जना न विदुरासुराः ।<br />न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥७॥
pravṛttiñ cha nivṛttiñ cha janā na vidur āsurāḥ<br />na śauchaṁ nāpi chāchāro na satyaṁ teṣu vidyate [7]
<span class="e2">āsurāḥ janāḥ</span>–Persons of demoniac nature;<span class="e2"> na viduḥ</span>–do not know;<span class="e2"> pravṛttim cha</span>–right action;<span class="e2"> nivṛttim cha</span>–and wrong action.<span class="e2"> na vidyate</span>–There is neither;<span class="e2"> śaucham</span>–purity; <span class="e2">na</span>–nor;<span class="e2"> āchāraḥ api</span>–good practices;<span class="e2"> na satyam cha</span>–nor truthfulness; <span class="e2">teṣu</span>–in them. [7]
7 The ungodly cannot distinguish between right and wrong action. No purity, good practices, or truthfulness can be found in them.
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् ।<br />अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहेतुकम् ॥८॥
asatyam apratiṣṭhaṁ te jagad āhur anīśvaram<br />aparaspara-sambhūtaṁ kim anyat kāma-hetukam [8]
<span class="e2">te</span>–They, the persons of demoniac nature; <span class="e2">āhuḥ</span>–say:<span class="e2"> jagat asatyam</span>–“The world is without truth;<span class="e2"> apratiṣṭham</span>–baseless;<span class="e2"> anīśvaram</span>–godless;<span class="e2"> aparaspara-sambhūtam</span>–and everything is born of male and female union.<span class="e2"> kāma-hetukam</span>–The reason for existence is lust alone.<span class="e2"> kim anyat</span>–What is there beyond this?” [8]
8 The persons of ungodly nature say the world is without truth, baseless, godless, and that everything is born of male and female union. They say that life has no purpose beyond lust.
एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः ।<br />प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्म्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥९॥
etāṁ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno ’lpa-buddhayaḥ<br />prabhavanty ugra-karmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato ’hitāḥ [9]
<span class="e2">avaṣṭabhya</span>–Holding; <span class="e2">etām</span>–such; <span class="e2">dṛṣṭim</span>–a view; (<span class="e2">asurāḥ</span>)–the demons;<span class="e2"> naṣṭa-ātmānaḥ</span>–depraved;<span class="e2"> alpa-buddhayaḥ</span>–of low intelligence;<span class="e2"> ugra-karmāṇaḥ</span>–of cruel acts; <span class="e2">ahitāḥ</span>–of inauspicious nature;<span class="e2"> prabhavanti</span>–become powerful;<span class="e2"> kṣayāya</span>–for the destruction;<span class="e2"> jagataḥ</span>–of the world. [9]
9 Holding such a view, the demons, depraved and of low intelligence, become powerful and engage in cruel, inauspicious acts for the destruction of the world.
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः ।<br />मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्त्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥१०॥
kāmam āśritya duṣpūraṁ dambha-māna-madānvitāḥ<br />mohād gṛhītvāsad-grāhān pravartante ’śuchi-vratāḥ [10]
<span class="e2">āśritya</span>–Giving themselves up to;<span class="e2"> duṣpūram</span>–insatiable; <span class="e2">kāmam</span>–desire; (<span class="e2">te</span>)–such demons;<span class="e2"> dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ</span>–full of vanity, pride, and arrogance; <span class="e2">mohāt</span>–deluded;<span class="e2"> asat-grāhān gṛhītvā</span>–by eagerness for mundane enjoyment;<span class="e2"> pravartante</span>–engage;<span class="e2"> aśuchi-vratāḥ</span>–in grave malpractices. [10]
10 Giving themselves up to the delusion of insatiable desires for mundane enjoyment, such demons, full of vanity, pride, and arrogance, engage in grave malpractices.
चिन्तामपरिमेयाञ्च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः ।<br />कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥११॥
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः ।<br />ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥१२॥
chintām aparimeyāñ cha pralayāntām upāśritāḥ<br />kāmopabhoga-paramā etāvad iti niśchitāḥ [11]
āśā-pāśa-śatair baddhāḥ kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ<br />īhante kāma-bhogārtham anyāyenārtha-sañchayān [12]
<span class="e2">pralaya-antām</span>–Until death;<span class="e2"> upāśritāḥ</span>–overwhelmed with;<span class="e2"> aparimeyām cha</span>–unlimited;<span class="e2"> chintām</span>–cares; (<span class="e2">te</span>)–they;<span class="e2"> niśchitāḥ iti</span>–consider that; <span class="e2">etāvat</span>–only;<span class="e2"> kāma-upabhoga-paramāḥ</span>–enjoyment of desires is the ultimate.<span class="e2"> baddhāḥ</span>–Bound;<span class="e2"> āśā-pāśa-śataiḥ</span>–by the snares of hundreds of wishes;<span class="e2"> kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ</span>–overcome with desire and anger; (<span class="e2">te</span>) <span class="e2">īhante</span>–they try;<span class="e2"> artha-sañchayān</span>–to amass wealth;<span class="e2"> anyāyena</span>–unlawfully;<span class="e2"> kāma-bhoga-artham</span>–for the fulfillment of their desires. [11–12]
11–12 Until death they remain burdened with endless cares. They think that mundane enjoyment is the goal of life. Bound by hundreds of wishes and overcome with desire and anger, they endeavour to amass wealth unlawfully to fulfill their desires.
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिदं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् ।<br />इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥१३॥
idam adya mayā labdham idaṁ prāpsye manoratham<br />idam astīdam api me bhaviṣyati punar dhanam [13]
<span class="e2">adya</span>–“Today; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> labdham</span>–was gained; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by me; (<span class="e2">punaḥ</span>)–and again;<span class="e2"> prāpsye</span>–I will get;<span class="e2"> idam manoratham</span>–this other desirable object. <span class="e2">idam</span>–This wealth; <span class="e2">asti me</span>–is mine; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–and again;<span class="e2"> idam api dhanam</span>–more wealth;<span class="e2"> bhaviṣyati</span>–will be; (<span class="e2">me</span>)–mine.” [13]
13 The ungodly persons say, “Today I got what I wanted, and tomorrow I will also get what I want. All this is my wealth, and I will have even more in the future.”
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि ।<br />ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥१४॥
asau mayā hataḥ śatrur haniṣye chāparān api<br />īśvaro ’ham ahaṁ bhogī siddho ’haṁ balavān sukhī [14]
<span class="e2">asau</span>–“This; <span class="e2">śatruḥ</span>–enemy; <span class="e2">hataḥ</span>–has been destroyed; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by me; <span class="e2">api cha</span>–and again;<span class="e2"> haniṣye</span>–I will destroy; <span class="e2">aparān</span>–others.<span class="e2"> aham īśvaraḥ</span>–I am the lord;<span class="e2"> aham bhogī</span>–I am the enjoyer;<span class="e2"> aham siddhaḥ</span>–I am successful;<span class="e2"> balavān</span>–powerful; <span class="e2">sukhī</span>–and happy.” [14]
14 “I have destroyed one enemy, and I will destroy others. I am successful, powerful, and happy.”
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया ।<br />यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥१५॥
āḍhyo ’bhijanavān asmi ko ’nyo ’sti sadṛśo mayā<br />yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ity ajñāna-vimohitāḥ [15]
(<span class="e2">aham</span>) <span class="e2">asmi</span>–“I am; <span class="e2">āḍhyaḥ</span>–rich;<span class="e2"> abhijanavān</span>–and high-born.<span class="e2"> kaḥ asti</span>–Who is; <span class="e2">anyaḥ</span>–another;<span class="e2"> mayā sadṛśaḥ</span>–like me? (<span class="e2">aham</span>)–I; <span class="e2">yakṣye</span>–will perform sacrifice;<span class="e2"> dāsyāmi</span>–give charity;<span class="e2"> modiṣye</span>–and enjoy.” <span class="e2">iti</span>–Thus;<span class="e2"> ajñāna-vimohitāḥ</span>–they are deluded by ignorant notions. [15]
15 “I am wealthy and aristocratic. Who can compare with me? I shall perform sacrifice, give charity, and enjoy myself.” Thus they are deluded by ignorance.
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः ।<br />प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥१६॥
aneka-chitta-vibhrāntā moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ<br />prasaktāḥ kāma-bhogeṣu patanti narake ’śuchau [16]
<span class="e2">aneka-chitta-vibhrāntāḥ</span>–Their minds full of many vain thoughts;<span class="e2"> moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ</span>–caught in the net of illusion;<span class="e2"> prasaktāḥ</span>–engrossed;<span class="e2"> kāma-bhogeṣu</span>–in mundane enjoyment;<span class="e2"> patanti</span>–they fall;<span class="e2"> aśuchau</span>–to a foul; <span class="e2">narake</span>–hell, like Vaitaraṇī. [16]
16 Their minds full of vain thoughts, caught in the net of illusion and engrossed in mundane enjoyment, such ungodly persons fall to a foul hell.
आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः ।<br />यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्व्वकम् ॥१७॥
ātma-sambhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhana-māna-madānvitāḥ<br />yajante nāma-yajñais te dambhenāvidhi-pūrvakam [17]
<span class="e2">ātma-sambhāvitāḥ</span>–Conceited;<span class="e2"> stabdhāḥ</span>–obstinate;<span class="e2"> dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ</span>–intoxicated by wealth and pride; <span class="e2">te</span>–those demons;<span class="e2"> avidhi-pūrvakam</span>–ignoring the scriptural injunctions;<span class="e2"> dambhena</span>–hypocritically;<span class="e2"> yajante</span>–perform sacrifices;<span class="e2"> nama-yajñaiḥ</span>–in name only (pseudo-sacrifices). [17]
17 Conceited, obstinate, and intoxicated by wealth and grandeur, ignoring the scriptural injunctions, these demons make a hypocritical show of sacrifices.
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधञ्च संश्रिताः ।<br />मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥१८॥
ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhañ cha saṁśritāḥ<br />mām ātma-para-deheṣu pradviṣanto ’bhyasūyakāḥ [18]
<span class="e2">saṁśritāḥ</span>–Given to;<span class="e2"> ahaṅkāram</span>–egoism; <span class="e2">balam</span>–power; <span class="e2">darpam</span>–pride; <span class="e2">kāmam</span>–lust;<span class="e2"> krodham cha</span>–and anger; (<span class="e2">te bhavanti</span>)–they are;<span class="e2"> pradviṣantaḥ</span>–resentful; <span class="e2">mām</span>–of Me; (<span class="e2">sthitam</span>)–who am situated;<span class="e2"> ātma-para-deheṣu</span>–within their own and others’ bodies;<span class="e2"> abhyasūyakāḥ</span>–and they ascribe faults to the good qualities of the saintly persons. [18]
18 Given to egoism, pomp and power, lust and anger, they are resentful of Me, who am situated in their own and others’ bodies as the Supersoul, and they ascribe faults to the good qualities of the saintly persons.
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् ।<br />क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥१९॥
tān ahaṁ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṁsāreṣu narādhamān<br />kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu [19]
<span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> ajasram</span>–continually;<span class="e2"> kṣipāmi</span>–cast; <span class="e2">tān</span>–these;<span class="e2"> dviṣataḥ</span>–resentful; <span class="e2">krūrān</span>–cruel;<span class="e2"> aśubhān</span>–inauspicious;<span class="e2"> narādhamān</span>–decadent persons;<span class="e2"> saṁsāreṣu</span>–into the cycle of birth and death;<span class="e2"> āsurīṣu yoniṣu eva</span>–in the wombs of the demoniac. [19]
19 I continually cast these resentful, cruel, inauspicious, and decadent persons into the demoniac species, in the cycle of birth and death.
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।<br />मामाप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥२०॥
āsurīṁ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani<br />mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṁ gatim [20]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> āpannāḥ</span>–taking;<span class="e2"> janmani janmani</span>–birth after birth; <span class="e2">āsurīm</span>–in demoniac; <span class="e2">yonim</span>–species; <span class="e2">mūḍhāḥ</span>–these deluded persons;<span class="e2"> aprāpya eva</span>–not reaching; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> yānti gatim</span>–suffer a fate;<span class="e2"> tataḥ adhamām</span>–worse than that. [20]
20 O Kaunteya, repeatedly taking birth in the demoniac species, these deluded persons cannot come to Me, and they descend to lower and lower planes.
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।<br />कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥२१॥
tri-vidhaṁ narakasyedaṁ dvāraṁ nāśanam ātmanaḥ<br />kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṁ tyajet [21]
<span class="e2">idam tri-vidham</span>–These three kinds of; <span class="e2">dvāram</span>–doors;<span class="e2"> narakasya</span>–of hell;<span class="e2"> ātmanaḥ nāśanam</span>–lead to self-destruction: <span class="e2">kāmaḥ</span>–lust;<span class="e2"> krodhaḥ</span>–anger;<span class="e2"> tathā lobhaḥ</span>–and greed; <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–so;<span class="e2"> etat trayam</span>–these three; <span class="e2">tyajet</span>–must be abandoned. [21]
21 Lust, anger, and greed are the three doors of hell leading to self-destruction, so they must be abandoned.
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः ।<br />आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥२२॥
etair vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamo-dvārais tribhir naraḥ<br />ācharaty ātmanaḥ śreyas tato yāti parāṁ gatim [22]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O Kaunteya; <span class="e2">naraḥ</span>–a person;<span class="e2"> vimuktaḥ</span>–liberated; <span class="e2">etaiḥ</span>–from these;<span class="e2"> tribhiḥ tamaḥ-dvāraiḥ</span>–three doors of darkness;<span class="e2"> ācharati</span>–acts; <span class="e2">śreyaḥ</span>–for the benefit;<span class="e2"> ātmanaḥ</span>–of the soul. <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–By that; <span class="e2">yāti</span>–he reaches; <span class="e2">parām</span>–the supreme; <span class="e2">gatim</span>–goal. [22]
22 O Kaunteya, one who is liberated from these three doors of darkness strives for the benefit of the soul, by which he attains the supreme destination.
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्त्तते कामचारतः ।<br />न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥२३॥
yaḥ śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya vartate kāma-chārataḥ<br />na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṁ na parāṁ gatim [23]
<span class="e2">saḥ yaḥ</span>–He who;<span class="e2"> utsṛjya</span>–disregarding;<span class="e2"> śāstra-vidhim</span>–the injunctions of the scriptures;<span class="e2"> vartate kāma-chārataḥ</span>–acts according to his own desires;<span class="e2"> avāpnoti</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> na siddhim</span>–neither perfection, purification;<span class="e2"> na sukham</span>–nor happiness;<span class="e2"> na parām gatim</span>–nor the supreme destination. [23]
23 One who acts according to his own desires, disregarding the scriptural injunctions, cannot attain perfection, happiness, or the supreme destination.
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्य्याकार्य्यव्यवस्थितौ ।<br />ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म्म कर्त्तुमिहार्हसि ॥२४॥
tasmāch chhāstraṁ pramāṇaṁ te kāryākārya-vyavasthitau<br />jñātvā śāstra-vidhānoktaṁ karma kartum ihārhasi [24]
<span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> śāstram</span>–the scriptural injunctions;<span class="e2"> kāryākārya-vyavasthitau</span>–concerning duty and non-duty;<span class="e2"> te pramāṇam</span>–are your authority. <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–Knowing;<span class="e2"> śāstra-vidhāna-uktam</span>–scripturally enjoined; <span class="e2">karma</span>–duty; <span class="e2">iha</span>–in this world of action; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>) <span class="e2">arhasi</span>–you ought; (<span class="e2">tat</span>) <span class="e2">kartum</span>–to act accordingly. [24]
24 Therefore, the scriptural injunctions for duty and non-duty are your authority. Knowing your duty in this world according to the scriptures (to act only for the Lord’s pleasure), you should act accordingly.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे दैवासुरसम्पद्विभागयोगो नाम षोडशोऽध्यायः ॥१६॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde daivāsura-<br />sampad-vibhāga-yogo nāma ṣoḍaśo ’dhyāyaḥ [16]
End of Chapter Sixteen<br />The Godly and Ungodly Natures<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

सप्तदशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Seventeen
Śraddhātraya-vibhāga-yoga <br />The Three Types of Faith
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः ।<br />तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥१॥
arjuna uvācha
ye śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ<br />teṣāṁ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ [1]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–O Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">kā</span>–what; <span class="e2">niṣṭhā</span>–is the position; <span class="e2">teṣām</span>–of those; <span class="e2">ye</span>–who;<span class="e2"> utsṛjya</span>–ignore;<span class="e2"> śāstra-vidhim</span>–the scriptural injunctions; <span class="e2">tu</span>–yet; <span class="e2">sraddhayā-anvitāḥ </span>(<span class="e2">santaḥ</span>)–faithfully;<span class="e2"> yajante</span>–worship? (<span class="e2">sa kim</span>)–Is that;<span class="e2"> sattvam</span>–in goodness;<span class="e2"> āho rajaḥ</span>–or passion; (<span class="e2">uta</span>) <span class="e2">tamaḥ</span>–or ignorance? [1]
1 Arjuna inquired: O Kṛṣṇa, what is the position of those who worship with faith, but ignore the injunctions of the scriptures? Is their faith in the mode of goodness, passion, or ignorance?
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।<br />सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
tri-vidhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṁ sā svabhāva-jā<br />sāttvikī rājasī chaiva tāmasī cheti tāṁ śṛṇu [2]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said:<span class="e2"> śraddhā eva</span>–Faith;<span class="e2"> dehinām</span>–of the living beings;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–is;<span class="e2"> tri-vidhā iti</span>–of these three types:<span class="e2"> sattvikī</span>–good;<span class="e2"> rājasī cha</span>–passionate;<span class="e2"> tāmasī cha</span>–and ignorant. <span class="e2">sā</span>–That faith;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-jā</span>–is born of their own nature acquired from impressions of previous lives.<span class="e2"> tām śṛṇu</span>–Now hear of that. [2]
2 The Supreme Lord said: Faith is of three types, born of the embodied soul’s acquired nature, whether good, passionate, or ignorant. Now hear of this:
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्व्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत ।<br />श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥३॥
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata<br />śraddhāmayo ’yaṁ puruṣo yo yach chhraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ [3]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O descendant of Bharata;<span class="e2"> śraddhā</span>–the faith;<span class="e2"> sarvasya</span>–of all living beings;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–is;<span class="e2"> sattva-anurūpā</span>–according to their consciousness.<span class="e2"> ayam puruṣaḥ</span>–The living being;<span class="e2"> śraddhā-mayaḥ</span>–possesses faith by constitution. <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–He; <span class="e2">saḥ eva</span>–is that;<span class="e2"> yaḥ yat śraddhaḥ</span>–which his faith is. [3]
3 O Bhārata, the faith of all living beings is governed by their consciousness. The living being possesses faith by constitution. He is that which his faith is.
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः ।<br />प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥४॥
yajante sāttvikā devān yakṣa-rakṣāṁsi rājasāḥ<br />pretān bhūta-gaṇāṁś chānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ [4]
<span class="e2">sāttvikāḥ</span>–Those with faith of the nature of goodness;<span class="e2"> yajante</span>–worship; <span class="e2">devān</span>–demigods of the nature of goodness.<span class="e2"> rājasāḥ</span>–Those of passionate faith;<span class="e2"> yajante</span>–worship;<span class="e2"> yakṣa-rakṣāṁsi</span>–the Yakṣa demigods and Rākṣasa demons of passionate nature. <span class="e2">anye</span>–Others;<span class="e2"> tāmasāḥ janāḥ</span>–who possess ignorant faith; (<span class="e2">yajante</span>)–worship;<span class="e2"> pretān bhūta-gaṇān cha</span>–the ghosts and spirits of the nature of ignorance. [4]
4 Persons with faith of the nature of goodness worship the demigods, persons with faith of a passionate nature worship the Yakṣa demigods and Rākṣasa demons, while those with faith of the nature of ignorance worship the ghosts and spirits.
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।<br />दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥५॥
कर्शयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः ।<br />मां चैवान्तः शरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥६॥
aśāstra-vihitaṁ ghoraṁ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ<br />dambhāhaṅkāra-saṁyuktāḥ kāma-rāga-balānvitāḥ [5]
karśayantaḥ śarīra-sthaṁ bhūta-grāmam achetasaḥ<br />māñ chaivāntaḥ śarīra-sthaṁ tān viddhy āsura-niśchayān [6]
<span class="e2">achetasaḥ</span>–Ignorant; <span class="e2">janāḥ</span>–persons; <span class="e2">ye</span>–who;<span class="e2"> tapyante</span>–perform; <span class="e2">ghoram</span>–severe; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerities;<span class="e2"> aśāstra-vihitam</span>–unsanctioned by the scriptures;<span class="e2"> dambha-ahaṅkāra-saṁyuktāḥ</span>–full of pride and egoism;<span class="e2"> kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ</span>–and impelled by desire, attachment, and power;<span class="e2"> karśayantaḥ</span>–torture;<span class="e2"> bhūta-grāmam</span>–the five basic material elements;<span class="e2"> śarīra-stham</span>–in the body; (<span class="e2">karśayantaḥ</span>)<span class="e2"> mām cha eva</span>–and also torment Me, in the form of My particle, the spirit soul, the jīvātman;<span class="e2"> antaḥ śarīra-stham</span>–in the body. <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–Know; <span class="e2">tān</span>–them;<span class="e2"> āsura-niśchayān</span>–to be of demoniacal conviction. [5–6]
5–6 Full of pride and egoism, motivated by ambition, attachment, and power, ignorant persons perform severe austerities unsanctioned by the scriptures and torture the body’s natural elements and the soul within. Know them to be of demoniacal faith.
आहारस्त्वपि सर्व्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः ।<br />यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥७॥
āhāras tv api sarvasya tri-vidho bhavati priyaḥ<br />yajñas tapas tathā dānaṁ teṣāṁ bhedam imaṁ śṛṇu [7]
(<span class="e2">guṇa bhedāt</span>)–According to the three modes of material nature;<span class="e2"> bhavati tu api</span>–there are also;<span class="e2"> tri-vidhaḥ āhāraḥ</span>–three kinds of food; <span class="e2">priyaḥ</span>–pleasing;<span class="e2"> sarvasya</span>–to everyone. <span class="e2">tathā</span>–There are similarly; (<span class="e2">tri vidham</span>)–three kinds; <span class="e2">yajñaḥ</span>–of sacrifice; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity; <span class="e2">dānam</span>–and charity. <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–Now hear of; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this; <span class="e2">bhedam</span>–classification; <span class="e2">teṣām</span>–of them. [7]
7 According to the three modes of material nature, there are also three kinds of food preference. In the same way, there are three kinds of sacrifice, three kinds of austerity, and three kinds of charity. Now hear of these:
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः ।<br />रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥८॥
āyuḥ-sattva-balārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ<br />rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvika-priyāḥ [8]
<span class="e2">āhārāḥ</span>–Foods;<span class="e2"> āyuḥ-sattva-bala-ārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ</span>–that increase longevity, vitality, strength, health, happiness, and loving kindness; <span class="e2">rasyāḥ</span>–tasty;<span class="e2"> snigdhāḥ</span>–succulent;<span class="e2"> sthirāḥ</span>–wholesome; <span class="e2">hṛdyāḥ</span>–and pleasant; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–are;<span class="e2"> sāttvika-priyāḥ</span>– dear to persons of the nature of goodness. [8]
8 Foods that increase longevity, vitality, strength, health, happiness, and loving kindness, and which are tasty, succulent, wholesome, and pleasant, are dear to persons of the nature of goodness.
कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरुक्षविदाहिनः ।<br />आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥९॥
kaṭv-amla-lavaṇāty-uṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rukṣa-vidāhinaḥ<br />āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkha-śokāmaya-pradāḥ [9]
<span class="e2">āhārāḥ</span>–Food; <span class="e2">kaṭu-amla-lavaṇa-ati-uṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rukṣa-vidāhinaḥ</span>–that is too bitter, too sour, too salty, too hot, too pungent, too dry, and overheating;<span class="e2"> duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-pradāḥ</span>–and which cause pain, sorrow, and <span class="e2">illness </span>(<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–are; <span class="e2">iṣṭāḥ</span>–dear;<span class="e2"> rājasasya</span>–to the passionate. [9]
9 Foods dear to persons of passionate nature are too bitter (nimba, etc.), too sour, too salty, too hot, too pungent (chilli pepper, etc.), too dry (dry-roasted chickpeas, etc.), and too heating (mustard seed, etc.). Such foods cause pain, sorrow, and illness.
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्य्युषितञ्च यत् ।<br />उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥१०॥
yāta-yāmaṁ gata-rasaṁ pūti paryuṣitañ cha yat<br />uchchhiṣṭam api chāmedhyaṁ bhojanaṁ tāmasa-priyam [10]
<span class="e2">yat bhojanam</span>–That food which is;<span class="e2"> yāta-yāmam</span>–cooked, but left to become cold;<span class="e2"> gata-rasam</span>–tasteless; <span class="e2">pūti</span>–odoriferous;<span class="e2"> paryuṣitam cha</span>–putrid;<span class="e2"> uchchhiṣṭam api</span>–remnants (other than that of worshippable persons);<span class="e2"> amedhyam cha</span>–and impure foods unofferable in sacrifice (meat, wine, and onions, etc.); (<span class="e2">tat bhavati</span>)–such food is;<span class="e2"> tāmasa-priyam</span>–dear to the ignorant. [10]
10 Dear to the ignorant are foods that are stale, tasteless, foul-smelling or were cooked the day before, remnants (other than that of worshippable persons), and impure foods (such as meat, wine, and onions).
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदिष्टो य इज्यते ।<br />यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥११॥
aphalākāṅkṣibhir yajño vidhi-diṣṭo ya ijyate<br />yaṣṭavyam eveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ [11]
<span class="e2">saḥ yajñaḥ</span>–That sacrifice;<span class="e2"> yaḥ ijyate</span>–which is performed;<span class="e2"> vidhi-diṣṭaḥ</span>–according to scriptural injunctions;<span class="e2"> aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ</span>–by one who does not hanker for its fruit;<span class="e2"> manaḥ samādhāya</span>–with the firm conviction;<span class="e2"> yaṣṭavyam eva iti</span>–and dutifully;<span class="e2"> sāttvikaḥ</span>–is sacrifice of the nature of goodness. [11]
11 That sacrifice which is in accordance with scriptural injunctions and faithfully performed by a person free from fruitive desire, is sacrifice of the nature of goodness.
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।<br />इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥१२॥
abhisandhāya tu phalaṁ dambhārtham api chaiva yat<br />ijyate bharata-śreṣṭha taṁ yajñaṁ viddhi rājasam [12]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharata-śreṣṭha</span>–O Bharat; <span class="e2">yat</span>–that which; <span class="e2">ijyate</span>–is performed;<span class="e2"> abhisandhāya</span>–motivated by; <span class="e2">phalam</span>–remuneration;<span class="e2"> dambha-artham api cha eva</span>–and which is a show of pomp and grandeur; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know;<span class="e2"> tam yajñam</span>–that sacrifice;<span class="e2"> rājasam</span>–to be of a passionate nature. [12]
12 But, O Bhārat, know that sacrifice which is performed in fruitive expectation and as a display of pomp and grandeur, is sacrifice of the nature of passion.
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।<br />श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥१३॥
vidhi-hīnam asṛṣṭānnaṁ mantra-hīnam adakṣiṇam<br />śraddhā-virahitaṁ yajñaṁ tāmasaṁ parichakṣate [13]
<span class="e2">vidhi-hīnam</span>–Non-scriptural; <span class="e2">yajñam</span>–sacrifice;<span class="e2"> asṛṣṭa-annam</span>–without the distribution of food, etc.;<span class="e2"> mantra-hīnam</span>–without mantra;<span class="e2"> adakṣiṇam</span>–without appropriate offerings to the priests;<span class="e2"> śraddhā-virahitam</span>–and without faith;<span class="e2"> parichakṣate</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> tāmasam</span>–ignorant. [13]
13 And that sacrifice which ignores the injunctions of the scriptures, which is performed without the distribution of foodstuffs, without uttering the appropriate mantras, without offerings to the priests, and without faith, is known as sacrifice in ignorance.
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्ज्जवम् ।<br />ब्रह्मचर्य्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥१४॥
deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanaṁ śaucham ārjavam<br />brahmacharyam ahiṁsā cha śārīraṁ tapa uchyate [14]
<span class="e2">deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanam</span>–Worship of the deity, the brāhmaṇ, the guru, and the enlightened soul;<span class="e2"> śaucham</span>–internal and external purity;<span class="e2"> ārjavam</span>–simplicity;<span class="e2"> brahmacharyam</span>–celibacy;<span class="e2"> ahiṁsā cha</span>–and nonviolence;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–are called;<span class="e2"> śārīram</span>–bodily; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity. [14]
14 Worship of the deity, the brāhmaṇ, the spiritual master, and the enlightened soul, purity, simplicity, celibacy, and nonviolence—these all constitute austerity of the body.
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितञ्च यत् ।<br />स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥१५॥
anudvega-karaṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priya-hitañ cha yat<br />svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ chaiva vāṅmayaṁ tapa uchyate [15]
<span class="e2">satyam</span>–Truthful; <span class="e2">vākyam</span>–speech; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> anudvega-karam</span>–does not disturb;<span class="e2"> priya-hitam cha</span>–and is pleasing yet beneficial;<span class="e2"> svādhyāya-abhyasanam cha eva</span>–and regular recitation of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> vāk-mayam</span>–verbal; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity. [15]
15 Speech which does not disturb others, which is truthful, pleasing yet beneficial, as well as regular recitation of the Vedas—all these are known as verbal austerity.
मनः प्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।<br />भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥१६॥
manaḥ prasādaḥ saumyatvaṁ maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ<br />bhāva-saṁśuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam uchyate [16]
<span class="e2">iti etat</span>–All these;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–are called;<span class="e2"> mānasam</span>–mental; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity:<span class="e2"> manaḥ prasādaḥ</span>–self-satisfaction;<span class="e2"> saumyatvam</span>–benevolence; <span class="e2">maunam</span>–stability;<span class="e2"> ātma-vinigrahaḥ</span>–mental control;<span class="e2"> bhāva-saṁśuddhiḥ</span>–and pure-heartedness.[16]
16 Self-satisfaction, benevolence, stability, mental control, and pure-heartedness are all known as mental austerity.
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः ।<br />अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥१७॥
śraddhayā parayā taptaṁ tapas tat tri-vidhaṁ naraiḥ<br />aphalākāṅkṣibhir yuktaiḥ sāttvikaṁ parichakṣate [17]
<span class="e2">taptam</span>–When practised;<span class="e2"> yuktaiḥ</span>–by the devout;<span class="e2"> aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ</span>–desireless; <span class="e2">naraiḥ</span>–person; <span class="e2">parayā</span>–with deep;<span class="e2"> śraddhayā</span>–faith; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> tri-vidham tapaḥ</span>–threefold austerity (bodily, verbal, and mental);<span class="e2"> parichakṣate</span>–are designated as;<span class="e2"> sāttvikam</span>–being of the nature of goodness. [17]
17 When performed by a desireless, devout soul with deep faith in the Supreme Lord, this threefold austerity of thought, word, and deed is of the nature of goodness.
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।<br />क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥१८॥
satkāra-māna-pūjārthaṁ tapo dambhena chaiva yat<br />kriyate tad iha proktaṁ rājasaṁ chalam adhruvam [18]
<span class="e2">tat</span>–That; <span class="e2">chalam</span>–unenduring;<span class="e2"> adhruvam</span>–transitory; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> kriyate</span>–is performed;<span class="e2"> satkāra-māna-pūja-artham</span>–for the sake of gain, worship, and fame;<span class="e2"> dambhena cha eva</span>–and performed with great pride;<span class="e2"> iha proktam</span>–is designated in this world as;<span class="e2"> rājasam</span>–passionate austerity. [18]
18 That unenduring, transitory austerity which is proudly performed for the sake of gain, worship, name, and fame, is known as austerity of the nature of passion.
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पिडया क्रियते तपः ।<br />परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥१९॥
mūḍha-grāheṇātmano yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ<br />parasyotsādanārthaṁ vā tat tāmasam udāhṛtam [19]
<span class="e2">tat tapaḥ</span>–That austerity; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> kriyate</span>–is performed;<span class="e2"> mūḍha-grāheṇa</span>–with dubious intent; <span class="e2">pīḍayā</span>–causing pain;<span class="e2"> ātmanaḥ</span>–to oneself; <span class="e2">vā</span>–or;<span class="e2"> utsādana-artham</span>–for harming;<span class="e2"> parasya</span>–others;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtam</span>–is described as;<span class="e2"> tāmasam</span>–ignorant. [19]
19 That austerity which is performed with dubious intent, causing self-torture, or meant to harm others, is known as austerity of the nature of ignorance.
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।<br />देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥२०॥
dātavyam iti yad dānaṁ dīyate ’nupakāriṇe<br />deśe kāle cha pātre cha tad dānaṁ sāttvikaṁ smṛtam [20]
<span class="e2">dānam</span>–The gift; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; <span class="e2">dīyate</span>–is given;<span class="e2"> anupakāriṇe iti</span>–without expectation of return; <span class="e2">deśe</span>–at an auspicious or holy place;<span class="e2"> kāle cha</span>–at an astrologically auspicious time; <span class="e2">pātre</span>–to a qualified recipient;<span class="e2"> dātavyam cha</span>–and with the conviction that it ought to be given;<span class="e2"> tat dānam</span>–that gift; <span class="e2">smṛtam</span>–is considered;<span class="e2"> sāttvikam</span>–to be of the nature of goodness. [20]
20 The gift which is given without expectation of return, with the conviction that it ought to be given, at an appropriate place and time, and to an appropriate recipient, is considered to be of the nature of goodness.
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।<br />दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥२१॥
yat tu praty-upakārārthaṁ phalam uddiśya vā punaḥ<br />dīyate cha parikliṣṭaṁ tad dānaṁ rājasaṁ smṛtam [21]
<span class="e2">yat tu</span>–And that which; <span class="e2">dīyate</span>–is given;<span class="e2"> prati-upakāra-artham</span>–with expectation of return; <span class="e2">vā</span>–or;<span class="e2"> phalam uddiśya</span>–for the purpose of a reward;<span class="e2"> punaḥ cha</span>–and moreover;<span class="e2"> parikliṣṭam</span>–(is given) begrudgingly;<span class="e2"> tat dānam</span>–that gift; <span class="e2">smṛtam</span>–is considered;<span class="e2"> rājasam</span>–to be of the nature of passion. [21]
21 Otherwise, the gift begrudgingly given in expectation of gaining something in return, or with a desire for a reward (such as the attainment of heaven), is considered to be of the nature of passion.
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।<br />असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥२२॥
adeśa-kāle yad dānam apātrebhyaś cha dīyate<br />asatkṛtam avajñātaṁ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam [22]
<span class="e2">yat dānam</span>–That gift which; <span class="e2">dīyate</span>–is given;<span class="e2"> asat-kṛtam</span>–disrespectfully;<span class="e2"> avajñātam cha</span>–and scornfully;<span class="e2"> adeśa-kāle</span>–at an improper place and time;<span class="e2"> apātrebhyaḥ</span>–to an undeserving recipient; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that gift;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtam</span>–is described as;<span class="e2"> tāmasam</span>–being of the nature of ignorance. [22]
22 The gift given disrespectfully and scornfully to an unworthy recipient at an improper place and time is considered to be of the nature of ignorance.
ओंत्सदिति निर्द्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ।<br />ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥२३॥
oṁ-tat-sad iti nirdeśo brahmaṇas tri-vidhaḥ smṛtaḥ<br />brāhmaṇās tena vedāś cha yajñāś cha vihitāḥ purā [23]
<span class="e2">iti</span>–These;<span class="e2"> tri-vidhaḥ</span>–three words:<span class="e2"> om-tat-sat</span>–<span class="e3">Om Tat Sat</span>; <span class="e2">smṛtaḥ</span>–are known in the scriptures as;<span class="e2"> nirdeśaḥ</span>–indicating;<span class="e2"> brahmaṇaḥ</span>–Brahma, the Supreme Spirit. <span class="e2">purā</span>–In ancient times, at the universal manifestation;<span class="e2"> brāhmaṇāḥ</span>–the brāhmaṇs;<span class="e2"> vedāḥ cha</span>–the Vedas;<span class="e2"> yajñāḥ cha</span>–and sacrifices;<span class="e2"> vihitāḥ</span>–were manifested; <span class="e2">tena</span>–by these three words. [23]
23 The scriptures say that the words <span class="e3">Om Tat Sat</span> indicate Brahma, the Supreme Spirit. At the time of the universal manifestation, the brāhmaṇs, the Vedas, and sacrifices were manifested by these three words.
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः ।<br />प्रवर्त्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥२४॥
tasmād om ity udāhṛtya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ<br />pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṁ brahma-vādinām [24]
<span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> vidhāna-uktāḥ</span>–scripturally prescribed;<span class="e2"> yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ</span>–duties of sacrifice, charity, and austerity;<span class="e2"> brahma-vādinām</span>–of the followers of the Vedas;<span class="e2"> satatam pravartante</span>–are always initiated;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtya</span>–uttering; <span class="e2">om iti</span>–the syllable <span class="e3">Om</span>, representing Brahma, the Absolute. [24]
24 Thus the followers of the Vedas always utter the syllable <span class="e3">Om</span> representing Brahma, the Absolute, to initiate their prescribed duties of sacrifice, charity, and austerity.
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः ।<br />दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥२५॥
tad ity anabhisandhāya phalaṁ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ<br />dāna-kriyāś cha vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ [25]
<span class="e2">mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ</span>–Persons aspiring for liberation; (<span class="e2">udāhṛtya</span>)–uttering; <span class="e2">tat iti</span>–the word <span class="e3">Tat</span>, representing Brahma, the Absolute;<span class="e2"> kriyante</span>–perform;<span class="e2"> vividhāḥ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ</span>–acts of various kinds of sacrifice and austerity;<span class="e2"> dāna-kriyāḥ cha</span>–and acts of charity;<span class="e2"> anabhisandhāya</span>–without motivation; <span class="e2">phalam</span>–for the fruits. [25]
25 Persons aspiring for liberation utter the word <span class="e3">Tat</span>, representing Brahma, the Absolute, to invoke the performance of various acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity without motivation for the results.
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते ।<br />प्रशस्ते कर्म्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥२६॥
sad-bhāve sādhu-bhāve cha sad ity etat prayujyate<br />praśaste karmaṇi tathā sach chhabdaḥ pārtha yujyate [26]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">sat iti</span>–the word <span class="e3">Sat</span>, representing Brahma, the Absolute;<span class="e2"> prayujyate</span>–is used;<span class="e2"> sat-bhāve</span>–to indicate truth, the nature of Brahma;<span class="e2"> sādhu-bhāve cha</span>–and persons dedicated to the truth, knowers of Brahma. <span class="e2">tathā</span>–Therefore;<span class="e2"> etat sat-śabdaḥ</span>–this word <span class="e3">Sat</span>;<span class="e2"> yujyate</span>–is uttered;<span class="e2"> praśaste karmaṇi</span>–during auspicious activities. [26]
26 O Pārtha, the word <span class="e3">Sat</span>, representing Brahma, the Absolute, indicates the truth and persons dedicated to the truth. Therefore, the word <span class="e3">Sat</span> is uttered to invoke the performance of auspicious activities.
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।<br />कर्म्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥२७॥
yajñe tapasi dāne cha sthitiḥ sad iti chochyate<br />karma chaiva tad-arthīyaṁ sad ity evābhidhīyate [27]
<span class="e2">sthitiḥ</span>–The eternality; <span class="e2">yajñe</span>–in sacrifice; <span class="e2">tapasi</span>–austerity;<span class="e2"> dāne cha</span>–and charity;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is described;<span class="e2"> sat iti cha</span>–by this word <span class="e3">Sat</span>.<span class="e2"> karma cha eva</span>–And action;<span class="e2"> tat-arthīyam</span>–for the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> abhidhīyate</span>–is designated;<span class="e2"> sat iti eva</span>–by the word <span class="e3">Sat</span>. [27]
27 The word <span class="e3">Sat</span> is said to indicate the eternality of sacrifice, austerity, and charity. And action for the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord is called <span class="e3">Sat</span>—truth.
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतञ्च यत् ।<br />असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥२८॥
aśraddhayā hutaṁ dattaṁ tapas taptaṁ kṛtañ cha yat<br />asad ity uchyate pārtha na cha tat pretya no iha [28]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">yat</span>–whatever; <span class="e2">hutam</span>–sacrifice is offered; <span class="e2">dattam</span>–charity is given;<span class="e2"> tapaḥ taptam</span>–austerity is endured; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">kṛtam</span>–action is performed;<span class="e2"> aśraddhayā</span>–without faith; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is described;<span class="e2"> asat iti</span>–as asat, untruth; (<span class="e2">yataḥ tat</span>)–because that; (<span class="e2">phalati</span>)–fructifies; <span class="e2">na u iha</span>–neither in this world;<span class="e2"> na cha pretya</span>–nor the next. [28]
28 O Pārtha, sacrifice, charity, and austerity or any action performed without faith in the Supreme is known as asat, or untruth. Such works cannot bring an auspicious result, either in this world or the next.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे <br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे श्रद्धात्रयविभागयोगो नाम सप्तदशोऽध्यायः ॥१७॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde śraddhā<br />traya-vibhāga-yogo nāma sapta-daśo ’dhyāyaḥ [17]
End of Chapter Seventeen<br />The Three Types of Faith<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

एकादशोऽध्यायः
Chapter Eighteen
Mokṣa-yoga <br />The Path of Liberation
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
सन्न्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ।<br />त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिसूदन ॥१॥
arjuna uvācha
sannyāsasya mahā-bāho tattvam ichchhāmi veditum<br />tyāgasya cha hṛṣīkeśa pṛthak keśinisūdana [1]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty hero; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> hṛṣīkeśa</span>–O Lord of all senses; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> keśinisūdana</span>–O slayer of the Keśi demon;<span class="e2"> ichchāmi</span>–I wish;<span class="e2"> veditum</span>–to understand;<span class="e2"> tattvam</span>–the subject;<span class="e2"> sannyāsasya</span>–of renunciation;<span class="e2"> tyāgasya cha</span>–and detachment; <span class="e2">pṛthak</span>–separately. [1]
1 Arjuna said: O almighty Lord, slayer of the demon Keśi, I wish to understand the subject of renunciation (sannyās) and detachment (tyāga), separately.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
काम्यानां कर्म्मणां न्यासं सन्न्यासं कवयो विदुः ।<br />सर्व्वकर्म्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥२॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
kāmyānāṁ karmaṇāṁ nyāsaṁ sannyāsaṁ kavayo viduḥ<br />sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṁ prāhus tyāgaṁ vichakṣaṇāḥ [2]
<span class="e2">śrī-bhagavān uvācha</span>–The Supreme Lord said:<span class="e2"> kavayaḥ</span>–the learned;<span class="e2"> vichakṣaṇāḥ</span>–enlightened personalities; <span class="e2">viduḥ</span>–know; <span class="e2">nyāsam</span>–renunciation;<span class="e2"> karmaṇām</span>–of actions;<span class="e2"> kāmyānām</span>–that are motivated by fruitive desires;<span class="e2"> sannyāsam</span>–as sannyās, renunciation; <span class="e2">prāhuḥ</span>–and they say that;<span class="e2"> sarva-karma-phala-tyāgam</span>–the renunciation of the fruits of all actions, whether daily, incidental, or fruitive; <span class="e2">tyāgam</span>–is detachment. [2]
2 The Supreme Lord said: Learned, enlightened persons know the giving up of fruitive action as renunciation, and the giving up of the fruits of all action as detachment.
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ।<br />यज्ञदानतपःकर्म्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥३॥
tyājyaṁ doṣavad ity eke karma prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ<br />yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyam iti chāpare [3]
<span class="e2">eke manīṣiṇaḥ</span>–Some scholars (generally the sāṅkhyas); <span class="e2">prāhuḥ</span>–declare that; <span class="e2">karma</span>–action;<span class="e2"> tyājyam</span>–should be given up;<span class="e2"> doṣavat iti</span>–as imperfect (due to violence, etc.);<span class="e2"> apare cha</span>–and others (generally the mīmāṁsakas); <span class="e2">iti </span>(<span class="e2">prāhuh</span>)–say that;<span class="e2"> yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma</span>–(scripturally enjoined) action of the nature of sacrifice, charity, and austerity;<span class="e2"> na tyājyam</span>–should not be abandoned. [3]
3 Some philosophers hold that action should be renounced as imperfect. Others hold that action of the nature of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should never be given up.
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।<br />त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्त्तितः ॥४॥
niśchayaṁ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama<br />tyāgo hi puruṣa-vyāghra tri-vidhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ [4]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharata-sattama</span>–O best of the Bhāratas; <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–hear; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> niśchayam</span>–perfect conclusion;<span class="e2"> tatra tyāge</span>–concerning tyāga, detachment, or the quality of renunciation; <span class="e2">hi</span>–since; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> puruṣa-vyāghra</span>–O best of men; <span class="e2">tyāgaḥ</span>–the quality of renunciation;<span class="e2"> samprakīrtitaḥ</span>–has been clearly described (in the scriptures);<span class="e2"> tri-vidhaḥ</span>–to be of three types. [4]
4 O best of the Bhāratas, hear My perfect conclusion concerning detachment, the quality of renunciation, since, O best of men, it has been clearly established that the quality of renunciation is of three types.
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म्म न त्याज्यं कार्य्यमेव तत् ।<br />यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥५॥
yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyaṁ kāryam eva tat<br />yajño dānaṁ tapaś chaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām [5]
<span class="e2">yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma</span>–Duties of sacrifice, charity, and austerity, etc.;<span class="e2"> na tyājyam</span>–should not be given up. <span class="e2">tat</span>–They; <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">kāryam</span>–must be performed; (<span class="e2">yataḥ</span>)–because; <span class="e2">yajñaḥ</span>–sacrifice; <span class="e2">dānam</span>–charity;<span class="e2"> tapaḥ cha</span>–and austerity; (<span class="e2">bhavanti</span>)–are;<span class="e2"> pāvanāni eva</span>–the purifiers;<span class="e2"> manīṣiṇām</span>–of the wise. [5]
5 Actions of the nature of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should never be abandoned. They must be performed for they are the purifiers of the wise.
एतान्यपि तु कर्म्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।<br />कर्त्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥६॥
etāny api tu karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalāni cha<br />kartavyānīti me pārtha niśchitaṁ matam uttamam [6]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">api tu</span>–but even; <span class="e2">etāni</span>–these;<span class="e2"> karmāṇi</span>–actions;<span class="e2"> kartavyāni</span>–must be performed;<span class="e2"> tyaktvā</span>–renouncing; <span class="e2">saṅgam</span>–attachment;<span class="e2"> phalāni cha</span>–and desire for the results. <span class="e2">iti</span>–This is; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> niśchitam</span>–definite;<span class="e2"> uttamam</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">matam</span>–perfect conclusion (siddhānta). [6]
6 But even these actions must be performed abandoning attachment and fruitive desire. O Pārtha, know this to be My perfect, supreme conclusion.
नियतस्य तु सन्न्यासः कर्म्मणो नोपपद्यते ।<br />मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्त्तितः ॥७॥
niyatasya tu sannyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate<br />mohāt tasya parityāgas tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ [7]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But;<span class="e2"> sannyāsaḥ</span>–renunciation;<span class="e2"> niyatasya</span>–of obligatory;<span class="e2"> karmaṇaḥ</span>–duties;<span class="e2"> na upapadyate</span>–cannot be justified.<span class="e2"> parityāgaḥ</span>–Abandonment; <span class="e2">tasya</span>–of those duties; <span class="e2">mohāt</span>–out of delusion;<span class="e2"> parikīrtitaḥ</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> tāmasaḥ</span>–renunciation of the nature of ignorance. [7]
7 Renunciation of one’s obligatory duties is wrong. The delusion of giving up these duties is called false renunciation, or renunciation of the nature of ignorance.
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् ।<br />स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥८॥
duḥkham ity eva yat karma kāya-kleśa-bhayāt tyajet<br />sa kṛtvā rājasaṁ tyāgaṁ naiva tyāga-phalaṁ labhet [8]
(<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>)–That person who; <span class="e2">iti </span>(<span class="e2">matvā</span>)–thinks that;<span class="e2"> yat karma</span>–such obligatory duties;<span class="e2"> duḥkham eva</span>–are troublesome; <span class="e2">tyajet</span>–and renounces them;<span class="e2"> kāya-kleśa-bhayāt</span>–out of fear of physical discomfort; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–that person; <span class="e2">kṛtvā</span>–by performing; <span class="e2">tyāgam</span>–renunciation;<span class="e2"> rājasam</span>–of the nature of passion;<span class="e2"> na labhet eva</span>–cannot attain;<span class="e2"> tyāga-phalam</span>–the fruit of detachment—enlightenment. [8]
8 One who abandons his obligatory duties out of fear of physical discomfort, considering them troublesome, performs renunciation of the nature of passion. Thus, he does not attain the fruit of true detachment.
कार्य्यमित्येव यत्कर्म्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलञ्चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥९॥
kāryam ity eva yat karma niyataṁ kriyate ’rjuna<br />saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalañ chaiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ [9]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> niyatam</span>–obligatory; <span class="e2">karma</span>–duties; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> kriyate</span>–are performed;<span class="e2"> kāryam iti eva</span>–as a matter of duty;<span class="e2"> tyaktvā</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">saṅgam</span>–attachment;<span class="e2"> phalam eva cha</span>–and fruitive desire;<span class="e2"> saḥ tyāgaḥ sāttvikaḥ</span>–constitute renunciation of the nature of goodness; (<span class="e2">me</span>) <span class="e2">mataḥ</span>–in My consideration. [9]
9 O Arjuna, performance of obligatory works as a matter of duty while abandoning attachment and fruitive desire, is renunciation of the nature of goodness. This is My opinion.
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म्म कुशले नानुषज्जते ।<br />त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥१०॥
na dveṣṭy akuśalaṁ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate<br />tyāgī sattva-samāviṣṭo medhāvī chhinna-saṁśayaḥ [10]
<span class="e2">medhāvī</span>–The wise; <span class="e2">tyāgī</span>–renunciate;<span class="e2"> sattva-samāviṣṭaḥ</span>–absorbed in the nature of goodness;<span class="e2"> chhinna-saṁśayaḥ</span>–having slashed all doubts;<span class="e2"> na dveṣṭi</span>–neither resents;<span class="e2"> akuśalam</span>–troublesome; <span class="e2">karma</span>–duties;<span class="e2"> na anuṣajjate</span>–nor is attached to; <span class="e2">kuśale</span>–duties which bestow happiness. [10]
10 The wise renunciate who is absorbed in the nature of goodness, and who has slashed all doubts, neither resents disagreeable duties nor is attached to agreeable works.
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्म्माण्यशेषतः ।<br />यस्तु कर्म्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥११॥
na hi deha-bhṛtā śakyaṁ tyaktuṁ karmāṇy aśeṣataḥ<br />yas tu karma-phala-tyāgī sa tyāgīty abhidhīyate [11]
<span class="e2">deha-bhṛtā</span>–The embodied soul;<span class="e2"> na śakyam hi</span>–can never;<span class="e2"> aśeṣataḥ</span>–fully;<span class="e2"> tyaktum</span>–renounce;<span class="e2"> karmāṇi</span>–actions; <span class="e2">tu</span>–however;<span class="e2"> abhidhīyate</span>–it is said; <span class="e2">iti</span>–that;<span class="e2"> yaḥ saḥ karma-phala-tyāgī</span>–one who renounces the fruits of action; <span class="e2">tyāgī</span>–is a renunciate. [11]
11 It is not possible for the embodied soul to fully renounce actions. However, one who renounces the fruits of his actions is a true renunciate.
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रञ्च त्रिविधं कर्म्मणः फलम् ।<br />भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु सन्न्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥१२॥
aniṣṭam iṣṭaṁ miśrañ cha tri-vidhaṁ karmaṇaḥ phalam<br />bhavaty atyāgināṁ pretya na tu sannyāsināṁ kvachit [12]
<span class="e2">tri-vidham phalam </span>(<span class="e2">iti</span>)–These three kinds of fruits;<span class="e2"> karmaṇaḥ</span>–of action;<span class="e2"> bhavati</span>–remain; <span class="e2">pretya</span>–after death;<span class="e2"> atyāginām</span>–for those who desire material enjoyment:<span class="e2"> aniṣṭam</span>–undesirable (low or hellish birth); <span class="e2">iṣṭam</span>–desirable (high or godly birth);<span class="e2"> miśram cha</span>–and mixed (human birth); <span class="e2">tu</span>–but; <span class="e2">na </span>(<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–these fruits do not ensue;<span class="e2"> kvachit</span>–at any time;<span class="e2"> sannyāsinām</span>–for those who are sannyāsī, renounced. [12]
12 After death, the three kinds of fruits of actions—good, bad, and mixed—accrue to those who have worldly desires, but never to those who are renounced.
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे ।<br />साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्व्वकर्म्मणाम् ॥१३॥
pañchaitāni mahā-bāho kāraṇāni nibodha me<br />sāṅkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarva-karmaṇām [13]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> mahā-bāho</span>–O mighty hero;<span class="e2"> nibodha</span>–know; <span class="e2">me</span>–from Me; <span class="e2">etāni</span>–these; <span class="e2">pañcha</span>–five;<span class="e2"> kāraṇāni</span>–causes;<span class="e2"> siddhaye</span>–of the accomplishment;<span class="e2"> sarva-karmaṇām</span>–of all actions;<span class="e2"> proktāni</span>–described;<span class="e2"> kṛtānte</span>–in the conclusive knowledge of action;<span class="e2"> sāṅkhye</span>–in the Vedānta scripture. [13]
13 O mighty hero, know from Me of the five causes of the accomplishment of all actions as described in the conclusive teachings of the scripture known as Sāṅkhya or Vedānta:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्त्ता करणञ्च पृथग्विधम् ।<br />विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवञ्चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥१४॥
adhiṣṭhānaṁ tathā kartā karaṇañ cha pṛthag-vidham<br />vividhāś cha pṛthak cheṣṭā daivañ chaivātra pañchamam [14]
<span class="e2">adhiṣṭānam</span>–(1) The basis, the body; <span class="e2">tathā</span>–and; <span class="e2">kartā</span>–(2) the ‘doer’, the ego of the knot of spirit and matter;<span class="e2"> pṛthak-vidham</span>–(3) the separate, various;<span class="e2"> karaṇam cha</span>–senses—eyes, ears, etc., as the instrument;<span class="e2"> vividhāḥ</span>–(4) the various;<span class="e2"> pṛthak cha</span>–and separate; <span class="e2">cheṣṭā</span>–endeavours or functions of the vital airs;<span class="e2"> atra pañchamam</span>–and the fifth factor;<span class="e2"> daivam eva cha</span>–(5) is the Divine, the Supersoul. [14]
14 (All actions are accomplished by these five causes:) The body, the performer (ego, a knot of spirit and matter), the instrument (the senses), the various endeavours, and the Divine (the Supersoul).
शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म्म प्रारभते नरः ।<br />न्यायं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥१५॥
śarīra-vāṅmanobhir yat karma prārabhate naraḥ<br />nyāyaṁ vā viparītaṁ vā pañchaite tasya hetavaḥ [15]
<span class="e2">yat karma</span>–Whatever action; <span class="e2">naraḥ</span>–a man;<span class="e2"> prārabhate</span>–performs;<span class="e2"> sarīra-vāk-manobhiḥ</span>–with his body, speech, and mind;<span class="e2"> nyāyam vā</span>–whether lawful;<span class="e2"> viparītam vā</span>–or unlawful;<span class="e2"> ete pañcha</span>–these five; <span class="e2">tasya</span>–are its;<span class="e2"> hetavaḥ</span>–causes. [15]
15 Whether lawful of unlawful, whatever action a man performs with his body, mind, or speech, is caused by these five elements.
तत्रैवं सति कर्त्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।<br />पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्म्मतिः ॥१६॥
tatraivaṁ sati kartāram ātmānaṁ kevalaṁ tu yaḥ<br />paśyaty akṛta-buddhitvān na sa paśyati durmatiḥ [16]
<span class="e2">tatra</span>–In this respect;<span class="e2"> evam sati tu</span>–despite this; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–whoever;<span class="e2"> paśyati</span>–sees;<span class="e2"> kevalam</span>–only;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–the living being;<span class="e2"> kartāram</span>–as the doer;<span class="e2"> saḥ durmatiḥ</span>–that ignorant person;<span class="e2"> akṛta-buddhitvāt</span>–due to impure intelligence;<span class="e2"> na paśyati</span>–does not see. [16]
16 But an ignorant person who sees only himself as the doer does not actually see, due to his impure intelligence.
यस्य नाहङ्कृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।<br />हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥१७॥
yasya nāhaṅkṛto bhāvo buddhir yasya na lipyate<br />hatvāpi sa imā̐l lokān na hanti na nibadhyate [17]
<span class="e2">yasya</span>–He within whom; <span class="e2">bhāvaḥ</span>–the mentality;<span class="e2"> ahaṅkṛtaḥ</span>–of considering oneself a doer; <span class="e2">na</span>–does not occur; <span class="e2">yasya</span>–and he whose;<span class="e2"> buddhiḥ</span>–intelligence;<span class="e2"> na lipyate</span>–is not attached to the fruits of actions; <span class="e2">saḥ</span>–such a person;<span class="e2"> hatvā api</span>–even if he kills;<span class="e2"> imān lokān</span>–the entire world;<span class="e2"> na hanti</span>–he neither kills anyone;<span class="e2"> na nibadhyate</span>–nor is he bound by action. [17]
17 He who is free from egoism (aversion to the Absolute), and whose intelligence is not implicated in worldly action—even if he kills the entire world, he neither kills nor is he bound by action.
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्म्मचोदना ।<br />करणं कर्म्म कर्त्तेति त्रिविधः कर्म्मसन्ग्रहः ॥१८॥
jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ parijñātā tri-vidhā karma-chodanā<br />karaṇaṁ karma karteti tri-vidhaḥ karma-saṅgrahaḥ [18]
<span class="e2">tri-vidhā iti</span>–These three are;<span class="e2"> karma-chodanā</span>–the driving force of action: <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge; <span class="e2">jñeyam</span>–the knowable;<span class="e2"> parijñātā</span>–the knower. <span class="e2">tri-vidhaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">iti</span>)–These three are;<span class="e2"> karma-saṅgrahaḥ</span>–the constitution of action:<span class="e2"> karaṇam</span>–the instrument, the senses; or the practice to attain the objective (sādhana); <span class="e2">karma</span>–the action; <span class="e2">kartā</span>–the performer. [18]
18 These three are the driving force of action: knowledge, the knowable, and the knower. These three are the constitution of action—the instrument, the action, and the performer.
ज्ञानं कर्म्म च कर्त्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।<br />प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥१९॥
jñānaṁ karma cha kartā cha tridhaiva guṇa-bhedataḥ<br />prochyate guṇa-saṅkhyāne yathāvach chhṛṇu tāny api [19]
<span class="e2">guṇa-saṅkhyāne</span>–In the sāṅkhya scripture; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–knowledge;<span class="e2"> karma cha</span>–action;<span class="e2"> kartā cha</span>–and the performer; (ete)<span class="e2"> prochyate</span>–are mentioned;<span class="e2"> tri-dhā eva</span>–in three divisions;<span class="e2"> guṇa-bhedataḥ</span>–according to the three modes of material nature. <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–now hear;<span class="e2"> tāni api</span>–of these, too;<span class="e2"> yathāvat</span>–as it is. [19]
19 In the sāṅkhya scripture, knowledge, action, and the performer have each been classified according to the three modes of material nature. Now hear of these from Me:
सर्व्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते ।<br />अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥२०॥
sarva-bhūteṣu yenaikaṁ bhāvam avyayam īkṣate<br />avibhaktaṁ vibhakteṣu taj jñānaṁ viddhi sāttvikam [20]
<span class="e2">viddhi</span>–You should know;<span class="e2"> tat jñānam</span>–that knowledge; <span class="e2">yena</span>–by which; <span class="e2">ekam</span>–one;<span class="e2"> avibhaktam</span>–undivided;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–imperishable; <span class="e2">bhāvam</span>–nature; <span class="e2">īkṣate</span>–is seen;<span class="e2"> vibhakteṣu sarva-bhūteṣu</span>–within all the diverse living beings;<span class="e2"> sāttvikam</span>–as knowledge of the nature of goodness. [20]
20 That knowledge by which the one imperishable and undivided principle (My superior divine potency) is seen to be present in all the diverse living beings is to be known as knowledge of the nature of goodness.
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् ।<br />वेत्ति सर्व्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥२१॥
