pṛthaktvena tu yaj jñānaṁ nānā-bhāvān-pṛthag-vidhān<br />vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu taj jñānaṁ viddhi rājasam [21]
<span class="e2">yat jñānam</span>–That knowledge by which; <span class="e2">vetti</span>–one experiences;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu</span>–within all;<span class="e2"> bhūteṣu</span>–living beings;<span class="e2"> pṛthaktvena</span>–separately;<span class="e2"> nānā-bhāvān</span>–many natures;<span class="e2"> pṛthak-vidhān</span>–engaged in many pursuits; <span class="e2">viddhi</span>–know;<span class="e2"> tat jñānaṁ tu</span>–that knowledge;<span class="e2"> rājasam</span>–to be of the nature of passion. [21]
21 That knowledge in which one experiences in the plane of living beings many separate (independent) entities engaged in many separate (clashing) pursuits is to be known as knowledge of the nature of passion.
यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्य्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् ।<br />अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पञ्च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥२२॥
yat tu kṛtsnavad ekasmin kārye saktam ahaitukam<br />atattvārthavad alpañ cha tat tāmasam udāhṛtam [22]
<span class="e2">tat</span>–That; <span class="e2">yat tu</span>–which; <span class="e2">saktam</span>–is attached;<span class="e2"> ekasmin kārye</span>–to the peripheral only, such as the body;<span class="e2"> kṛtsnavat</span>–as everything;<span class="e2"> ahaitukam</span>–(and which is) irrational;<span class="e2"> atattva-arthavat</span>–not seeking the truth—without spiritual or scriptural conception;<span class="e2"> alpam cha</span>–and trivial;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtam</span>–is said to be;<span class="e2"> tāmasam</span>–knowledge of the nature of ignorance. [22]
22 And that ideology which is stubbornly attached to the peripheral only, considering it to be all-in-all, without spiritual or scriptural conception, without seeking the truth, and based on trivialities alone, is said to be knowledge of the (animalistic) nature of ignorance.
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् <br />अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥२३॥
niyataṁ saṅga-rahitam arāga-dveṣataḥ kṛtam<br />aphala-prepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam uchyate [23]
<span class="e2">tat karma yat</span>–That action which is;<span class="e2"> niyatam</span>–constantly; <span class="e2">kṛtam</span>–performed;<span class="e2"> saṅga-rahitam</span>–without attachment;<span class="e2"> aphala-prepsunā</span>–by a person without fruitive desire;<span class="e2"> arāga-dveṣataḥ</span>–unbiased by likes and dislikes;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> sāttvikam</span>–action of the nature of goodness. [23]
23 That obligatory action which is faithfully executed without attachment by a person who does not seek its rewards and who is unbiased by likes and dislikes, is said to be action of the nature of goodness.
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः ।<br />क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥२४॥
yat tu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ<br />kriyate bahulāyāsaṁ tad rājasam udāhṛtam [24]
<span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–Again;<span class="e2"> tat karma yat tu</span>–that action which is;<span class="e2"> kriyate</span>–performed;<span class="e2"> kāma-īpsunā</span>–by one desiring the result; <span class="e2">vā</span>–or;<span class="e2"> sa-ahaṅkāreṇa</span>–by an egotistic person;<span class="e2"> bahula-āyāsam</span>–with great endeavour;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtam</span>–is said to be;<span class="e2"> rājasam</span>–of the nature of passion. [24]
24 And that action which is performed with great endeavour by an egotistic person desiring its fruits, is said to be action of the nature of passion.
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् ।<br />मोहादारभ्यते कर्म्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥२५॥
anubandhaṁ kṣayaṁ hiṁsām anapekṣya cha pauruṣam<br />mohād ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam uchyate [25]
<span class="e2">tat karma yat</span>–That action which;<span class="e2"> ārabhyate</span>–is undertaken; <span class="e2">mohāt</span>–due to delusion;<span class="e2"> anapekṣya</span>–without considering;<span class="e2"> anubandham</span>–consequence; <span class="e2">kṣayam</span>–loss; <span class="e2">hiṁsām</span>–harm to others;<span class="e2"> pauruṣam cha</span>–and one’s capability of performing it;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> tāmasam</span>–action of the nature of ignorance. [25]
25 And that work which is undertaken out of delusion, without consideration for its consequences, its loss, harm to others, and one’s capability of performing it, is called action of the nature of ignorance.
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः ।<br />सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्व्विकारः कर्त्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥२६॥
mukta-saṅgo ’nahaṁvādī dhṛty-utsāha-samanvitaḥ<br />siddhy-asiddhyor nirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika uchyate [26]
<span class="e2">mukta-saṅgaḥ</span>–Unattached;<span class="e2"> anaham-vādi</span>–without ego;<span class="e2"> dhṛti-utsāha-samanvitaḥ</span>–patient, enthusiastic; <span class="e2">kartā</span>–the worker;<span class="e2"> nirvikāraḥ</span>–who is unaffected;<span class="e2"> siddhi-asiddhyoḥ</span>–in success or failure;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> sāttvikaḥ</span>–a worker of the nature of goodness. [26]
26 The worker who is unattached, without ego, patient, enthusiastic, and unaffected in success or failure, is known as a worker of the nature of goodness.
रागी कर्म्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः ।<br />हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्त्ता राजसः परिकीर्त्तितः ॥२७॥
rāgī karma-phala-prepsur lubdho hiṁsātmako ’śuchiḥ<br />harṣa-śokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ [27]
<span class="e2">rāgī</span>–The attached;<span class="e2"> karma-phala-prepsuḥ</span>–desirer of the fruits of action;<span class="e2"> lubdhaḥ</span>–covetous;<span class="e2"> hiṁsā-ātmakaḥ</span>–cruel-natured; <span class="e2">kartā</span>–worker;<span class="e2"> aśuchiḥ</span>–engaged in unscriptural or abominable practices;<span class="e2"> harṣa-śoka-anvitaḥ</span>–and always subject to joy and sorrow;<span class="e2"> parikīrtitaḥ</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> rājasaḥ</span>–a worker of the nature of passion. [27]
27 The worker who is attached, desirous of the fruits of action, covetous, cruel, engaged in abominable practices not sanctioned by the scriptures, and always subject to joy and sorrow, is known as a worker of the nature of passion.
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः ।<br />विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्त्ता तामस उच्यते ॥२८॥
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko ’lasaḥ<br />viṣādī dīrgha-sūtrī cha kartā tāmasa uchyate [28]
<span class="e2">ayuktaḥ</span>–The uncontrolled;<span class="e2"> prākṛtaḥ</span>–vulgar;<span class="e2"> stabdhaḥ</span>–stubbornly arrogant; <span class="e2">śaṭhaḥ</span>–deceitful;<span class="e2"> naiṣkṛtikaḥ</span>–offensive; <span class="e2">alasaḥ</span>–lazy; <span class="e2">viṣādī</span>–despondent;<span class="e2"> dīrgha-sūtrī cha</span>–procrastinating; <span class="e2">kartā</span>–worker;<span class="e2"> uchyate</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> tāmasaḥ</span>–a worker of the nature of ignorance. [28]
28 The worker who is uncontrolled, vulgar, arrogant, deceitful, offensive, lazy, despondent, and a procrastinator is known as a worker of the nature of ignorance.
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु ।<br />प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥२९॥
buddher bhedaṁ dhṛteś chaiva guṇatas tri-vidhaṁ śṛṇu<br />prochyamānam aśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanañjaya [29]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dhanañjaya</span>–O Arjuna; <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–hear;<span class="e2"> prochyamānam</span>–as I describe;<span class="e2"> aśeṣeṇa</span>–fully;<span class="e2"> pṛthaktvena</span>–and distinctly;<span class="e2"> tri-vidham bhedam</span>–the three types;<span class="e2"> buddheḥ</span>–of intelligence;<span class="e2"> dhṛteḥ cha eva</span>–and determination;<span class="e2"> guṇataḥ</span>–according to the modes of nature. [29]
29 O Dhanañjaya, now listen attentively. I shall clearly describe the three types of intelligence and determination, according to the modes of nature:
प्रवृत्तिञ्च निवृत्तिञ्च कार्य्याकार्य्ये भयाभये ।<br />बन्धं मोक्षञ्च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥३०॥
pravṛttiñ cha nivṛttiñ cha kāryākārye bhayābhaye<br />bandhaṁ mokṣañ cha yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī [30]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> sāttvikī buddhiḥ</span>–intelligence of the nature of goodness; <span class="e2">sā yā</span>–is that which; <span class="e2">vetti</span>–distinguishes;<span class="e2"> pravṛttim cha</span>–virtuous engagement;<span class="e2"> nivṛttim cha</span>–and abstinence from vice;<span class="e2"> kārya-akārye</span>–duty and non-duty;<span class="e2"> bhaya-abhaye</span>–danger and safety;<span class="e2"> bandham mokṣam cha</span>–and bondage and liberation. [30]
30 O Pārtha, intelligence of the nature of goodness is that which can distinguish (virtuous) engagement and abstinence (from vice), duty and non-duty, danger and safety, and bondage and liberation.
यया धर्म्ममधर्म्मञ्च कार्य्यञ्चाकार्य्यमेव च ।<br />अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥३१॥
yayā dharmam adharmañ cha kāryañ chākāryam eva cha<br />ayathāvat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī [31]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha;<span class="e2"> rājasī buddhiḥ</span>–intelligence of the nature of passion; <span class="e2">sā yayā</span>–is that by which;<span class="e2"> dharmam</span>–religion;<span class="e2"> adharmam cha</span>–and irreligion;<span class="e2"> kāryam cha</span>–and duty;<span class="e2"> akāryam eva cha</span>–and non-duty;<span class="e2"> prajānāti ayathāvat</span>–are misunderstood. [31]
31 O Pārtha, intelligence of the nature of passion is that which causes an erroneous perception of religion, irreligion, duty, and non-duty.
अधर्म्मं धर्म्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता ।<br />सर्व्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥३२॥
adharmaṁ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā<br />sarvārthān viparītāṁś cha buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī [32]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha;<span class="e2"> tāmasī buddhiḥ</span>–intelligence of the nature of ignorance; <span class="e2">āvṛtā</span>–covered; <span class="e2">tamasā</span>–by the mode of ignorance; <span class="e2">sā yā</span>–is that which;<span class="e2"> manyate</span>–considers;<span class="e2"> adharmam</span>–vice;<span class="e2"> dharmam</span>–virtue;<span class="e2"> sarva-arthān cha</span>–and all knowable objects;<span class="e2"> viparītān iti</span>–contrary to what they are. [32]
32 Intelligence of the nature of ignorance is covered by illusion, whereby vice is considered virtue, and everything is taken to be the opposite of the reality.
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः ।<br />योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥३३॥
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥ-prāṇendriya-kriyāḥ<br />yogenāvyabhichāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī [33]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O Pārtha;<span class="e2"> yayā avyabhichāriṇyā dhṛtyā</span>–that unwavering determination which; <span class="e2">yogena</span>–with single-minded concentration;<span class="e2"> dhārayate</span>–controls;<span class="e2"> manaḥ-prāṇa-indriya-kriyāḥ</span>–the functions of the mind, life forces, and senses;<span class="e2"> sā dhṛtiḥ sāttvikī</span>–is determination of the nature of goodness. [33]
33 O Pārtha, determination of the nature of goodness is that determination which unfailingly and with single-minded concentration controls the functions of the mind, the life-airs, and the senses.
यया तु धर्म्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्ज्जुन ।<br />प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥३४॥
yayā tu dharma-kāmārthān dhṛtyā dhārayate ’rjuna<br />prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī [34]
<span class="e2">tu</span>–But; (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> pārtha arjuna</span>–O Pārtha, Arjuna;<span class="e2"> yayā dhṛtyā</span>–determination by which;<span class="e2"> dharma-kāma-arthān</span>–religiosity, desire, and wealth;<span class="e2"> dhārayate</span>–are held; (<span class="e2">prādhānyena</span>)–foremost;<span class="e2"> prasaṅgena</span>–by the contact of which; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–one becomes;<span class="e2"> phala-ākāṅkṣī</span>–desirous of their fruits;<span class="e2"> sā dhṛtiḥ</span>–that determination; <span class="e2">rājasī</span>–is of the nature of passion. [34]
34 O Pārtha, O Arjuna, determination of the nature of passion is that fruitive, attached determination which adheres to religiosity for the purpose of amassing wealth to fulfill mundane desires.
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।<br />न विमुञ्चति दुर्म्मेधा धृतिः सा तामसी मता ॥३५॥
yayā svapnaṁ bhayaṁ śokaṁ viṣādaṁ madam eva cha<br />na vimuñchati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā tāmasī matā [35]
<span class="e2">sā dhṛtiḥ</span>–That determination; <span class="e2">yayā</span>–by which;<span class="e2"> durmedhāḥ</span>–a foolish person;<span class="e2"> na vimuñchati</span>–never leaves;<span class="e2"> svapnam</span>–sleep; <span class="e2">bhayam</span>–fear; <span class="e2">śokam</span>–sorrow;<span class="e2"> viṣādam</span>–depression;<span class="e2"> madam eva cha</span>–pride, arrogance; <span class="e2">matā</span>–is considered; <span class="e2">tāmasī</span>–determination of the nature of ignorance. [35]
35 Determination of the nature of ignorance is that by which a foolish person does not give up sleep, fear, sorrow, depression, and arrogance.
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।<br />अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तञ्च निगच्छति ॥३६।
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।<br />तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥३७॥
sukhaṁ tv idānīṁ tri-vidhaṁ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha<br />abhyāsād ramate yatra duḥkhāntañ cha nigachchhati [36]
yat tad agre viṣam iva pariṇāme ’mṛtopamam<br />tat sukhaṁ sāttvikaṁ proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam [37]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bharatarṣabha</span>–O best of the Bhāratas;<span class="e2"> idānīm tu</span>–now; <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–hear; <span class="e2">me</span>–from Me;<span class="e2"> tri-vidham sukham</span>–about the three kinds of happiness: <span class="e2">yatra</span>–that in which; <span class="e2">ramate</span>–one delights;<span class="e2"> abhyāsāt</span>–through his practices;<span class="e2"> nigachchhati cha</span>–and attains;<span class="e2"> duḥkha-antam</span>–the cessation of unhappiness; <span class="e2">yat tat</span>–and that which; <span class="e2">agre</span>–initially;<span class="e2"> viṣam iva</span>–is like poison;<span class="e2"> pariṇāme</span>–and subsequently;<span class="e2"> amṛta-upamam</span>–like nectar;<span class="e2"> tat sukham</span>–such happiness;<span class="e2"> ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam</span>–born of the purity of self-realisation;<span class="e2"> proktam</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> sāttvikam</span>–happiness of the nature of goodness. [36–37]
36–37 O Bharatarṣabha, now hear from Me about the three kinds of happiness: That state in which one is joyful through his practices while attaining the cessation of all unhappiness, and which in the beginning is like poison but ultimately like nectar, and which is born of the purity of self-realisation—that happiness is said to be of the nature of goodness.
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् ।<br />परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥३८।
viṣayendriya-saṁyogād yat tad agre ’mṛtopamam<br />pariṇāme viṣam iva tat sukhaṁ rājasaṁ smṛtam [38]
<span class="e2">tat yat</span>–That which; (<span class="e2">jāyate</span>)–is born;<span class="e2"> viṣaya-indriya-saṁyogāt</span>–from the contact of the senses with their objects; <span class="e2">agre</span>–and in the beginning;<span class="e2"> amṛta-upamam</span>–is like nectar;<span class="e2"> pariṇāme</span>–and subsequently;<span class="e2"> viṣam iva</span>–like poison;<span class="e2"> tat sukham</span>–that happiness; <span class="e2">smṛtam</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> rājasam</span>–happiness of the nature of passion. [38]
38 That happiness which is born of the contact of the senses with their objects, and which is like nectar in the beginning but poison in the end, is said to be happiness of the nature of passion.
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः ।<br />निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥३९॥
yad agre chānubandhe cha sukhaṁ mohanam ātmanaḥ<br />nidrālasya-pramādotthaṁ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam [39]
<span class="e2">nidrā-ālasya-pramāda-uttham</span>–Born of sleep, laziness, and illusion;<span class="e2"> yat sukham</span>–that happiness which;<span class="e2"> agre cha</span>–in the beginning;<span class="e2"> anubandhe cha</span>–and in the end;<span class="e2"> ātmanaḥ mohanam</span>–is self-deception; <span class="e2">tat</span>–such happiness;<span class="e2"> udāhṛtam</span>–is called;<span class="e2"> tāmasam</span>–happiness of the nature of ignorance. [39]
39 That happiness which is self-deception from beginning to end, and which arises from sleep, laziness, and illusion, is called happiness of the nature of ignorance.
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।<br />सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः ॥४०॥
na tad asti pṛthivyāṁ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ<br />sattvaṁ prakṛti-jair muktaṁ yad ebhiḥ syāt tribhir guṇaiḥ [40]
<span class="e2">pṛthivyām vā</span>–Either on earth; (<span class="e2">manuṣyādiṣu</span>)–amongst the humans, etc.;<span class="e2"> vā punaḥ</span>–or again; <span class="e2">divi</span>–in the heavenly plane; <span class="e2">deveṣu</span>–amongst the demigods; <span class="e2">na asti</span>–there is no;<span class="e2"> tat sattvam</span>–such entity; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which;<span class="e2"> muktam syāt</span>–can be free;<span class="e2"> ebhiḥ tribhiḥ guṇaiḥ</span>–from these three modes;<span class="e2"> prakṛti-jaiḥ</span>–born of material nature. [40]
40 Amongst all species on earth including the humans or amongst even the celestial gods in the heavenly plane, there is no entity that can be free from these three modes which are born of material nature.
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणाञ्च परन्तप ।<br />कर्म्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुनैः ॥४१॥
brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśāṁ śūdrāṇāñ cha parantapa<br />karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāva-prabhavair gunaiḥ [41]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> parantapa</span>–O vanquisher of the enemy;<span class="e2"> karmāṇi</span>–the duties;<span class="e2"> brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśām</span>–of the brāhmaṇ, kṣatriya, and vaiśya;<span class="e2"> śūdrāṇām cha</span>–and śūdra sections;<span class="e2"> pravibhaktāni</span>–are appropriately classified; <span class="e2">guṇaiḥ</span>–according to the qualities of goodness, passion, and ignorance;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-prabhavaiḥ</span>–born of their natures. [41]
41 O Parantapa, according to their natures, the duties of the brāhmaṇs, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras are appropriately classified.
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्ज्जवमेव च ।<br />ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म्म स्वभावजम् ॥४२॥
śamo damas tapaḥ śauchaṁ kṣāntir ārjavam eva cha<br />jñānaṁ vijñānam āstikyaṁ brahma-karma svabhāva-jam [42]
(<span class="e2">etāni</span>)–All these; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–are;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-jam</span>–the natural;<span class="e2"> brahma-karma</span>–duties of the brāhmaṇs: <span class="e2">śamaḥ</span>–internal sense-control; <span class="e2">damaḥ</span>–external sense-control; <span class="e2">tapaḥ</span>–austerity;<span class="e2"> śaucham</span>–external and internal purity;<span class="e2"> kṣāntiḥ</span>–forbearance;<span class="e2"> ārjavam eva cha</span>–straightforwardness; <span class="e2">jñānam</span>–scriptural knowledge;<span class="e2"> vijñānam</span>–realisation of essential truth;<span class="e2"> āstikyam</span>–theistic mentality or firm faith in the teachings of the scriptures. [42]
42 Internal and external sense-control, austerity, purity, forbearance, straightforwardness, knowledge, realisation, and theistic mentality—these are the natural duties of the brāhmaṇs.
शौर्य्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।<br />दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म्म स्वभावजम् ॥४३॥
śauryaṁ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṁ yuddhe chāpy apalāyanam<br />dānam īśvara-bhāvaś cha kṣātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam [43]
(<span class="e2">etāni</span>)–All these; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–are;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-jam</span>–the natural;<span class="e2"> kṣātram karma</span>–duties of the kṣatriyas:<span class="e2"> śauryam</span>–prowess; <span class="e2">tejaḥ</span>–valour; <span class="e2">dhṛtiḥ</span>–endurance;<span class="e2"> dākṣyaṁ</span>–dexterity;<span class="e2"> apalāyanam</span>–never retreating;<span class="e2"> yuddhe cha api</span>–in battle; <span class="e2">dānam</span>–generosity;<span class="e2"> īśvara-bhāvaḥ cha</span>–and regality. [43]
43 Prowess, valour, endurance, dexterity, never retreating in battle, generosity, and regality—these are the characteristic duties of the kṣatriyas.
कृषिगोरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म्म स्वभावजम् ।<br />परिचर्य्यात्मकं कर्म्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥४४॥
kṛṣi-gorakṣya-vāṇijyaṁ vaiśya-karma svabhāva-jam<br />paricharyātmakaṁ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāva-jam [44]
(<span class="e2">etāni</span>)–All these; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–are;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-jam</span>–the natural;<span class="e2"> vaiśya-karma</span>–functions of the vaiśyas:<span class="e2"> kṛṣi-go-rakṣya-vāṇijyaṁ</span>–agriculture, cow protection, and trade.<span class="e2"> karma api</span>–The duty;<span class="e2"> paricharyā-ātmakam</span>–of service to the brāhmaṇs, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-jam</span>–is natural;<span class="e2"> śūdrasya</span>–for the śūdra section. [44]
44 Agriculture, cow protection, and trade are the natural work of the vaiśyas; and natural to the śūdras is service to the brāhmaṇs, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas (assisting them in their various works).
स्वे स्वे कर्म्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।<br />स्वकर्म्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥४५॥
sve sve karmaṇy abhirataḥ saṁsiddhiṁ labhate naraḥ<br />svakarma-nirataḥ siddhiṁ yathā vindati tach chhṛṇu [45]
<span class="e2">naraḥ</span>–The man;<span class="e2"> abhirataḥ</span>–devoted;<span class="e2"> sve sve karmaṇi</span>–to his own appropriate duty;<span class="e2"> labhate</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> saṁsiddhim</span>–perfection in self-knowledge.<span class="e2"> śṛṇu tat</span>–Now hear; <span class="e2">yathā</span>–how;<span class="e2"> svakarma-nirataḥ</span>–one dedicated to executing his prescribed duty;<span class="e2"> vindati</span>– attains;<span class="e2"> siddhim</span>–perfection. [45]
45 One who devotes himself to his own duty attains perfection in self-knowledge. Now hear from Me how a person attains perfection through devotion to his own duty:
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्व्वमिदं ततम् ।<br />स्वकर्म्मणा तमभ्यर्च्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥४६॥
yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṁ yena sarvam idaṁ tatam<br />svakarmaṇā tam abhyarchya siddhiṁ vindati mānavaḥ [46]
<span class="e2">mānavaḥ</span>–A man;<span class="e2"> vindati</span>–attains;<span class="e2"> siddhim</span>–perfection;<span class="e2"> abhyarchya</span>–by worshipping;<span class="e2"> svakarmaṇā</span>–through his appropriate, prescribed duty; <span class="e2">tam</span>–that Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">yataḥ</span>–from whom occurs;<span class="e2"> pravṛttiḥ</span>–the manifestation or impetus;<span class="e2"> bhūtānām</span>–of all living beings; <span class="e2">yena</span>–and by whom, individually and collectively; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this; <span class="e2">sarvam</span>–entire universe; <span class="e2">tatam</span>–is pervaded. [46]
46 A man achieves perfection by worshipping, through his prescribed duties, the Supreme Lord from whom all beings originate, by whom all beings are engaged, and who (individually and collectively) pervades the entire universe.
श्रेयान्स्वधर्म्मो विगुणः परधर्म्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।<br />स्वभावनियतं कर्म्म कुर्व्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥४७॥
śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt<br />svabhāva-niyataṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam [47]
<span class="e2">svadharmaḥ</span>–One’s own prescribed duty;<span class="e2"> viguṇaḥ</span>–though imperfect; <span class="e2">śreyān</span>–is better;<span class="e2"> para-dharmāt</span>–than another’s duties;<span class="e2"> su-anuṣṭhitāt</span>–executed well. <span class="e2">kurvan</span>–By doing; <span class="e2">karma</span>–the duty;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-niyatam</span>–prescribed according to his nature; (<span class="e2">mānavaḥ</span>)–a man;<span class="e2"> kilbiṣam na āpnoti</span>–does not incur sin. [47]
47 One’s own duty, though imperfect, is better than another’s executed well. Sin is never incurred by a man fulfilling the duty prescribed according to his nature.
सहजं कर्म्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।<br />सर्व्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥४८॥
saha-jaṁ karma kaunteya sa-doṣam api na tyajet<br />sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnir ivāvṛtāḥ [48]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> sa-doṣam api</span>–although imperfect; <span class="e2">karma</span>–action;<span class="e2"> saha-jam</span>–prescribed according to one’s nature;<span class="e2"> na tyajet</span>–must not be given up; <span class="e2">hi</span>–for;<span class="e2"> sarva-ārambhāḥ</span>–all undertakings; <span class="e2">āvṛtāḥ</span>–are covered; <span class="e2">doṣeṇa</span>–by defects;<span class="e2"> agniḥ iva</span>–as fire is covered;<span class="e2"> dhūmena</span>–by smoke. [48]
48 O Kaunteya, even though it may be imperfect, one should not give up the duty prescribed according to his nature. Verily, all action (karma) is (generally) covered by imperfection, as fire is covered by smoke.
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्व्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः।<br />नैष्कर्म्म्यसिद्धिं परमां सन्न्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥४९॥
asakta-buddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigata-spṛhaḥ<br />naiṣkarmya-siddhiṁ paramāṁ sannyāsenādhigachchhati [49]
<span class="e2">asakta-buddhiḥ</span>–One with the wisdom of detachment;<span class="e2"> sarvatra</span>–from all mundane objects;<span class="e2"> jita-ātmā</span>–the self-controlled;<span class="e2"> vigata-spṛhaḥ</span>–person whose desires have gone;<span class="e2"> adhigachchhati</span>–attains to;<span class="e2"> paramām naiṣkarmya-siddhim</span>–the higher state, of transcending all duties;<span class="e2"> sannyāsena</span>–by renouncing the fruits of his actions. [49]
49 One who has the wisdom of detachment from all mundane objects, who is self-controlled, and whose desires have gone—such a person attains the perfection of transcending all duties in the world by renouncing the fruits of his actions.
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे ।<br />समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥५०॥
siddhiṁ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me<br />samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā [50]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">yathā</span>–how;<span class="e2"> siddhim prāptaḥ</span>–the person who has achieved the state of transcending all duties; <span class="e2">āpnoti</span>–attains to; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–Brahma, the Absolute;<span class="e2"> yā parā niṣṭhā</span>–the ultimate state;<span class="e2"> jñānasya</span>–of knowledge;<span class="e2"> tathā nibodha</span>–now understand that;<span class="e2"> samāsena eva</span>–in brief; <span class="e2">me</span>–from Me. [50]
50 O Kaunteya, now know from Me in brief how the person who has attained transcendence of all duties reaches the transcendental plane of the Absolute, the ultimate state of knowledge (spiritual awakening):
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च ।<br />शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥५१॥
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।<br />ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥५२॥
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।<br />विमुच्य निर्म्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥५३॥
buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṁ niyamya cha<br />śabdādīn viṣayāṁs tyaktvā rāga-dveṣau vyudasya cha [51]
vivikta-sevī laghv-āśī yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ<br />dhyāna-yoga-paro nityaṁ vairāgyaṁ samupāśritaḥ [52]
ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ parigraham<br />vimuchya nirmamaḥ śānto brahma-bhūyāya kalpate [53]
<span class="e2">yuktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–A person possessing;<span class="e2"> viśuddhayā buddhyā</span>–intelligence of the nature of goodness;<span class="e2"> niyamya cha</span>–and controlling;<span class="e2"> ātmānam</span>–the mind; <span class="e2">dhṛtyā</span>–through determination of the nature of goodness;<span class="e2"> tyaktvā</span>–rejecting;<span class="e2"> viṣayān</span>–the sense objects;<span class="e2"> śabdādīn</span>–of sound, touch, etc.;<span class="e2"> vyudasya cha</span>–abandoning;<span class="e2"> rāga-dveṣau</span>–attachment and aversion—likes and dislikes;<span class="e2"> vivikta-sevī</span>–remaining free from the association of materialistic persons;<span class="e2"> laghu-āśī</span>–a temperate eater;<span class="e2"> yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ</span>–disciplining the body, mind, and speech; <span class="e2">nityam</span>–and constantly;<span class="e2"> dhyāna-yoga-paraḥ</span>–absorbed in meditation on the Supreme Lord;<span class="e2"> vairāgyam samupāśritah</span>–fully detached from the mundane;<span class="e2"> vimuchya</span>–giving up;<span class="e2"> ahaṅkāram</span>–ego—considering oneself ‘the doer’; <span class="e2">balam</span>–power; <span class="e2">darpam</span>–vanity; <span class="e2">kāmam</span>–desire;<span class="e2"> krodham</span>–anger;<span class="e2"> parigraham</span>–possessiveness; <span class="e2">śāntaḥ</span>–being at peace;<span class="e2"> nirmamaḥ</span>–not thinking of anything as ‘mine’;<span class="e2"> kalpate</span>–is qualified;<span class="e2"> brahma-bhūyāya</span>–for spiritual realisation. [51–53].
51–53 Endowed with intelligence of the nature of goodness, mentally controlled through determination of the nature of goodness, rejecting the sense objects of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, abandoning attachment and aversion, free from the association of materialistic persons, a temperate eater, disciplining the body, mind, and speech, constantly absorbed in thought of the Supreme Lord, and fully detached from the mundane world; giving up ego, power, vanity, desire, anger, and possessiveness, not thinking of anything as ‘mine’; being at peace—such a person is qualified for spiritual realisation.
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।<br />समः सर्व्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥५४॥
brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śochati na kāṅkṣati<br />samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām [54]
<span class="e2">prasanna-ātmā</span>–The joyful, enlightened soul;<span class="e2"> brahma-bhūtaḥ</span>–who has attained his divine nature;<span class="e2"> na śochati</span>–neither sorrows;<span class="e2"> na kāṅkṣati</span>–nor desires. <span class="e2">samaḥ</span>–Being of equal vision;<span class="e2"> sarveṣu</span>–for all;<span class="e2"> bhūteṣu</span>–living beings (considering My superior potency to be in everything);<span class="e2"> labhate</span>–he attains; <span class="e2">parām</span>–transcendental;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktim</span>–devotion to Me. [54]
54 The joyful-hearted, enlightened soul who has attained his divine nature neither sorrows nor desires. Seeing all beings equally, he comes to attain transcendental loving devotion to Me.
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः ।<br />ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥५५॥
bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś chāsmi tattvataḥ<br />tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā viśate tad-anantaram [55]
<span class="e2">bhaktyā</span>–Through devotion; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–he;<span class="e2"> abhijānāti</span>–can well know; <span class="e2">mām</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> tattvataḥ</span>–in reality; <span class="e2">yāvān</span>–as far as being the Master of all opulences; <span class="e2">yaḥ cha </span>(<span class="e2">aham</span>)<span class="e2"> asmi</span>–and that which I am. <span class="e2">jñātvā</span>–Thus knowing Me;<span class="e2"> tattvataḥ</span>–in truth; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–he;<span class="e2"> tat-anantaram</span>–thereafter; <span class="e2">tataḥ</span>–by the potency of that devotion; <span class="e2">viśate</span>–enters; <span class="e2">mām</span>–My eternal Pastimes (nitya-līlā), non-different from Me. [55]
55 Through devotion, he realises that I am the Lord of all potencies and the Sweet Absolute. Then, realising his divine relationship with Me, he enters the company of My intimate associates who are non-different from My very self.
सर्व्वकर्म्माण्यपि सदा कुर्व्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः ।<br />मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥५६॥
sarva-karmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo mad-vyapāśrayaḥ<br />mat-prasādād avāpnoti śāśvataṁ padam avyayam [56]
<span class="e2">api</span>–Although; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–ever;<span class="e2"> kurvāṇaḥ</span>–active; <span class="e2">sarva-karmāṇi</span>–in all duties;<span class="e2"> mat-vyapāśrayaḥ</span>–My surrendered souls;<span class="e2"> avāpnoti</span>–attain;<span class="e2"> śāśvataṁ</span>–the eternal;<span class="e2"> avyayam</span>–immutable (flourishing); <span class="e2">padam</span>–plane (of service);<span class="e2"> mat-prasādāt</span>–by My grace. [56]
56 Although ever active in all duties, those who have taken refuge in Me attain, by My grace, the eternal, indestructible plane (of service).
चेतसा सर्व्वकर्म्माणि मयि सन्न्यस्य मत्परः ।<br />बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥५७॥
chetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-paraḥ<br />buddhi-yogam upāśritya mach-chittaḥ satataṁ bhava [57]
<span class="e2">sannyasya</span>–Offering;<span class="e2"> chetasā</span>–whole-heartedly;<span class="e2"> sarva-karmāṇi</span>–all actions; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–to Me;<span class="e2"> mat-paraḥ</span>–keeping Me as the supreme objective;<span class="e2"> upāśritya</span>–and taking refuge;<span class="e2"> buddhi-yogam</span>–in dedicating your intelligence to Me; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–be;<span class="e2"> satatam</span>–ever;<span class="e2"> mat-chittaḥ</span>–devoted to Me. [57]
57 Whole-heartedly offering your every action to Me, keeping Me as the supreme objective and fully dedicating your intelligence to Me (being unattached to worldly action), be ever devoted to Me.
मच्चित्तः सर्व्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।<br />अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥५८॥
mach-chittaḥ sarva-durgāṇi mat-prasādāt tariṣyasi<br />atha chet tvam ahaṅkārān na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi [58]
<span class="e2">mach-chittaḥ</span>–Giving your heart to Me; <span class="e2">tvam</span>–you;<span class="e2"> tariṣyasi</span>–will cross;<span class="e2"> sarva-durgāṇi</span>–all obstacles;<span class="e2"> mat-prasādāt</span>–by My grace.<span class="e2"> atha chet</span>–Yet, if;<span class="e2"> ahaṅkārāt</span>–out of pride;<span class="e2"> na śroṣyasi</span>–you do not heed (My words); (<span class="e2">tarhi</span>)–then;<span class="e2"> vinaṅkṣyasi</span>–you will perish. [58]
58 Giving your heart to Me, you will be able to overcome all obstacles by My grace. But if out of pride you do not heed My words, you will perish.
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।<br />मिथ्यैव व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥५९॥
yad ahaṅkāram āśritya na yotsya iti manyase<br />mithyaiva vyavasāyas te prakṛtis tvāṁ niyokṣyati [59]
<span class="e2">āśritya</span>–Resorting to;<span class="e2"> ahaṅkāram</span>–pride;<span class="e2"> yat manyase iti</span>–you are thinking;<span class="e2"> na yotsya</span>–“I shall not fight”; (<span class="e2">eṣaḥ</span>)–but such;<span class="e2"> vyavasāyaḥ</span>–a decision; <span class="e2">te</span>–of yours; (<span class="e2">bhaviṣyati</span>)–will be;<span class="e2"> mithyā eva</span>–only in vain.<span class="e2"> prakṛtiḥ</span>–The nature befitting a kṣatriya;<span class="e2"> niyokṣyati</span>–will compel; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–you. [59]
59 Out of pride you are thinking, “I shall not fight.” But your decision will be in vain, for your nature (as a kṣatriya) will compel you to fight.
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्म्मणा ।<br />कर्त्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥६०॥
svabhāva-jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā<br />kartuṁ nechchhasi yan mohāt kariṣyasy avaśo ’pi tat [60]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> kaunteya</span>–O son of Kuntī; <span class="e2">nibaddhaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–being bound; <span class="e2">svena</span>–by your;<span class="e2"> karmaṇā</span>–duty;<span class="e2"> svabhāva-jena</span>–born of your nature; <span class="e2">tat api</span>–that very action; <span class="e2">yat</span>–which; <span class="e2">mohāt</span>–out of delusion; (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–you;<span class="e2"> na ichchhasi</span>–do not wish; <span class="e2">kartum</span>–to perform;<span class="e2"> kariṣyasi</span>–you will do; <span class="e2">avaśaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–inevitably. [60]
60 O Kaunteya, being bound by the duty born of your nature, that very action which out of delusion you are now avoiding will be inevitably executed by you.
ईश्वरः सर्व्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्ज्जुन तिष्ठति ।<br />भ्रामयन्सर्व्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥६१॥
īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe ’rjuna tiṣṭhati<br />bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā [61]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">arjuna</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtānām</span>–for all beings;<span class="e2"> īśvaraḥ</span>–the Supreme Lord as the Supersoul;<span class="e2"> tiṣṭhati</span>–is situated;<span class="e2"> hṛd-deśe</span>–in region of the heart. <span class="e2">māyayā</span>–By His illusory potency;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhūtāni bhrāmayan</span>–He causes all beings to revolve (through many existences); <span class="e2">yantra-ārūḍhāni </span>(<span class="e2">iva</span>)–as though riding a carousel. [61]
61 O Arjuna, the Supreme Lord is situated in the hearts of all beings, and by His deluding potency He causes them to revolve (through many existences) like puppets riding a carousel.
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्व्वभावेन भारत ।<br />तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥६२॥
tam eva śaraṇaṁ gachchha sarva-bhāvena bhārata<br />tat prasādāt parāṁ śāntiṁ sthānaṁ prāpsyasi śāśvatam [62]
(<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> bhārata</span>–O Bhārat; (<span class="e2">ataḥ</span>)–therefore;<span class="e2"> saraṇam gachchha</span>–surrender;<span class="e2"> sarva-bhāvena</span>–wholeheartedly; <span class="e2">tam eva</span>–unto Him, alone.<span class="e2"> tat-prasādāt</span>–By His grace;<span class="e2"> prāpsyasi</span>–you will attain; <span class="e2">parām</span>–the supreme; <span class="e2">śāntim</span>–peace;<span class="e2"> śāśvatam</span>–the eternal;<span class="e2"> sthānam</span>–abode. [62]
62 O Bhārat, wholeheartedly surrender to Him. By His grace you will attain the supreme peace and the eternal abode.
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया ।<br />विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥६३॥
iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā<br />vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathechchhasi tathā kuru [63]
<span class="e2">iti</span>–Up to this point; <span class="e2">guhyāt</span>–from profound;<span class="e2"> guhyataram jñānam</span>–to more profound knowledge;<span class="e2"> ākhyātam</span>–has been disclosed; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by Me; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you.<span class="e2"> aśeṣeṇa</span>–Fully;<span class="e2"> vimṛśya</span>–considering; <span class="e2">etat</span>–that; <span class="e2">kuru</span>–do; <span class="e2">yathā</span>–as;<span class="e2"> ichchhasi</span>–you wish; <span class="e2">tathā</span>– accordingly. [63]
63 I have now revealed more and more profound teachings to you. Duly consider this, and then do as you wish.
सर्व्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।<br />इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥६४॥
sarva-guhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṁ vachaḥ<br />iṣṭo ’si me dṛḍham iti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam [64]
<span class="e2">bhūyaḥ</span>–Again; <span class="e2">śṛṇu</span>–hear; <span class="e2">me</span>–My;<span class="e2"> paramam</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">vachaḥ</span>–teaching.<span class="e2"> sarva-guhyatamam</span>–most profound of all. (<span class="e2">tvam</span>)–You; <span class="e2">asi</span>–are; <span class="e2">dṛḍham</span>–extremely; <span class="e2">iṣṭaḥ</span>–dear; <span class="e2">me</span>–to Me;<span class="e2"> iti tataḥ</span>–so;<span class="e2"> vakṣyāmi</span>–I am speaking; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you; <span class="e2">hitam</span>–for your benefit. [64]
64 Now again hear My supreme teaching, the most hidden treasure of all. I tell you this for your benefit as you are most dear to Me.
Commentary
According to Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur (Vidvad-rañjan commentary, 9.1), the wisdom of self-realisation in the second and third chapters of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> are the profound (<span class="e3">guhyam</span>) teachings of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. The Lord’s descriptions of Himself as the Supreme in the seventh and eighth chapters are more profound (<span class="e3">guhyataram</span>), as such knowledge gives birth to devotion. In chapter nine, the most profound (<span class="e3">guhyatamam</span>) teachings begin as the Lord describes the symptoms of exclusive devotion (kevalā-bhakti).
Because His devotee Arjuna is very dear to Him, the Lord now repeats His secret teaching for Arjuna’s benefit. This time, however, He reveals His most hidden of all hidden treasures (<span class="e3">sarva-guhyatamam</span>), His most affectionate advice: “Arjuna, you are most dear to Me, so I will now divulge the whole truth to you.”
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।<br />मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥६५॥
man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru<br />mām evaiṣyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo ’si me [65]
<span class="e2">bhava</span>–Be;<span class="e2"> mat-manāḥ</span>–of mind dedicated to Me;<span class="e2"> mat-bhaktaḥ</span>–devoted to Me;<span class="e2"> mat-yājī</span>–be My worshipper;<span class="e2"> namaskuru</span>–and offer obeisance—offer yourself; <span class="e2">mām</span>–to Me; (<span class="e2">tarhi</span>)–then; <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">eṣyasi</span>–you will come; <span class="e2">mām</span>–to Me. <span class="e2">satyam</span>–Truly;<span class="e2"> pratijāne</span>–I promise this; <span class="e2">te</span>–to you; (<span class="e2">yataḥ tvam</span>)–as you; <span class="e2">asi</span>–are; <span class="e2">priyaḥ</span>–dear; <span class="e2">me</span>–to Me. [65]
65 Think of Me always, devote yourself to Me, worship Me, and bow to Me, and surely you will come to Me. I promise you this, because you are dear to Me.
सर्व्वधर्म्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।<br />अहं त्वां सर्व्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥६६॥
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja<br />ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śuchaḥ [66]
<span class="e2">parityajya</span>–Totally rejecting;<span class="e2"> sarva-dharmān</span>–all kinds of religion;<span class="e2"> śaraṇam vraja</span>–take shelter; <span class="e2">mām</span>–of Me; <span class="e2">ekam</span>–alone. <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> mokṣayiṣyāmi</span>–will liberate; <span class="e2">tvām</span>–you;<span class="e2"> sarva-pāpebhyaḥ</span>–from all kinds of sins.<span class="e2"> mā śuchaḥ</span>–Do not despair. [66]
66 Give up all kinds of religion and surrender to Me alone. I will liberate you from all sins. Do not despair.
Commentary
Here, the glory of the hidden purpose in the <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span> is sung (<span class="e3">Gītā-gūḍhārtha-gauravam</span>): “Give up all engagements and come to Me. You won’t have to repent, Arjuna, because I am everything to you, and you are everything to Me. This is the most hidden of all hidden truths. What more can I say? And you will find this in Vraja.”
There is a literary ornament in Sanskrit called dhvani, echo, by which a word ‘echoes’, suggests, an additional meaning. Here, such a hint is given. <span class="e3">Mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ ‘vraja’</span>*: “You may ‘go’ to ‘Vraja’, and there you will find the most hidden of all hidden truths (<span class="e3">sarva-guhyatamam</span>). The deepest secret of the inner loving heart has been fully revealed there: I am beyond all conceptions of religion, society, friends—everything. My position is above everything, and in the heart of the heart of everything. In the eternal land of Vraja, you will experience the whole conception of beauty. Dismiss all other engagements and prospects, and come to Me alone. Your inner hankering will be fulfilled beyond your expectations. You will find such dignity in Me that you will be beyond reaction and repentance.” This is the deepest meaning of the highest glory.
If one comes to this conception, everything else will be seen as sin (<span class="e3">Ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi</span>). Everything conceived of as duty or purity in this material world will be seen as sinful, and all conceptions of religiosity will be reduced to the level of sin. In the absolute plane, everything and everyone belongs wholly to Kṛṣṇa, and the slightest deviation from this ideal is no better than committing sin. Mere self-forgetfulness leads to impersonalism and culminates in deep slumber. But self-forgetfulness (<span class="e3">sarva-dharmān parityajya</span>) in Kṛṣṇa’s service (<span class="e3">Mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja</span>) is positive and living. It is the full, absolute plane of life.
The hidden treasure attracts our hearts. We have been deprived of our heart’s deepest interest. Though we have a natural claim to it, it has been hidden from us (<span class="e3">śrutibhir vimṛgyām</span>). In an unparalleled way, <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> considers all these aspects and directs us to the correct meaning and conclusion of all the Upaniṣads. From this point, the <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> begins.
*In the verse, <span class="e3">vraja</span> means ‘go’, and <span class="e3">Vraja</span> is also a name of Vṛndāvan.
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।<br />न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥६७॥
idaṁ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadāchana<br />na chāśuśrūṣave vāchyaṁ na cha māṁ yo ’bhyasūyati [67]
<span class="e2">te</span>–You;<span class="e2"> kadāchana na vāchyam</span>–should never disclose; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> atapaskāya</span>–to one devoid of self-sacrifice;<span class="e2"> na abhaktāya</span>–nor to a non-devotee;<span class="e2"> aśuśrūṣave na cha</span>–nor to one who is averse to My service;<span class="e2"> yaḥ na cha</span>–nor to one who;<span class="e2"> abhyasūyati</span>–is resentful; <span class="e2">mām</span>–towards Me. [67]
67 You should never disclose this hidden treasure to one devoid of self-sacrifice, to the non-devotee, to the faithless, to one who is averse to My service, or to one who is resentful towards Me.
य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।<br />भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥६८॥
ya imaṁ paramaṁ guhyaṁ mad-bhakteṣv abhidhāsyati<br />bhaktiṁ mayi parāṁ kṛtvā mām evaiṣyaty asaṁśayaḥ [68]
<span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–One who;<span class="e2"> abhidhāsyati</span>–sings the glories of; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> paramam</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">guhyam</span>–secret;<span class="e2"> mat-bhakteṣu</span>–to My devotees; (<span class="e2">saḥ</span>)–such a person; <span class="e2">kṛtvā</span>–attaining; <span class="e2">parām</span>–transcendental;<span class="e2"> bhaktim</span>–devotion; <span class="e2">mayi</span>–to Me; <span class="e2">eṣyati</span>–will reach; <span class="e2">mām eva</span>–Me;<span class="e2"> asaṁśayaḥ</span>–without a doubt. [68]
68 One who reveals the glories of this supreme secret to My devotees will attain transcendental devotion to Me and reach Me without a doubt.
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।<br />भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥६९॥
na cha tasmān manuṣyeṣu kaśchin me priya-kṛttamaḥ<br />bhavitā na cha me tasmād anyaḥ priyataro bhuvi [69]
<span class="e2">manuṣyeṣu</span>–In human society;<span class="e2"> na cha kaśchit</span>–no one;<span class="e2"> me priya-kṛttamaḥ</span>–pleases Me more by his actions; <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>–than he (the preacher of <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span>); <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> na bhavitā</span>–there will not be; <span class="e2">anyaḥ</span>–any other;<span class="e2"> priyataraḥ</span>–dearer; <span class="e2">me</span>–to Me; <span class="e2">tasmāt</span>– than he; <span class="e2">bhuvi</span>–in the world. [69]
69 In the entire human society there is no one who pleases Me by his actions more than he (who preaches the glories of the <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span>), nor will there ever be anyone in the world dearer to Me than he.
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।<br />ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥७०॥
adhyeṣyate cha ya imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṁvādam āvayoḥ<br />jñāna-yajñena tenāham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ [70]
<span class="e2">yaḥ cha</span>–And for he who;<span class="e2"> adhyeṣyate</span>–studies; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> dharmyam</span>–holy;<span class="e2"> saṁvādam</span>–conversation; <span class="e2">āvayoḥ</span>–of ours; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I; <span class="e2">syām</span>–shall be; <span class="e2">iṣṭaḥ</span>–worshipped; <span class="e2">tena</span>–by that (by him);<span class="e2"> jñāna-yajñena</span>–by the ‘knowledge-sacrifice’. <span class="e2">iti</span>–That;<span class="e2"> me matiḥ</span>–is My opinion. [70]
70 And one who studies with devotion this holy conversation of ours will worship Me by the ‘knowledge-sacrifice’. This is My conclusion.
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।<br />सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्म्मणाम् ॥७१॥
śraddhāvān anasūyaś cha śṛṇuyād api yo naraḥ<br />so ’pi muktaḥ śubhā̐l lokān prāpnuyāt puṇya-karmaṇām [71]
<span class="e2">saḥ naraḥ api</span>–That person, too;<span class="e2"> śraddhāvān</span>–possessing faith;<span class="e2"> anasūyaḥ cha</span>–and without resentment; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–who;<span class="e2"> śṛṇuyāt api</span>–only hears; <span class="e2">muktaḥ </span>(<span class="e2">san</span>)–shall be liberated; (<span class="e2">pāpāt</span>)–from sin;<span class="e2"> prāpnuyāt</span>–and will reach; <span class="e2">śubhān</span>–the auspicious; <span class="e2">lokān</span>–abodes; (<span class="e2">prāpya</span>)–attainable;<span class="e2"> puṇya-karmaṇām</span>–by the performers of virtuous acts. [71]
71 Simply by hearing this with an open heart, a faithful person is liberated and attains to the auspicious abodes of the virtuous souls.
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।<br />कच्चिदज्ञानसम्मोहः प्रणष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥७२॥
kachchid etach chhrutaṁ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa chetasā<br />kachchid ajñāna-sammohaḥ praṇaṣṭas te dhanañjaya [72]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">pārtha</span>–O son of Kuntī;<span class="e2"> kachchit</span>–has; <span class="e2">etat</span>–this <span class="e3">Gītā</span>; <span class="e2">śrutam</span>–been heard; <span class="e2">tvayā</span>–by you;<span class="e2"> ekāgrena</span>–with your single-minded;<span class="e2"> chetasā</span>–attention? (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> dhanañjaya</span>–O Arjuna;<span class="e2"> kachchit te</span>–has your;<span class="e2"> ajñāna-sammohaḥ</span>–ignorance and delusion;<span class="e2"> praṇaṣṭaḥ</span>–been dispelled? [72]
72 O Pārtha, have you listened to this with your undivided attention? O Dhanañjaya, are you now free from the darkness of your delusion?
अर्ज्जुन उवाच ।
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत ।<br />स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥७३॥
arjuna uvācha
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtir labdhā tvat prasādān mayāchyuta<br />sthito ’smi gata-sandehaḥ kariṣye vachanaṁ tava [73]
<span class="e2">arjunaḥ uvācha</span>–Arjuna said: (<span class="e2">he</span>)<span class="e2"> achyuta</span>–O Śrī Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> tvat prasādāt</span>–by Your grace; (<span class="e2">me</span>)–my; <span class="e2">mohaḥ</span>–delusion; <span class="e2">naṣṭaḥ</span>–is dispelled. <span class="e2">smṛtiḥ</span>–Self-remembrance; <span class="e2">labdhā</span>–is regained; <span class="e2">mayā</span>–by me.<span class="e2"> sthitaḥ asmi</span>–I am steady.<span class="e2"> gata-sandehaḥ</span>–My doubts have gone.<span class="e2"> kariṣye</span>–I shall follow; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> vachanam</span>–instructions. [73]
73 Arjuna said: O infallible one, by Your grace my delusion is now gone, I can now remember who I am, my doubts are destroyed, and I am firm in my resolve. I shall follow Your instructions.
सञ्जय उवाच ।
इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।<br />संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥७४॥
sañjaya uvācha
ity ahaṁ vāsudevasya pārthasya cha mahātmanaḥ<br />saṁvādam imam aśrauṣam adbhutaṁ roma-harṣaṇam [74]
<span class="e2">sañjayaḥ uvācha</span>–Sañjaya said: <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> aśrauṣam</span>–heard; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this;<span class="e2"> adbhutam</span>–wonderful;<span class="e2"> roma-harṣaṇam</span>–thrilling;<span class="e2"> saṁvādam</span>–conversation;<span class="e2"> mahā-ātmanaḥ vāsudevasya</span>–of the Supreme Soul Vāsudeva;<span class="e2"> pārthasya cha</span>–and Arjuna. [74]
74 Sañjaya said: Thus, I heard this wondrous conversation of the Supreme Soul Vāsudev and the son of Pṛthā, Arjuna, which arouses ecstasy in the hearts of all.
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानिमं गुह्यमहं परम् ।<br />योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥७५॥
vyāsa-prasādāch chhrutavān imaṁ guhyam ahaṁ param<br />yogaṁ yogeśvarāt kṛṣṇāt sākṣāt-kathayataḥ svayam [75]
<span class="e2">vyāsa-prasādāt</span>–By the grace of Śrī Vyāsadev; <span class="e2">aham</span>–I;<span class="e2"> śrutavān</span>–heard; <span class="e2">imam</span>–this; <span class="e2">param</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">guhyam</span>–secret; <span class="e2">yogam</span>–yoga (yoga of action, knowledge, and devotion);<span class="e2"> sākṣāt-kathayataḥ</span>–spoken directly;<span class="e2"> yogeśvarāt</span>–by the Lord of yoga;<span class="e2"> kṛṣṇāt svayam</span>–Kṛṣṇa Himself. [75]
75 By the mercy of Śrī Vyāsadev I heard this supreme secret teaching of yoga, sung directly by the Supreme Lord of yoga, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself.
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।<br />केशवार्ज्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥७६॥
rājan saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya saṁvādam imam adbhutam<br />keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṁ hṛṣyāmi cha muhur muhuḥ [76]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">rājan</span>–O King Dhṛtarāṣṭra;<span class="e2"> saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya</span>–ever remembering;<span class="e2"> imam adbhutam</span>–this miraculous; <span class="e2">puṇyam</span>–sacred;<span class="e2"> saṁvādam</span>–conversation;<span class="e2"> keśava-arjuna-yoḥ</span>–of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna;<span class="e2"> hṛṣyāmi</span>–my heart thrills;<span class="e2"> muhuḥ muhuḥ cha</span>–repeatedly. [76]
76 O King, ever remembering this miraculous, sacred conversation of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, my heart thrills over and over again.
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।<br />विस्मयो मे महान्राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥७७॥
tach cha saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya rūpam atyadbhutaṁ hareḥ<br />vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi cha punaḥ punaḥ [77]
(<span class="e2">he</span>) <span class="e2">rājan</span>–O King;<span class="e2"> saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya cha</span>–and repeatedly remembering; <span class="e2">tat</span>–that;<span class="e2"> ati-adbhutam</span>–most miraculous; <span class="e2">rūpam</span>–universal form; <span class="e2">hareḥ</span>–of the Lord, Śrī Hari; <span class="e2">me</span>–my; <span class="e2">mahān</span>–great;<span class="e2"> vismayaḥ</span>–wonder; (<span class="e2">bhavati</span>)–occurs; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and;<span class="e2"> hṛṣyāmi</span>–and I thrill with ecstasy;<span class="e2"> punaḥ punaḥ</span>–again and again. [77]
77 And remembering, O King, I marvel at that astonishing, almighty universal form of the Supreme Lord Hari, and my whole being thrills with ecstasy.
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।<br />तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥७८॥
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ<br />tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama [78]
<span class="e2">yatra</span>–Where there is;<span class="e2"> yoga-īśvaraḥ</span>–the Lord of yoga, the objective of yoga; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇaḥ</span>–Lord Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">yatra</span>–where there is;<span class="e2"> dhanuḥ-dharaḥ pārthaḥ</span>–Arjuna with bow in hand, the winner of wealth; <span class="e2">tatra</span>–there; <span class="e2">dhruvā</span>–prevails; <span class="e2">śrīḥ</span>–fortune;<span class="e2"> vijayaḥ</span>–victory, Jayaśrī; <span class="e2">bhūtiḥ</span>–prosperity; <span class="e2">nītiḥ</span>–and virtue. (<span class="e2">iti</span>)–This is; <span class="e2">mama</span>–my; <span class="e2">matiḥ</span>–opinion. [78]
78 Where there is Yogeśvar Kṛṣṇa, and where there is Arjuna, the winner of wealth with bow in hand, there prevails fortune, victory, prosperity, and virtue. This is my opinion.
इति श्रीमहाभारते शतसाहस्र्यां संहितायां वैयासिक्या भीष्मपर्व्वणि<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे<br />श्रीकृष्णार्ज्जुनसंवादे मोक्षयोगो नामष्टादशोऽध्यायः ॥१८॥
iti śrī-mahābhārate śata-sāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ vaiyāsikyāṁ<br />bhīṣma-parvaṇi śrīmad-bhagavad-gītāsūpaniṣatsu brahma<br />vidyāyāṁ yoga-śāstre śrī-kṛṣṇārjuna-saṁvāde mokṣa<br />yogo nāmaṣṭādaśo ’dhyāyaḥ [18]
End of Chapter Eighteen<br />The Path of Liberation<br />from the conversation<br />of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna<br />in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā Upaniṣad</span>,<br />the yoga scripture of transcendental knowledge<br />in Bhīṣma Parva of <span class="e3">Śrī Mahābhārata</span>, the holy scripture<br />revealed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in a hundred thousand verses.

श्रीगीतामाहात्म्यम् ।
The Glories of the <span class="e2">Gītā</span>
गीताशास्त्रमिदं पुण्यं यः पठेत्प्रयतः पुमान् ।<br />विष्णोः पदमवाप्नोति भयशोकादिवर्ज्जितः ॥१॥
gītā-śāstram idaṁ puṇyaṁ yaḥ paṭhet prayataḥ pumān<br />viṣṇoḥ padam avāpnoti bhaya-śokādi-varjitaḥ [1]
1 This <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span> scripture is the bestower of all good. One who regularly studies it with devotion will attain to the holy abode of Lord Viṣṇu, the plane of freedom from all distress, fear, and sorrow.
गीताध्ययनशीलस्य प्राणायामपरस्य च ।<br />नैव सन्ति हि पापानि पूर्व्वजन्मकृतानि च ॥२॥
gītādhyayana-śīlasya prāṇāyāma-parasya cha<br />naiva santi hi pāpāni pūrva-janma-kṛtāni cha [2]
2 For a self-controlled person who seriously studies this <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span> scripture, not a trace of sin from this life or even from the previous life remains, as all the sins of such a person are burnt to ashes.
मलनिर्मोचनं पुंसां जलस्नानं दिने दिने ।<br />सकृद्गीताम्भसि स्नानं संसारमलनाशनम् ॥३॥
malanir mochanaṁ puṁsāṁ jala-snānaṁ dine dine<br />sakṛd-gītāmbhasi snānaṁ saṁsāra-mala-nāśanam [3]
3 As a person bathes every day to cleanse the body, similarly, by bathing only once in the waters of the <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span> (reading the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> once with devotion) all the dirt of painful material existence is washed away.
गीता सुगीता कर्त्तव्या किमन्यैः शास्त्रविस्तरैः ।<br />या स्वयं पद्मनाभस्य मुखपद्माद्विनिःसृता ॥४॥
gītā sugītā kartavyā kim anyaiḥ śāstra-vistaraiḥ<br />yā svayaṁ padma-nābhasya mukha-padmād viniḥsṛtā [4]
4 The <span class="e3">Gītā</span> should always be sung with devotion. This divine song emanated from the holy lotus mouth of the Supreme Lord Himself, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. What more can any other scriptures give?
भारतामृतसर्व्वस्वं विष्णोर्वक्त्राद्विनिःसृतम् ।<br />गीतागङ्गोदकं पीत्वा पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥५॥
bhāratāmṛta-sarvasvaṁ viṣṇor vaktrād viniḥsṛtam<br />gītā-gaṅgodakaṁ pītvā punar janma na vidyate [5]
5 By drinking the Ganges waters of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> (by singing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> with devotion), the nectar of the <span class="e3">Mahābhārata</span> emanating from the lotus mouth of Lord Viṣṇu, one will never take birth in the material world again.
सर्व्वोपनिषदो गावो दोग्धा गोपालनन्दनः ।<br />पार्थो वत्सः सुधीर्भोक्ता दुग्धं गीतामृतं महत् ॥६॥
sarvopaniṣado gāvo dogdhā gopāla-nandanaḥ<br />pārtho vatsaḥ sudhīr bhoktā dugdhaṁ gītāmṛtaṁ mahat [6]
6 All the Upaniṣads are as the cow, and the milker of the cow is Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda. Arjuna is the calf, the nectar of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is the milk, and the fortunate devotees are the enjoyers of the milk.
एकं शास्त्रं देवकीपुत्रगीतम्<br />एको देवो देवकीपुत्र एव ।<br />एको मन्त्रस्तस्य नामानि यानि<br />कर्म्माप्येकं तस्य देवस्य सेवा ॥७॥
ekaṁ śāstraṁ devakī-putra-gītam<br />eko devo devakī-putra eva<br />eko mantras tasya nāmāni yāni<br />karmāpy ekaṁ tasya devasya sevā [7]
7 There need be only one scripture—the holy <span class="e3">Gītā</span> sung by Śrī Kṛṣṇa; only one worshippable Lord—Śrī Kṛṣṇa; only one mantra—His Holy Names; and only one work—devotional service to the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

श्रीवैष्णवीय तन्त्रसारोक्त<br />श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतामाहात्म्यम्
The Glories of <span class="e2">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span><br />from <span class="e2">Śrī-Vaiṣṇavīya-tantra-sāra</span>
ऋषिरुवाच ।
गीतायाश्चैव माहात्म्यं यथावत्सूत मे वद ।<br />पुरा नारायणक्षेत्रे व्यासेन मुनिनोदितम् ॥१॥
ṛṣir uvācha
gītāyāś chaiva māhātmyaṁ yathāvat sūta me vada<br />purā nārāyaṇa-kṣetre vyāsena muninoditam [1]
1 The sage said: O Sūta, please tell us of the glories of <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span>, as expressed long ago at Nārāyaṇ Kṣetra by the great sage Śrīla Vyāsadev.
सूत उवाच ।
भद्रं भगवता पृष्टं यद्धि गुप्ततमं परम् ।<br />शक्यते केन तद्वक्तुं गीतामाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥२॥
sūta uvācha
bhadraṁ bhagavatā pṛṣṭaṁ yaddhi guptatamaṁ param<br />śakyate kena tad vaktuṁ gītā-māhātmyam uttamam [2]
2 Sūta Goswāmī said: O venerable one, your request is most auspicious. Indeed, who can describe the transcendental glories of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>, the most hidden of all treasures?
कृष्णो जानाति वै सम्यक्कञ्चित्कुन्तीसुतः फलम् ।<br />व्यासो वा व्यासपुत्रो वा याज्ञवल्क्योऽथ मैथिलः ॥३॥
kṛṣṇo jānāti vai samyak kiñchit kuntī-sutaḥ phalam<br />vyāso vā vyāsa-putro vā yājñavalkyo ’tha maithilaḥ [3]
3 Certainly Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is in full knowledge of those glories; and so Arjuna, the son of Kuntī, knows of them; and Vyāsadev, Śukadev, Yājñavalkya, and the saintly King Janaka, too.
अन्ये श्रवणतः श्रुत्वा लेशं सङ्कीर्त्तयन्ति च ।<br />तस्मात्किञ्चिद्वदाम्यत्र व्यासस्य स्यान्मया श्रुतम् ॥४॥
anye śravaṇataḥ śrutvā leśaṁ saṅkīrtayanti cha<br />tasmāt kiñchid vadāmy atra vyāsasya syān mayā śrutam [4]
4 Others too, who have heard but a little of the glories of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>, are engaged in singing them. And so I shall now speak of the glories of <span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span> as I heard them from Vyāsadev:
सर्व्वोपनिषदो गावो दोग्धा गोपालनन्दनः ।<br />पार्थो वत्सः सुधीर्भोक्ता दुग्धं गीतामृतं महत् ॥५॥
sarvopaniṣado gāvo dogdhā gopāla-nandanaḥ<br />pārtho vatsaḥ sudhīr bhoktā dugdhaṁ gītāmṛtaṁ mahat [5]
5 All the Upaniṣads are personified as the cow, Śrī Kṛṣṇa is milker of the cow, Arjuna is the calf, the nectar of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is the milk, and the fortunate devotees are the enjoyers of the milk.
सारथ्यमर्ज्जुनस्यादौ कुर्व्वन्गीतामृतं ददौ ।<br />लोकत्रयोपकाराय तस्मै कृष्णात्मने नमः ॥६॥
sārathyam arjunasyādau kurvan gītāmṛtaṁ dadau<br />loka-trayopakārāya tasmai kṛṣṇātmane namaḥ [6]
6 I first offer my obeisances unto Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa who accepted the position of the chariot driver of Arjuna, just to distribute this nectar of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> for the benefit of the three worlds.
संसारसागरं घोरं तर्त्तुमिच्छति यो नरः ।<br />गीतानावं समासाद्य पारं याति सुखेन सः ॥७॥
saṁsāra-sāgaraṁ ghoraṁ tartum ichchhati yo naraḥ<br />gītā-nāvaṁ samāsādya pāraṁ yāti sukhena saḥ [7]
7 A person desiring to cross over the treacherous ocean of material suffering can do so very easily by taking refuge in the boat of the <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span>.
गीताज्ञानं श्रुतं नैव सदैवाभ्यासयोगतः ।<br />मोक्षमिच्छति मूढात्मा याति बालकहास्यताम् ॥८॥
gītā-jñānaṁ śrutaṁ naiva sadaivābhyāsa-yogataḥ<br />mokṣam ichchhati mūḍhātmā yāti bālaka-hāsyatām [8]
8 A foolish person who desires liberation by constant yoga practice without hearing the wisdom of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, is to be considered childish.
ये शृण्वन्ति पठन्त्येव गीताशास्त्रमहर्निशम् ।<br />न ते वै मानुषा ज्ञेया देवरूपा न संशयः ॥९॥
ye śṛṇvanti paṭhanty eva gītā-śāstram ahar niśam<br />na te vai mānuṣā jñeyā deva-rūpā na saṁśayaḥ [9]
9 Persons who day and night hear and sing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> are never to be taken as mere human beings. Without doubt, they are as gods in this world.
गीताज्ञानेन सम्बोधं कृष्णः प्राहार्ज्जुनाय वै ।<br />भक्तितत्त्वं परं तत्र सगुणं वाथ निर्गुणम् ॥१०॥
gītā-jñānena sambodhaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ prāhārjunāya vai<br />bhakti-tattvaṁ paraṁ tatra sa-guṇaṁ vātha nirguṇam [10]
10 To enlighten Arjuna with the wisdom of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, Lord Kṛṣṇachandra has revealed the supremacy of devotion, either in this world or in the transcendental plane.
सोपानाष्टादशैरेवं भुक्तिमुक्तिसमुच्छ्रितैः ।<br />क्रमशश्चित्तशुद्धिः स्यात्प्रेमभक्त्यादिकर्म्मसु ॥११॥
sopānāṣṭādaśair evaṁ bhukti-mukti-samuchchhritaiḥ<br />kramaśaś chitta-śuddhiḥ syāt prema-bhakty ādi karmasu [11]
11 Thus, the wisdom of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is a ladder of eighteen chapters, ascending which one rises above sense enjoyment and liberation (bhukti-mukti), and gradually attains purification of the heart and the qualification of loving devotional service to the Supreme Lord.
साधोर्गीताम्भसि स्नानं संसारमलनाशनम् ।<br />श्रद्धाहीनस्य तत्कार्य्यं हस्तिस्नानं वृथैव तत् ॥१२॥
sādhor gītāmbhasi snānaṁ saṁsāra-mala-nāśanam<br />śraddhā-hīnasya tat kāryaṁ hasti-snānaṁ vṛthaiva tat [12]
12 Bathing in the pure waters of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, the devotees are liberated from the contamination of the mundane world. However, persons lacking faith in the Lord may attempt this, but in vain, like an elephant’s bathing. (The elephant immediately rolls in the dust after bathing).
गीतायाश्च न जानाति पठनं नैव पाठनम् ।<br />स एव मानुषे लोके मोघकर्म्मकरो भवेत् ॥१३॥
gītāyāś cha na jānāti paṭhanaṁ naiva pāṭhanam<br />sa eva mānuṣe loke mogha-karma-karo bhavet [13]
13 A person who knows nothing of learning and teaching the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> fails in the duty of the human being.
तस्माद्गीतां न जानाति नाधमस्तत्परो जनः ।<br />धिक्तस्य मानुषं देहं विज्ञानं कुलशीलताम् ॥१४॥
tasmād gītāṁ na jānāti nādhamas tat paro janaḥ<br />dhik tasya mānuṣaṁ dehaṁ vijñānaṁ kula-śīlatām [14]
14 Therefore, there is none more fallen than he who is ignorant of the teachings of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>. Shame on his human birth, his learning, his dignity, and his entire family.
गीतार्थं न विजानाति नाधमस्तत्परो जनः ।<br />धिक्शरीरं शुभं शीलं विभवन्तद्गृहाश्रमम् ॥१५॥
gītārthaṁ na vijānāti nādhamas tat paro janaḥ<br />dhik śarīraṁ śubhaṁ śīlaṁ vibhavantad gṛhāśramam [15]
15 There is none more fallen than he who is ignorant of the meaning of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>. Shame on his bodily beauty, his character, his wealth, and his home.
गीताशास्त्रं न जानाति नाधमस्तत्परो जनः ।<br />धिक्प्रारब्धं प्रतिष्ठाञ्च पूजां दानं महत्तमम् ॥१६॥
gītā-śāstraṁ na jānāti nādhamas tat paro janaḥ<br />dhik prārabdhaṁ pratiṣṭhāñ cha pūjāṁ dānaṁ mahattamam [16]
16 There is none more fallen than he who is ignorant of the scripture <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span>. Shame on his undertakings, his reputation, his worship, his charity, and his honour.
गीताशास्त्रे मतिर्नास्ति सर्व्वं तन्निष्फलं जगुः ।<br />धिक्तस्य ज्ञानदातारं व्रतं निष्ठां तपो यशः ॥१७॥
gītā-śāstre matir nāsti sarvaṁ tan niṣphalaṁ jaguḥ<br />dhik tasya jñāna-dātāraṁ vrataṁ niṣṭhāṁ tapo yaśaḥ [17]
17 A person who does not care for the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> scripture is to be known as a failure in all respects. Shame on his teacher, his vows, his faith, his austerity, and his renown.
गीतार्थपठनं नास्ति नाधमस्तत्परो जनः ।<br />गीतागीतं न यज्ज्ञानं तद्विद्ध्यासुरसम्मतम् ।<br />तन्मोघं धर्म्मरहितं वेदवेदान्तगर्हितम् ॥१८॥
gītārtha-paṭhanaṁ nāsti nādhamas tat paro janaḥ<br />gītā-gītaṁ na yaj jñānaṁ tad viddhy āsura-sammatam<br />tan moghaṁ dharma-rahitaṁ veda-vedānta-garhitam [18]
18 There is none more fallen than he who does not study the purport of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>; and that knowledge which is not glorified in the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> should be known as demoniac, futile, unvirtuous, and rejected by the Vedas and the Upaniṣads.
तस्माद्धर्म्ममयी गीता सर्व्वज्ञानप्रयोजिका ।<br />सर्व्वशास्त्रसारभूता विशुद्धा सा विशिष्यते ॥१९॥
tasmād dharma-mayī gītā sarva-jñāna-prayojikā<br />sarva-śāstra-sāra-bhūtā viśuddhā sā viśiṣyate [19]
19 Therefore, the holy <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is universally respected as the compilation of the essence of all scriptures and the source of all wisdom.
योऽधीते विष्णुपर्व्वाहे गीतां श्रीहरिवासरे ।<br />स्वपन्जाग्रत्चलन्तिष्ठन्शत्रुभिर्न स हीयते ॥२०॥
yo ’dhīte viṣṇu-parvāhe gītāṁ śrī-hari-vāsare<br />svapan jāgrat chalan tiṣṭhan śatrubhir na sa hīyate [20]
20 One who studies the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> on the holy festival days of the advent of the Supreme Lord, and on the holy fasting days, especially Ekādaśī—such a person, whether awake or asleep, moving or still, is never defeated by enemies.
शालग्रामशिलायां वा देवागारे शिवालये ।<br />तीर्थे नद्यां पठेद्गीतां सौभाग्यं लभते ध्रुवम् ॥२१॥
śālagrāma-śilāyāṁ vā devāgāre śivālaye<br />tīrthe nadyāṁ paṭhed gītāṁ saubhāgyaṁ labhate dhruvam [21]
21 One who sings the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> before the Śālagrām-śilā Deity, or in a Temple of the Supreme Lord, or in a Temple of Lord Śiva, at a holy place of pilgrimage, or on the bank of a holy river—certainly such a person attains to all good fortune.
देवकीनन्दनः कृष्णो गीतापाठेन तुष्यति ।<br />यथा न वेदैर्दानेन यज्ञतीर्थव्रतादिभिः ॥२२॥
devakī-nandanaḥ kṛṣṇo gītā-pāṭhena tuṣyati<br />yathā na vedair dānena yajña-tīrtha-vratādibhiḥ [22]
22 Neither the singing of the Vedas, nor the performance of charity, sacrifice, pilgrimage, or vows, can bring such satisfaction to Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, as does the singing of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>.
गीताधीता च येनापि भक्तिभावेन चेतसा ।<br />वेदशास्त्रपुराणानि तेनाधीतानि सर्व्वशः ॥२३॥
gītādhītā cha yenāpi bhakti-bhāvena chetasā<br />veda-śāstra-purāṇāni tenādhītāni sarvaśaḥ [23]
23 The study of the Vedas and Purāṇas, verily the study of all the scriptures, is fulfilled in all respects by one who studies the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> with devotion.
योगस्थाने सिद्धपीठे शिलाग्रे सत्सभासु च ।<br />यज्ञे च विष्णुभक्ताग्रे पठन्सिद्धिं परां लभेत् ॥२४॥
yoga-sthāne siddha-pīṭhe śilāgre sat-sabhāsu cha<br />yajñe cha viṣṇu-bhaktāgre paṭhan siddhiṁ parāṁ labhet [24]
24 The highest perfection of life is attained by one who sings the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> at a place of yoga meditation, at a place of worship, before the Śālagrām-śilā, in the association of saintly persons, during a sacrifice, and before a devotee of Viṣṇu.
गीतापाठञ्च श्रवणं यः करोति दिने दिने ।<br />क्रतवो वाजिमेधाद्याः कृतास्तेन सदक्षिणाः ॥२५॥
gītā-pāṭhañ cha śravaṇaṁ yaḥ karoti dine dine<br />kratavo vājimedhādyāḥ kṛtās tena sa-dakṣiṇāḥ [25]
25 One who daily hears and sings the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is to be considered as having accomplished the performance of all sacrifices such as the Aśvamedha and others, including the receiving of the sacrificial gifts.
यः शृणोति च गीतार्थं कीर्त्तयत्येव यः परम् ।<br />श्रावयेच्च परार्थं वै स प्रयाति परं पदम् ॥२६॥
yaḥ śṛṇoti cha gītārthaṁ kīrtayaty eva yaḥ param<br />śrāvayech cha parārthaṁ vai sa prayāti paraṁ padam [26]
26 One who attentively hears and sings the glories of the purport of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, or reiterates it to others, attains to the supreme destination.
गीतायाः पुस्तकं शुद्धं योऽर्पयत्येव सादरात् ।<br />विधिना भक्तिभावेन तस्य भार्य्या प्रिया भवेत् ॥२७॥
gītāyāḥ pustakaṁ śuddhaṁ yo ’rpayaty eva sādarāt<br />vidhinā bhakti-bhāvena tasya bhāryā priyā bhavet [27]
27 One who, with respect and devotion, and according to scriptural directives makes a gift of this holy book, the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>—such a person’s wife will be devoted.
यशः सौभाग्यमारोग्यं लभते नात्र संशयः ।<br />दयितानां प्रियो भूत्वा परमं सुखमश्नुते ॥२८॥
yaśaḥ saubhāgyam ārogyaṁ labhate nātra saṁśayaḥ<br />dayitānāṁ priyo bhūtvā paramaṁ sukham aśnute [28]
28 And without a doubt, he shall enjoy fame, fortune, and good health. He shall enjoy the affection of those dear to him, and he shall know the highest happiness.
अभिचारोद्भवं दुःखं वरशापागतञ्च यत् ।<br />नोपसर्पति तत्रैव यत्र गीतार्च्चनं गृहे ॥२९॥
abhichārodbhavaṁ duḥkhaṁ vara-śāpāgatañ cha yat<br />nopasarpati tatraiva yatra gītārchanaṁ gṛhe [29]
29 The sorrow caused by a terrible curse or black rites can never enter the home where the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is worshipped.
तापत्रयोद्भवा पीडा नैव व्याधिर्भवेत्क्वचित् ।<br />न शापो नैव पापञ्च दुर्गतिर्नरकं न च ॥३०॥
tāpa-trayodbhavā pīḍā naiva vyādhir bhavet kvachit<br />na śāpo naiva pāpañ cha durgatir narakaṁ na cha [30]
30 In that house there is never suffering of the threefold miseries, nor fear of any illness, curse, sin, misfortune, or hellish existence.
विस्फोटकादयो देहे न बाधन्ते कदाचन ।<br />लभेत्कृष्णपदे दास्यां भक्तिञ्चाव्यभिचारिणीम् ॥३१॥
visphoṭakādayo dehe na bādhante kadāchana<br />labhet kṛṣṇa-pade dāsyāṁ bhaktiñ chāvyabhichāriṇīm [31]
31 In that house, no one is ever afflicted with infectious diseases, and the residents attain undeviating devotion in service to the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
जायते सततं सख्यं सर्व्वजीवगणैः सह ।<br />प्रारब्धं भुञ्जतो वापि गीताभ्यासरतस्य च ॥३२॥
jāyate satataṁ sakhyaṁ sarva-jīva-gaṇaiḥ saha<br />prārabdhaṁ bhuñjato vāpi gītābhyāsa-ratasya cha [32]
32 A person devoted to singing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> acquires a friendly disposition to all living beings, despite the desirable or undesirable reactions of his previous actions.
स मुक्तः स सुखी लोके कर्म्मणा नोपलिप्यते ।<br />महापापातिपापानि गीताध्यायी करोति चेत् ।<br />न किञ्चित्स्पृश्यते तस्य नलिनीदलमम्भसा ॥३३॥
sa muktaḥ sa sukhī loke karmaṇā nopalipyate<br />mahā-pāpāti-pāpāni gītādhyāyī karoti chet<br />na kiñchit spṛśyate tasya nalinī-dalam-ambhasā [33]
33 He is liberated, and he is happy. He is never implicated by his actions. Even if perchance that person who studies the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> commits terrible sin, he is as unaffected as the lotus leaf that remains untouched by even a drop of water.
अनाचारोद्भवं पापमवाच्यादिकृतञ्च यत् ।<br />अभक्ष्यभक्षजं दोषमस्पृश्यस्पर्शजं तथा ॥३४॥
ज्ञानाज्ञानकृतं नित्यमिन्द्रियैर्जनितञ्च यत् ।<br />तत्सर्व्वं नाशमायाति गीतापाठेन तत्क्षणात् ॥३५॥
anāchārodbhavaṁ pāpam avāchyādi-kṛtañ cha yat<br />abhakṣya-bhakṣajaṁ doṣam aspṛśya-sparśajaṁ tathā [34]
jñānājñāna-kṛtaṁ nityam indriyair janitañ cha yat<br />tat sarvaṁ nāśam āyāti gītā-pāṭhena tat-kṣaṇāt [35]
34–35 Whether the inauspiciousness of wrong action or malevolent speech, of eating unacceptable food or touching the untouchable, or sin knowingly or unknowingly contracted through the senses in the course of daily activities—all evils are immediately dispelled by singing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> with devotion.
सर्व्वत्र प्रतिभोक्ता च प्रतिगृह्य च सर्व्वशः ।<br />गीतापाठं प्रकुर्व्वाणो न लिप्येत कदाचन ॥३६॥
sarvatra pratibhoktā cha pratigṛhya cha sarvaśaḥ<br />gītā-pāṭhaṁ prakurvāṇo na lipyeta kadāchana [36]
36 One sincerely devoted to singing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is never implicated despite accepting food in all places or gifts in all kinds of circumstances.
रत्नपूर्णां महीं सर्व्वां प्रतिगृह्याविधानतः ।<br />गीतापाठेन चैकेन शुद्धस्फटिकवत्सदा ॥३७॥
ratna-pūrṇāṁ mahīṁ sarvāṁ pratigṛhyāvidhānataḥ<br />gītā-pāṭhena chaikena śuddha-sphaṭikavat sadā [37]
37 One who takes unlawful possession of the entire earth full of jewels—he, too, will be innocent; by singing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> but once, his heart will be as clear as crystal.
यस्यान्तःकरणं नित्यं गीतायां रमते सदा ।<br />स साग्निकः सदा जापी क्रियावान्स च पण्डितः ॥३८॥
yasyāntaḥkaraṇaṁ nityaṁ gītāyāṁ ramate sadā<br />sa sāgnikaḥ sadā jāpī kriyāvān sa cha paṇḍitaḥ [38]
38 A person whose heart is ever joyfully absorbed in the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is to be considered fully accomplished in sacrifices, always in prayer, perfect in his actions, and truly learned.
दर्शनीयः स धनवान्स योगी ज्ञानवानपि ।<br />स एव याज्ञिको याजी सर्व्ववेदार्थदर्शकः ॥३९॥
darśanīyaḥ sa dhanavān sa yogī jñānavān api<br />sa eva yājñiko yājī sarva-vedārtha-darśakaḥ [39]
39 All are benefitted simply by seeing him. He is glorious, he is a yogī, and he is wise. He is a knower of sacrifice, he is engaged in sacrifice, and he is a knower of the purport of all the Vedas.
गीतायाः पुस्तकं यत्र नित्यपाठश्च वर्त्तते ।<br />तत्र सर्व्वाणि तीर्थानि प्रयागादीनि भूतले ॥४०॥
gītāyāḥ pustakaṁ yatra nitya-pāṭhaś cha vartate<br />tatra sarvāṇi tīrthāni prayāgādīni bhūtale [40]
40 All the holy places in this world, such as Prayāg and others, are present wherever the holy book of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is present and sung constantly.
निवसन्ति सदा देहे देहशेषेऽपि सर्व्वदा ।<br />सर्व्वे देवाश्च ऋषयो योगिनो देहरक्षकाः ॥४१॥
nivasanti sadā dehe deha-śeṣe ’pi sarvadā<br />sarve devāś cha ṛṣayo yogino deha-rakṣakāḥ [41]
41 For one who constantly studies the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, the demigods, sages, and yogīs all preside as guardians in the body, even at the time of death.
गोपालो बालकृष्णोऽपि नारदध्रुवपार्षदैः ।<br />सहायो जायते शीघ्रं यत्र गीता प्रवर्त्तते ॥४२॥
gopālo bāla-kṛṣṇo ’pi nārada-dhruva-pārṣadaiḥ<br />sahāyo jāyate śīghraṁ yatra gītā pravartate [42]
42 Wherever the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is sung, the gracious cowherd boy Śrī Kṛṣṇa swiftly appears as a friend, accompanied by His associates Nārad, Dhruva, and others.
यत्र गीताविचारश्च पठनं पाठनं तथा ।<br />मोदते तत्र श्रीकृष्णो भगवान्राधया सह ॥४३॥
yatra gītā-vichāraś cha paṭhanaṁ pāṭhanaṁ tathā<br />modate tatra śrī-kṛṣṇo bhagavān rādhayā saha [43]
43 Wherever the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> scripture is discussed, studied, and taught, the Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa comes with great joy, accompanied by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
गीता मे हृदयं पार्थ गीता मे सारमुत्तमम् ।<br />गीता मे ज्ञानमत्युग्रं गीता मे ज्ञानमव्ययम् ॥४४॥
śrī-bhagavān uvācha
gītā me hṛdayaṁ pārtha gītā me sāram uttamam<br />gītā me jñānam aty ugraṁ gītā me jñānam avyayam [44]
44 The Supreme Lord said: O Pārtha, the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My heart, the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My supreme essence, and the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is the most powerful, imperishable knowledge of Me.
गीता मे चोत्तमं स्थानं गीता मे परमं पदम् ।<br />गीता मे परमं गुह्यं गीता मे परमो गुरुः ॥४५॥
gītā me chottamaṁ sthānaṁ gītā me paramaṁ padam<br />gītā me paramaṁ guhyaṁ gītā me paramo guruḥ [45]
45 The <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My supreme place, the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My supreme plane, the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My most hidden treasure, the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My supreme teacher.
गीताश्रयेऽहं तिष्ठामि गीता मे परमं गृहम् ।<br />गीताज्ञानं समाश्रित्य त्रिलोकीं पालयाम्यहम् ॥४६॥
gītāśraye ’haṁ tiṣṭhāmi gītā me paramaṁ gṛham<br />gītā-jñānaṁ samāśritya trilokīṁ pālayāmy aham [46]
