46 I am present within the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, and the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My supreme abode. I maintain the three worlds by the eternal wisdom of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>.
गीता मे परमा विद्या ब्रह्मरूपा न संशयः ।<br />अर्धमात्राहरा नित्यमनिर्व्वाच्यपदात्मिका ॥४७॥
gītā me paramā-vidyā brahma-rūpā na saṁśayaḥ<br />ardha-mātrā-harā nityam anirvāchya-padātmikā [47]
47 The <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is My transcendental wisdom, My own self, conveyed by every letter and comprised of eternally ineffable verses.
गीतानामानि वक्ष्यामि गुह्यानि शृणु पाण्डव ।<br />कीर्त्तनात्सर्व्वपापानि विलयं यान्ति तत्क्षणात् ॥४८॥
gītā-nāmāni vakṣyāmi guhyāni śṛṇu pāṇḍava<br />kīrtanāt sarva-pāpāni vilayaṁ yānti tat-kṣaṇāt [48]
48 O Pāṇḍava, I shall tell you the holy names of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>. By singing these names, one is immediately absolved of all sins. Hear now those confidential names from Me:
गङ्गा गीता च सावित्री सीता सत्या पतिव्रता ।<br />ब्रह्मावलिर्ब्रह्मविद्या त्रिसन्ध्या मुक्तगेहिनी ॥४९॥
अर्धमात्रा चिदानन्दा भवघ्नी भ्रान्तिनाशिनी ।<br />वेदत्रयी परानन्दा तत्त्वार्थज्ञानमञ्जरी ॥५०॥
gaṅgā gītā cha sāvitrī sītā satyā pativratā<br />brahmāvalir brahma-vidyā tri-sandhyā mukta-gehinī [49]
ardha-mātrā chidānandā bhava-ghnī bhrānti-nāśinī<br />veda-trayī parānandā tattvārtha-jñāna-mañjarī [50]
49–50 Gaṅgā, Gītā, Sāvitrī, Sītā, Satyā, Pativratā, Brahmāvalī, Brahmavidyā, Trisandhyā, Mukta-gehinī, Ardhamātrā, Chidānandā, Bhavaghnī, Bhrānti-nāśinī, Vedatrayī, Parānandā, and Tattvārtha-jñāna-mañjarī.
इत्येतानि जपेन्नित्यं नरो निश्चलमानसः ।<br />ज्ञानसिद्धिं लभेन्नित्यं तथान्ते परमं पदम् ॥५१॥
ity etāni japen nityaṁ naro niśchala-mānasaḥ<br />jñāna-siddhiṁ labhen nityaṁ tathānte paramaṁ padam [51]
51 One who, with unflickering mind, regularly chants these confidential holy names, achieves perfection in divine knowledge, and finally reaches the supreme destination.
पाठेऽसमर्थः सम्पूर्णे तदर्धं पाठमाचरेत् ।<br />तदा गोदानजं पुण्यं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥५२॥
pāṭhe ’samarthaḥ sampūrṇe tad ardhaṁ pāṭham ācharet<br />tadā go-dāna-jaṁ puṇyaṁ labhate nātra saṁśayaḥ [52]
52 If one is unable to sing the entire <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, half of it should be sung. Then, without doubt, the piety gained by making a gift of cows will be attained.
त्रिभागं पठमानस्तु सोमयागफलं लभेत् ।<br />षडंशं जपमानस्तु गङ्गास्नानफलं लभेत् ॥५३॥
tri-bhāgaṁ paṭhamānas tu soma-yāga-phalaṁ labhet<br />ṣaḍ-aṁśaṁ japamānas tu gaṅgā-snāna-phalaṁ labhet [53]
53 One will achieve the fruit of the soma sacrifice by singing one third of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, and the result of bathing in the Ganges is achieved by chanting a sixth of it.
तथाध्यायद्वयं नित्यं पठमानो निरन्तरम् ।<br />इन्द्रलोकमवाप्नोति कल्पमेकं वसेद्ध्रुवम् ॥५४॥
tathādhyāya-dvayaṁ nityaṁ paṭhamāno nirantaram<br />indra-lokam avāpnoti kalpam ekaṁ vased dhruvam [54]
54 One who unfailingly sings two of its chapters everyday will surely attain residence in the abode of Lord Indra for one millennium.
एकमध्यायकं नित्यं पठते भक्तिसंयुतः ।<br />रुद्रलोकमवाप्नोति गणो भूत्वा वसेच्चिरम् ॥५५॥
ekam adhyāyakaṁ nityaṁ paṭhate bhakti-saṁyutaḥ<br />rudra-lokam avāpnoti gaṇo bhūtvā vasech chiram [55]
55 One who sings with devotion one chapter daily will be recognised as an associate of Lord Śiva, and he will attain residence in the abode of Lord Śiva for immeasurable time.
अध्यायार्धञ्च पादं वा नित्यं यः पठते जनः ।<br />प्राप्नोति रविलोकं स मन्वन्तरसमाः शतम् ॥५६॥
adhyāyārdhañ cha pādaṁ vā nityaṁ yaḥ paṭhate janaḥ<br />prāpnoti ravi-lokaṁ sa manvantara-samāḥ śatam [56]
56 A person who daily sings one half or only one quarter of a chapter will achieve residence in the abode of the sun for the time of one hundred Manus.
गीतायाः श्लोकदशकं सप्त पञ्च चतुष्टयम् ।<br />त्रिद्व्येकमर्धमथवा श्लोकानां यः पठेन्नरः ।<br />चन्द्रलोकमवाप्नोति वर्षाणामयुतं तथा ॥५७॥
gītāyāḥ śloka-daśakaṁ sapta pañcha chatuṣṭayam<br />tri-dvy-ekam-ardham athavā ślokānāṁ yaḥ paṭhen naraḥ<br />chandra-lokam avāpnoti varṣāṇām ayutaṁ tathā [57]
57 A person who faithfully sings ten, seven, five, four, three, two verses, one, or only half a verse of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, will attain residence on the moon for ten thousand years.
गीतार्धमेकपादञ्च श्लोकमध्यायमेव च ।<br />स्मरंस्त्यक्त्वा जनो देहं प्रयाति परमं पदम् ॥५८॥
gītārdham eka pādañ cha ślokam adhyāyam eva cha<br />smaraṁs tyaktvā jano dehaṁ prayāti paramaṁ padam [58]
58 One who, at the time of leaving the body, remembers half the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, a quarter of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, one chapter or only one verse of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>—he reaches the supreme destination.
गीतार्थमपि पाठं वा शृणुयादन्तकालतः ।<br />महापातकयुक्तोऽपि मुक्तिभागी भवेज्जनः ॥५९॥
gītārtham api pāṭhaṁ vā śṛṇuyād anta-kālataḥ<br />mahā-pātaka-yukto ’pi mukti-bhāgī bhavej janaḥ [59]
59 By singing or hearing the purport of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> at the time of death even a greatly sinful person qualifies for liberation.
गीतापुस्तकसंयुक्तः प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा प्रयाति यः ।<br />स वैकुण्ठमवाप्नोति विष्णुना सह मोदते ॥६०॥
gītā-pustaka-saṁyuktaḥ prāṇāṁs tyaktvā prayāti yaḥ<br />sa vaikuṇṭham avāpnoti viṣṇunā saha modate [60]
60 One who is touching the holy book of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> at the time of leaving the body will attain to Vaikuṇṭha and joyfully reside in the association of the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu.
गीताध्यायसमायुक्तो मृतो मानुषतां व्रजेत् ।<br />गीताभ्यासं पुनः कृत्वा लभते मुक्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥६१॥
gītādhyāya-samāyukto mṛto mānuṣatāṁ vrajet<br />gītābhyāsaṁ punaḥ kṛtvā labhate muktim uttamām [61]
61 One whose concentration is intent on just one chapter of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> will attain a human birth after death. Then, again studying the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, he achieves the ultimate liberation.
गीतेत्युच्चारसंयुक्तो म्रियमाणो गतिं लभेत् ॥६२॥
gītety-uchchāra-saṁyukto mriyamāṇo gatiṁ labhet [62]
62 One who utters the word ‘Gītā’ at the time of death attains his life’s fulfillment.
यद्यत्कर्म्म च सर्व्वत्र गीतापाठप्रकीर्त्तिमत् ।<br />तत्तत्कर्म्म च निर्द्दोसं भूत्वा पूर्णत्वमाप्नुयात् ॥६३॥
yad yat karma cha sarvatra gītā-pāṭha-prakīrtimat<br />tat tat karma cha nirdosaṁ bhūtvā pūrṇatvam āpnuyāt [63]
63 All actions performed along with the singing of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> become purified and successful.
पितॄनुद्दिश्य यः श्राद्धे गीतापाठं करोति हि ।<br />सन्तुष्टाः पितरस्तस्य निरयाद्यान्ति स्वर्गतिम् ॥६४॥
pitṝn-uddiśya yaḥ śrāddhe gītā-pāṭhaṁ karoti hi<br />santuṣṭāḥ pitaras tasya nirayād yānti svargatim [64]
64 A person who sings the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> during the performance of obsequial ceremonies satisfies his forefathers, who, being liberated from a hellish existence, ascend to heaven.
गीतापाठेन सन्तुष्टाः पितरः श्राद्धतर्पिताः ।<br />पितृलोकं प्रयान्त्येव पुत्राशीर्व्वादतत्पराः ॥६५॥
gītā-pāṭhena santuṣṭāḥ pitaraḥ śrāddha-tarpitāḥ<br />pitṛ-lokaṁ prayānty eva putrāśīrvāda tat parāḥ [65]
65 Satisfied by the offerings accompanied by the singing of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, the ancestors offer their descendant their blessings and ascend to the heavenly plane known as Pitṛloka.
गीतापुस्तकदानञ्च धेनुपुच्छसमन्वितम् ।<br />कृत्वा च तद्दिने सम्यक्कृतार्थो जायते जनः ॥६६॥
gītā-pustaka-dānañ cha dhenu-puchchha-samanvitam<br />kṛtvā cha tad dine samyak kṛtārtho jāyate janaḥ [66]
66 A person who makes a gift of a book of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> with a yak-tail whisk achieves success in all his endeavours that day.
पुस्तकं हेमसंयुक्तं गीतायाः प्रकरोति यः ।<br />दत्त्वा विप्राय विदुषे जायते न पुनर्भवम् ॥६७॥
pustakaṁ hema-saṁyuktaṁ gītāyāḥ prakaroti yaḥ<br />dattvā viprāya viduṣe jāyate na punar bhavam [67]
67 One who makes a gift of a book of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> along with a presentation of gold to a learned brāhmaṇ, never takes birth in the material world again.
शतपुस्तकदानञ्च गीतायाः प्रकरोति यः ।<br />स याति ब्रह्मसदनं पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥६८॥
śata-pustaka-dānañ cha gītāyāḥ prakaroti yaḥ<br />sa yāti brahma-sadanaṁ punar-āvṛtti-durlabham [68]
68 One who makes a gift of one hundred copies of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> attains to the plane of the Absolute wherefrom rebirth practically never occurs.
गीतादानप्रभावेन सप्तकल्पमिताः समाः ।<br />विष्णुलोकमवाप्यन्ते विष्णुना सह मोदते ॥६९॥
gītā-dāna-prabhāvena sapta-kalpa-mitāḥ samāḥ<br />viṣṇu-lokam avāpyante viṣṇunā saha modate [69]
69 By the potency of making a gift of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, one attains residence in the abode of Lord Viṣṇu for seven millenniums and joyfully associates with the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu.
सम्यक्श्रुत्वा च गीतार्थं पुस्तकं यः प्रदापयेत् ।<br />तस्मै प्रीतः श्रीभगवान्ददाति मानसेप्सितम् ॥७०॥
samyak śrutvā cha gītārthaṁ pustakaṁ yaḥ pradāpayet<br />tasmai prītaḥ śrī-bhagavān dadāti mānasepsitam [70]
70 One who attentively hears the purport of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> and makes a gift of that book to a brāhmaṇ—he brings satisfaction to the Supreme Lord, who blesses him with the fulfillment of all his aspirations.
न शृणोति न पठति गीताममृतरूपिणीम् ।<br />हस्तात्त्यक्त्वामृतं प्राप्तं स नरो विषमश्नुते ॥७१॥
na śṛṇoti na paṭhati gītām-amṛta-rūpiṇīm<br />hastāt tyaktvāmṛtaṁ prāptaṁ sa naro viṣam aśnute [71]
71 A person who neither sings nor hears the nectarean <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is like one who has nectar in his hand yet leaves it aside to drink poison.
जनः संसारदुःखार्त्तो गीताज्ञानं समालभेत् ।<br />पीत्वा गीतामृतं लोके लब्ध्वा भक्तिं सुखी भवेत् ॥७२॥
janaḥ saṁsāra-duḥkhārto gītā-jñānaṁ samālabhet<br />pītvā gītāmṛtaṁ loke labdhvā bhaktiṁ sukhī bhavet [72]
72 When persons suffering in this world of death discover the wisdom of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> and drink the nectar of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, they take refuge in devotion to the Supreme Lord and become truly happy.
गीतामाश्रित्य बहवो भूभुजो जनकादयः ।<br />निर्धूतकल्मषा लोके गतास्ते परमं पदम् ॥७३॥
gītām āśritya bahavo bhū-bhujo janakādayaḥ<br />nirdhūta-kalmaṣā loke gatās te paramaṁ padam [73]
73 Many saintly kings such as King Janaka and others took shelter in the wisdom of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, and becoming purified of all sins, achieved the supreme destination.
गीतासु न विशेषोऽस्ति जनेषूच्चावचेषु च ।<br />ज्ञानेष्वेव समग्रेषु समा ब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी ॥७४॥
gītāsu na viśeṣo ’sti janeṣūchchāvacheṣu cha<br />jñāneṣv eva samagreṣu samā brahma-svarūpiṇī [74]
74 Neither high nor low birth qualifies or disqualifies a faithful person in the singing of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, since of all kinds of knowledge, the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is the embodiment of Brahma and equal to all.
योऽभिमानेन गर्व्वेण गीतानिन्दां करोति च ।<br />स याति नरकं घोरं यावदाहूतसम्प्लवम् ॥७५॥
yo ’bhimānena garveṇa gītā-nindāṁ karoti cha<br />sa yāti narakaṁ ghoraṁ yāvad āhūta-samplavam [75]
75 A person who out of egoism and pride blasphemes the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> will have to reside in terrible hell up to the time of the universal annihilation.
अहंकारेण मूढात्मा गीतार्थं नैव मन्यते ।<br />कुम्भीपाकेषु पच्येत यावत्कल्पक्षयो भवेत् ॥७६॥
ahaṅkāreṇa mūḍhātmā gītārthaṁ naiva manyate<br />kumbhī-pākeṣu pachyeta yāvat kalpa-kṣayo bhavet [76]
76 That foolish person who, deluded by egoism, disregards the purport of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> must remain boiling in oil in the hell known as Kumbhīpāka until the annihilation at the end of the millennium.
गीतार्थं वाच्यमानं यो न शृणोति समासतः ।<br />स शूकरभवां योनिमनेकामधिगच्छति ॥७७॥
gītārthaṁ vāchyamānaṁ yo na śṛṇoti samāsataḥ<br />sa śūkara-bhavāṁ yonim anekām adhigachchhati [77]
77 One who makes much of speaking about the purport of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> yet never properly hears about it, repeatedly takes birth as a hog.
चौर्य्यं कृत्वा च गीतायां पुस्तकं यः समानयेत् ।<br />न तस्य सफलं किञ्चित्पठनञ्च वृथा भवेत् ॥७८॥
chauryaṁ kṛtvā cha gītāyāṁ pustakaṁ yaḥ samānayet<br />na tasya saphalaṁ kiñchit paṭhanañ cha vṛthā bhavet [78]
78 A person who obtains the book of <span class="e3">Gītā</span> by theft is unsuccessful in all his endeavours, and even his attempt to sing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> will be in vain.
यः श्रुत्वा नैव गीताञ्च मोदते परमार्थतः ।<br />नैव तस्य फलं लोके प्रमत्तस्य यथा श्रमः ॥७९॥
yaḥ śrutvā naiva gītāñ cha modate paramārthataḥ<br />naiva tasya phalaṁ loke pramattasya yathā śramaḥ [79]
79 One who, hearing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, does not experience spiritual joy—his life is fruitless, like the labour of one deluded.
गीतां श्रुत्वा हिरण्यञ्च भोज्यं पट्टाम्बरं तथा ।<br />निवेदयेत्प्रदानार्थं प्रीतये परमात्मनः ॥८०॥
gītāṁ śrutvā hiraṇyañ cha bhojyaṁ paṭṭāmbaraṁ tathā<br />nivedayet pradānārthaṁ prītaye paramātmanaḥ [80]
80 To please the Supreme Lord, after hearing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> one should offer gold, food, and silken cloth to a Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇ.
वाचकं पूजयेद्भक्त्या द्रव्यवस्त्राद्युपस्करैः ।<br />अनेकैर्बहुधा प्रीत्या तुष्यतां भगवान्हरिः ॥८१॥
vāchakaṁ pūjayed bhaktyā dravya-vastrādy upaskaraiḥ<br />anekair bahudhā prītyā tuṣyatāṁ bhagavān hariḥ [81]
81 To satisfy the Supreme Lord Hari, one must worship the speaker of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> with devotion, offering him cloth and many worshipful presentations.
सूत उवाच ।
माहात्म्यमेतद्गीतायाः कृष्णप्रोक्तं पुरातनम् ।<br />गीतान्ते पठते यस्तु यथोक्तफलभाग्भवेत् ॥८२॥
sūta uvācha
māhātmyam etad gītāyāḥ kṛṣṇa-proktaṁ purātanam<br />gītānte paṭhate yas tu yathokta-phala-bhāg bhavet [82]
82 Sūta Goswāmī said: These eternal glories of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> are sung by the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself. One who sings the glories of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> on completion of singing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> can partake of the fruits of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> as mentioned herein.
गीतायाः पठनं कृत्वा माहात्म्यं नैव यः पठेत् ।<br />वृथा पाठफलं तस्य श्रम एव उदाहृतः ॥८३॥
gītāyāḥ paṭhanaṁ kṛtvā māhātmyaṁ naiva yaḥ paṭhet<br />vṛthā pāṭha-phalaṁ tasya śrama eva udāhṛtaḥ [83]
83 The attempt to sing the <span class="e3">Gītā</span> is but fruitless labour for a person who neglects to conclude with singing the glories of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>.
एतन्माहात्म्यसंयुक्तं गीतापाठं करोति यः ।<br />श्रद्धया यः शृणोत्येव परमां गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥८४॥
etan māhātmya-saṁyuktaṁ gītā-pāṭhaṁ karoti yaḥ<br />śraddhayā yaḥ śṛṇoty eva paramāṁ gatim āpnuyāt [84]
84 One who with heart’s faith hears or sings the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, complete with the glories of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, reaches the supreme destination.
श्रुत्वा गीतामर्थयुक्तां माहात्म्यं यः शृणोति च ।<br />तस्य पुण्यफलं लोके भवेत्सर्व्वसुखावहम् ॥८५॥
śrutvā gītām artha-yuktāṁ māhātmyaṁ yaḥ śṛṇoti cha<br />tasya puṇya-phalaṁ loke bhavet sarva-sukhāvaham [85]
85 One who with faith hears this meaningful <span class="e3">Gītā</span>—song divine, and hears in conclusion the glories of the <span class="e3">Gītā</span>, shall reap the fruits of virtue in this world, and his life will be filled with joy.
इति श्रीवैष्णवीयतन्त्रसारे श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतामाहात्म्यं सम्पूर्णम्।<br />सम्पूर्णोऽयं ग्रन्थः। श्री कृष्णार्पणमस्तु।
iti śrī-vaiṣṇavīya-tantra-sāre śrīmad-bhagavad-<br />gītā-māhātmyaṁ sampūrṇam<br />sampūrṇo ’yaṁ granthaḥ<br />śrī kṛṣṇārpaṇam astu
Thus is completed The Glories of Śrī <span class="e3">Gītā</span><br />from the <span class="e3">Śrī-Vaiṣṇavīya-tantra-sāra</span>.<br />Thus is completed <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span>,<br />The Hidden Treasure of the Sweet Absolute.<br />May Śrī Kṛṣṇa mercifully accept this offering.

Glossary
(Sanskrit terms and abbreviations used in this edition)
<span class="e2">abhidheya: </span>the means to the end.
<span class="e2">āchārya: </span>learned, venerable preceptor who teaches by example.
<span class="e2">achintya-bhedābheda-tattva: </span>the principle of inconceivable oneness and difference.
<span class="e2">Adhokṣaja: </span>a name of the Supreme Lord; that witch is above sense perception.
<span class="e2">ādhyātmika, ādhibhautika, ādhidaivika: </span>pertaining to the psycho-physiological or to the self; pertaining to other beings or elements; pertaining to natural phenomena or the functions of the demigods.
<span class="e2">Aditi: </span>mother of the Ādityas and other demigods, daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Kaśyapa, and mother of Lord Viṣṇu in His dwarf incarnation of Vāmandev.
<span class="e2">Āditya(s): </span>Vāmandev; the solar gods.
<span class="e2">Agni: </span>the fire-god.
<span class="e2">ananya-bhakti: </span>exclusive devotion.
<span class="e2">Āryan: </span>an inhabitant of Āryāvarta; nobleman/person.
<span class="e2">aṣṭāṅga-yoga: </span>meditational yoga performed in eight steps: yama, niyama, āsan, prāṇāyām, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyān, and samādhi, viz., self-control, mental restraint, posture, breath-control, restraint of the senses, steady mental control, meditation, and meditational trance centered on Lord Viṣṇu. Generally impractical in the present age.
<span class="e2">Aśvinī Kumāras: </span>the twin sons of Aśvinī, the wife of the sun-god.
<span class="e2">Bhagavān: </span>the personal and highest aspect of the Absolute.
<span class="e2">bhajan: </span>internal devotion; service.
<span class="e2">bhakti-yoga: </span>devotional connection with the Supreme Lord.
<span class="e2">Bhīṣma: </span>son of Śantanu to Gaṅgā. A lifelong celibate, he became the, guardian of both the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas. In the battle of Kurukṣetra, he was the great general who headed the army of the Kauravas.
<span class="e2">Bhīṣma-parva: </span>the sixth book of the epic <span class="e3">Mahābhārata</span>.
<span class="e2">Brahmā (Lord): </span>demigod-creator of the universe and the presiding deity of the mode of passion. In another capacity, he takes the position of an Āchārya.
<span class="e2">brahmachārī: </span>celibate spiritual student.
<span class="e2">Brahmaloka: </span>(i) the abode of Lord Brahmā, Satyaloka, (ii) Brahma, above the mundane plane, yet below the plane wherein devotional service to the Lord begins, i.e., Vaikuṇṭha.
<span class="e2">Brahma: </span>the Absolute; the impersonal aspect of the Absolute; the Supreme Spirit; the spiritual effulgence of the Lord, spirit.
<span class="e2">brāhmaṇ: </span>a knower of Brahma; person of the priestly class.
<span class="e2">buddhi-yoga: </span>theistic wisdom.
<span class="e12">Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span><span class="e2"> (Śrī): </span>the pastimes and teachings os Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, by Śrīla Kṛṣṇadās Kavirāj Goswāmī.
<span class="e2">Chandra: </span>the demigod of the moon; the moon.
<span class="e2">Chāndrāyaṇ: </span>a type of penance performed by eating only fifteen mouthfuls of food on the full-moon day, reducing one’s food by a day, and then increasing by one mouthful daily during the moon’s waxing up to the next full moon.
<span class="e2">chatur-yuga: </span>see <span class="e3">yuga</span>.
<span class="e2">dāsya (rasa): </span>divine relationship of servitude to the Supreme Lord.
<span class="e2">demigods, gods: </span>celestial beings.
<span class="e2">Devakī: </span>Kṛṣṇa’s mother in Mathurā.
<span class="e2">dhām: </span>abode.
<span class="e2">dharma: </span>nature; religion; duty.
<span class="e2">Dhṛṣṭadyumna: </span>a son of Drupada and brother of Draupadī; he acted as commander-in-chief of the Pāṇḍavas’ forces.
<span class="e2">Dhṛtarāṣtra, King: </span>the brother of Pāṇḍu. He was disqualified from occupying the throne due to his blindness and tried to establish his eldest son Duryodhan as the emperor. Father of one hundred sons (Kauravas).
<span class="e2">dhyān: </span>meditation.
<span class="e2">Draupadī: </span>the daughter of Drupada, the wife of the Pāṇḍavas.
<span class="e2">Droṇāchārya, Droṇa: </span>the son of the sage Bharadvāja and the military preceptor of both the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas.
<span class="e2">Drupada: </span>a king of the country known as Pāñchālas, the father of Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Draupadī.
<span class="e2">Duryodhan: </span>the eldest son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
<span class="e2">Ekādaśī: </span>fasting day on the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight.
<span class="e2">Gāndhārī: </span>the wife of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
<span class="e2">Gandharva: </span>celestial singer or musician.
<span class="e2">Gauḍīya sampradāya: </span>the divine succession following Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.
<span class="e2">Gaurāṅga (Śrī): </span>the golden Lord, Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.
<span class="e2">gāyatrī: </span>sacred mantra chanted by brāhmaṇs; Vedic metre.
<span class="e2">goswāmī: </span>sense-controlled ascetic.
<span class="e2">gopī(s): </span>cowherd girl; wife of a cowherd; the most intimate associates beloved of Lord Kṛṣṇa in madhura-rasa, in the pastimes of Vṛndāvan.
<span class="e2">Govinda: </span>Lord Kṛṣṇa: the object of the Vedas and the Lord of the cows, the earth, the Vedas, and the senses; cowherd.
<span class="e2">gṛhastha: </span>married person.
<span class="e2">guhya-guhyatara-guhyatama: </span>hidden, more hidden, and most hidden.
<span class="e2">guṇa: </span>quality, mode (of material nature); rope.
<span class="e2">Guru, Gurudev: </span>spiritual master.
<span class="e2">Hanumān: </span>the most devoted and loyal servitor of Lord Rāmachandra; he is the ideal of dāsya-rasa.
<span class="e2">Hiraṇyagarbha: </span>Lord Brahmā.
<span class="e2">hlādinī-śakti: </span>the divine ecstasy potency of the Lord, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
<span class="e2">Ikṣvāku: </span>a king of the solar dynasty, the son of Vaivasvata Manu.
<span class="e2">Indra: </span>the demigod who is king of the heavenly plane.
<span class="e2">Jagannātha Purī: </span>the holy city in Odisha, India, where Lord Kṛṣṇa is worshiped as Lord Jagannāth, the Lord of the universe.
<span class="e2">Janaka (King): </span>the father of Śītā Devī, the consort of Lord Rāmachandra.
<span class="e2">Jīva Goswāmī (Śrīla): </span>one of the six goswāmīs, apostles of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu. In his writings, he illustrated the supremacy of the Kṛṣṇa conception on the authority of the revealed scriptures.
<span class="e2">jīva, jīvātma: </span>soul, self.
<span class="e2">jñān: </span>knowledge; knowledge of Brahma; knowledge of the supremacy of the Supreme Lord; knowledge of one’s divine relationship (sambandha) with the Lord; knowledge of pure devotion for the Lord.
<span class="e2">jñāna-śūnyā-bhakti: </span>noncalculative devotion or attraction to the Lord and His service by natural affinity.
<span class="e2">jñāna-yoga: </span>the way of knowledge.
<span class="e2">jñānī: </span>learned person.
<span class="e2">Kali-yuga: </span>the age of quarrel, the present age. The present Kali-yuga began on the 28th chatur-yuga of Vaivasvata Manu (about 5,000 years ago). The battle of Kurukṣetra was fought at this time.
<span class="e2">Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī Viṣṇu: </span>Kāraṇodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, Mahāviṣṇu. The first four-armed plenary expansion of Lord Kṛṣṇa, from whose pores the innumerable universes emanate.
<span class="e2">karma: </span>action; worldly action; good or bad actions; fruitive action; moral duty.
<span class="e2">Karma-kāṇḍa: </span>the department of the Vedas externally advocating ceremonial and sacrificial rites which reward one with piety and attainment of haven.
<span class="e2">karma-yoga: </span>the path of dutifulness, the way of action.
<span class="e2">karmī: </span>fruitive worker; fruitive religionist; active person.
<span class="e2">Karṇa: </span>the son of Kuntī by the sun-god. He became the most intimate friend of Duryodhan.
<span class="e2">Kaunteya: </span>Arjuna, the son of Kuntī.
<span class="e2">Kauravas: </span>the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; descendants of Kuru.
<span class="e2">kevalā-bhakti: </span>ananya-bhakti.
<span class="e2">kīrtan: </span>singing or narrating the glories of the Lord.
<span class="e2">Kṛṣṇa: </span>the all-attractive Supreme Lord, the Lord of love; the male aspect of the Godhead.
<span class="e2">Kṛṣṇa-kathā: </span>transcendental narrations about Kṛṣṇa.
<span class="e2">kṣatriya: </span>warrior, a person of the warrior class.
<span class="e2">kṣetra: </span>field; the field of action as the habitat of the conditioned soul.
<span class="e2">kṣetrajña: </span>the knower of the field; the soul; the Supersoul.
<span class="e2">Kubera: </span>the god of riches, the presiding deity of the northern quarter and half-brother of Rāvaṇa, he is the king of the Yakṣas and Kinnaras and a friend of Rudra. He resides in Kailās.
<span class="e2">Kuntī: </span>Pṛthā, the first wife of Pāṇḍu, and mother of Yudhiṣṭhir by the god Yama, Bhīma by the god Vāyu, and Arjuna by the god Indra. Mother of Karṇa by the god Sūrya.
<span class="e2">Kuru(s): </span>a place at the location of modern Delhi; name of the kings of this land.
<span class="e2">Kurukṣetra: </span>a holy plain near Delhi, the scene of the great war between the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas.
<span class="e2">līlā: </span>divine pastimes.
<span class="e2">loka: </span>plane of life; world; people.
<span class="e2">madhura (rasa): </span>the highest of all divine relationships with the Lord, the relationship of consorthood.
<span class="e2">Madhusūdan: </span>Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of the demon Madhu.
<span class="e12">Mahābhārata</span><span class="e2">: </span>the great scripture which describes the saga of the history of the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas, composed by Śrīla Vyāsadev in eighteen pārvas or books.
<span class="e2">mantra: </span>a sacred incantation which delivers one through meditation upon it.
<span class="e2">Manus: </span>the fourteen progenitors of mankind who appear successively within one day of Lord Brahmā. The present Manu is Vaivasvata Manu.
<span class="e2">Māyāpur: </span>the holy land in the centre of Nabadwīp, West Bengal, place of the advent of Lord Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.
<span class="e2">Nanda Mahārāj: </span>Kṛṣṇa’s father in Vṛndāvana-līlā.
<span class="e2">Nārāyaṇ: </span>Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa’s four-armed plenary expansion.
<span class="e2">Navadvīpa, Nabadwīp (coll.), (Dhāma, Dhām [coll.]): </span>the holy abode of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, manifest in this world in West Bengal.
<span class="e2">Nimāi: </span>a name of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, due to His advent under the Nimba tree.
<span class="e2">niṣkām: </span>desireless.
<span class="e2">niṣkām karma-yoga: </span>the yoga or path of selfless action or duty.
<span class="e2">Oṁ, Oṁkāra: </span>the sacred monosyllable, sound representation of the Absolute Truth.
<span class="e2">pañcha-mahāyajña: </span>five types of daily sacrifices preformed by brāhmaṇs as mentioned in the scripture <span class="e3">Manu-saṁhitā</span>: (i) Brahma-yajña: study of the Vedas; (ii) Ptṛ-yajña: offering obsequial oblations to one’s ancestors; (iii) Deva-yajña: offering clarified butter to the gods through the Vedic fire sacrifice; (iv) Bhūta-yajña: offering food to other beings, and (v) Nṛ-yajña: honouring guests.
<span class="e2">pañcha-sūnā: </span>fivefold sin inadvertently committed in a household by killing living beings in the course of (i) cooking; (ii) grinding (spices, etc.); (iii) sweeping; (iv) husking grain, and (v) washing.
<span class="e2">Pāṇḍavas: </span>the five sons of Pāṇḍu: Yudhiṣṭhir, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakul, and Sahadev.
<span class="e2">Parabrahma: </span>the Supreme Brahma; the Supreme Lord.
<span class="e2">Paramātma, Paramātmā: </span>The Supersoul, Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, the aspect of the Supreme Lord present within the hearts of all living beings.
<span class="e2">Paraśurām: </span>the incarnation of the Lord who admonished the kṣatriya race with his axe.
<span class="e2">Pātañjala (-yoga): </span>the yoga system taught by Patañjali.
<span class="e2">prāṇa:</span> air of the body, ten kinds: prāṇa—outgoing; apāna—descending; vyāna—contracting and expanding (respirational); samāna—digestive; udāna—rising; nāga—belching; kūrma—opening of the eyes, awakening; kṛkara—sneezing; devadatta—yawning; and dhanañjaya—always pervading the body, whether alive or dead (Śrī Śrīdhar Swāmipād).
<span class="e2">prayojan: </span>aim, objective.
<span class="e2">prema, Kṛṣṇa-prema: </span>divine love for Kṛṣṇa.
<span class="e2">prema-bhakti: </span>devotional service in divine love.
<span class="e2">Pṛthā: </span>Kuntī.
<span class="e2">Rādhārāṇī (Śrīmatī): </span>The female aspect of the Godhead.
<span class="e2">rāga-mārg: </span>the path of divine love.
<span class="e2">raja-guṇa: </span>the material mode of passion.
<span class="e2">rasa: </span>divine ecstasy; divine relationship with the Lord, the five primary relationships of tranquillity, servitude, friendship, parenthood, and consorthood.
<span class="e2">Rāsa-līlā: </span>the divine dance of love, conducted by Lord Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs in Vṛndāvan.
<span class="e2">ṛṣi: </span>seer, sage.
<span class="e2">Rūpa Goswāmī (Śrīla): </span>the eternal associate of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, recognised in the Gauḍīya sampradāya as the foremost authority of the teachings of Śrī Chaitanya.
<span class="e2">Śachī Devī (Śrīmatī): </span>the mother of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.
<span class="e2">sādhana: </span>religious or spiritual practice.
<span class="e2">sādhu-saṅga: </span>association of saints or devotees of the Lord.
<span class="e2">sakhya (rasa): </span>divine relationship of friendship with the Lord.
<span class="e2">sambandha: </span>relationship.
<span class="e2">Sañjaya: </span>the charioteer of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
<span class="e2">sāṅkhya: </span>knowledge of the soul; the Vedānta scriptures.
<span class="e2">saṅkīrtan: </span>congregational chanting of the Holy Names of the Lord.
<span class="e2">sannyās: </span>renunciation; the renounced order.
<span class="e2">sannyāsī: </span>a person of the renounced order.
<span class="e2">śānta (rasa): </span>divine relationship of tranquillity.
<span class="e2">sattva-guṇa: </span>the mode of goodness, the chief of the three modes of material nature.
<span class="e2">Satyaloka: </span>the abode of Lord Brahmā.
<span class="e2">SB: </span><span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span>.
<span class="e2">Śiva (Lord): </span>the demigod of the mode of ignorance and of universal annihilation.
<span class="e2">smaraṇam: </span>devotional remembrance of the Lord.
<span class="e2">smṛti: </span>that which is remembered; that which is authored; book of civil or religious law such as the <span class="e3">Manu-smṛti</span> or <span class="e3">Manu-saṁhitā</span>.
<span class="e2">śraddhā: </span>faith in devotion.
<span class="e2">śravaṇam: </span>devotional practice of hearing the glories of the Lord.
<span class="e12">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span><span class="e2"> (</span><span class="e12">Mahāpurāṇa</span><span class="e2">): </span>one of the eighteen Purāṇas, a holy scripture exclusively on the subject of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Śrīla Vyāsadev’s own commentary on Vedānta.
<span class="e2">śruti: </span>that which is heard or known by revelation; the Vedas.
<span class="e2">śūdra: </span>labourer.
<span class="e2">Supersoul: </span>see Paramātma.
<span class="e2">Sūrya: </span>the demigod of the sun, the sun-god, Vivasvān; the sun.
<span class="e2">Śyāmasundar: </span>Lord Kṛṣṇa of beautiful, charming humanlike feature, whose body is of a blackish hue like a soft raincloud.
<span class="e2">tama-guṇa: </span>the material mode of ignorance.
<span class="e2">Upaniṣads: </span>the conclusions of the Vedas, giving knowledge of the Supreme Spirit; Vedānta.
<span class="e2">Vaikuṇṭha: </span>plane of the spiritual world (above the heavenly planes, and above Virajā and Brahmaloka). In Vaikuṇṭha, the Lord is worshipped in His Nārāyaṇ or Viṣṇu expansions. Above Vaikuṇṭha is Goloka.
<span class="e2">Vaiṣṇava: </span>a devotee of the Supreme Lord, Viṣṇu.
<span class="e2">vaiśya: </span>farmer, merchant.
<span class="e2">Vaitaraṇī: </span>river of hell, river of death.
<span class="e2">vānaprastha: </span>the retired order of life.
<span class="e2">varṇāśram, daiva-varṇāśram: </span>the God-centered socio-religious system consisting of four social orders or varṇas (brāhmaṇ, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra) and four religious orders or āśrams (brahmacharya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha, and sannyās). When the system is adulterated by atheistic tendencies it is known as āsura-varṇāśram.
<span class="e2">Varuṇa: </span>the demigod of the ocean and the Western direction.
<span class="e2">Vasudev: </span>the father of Lord Kṛṣṇa when He appears in Mathurā.
<span class="e2">Vāsudev: </span>Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vasudev.
<span class="e2">vātsalya (rasa): </span>divine parenthood of the Lord.
<span class="e2">Veda: </span>(i) knowledge; (ii) the holy scriptures <span class="e3">Ṛg-</span>, <span class="e3">Yajur-</span>, <span class="e3">Sāma-</span>, and <span class="e3">Atharva </span>Vedas.
<span class="e2">Vedānta: </span>the conclusion of the Vedas; an Upaniṣad.
<span class="e2">Vedānta-sūtra: </span>Brahma-sūtra, the aphorisms of Vedānta philosophy by Śrīla Vyāsadev.
<span class="e2">vijñān: </span>science; realised knowledge; spiritual knowledge.
<span class="e2">Virajā (River): </span>the passive plane, above the material plane but below Brahma.
<span class="e2">Viṣṇu:</span> the all-pervading Supreme Lord: (i) the four-armed plenary expansions of Lord Kṛṣṇa who preside over each of the innumerable Vaikuṇṭha planes situated in the spiritual sky above the impersonal Brahma; (ii) Kāraṇārnavaśāyī Viṣṇu or Mahāviṣṇu; (iii) Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, who expands from Mahāviṣṇu and enters into every universe; (iv) Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, who expands from Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and enters into the hearts of all living beings as the Supersoul, and who maintains the universe by the mode of goodness.
<span class="e2">Vraja, Vṛndāvan (Dhām): </span>the Supreme Abode of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. The highest abode in the spiritual realm, Goloka Vṛndāvan, which is situated above Vaikuṇṭha; in this world it is manifest as (Gokula) Vṛndāvan in Mathurā district, Uttar Pradesh, North India (coll. Vrindaban.)
<span class="e2">Vyāsadev: </span>Vedavyās; the great eternal sage empowered by the Supreme Lord to compile the Vedas and reveal the Purāṇas, <span class="e3">Mahābhārata</span>, <span class="e3">Vedānta-sūtra</span>, <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span>, etc.
<span class="e2">vibhūti: </span>power; expansion; opulences.
<span class="e2">Yaśodā: </span>Lord Kṛṣṇa’s mother in Vṛndāvan-līlā.
<span class="e2">yoga: </span>(i) yoking, uniting, connecting; (ii) path, way, course, means, mode.
<span class="e2">Yudhiṣṭhir: </span>the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas and rightful heir to the throne of Hastināpur; he was crowned emperor after the defeat of the Kauravas in the battle of Kurukṣetra.
<span class="e2">yuga: </span>an age of the world. The four ages are Kṛta or Satya, Tretā, Dvāpar, and Kali, the duration of each being 1,728,000, 1,296,000, 864,000, and 432,000 years respectively. They are also known as the Golden, Silver, Copper, and Iron Ages. With each successive age, there is a gradual decline of moral and religious qualities. The four ages together comprise one chatur-yuga.
<span class="e2">yukta-vairāgya: </span>detachment from the mundane, attained by the devotee who offers everything in the service of the Lord.

All glory to Śrī Guru and Śrī Gaurāṅga

Translator’s Note
I bow at the feet of Śrī Gurudev, the Vaiṣṇavas, and the all-merciful Śrī Śrī Gaura-Nityānanda. I place this book in their hands and pray that it pleases their hearts.
Content
This edition of <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> and <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga</span> has been prepared from Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh’s Bengali publications of these texts and includes translations of their publisher’s notes. A Bengali poem by Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj which invites everyone to join Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām Parikramā sets the tone of the book. Preceding the primary texts is the preface from Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s original publication of <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> in 403 Chaitanyābda (1888 ), as well as his poem <span class="e3">Śrīman Navadvīpa-dhāma-vandanā</span>, which summarises the entire <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> in twenty Sanskrit verses.
Following <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> and <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga</span> is a set of excerpts from Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s writing and an overview of the glories of Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām compiled from lectures by Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj. The list of the ten offences to the Holy Dhām, a glossary, and the map of Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām prepared by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur have been included at the back.
Translation
The texts of <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> and <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga</span> are presented in a four-fold format: 1) the Bengali text of each verse, 2) its Roman transliteration, 3) its English prose-ordered phrase-by-phrase gloss, and 4) its English prose translation. In this edition, punctuation marks to indicate grammatical compounds, speech, and past active participles have been inserted into the Bengali text and its transliteration to aid comprehension. When reading the prose-ordered phrase-by-phrase gloss—a style of translation known as <span class="e3">anvaya</span>, which is common in Bengali translation of Sanskrit—please note: 1) past active participles are often conjugated in tandem with the finite verb they accompany, 2) verb tenses are often translated to suit idiomatic usage in English (e.g. present tense and present perfect tense are often translated as simple past tense), 3) idiomatic uses of the passive voice in Bengali are translated in the active voice in English, and 4) correlative pronouns and prepositional cases are typically translated in the simplest grammatically equivalent forms possible. It is our hope that this method of presentation will aid readers in appreciating the simplicity and sweetness of the Bengali text itself.
Origin
This book has been prepared under the auspices of Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh’s Present-Sevāite-Āchārya, Om Viṣṇupād Śrīla Bhakti Nirmal Āchārya Mahārāj. Śrīpād Bhakti Rañjan Madhusūdan Mahārāj oversaw the production of the book and edited the final manuscript. Śrīpād Bhakti Prapanna Tīrtha Mahārāj and Lalita Mādhava Prabhu greatly assisted with translation. Śrī Viśākhā Devī Dāsī provided invaluable assistance, and numerous other devotees contributed with editorial suggestions and corrections. Śrīmān Purujit Prabhu financed the printing. We are indebted to all these devotees for their gracious contributions.
Purpose
Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s prophecy that Hari-nām-saṅkīrtan would spread to every town and village of the world; Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s prophecy that people from all over the world would come to Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām and join the Bengalis in chanting the glories of Śrī Gaurasundar; and Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur’s prophecy that Westerners would learn Bengali just to study the writings of the Rūpānuga sampradāya’s Āchāryas are becoming fulfilled more and more gloriously with each passing year. It is our hope that this publication will serve to further all three of these expressions of divine will. May souls all over the world read the glories of Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām in this book and be inspired to continue the saṅkīrtan of Śrī Gaurasundar wherever they may be. May they be inspired to travel to Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām and perform parikramā in the company of devotees from Bengal and all over the world. May they pause their joyous saṅkīrtan from place to place throughout the Dhām to recite the glories of the Dhām as revealed by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur. May they thus taste the nectar in the life of a surrendered soul:
gaura āmāra	<span class="e10">ye saba sthāne</span><br />	<span class="e11">karala bhramaṇa raṅge</span><br />se saba sthāna	<span class="e10">heriba āmi</span><br />	<span class="e11">praṇayi-bhakata-saṅge</span><br />gaura-vihita	<span class="e10">kīrtana śuni’</span><br />	<span class="e11">￼ānande hṛdaya nāche</span>
(Śaraṇāgati: 31.3–4)
“In the company of loving devotees, we visit the places where our Śrī Gaurasundar performed Pastimes, and as we hear the kīrtan prescribed by Him, our hearts dance with joy.”
Humbly,
Bhakti Kamal Tyāgī
On the disappearance day of
Śrīla Śrīnivās Āchārya,
10 November 2013
Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh
Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām

Publisher’s Note
Translated from the 1988 Bengali edition of <br /><span class="e2">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span>
By the boundless grace of our great-grand Gurudev, Om Viṣṇupād Śrīla Ṭhākur Bhakti Vinod, our long-standing desire to publish <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> has been fulfilled. Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām is Gupta Vṛndāvan [Hidden Vṛndāvan]. Circumambulating the thirty-two miles of Śrī Vṛndāvan Dhām is a deeply cherished devotional practice for greatly enthusiastic devotees, yet Śrī Gaura’s devotees circumambulate Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām for the satisfaction of Śrī Śachī Nandan Gaurahari with even more enthusiasm and attain eternal good fortune. This circumambulation takes place unfailingly every year in an organised way from the chief original Maṭh—Śrī Chaitanya Maṭh, Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh, and other ashrams. In particular, assembled devotees from all corners of the world participate in the circumambulation of Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām arranged by Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh—which was established by Śrīla Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj in Kolerganj, Nabadwīp—and attain the highest fortune. By their earnest request, and for the benefit of all devotees who circumambulate the Holy Dhām, we have published this holy book which bestows the highest fortune of revelation of the Holy Dhām; we are thus greatly fortunate.
Śrīla Narottam Ṭhākur has written,
śrī-gauḍa-maṇḍala-bhūmi	<span class="e5">yebā jāne chintāmaṇi</span><br />	<span class="e6">tāra haya vraja-bhūme vāsa</span>
(Prārthanā: 39.3)
[“One who knows the holy land of Gauḍa to be made of wish-fulfilling gemstone resides in the land of Vraja.”]
The true form of the Dhām manifests only in the hearts of fortunate souls who are established, by the grace of Śrī Guru, in the spiritual land of dedication with proper sambandha-jñān [understanding of their relationship with the Lord]. Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu’s verse <span class="e3">ataḥ Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-nāmādi*</span> clearly teaches us this principle. So, awakening and increasing our propensity for dedication (sevā) is our one and only necessity, and this is possible only by attaining the grace of Śrī Guru and the sādhus. Thus, our one and only duty is to adhere to the practice of living a life of resolute faith and subservience to Śrī Guru and the sādhus.
dīkṣā-kāle bhakta kare ātma-samarpaṇa<br />sei kāle kṛṣṇa tāre kare ātma-sama<br />sei deha kare tāra chid-ānandamaya<br />aprākṛta-dehe tā̐ra charaṇa bhajaya
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta, Antya-līlā, 4.192–193)
[“At the time of initiation, devotees fully surrender themselves, and Kṛṣṇa accepts them. Kṛṣṇa makes their body spiritual and joyful, and in that supramundane body they serve Kṛṣṇa’s feet.”]
The Lord’s Name, Form, Qualities, Pastimes, Associates, and Glory are all supramundane. Only by Śrī Guru’s grace can a surrendered soul see the Lord’s supramundane Dhām with eyes free from māyā and attain the fortune of service there. May the nature of the Holy Dhām—<span class="e3">chintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa-lakṣāvṛteṣu surabhīr abhipālayantam</span> [“the abode made of wish-fulfilling gemstone covered by millions of wish-fulfilling trees where Śrī Govinda tends His cows”]—be realised by reading this book. This is my earnest prayer at the holy feet of Śrī Guru, the Vaiṣṇavas, and the Lord of the Dhām, Śrīman Mahāprabhu. Enough verbosity.
Publisher
The humble and fallen,
Śrī Bhakti Sundar Govinda
(in the pen name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Śaraṇ Brahmachārī)
*ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ<br />sevonmukhe hi jihvādau svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ
(Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu: Pūrva-vibhāga, 2.232)
[“Although Kṛṣṇa’s Name, Form, Qualities, and Pastimes cannot be grasped by the material senses, through the spirit of dedication they manifest themselves on the tongue and to the other senses.”]

Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-parikramāya Āhvāna
An invitation to Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām Parikramā
Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
Originally published in <span class="e3">Śrī Gauḍīya Darśan</span>:<br />Volume 1, Issue 8, Sunday, 11 March 1956
	<span class="e6">bhramite habe nā āra—e-chhār bhuvana</span><br />anitya e deha-rathe	<span class="e5">chaḍiyā mṛtyura pathe</span><br />	<span class="e6">hiṁsra-śārddūla-pūrṇa saṁsāra-kānana</span><br />	<span class="e6">bhramite habe nā āra e-chhāra bhuvana [1]</span>
You do not have to wander any longer in this miserable world, riding along the path of death in the chariot of this temporary body within the forest of material existence, which is filled with ferocious tigers. You do not have to wander any longer in this miserable world.
añchale añchala bā̐dhi’	<span class="e5">yauvanera sādha sādhi’</span><br />	<span class="e6">‘gṛha-vrata’ nāme śudhu hale parichita</span><br />janma-janmāntara dhari’	<span class="e5">gṛha parikramā kari’</span><br />	<span class="e6">bujhile ki māyā-bhūmi—kaṇṭaka-āvṛta? [2]</span>
Getting married and pursuing the desires of youth, you have known the ‘vow of household life’ in name only. Continuing in this way birth after birth, circling about in household life, have you realised that the land of Māyā is covered with thorns?
ārao karitechha mana	<span class="e5">bhramaṇera āyojana—</span><br />	<span class="e6">deśa hate videśete grāma-grāmāntare,</span><br />ekhano meṭeni āśā	<span class="e5">ārao bā̐dhitechhe vāsā—</span><br />	<span class="e6">du’dinera pāntha-śālā—pṛthivīra pare? [3]</span>
Still your mind is making arrangements to continue your wandering from country to country and village to village, when even now your desires have never been fulfilled? Still you are going to build a residence—a mere temporary inn which lasts but a few days—upon this earth?
mahāmāyā-moha-ghore	<span class="e5">āra kata-kāla ore!</span><br />	<span class="e6">anitya o gṛhaṭire—karabi bhramaṇa,</span><br />dārā-putra-paribāra	<span class="e5">asāra-anitya chhāra</span><br />	<span class="e6">bile—khāle—ā̐stākuḍe mile ki ratana? [4]</span>
Hey! How much longer will you wander in the darkness of Mahāmāyā’s illusion in that temporary home? Your wife, sons, and family are worthless, temporary, and miserable. Will you find a jewel within a swamp, trench, or rubbish heap?
pāye dhari’ kahi sāra	<span class="e5">bhramite habe nā āra</span><br />	<span class="e6">nāhi hethā bharasāra—eka-bindu jala,</span><br />nāhi āśā sāntvanāra,	<span class="e5">āchhe śudhu hāhākāra</span><br />	<span class="e6">samasta saṁsāra bharā—jalanta-anala [5]</span>
Clasping your feet, I tell you this essential truth: you do not have to wander any longer. There is not one drop of the water of hope here. There is no hope of any solace but only cries of distress here. The burdens of material existence are like a blazing fire.
bhramite habe nā āra saṁsāra-kānane<br />“ai śona”, gaura-jana ḍāke sarva-jane [6]
You do not have to wander any longer in the forest of material existence. The devotees of Gaura call everyone: “Hey, listen!
“āya āya tvarā kari’	<span class="e5">bāla-vṛddha nara-nārī</span><br />	<span class="e6">divya-chintāmaṇi-dhāma—gaura-janma-bhūmi</span><br />praṇayi-bhakta sane	<span class="e5">jīvanera śubha-kṣaṇe</span><br />	<span class="e6">gaurāṅga-janma-dine āya parikrami’ [7]</span>
“Men and women, young and old, come immediately! Come to the divine abode made of wish-fulfilling gemstone, the land of Śrī Gaurāṅga’s advent! Come and circumambulate this land in the company of loving devotees at the most auspicious time in life: the day of Śrī Gaurāṅga’s advent.
dhāma-parikramā kare	<span class="e5">sāṅga habe chira-tare</span><br />	<span class="e6">ananta janama dhare brahmāṇḍa-bhramaṇa,</span><br />dūre yābe bhava-roga	<span class="e5">khaṇḍibe sakala bhoga</span><br />	<span class="e6">bhūloke-goloka-lābha”ḍāke gaura-jana [8]</span>
“Circumambulate this divine abode and your prolonged wandering throughout this universe for innumerable births will end. The disease of material existence will go away, all your suffering will be cut away, and you will attain Goloka on this earth.” So call the devotees of Gaura.
bhramite habe nā āra e-chhāra bhuvana [9]
You do not have to wander any longer in this miserable world.

Circumambulating The Dhām
Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
Those days have gone by, when I guided the parikramā, singing and dancing in the front. I was mad when I guided the parikramā: I became almost mad to sing and dance in the Name of Gaurāṅga. I would do so almost without any fatigue. Those days have gone by. Now I cannot go.
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> We can get a palanquin. Then you can come with us.
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Gauraharibol, Gauraharibol, Gauraharibol … I am pleased to think that so many of you will dance somewhere in Gaura Maṇḍal taking the Name. That makes me more proud. We feel more proud to think that so many souls are adding to the glorious opulence of Gaura Dhām, as foretold by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur: “The day is not far off when the devotees from the Western countries will mix with the Eastern devotees, and they will chant and dance together in the Name of Gaurasundar and Nityānanda.”

Preface
A translation of the preface to the original publication of <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> written by
Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur
“As there are books about the glory of other Dhāms, so there should be a book about the glory of Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām”—long ago this desire arose in the hearts of the sādhus. But because such a book cannot be published until Śrīman Nityānanda Prabhu desires it, it has remained unpublished. Now that a suitable time has arrived by the inspiration of Śrīman Nityānanda Prabhu, and with the sanction of the Vaiṣṇava sādhus, I have published this book.
Using the descriptions of the Dhām in Śrīman Narahari Dās’s <span class="e3">Bhakti-ratnākara</span> and <span class="e3">Navadvīpa-dhāma-parikramā-paddhati</span>, and those made by Śrī Narottam Ṭhākur, Śrī Paramānanda Dās, and other writers as a basis, I have visited all the villages within the thirty-two mile circumference of Śrīman Nabadwīp Dhām, collected verbal accounts from knowledgeable residents of those places, gathered all the clues about the Dhām within the scriptures, and then composed this book.
In scriptures such as the Vedas and Purāṇas, there are numerous clues about Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām. Upon reading the verse from <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (7.9.38) cited below, it is easily understood that the scriptures have also described the hidden Avatār (Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu) in a hidden way:
dharmaṁ mahāpuruṣa pāsi yugānuvṛttaṁ<br />chhannaḥ kalau yad abhavas triyugo ’tha sa tvam
[“O Supreme Lord! You protect the dharma in accordance with each age. Because You are hidden in the Age of Kali, You are known as Triyuga, He who appears in three ages.”]
The small map included in this book was prepared from a government authorised topographic map. Therefore, it should be considered accurate. As the map’s scale is small, only the names of the principal places have been given.

All glory to Śrī Guru and Śrī Gaurāṅga
Śrīman Navadvīpa-dhāma-vandanā
A summary of <br /><span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya</span> <br />in twenty Sanskrit verses
Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur
śrutich chhāndogyākhyā vadati paramaṁ brahma-purakaṁ<br />smṛtir vaikuṇṭhākhyāṁ vadati kila yaṁ viṣṇu-sadanam<br />sitadvīpaṁ chānye virala-rasiko yaṁ vraja-vanaṁ<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [1]
The śruti known as <span class="e3">Chhāndogya</span> calls it ‘the city of the Supreme Absolute’. The smṛti calls it ‘Vaikuṇṭha’, the abode of Lord Viṣṇu. Others know it as ‘the white island’. The rare relishers of rasa call it ‘the forest of Vraja’. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe brahmā nija-kucharitāt moha-janitāt<br />kṛpā-sindhuṁ gauraṁ satata-manu-taptaḥ samabhajat<br />prabhus tasmai gūḍhāṁ nija-hṛdaya-vāñchhāṁ samavadat<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [2]
In one of its regions, Brahmā, constantly repenting for his misbehaviour caused by bewilderment, worshipped Gaura, the ocean of mercy. The Lord then fulfilled the deepest desire in Brahmā’s heart. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe gaurī giri-vara-sutā viśva-jananī<br />śachī-sūnor dṛṣṭvā bhajana-viṣayaṁ rūpam atulam<br />svasīmante prādāt prabhu-charaṇa-reṇuṁ bhagavatī<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [3]
In one of its regions, Bhagavatī, the golden-complexioned daughter of the Himalayas, the mother of the universe, beheld the unparalleled form of the object of her worship, the son of Śachī. She then placed the dust of the Lord’s feet upon the parting in her hair. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe vajrī nija-kumati-taptaḥ susurabhiṁ<br />samāśritya premṇā druma-tala-samīpe hari-padam<br />bhajan sākṣād gaurād varam ati-śubhaṁ prāpa vibudho<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [4]
In one of its regions, the wielder of the thunderbolt, Lord Indra, remorseful for his impudence, took shelter of beautiful Surabhi, lovingly worshipped the feet of the Lord beside a tree, and attained a most auspicious boon from Gaura Himself. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe saptarṣi-gaṇa-bhajanākṛṣṭa-hṛdayaḥ<br />aho! gauraḥ sārddha-prahara-samaye prādurabhavat<br />varaṁ tebhyaḥ prādāch charama-samaye yad dhitakaraṁ<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [5]
In one of its regions, His heart attracted by their service, Gaura appeared to the seven sages at noon, and, oh, bestowed upon them a pleasing boon at the perfect time! I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe kaśchid dvija-kula-patiḥ puṣkara-matiḥ<br />svavārddhakyāt tīrtha-bhramaṇa-viṣaye śakti-rahitaḥ<br />dadarśāgre tīrthaṁ parama-śubhadaṁ puṣkaram api<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [6]
In one of its regions, a brāhmaṇ chief, who longed for Puṣkara Tirtha but because of his old age lacked the ability to make the pilgrimage there, saw the supremely auspicious Puṣkara Tīrtha before him. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe kolākṛti-dhṛg ati-chitraṁ makha-patiṁ<br />svabhaktāya prītyā ratim ati-viśuddhāṁ tribhuvane<br />dadau śrī-gaurāṅge svabhajana-balākṛṣṭa-hṛdayo<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [7]
In one of its regions, the Lord of sacrifice, who bears the dazzling form of a boar, His heart was drawn by the power of His devotee’s service, affectionately bestowed upon His devotee the purest thing in the three worlds—love for Śrī Gaurāṅga. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe kuñje nija-bala-vṛto ’yaṁ ṛtu-patiḥ<br />naṭantaṁ chaitanyaṁ svagaṇa-pariyuktaṁ samabhajat<br />latā-gulmākīrṇe phala-kusuma-bhāra-praṇamite<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [8]
In one of its regions, the king of the seasons, checking his own power, worshipped Śrī Chaitanya, who, along with His associates, was dancing in a grove whose creepers and shrubs, laden with fruits and flowers, bowed to Him. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe jahnur bhajana-samaye śubhra-salilāṁ<br />samāyātāṁ dṛṣṭvā pratikūla-taraṅgāṁ samapibat<br />amuñchat tāṁ bhaktyā punar api munir jahnu-tanayāṁ<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [9]
In one of its regions, Jahnu Muni, upon seeing the Gaṅgā’s glistening waters approaching during his worship, drank her distracting waves. He then released her again as his daughter because of the devotion (of King Bhagīrath). I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe rāmo daśaratha-suto lakṣmaṇa-yutaḥ<br />purā sītā-sārddhaṁ katipaya-dinaṁ gāṅga-puline<br />avātsīt tretāyāṁ muni-nikaro modadruma-tale<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [10]
In one of its regions, in the Tretā-yuga of a previous era, the son of Daśarath, the wealth of the sages, Rāma, with his other half, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇ, resided for a few days on the bank of the Gaṅgā beneath a pleasure tree. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe nārāyaṇam api paraṁ nārada-munir<br />dadarśāyaṁ sākṣāt sakala-bhajanīyaṁ sura-varam<br />apaśyat taṁ paśchāt parama-puruṣaṁ gaura-vapuṣaṁ<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [11]
In one of its regions, the sage Nārad directly beheld the greatest of Gods, Nārāyaṇ, who is supremely worshippable to all, and then saw the Supreme Lord in His golden form. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe pārtho drupada-tanayā-sevita-padaḥ<br />avātsīt sabhrātaḥ katipaya-dinaṁ gaura-kṛpayā<br />mahāraṇye puṇye muni-nikara-sevye hari-sakhaḥ<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [12]
In one of its regions, by the grace of Gaura, the Lord’s friend Arjuna, served by Draupadī and accompanied by his brothers, resided for a few days in a large, auspicious forest that is worshipped by hosts of sages. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yad ekāṁśe rudraḥ svagaṇa-sahitaḥ prema-galitaḥ<br />naṭan mandaṁ mandaṁ kara-ḍamaru-vādya-pramuditaḥ<br />aho! gāyatyuchchaiḥ satatam api viśvambharam asau<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [13]
In one of its regions, Rudra, lost in divine love, gently dances with his associates, enlivened by the sound of ḍamarus. Oh! How he continuously sings about Viśvambhar in this place! I bow here to  Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yathā sthāne sthāne jala-parivṛtās tīrtha-nikarāḥ<br />virājante śaśvat sakala-muni-sevyā hy agha-harāḥ<br />tathā devāḥ sarve girīśa-parameṣṭhi-prabhṛtayo<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [14]
An abundance of holy places, surrounded by water, shine eternally throughout this land. Attended by Śiva, Brahmā, and all the other gods, these places destroy all sin and are worshippable to all the sages. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yathā prauḍhā māyā svapati-sahitā vaiṣṇava-ripūn<br />jaḍānandaṁ datvā hari-niyama-kartrī chhalayati<br />mṛṣā-śāstrāchārair mada-vichalitān mohayati cha<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [15]
Here, Prauḍhā Māyā, the Lord’s warden, along with her husband, deceives the enemies of the Vaiṣṇavas by giving them material happiness and bewilders those who are blinded by pride in their futile study of the scriptures. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yathā vaiṣā kālī danuja-dalanī śambhu-ramaṇī<br />harer bhaktān snehāt kapaṭa-rahitā pālayati cha<br />parānandaṁ gauraṁ bhajati niyataṁ prema-galitā<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [16]
Here, Kālī, the wife of Śambhu and destroyer of the demons, sincerely protects the devotees of the Lord out of affection for them. Lost in divine love, she eternally worships Gaura in ecstasy. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
yathā vāṇī sākṣāt prabhu-charaṇa-sevāśaya-ratā<br />dvijātibhyo vidyāṁ nikhila-naya-śāstrādi-viṣayām<br />dadāty eṣā nityaṁ vibudha-taṭinī-tīra-viṣaye<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [17]
Saraswatī, the goddess of speech, whose heart is given to the service of the Lord’s feet, eternally resides on the bank of the Gaṅgā in this land and personally bestows upon the brāhmaṇs knowledge of all the scriptures on conduct and other subjects. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
hariḥ śrīmad-rādhā-dyuti-kavalitaḥ pārṣada-vṛtaḥ<br />śachī-garbhodbhūtaḥ kali-kaluṣa-nāśodyata-manaḥ<br />yathā nāmnaḥ saṅkīrtanam ati-pavitraṁ samakarot<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [18]
Adorned with the lustre of Śrī Rādhā, the Lord appeared here from the womb of Śrī Śachī. Intent on purging the filth of Kali, He engaged in supremely purifying chanting of the Name, accompanied by His associates. I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
aho! bhaktāḥ kechit parama-ramaṇīye jana-pade<br />naṭantaṁ gaurāṅgaṁ nija-jana-balākā-parivṛtam<br />yathā paśyanty addhā hari-bhajana-siddhau svanayanair<br />navadvīpaṁ vande tam iha paramānanda-nilayam [19]
Oh! Here, some devotees, expert in the service of the Lord, directly see with their own eyes Śrī Gaurāṅga dancing amidst His associates and their wives in this supremely beautiful city! I bow here to Nabadwīp, the abode of supreme joy.
navadvīpe yo vai kṛta-nivasatir dvaidha-rahitaḥ<br />idaṁ stotraṁ bhaktyā paṭhati hari-pūjādi-samaye<br />chidānande sākṣāt praṇaya-sukha-bhāvaṁ bhagavati<br />śachī-sūnau kṛṣṇe parama-ramaṇīyaṁ sa labhate [20]
One who resides in Nabadwīp without duplicity and recites this prayer with devotion at the time of worshipping the Lord, genuinely attains the supremely delightful joy of love for the Lord, the embodiment of spiritual ecstasy—the son of Śachī, who is Kṛṣṇa Himself.

Chapter One
The Glories of the Dhām
জয় জয় নবদ্বীপচন্দ্র শচীসুত ।<br />জয় জয় নিত্যানন্দরায় অবধূত ॥১॥
jaya jaya navadvīpa-chandra śachī-suta<br />jaya jaya nityānanda-rāya avadhūta [1]
<span class="e2">jaya</span> <span class="e2">jaya</span>–All glory <span class="e2">śachī-suta</span>–to the son of Śachī, Śrī Chaitanya, <span class="e2">navadvīpa-chandra</span>–the moon of Nabadwīp! <span class="e2">jaya</span> <span class="e2">jaya</span>–All glory <span class="e2">avadhūta</span>–to the renunciant <span class="e2">nityānanda-rāya</span>–Nityānanda Rāy! [1]
All glory to the son of Śachī, the moon of Nabadwīp! All glory to the avadhūt Nityānanda Rāy!
জয় জয় শ্রীঅদ্বৈত প্রভু মহাশয় ।<br />গদাধর শ্রীবাস পণ্ডিত জয় জয় ॥২॥
jaya jaya śrī-advaita prabhu mahāśaya<br />gadādhara śrīvāsa paṇḍita jaya jaya [2]
<span class="e2">jaya jaya</span>–All glory <span class="e2">mahāśaya</span>–to the worshippable <span class="e2">śrī-advaita</span> <span class="e2">prabhu</span>–Śrī Advaita Prabhu! <span class="e2">jaya jaya</span>–All glory <span class="e2">gadādhara</span>–to Gadādhar Paṇḍit [and] <span class="e2">śrīvāsa paṇḍita</span>–Śrīvās Paṇḍit! [2]
All glory to the worshippable Śrī Advaita Prabhu! All glory to Gadādhar Paṇḍit and Śrīvās Paṇḍit!
জয় নবদ্বীপধাম সর্ব্বধাম-সার ।<br />জয় নবদ্বীপবাসী গৌরপরিবার ॥৩॥
jaya navadvīpa-dhāma sarva-dhāma-sāra<br />jaya navadvīpa-vāsī gaura-parivāra [3]
<span class="e2">jaya</span>–All glory <span class="e2">navadvīpa-dhāma</span>–to Nabadwīp Dhām, <span class="e2">sarva-dhāma-sāra</span>–the best of all abodes! <span class="e2">jaya</span>–All glory <span class="e2">navadvīpa-vāsī</span>–to the residents of Nabadwīp, <span class="e2">gaura-parivāra</span>–the associates of Śrī Gaura! [3]
All glory to Nabadwīp Dhām, the best of all abodes! All glory to the residents of Nabadwīp, the associates of Śrī Gaura!
সকল ভকতপদে করিয়া প্রণাম ।<br />সংক্ষেপে বর্ণিব আমি নবদ্বীপধাম ॥৪॥
sakala bhakata-pade kariyā praṇāma<br />saṁkṣepe varṇiba āmi navadvīpa-dhāma [4]
<span class="e2">praṇāma kariyā</span>–Bowing <span class="e2">sakala</span> <span class="e2">bhakata-pade</span>–at the feet of all the devotees,<span class="e2"> āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">varṇiba</span>–will describe <span class="e2">navadvīpa-dhāma</span>–Nabadwīp Dhām <span class="e2">saṁkṣepe</span>–briefly. [4]
Bowing at the feet of all the devotees, I will briefly describe Nabadwīp Dhām.
নবদ্বীপমণ্ডলের মহিমা অপার ।<br />ব্রহ্মা আদি নাহি জানে বর্ণে সাধ্য কার ॥৫॥
navadvīpa-maṇḍalera mahimā apāra<br />brahmā ādi nāhi jāne varṇe sādhya kāra [5]
<span class="e2">mahimā</span>–The glories <span class="e2">navadvīpa-maṇḍalera</span>–of the district of Nabadwīp [are] <span class="e2">apāra</span>–unlimited. <span class="e2">brahmā</span>–Brahmā [and] <span class="e2">ādi</span>–the other gods <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–do not <span class="e2">jāne</span>–know [them]. <span class="e2">kāra</span>–Who <span class="e2">sādhya varṇe</span>–can describe [them]? [5]
The glories of Nabadwīp Maṇḍal are unlimited. Brahmā and the other gods do not know them. So, who can describe them?
সহস্র বদনে শেষ বর্ণিতে অক্ষম ।<br />ক্ষুদ্রজীব আমি কিসে হইব সক্ষম ॥৬॥
sahasra vadane śeṣa varṇite akṣama<br />kṣudra-jīva āmi kise ha-iba sakṣama [6]
<span class="e2">śeṣa</span>–Ananta Śeṣa [is] <span class="e2">akṣama</span>–unable <span class="e2">varṇite</span>–to describe [them] <span class="e2">sahasra</span> <span class="e2">vadane</span>–with thousands of mouths. <span class="e2">kise</span>–How <span class="e2">ha-iba</span>–will <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I, <span class="e2">kṣudra-jīva</span>–a tiny soul, <span class="e2">sakṣama</span>–be able [to]? [6]
Ananta Śeṣa is unable to describe them with thousands of mouths. So, how will I, a tiny soul, be able to?
সত্য বটে নবদ্বীপ মহিমা অনন্ত ।<br />দেব-দেব মহাদেব নাহি পায় অন্ত ॥৭॥
satya vaṭe navadvīpa mahimā ananta<br />deva-deva mahādeva nāhi pāya anta [7]
<span class="e2">vaṭe</span>–It is <span class="e2">satya</span>–true [that] <span class="e2">mahimā</span>–the glories <span class="e2">navadvīpa</span>–of Nabadwīp [are] <span class="e2">ananta</span>–unlimited. <span class="e2">deva-deva</span>–The god of gods, <span class="e2">mahādeva</span>–Lord Śiva, <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–cannot <span class="e2">pāya</span>–reach [their] <span class="e2">anta</span>–end. [7]
It is true that the glories of Nabadwīp are unlimited. The god of gods, Lord Śiva, cannot reach their end.
তথাপি চৈতন্যচন্দ্র-ইচ্ছা বলবান্ ।<br />সেই ইচ্ছাবশে ভক্ত আজ্ঞার বিধান ॥৮॥
tathāpi chaitanya-chandra-ichchhā balavan<br />sei ichchhā-vaśe bhakta ājñāra vidhāna [8]
<span class="e2">tathāpi</span>–Still, <span class="e2">chaitanya-chandra-ichchhā</span>–the will of the moon-like Śrī Chaitanya [is] <span class="e2">balavan</span>–powerful, [and] <span class="e2">ājñāra</span> <span class="e2">vidhāna</span>–the arrangement of the orders <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–of the devotees [is] <span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">ichchhā-vaśe</span>–under the control of His will. [8]
Still, the will of the moon-like Śrī Chaitanya is all-powerful, and under its control, the devotees give orders.
ভক্তগণে আজ্ঞা দিল চৈতন্য ইচ্ছায় ।<br />নদীয়া-মাহাত্ম্য বর্ণি ভক্তের কৃপায় ॥৯॥
bhakta-gaṇe ājñā dila chaitanya ichhāya<br />nadīyā-māhātmya varṇi bhaktera kṛpāya [9]
<span class="e2">chaitanya ichhāya</span>–By the will of Śrī Chaitanya, <span class="e2">bhakta-gaṇe</span>–the devotees <span class="e2">ājñā</span> <span class="e2">dila</span>–have ordered [me]. <span class="e2">varṇi</span>–I describe <span class="e2">nadīyā-māhātmya</span>–the glories of Nadia <span class="e2">bhaktera</span> <span class="e2">kṛpāya</span>–by the mercy of the devotees. [9]
By the will of Śrī Chaitanya, the devotees have ordered me, and so I describe the glories of Nadia by their mercy.
আর এক কথা আছে গূঢ় অতিশয় ।<br />কহিতে না ইচ্ছা হয় না কহিলে নয় ॥১০॥
āra eka kathā āchhe gūḍha atiśaya<br />kahite nā ichchhā haya nā kahile naya [10]
<span class="e2">āchhe</span>–There is <span class="e2">āra</span> <span class="e2">eka</span>–another <span class="e2">atiśaya</span>–very <span class="e2">gūḍha</span>–confidential <span class="e2">kathā</span>–subject, [which] <span class="e2">ichchhā</span> <span class="e2">haya nā</span>–I do not want <span class="e2">kahite</span>–to mention [yet] <span class="e2">naya</span>–cannot <span class="e2">nā</span>–not <span class="e2">kahile</span>–mention. [10]
There is another very confidential subject, which I do not want to mention, yet cannot but mention.
যে অবধি শ্রীচৈতন্য অপ্রকট হৈল ।<br />ধাম-লীলা প্রকাশিতে ভক্তে আজ্ঞা দিল ॥১১॥
ye avadhi śrī-chaitanya aprakaṭa haila<br />dhāma-līlā prakāśite bhakte ājñā dila [11]
<span class="e2">ye</span> <span class="e2">avadhi</span>–When <span class="e2">śrī-chaitanya</span>–Śrī Chaitanya <span class="e2">aprakaṭa</span> <span class="e2">haila</span>–disappeared, <span class="e2">ājñā</span> <span class="e2">dila</span>–He ordered <span class="e2">bhakte</span>–the devotees <span class="e2">prakāśite</span>–to reveal [His] <span class="e2">dhāma-līlā</span>–abode and Pastimes. [11]
When Śrī Chaitanya disappeared, He ordered the devotees to reveal His abode and Pastimes.
সর্ব্ব-অবতার হৈতে গূঢ় অবতার ।<br />শ্রীচৈতন্যচন্দ্র মোর বিদিত সংসার ॥১২॥
sarva-avatāra haite gūḍha avatāra<br />śrī-chaitanya-chandra mora vidita saṁsāra [12]
<span class="e2">haite</span>–Of <span class="e2">sarva</span>–all <span class="e2">avatāra</span>–Avatārs, <span class="e2">mora</span>–our <span class="e2">śrī-chaitanya-chandra</span>–moon-like Śrī Chaitanya [is the most] <span class="e2">gūḍha</span>–confidential <span class="e2">avatāra</span>–Avatār <span class="e2">vidita</span>–known <span class="e2">saṁsāra</span>–in this world. [12]
Of all Avatārs, our moon-like Śrī Chaitanya is the most confidential known in this world.
গূঢ়লীলা শাস্ত্রে গূঢ়রূপে উক্ত হয় ।<br />অভক্ত জনের চিত্তে না হয় উদয় ॥১৩॥
gūḍha-līlā śāstre gūḍha-rūpe ukta haya<br />abhakta janera chitte nā haya udaya [13]
[His] <span class="e2">gūḍha-līlā</span>–confidential Pastimes <span class="e2">haya</span>–are <span class="e2">ukta</span>–mentioned <span class="e2">gūḍha-rūpe</span>–confidentially <span class="e2">śāstre</span>–in the scriptures. [They] <span class="e2">udaya haya nā</span>–do not appear <span class="e2">chitte</span>–in the hearts <span class="e2">abhakta</span> <span class="e2">janera</span>–of non-devotees. [13]
His confidential Pastimes are mentioned confidentially in the scriptures. They are not revealed in the hearts of non-devotees.
সে লীলা সম্বন্ধে যত গূঢ় শাস্ত্র ছিল ।<br />মায়াদেবী বহুকাল আচ্ছাদি’ রাখিল ॥১৪॥
se līlā sambandhe yata gūḍha śāstra chhila<br />māyā-devī bahu-kāla āchchhādi’ rākhila [14]
<span class="e2">bahu-kāla</span>–For a long time, <span class="e2">māyā-devī</span>–Māyā Devī <span class="e2">āchchhādi’</span> <span class="e2">rākhila</span>–hid <span class="e2">yata</span>–the <span class="e2">gūḍha</span>–confidential <span class="e2">śāstra</span>–scriptures <span class="e2">chhila</span>–that existed <span class="e2">sambandhe</span>–about <span class="e2">se</span>–those <span class="e2">līlā</span>–Pastimes. [14]
For a long time, Māyā Devī hid the confidential scriptures that existed about His Pastimes.
অপ্রকট শাস্ত্র বহু রহে যথা তথা ।<br />প্রকট শাস্ত্রেও যত চৈতন্যের কথা ॥১৫॥
সে সকল মায়াদেবী পণ্ডিত নয়ন ।<br />আবরিয়া রাখে গুপ্তভাবে অনুক্ষণ ॥১৬॥
aprakaṭa śāstra bahu rahe yathā tathā<br />prakaṭa śāstreo yata chaitanyera kathā [15]
se sakala māyā-devī paṇḍita nayana<br />āvariyā rākhe gupta-bhāve anukṣaṇa [16]
<span class="e2">māyā-devī</span>–Māyā Devī <span class="e2">āvariyā</span>–covered <span class="e2">paṇḍita</span> <span class="e2">nayana</span>–the eyes of the scholars [and] <span class="e2">anukṣaṇa</span>–at all times <span class="e2">rākhe</span>–kept <span class="e2">gupta-bhāve</span>–secret <span class="e2">yata se sakala</span>–all <span class="e2">kathā</span>–the descriptions <span class="e2">chaitanyera</span>–of Śrī Chaitanya <span class="e2">prakaṭa</span> <span class="e2">śāstreo</span>–throughout both the manifest scriptures [and] <span class="e2">bahu</span>–the numerous <span class="e2">aprakaṭa</span>–unmanifest <span class="e2">śāstra</span>–scriptures <span class="e2">rahe</span>–that existed <span class="e2">yathā</span> <span class="e2">tathā</span>–here and there. [15<span class="e2">–</span>16]
Māyā Devī covered the eyes of the scholars and at all times kept secret all the descriptions of Śrī Chaitanya throughout both the manifest and unmanifest scriptures.
গৌরের গম্ভীর লীলা হৈলে অপ্রকট ।<br />প্রভু-ইচ্ছা জানি’ মায়া হয় অকপট ॥১৭॥
gaurera gambhīra līlā haile aprakaṭa<br />prabhu-ichchhā jāni’ māyā haya akapaṭa [17]
[When] <span class="e2">gambhīra</span>–the deep <span class="e2">līlā</span>–Pastimes <span class="e2">gaurera</span>–of Śrī Gaura <span class="e2">haile</span>–became <span class="e2">aprakaṭa</span>–unmanifest, <span class="e2">māyā</span>–Māyā <span class="e2">jāni’</span>–understood <span class="e2">prabhu-ichchhā</span>–the will of the Lord [and] <span class="e2">akapaṭa haya</span>–became non-deceitful. [17]
When the deep Pastimes of Śrī Gaura became unmanifest, Māyā understood the will of the Lord and withdrew her deception.
উঠাইয়া লৈল জাল জীবচক্ষু হৈতে ।<br />প্রকাশিল গৌরতত্ত্ব এ জড় জগতে ॥১৮॥
uṭhāiyā laila jāla jīva-chakṣu haite<br />prakāśila gaura-tattva e jaḍa jagate [18]
<span class="e2">māyā</span>–Māyā <span class="e2">uṭhāiyā</span> <span class="e2">laila</span>–lifted <span class="e2">jāla</span>–[her] veil <span class="e2">haite</span>–from <span class="e2">jīva-chakṣu</span>–from the eyes of the souls [and] <span class="e2">prakāśila</span>–revealed <span class="e2">gaura-tattva</span>–the truth about Śrī Gaura <span class="e2">e</span> <span class="e2">jaḍa</span> <span class="e2">jagate</span>–to the material world. [18]
Māyā lifted her veil from the eyes of the souls and revealed the truth about Śrī Gaura to the material world.
গুপ্তশাস্ত্র অনায়াসে হইল প্রকট ।<br />ঘুচিল জীবের যত যুক্তির সঙ্কট ॥১৯॥
gupta-śāstra anāyāse ha-ila prakaṭa<br />ghuchila jīvera yata yuktira saṅkaṭa [19]
<span class="e2">gupta-śāstra</span>–The hidden scriptures [then] <span class="e2">prakaṭa ha-ila</span>–appeared <span class="e2">anāyāse</span>–clearly [and] <span class="e2">ghuchila</span>–dispelled <span class="e2">yuktira</span> <span class="e2">saṅkaṭa</span>–the doubts <span class="e2">yata</span> <span class="e2">jīvera</span>–of all souls. [19]
The hidden scriptures then appeared clearly and dispelled the doubts of all souls.
বড়ই দয়ালু প্রভু নিত্যানন্দরায় ।<br />গৌরতত্ত্ব প্রকাশিল জীবের হিয়ায় ॥২০॥
baḍa-i dayālu prabhu nityānanda-rāya<br />gaura-tattva prakāśila jīvera hiyāya [20]
[The] <span class="e2">baḍa-i</span>–extremely <span class="e2">dayālu</span>–merciful <span class="e2">prabhu</span>–Lord, <span class="e2">nityānanda-rāya</span>–Nityānanda Rāy, <span class="e2">prakāśila</span>–revealed <span class="e2">gaura-tattva</span>–the truth about Śrī Gaura <span class="e2">jīvera</span> <span class="e2">hiyāya</span>–in the hearts of the souls. [20]
The extremely merciful Nityānanda Prabhu revealed the truth about Śrī Gaura in the hearts of the souls.
তাঁর আজ্ঞা পেয়ে মায়া ছাড়ে আবরণ ।<br />সুভক্ত পণ্ডিতগণ পায় শাস্ত্র-ধন ॥২১॥
tā̐ra ājñā peye māyā chhāḍe āvaraṇa<br />subhakta paṇḍita-gaṇa pāya śāstra-dhana [21]
<span class="e2">peye</span>–Receiving <span class="e2">tā̐ra</span>–His <span class="e2">ājñā</span>–order, <span class="e2">māyā</span>–Māyā <span class="e2">chhāḍe</span>–removed <span class="e2">āvaraṇa</span>–[her] veil, [and] <span class="e2">subhakta paṇḍita-gaṇa</span>–the wise devotees <span class="e2">pāya</span>–discovered <span class="e2">śāstra-dhana</span>–the wealth of the scriptures. [21]
Receiving His order, Māyā removed her veil, and the wise devotees discovered the wealth of the scriptures.
ইহাতে সন্দেহ যার না হয় খণ্ডন ।<br />সে অভাগা বৃথা কেন ধরয় জীবন ॥২২॥
ihāte sandeha yāra nā haya khaṇḍana<br />se abhāgā vṛthā kena dharaya jīvana [22]
<span class="e2">yāra se</span>–Those whose <span class="e2">sandeha</span>–doubts <span class="e2">khaṇḍana haya nā</span>–are not dispelled <span class="e2">ihāte</span>–by this [are] <span class="e2">abhāgā</span>–unfortunate. <span class="e2">kena</span>–Why <span class="e2">jīvana dharaya</span>–do [they] continue [their] lives <span class="e2">vṛthā</span>–meaninglessly? [22]
Those whose doubts are not dispelled by this are unfortunate. Why do such persons meaninglessly continue their lives?
যে কালে ঈশ্বর যেই কৃপা বিতরয় ।<br />ভাগ্যবন্ত জন তাহে বড় সুখী হয় ॥২৩॥
ye kāle īśvara yei kṛpā vitaraya<br />bhāgyavanta jana tāhe baḍa sukhī haya [23]
<span class="e2">ye</span> <span class="e2">kāle</span>–Whenever [and] <span class="e2">yei tāhe</span>–howsoever <span class="e2">īśvara</span>–the Lord <span class="e2">kṛpā</span> <span class="e2">vitaraya</span>–bestows [His] mercy, <span class="e2">bhāgyavanta</span>–the fortunate <span class="e2">jana</span>–souls <span class="e2">haya</span>–become <span class="e2">baḍa</span>–extremely <span class="e2">sukhī</span>–happy. [23]
Whenever and howsoever the Lord bestows His mercy, the fortunate souls become extremely happy.
দুর্ভাগা লক্ষণ এই জান সর্ব্বজন ।<br />নিজ বুদ্ধি বড় বলি’ করিয়া গণন ॥২৪॥
ঈশ্বরের কৃপা নাহি করয় স্বীকার ।<br />কুতর্কে মায়ার গর্ত্তে পড়ে বারবার ॥২৫॥
durbhāgā lakṣaṇa ei jāna sarva-jana<br />nija buddhi baḍa bali’ kariyā gaṇana [24]
īśvarera kṛpā nāhi karaya svīkāra<br />kutarke māyāra garte paḍe bāra-bāra [25]
<span class="e2">sarva-jana</span>–Everyone <span class="e2">jāna</span>–should know <span class="e2">ei</span>–the <span class="e2">lakṣaṇa</span>–symptoms <span class="e2">durbhāgā</span>–of misfortune: <span class="e2">gaṇana kariyā</span>–considering [their] <span class="e2">nija</span>–own <span class="e2">buddhi</span>–intelligence <span class="e2">bali’</span>–to be<span class="e2"> baḍa</span>–great, [souls] <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–do not <span class="e2">svīkāra karaya</span>–accept <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–the mercy <span class="e2">īśvarera</span>–of the Lord. <span class="e2">kutarke</span>–Through false arguments, <span class="e2">paḍe</span>–souls fall <span class="e2">māyāra garte</span>–in Māyā’s traps <span class="e2">bāra-bāra</span>–again and again. [24<span class="e2">–</span>25]
Everyone should know the symptoms of misfortune: to consider your own intelligence to be great and not accept the mercy of the Lord. Through false arguments, souls fall into Māyā’s traps again and again.
“এস হে কলির জীব ছাড় কুটিনাটি ।<br />নির্ম্মল গৌরাঙ্গ-প্রেম লহ পরিপাটি” ॥২৬॥
“esa he kalira jīva chhāḍa kuṭināṭi<br />nirmala gaurāṅga-prema laha paripāṭi” [26]
<span class="e2">“he</span>–“O <span class="e2">jīva</span>–souls <span class="e2">kalira</span>–of Kali-yuga, <span class="e2">esa</span>–come! <span class="e2">chhāḍa</span>–Give up <span class="e2">kuṭināṭi</span>–duplicity, [and] <span class="e2">laha</span>–accept <span class="e2">nirmala</span>–pure <span class="e2">gaurāṅga-prema</span>–divine love for Śrī Gaurāṅga <span class="e2">paripāṭi”</span>–in full!” [26]
“O souls of Kali-yuga, come! Give up duplicity, and accept pure divine love for Śrī Gaurāṅga in full!”
এই বলি’ নিত্যানন্দ ডাকে বারবার ।<br />তবু ত দুর্ভাগা জন না করে স্বীকার ॥২৭॥
ei bali’ nityānanda ḍāke bāra-bāra<br />tabu ta durbhāgā jana nā kare svīkāra [27]
<span class="e2">bali’</span>–Saying <span class="e2">ei</span>–this, <span class="e2">nityānanda</span>–Nityānanda <span class="e2">ḍāke</span>–calls out <span class="e2">bāra-bāra</span>–again and again. <span class="e2">tabu</span> <span class="e2">ta</span>–Still, <span class="e2">durbhāgā</span>–unfortunate <span class="e2">jana</span>–souls <span class="e2">svīkāra kare nā</span>–do not accept. [27]
Saying this, Nityānanda calls out again and again. Still, unfortunate souls do not accept.
কেন যে এমন প্রেমে করে অনাদর ।<br />বিচার করিয়া দেখ হইয়া তৎপর ॥২৮॥
kena ye emana preme kare anādara<br />vichāra kariyā dekha ha-iyā tatpara [28]
<span class="e2">vichāra kariyā dekha</span>–Let us consider <span class="e2">tatpara ha-iyā</span>–carefully <span class="e2">kena</span>–why <span class="e2">ye</span>–they <span class="e2">anādara kare</span>–disregard <span class="e2">emana</span>–such <span class="e2">preme</span>–divine love. [28]
Let us consider carefully why souls disregard divine love.
সুখ লাগি সর্ব্বজীব নানা যুক্তি করে ।<br />তর্ক করে যোগ করে সংসার ভিতরে ॥২৯॥
sukha-lāgi sarva-jīva nānā yukti kare<br />tarka kare yoga kare saṁsāra bhitare [29]
