When will I go to that assembly, bow from a distance, and then join them? Hearing accounts from the mouth of Vyāsadev of Gaura’s Pastimes of delivering the fallen souls, I will sigh with divine love.
কতক্ষণ পরে পুনঃ সভা না দেখিয়া ।<br />কাঁদিব “গৌরাঙ্গ” বলি’ ভূমে লুটাইয়া ॥<br />দ্বিপ্রহর দিনে ক্ষুধা হইলে উদয় ।<br />ভোজনার্থে বনফল করিব সঞ্চয় ॥১২৮॥
kata-kṣaṇa pare punaḥ sabhā nā dekhiyā<br />kā̐diba “gaurāṅga” bali’ bhūme luṭāiyā<br />dviprahara dine kṣudhā ha-ile udaya<br />bhojanārthe vana-phala kariba sañchaya [128]
<span class="e2">pare</span>–After <span class="e2">kata-kṣaṇa</span>–some time, <span class="e2">nā</span>–not <span class="e2">dekhiyā</span>–seeing <span class="e2">sabhā</span>–the assembly <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–any more, <span class="e2">kā̐diba bali’</span>–I will cry out <span class="e2">“gaurāṅga”</span>–“Gaurāṅga” [and] <span class="e2">luṭāiyā</span>–roll <span class="e2">bhūme</span>–on the ground. <span class="e2">kṣudhā udaya ha-ile</span>–When I feel hungry <span class="e2">dviprahara</span> <span class="e2">dine</span>–at midday, <span class="e2">sañchaya</span> <span class="e2">kariba</span>–I will collect <span class="e2">vana-phala</span>–fruits from the forest <span class="e2">bhojanārthe</span>–to eat. [128]
After some time, no longer seeing the assembly, I will cry out “Gaurāṅga” and roll on the ground. When I feel hungry at midday, I will collect fruits from the forest to eat.
এ মত সময়ে কৃষ্ণা পাণ্ডব-গৃহিণী ।<br />শাক অন্ন লয়ে কবে আসিবে অমনি ॥<br />বলিবেন, “বৎস লহ আতিথ্য আমার ।<br />গৌরাঙ্গ-প্রসাদ অন্নমুষ্টি দুই চার” ॥১২৯॥
e mata samaye kṛṣṇā pāṇḍava-gṛhiṇī<br />śāka anna laye kabe āsibe amani<br />balibena, “vatsa laha ātithya āmāra<br />gaurāṅga-prasāda anna-muṣṭi dui chāra” [129]
<span class="e2">kabe</span>–When [will] <span class="e2">kṛṣṇā</span>–Draupadī, <span class="e2">pāṇḍava-gṛhiṇī</span>–the wife of the Pāṇḍavas, <span class="e2">amani</span>–quickly <span class="e2">laye</span> <span class="e2">āsibe</span>–bring <span class="e2">śāka</span>–cooked greens [and] <span class="e2">anna</span>–rice <span class="e2">e mata</span> <span class="e2">samaye</span>–at that time, [and] <span class="e2">balibena</span>–say, <span class="e2">“vatsa</span>–“[My] child, <span class="e2">laha</span>–take <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my <span class="e2">ātithya</span>–offering [of] <span class="e2">dui</span>–two [or] <span class="e2">chāra</span>–four <span class="e2">anna-muṣṭi prasāda</span>–handfuls of rice-remnants <span class="e2">gaurāṅga”</span>–from Gaurāṅga”? [129]
When will Draupadī, the wife of the Pāṇḍavas, then quickly bring some rice and śāk and say, “My child, take my offering of a few handfuls of Gaurāṅga’s prasād”?
সাষ্টাঙ্গে প্রণমি’ তাঁরে আমি অকিঞ্চন ।<br />কর পাতি’ শাক অন্ন করিব গ্রহণ ॥<br />গৌরাঙ্গপ্রসাদ অন্ন শাক চমৎকার ।<br />সেবা করি’ ধন্য হবে রসনা আমার ॥১৩০॥
sāṣṭāṅge praṇami’ tā̐re āmi akiñchana<br />kara pāti’ śāka anna kariba grahaṇa<br />gaurāṅga-prasāda anna śāka chamatkāra<br />sevā kari’ dhanya habe rasanā āmāra [130]
<span class="e2">āmi</span>–I, [as] <span class="e2">akiñchana</span>–a surrendered soul, <span class="e2">sāṣṭāṅge</span> <span class="e2">praṇami’</span>–will prostrate myself <span class="e2">tā̐re</span>–before her, <span class="e2">pāti’</span>–extend [my] <span class="e2">kara</span>–hands, [and] <span class="e2">grahaṇa kariba</span>–accept <span class="e2">śāka</span>–the greens [and] <span class="e2">anna</span>–rice. <span class="e2">sevā</span> <span class="e2">kari’</span>–Honouring <span class="e2">gaurāṅga</span>–Gaurāṅga’s <span class="e2">chamatkāra</span>–wonderful <span class="e2">anna</span>–rice [and] <span class="e2">śāka</span>–greens <span class="e2">prasāda</span>–prasād, <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my <span class="e2">rasanā</span>–tongue <span class="e2">habe</span>–will be <span class="e2">dhanya</span>–blessed. [130]
I, as a surrendered soul, will prostrate myself before her, extend my hands, and accept the rice and śāk. Honouring Gaurāṅga’s wonderful rice and śāk prasād, my tongue will be blessed.
মহাপ্রসাদের কৃপা যেই জীবে হয় ।<br />শুদ্ধকৃষ্ণভক্তি তার মিলিবে নিশ্চয় ॥<br />সেই কৃপা নিত্য যেন হয় ত আমার ।<br />অনায়াসে ছাড়ি’ যাব অনন্ত মায়ার ॥১৩১॥
mahāprasādera kṛpā yei jīve haya<br />śuddha-kṛṣṇa-bhakti tāra milibe niśchaya<br />sei kṛpā nitya yena haya ta āmāra<br />anāyāse chhāḍi’ yāba ananta māyāra [131]
<span class="e2">yei jīve tāra</span>–A soul who <span class="e2">haya</span>–receives <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–the grace <span class="e2">mahāprasādera</span>–of mahāprasād <span class="e2">niśchaya milibe</span>–will certainly attain <span class="e2">śuddha-kṛṣṇa-bhakti</span>–pure devotion to Kṛṣṇa. [May] <span class="e2">nitya</span> <span class="e2">āmāra ta haya</span>–I eternally receive <span class="e2">sei</span>–such <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–grace <span class="e2">yena</span>–so that <span class="e2">anāyāse</span> <span class="e2">chhāḍi’ yāba</span>–I may easily leave behind <span class="e2">māyāra ananta</span>–the unending illusion. [131]
A soul who receives the grace of mahāprasād will certainly attain pure devotion to Kṛṣṇa. May I eternally receive such grace so that I may easily leave behind the unending illusion.
দৌপদী-প্রদত্ত মহাপ্রসাদ পাইয়া ।<br />উপনীত হব কবে রুদ্রদ্বীপে গিয়া ॥<br />কৈলাস যাঁহার প্রভা মাত্র ত্রিভুবনে ।<br />সেই রুদ্রদ্বীপ শোভে নবদ্বীপবনে ॥১৩২॥
draupadī-pradatta mahāprasāda pāiyā<br />upanīta haba kabe rudradvīpe giyā<br />kailāsa yā̐hāra prabhā mātra tribhuvane<br />sei rudradvīpa śobhe navadvīpa-vane [132]
<span class="e2">kabe</span>–When <span class="e2">pāiyā</span>–will I receive <span class="e2">mahāprasāda</span>–mahāprasād <span class="e2">draupadī-pradatta</span>–given by Draupadī [and] <span class="e2">giyā upanīta</span> <span class="e2">haba</span>–arrive <span class="e2">rudradvīpe</span>–in Rudradwīp? <span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">rudradvīpa</span>–Rudradwīp, <span class="e2">yā̐hāra</span>–whose <span class="e2">prabhā</span>–lustre <span class="e2">tribhuvane</span>–in the three worlds [can be compared] <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only <span class="e2">kailāsa</span>–to Mount Kailās, <span class="e2">śobhe</span>–shines <span class="e2">navadvīpa-vane</span>–in the forests of Nabadwīp. [132]
When will I receive mahāprasād given by Draupadī and then arrive in Rudradwīp? Rudradwīp, whose lustre can be compared in the three worlds only to Mount Kailās, shines in the forests of Nabadwīp.
যথা নীল লোহিতাদি রুদ্র একাদশ ।<br />নৃত্য করে গৌরপ্রেমে হইয়া বিবশ ॥<br />যথায় দুর্ব্বাসামুনি করিয়া আশ্রম ।<br />গৌরাঙ্গচরণ ভজে ছাড়ি’ যোগভ্রম ॥১৩৩॥
yathā nīla lohitādi rudra ekādaśa<br />nṛtya kare gaura-preme ha-iyā vivaśa<br />yathāya durvāsā-muni kariyā āśrama<br />gaurāṅga-charaṇa bhaje chhāḍi’ yoga-bhrama [133]
<span class="e2">yathā</span>–Here, <span class="e2">ekādaśa</span>–the eleven <span class="e2">nīla</span>–blue, <span class="e2">lohitādi</span>–red, and other complexioned <span class="e2">rudra</span>–Rudras <span class="e2">nṛtya</span> <span class="e2">kare</span>–dance, <span class="e2">vivaśa ha-iyā</span>–overwhelmed <span class="e2">gaura-preme</span>–with divine love for Gaura. <span class="e2">yathāya</span>–Here, <span class="e2">durvāsā-muni</span>–the sage Durvāsā <span class="e2">āśrama kariyā</span>–took shelter, <span class="e2">chhāḍi’</span>–gave up [his] <span class="e2">yoga-bhrama</span>–mistaken yoga practice, [and] <span class="e2">bhaje</span>–worshipped <span class="e2">gaurāṅga-charaṇa</span>–the feet of Gaurāṅga. [133]
Here, the eleven Rudras, who are of blue, red, and other complexions, dance, overwhelmed with divine love for Gaura. Here, Durvāsā Muni took shelter, gave up his mistaken yoga practice, and worshipped the feet of Gaurāṅga.
অষ্টাবক্র-দত্তাত্রের-আদি যোগিগণ ।<br />ছাড়িয়া অদ্বৈত-বুদ্ধি সহ পঞ্চানন ॥<br />শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্যপদধ্যানে হয় রত ।<br />সাযুজ্য মুক্তিতে ছাড়ে হইয়া বিরত ॥১৩৪॥
aṣṭāvakra-dattātreya-ādi yogi-gaṇa<br />chhāḍiyā advaita-buddhi saha pañchānana<br />śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-pada-dhyāne haya rata<br />sāyujya muktike chhāḍe ha-iyā virata [134]
<span class="e2">aṣṭāvakra-dattātreya</span>-<span class="e2">ādi yogi-gaṇa</span>–Aṣṭāvakra, Dattātreya, and other yogīs, <span class="e2">saha</span>–along with <span class="e2">pañchānana</span>–Lord Śiva, <span class="e2">chhāḍiyā</span>–abandoned <span class="e2">advaita-buddhi</span>–monistic thought [and] <span class="e2">rata haya</span>–engaged in <span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-pada-dhyāne</span>–meditation on the feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya. <span class="e2">chhāḍe</span>–They rejected <span class="e2">sāyujya</span> <span class="e2">muktike</span>–sāyujya-mukti (immersion into the effulgence or body of the Lord), <span class="e2">virata ha-iyā</span>–having become disinterested [in it]. [134]
Here, Aṣṭāvakra, Dattātreya, and other yogīs, along with Lord Śiva, abandoned monistic thought and meditated on the feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya. They rejected the liberation of immersion into the Absolute, having become disinterested in it.
কভু আমি ভ্রমিতে ভ্রমিতে রুদ্রবন ।<br />মেঢ্রস্থল-সন্নিকটে করিব গমন ॥<br />বসিব তথায় গৌরপদ-ধ্যান করি’ ।<br />অদূরে দেখিব দেবী পরমা সুন্দরী ॥১৩৫॥
kabhu āmi bhramite bhramite rudravana<br />meḍhra-sthala-sannikaṭe kariba gamana<br />basiba tathāya gaura-pada-dhyāna kari’<br />adūre dekhiba devī paramā sundarī [135]
<span class="e2">kabhu</span>–Sometimes <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">bhramite</span> <span class="e2">bhramite</span>–will roam <span class="e2">rudravana</span>–throughout Rudravan [and] <span class="e2">sannikaṭe gamana kariba</span>–visit <span class="e2">meḍhra</span>-<span class="e2">sthala</span>–Meḍhra Sthal (the place of a Śiva-liṅga). <span class="e2">basiba</span>–I will sit <span class="e2">tathāya</span>–there <span class="e2">dhyāna kari’</span>–meditating <span class="e2">gaura-pada</span>–on the feet of Gaura [and] <span class="e2">dekhiba</span>–see [an] <span class="e2">paramā</span>–extremely <span class="e2">sundarī</span>–beautiful <span class="e2">devī</span>–goddess <span class="e2">adūre</span>–nearby. [135]
Sometimes I will roam throughout the forest of Rudravan and visit Meḍhra Sthal. I will sit there meditating on the feet of Gaura and see an extremely beautiful goddess nearby.
বনদেবী মনে করি’ করিব প্রণাম ।<br />জিজ্ঞাসিব, “বল মাতা কিবা তব নাম” ॥<br />অশ্রুমুখী দেবী তবে বলিবে বচন ।<br />“শুন বাছা মোর দুঃখ অকথ্যকথন ॥১৩৬॥
vana-devī mane kari’ kariba praṇāma<br />jijñāsiba, “bala mātā kibā tava nāma”<br />aśru-mukhī devī tabe balibe vachana<br />“śuna vāchhā mora duḥkha akathya-kathana [136]
<span class="e2">mane</span> <span class="e2">kari’</span>–Considering [her] <span class="e2">vana-devī</span>–a forest goddess, <span class="e2">praṇāma</span> <span class="e2">kariba</span>–I will bow [and] <span class="e2">jijñāsiba</span>–ask <span class="e2">“mātā</span>–“O Mother, <span class="e2">bala</span>–tell [me,]<span class="e2"> kibā</span>–what [is] <span class="e2">tava</span>–your <span class="e2">nāma</span>–name?” <span class="e2">tabe</span>–Then, <span class="e2">aśru-mukhī</span>–with a crying face, <span class="e2">devī</span>–the goddess <span class="e2">vachana</span> <span class="e2">balibe</span>–will say, <span class="e2">“śuna</span>–“Listen <span class="e2">vāchhā</span>–child, <span class="e2">mora</span>–my <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–sorrow [is] <span class="e2">akathya-kathana</span>–indescribable. [136]
Considering her a forest goddess, I will bow to her and ask, “O Mother, please tell me your name.” Then, with tears in her eyes, the goddess will say, “Listen child, my sorrow is impossible to describe.
পঞ্চবিধ জ্ঞান কন্যা মোরা পঞ্চজন ।<br />পঞ্চবিধ মুক্তি নাম করেছ শ্রবণ ॥<br />সালোক্য সামীপ্য সাষ্টি সারূপ্য নির্ব্বাণ ।<br />নির্ব্বাণ-সাযুজ্য মোরে নাম কৈল দান ॥১৩৭॥
pañcha-vidha jñāna kanyā morā pañcha-jana<br />pañcha-vidha mukti nāma karechha śravaṇa<br />sālokya sāmīpya sārṣṭi sārūpya nirvāṇa<br />nirvāṇa-sāyujya more nāma kaila dāna [137]
<span class="e2">morā</span>–I [am one of] <span class="e2">pañcha-jana kanyā</span>–the five daughters <span class="e2">pañcha-vidha</span> <span class="e2">jñāna</span>–of the five types of knowledge. <span class="e2">śravaṇa karechha</span>–You have heard <span class="e2">nāma</span>–the names <span class="e2">pañcha-vidha</span> <span class="e2">mukti</span>–of the five types of liberation: <span class="e2">sālokya</span>–sālokya (residing in the Lord’s abode), <span class="e2">sāmīpya</span>–sāmīpya (being in the Lord’s presence), <span class="e2">sārṣṭi</span>–sārṣṭi (having opulence like the Lord’s), <span class="e2">sārūpya</span>–sārūpya (having a form like the Lord’s), [and] <span class="e2">nirvāṇa</span>–cessation, sāyujya (merging into the Lord). [My father] <span class="e2">dāna kaila</span>–gave <span class="e2">more</span>–me <span class="e2">nāma</span>–the names <span class="e2">nirvāṇa-sāyujya</span>–Nirvāṇa and Sāyujya. [137]
“I am one of the daughters of the five types of knowledge. You have heard the names of the five types of liberation: sālokya, sāmīpya, sārṣṭi, sārūpya, and nirvāṇa. My father gave me the names Nirvāṇa and Sāyujya.
চারি ভগ্নী গেলা চলি’ বৈকুণ্ঠনগর ।<br />আমি ত’ রহিনু একা পড়িয়া ফাঁপর ॥<br />শিবের কৃপায় দত্তাত্রের আদিজন ।<br />কিছুদিন আমা-প্রতি করিল যতন ॥১৩৮॥
chāri bhagnī gelā chali’ vaikuṇṭha-nagara<br />āmi ta’ rahinu ekā paḍiyā phā̐para<br />śivera kṛpāya dattātreya-ādi-jana<br />kichhu-dina āmā-prati karila yatana [138]
[My] <span class="e2">chāri</span>–four <span class="e2">bhagnī</span>–sisters <span class="e2">chali’</span> <span class="e2">gelā</span>–went <span class="e2">vaikuṇṭha-nagara</span>–to Vaikuṇṭha Dhām. <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">ta’</span> <span class="e2">rahinu</span>–have stayed behind, <span class="e2">ekā</span>–alone [and] <span class="e2">phā̐para paḍiyā</span>–bewildered. <span class="e2">śivera</span> <span class="e2">kṛpāya</span>–By Śiva’s mercy, <span class="e2">dattātreya</span>–Dattātreya [and] <span class="e2">ādi-jana</span>–and other sages <span class="e2">yatana karila</span>–cared <span class="e2">āmā-prati</span>–for me <span class="e2">kichhu-dina</span>–for some time. [138]
“My four sisters—Sālokya, Sārūpya, Sāmīpya, and Sārṣṭi—went to Vaikuṇṭha. Only I have stayed behind, alone and bewildered. By Śiva’s mercy, Dattātreya and other sages cared for me for some time.
এবে সেই ঋষিগণ ছাড়িয়া আমায় ।<br />রুদ্রদ্বীপে বৈসে এই সর্ব্বলোকে গায় ॥<br />বৃথা আমি অন্বেষণ করি সেই সবে ।<br />দেখা নাহি পাই আর পাব কোথা কবে ॥১৩৯॥
ebe sei ṛṣi-gaṇa chhāḍiyā āmāya<br />rudradvīpe vaise ei sarva-loke gāya<br />vṛthā āmi anveṣaṇa kari sei sabe<br />dekhā nāhi pāi āra pāba kothā kabe [139]
<span class="e2">ebe</span>–Now <span class="e2">sarva-loke</span>–everyone <span class="e2">gāya</span>–says <span class="e2">ei</span>–that <span class="e2">sei</span>–those <span class="e2">ṛṣi-gaṇa</span>–sages <span class="e2">chhāḍiyā</span>–have rejected <span class="e2">āmāya</span>–me [and] <span class="e2">vaise</span>–taken up residence <span class="e2">rudradvīpe</span>–in Rudradwīp. <span class="e2">vṛthā</span>–In vain, <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">anveṣaṇa</span> <span class="e2">kari</span>–search, [but] <span class="e2">dekhā</span> <span class="e2">pāi nāhi</span>–I have not found <span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">sabe</span>–them. <span class="e2">kabe</span>–When [and] <span class="e2">kothā</span>–where <span class="e2">pāba</span>–will I find [them] <span class="e2">āra</span>–again? [139]
“Now everyone says that those sages have rejected me and taken up residence in Rudradwīp. In vain, I search for them, but I have not found them. When and where will I find them again?
শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গপ্রভু সর্ব্বজনে নিস্তারিল ।<br />কেবল আমার প্রতি নির্দয় হইল ॥<br />আমি যেই স্থানে এবে ছাড়িব জীবন ।<br />নিদয়া বলিয়া স্থান জানু সর্ব্বজন” ॥১৪০॥
śrī-gaurāṅga-prabhu sarva-jane nistārila<br />kevala āmāra prati nirdaya ha-ila<br />āmi yei sthāne ebe chhāḍiba jīvana<br />nidayā baliyā sthāna jānu sarva-jana” [140]
<span class="e2">śrī-gaurāṅga-prabhu</span>–Śrī Gaurāṅga Prabhu <span class="e2">nistārila</span>–delivered <span class="e2">sarva-jane</span>–everyone. <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–He was <span class="e2">kevala</span>–only <span class="e2">nirdaya</span>–merciless <span class="e2">prati</span>–towards <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–me. <span class="e2">sarva-jana</span>–Everyone <span class="e2">jānu</span>–will know <span class="e2">yei</span> <span class="e2">sthāne sthāna</span>–the place where <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">ebe</span> <span class="e2">chhāḍiba</span>–will now give up [my] <span class="e2">jīvana</span>–life <span class="e2">baliyā</span>–as <span class="e2">nidayā”</span>–‘Nidayā’ (‘Merciless’)”. [140]
“Śrī Gaurāṅga Prabhu delivered everyone. He was only merciless towards me. Everyone will know the place where I will now give up my life as ‘Nidayā’ (‘Merciless’).”
সাযুজ্যের নাম শুনি’ কাঁপিবে হৃদয় ।<br />পূতনা রাক্ষসী বলি’ হবে বড় ভয় ॥<br />আঁখি মুদি’ সেই স্থানে পড়িয়া রহিব ।<br />কোন মহাজনস্পর্শে তখন উঠিব ॥১৪১॥
sāyujyera nāma śuni’ kā̐pibe hṛdaya<br />pūtanā rākṣasī bali’ habe baḍa bhaya<br />ā̐khi mudi’ sei sthāne paḍiyā rahiba<br />kona mahājana-sparśe takhana uṭhiba [141]
<span class="e2">śuni’</span>–Hearing <span class="e2">nāma</span>–the name <span class="e2">sāyujyera</span>–of Sāyujya, [my] <span class="e2">hṛdaya</span>–heart <span class="e2">kā̐pibe</span>–will tremble [and] <span class="e2">habe</span>–will be stricken [with] <span class="e2">baḍa</span>–intense <span class="e2">bhaya</span>–fear <span class="e2">bali’</span>–as though [she is] <span class="e2">rākṣasī</span>–the demoness <span class="e2">pūtanā</span>–Pūtanā. <span class="e2">mudi’</span>–I will close [my] <span class="e2">ā̐khi</span>–eyes [and] <span class="e2">paḍiyā</span> <span class="e2">rahiba</span>–fall down <span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">sthāne</span>–there. <span class="e2">takhana</span>–Then, <span class="e2">uṭhiba</span>–I will arise <span class="e2">kona</span> <span class="e2">mahājana-sparśe</span>–at the touch of some great soul. [141]
Hearing the name Sāyujya, my heart will tremble and become stricken with intense fear as though she is the demoness Pūtanā. I will close my eyes and fall to the ground. Then, I will arise at the touch of some great soul.
উঠিয়া দেখিব আমি দেবপঞ্চানন ।<br />“ববম্ ববম্” বলি’ করিয়া নর্ত্তন ॥<br />গাইবেন, “শ্রীশচীনন্দন দয়াময় ।<br />দয়া কর সর্ব্বজীবে দূর কর ভয়” ॥১৪২॥
uṭhiyā dekhiba āmi deva-pañchānana<br />“babam babam” bali’ kariyā nartana<br />gāibena, “śrī-śachī-nandana dayāmaya<br />dayā kara sarva-jīve dūra kara bhaya” [142]
<span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">uṭhiyā</span>–will arise [and] <span class="e2">dekhiba</span>–see <span class="e2">deva-pañchānana</span>–Lord Śiva <span class="e2">nartana kariyā</span>–dancing [and] <span class="e2">bali’</span>–exclaiming, <span class="e2">“babam</span>–Babam! <span class="e2">babam”</span>–Babam!” <span class="e2">gāibena</span>–He will sing, <span class="e2">“śrī-śachī-nandana</span>–“O son of Śachī! <span class="e2">dayāmaya</span>–O merciful Lord! <span class="e2">dayā</span> <span class="e2">kara</span>–Bless <span class="e2">sarva-jīve</span>–all souls, [and] <span class="e2">dūra</span> <span class="e2">kara</span>–drive away [their] <span class="e2">bhaya”</span>–fear!” [142]
I will arise and see Lord Śiva dancing and exclaiming, “Babam! Babam!” He will sing, “O son of Śachī! O merciful Lord! Please bless all souls and drive away their fear!”
দেবদেব মহাদেবচরণে পড়িব ।<br />স্বভাব-শোধন লাগি’ পদে নিবেদিব ॥<br />দয়া করি’ বিশ্বেশ্বর মস্তক আমার ।<br />ধরিয়া চরণ দিবে উপদেশ-সার ॥১৪৩॥
deva-deva mahādeva-charaṇe paḍiba<br />svabhāva-śodhana lāgi’ pade nivediba<br />dayā kari’ viśveśvara mastaka āmāra<br />dhariyā charaṇa dibe upadeśa-sāra [143]
<span class="e2">paḍiba</span>–I will bow <span class="e2">mahādeva-charaṇe</span>–at the feet of Mahādev, <span class="e2">deva-deva</span>–the god of gods, [and] <span class="e2">nivediba</span>–pray <span class="e2">pade</span>–at [his] feet <span class="e2">lāgi’</span>–for <span class="e2">svabhāva-śodhana</span>–the purification of my nature. <span class="e2">dayā</span> <span class="e2">kari’</span>–Mercifully, <span class="e2">viśveśvara</span>–the lord of the universe <span class="e2">dhariyā</span>–will place [his] <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet <span class="e2">āmāra mastaka</span>–on my head [and] <span class="e2">dibe</span>–give [me] <span class="e2">upadeśa-sāra</span>–nectarean instructions. [143]
I will bow at the feet of Mahādev, the god of gods, and pray at his feet for the purification of my heart. Mercifully, the lord of the universe will place his feet on my head and give me nectarean instructions.
বলিবেন, “ওহে শুন কৃষ্ণভক্তি সার ।<br />জ্ঞান-কর্ম্ম-মুক্তিচেষ্টা যোগ আদি ছার ॥<br />আমার কৃপায় তুমি পরাজিয়া মায়া ।<br />অতি শীঘ্র প্রাপ্ত হবে গৌরপদছায়া ॥১৪৪॥
balibena, “ohe śuna kṛṣṇa-bhakti sāra<br />jñāna-karma-mukti-cheṣṭā yoga ādi chhāra<br />āmāra kṛpāya tumi parājiyā māyā<br />ati śīghra prāpta habe gaura-pada-chhāyā [144]
<span class="e2">balibena</span>–He will say, <span class="e2">“ohe</span>–“Hey, <span class="e2">śuna</span>–listen! <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-bhakti</span>–Devotion to Kṛṣṇa [is] <span class="e2">sāra</span>–supreme. <span class="e2">jñāna</span>–Renunciation, <span class="e2">karma</span>–exploitation, <span class="e2">yoga</span>–yoga, <span class="e2">ādi mukti-cheṣṭā</span>–and other endeavours for liberation [are] <span class="e2">chhāra</span>–useless. <span class="e2">āmāra</span> <span class="e2">kṛpāya</span>–By my grace, <span class="e2">tumi</span>–you <span class="e2">parājiyā</span>–will overcome <span class="e2">māyā</span>–illusion [and] <span class="e2">ati</span>–very <span class="e2">śīghra</span>–quickly <span class="e2">prāpta</span> <span class="e2">habe</span>–attain <span class="e2">gaura-pada-chhāyā</span>–the shade of Gaura’s feet. [144]
He will say, “Listen! Devotion to Kṛṣṇa is supreme. Exploitation, renunciation, yoga, and all other endeavours for liberation are useless. By my grace, you will overcome māyā and very quickly attain the shade of Gaura’s feet.
দক্ষিণে পুলিন দেখ অতি মনোহর ।<br />বৃন্দাবনধাম নবদ্বীপের ভিতর ॥<br />তথা গিয়া কৃষ্ণলীলা কর দরশন ।<br />অচিরে পাইবে রাধিকার শ্রীচরণ” ॥১৪৫॥
dakṣiṇe pulina dekha ati manohara<br />vṛndāvana-dhāma navadvīpera bhitara<br />tathā giyā kṛṣṇa-līlā kara daraśana<br />achire pāibe rādhikāra śrī-charaṇa” [145]
<span class="e2">dakṣiṇe</span>–To the south, <span class="e2">dekha</span>–see [the] <span class="e2">ati</span> <span class="e2">manohara</span>–enchanting <span class="e2">pulina</span>–Śrī Pulina, <span class="e2">vṛndāvana-dhāma</span>–Vṛndāvan Dhām <span class="e2">navadvīpera</span> <span class="e2">bhitara</span>–within Nabadwīp. <span class="e2">giyā</span>–Go <span class="e2">tathā</span>–there [and] <span class="e2">daraśana kara</span>–see <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-līlā</span>–the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. <span class="e2">achire</span>–Soon <span class="e2">pāibe</span>–you will attain <span class="e2">śrī-charaṇa</span>–the holy feet <span class="e2">rādhikāra”</span>–of Śrī Rādhikā.” [145]
“To the south, see the enchanting Śrī Pulina, Vṛndāvan Dhām within Nabadwīp. Go there and see the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. Soon you will attain the holy feet of Śrī Rādhikā.”
শম্ভু অদর্শন হবে উপদেশ দিয়া ।<br />প্রণমি’ চলিব আমি কাঁদিয়া কাঁদিয়া ॥<br />কতক্ষণে শ্রীপুলিন করিয়া দর্শন ।<br />ভূমে গড়াগড়ি দিয়া হব অচেতন ॥১৪৬॥
śambhu adarśana habe upadeśa diyā<br />praṇami’ chaliba āmi kā̐diyā kā̐diyā<br />kata-kṣaṇe śrī-pulina kariyā darśana<br />bhūmi gaḍāgaḍi diyā haba achetana [146]
<span class="e2">śambhu</span>–Lord Śiva <span class="e2">upadeśa</span> <span class="e2">diyā</span>–will instruct [me and then] <span class="e2">adarśana</span> <span class="e2">habe</span>–disappear. <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">praṇami’</span>–will bow [and] <span class="e2">chaliba</span>–depart <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span> <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–crying. <span class="e2">darśana kariyā</span>–Seeing <span class="e2">śrī-pulina</span>–Śrī Pulina <span class="e2">kata-kṣaṇe</span>–after some time, <span class="e2">gaḍāgaḍi</span> <span class="e2">diyā</span>–I will roll <span class="e2">bhūmi</span>–on the ground [and] <span class="e2">achetana haba</span>–faint. [146]
Lord Śiva will instruct me and then disappear. I will bow and depart, crying. Seeing Śrī Pulina after some time, I will roll on the ground and faint.
অচেতনকালে স্বপ্ন-স্বরূপ-সমাধি ॥<br />উদিবে অপূর্ব্ব মূর্ত্তি নিজকার্য্য সাধি’ ॥<br />তখন জানিব আমি কমলমঞ্জরী ।<br />শ্রীঅনঙ্গমঞ্জরীর নিত্য বিধিকারী ॥১৪৭॥
achetana-kāle svapna-svarūpa-samādhi<br />udibe apūrva mūrti nija-kārya sādhi’<br />takhana jāniba āmi kamala-mañjarī<br />śrī-anaṅga-mañjarīra nitya vidhikārī [147]
<span class="e2">achetana-kāle</span>–While unconscious, <span class="e2">svapna-svarūpa-samādhi</span>–in a dream-like trance, <span class="e2">apūrva</span> <span class="e2">mūrti</span>–a wondrous figure <span class="e2">udibe</span>–will appear, <span class="e2">sādhi’</span>–performing <span class="e2">nija-kārya</span>–her duties. <span class="e2">takhana</span>–Then <span class="e2">jāniba</span>–I will understand [that] <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I [am] <span class="e2">kamala-mañjarī</span>–Kamala Mañjarī, <span class="e2">nitya</span> <span class="e2">vidhikārī</span>–the eternal servant <span class="e2">śrī-anaṅga-mañjarīra</span>–of Śrī Anaṅga Mañjarī. [147]
While unconscious, in a dream-like trance, a wondrous figure will appear, performing her duties. Then I will understand that I am Kamala Mañjarī, the eternal servant of Śrī Anaṅga Mañjarī.
অনঙ্গমঞ্জরী মোর হৃদয়-ঈশ্বরী ।<br />দেখাইবে কৃপা করি’ নিজ যূথেশ্বরী ॥<br />শ্রীকর্পূরসেবা মোরে করিবে অর্পণ ।<br />যুগলবিলাস করাইবে প্রদর্শন ॥১৪৮॥
anaṅga-mañjarī mora hṛdaya-īśvarī<br />dekhāibe kṛpā kari’ nija yūtheśvarī<br />śrī-karpūra-sevā more karibe arpaṇa<br />yugala-vilāsa karāibe pradarśana [148]
<span class="e2">anaṅga-mañjarī</span>–Anaṅga Mañjarī [is] <span class="e2">mora</span> <span class="e2">hṛdaya-īśvarī</span>–the mistress of my heart. <span class="e2">kṛpā</span> <span class="e2">kari’</span>–Mercifully, <span class="e2">dekhāibe</span>–she will introduce [me to] <span class="e2">nija</span>–her <span class="e2">yūtheśvarī</span>–group leader (Lalitā Sakhī), <span class="e2">arpaṇa karibe</span>–give <span class="e2">śrī-karpūra-sevā</span>–camphor service, [and] <span class="e2">pradarśana karāibe</span>–show <span class="e2">more</span>–me <span class="e2">yugala-vilāsa</span>–the Pastimes of the Divine Couple. [148]
Anaṅga Mañjarī is the mistress of my heart. Mercifully, she will introduce me to her group leader (Śrī Lalitā Sakhī), give me the service of preparing camphor, and show me the Pastimes of the Divine Couple.
পুলিন-নিকটে স্থান শ্রীরাসমণ্ডল ।<br />গোপেন্দ্রনন্দনলীলা তথা নিরমল ॥<br />শতকোটী-গোপী-মাঝে মহারাসেশ্বরী ।<br />সহ নৃত্য করে কৃষ্ণ সর্ব্বচিত্ত হরি’ ॥১৪৯॥
pulina-nikaṭe sthāna śrī-rāsa-maṇḍala<br />gopendra-nandana-līlā tathā niramala<br />śata-koṭī-gopī-mājhe mahārāseśvarī<br />saha nṛtya kare kṛṣṇa sarva-chitta hari’ [149]
<span class="e2">pulina-nikaṭe</span>–Near Śrī Pulina [is] <span class="e2">śrī-rāsa-maṇḍala sthāna</span>–the place of the Rāsa Dance, <span class="e2">tathā</span>–where <span class="e2">niramala gopendra-nandana-līlā</span>–the pure Pastimes of the Prince of the cowherds [take place]. <span class="e2">śata-koṭī-gopī-mājhe</span>–In the midst of billions of gopīs, <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–Kṛṣṇa <span class="e2">nṛtya</span> <span class="e2">kare</span>–dances <span class="e2">saha</span>–with <span class="e2">mahārāseśvarī</span>–the Queen of Rāsa [and] <span class="e2">hari’</span>–steals <span class="e2">sarva-chitta</span>–the hearts of all. [149]
Near Śrī Pulina is the Rāsa Maṇḍal, where the pure Pastimes of the Prince of the cowherds take place. In the midst of billions of gopīs, Śrī Kṛṣṇa dances with Śrī Rādhā, the Queen of Rāsa, and steals the hearts of all.
সে রাসলাস্যের শোভা নাহি ত্রিভুবনে ।<br />বহু ভাগ্যে যেবা দেখে মজে সেই ক্ষণে ॥<br />স্ব-সমাধি ভাগ্যবলে কেহ কভু পায় ।<br />সে শোভাদর্শনসুখ ছাড়িতে না চায় ॥১৫০॥
se rāsa-lāsyera śobhā nāhi tribhuvane<br />bahu bhāgye yebā dekhe maje sei kṣaṇe<br />sva-samādhi bhāgya-bale keha kabhu pāya<br />se śobhā-darśana-sukha chhāḍite nā chāya [150]
<span class="e2">se śobhā</span>–The beauty <span class="e2">rāsa-lāsyera</span>–of the amorous Rāsa Dance <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–does not exist [anywhere] <span class="e2">tribhuvane</span>–within the three worlds! <span class="e2">yebā</span>–Anyone [who,] <span class="e2">bahu</span> <span class="e2">bhāgye</span>–by great fortune, <span class="e2">dekhe</span>–sees [it] <span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">kṣaṇe</span>–immediately <span class="e2">maje</span>–becomes enchanted. <span class="e2">keha</span>–Those [who,] <span class="e2">bhāgya-bale</span>–by good fortune, <span class="e2">pāya</span>–attain <span class="e2">sva-samādhi</span>–full consciousness of the self <span class="e2">kabhu</span> <span class="e2">nā</span>–never <span class="e2">chāya</span>–desire <span class="e2">chhāḍite</span>–to give up <span class="e2">se</span> <span class="e2">śobhā-darśana-sukha</span>–the joy of that beautiful vision. [150]
The beauty of the amorous Rāsa Dance does not exist anywhere within the three worlds! Anyone who, by great fortune, sees it is immediately enchanted. Those who, by good fortune, attain samādhi never desire to give up the joy of that beautiful vision.
দেখিব যে শোভা তাহা বর্ণিতে নারিব ।<br />হৃদয়ে রাখিয়া সদা দর্শন করিব ॥<br />নিজ কুঞ্জে বসি’ হৃদি মাঝে আলোচিব ।<br />সখীর নির্দ্দেশ মতে সতত সেবিব ॥১৫১॥
dekhiba ye śobhā tāhā varṇite nāriba<br />hṛdaye rākhiyā sadā darśana kariba<br />nija kuñje vasi’ hṛdi mājhe ālochiba<br />sakhīra nirdeśa mate satata seviba [151]
<span class="e2">nāriba</span>–I will not be able <span class="e2">varṇite</span>–to describe <span class="e2">ye</span> <span class="e2">śobhā</span>–the beauty <span class="e2">tāhā</span>–that <span class="e2">dekhiba</span>–I will see. <span class="e2">rākhiyā</span>–I will hold [it] <span class="e2">hṛdaye</span>–in [my] heart [and] <span class="e2">darśana</span> <span class="e2">kariba</span>–observe [it] <span class="e2">sadā</span>–forever. <span class="e2">vasi’</span>–I will live <span class="e2">nija</span> <span class="e2">kuñje</span>–in my grove, <span class="e2">ālochiba</span>–go over [it] <span class="e2">hṛdi</span> <span class="e2">mājhe</span>–within [my] heart, [and] <span class="e2">satata</span>–constantly <span class="e2">seviba</span>–serve <span class="e2">mate</span>–according to <span class="e2">nirdeśa</span>–the directions <span class="e2">sakhīra</span>–of the sakhīs. [151]
I will not be able to describe the beauty that I will see. I will hold it within my heart and observe it forever. I will live in my grove, go over it within my heart, and constantly serve according to the directions of the sakhīs.
অনঙ্গমঞ্জরী সখী রাধিকাভগিণী ।<br />মোরে কৃপা করি’ ধাম দেখাবে আপনি ॥<br />রাসস্থলী-পশ্চিমেতে শ্রীধীর সমীর ।<br />কিছু দূরে বংশীবট শ্রীযুমনাতীর ॥১৫২॥
anaṅga-mañjarī sakhī rādhikā-bhagiṇī<br />more kṛpā kari’ dhāma dekhābe āpani<br />rāsa-sthalī-paśchimete śrī-dhīra samīra<br />kichhu dūre vaṁśī-vaṭa śrī-yamunā-tīra [152]
<span class="e2">kṛpā</span> <span class="e2">kari’</span>–Mercifully, <span class="e2">anaṅga-mañjarī sakhī</span>–Anaṅga Mañjarī Sakhī, <span class="e2">rādhikā-bhagiṇī</span>–the younger sister of Rādhikā, <span class="e2">āpani dekhābe</span>–will personally show <span class="e2">more</span>–me <span class="e2">dhāma</span>–the abode. <span class="e2">rāsa-sthalī-paśchimete</span>–West of Rāsa Sthalī [is] <span class="e2">śrī-dhīra</span> <span class="e2">samīra</span>–Śrī Dhīra Samīra, [and] <span class="e2">kichhu</span> <span class="e2">dūre</span>–a little further [is] <span class="e2">vaṁśī-vaṭa</span>–Vaṁśī Vaṭ [and] <span class="e2">śrī-yamunā-tīra</span>–the bank of the Yamunā. [152]
Mercifully, Anaṅga Mañjarī Sakhī, the younger sister of Rādhikā, will personally show me the Dhām. West of Rāsa Sthalī is Śrī Dhīra Samīra, and a little further is Vaṁśī Vaṭ and the bank of the Yamunā.
শ্রীরূপমঞ্জরী-প্রশ্নে ঈশ্বরী আমার ।<br />বলিবে, “এ নবদাসী সখী ললিতার ॥<br />কমলমঞ্জরী-নাম গৌরাঙ্গৈকগতি ।<br />কৃপা করি’ দেহ এবে রাগমার্গে গতি” ॥১৫৩॥
śrī-rūpa-mañjarī-praśne īśvarī āmāra<br />balibe, “e nava-dāsī sakhī lalitāra<br />kamala-mañjarī-nāma gaurāṅgaika-gati<br />kṛpā kari’ deha ebe rāga-mārge gati” [153]
<span class="e2">śrī-rūpa-mañjarī-praśne</span>–To the enquiry of Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my <span class="e2">īśvarī</span>–mistress <span class="e2">balibe</span>–will say, <span class="e2">“e</span>–“This <span class="e2">nava-dāsī</span>–new servant <span class="e2">sakhī</span> <span class="e2">lalitāra</span>–belongs to Lalitā Sakhī. [Her] <span class="e2">nāma</span>–name [is] <span class="e2">kamala-mañjarī</span>–Kamala Mañjarī, [and] <span class="e2">gaurāṅgaika-gati</span>–Gaurāṅga is [her] only shelter. <span class="e2">ebe</span>–Now <span class="e2">kṛpā</span> <span class="e2">kari’</span>–kindly <span class="e2">deha</span>–give [her] <span class="e2">gati</span>–entrance <span class="e2">rāga-mārge”</span>–into rāga-mārg (the path of divine love).” [153]
Responding to the enquiry of Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, my mistress Anaṅga Mañjarī will say, “This new servant belongs to Lalitā Sakhī. Her name is Kamala Mañjarī, and Śrī Gaurāṅga is her only shelter. Now kindly give her entrance into the path of love.”
ঈশ্বরীর কথা শুনি’ শ্রীরূপ মঞ্জরী ।<br />বুলাইবে কৃপা-হস্ত মম দেহোপরি ॥<br />সহসা হইবে মোর রাগের উদয় ।<br />রূপানুগ ভজনেতে স্পৃহা অতিশয় ॥১৫৪॥
īśvarīra kathā śuni’ śrī-rūpa mañjarī<br />bulāibe kṛpā-hasta mama dehopari<br />sahasā ha-ibe mora rāgera udaya<br />rūpānuga bhajanete spṛhā atiśaya [154]
<span class="e2">śuni’</span>–Hearing <span class="e2">kathā</span>–the words <span class="e2">īśvarīra</span>–of [my] mistress, <span class="e2">śrī-rūpa</span> <span class="e2">mañjarī</span>–Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī <span class="e2">bulāibe</span>–will stroke [her] <span class="e2">kṛpā-hasta</span>–kind hand <span class="e2">mama</span> <span class="e2">dehopari</span>–along my body, [and] <span class="e2">sahasā</span>–immediately <span class="e2">mora</span>–my <span class="e2">rāgera</span>–love [and] <span class="e2">atiśaya</span>–intense <span class="e2">spṛhā</span>–desire <span class="e2">bhajanete</span>–for service <span class="e2">rūpānuga</span>–as Śrī Rūpa’s follower <span class="e2">udaya ha-ibe</span>–will awaken. [154]
Hearing the words of my mistress, Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī will stroke my body with her kind hand, and immediately my love and intense desire to serve as her follower will awaken.
তড়িদ্বর্ণা তারাবলী বসন-ভূষণে ।<br />শ্রীকর্পুর-পাত্র করে সখীর চরণে ॥<br />দণ্ডবৎ হইয়া আমি পড়িব তখন ।<br />মাগিব অনন্যভাবে রাধার চরণ ॥১৫৫॥
taḍid-varṇā tārāvalī vasana-bhūṣaṇe<br />śrī-karpūra-pātra kare sakhīra charaṇe<br />daṇḍavat ha-iyā āmi paḍiba takhana<br />māgiba ananya-bhāve rādhāra charaṇa [155]
<span class="e2">taḍid-varṇā</span>–With a lightning-like complexion, <span class="e2">tārāvalī</span> <span class="e2">vasana-bhūṣaṇe</span>–a dress ornamented with stars, [and] <span class="e2">śrī-karpūra-pātra</span>–a camphor tray <span class="e2">kare</span>–in hand, <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">daṇḍavat</span> <span class="e2">ha-iyā paḍiba</span>–will bow <span class="e2">sakhīra</span> <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–at the feet of the sakhīs [and] <span class="e2">takhana</span>–then <span class="e2">māgiba</span>–pray <span class="e2">ananya-bhāve</span>–for exclusive devotion <span class="e2">rādhāra</span> <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–to the feet of Rādhā. [155]
With a lightning-like complexion, a dress ornamented with stars, and a camphor tray in hand, I will bow at the feet of the sakhīs and pray for exclusive devotion to the feet of Rādhā.
শ্রীরূপমঞ্জরী ও শ্রীঅনঙ্গমঞ্জরী ।<br />লবে যথা স্বানন্দসুখদকুঞ্জেশ্বরী ॥<br />রাধা-শ্রীচরণ-সেবা সদা চিন্তা করে ।<br />শ্রীললিতা সুললিতা স্বকুঞ্জ-ভিতরে ॥১৫৬॥
śrī-rūpa-mañjarī o śrī-anaṅga-mañjarī<br />labe yathā svānanda-sukhada-kuñjeśvarī<br />rādhā-śrī-charaṇa-sevā sadā chintā kare<br />śrī-lalitā sulalitā svakuñja-bhitare [156]
<span class="e2">śrī-rūpa-mañjarī</span>–Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī <span class="e2">o</span>–and <span class="e2">śrī-anaṅga-mañjarī</span>–Śrī Anaṅga Mañjarī <span class="e2">labe</span>–will take [me] <span class="e2">yathā</span>–to <span class="e2">śrī-lalitā</span>–Śrī Lalitā Sakhī, <span class="e2">svānanda-sukhada-kuñjeśvarī</span>–the mistress of Svānanda Sukhada Kuñj (‘the grove that gives the pleasure of the soul’s joy’), [who] <span class="e2">sadā</span>–constantly <span class="e2">chintā</span> <span class="e2">kare</span>–meditates <span class="e2">rādhā-śrī-charaṇa-sevā</span>–on the service of the holy feet of Rādhā <span class="e2">sulalitā</span> <span class="e2">svakuñja-bhitare</span>–within her enchanting grove. [156]
Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī and Śrī Anaṅga Mañjarī will take me to Śrī Lalitā Sakhī, the mistress of Svānanda Sukhada Kuñja, who constantly meditates on the service of the holy feet of Rādhā within her enchanting grove.
সাষ্টাঙ্গে বন্দিব আমি তাঁহার চরণ ।<br />সখী করিবেন মম কথা বিজ্ঞাপন ॥<br />বলিবেন, “নবদ্বীপবাসী এই জন ।<br />তব দাসী হয়ে মাগে যুগলসেবন” ॥১৫৭॥
sāṣṭāṅge vandiba āmi tā̐hāra charaṇa<br />sakhī karibena mama kathā vijñāpana<br />balibena, “navadvīpa-vāsī ei jana<br />tava dāsī haye māge yugala-sevana” [157]
<span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">sāṣṭāṅge</span> <span class="e2">vandiba</span>–will prostrate myself <span class="e2">tā̐hāra</span> <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–at her feet, [and] <span class="e2">sakhī</span>–the sakhīs <span class="e2">mama</span> <span class="e2">kathā</span> <span class="e2">vijñāpana karibena</span>–will introduce me. <span class="e2">balibena</span>–They will say, <span class="e2">“ei</span> <span class="e2">jana</span>–“She <span class="e2">navadvīpa-vāsī</span>–is a resident of Nabadwīp, [and she] <span class="e2">māge</span>–begs <span class="e2">yugala-sevana</span>–to serve the Divine Couple <span class="e2">tava</span> <span class="e2">dāsī</span> <span class="e2">haye”</span>–as your servant.”[157]
I will prostrate myself at her feet, and the sakhīs will introduce me. They will say, “She is a resident of Nabadwīp, and she begs to serve the Divine Couple as your servant.”
প্রসন্ন হইয়া তবে ললিতা সুন্দরী ।<br />শৈষী-শক্তি প্রতি কবে, “শুন প্রিয়ঙ্করি ॥<br />তোমার কুঞ্জের পার্শ্বে করি’ স্থান দান ।<br />রাখিয়া যতন কর ঈপ্সিত বিধান ॥১৫৮॥
prasanna ha-iyā tabe lalitā sundarī<br />śaiṣī-śakti prati kabe, “śuna priyaṅkari<br />tomāra kuñjera pārśve kari’ sthāna dāna<br />rākhiyā yatana kara īpsita vidhāna [158]
<span class="e2">prasanna</span> <span class="e2">ha-iyā</span>–Pleased, <span class="e2">lalitā</span> <span class="e2">sundarī</span>–Lalitā Sundarī <span class="e2">kabe</span>–will say <span class="e2">tabe</span>–then <span class="e2">śaiṣī-śakti prati</span>–to Anaṅga Mañjarī, <span class="e2">“priyaṅkari</span>–“O dear friend, <span class="e2">śuna</span>–listen! [Please] <span class="e2">dāna kari’</span>–give [her] <span class="e2">sthāna</span>–a place <span class="e2">pārśve</span>–beside <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–your <span class="e2">kuñjera</span>–grove, <span class="e2">yatana rākhiyā</span>–care [for her, and] <span class="e2">vidhāna kara</span>–fulfil [her] <span class="e2">īpsita</span>–desires. [158]
Pleased, Lalitā Sundarī will then say to Anaṅga Mañjarī, “O dear friend, listen! Please give her a place beside your grove, care for her, and fulfil her desires.
তোমার সেবার কালে সঙ্গে লয়ে যাবে ।<br />ক্রমে তব দাসী রাধাপ্রসাদ পাইবে ॥<br />শ্রীরাধাপ্রসাদ বিনা শ্রীযুগলসেবা ।<br />বল দেখি কোন্ কালে পাইয়াছে কেবা” ॥১৫৯॥
tomāra sevāra kāle saṅge laye yābe<br />krame tava dāsī rādhā-prasāda pāibe<br />śrī-rādhā-prasāda vinā śrī-yugala-sevā<br />bala dekhi kon kāle pāiyāchhe kebā” [159]
<span class="e2">laye</span> <span class="e2">yābe</span>–Take [her] <span class="e2">saṅge</span>–with [you] <span class="e2">tomāra</span> <span class="e2">sevāra</span> <span class="e2">kāle</span>–at the time of your service. <span class="e2">krame</span>–Gradually <span class="e2">tava</span>–your <span class="e2">dāsī</span>–servant <span class="e2">pāibe</span>–will attain <span class="e2">rādhā-prasāda</span>–the grace of Rādhā; <span class="e2">bala</span> <span class="e2">dekhi</span>–consider, <span class="e2">kebā</span>–who <span class="e2">kon kāle</span> <span class="e2">pāiyāchhe</span>–has ever attained <span class="e2">śrī-yugala-sevā</span>–the service of the Divine Couple <span class="e2">vinā</span>–without <span class="e2">śrī-rādhā-prasāda”</span>–the grace of Śrī Rādhā?” [159]
“Take her with you at the time of your service. Gradually she will attain the grace of Rādhā; consider, who has ever attained the service of the Divine Couple without the grace of Śrī Rādhā?”
ললিতার বাক্য শুনি’ অনঙ্গমঞ্জরী ।<br />রাখিবেন নিজকুঞ্জে নিজদাসী করি’ ॥<br />যুগল-সেবার কালে সঙ্গিনী করিয়া ।<br />লইবে আমারে তেঁহ স্নেহ প্রকাশিয়া ॥১৬০॥
lalitāra vākya śuni’ anaṅga-mañjarī<br />rākhibena nija-kuñje nija-dāsī kari’<br />yugala-sevāra kāle saṅginī kariyā<br />la-ibe āmāre te̐ha sneha prakāśiyā [160]
<span class="e2">śuni’</span>–Hearing <span class="e2">vākya</span>–the words <span class="e2">lalitāra</span>–of Lalitā, <span class="e2">anaṅga-mañjarī</span>–Anaṅga Mañjarī <span class="e2">rākhibena</span>–will keep [me] <span class="e2">nija-kuñje</span>–in her grove [and] <span class="e2">kari’</span>–make [me] <span class="e2">nija-dāsī</span>–her servant. <span class="e2">kāle</span>–At the time <span class="e2">yugala-sevāra</span>–of [her] service to the Divine Couple, <span class="e2">te̐ha</span>–she <span class="e2">āmāre saṅginī</span> <span class="e2">kariyā</span>–will make me [her] companion [and] <span class="e2">sneha</span> <span class="e2">prakāśiyā</span>–affectionately <span class="e2">la-ibe</span>–bring [me with her]. [160]
Hearing the words of Lalitā, Anaṅga Mañjarī will keep me in her grove and make me her servant. At the time of her service to the Divine Couple, she will make me her companion and affectionately bring me with her.
দূরে হৈতে নিজ কার্য্য করি’ সম্পাদন ।<br />হেরিব যুগলরূপ প্রিয়-দরশন ॥<br />কভু বা শ্রীমতী মোরে আজ্ঞা প্রকাশিয়া ।<br />দেখাইবে নিজ কৃপা পদছায়া দিয়া ॥১৬১॥
dūre haite nija kārya kari’ sampādana<br />heriba yugala-rūpa priya-daraśana<br />kabhu vā śrīmatī more ājñā prakāśiyā<br />dekhāibe nija kṛpā pada-chhāyā diyā [161]
<span class="e2">sampādana kari’</span>–I will perform <span class="e2">nija</span>–my <span class="e2">kārya</span>–duties <span class="e2">haite</span>–from <span class="e2">dūre</span>–a distance [and] <span class="e2">priya-darśana heriba</span>–behold the beloved <span class="e2">yugala-rūpa</span>–Divine Couple. <span class="e2">kabhu</span> <span class="e2">vā</span>–Sometimes <span class="e2">śrīmatī</span>–Rādhā <span class="e2">ājñā</span> <span class="e2">prakāśiyā</span>–will instruct <span class="e2">more</span>–me, <span class="e2">dekhāibe</span>–show [me] <span class="e2">nija</span>–Her <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–grace, [and] <span class="e2">pada-chhāyā diyā</span>–give [me] the shade of [Her] feet. [161]
I will perform my duties from a distance and behold the beloved Divine Couple. Sometimes Śrīmatī will instruct me, show me Her grace, and give me the shade of Her feet.
সেই ত সেবায় আমি রব চিরদিন ।<br />ক্রমে সেবা-কার্য্যে আমি হইব প্রবীণ ॥<br />সেবার কৌশলে রাধাগোবিন্দ তুষিব ।<br />কভু কভু অলঙ্কার প্রসাদ লভিব ॥১৬২॥
sei ta sevāya āmi raba chira-dina<br />krame sevā-kārye āmi ha-iba pravīṇa<br />sevāra kauśale rādhā-govinda tuṣiba<br />kabhu kabhu alaṅkāra prasāda labhiba [162]
<span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">sei ta</span> <span class="e2">sevāya</span> <span class="e2">raba</span>–will continue my service <span class="e2">chira-dina</span>–every day, [and] <span class="e2">krame</span>–gradually <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I <span class="e2">pravīṇa ha-iba</span>–will become proficient <span class="e2">sevā-kārye</span>–in rendering the service. <span class="e2">sevāra kauśale</span>–With [my] service expertise, <span class="e2">tuṣiba</span>–I will please <span class="e2">rādhā-govinda</span>–Rādhā and Govinda, [and] <span class="e2">kabhu</span> <span class="e2">kabhu</span>–sometimes <span class="e2">labhiba</span>–I will receive <span class="e2">alaṅkāra</span>–ornaments [as Their] <span class="e2">prasāda</span>–prasād. [162]
I will continue my service every day, and gradually I will become proficient at it. With my service expertise, I will please Rādhā and Govinda, and sometimes I will receive ornaments as Their prasād.
স্বপ্ন-ভঙ্গে ধীরে ধীরে কাঁদিয়া কাঁদিয়া ।<br />ভাগীরথী পার হব পুলিন দেখিয়া ॥<br />ঈশোদ্যান-সন্নিকটে নিজ-কুঞ্জে বসি’ ।<br />ভজিব যুগলধন শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ-শশী ॥১৬৩॥
svapna-bhaṅge dhīre dhīre kā̐diyā kā̐diyā<br />bhāgīrathī pāra haba pulina dekhiyā<br />īśodyāna-sannikaṭe nija-kuñje vasi’<br />bhajiba yugala-dhana śrī-gaurāṅga-śaśī [163]
<span class="e2">svapna-bhaṅge</span>–When [my] dream breaks, <span class="e2">dhīre</span> <span class="e2">dhīre</span>–slowly, <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span> <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–crying, <span class="e2">pāra</span> <span class="e2">haba</span>–I will cross <span class="e2">bhāgīrathī</span>–the Gaṅgā <span class="e2">dekhiyā</span>–looking <span class="e2">pulina</span>–at Śrī Pulina. <span class="e2">vasi’</span>–Living <span class="e2">nija-kuñje</span>–in my grove <span class="e2">īśodyāna-sannikaṭe</span>–near Īśodyān, <span class="e2">bhajiba</span>–I will worship <span class="e2">yugala-dhana</span>–the Divine Couple [and] <span class="e2">śrī-gaurāṅga-śaśī</span>–moon-like Śrī Gaurāṅga. [163]
When my dream breaks, slowly, crying, I will cross the Gaṅgā, looking at Śrī Pulina. Living in my grove near Īśodyān, I will worship the Divine Couple and moon-like Śrī Gaurāṅga.
স্বনিয়মে থাকি’ রাধাগোবিন্দ ভজিব ।<br />রাধাকুণ্ড বৃন্দাবন সতত হেরিব ॥<br />অনঙ্গমঞ্জরীসখী-চরণ স্মরিয়া ।<br />নিজ-সেবানন্দে রব প্রেমেতে ডুবিয়া ॥১৬৪॥
svaniyame thāki’ rādhā-govinda bhajiba<br />rādhā-kuṇḍa vṛndāvana satata heriba<br />anaṅga-mañjarī-sakhī-charaṇa smariyā<br />nija-sevānande raba premete ḍubiyā [164]
<span class="e2">svaniyame</span> <span class="e2">thāki’</span>–Engaging in [my] duties, <span class="e2">bhajiba</span>–I will worship <span class="e2">rādhā-govinda</span>–Rādhā-Govinda, [and] <span class="e2">satata</span>–constantly <span class="e2">heriba</span>–see <span class="e2">rādhā-kuṇḍa</span>–Rādhā Kuṇḍa [and] <span class="e2">vṛndāvana</span>–Vṛndāvan. <span class="e2">smariyā</span>–I will remember <span class="e2">anaṅga-mañjarī-sakhī-charaṇa</span>–the feet of Anaṅga Mañjarī, <span class="e2">nija-sevānande</span> <span class="e2">raba</span>–continue my service—my joy— [and] <span class="e2">ḍubiyā</span>–swim <span class="e2">premete</span>–in divine love. [164]
Engaging in my duties, I will worship Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Govinda and constantly see Rādhā Kuṇḍa and Vṛndāvan. I will remember the feet of Anaṅga Mañjarī, continue my service—my joy—and thus swim in divine love.
শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য প্রভুর দাস-অনুদাস ।<br />এ ভক্তিবিনোদ মাগে নবদ্বীপ-বাস ॥<br />রূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে আকুতি করিয়া ।<br />নিজাভীষ্ট-সিদ্ধি মাগে ব্যাকুল হইয়া ॥১৬৫॥
śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya prabhura dāsa-anudāsa<br />e bhakti-vinoda māge navadvīpa-vāsa<br />rūpa-raghunātha-pade ākuti kariyā<br />nijābhīṣṭa-siddhi māge vyākula ha-iyā [165]
<span class="e2">e</span> <span class="e2">bhakti-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod, <span class="e2">dāsa-anudāsa</span>–a servant of the servant <span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya</span> <span class="e2">prabhura</span>–of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, <span class="e2">māge</span>–prays <span class="e2">navadvīpa-vāsa</span>–for residence in Nabadwīp. <span class="e2">ākuti</span> <span class="e2">kariyā</span>–Yearning <span class="e2">rūpa-raghunātha-pade</span>–for the feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunāth, [he] <span class="e2">vyākula ha-iyā</span>–desperately <span class="e2">māge</span>–prays <span class="e2">nijābhīṣṭa-siddhi</span>–for the fulfilment of his desires. [165]
Bhakti Vinod, a servant of the servant of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, prays for residence in Nabadwīp. Yearning for the feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunāth, he desperately prays for the fulfilment of his desires.
নবদ্বীপ-বৃন্দাবন-ক্ষেত্রবাসিগণ ।<br />ঈশাক্ষেত্রে কর মোরে অচিরে স্থাপন ॥<br />তোমাদের ক্ষেত্র এই, আমি-মাত্র দাস ।<br />তোমাসবা-সেবাচ্ছলে পাই ক্ষেত্রবাস ॥১৬৬॥
navadvīpa-vṛndāvana-kṣetra-vāsi-gaṇa<br />īśā-kṣetre kara more achire sthāpana<br />tomādera kṣetra ei, āmi-mātra dāsa<br />tomā-sabā-sevā-chchhale pāi kṣetra-vāsa [166]
<span class="e2">navadvīpa-vṛndāvana-kṣetra-vāsi-gaṇa</span>–O residents of Nabadwīp and Vṛndāvan, <span class="e2">achire</span>–quickly <span class="e2">sthāpana kara</span>–establish <span class="e2">more</span>–me <span class="e2">īśā-kṣetre</span>–in the abode of the Lord. <span class="e2">ei</span>–It [is] <span class="e2">tomādera</span>–your <span class="e2">kṣetra</span>–abode, [and] <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I [am]<span class="e2"> mātra</span>–simply [your] <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servant. <span class="e2">tomā-sabā-sevā-chchhale</span>–By serving you all, <span class="e2">pāi</span>–I will attain <span class="e2">kṣetra-vāsa</span>–residence in [your] abode. [166]
O residents of Nabadwīp and Vṛndāvan, quickly give me a place in the abode of the Lord. It is your abode, and I am simply your servant. By serving you all, I will attain residence in the Dhām.
নবদ্বীপ কর মোরে কৃপা-বিতরণ ।<br />তব কৃপা বিনা ক্ষেত্র লভে কোন্ জন ॥<br />আমার যোগ্যতা লয়ে না কর বিচার ।<br />জাহ্নবানিতাই-আজ্ঞা করিয়াছি সার ॥১৬৭॥
navadvīpa kara more kṛpā-vitaraṇa<br />tava kṛpā vinā kṣetra labhe kon jana<br />āmāra yogyatā laye nā kara vichāra<br />jāhnavā-nitāi-ājñā kariyāchhi sāra [167]
<span class="e2">navadvīpa</span>–O Nabadwīp! <span class="e2">kṛpā-vitaraṇa kara</span>–Please bestow mercy <span class="e2">more</span>–upon me. <span class="e2">kon jana</span>–Who <span class="e2">labhe</span>–attains <span class="e2">kṣetra</span>–the [Lord’s] abode <span class="e2">vinā</span>–without <span class="e2">tava</span>–your <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–mercy? <span class="e2">kara nā</span>–Please do not <span class="e2">vichāra</span>–judge <span class="e2">laye āmāra yogyatā</span>–my worthiness. <span class="e2">kariyāchhi</span>–I have accepted <span class="e2">jāhnavā-nitāi-ājñā</span>–the instructions of Jāhnavā and Nitāi <span class="e2">sāra</span>–as all-in-all. [167]
O Nabadwīp! Please bestow mercy upon me. Who attains the Lord’s abode without your mercy? Please do not judge my worthiness. I have accepted the instructions of Jāhnavā and Nitāi as all-in-all.
শ্রদ্ধায় পড়িবে যেই এ ভাব-তরঙ্গ ।<br />উদিবে তাহার মনে গৌর-রস-রঙ্গ ॥<br />শ্রীস্বরূপদামোদর তারে করি’ দয়া ।<br />লইবে নিজের গণে দিয়া পদছায়া ॥১৬৮॥
śraddhāya paḍibe yei e bhāva-taraṅga<br />udibe tāhāra mane gaura-rasa-raṅga<br />śrī-svarūpa-dāmodara tāre kari’ dayā<br />la-ibe nijera gaṇe diyā pada-chhāyā [168]
<span class="e2">gaura-rasa-raṅga</span>–The joy of devotion to Gaura <span class="e2">udibe</span>–will arise <span class="e2">mane</span>–within the heart <span class="e2">yei tāhāra</span>–of those who <span class="e2">paḍibe</span>–read <span class="e2">e</span> <span class="e2">bhāva-taraṅga</span>–this <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga</span> <span class="e2">śraddhāya</span>–with faith. <span class="e2">śrī-svarūpa-dāmodara</span>–Śrī Svarūp Dāmodar <span class="e2">dayā kari’</span>–will bless <span class="e2">tāre</span>–them, <span class="e2">la-ibe</span>–accept [them] <span class="e2">nijera</span> <span class="e2">gaṇe</span>–within his group, [and] <span class="e2">diyā</span>–give [them] <span class="e2">pada-chhāyā</span>–the shade of his feet. [168]
The joy of devotion to Gaura will arise within the heart of those who read this <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga</span> with faith. Śrī Svarūp Dāmodar will bless them, accept them within his group, and give them the shade of his feet.
শ্রীনবদ্বীপ-ভাবতরঙ্গ সমাপ্ত ।
śrī-navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga samāpta
Thus ends <span class="e3">Śrī Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga</span>.

Śrī Gaura Kṛṣṇa Tattva
Excerpts from the writings of
Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur
<span class="e2">Question:</span> Are Kṛṣṇa and Gaura separate entities? What is the difference between Them?
<span class="e2">Answer:</span> Kṛṣṇa and Gaura are not separate entities. They are both relishers of madhura-rasa. There is only one slight difference between Them: there are two forms of mādhurya-rasa—mādhurya and audārya—and in Kṛṣṇa, mādhurya is prominent, while in Gaura, audārya is prominent.
(<span class="e3">Jaiva-dharma</span>, Chapter 17)
<span class="e2">Question:</span> Who came first, Śrī Kṛṣṇa or Śrī Chaitanya?
<span class="e2">Answer:</span> Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Śrī Chaitanya both exist eternally. Who came first and who came after cannot be said. “Śrī Chaitanya was first, later He became Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and They (Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa) have now combined again as Śrī Chaitanya.” The purport of this statement (Cc: Ādi, 1.5) is not that one was first and the other came after, but that both exist eternally.
(<span class="e3">Jaiva-dharma</span>, Chapter 14)
<span class="e2">Question:</span> Why is it a disturbance to worship Gaura and neglect Kṛṣṇa, or worship Kṛṣṇa and neglect Gaura?
<span class="e2">Answer:</span> Those who have decided to give up the worship of Kṛṣṇa by praying to ‘Śrī Gaurāṅga’ do not follow the instructions of Śrī Gaurāṅga. This is unfortunate. There is no difference between Gaura and Kṛṣṇa. Those who think that if they take shelter at the feet of Gaurāṅga, they do not need to remember Kṛṣṇa any more, think that Gaura and Kṛṣṇa are different. There is no difference between the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and the Pastimes of Gaura. They are one. In the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, the object of worship is prominent, and in the Pastimes of Gaurāṅga, the method of worship is prominent. Neither the object of worship without the method, nor simply the method without the object of worship, can ever be complete. The more one recites the Pastimes of Śrī Gaurāṅga, the more one develops divine love for the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, and the more one recites the Pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the more one remembers the Pastimes of Śrī Gaura. Neither Gaura without Kṛṣṇa, nor Kṛṣṇa without Gaura, ever seem right. When one believes that Gaura is the highest object of worship, Śrī Gaurāṅga’s Pastimes as Kṛṣṇa are fully revealed. Although all these points are highly confidential, sadly they are in need of being disclosed. “We will worship Gaura, but we will not remember Kṛṣṇa anymore”—such a statement is tantamount to wickedness. Similarly, the notion that, “We will worship Kṛṣṇa, but we will not remember Gaura” must also be considered a great misfortune.
(<span class="e3">Sajjana-toṣaṇī:</span> 11.6, ‘Gaura-Kṛṣṇa Abheda’)
<span class="e2">Question:</span> In what plane do the associates in the Pastimes of Śrī Gaura and the associates in the Pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa reside together?
<span class="e2">Answer:</span> In the original Vṛndāvan, the abode of Kṛṣṇa and the abode of Gaura exist as two separate chambers. In the abode of Kṛṣṇa, the eternally perfect and liberated associates relish audārya predominated by mādhurya; they are Kṛṣṇa’s associates. In the abode of Śrī Gaura, all these eternally perfect and liberated associates relish mādhurya predominated by audārya. In some cases, they exist in multiple forms in both abodes; and in some cases, they exist in one abode in one form and do not reside in the other abode. Those who are strict worshippers of Gaura in the practising stage will serve only in the abode of Gaura in the perfected stage. Those who are strict worshippers of Kṛṣṇa in the practising stage take shelter in the abode of Kṛṣṇa in the perfected stage. Those who are worshippers of both Kṛṣṇa and Gaura during the practising stage assume two forms and reside in both abodes simultaneously in the perfected stage. This is the ultimate secret behind the inconceivable difference and non-difference (achintya-bhedābheda) of Gaura and Kṛṣṇa.
(<span class="e3">Jaiva-dharma</span>, Chapter 17)

The Land of Sweetness
An overview of the glories <br />of Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām <br />compiled from the lectures
of
Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
After his retirement, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur wanted to go to Vṛndāvan and pass the rest of his life there, but he repeatedly had a dream in which he was told that he must discover the actual birthplace of Śrī Chaitanyadev. He could not neglect the dream. He again entered into service at Krishnanagar, and there he consulted the records of the locality. With the help of those records, and by his divine inspiration, he discovered the birthplace at the Yoga Pīṭh in Māyāpur. Then, with deepened interest, he visited the entire Nabadwīp Maṇḍal. With reference to the scriptures, he gave a description of both the ancient and contemporary holy places in the Dhām of Mahāprabhu. He established a committee to ensure that the service of Mahāprabhu’s place of advent would continue. Lastly, he handed it over to our Prabhupād, Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Goswāmī.
Infinite courage of the pioneer
When Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur began the service of the Dhām and Mahāprabhu, he had to do many things to attract the public to accept his discovery of the Dhām as authentic. At that time, the place was uninhabited. Gradually a brick building was made, and the worship of the Deity of Mahāprabhu was begun.
The Temple came later. Generally, the brāhmaṇ cooks he required would not stay there very long because it was an isolated place and there were violent elements nearby. To ensure that the service continued, he had to undergo many undesirable things. For example, sometimes he had to prepare gañjikā (hemp) by his own hand for the cook! Otherwise, the cook would have left. At times, when ‘respectable’ persons came, he had to make arrangements for tobacco. There were many other trials.
The Ṭhākur’s foresight
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> Śrīla Ṭhākur Bhakti Vinod also had a great vision for the world.
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Yes. He saw in his divine eye that prema-dharma, the religion based on divine love, is so self-evident in character that the intelligent could never avoid embracing such a conception of pure religion as the highest. Love—prema: the fine intellect cannot but detect the purity in the love of religion in its highest conception. His idea was: “With an unbiased mind, the Western thinkers cannot but appreciate the doctrine of divine love, as given out by Śrī Chaitanyadev. So, I am sure that in the future many of the Western scholars will come under the flag of Śrī Chaitanyadev.” This was his conviction, and he mentioned this in lectures that he delivered throughout Bengal.
When Śrīpād Bhakti Sāraṅga Goswāmī Mahārāj returned from preaching in England, he brought one Mr. Burchett back with him. A meeting was held at the Bag Bazaar Maṭh. That meeting was presided over by a gentleman of the name Kiraṇ Dutta, a good scholar and a Theosophist. In his talk he said, “When we were students at City College, Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur delivered a lecture there to the effect that in the near future Western scholars would come and join the saṅkīrtan under the banner of Mahāprabhu. Now, clearly, I can bear witness to the fact that his prediction is beginning to come true. I heard the lecture in my young days, and now in my old age I see the evidence—it is going to be true. I am very glad for that.”
The eye of faith
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> In <span class="e3">Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga</span>, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur seems to be having actual visions of the Pastimes of the Lord on the various islands of Nabadwīp. Yet he writes in such a way that he also seems to be aspiring for those visions. Is he actually having those visions?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Yes, of course. His vision is inspired. The Dhām has inspired these two perspectives in him. The Dhām allows us to see according to the degree of our devotion. A doctor sees a patient according to his capacity. A higher politician can see a higher strategy, and so on. Higher intelligence can see deeper. Such is the case always. A detector can see the depth afforded by its capacity. The x-ray can detect to a certain depth, and the microscope has another dimension of utility. There is revelation according to one’s capacity. Deserve—and have.
In an ordinary country there is a capital. The capital is where the existence and position of the king is more intense than in the general section of the country. Similarly, the Lord is everywhere, but His concentrated existence is found in the Dhām, or the holy abode. With fully developed vision, we can feel the special characteristic of the Dhām. We will find His presence everywhere, but with particular intensity in the Dhām. With the awakening of our real eye, we should be able to feel and appreciate according to this criterion. There is no question of a Dhām for those who have no eye to see. There is also a hierarchy in the Dhām. All have a serving attitude. Whether birds, beasts, worms, or insects—everything contributes to the Reality. Their feeling of heart, their gesture, posture, and movement—everything contributes exclusively to the Pastimes of the Lord.
<span class="e3">Dhāmera svarūpa sphuribe nayane</span>: in a song, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur aspires for that pure vision of the Dhām. Otherwise, it may appear quite ordinary to us, like a jungle. The purity of Ganges water is only perceived by those who have proper faith [śraddhā]. Otherwise, to others’ eyes, it is ordinary water. The same applies to the Deity [Śrī Mūrti]. One may think that the Śrī Mūrti of Lord Jagannāth in Purī appears to be a somewhat awkward figure. His arms seem incomplete, His feet are not visible, and His eyes are enormous. Yet Mahāprabhu stood before Him for hours shedding tears, and no one could move Him from that place. What did Mahāprabhu see in that figure, and what is He to our eyes? So, according to the depth of the vision of our inner eye, we can perceive the Dhām, the Deity, and the purifying Ganges water. <span class="e3">Śraddhāmayo ’yam puruṣaḥ</span> (Bg: 17.3): “The nature of a person is based on faith.” Of what value is a mirror without an eye? In a looking-glass we should find the reflection, but if the eye is absent, what will the subject see in the glass? The eye to see—faith—is necessary. According to one’s śraddhā, the specific character of the Dhām as distinct from all other places will come into view, disclosing its real form. Everything depends on śraddhā [faith].
The capital of theism
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> Did Lord Nṛsiṁhadev have some connection in Nabadwīp at Nṛsiṁha Pallī?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Yes. All the different representations of theism have been absorbed in Nabadwīp Dhām. In the capital, all provincial authorities have some representation. In Delhi, regions such as Bengal, Madras, and Bihar have their representatives. The highest conception of theism is in Nabadwīp, so naturally representation of all other theistic conceptions is here in some form or another. Śiva, Devī, Jagannāth, Nṛsiṁhadev, and so many others represent themselves here to honour the highest conception of theism. They think it necessary. They feel they must have some representation here. It shows how all the different conceptions of theism are adjusted in full-fledged theism, which is all-inclusive.
When Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur was staying in Godrumadwīp, he noticed that every day early in the morning, a flow of wind would come through his yard towards the Yoga Pīṭh, the birthplace of Mahāprabhu. He began to search most earnestly to detect the reason for this in a prayerful mood. Then one day, he found that Nṛsiṁhadev was going every day early in the morning from Nṛsiṁha Pallī to attend maṅgal ārati at Mahāprabhu’s birthplace.
Everything has a conscious, personal form. To the degree that there is connection with the conscious personality within things, there is more attraction.
A favourable atmosphere
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> Can you tell us more about Dhām-tattva. It seems unclear.
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Everything is favourable, but we cannot see it. Rather, we see that everything is unfavourable to us. Apparently, our home has become the abode of our enemy. It looks like that to us.
Generally, it is expected that in other parts of the country there may be other conditions, but that the Dhām must be favourable to the life of a devotee. But here [in Nabadwīp], on the surface, we find more difficulties for devotees. How are we to harmonise and adjust to this? Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur said,
ekhana ye brahma-kule chaitanyera ari<br />tāke jāni chaitanyera līlā-puṣṭikārī
(Kalyāna-kalpa-taru: Prārthanā-lālasāmayī, 4.11)
“Though in these days we find many in the bodies of brāhmaṇs who oppose the cult of Śrī Chaitanyadev, in the fullest adjustment we should conceive of them as līlā-puṣṭikārī, a necessary, indirect help to the Lord’s Pastimes.”
There is direct help and indirect help. Indirect help is necessary to enhance the activity of the direct school. In this way, we are to adjust. In Vṛndāvan also, so many demons—Kaṁsa and his agents—will always be there. We must be prepared for that. And it is necessary. Opposition is always necessary in the highest quarter.
aher iva gatiḥ premṇaḥ svabhāva-kuṭilā bhavet
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Madhya-līlā, 8.110)
[“Like a snake, the movement of divine love is by nature crooked.”]
Līlā, fundamentally, requires opposition. It is necessary to help the positive side from a different direction. The more trouble there is to acquire wealth, the more there is taste for it. The greater the hunger, the greater the taste. So, we should not be cowed down by superficial opposition. It is tasteful. We want the highest thing, but without undergoing any sort of trouble? That would be injustice.
Our Madan Manohar Prabhu says, “Vṛndāvan is very favourable. There, when we wander in the street, people do not insult us. Here [in Nabadwīp], if we go to the bazaar, people come to bite us like tigers if they see tilak or anything of the sort. Vṛndāvan is free from such trouble. So, I think I should live in Vṛndāvan.”
We must be attentive to our highest attainment. In Vṛndāvan, external life may be comfortable, but the internal process is difficult. If we can collect a ticket from here [Nabadwīp], from Nityānanda Prabhu and Mahāprabhu, then Vṛndāvan, the highest plane of the purest character, is within our fist. So, the trouble here ultimately pays us in cash for the highest goal.
Divine vision
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> Since I am now in Nabadwīp, what special service is very important to do while I am here?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Acquire the proper angle of vision. This is most important everywhere. Only we are to acquire the proper angle of vision: a new eye, divya-dṛṣṭi [divine vision]. Dīkṣā [initiation] means divya-dṛṣṭi: to pierce through our prejudiced estimation and have a proper view into the reality of things. That is what is necessary everywhere. Sādhana [spiritual practice] as a whole means that: realisation.
We must die to live. To have a spiritual life, we will have to die as we are at present. The whole mental system has to be dissolved. It is full of nothing but misunderstanding and prejudices gathered from a selfish standpoint. Everything we know has been estimated from a selfish standpoint, be it very meagre or extended selfishness. The standpoint of a country or a nation means extended selfishness. “I am not selfish. I stand for the cause of my country.” Someone may speak this way, but such a conception is actually extended selfishness. In the infinite, what is the meaning or value of that extension, of a country? It has no meaning. We are to acquire nothing less than an infinite standpoint, an angle of vision into the infinite.
How do we look at the environment from a universal standpoint? From the standpoint of Kṛṣṇa’s interest, the central interest, the Absolute’s interest. That leads us to the conception of the Absolute as Kṛṣṇa, the Autocrat, who is beauty personified. We are to learn to see everything here from that standpoint. We must give up our so-called real estimation of the environment. It has no value.
What is real? Everything here is transient, deceiving. Whatever we draw from outside is deceptive. It may stand for some time and for a particular section, but it is a relative truth, a relative truth in the misconceived world. There is also relative truth from the absolute standpoint, but that is another thing. From the absolute standpoint, there is relative truth according to a gradation, a hierarchy. But that is different from relative truth based on misconception. Within the misconceived world, everything is misconception, or a part of a part of a misconception, or a misconception of different quality and quantity.
Dīkṣā means divya-jñān [divine knowledge], and divya-jñān means knowledge gathered from the absolute standpoint, not a self-centred, country-centred, nation-centred, humanity-centred, or even ‘whole animation-centred’ standpoint. We are to learn nothing less than infinite-centred calculation.
He is for Himself, and everything is for Him. What value does anything have in bringing satisfaction to the Lord? We are to learn how to calculate how much something can contribute to Kṛṣṇa’s satisfaction. We are to enquire and know that. How much can something supply satisfaction to Kṛṣṇa? How much can it be used in Kṛṣṇa’s interest? We must convert ourselves into agents that look for Kṛṣṇa’s interest in the environment. We are to search out Kṛṣṇa’s interest, Gaurāṅga’s interest, and give up our self-interest of different types found in different layers. That is the main thing. That is dīkṣā, and that is what is wanted. Kṛṣṇa must be allowed to sit on the throne of our heart where the ego is now, and according to Him we will try to look at anything and everything.
The structure of the Dhām
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> We have heard that the nine islands of Nabadwīp represent the nine fundamental processes of devotional service.
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām is envisaged as a lotus flower. The centre of the lotus is the birthplace of Mahāprabhu, and it represents ātma-nivedanam [self-surrender]. One has to first surrender, and then all the practices of devotion follow. The petals of the lotus represent śravaṇam, kīrtanam, smaraṇam, pāda-sevanam, archanam, vandanam, and dāsyam [hearing, chanting, remembering, serving the Lord’s feet, worshipping, praying, and servitorship]. Sakhyam [friendship] is situated half on one side of the Ganges and half on the other. In this way, the nine islands of Nabadwīp are represented as a lotus flower embodying the nine standard practices of devotion.
Dhām parikramā
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> Please tell us something about Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām parikramā (circumambulation).
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> We should try to become more acquainted with the realistic view of Nabadwīp. When travelling to these places, we are reminded by the incidents connected with them how such representation comes from each place. All of them taken together promote our understanding as to what is devotion proper.
Ātma-nivedanam, full self-surrender, is the basis of all. After ātma-nivedanam, the plane of life will be categorically changed. After surrendering to the central direction, whatever will be done by us will come to have recognition as devotion. That is devotion. Ātma-nivedanam is selflessness plus self-surrendering. Self-surrendering presupposes selflessness. Selfish actions come to an end and selflessness is also crossed, and then self-surrendered life begins—and that is devotion proper.
There are so many incidents, stories, and sceneries connected with Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām parikramā, but all are meaning to help us in our life of absolute adjustment. If one can catch that, then by his parikramā through different holy places and his hearing about local ‘historical’ incidents, he will receive eternal instructions in various conceptions of devotion. He will receive encouragement in this way.
It is not like the parikramā of the ordinary people in the general Hindu section of society who also go out on pilgrimage. The general people come in contact with the holy places, and they have some holy association, but their main object is to gain some unseen help in their present life. They want their desires of this present life to be satisfied by some invisible help. It is puṇya-kāmanā—to acquire good merit to help success in their present life according to their conception. It is not śuddha-bhakti. The objective of Gauḍīya Maṭh people is quite different.
The kīrtan of love
Saṅkīrtan is the central service recommended by Mahāprabhu, especially for the Age of Kali. Saṅkīrtan means to listen and reproduce. To hear and tell. And the telling, the expression, the reproduction, is the more powerful thing. We are to exert ourselves to the utmost for kīrtan. Kīrtan means to preach, and that has been recommended as the highest method of attainment, especially for beginners. Assert as much as you can; engage yourself in preaching, spreading the truth that you imbibe from the higher source. Thereby, you will be benefitted the most. Exert yourself to spread the news of the Lord, the Truth. Then His omnipotent supply from above will be lavishly extended to you. As much as you can sell, so much you will be furnished with materials by the capitalist. So go on. He is not a capitalist of the mundane world. He is a capitalist of real property: devotion, service, prema. That is the only property in this world. What can dispossess us of everything and fulfil all our wants? What can compensate us and take the place of everything else? Only prema. No other thing can give us perfect health. Only prema: love. Love is above everything. Love is the only wealth in this world.
Mahāprabhu, Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Prabhu, and others came with this. They came and continue to come now and then to the world with these tidings that bring such a high prospect into our life. After coming, anyhow, into a human birth, if we do not try for that prospect, then we commit suicide; our actions amount to nothing more.
Śrī Gauḍīya Maṭh’s Dhām-parikramā invites everyone to try for that, to try to acquire that wealth. However small, or of whatever character it may be, its object is connected with that highest plane given by Mahāprabhu Śrī Chaitanyadev, the Lord of love and the distribution of love.
The mercy of Nabadwīp
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> Could you elaborate on how it is necessary to get the mercy of Nabadwīp Dhām before Vṛndāvan Dhām.
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> First, we must try to approach Nityānanda Prabhu. He is the Lord of Nabadwīp Dhām. To secure a ticket, His permission is necessary first.
yathā yathā gaura-padāravinde<br />vindeta bhaktiṁ kṛta-puṇya-rāśiḥ<br />tathā tathotsarpati hṛdy akasmād<br />rādhā-padāmbhoja-sudhāmburāśiḥ
(Śrī Chaitanya-chandrāmṛta: 88)
As much as we are able to dedicate ourselves to the divine feet of Śrī Gaurāṅga, automatically and suddenly we will find that we are taken into Vṛndāvan to Rādhārāṇī. The real key is here in Nabadwīp with Śrī Gaurāṅga. We are to enter the confidential circle of Gaurāṅga and Nityānanda, who are the most benevolent.
Nityānanda used to roam along both sides of the Ganges calling out to one and all, “Come! Join the camp of Śrī Gaurāṅga!
bhaja gaurāṅga kaha gaurāṅga laha gaurāṅgera nāma<br />ye jana gaurāṅga bhaje se haya āmāra prāṇa
“The life of my life is one who has come to take shelter under the direction of My Lord Gaurāṅga. O fallen souls, gather round and beg My Lord Gaurāṅga for His grace!”
Automatically you will find yourself in Vṛndāvan. All the undesirable things within you will be cleared in no time, and, unconsciously, your pristine inner self will emerge. It will find suddenly that it is in the midst of the desired soil, Vṛndāvan, which is filled with the most wonderful paraphernalia; you will find you are at home, back at home. Get a ticket here in Nabadwīp, and you will quickly reach your home.
It is like a direct flight from Kolkata to New York, with no break necessary in the journey. Nabadwīp is Gupta Vṛndāvan: it is suppressed and covered, but really Vṛndāvan. Outwardly, it is covered by magnanimity, added generosity, to enlist the fallen souls, the culprits. Through grace, their disease will be cured, and they will become fit to be a proper child of the soil of divine love, Vṛndāvan. As Vṛndāvan is not temporary, but permanent, so its recruiting office and staff are also permanent. They are always doing Their work. Sometimes They are more busy, sometimes less busy, but They are always there. That is Nabadwīp.
The land of sweetness
Once a gentleman challenged me, “Why do you confine Śrī Chaitanyadev to Bengal? Why do you say Śrī Chaitanyadev’s followers are ‘Gauḍīya’ Vaiṣṇavas? You chant the Lord’s Names: ‘Chaitanya’, ‘Gaura’, ‘Nimāi’, and so on. But ‘Gauḍa’ means Bengal. To say ‘Gauḍīya’ Vaiṣṇava is to confine Śrī Chaitanyadev to a province. Why do you promote ‘Gauḍīya’ Maṭh and ‘Gauḍīya’ Vaiṣṇava-dharma? I cannot adjust to this.”
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> What should be the answer to that Mahārāj?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> It is generally given that ‘Vṛndāvan’ does not mean a particular province, town, or forest; it has its broad meaning. So, ‘Nabadwīp’ and ‘Gauḍa’ may be taken in that sense. If we can understand Nabadwīp Dhām proper, then we will understand that Nabadwīp Dhām is not situated in a particular province. It has the dignity that Vṛndāvan has.
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> So Gauḍa Maṇḍal is the same as Vraja Maṇḍal?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Gauḍa Maṇḍal is Vraja Maṇḍal. The word ‘Gauḍa’ comes from the word ‘guḍ’. ‘Guḍ’ means miṣṭi, sweet. When something is sweet, it may be described by the synonym ‘guḍ’. Guḍ represents sweetness. So, Gauḍa Maṇḍal: ‘the sweet land’. There is no sweetness anywhere like that found in Vṛndāvan and Nabadwīp. In Vṛndāvan, it is confined in a particular group, but in Nabadwīp, it is being distributed. Here people come to know, “Yes. It is sweet.” They get the chance to taste, appreciate, and declare, “Yes! It is sweet!” But in Vṛndāvan, even Lakṣmī Devī cannot purchase a ticket. Lakṣmī Devī, the goddess of wealth, cannot purchase a ticket to enter the Rāsa-līlā.
<span class="e2">Devotee:</span> So Nabadwīp is the actual land of nectar?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> At least the public may come to understand that nectar does exist. Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa tasted nectar in Their harem in Vṛndāvan, and then They combined to distribute it to the public in Nabadwīp. That is the unique thing about Nabadwīp: the two highest interested parties have combined to give nectar to others.
Eternal necessity
