Just prior to the withdrawal of his manifest līlā, my causelessly merciful Divine Master, Śrīla Saraswatī Ṭhākur, handed me over to the holy feet of that divine personality by having me sing the glorious prayer unto his lotus feet (<span class="e3">Śrī Rūpa-Mañjarī-pada</span>). Despite my lowliness, when will—disregarding all my various qualifications and disqualifications—Śrīmad Rūpa Prabhu grace me with the dust of his holy lotus feet?

श्रीदयितदासप्रणतिपञ्चकम्
Śrī Dayita-Dās-praṇati-pañchakam
Homage unto Śrī Dayita Dās
भयभञ्जनजयशंसनकरुणायतनयनम्।<br />कनकोत्पलजनकोज्ज्वलरससागरचयनम्॥<br />मुखरीकृतधरणीतलहरिकीर्त्तनरसनम्।<br />क्षितिपावनभवतारणपिहितारुणवसनम्॥<br />शुभदोदयदिवसे वृषरविजानिजदयितम्।<br />प्रणमामि च चरणान्तिकपरिचारकसहितम् ॥१॥
bhayabhañjana-jayaśaṁsana-karuṇāyatanayanam<br />kanakotpala-janakojjvala-rasasāgara-chayanam<br />mukharīkṛta-dharaṇītala-harikīrtana-rasanam<br />kṣitipāvana-bhavatāraṇa-pihitāruṇa-vasanam<br />śubhadodaya-divase vṛṣaravijā-nija-dayitam<br />praṇamāmi cha charaṇāntika-parichāraka-sahitam [1]
He (of divine form) came forth from the birthplace of the golden lotus—the ocean of the mellow of divine consorthood. His large, merciful eyes dispel (the suffering souls’) fear and proclaim (the surrendered souls’) victory. His tongue (constantly) vibrates the whole earth planet with Śrī Kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtan, his beauty resplendent in the robes of the sun’s radiance (saffron) that purifies the universe and dispels the suffering of material existence. On his holy day of advent, I (again and again) bow down unto that beloved associate of Śrī Vṛṣabhānu Nandinī, and the servitors of his lotus feet.
शरणागतभजनव्रतचिरपालनचरणम्।<br />सुकृतालयसरलाशयसुजनाखिलवरणम्॥<br />हरिसाधनकृतबाधनजनशासनकलनम्।<br />सचराचरकरुणाकरनिखिलाशिवदलनम्॥<br />शुभदोदयदिवसे वृषरविजानिजदयितम्।<br />प्रणमामि च चरणान्तिकपरिचारकसहितम् ॥२॥
śaraṇāgata-bhajanavrata-chirapālana-charaṇam<br />sukṛtālaya-saralāśaya-sujanākhila-varaṇam<br />harisādhana-kṛtabādhana-janaśāsana-kalanam<br />sacharāchara-karuṇākara-nikhilāśiva-dalanam<br />śubhadodaya-divase vṛṣaravijā-nija-dayitam<br />praṇamāmi cha charaṇāntika-parichāraka-sahitam [2]
The devotees surrendered in pure devotion are eternally protected at his lotus feet. He is worshippable by the pure souls endowed with sincerity and good fortune, and he accepts (even) those who obstruct the service of Śrī Hari, just to rectify them. As the very fountainhead of mercy upon all mobile and immobile beings, he crushes the inauspiciousness of the whole universe. On his holy day of advent, I (again and again) bow down unto that beloved associate of Śrī Vṛṣabhānu Nandinī, and the servitors of his lotus feet.
अतिलौकिकगतितौलिकरतिकौतुकवपुषम्।<br />अतिदैवतमतिवैष्णवयतिवैभवपुरुषम्॥<br />ससनातनरघुरूपकपरमाणुगचरितम्।<br />सुविचारक इव जीवक इति साधुभिरुदितम्॥<br />शुभदोदयदिवसे वृषरविजानिजदयितम्।<br />प्रणमामि च चरणान्तिकपरिचारकसहितम् ॥३॥
atilaukika-gatitaulika-ratikautuka-vapuṣam<br />atidaivata-mativaiṣṇava-yati-vaibhava-puruṣam<br />sasanātana-raghurūpaka-paramāṇugacharitam<br />suvichāraka iva jīvaka iti sādhubhiruditam<br />śubhadodaya-divase vṛṣaravijā-nija-dayitam<br />praṇamāmi cha charaṇāntika-parichāraka-sahitam [3]
Like a miracle, his body moves with a joyful elegance and charm beyond the world’s understanding, fulfilling the artist’s aspiration. (Or, dancing in Pastimes transcendental to the world, his artistic form incites divine love’s hankering). His intellect surpasses that of (even) the demigods, and he is nobility incarnate as the commander-in-chief of the Vaiṣṇava sannyāsīs (tridaṇḍi yatis). The sādhus of profound intellect describe the nature of his personality as meticulously in the line of Śrī Sanātan, Śrī Rūpa, and Śrī Raghunāth, and they speak of him as being on the same plane as Śrī Jīvapād (being superbly replete in perfect theistic conclusions). On his holy day of advent, I (again and again) bow down unto that beloved associate of Śrī Vṛṣabhānu Nandinī, and the servitors of his lotus feet.
सरसीतटसुखदोटजनिकटप्रियभजनम्।<br />ललितामुखललनाकुलपरमादरयजनम्॥<br />व्रजकाननबहुमाननकमलप्रियनयनम्।<br />गुणमञ्जरिगरिमागुणहरिवासनवयनम्॥<br />शुभदोदयदिवसे वृषरविजानिजदयितम्।<br />प्रणमामि च चरणान्तिकपरिचारकसहितम् ॥४॥
sarasītaṭa-sukhadoṭaja-nikaṭapriyabhajanam<br />lalitāmukha-lalanākula-paramādarayajanam<br />vrajakānana-bahumānana-kamalapriyanayanam<br />guṇamañjari-garimā-guṇa-harivāsanavayanam<br />śubhadodaya-divase vṛṣaravijā-nija-dayitam<br />praṇamāmi cha charaṇāntika-parichāraka-sahitam [4]
On the bank of Śrī Rādhā Kuṇḍa at Svānanda Sukhada Kuñja, he is devoted to the service of his beloved, and (furthermore) he is greatly endeared to the divine damsels of Vraja headed by Lalitā. He is most favourite to Kamala Mañjarī who is pre-eminent in Vṛndāvan, and with the glorious qualities of Guṇa Mañjarī he builds the residence of Śrī Hari. On his holy day of advent, I (again and again) bow down unto that beloved associate of Śrī Vṛṣabhānu Nandinī, and the servitors of his lotus feet.
विमलोत्सवममलोत्कलपुरुषोत्तमजननम्।<br />पतितोद्धृतिकरुणास्तृतिकृतनूतनपुलिनम्॥<br />मथुरापुरपुरुषोत्तमसमगौरपुरटनम्।<br />हरिकामकहरिधामकहरिनामकरटनम्॥<br />शुभदोदयदिवसे वृषरविजानिजदयितम्।<br />प्रणमामि च चरणान्तिकपरिचारकसहितम् ॥५॥
vimalotsavam amalotkala-puruṣottama-jananam<br />patitoddhṛti-karuṇāstṛti-kṛtanūtana-pulinam<br />mathurāpura-puruṣottama-samagaurapuraṭanam<br />harikāmaka-haridhāmaka-harināmaka-raṭanam<br />śubhadodaya-divase vṛṣaravijā-nija-dayitam<br />praṇamāmi cha charaṇāntika-parichāraka-sahitam [5]
He is immaculate joy incarnate, or, he is the graciousness or the joy of Vimalā Devī. He manifested the Pastimes of his advent at Puruṣottam Kṣetra in the holy land of Orissa, and he revealed his Pastimes of delivering the fallen souls and extending his mercy upon them (by awarding them the gift of divine love) at the ‘new isles’, or Nabadwīp. Circumambulating Gaura Dhām in the same way as traditionally done at Vraja Dhām and Puruṣottam Dhām, he continuously propagates—the loving desire of Vraja, the divine abode of Vaikuṇṭha, and the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa. On his day of holy advent, I (again and again) make my obeisance unto that dear associate of Śrī Vṛṣabhānu Nandinī and the servitors of his holy lotus feet.

End Notes
(1<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">kṛṣṇeti yasya giri taṁ manasādriyeta<br />dīkṣāsti chet praṇatibhiś cha bhajantam īśam<br />śuśrūṣayā bhajana-vijñam ananyam anya-<br />nindādi-śūnya-hṛdam īpsita-saṅga-labdhyā</span>
“One who chants Kṛṣṇa’s Name (the kaniṣṭha-adhikārī) should be honoured within the heart. One who is initiated and engaged in the Lord’s service (the madhyam-adhikārī) should be honoured with obeisance. One who is expert in devotion, who sees nothing apart from Kṛṣṇa, and whose heart is free from the duality of criticising and praising others (the uttam-adhikārī) should be considered most desirable association and honoured through submissive service.”
(2<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">utsāhān niśchayād dhairyāt tat tat karma-pravartanāt<br />saṅga-tyāgāt sato vṛtteḥ ṣaḍbhir bhaktiḥ prasiddhyati</span>
“Devotion is nourished by these six qualities: (1) enthusiasm; (2) faith; (3) perseverance; (4) engaging in activities that satisfy the Lord and His devotees; (5) abandoning all bad association and wrong attachment; and (6) following the behaviour prescribed by pure devotees.”
(3<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">tan-nāma-rūpa-charitādi-sukīrtanānu-<br />smṛtyoḥ krameṇa rasanā-manasī niyojya<br />tiṣṭhan vraje tad anurāgi-janānugāmī<br />kālaṁ nayed akhilam ity upadeśa-sāraḥ</span>
“Having engaged one’s tongue and mind in the gradual process of chanting and remembering Kṛṣṇa’s Names, Forms, Qualities, and Pastimes, one should reside in Vraja and spend all of their time as a follower of those who have deep loving attachment to Kṛṣṇa. This is the essence of all instruction.”
(4<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">vaikuṇṭhāj janito varā madhu-purī tatrāpi rāsotsavād-<br />vṛndāraṇyam udāra-pāṇi-ramaṇāt tatrāpi govardhanaḥ<br />rādhā-kuṇḍam ihāpi gokula-pateḥ premāmṛtāplāvanāt<br />kuryād asya virājato giri-taṭe sevāṁ vivekī na kaḥ</span>
“Above Vaikuṇṭha is Mathurā, where Kṛṣṇa took birth. Above Mathurā is Vṛndāvan, where Kṛṣṇa enjoys the Rāsa festival. Above Vṛndāvan is Govardhan, where Kṛṣṇa plays amorously. Above Govardhan is Rādhā Kuṇḍa, where the nectar of love overflows. What wise soul would not serve Rādhā Kuṇḍa beside Govardhan Hill?”
(5<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">gurau goṣṭhe goṣṭhālayiṣu sujane bhū-suragaṇe<br />sva-mantre śrī-nāmni vraja-nava-yuva-dvandva-śaraṇe<br />sadā dambhaṁ hitvā kuru ratim apūrvām atitarām<br />aye svāntar bhrātaś chaṭubhir abhiyāche dhṛta-padaḥ</span>
“O mind! O brother! I grasp your feet and implore you: give up your pride and constantly devote yourself with unprecedented intensity to Śrī Guru, Vraja, Vraja’s residents, the Vaiṣṇavas, the brāhmaṇs, your mantra for worship, the Holy Name, and the Divine Couple of Vraja’s shelter.”
(6<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">aty-āhāraḥ prayāsaś cha prajalpo niyamāgrahaḥ<br />jana-saṅgaś cha laulyañ cha ṣaḍbhir bhaktir vinaśyati</span>
“Devotion is destroyed by these six defects: (1) over-accumulation; (2) materialistic endeavour; (3) unnecessary talk; (4) rejecting guidelines meant for one’s self and following guidelines meant for others; (5) association with non-devotees; and (6) fickle-mindedness.”
(7<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">tava dāsya-sukhaika-saṅgināṁ<br />bhavaneṣv astv-api kīṭa-janma me<br />itarāv asatheṣu mā sma bhūd<br />api janma chaturmukhātmanā</span>
“O Lord! Let me take birth, even as a worm, in the home of those whose sole happiness is Your service. O Lord, never let me take birth, even as Brahmā, among those who are averse to You.”
(8<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">dṛṣṭaiḥ svabhāva-janitair vapuṣaś cha doṣair<br />na prākṛtatvam iha bhakta-janasya paśyet<br />gaṅgāmbhasāṁ na khalu bud-buda-phena-paṅkair<br />brahma-dravatvam apagachchhati nīra-dharmaiḥ</span>
“One should not consider devotees in this world mundane despite the presence of visible faults within their inborn nature and body. The water of the Ganges never loses its spiritual nature despite the fact that it exhibits bubbles, foam, and mud, which naturally appear within river water.”
(9<span class="e20">)</span> <span class="e2">asad-vārtā-veśyā visṛja mati-sarvasva-haraṇīḥ<br />kathā mukti-vyāghryā na śṛṇu kila sarvātma-gilanīḥ<br />api tyaktvā lakṣmī-pati-ratim ito vyoma-nayanīṁ<br />vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇau sva-rati-maṇi-dau tvaṁ bhaja manaḥ</span>
“O mind! Stay away from the prostitute of worldly talk, who steals the wealth of one’s devotion. Do not listen to the words of the tigress of liberation, who devours the entire self. Forsake even devotion to Lakṣmī’s Lord, who resides in Vaikuṇṭha. Serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vraja, the givers of the jewel of devotion to Themselves.”
(10<span class="e21">)</span> <span class="e2">idaṁ śarīraṁ śata-sandhi-jarjaraṁ<br />pataty avaśyaṁ pariṇāma-peśalam<br />kim auṣadhaṁ pṛchchhasi mūḍha durmate<br />nirāmayaṁ kṛṣṇa-rasāyanaṁ piba</span>
“This body, made up of hundreds of worn-out joints, will certainly perish and decompose. O foolish, wicked mind! What remedy are you searching for? Drink the healing elixir of Kṛṣṇa’s Name.”
(11<span class="e21">)</span> <span class="e2">naitan manas tava kathāsu vikuṇṭha-nātha<br />samprīyate durita-duṣṭam asādhu tīvram<br />kāmāturaṁ harṣa-śoka-bhayaiṣaṇārtaṁ<br />tasmin kathaṁ tava gatiṁ vimṛśāmi dīnaḥ</span>
“O Lord of Vaikuṇṭha! My mind is polluted by sin, disgraceful, obstinate, lustful, and disturbed by desires arising from pleasure, lamentation, and fear. It is not satisfied by discussion of You. So how shall this lowly soul contemplate Your Pastimes?”
(12<span class="e21">)</span> <span class="e2">jihvaikato ’chyuta vikarṣati māvitṛptā<br />śiśno ’nyatas tvag-udaraṁ śravaṇaṁ kutaśchit<br />ghrāṇo ’nyataś chapala-dṛk kva cha karma-śaktir<br />bahvyaḥ sapatnya iva geha-patiṁ lunanti</span>
“O Lord, like numerous co-wives dragging a householder in different directions, my insatiable tongue, genitals, skin, belly, ears, nose, restless eyes, and faculties of movement pull me in different directions and ruin me.”
(13<span class="e21">)</span> <span class="e2">tad astu me nātha sa bhūri-bhāgo<br />bhave ’tra vānyatra tu v</span><span class="e2">ā tiraśchām<br />yenāham eko ’pi bhavaj-janānāṁ<br />bhūtvā niṣeve tava pāda-pallavam</span>
“O Lord, be it as Brahmā or otherwise as an animal, may I attain the great fortune of being born as one of Your devotees and serving Your tender feet.”

All glory to Śrī Guru and Śrī Gaurāṅga

Translator’s Note
I bow at the feet of Śrī Gurudev, the Vaiṣṇavas, Śrī Gaurasundar, and all the Lord’s exalted associates. They are our eternal shelter. With hope and joy, I present this offering to them, praying that it is satisfying to their hearts.
Content
This edition of <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span> has been prepared from the Bengali version of the text edited by Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur and published by Śrī Gauḍīya Maṭh. Reference has also been made to the original publication of the text by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur in <span class="e3">Śrī Sajjana-toṣaṇī</span>. An introduction to the author and his message precedes the text, as does an article in praise of <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span> compiled from lectures by Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj. Following the text, a glossary summarises important terms, references, persons, and places that are mentioned throughout the book.
Translation
The text of <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span> is presented in a four-fold format: 1) the Bengali text of each verse, 2) its Roman transliteration, 3) its English prose-ordered phrase-by-phrase gloss, and 4) its English prose translation.
In this edition, punctuation marks to indicate grammatical compounds, speech, and past active participles have been inserted into the Bengali text and its transliteration to aid comprehension. When reading the prose-ordered phrase-by-phrase gloss, a style of translation known as <span class="e3">anvaya</span> which is common in Bengali translation of Sanskrit, please note:
1) Past active participles are often conjugated in tandem with the finite verb they accompany.
2) Verb tenses are often translated to suit idiomatic usage in English (e.g. present tense and present perfect tense are often translated as simple past tense).
3) Idiomatic uses of the passive voice in Bengali are translated in the active voice in English.
4) Correlative pronouns and prepositional cases are typically translated in the simplest grammatically equivalent forms possible.
5) Grammatically inferred and thematically implied prepositions and pronouns are set in square brackets.
It is our hope that this method of presentation, combined with a minimalistic approach to the translation, will aid readers in appreciating Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s Bengali itself, which is delightfully bold, vivid, and sweet.
Origin
This book has been prepared at the express request of Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh’s present Sevāite-President-Āchārya Om Viṣṇupād Śrīla Bhakti Nirmal Āchārya Mahārāj. It is his desire that Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s bright and concise instructions guide devotees in their practice and preaching.
Numerous devotees collaborated on this publication. Śrīpād Bhakti Prapanna Tīrtha Mahārāj assisted with the translation of the text, Jagadānanda Dās Adhikārī, Viśākhā Devī Dāsī, and others provided valuable editorial assistance, and Śrīpād Bhakti Rañjan Madhusūdan Mahārāj checked over the publication as a whole. We are deeply grateful for the selfless contributions they have all made.
Should any errors or shortcomings be found within the text, we pray the swan-like Vaiṣṇavas will overlook them, forgive us, and relish the essence of <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span>.

Introduction
The author
The place and time of Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s appearance and disappearance are generally considered unknown. On the basis of <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span>, in which Jagadānanda Paṇḍit refers to Kavi Karṇapūr as a ‘resident of my village’ (Pv: 8.15), it is understood that he spent his early life in Kāñchan Pallī, a town seventy kilometres south of Nabadwīp (now known as Kanchrapara). He further explains that Śivānanda Sen, Kavi Karṇapūr’s father, taught him <span class="e3">Bhagavad-gītā</span> in his youth and brought him to Nadia (Pv: 8.17–8). It appears that this took place while Jagadānanda was still quite young, as elsewhere he sweetly describes having a quarrel with Śrī Gaurasundar as a schoolboy in Nadia (Pv: 2.18). From this time on, Jagadānanda Paṇḍit spent his entire life in the Lord’s association. Through descriptions in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> and <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-bhāgavat</span>, it is known that Jagadānanda was present throughout the Lord’s Pastimes in Nadia, accompanied the Lord to Purī after His sannyās, and, apart from once visiting Vṛndāvan and making periodic trips to Bengal on the Lord’s order, lived and served in the Lord’s close association for the remainder of His Pastimes.
<span class="e3">Śrī Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā</span> (51) identifies Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit as a manifestation of Satyabhāmā, and in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s extraordinary character and unique relationship with Śrīman Mahāprabhu are glorified profusely:
paṇḍita jagadānanda prabhura prāṇa-rūpa<br />loke khyāta ye̐ho satyabhāmāra svarūpa
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Ādi-līlā, 10.21)
“Jagadānanda Paṇḍit is the life of the Lord. He is known everywhere as a manifestation of Satyabhāmā.”
prabhura atyanta priya paṇḍita-jagadānanda<br />yāhāra charitre prabhu pāyena ānanda
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Antya-līlā, 19.4)
“Jagadānanda Paṇḍit was extremely dear to the Lord. The Lord derived great pleasure from his character.”
Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s relationship with the Lord was on the highest platform of intimacy—madhura-rasa.
purīra vātsalya mukhya	rāmānandera śuddha-sakhya<br />	govindādyera śuddha-dāsya-rasa<br />gadādhara jagadānanda	svarūpera (mukhya) rasānanda<br />	ei chāri-bhāve prabhu vaśa
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Madhya-līlā, 2.78)
“The vātsalya of Paramānanda Purī, pure sakhya of Rāmānanda Rāy, pure dāsya of Govinda, and the joy of the madhura rasa of Gadādhar, Jagadānanda, and Svarūp Damodar—the Lord was captivated by these four moods.”
Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s love was characterised by vāmya-bhāva, the mood predominant in Vṛndāvan amongst Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Her entourage (as well as their expansions in Dvārakā—Satyabhāmā and her attendants).
jagadānanda-paṇḍitera śuddha gāḍha bhāva<br />satyabhāmā-prāya prema “vāmya-svabhāva”<br />bāra bāra praṇaya kalaha kare prabhu-sane<br />anyo ’nye khaṭmaṭi chale dui-jane
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Antya-līlā, 7.138–9)
“Jagadānanda Paṇḍit has deep, pure devotion, and, like Satyabhāmā, his love is ‘leftist’. Again and again, he lovingly quarrels with the Lord. There are always disagreements between them.”
prītye karite chāhe prabhura lālana-pālana<br />vairāgya-loka-bhaye prabhu nā māne kakhana<br />dui-jane khaṭmaṭi lāgāya kondala
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Ādi-līlā, 10.22–3)
“Out of love, Jagadānanda desires to comfort the Lord, but because the Lord is a renunciant and thus concerned about public opinion, He never accepts this. Thus, they disagree and quarrel.”
jagadānande-prabhute prema chale ei-mate<br />satyabhāmā-kṛṣṇe yaichhe śuni bhāgavate<br />jagadānandera saubhāgyera ke kahibe sīmā?<br />jagadānandera saubhāgyera te̐ha se upamā
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Antya-līlā, 12.152–3)
“Divine love flowed between Jagadānanda and the Lord as we hear in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>that it did between Satyabhāmā and Kṛṣṇa. Who can describe the extent of Jagadānanda’s fortune? He is the only comparison that there is for his fortune (his fortune is incomparable).”
Jagadānanda Paṇḍit not only had profoundly intimate Pastimes with the Lord, he also had the deepest form of association with the Lord’s devotees—he would relieve them of their sorrow in separation from the Lord.
prati-vatsara prabhu tā̐re pāṭhāna nadīyāte<br />vichchheda-duḥkhitā jāni’ jananī āśvāsite<br />nadīyāra bhakta-gaṇe sabāre mililā<br />jagadānande pāñā sabe ānandita hailā<br />chaitanyera marma-kathā śune tā̐ra mukhe<br />āpanā pāsare sabe chaitanya-kathā-sukhe<br />jagadānanda milite yāya yei bhakta-ghare<br />sei sei bhakta sukhe āpanā pāsare
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Antya-līlā, 12.5, 96, 99–100)
“Knowing His mother to be sorrowful in separation, the Lord sent Jagadānanda Paṇḍit to Nadia every year to console her. Jagadānanda would also meet with all the other devotees in Nadia, and they would all be overjoyed to meet him. They would hear confidential discussion of Śrī Chaitanya from his mouth and forget themselves in the joy of the discussions. In every home Jagadānanda visited, the devotees forgot themselves out of joy.”
Jagadānanda Paṇḍit is thus most dear to the Lord and all His devotees. May his service and teachings be worshipped eternally.
chaitanyera prema-pātra jagadānanda dhanya<br />yāre mile sei māne, “pāilu̐ chaitanya”
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Antya-līlā, 12.101)
“All glory to Jagadānanda, the carrier of Śrī Chaitanya’s love! Whoever meets him feels, ‘I have met Śrī Chaitanya!’”
The composition
Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit explains in <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span> how he came to compose this book:
“I prostrate myself at the feet of my beloved Gaura and write this <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span>, having received the order of the devotees.” (Pv: 3.7)
“I write whatever comes to my mind about Gaurāṅga’s Pastimes, whenever it does, even if it is out of sequence.” (Pv: 15.1)
“Svarūp Dāmodar asked me, ‘O Paṇḍit, what are you writing?’ I replied, ‘I am writing about whom I love.’ (Pv: 2.4)
“Svarūp Dāmodar said, ‘Then write about the Pastimes of the Lord that the world will be greatly benefitted by reading about.’ (Pv: 2.6)
“I replied, ‘I don’t know what is beneficial for the world. I simply write whatever I like.’ Svarūp left, considering me mad. Sitting alone, I write, meditating on the Lord. My mind cries, my heart cries, my eyes cry, and whenever something comes to mind, I write it down.” (Pv: 2.7, 8, 10)
The name
In <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span>, Śrīla Kṛṣṇadās Kavirāj Goswāmī writes,
jagadānandera ‘prema-vivarta’ śune yei jana<br />premera ‘svarūpa’ jāne, pāya prema-dhana
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Antya-līlā, 12.154)
“Anyone who hears of Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s <span class="e3">prema-vivarta</span> understands the nature of divine love and attains its wealth.”
In his commentary on <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span>, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur explains the meaning of ‘<span class="e3">prema-vivarta</span>’: “One meaning intended is (Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s) transformations of love (<span class="e3">premera vivarta</span>)—his indignant behaviour during loving affairs. A second meaning is the book entitled ‘<span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span>’ written by Jagadānanda Paṇḍit himself about Śrīman Mahāprabhu.”
Throughout <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span>, Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit describes the reveries, emotions, and ecstasies he experiences:
“The pangs and transformations of love constantly dance within my mind. I quarrel with Gaura every day, and thus I am known as ‘Angry Jagāi’.” (Pv: 5.1)
“I cannot tolerate a moment of separation as Gaura dances in my heart. He does not let me die, but when I live, we quarrel. How does my life go on?” (Pv: 13.10)
“Transformations of love make me dance, but, not understanding them, I am dying.” (Pv: 13.4)
“Those who have love for Gorā undergo distress: that love pulls their hearts in opposite directions simultaneously.” (Pv: 13.13)
The substance
Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s only known writing, <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span>, is immensely valuable to the followers of Śrīman Mahāprabhu. Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit describes his Pastimes with the Lord in a sweet, loving manner as though he is reminiscing with an intimate friend, adding details that deepen the meaning of many of the Pastimes recorded in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta, </span>such as his travelling to Vṛndāvan, his conversations with Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī, and his quarrel with the Lord over a pot of sandalwood oil. He also recounts Pastimes of the Lord that are not recorded anywhere else, such as his quarrelling with the Lord as a schoolboy (Pv: 2.18) and the Lord showing affection to the cowherd boys of Nadia by liberating a croco­dile (Pv: 12.15). Weaved throughout these narrations are profound expressions of union in separation that reveal the mood and ideal with which the Lord’s intimate associates serve Him.
Throughout <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span>, prominent teachings of the Gauḍīya–Vaiṣṇavas as given in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> are highlighted:
Śrī Gaurasundar is Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa combined (Cc: Ādi, 1.5):
<span class="e2">“</span>The Absolute is sometimes two, as Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and sometimes one, as Śrī Chaitanya, the Supreme Being.” (Pv: 1.2)
Svayam Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa appeared as Śrī Gaurasundar to explore the mystery of Śrī Rādhā’s love for Him (Cc: Ādi, 1.6):
[The Lord decided:] “I will take Rādhā’s heart and halo, become Gaura, and relish Kṛṣṇa’s sweetness in the mood of a devotee.” (Pv: 11.10)
Śrī Gaurasundar’s Pastimes are superior to all other līlās and forms of the Lord (Cc: Madhya, 25.264):
“Golden Kṛṣṇa appeared to fulfil His desires, and feels more joy in Nabadwīp Dhām than He does in Vraja.” (Pv: 1.39)
Rādhā-dāsyam is the essence of Śrī Gaurasundar’s ideal and gift (Cc: Madhya, 8.97):
[Jagadānanda Paṇḍit:] “I am a maidservant of Rādhā’s feet, and I love the form of the Lord that is adorned with Her halo (Śrī Gaurāṅga).” (Pv: 1.53)
The Lord appeared both as Śrī Gaurāṅga and as His Name to deliver the souls of Kali-yuga (Cc: Ādi, 1.4, 17.22):
<span class="e2">“</span>Being merciful to the conditioned souls, Kṛṣṇa appeared as His Name, and being compassionate to the souls of Kali-yuga, He appeared as Gaura.” (Pv: 7.17)
Śrī Hari-nām-saṅkīrtan is the dharma of the modern age (Cc: Ādi, 7.74):
“O devotees, hear about the dharma in the Age of Kali: there is no duty other than chanting the Name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.” (Pv: 19.3)
True devotees of the Name always avoid the association of non-devotees and those attached to the pleasures of the world (Cc: Madhya, 22.84):
“Brother, the Name of Kṛṣṇa never appears in bad association: the letters of the Name may appear, but the Name never does.” (Pv: 7.1)
The Name must be chanted without offence (Cc: Ādi, 8.24):
“Only by very carefully avoiding the offences to the Name does the soul attain all perfection and reach the Lord. Those who understand the offences but are unconcerned about avoiding them are foolish and suffer forever.” (Pv: 19.115, 124)
Surrender is the essence of avoiding offences, chanting the Name, and the practice of devotion itself (Cc: Madhya, 22.33, 99):
“When you sincerely take shelter of the Lord, all your offences are destroyed, you never again have any taste for sin and suffering, your piety and sins disappear, and you conquer the illusory environment.” (Pv: 19.108–9)
Only detachment produced by devotion is natural (Cc: Madhya, 16.238–9):
“Service to Kṛṣṇa and the sādhus is relishable to the soul. By simply opposing material nature, you end up completely disheartened.” (Pv: 9.7)
The soul, a part and parcel of Kṛṣṇa’s energy, is Kṛṣṇa’s eternal servant and naturally serves Him under the spell of His all-attractive nature (Cc: Madhya, 20.108–9, 21.102):
“The soul is a spiritual spark, and Kṛṣṇa is the spiritual sun. Seeing eternal Kṛṣṇa, the soul adores Him.” (Pv: 6.1)
The only qualification for devotion is faith (Cc: Madhya, 22.64):
“Every human being—if they have faith—is qualified to chant the Name. The arguments and brashness of speculators about caste and class do not count for anything.” (Pv: 10.1)
Having desires contrary to the Lord’s will is the one and only cause of the soul’s fall, illusion, and suffering (Cc: Madhya, 20.117):
“When the soul becomes averse to Kṛṣṇa and desires enjoyment, nearby Māyā seizes them.<span class="e2"> </span>Forgetting, ‘I am an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa’, the soul becomes a slave of Māyā and wanders indefinitely (suffering the consequences of their actions in the material world).” (Pv: 6.2, 4)
Sādhu-saṅga is the fundamental basis of deliverance and devotion (Cc: Madhya, 22.45, 80):
“When the souls’ wandering throughout saṁsāra comes to an end, then, according to their fortune, they attain the association of the sādhus. Brother, as a result of association with the sādhus, devotion to Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of all Lords, appears within their hearts.” (Pv: 12.3–4)
The combination of service to the devotees and service to the Name is the essence of the practice given by Śrī Gaurasundar (Cc: Madhya, 22.124):
“I want only to chant the Name of Kṛṣṇa in the association of the sādhus—there is no other way to conquer saṁsāra.” (Pv: 6.13)
Serving Vaiṣṇavas is real service to the Lord (Cc: Madhya, 16.70):
“Serve Gaura’s devotees with perfect sincerity, and then, brother, you will reach Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s feet.” (Pv: 7.18)
Divine love is the supreme goal of devotional practice (Cc: Madhya, 19.164):
“Be free from offences and chant the Name of Kṛṣṇa. Then divine love will come with the Name and reside within your heart.” (Pv: 19.156)
Divine love captivates the Lord Himself (Cc: Madhya, 8.88):
“The Lord never leaves the sincere hearts of those who have bound His lotus feet with the rope of divine love.” (Pv: 12.25)
Divine love is the supreme fulfilment (Cc: Madhya, 2.49):
“Love for Kṛṣṇa is perfectly pure, like the pure water of the Ganges; it is an ocean of nectar. Within such pure love, there is not even a trace of mundanity. It is like a white cloth free from even one spot of ink. Pure love is an ocean of joy. I have received one drop of it, and this drop floods the world.” (Pv: 16.15–6)
<span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span> thus serves as a comprehensive companion to <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span>. In a text less than one-tenth of <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta’s </span>length, Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit has presented the gist of Gauḍīya–Vaiṣṇava theology—sambandha, abhidheya, and prayojan—in clear-cut, energetic summaries composed in sweet vernacular rhyme. Those whose hearts are thrilled to hear the essential principles of sincerity, surrender, and devotion propounded with emphatic conviction are nourished in full by <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta.</span> Bearing in mind that our Guru-varga reveres <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> as the most revolutionary theological literature to have ever seen the light of day, when we read and reflect on <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span>, which presents <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta’s</span> wealth in a condensed and vibrant form, we can only marvel at the profundity of this simple gift. What will we not attain by taking its substance to heart?
Prayer
Holding on our heads the ideal of unconditional devotion to Śrī Gurudev, the Vaiṣṇavas, Śrī Gaurasundar, and the Lord’s eternal associates, we invoke the blessings of Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit and pray that the words of Śrīla Kṛṣṇadās Kavirāj Goswāmī may soon shine true in the hearts of all the readers:
jagadānandera ‘prema-vivarta’ śune yei jana<br />premera ‘svarūpa’ jāne, pāya prema-dhana
“Anyone who hears Jagadānanda’s <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span> understands the nature of divine love and attains its wealth.”

In Praise of <span class="e31">Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta</span>
Compiled from the talks of
Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
Śrīla Jagadānanda Paṇḍit collected his notes on Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s Pastimes and teachings, and presented them in the form of a book named <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span>. This book was published by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur and is full of Gauḍīya siddhānta.
<span class="e32">Student:</span> Some people say <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span> was written by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, not Jagadānanda Paṇḍit.
<span class="e32">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> If we can understand that <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> is the highest development of theism and the teachings of Śrī Chaitanyadev are the highest, full-fledged form of that theism, then anything that correlates with them has value and cannot but be true. Some claim that <span class="e3">Śrī Brahma-saṁhitā</span> was written by Śrī Chaitanyadev. Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī has shown that there really was a <span class="e3">Brahma-saṁhitā</span> with one hundred chapters and that the <span class="e3">Brahma-saṁhitā</span> given by Śrī Chaitanyadev is one chapter from that book. Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, however, also wrote, “We do not find any book by Śrī Chaitanyadev Himself anywhere. If <span class="e3">Brahma-saṁhitā</span> comes from Him, then we are very proud and satisfied that He has left us at least one book.” We may see <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span> in this way.
There are many things mentioned in <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span> that greatly help the Gauḍīya Maṭh’s propaganda. A particular opposition camp of the Gauḍīya Maṭh says that Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur has written <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span> in the name of Jagadānanda Paṇḍit because the book supports the Gauḍīya Maṭh’s position very well. For example, a section of sahajiyās say that there is no Ekādaśī in Purī. They say that when Mahāprabhu lived in Purī, He did not follow Ekādaśī because in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> He is always found to be taking mahāprasād. They say that in Purī even on Ekādaśī we should not fast because there is always mahāprasād present, and there mahāprasād cannot be refused. It is, however, clearly stated in Jagadānanda Paṇḍit’s <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span> that when Mahāprabhu was offered mahāprasād on Ekādaśī, He touched it to His head, kept it respectfully nearby, performed kīrtan the whole day and night, and then took the prasād the next morning. Many similar points that are very helpful for the preaching of the Gauḍīya Maṭh are found in <span class="e3">Prema-vivarta</span>.
<span class="e32">Student:</span> Was Jagadānanda Paṇḍit in the mood of Satyabhāmā or was he an incarnation of Satyabhāmā?
<span class="e32">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> He was an incarnation of Satyabhāmā. Satyabhāmā’s mood is known as vāmya-bhāva, opposition. She is very sentimental. She apparently opposes the Lord and behaves insistently. Ostentatiously, she opposes the Lord, but from the heart she has no opposition to Him, only loving emotions. Jagadānanda Paṇḍit sometimes played with the Lord in a way that might seem sinful. He was full of sentiments, but he has the highest qualification of having the greatest attraction to Mahāprabhu.
Once, Jagadānanda Paṇḍit asked Mahāprabhu for permission to go to Vṛndāvan. Mahāprabhu granted him permission but gave him instructions to follow while he was there.
mathurā gele sanātana-saṅgei rahibā<br />mathurāra svāmī sabera charaṇa vandibā<br />dūre rahi’ bhakti kariha saṅge nā rahibā<br />tā̐-sabāra āchāra-cheṣṭā la-ite nāribā<br />sanātana-saṅge kariha vana daraśana<br />sanātanera saṅga nā chhāḍibā eka-kṣaṇa<br />śīghra āsiha, tāhā̐ nā rahiha chira-kāla<br />govardhane nā chaḍiha dekhite ‘gopāla’
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Antya-līlā, 13.36–39)
“You may go to Vṛndāvan, but do not remain there for a long time and do not climb on top of Govardhan to see Mādhavendra Purī’s Gopāl. Offer respect to the Vraja-vāsīs, but do not imitate their practices. And as long as you are there, stay under the guidance of Sanātan.”
<span class="e32">Student:</span> Why did the Lord tell Jagadānanda Paṇḍit not to come too close to the Vraja-vāsīs?
<span class="e32">Śrīla Śrīdhar Mahārāj:</span> Although the Lord was advising Jagadānanda, these instructions are really for us. They are to warn us that the Vraja-vāsīs may not be scrupulous about following physical practices, and that we should not imitate their external behaviour. Also, in Vraja at that time, everyone was not a follower of Chaitanyadev. They were followers of Nimbārka Āchārya, Viṣṇu Swāmī, and others. Furthermore, it was a period of Mohammedan rule. Under those circumstances, Mahāprabhu did not want Jagadānanda’s sentiments to be publicly exposed in Vraja Maṇḍal. Sanātan Goswāmī was the most sober and respected follower of Mahāprabhu there, and he could deal with things in the locality well. Jagadānanda was very intolerant of anyone who did not follow Mahāprabhu. He had many eccentricities, and he could create havoc. Mahāprabhu thought, “He quarrels even with Me here. He won’t care for anyone there. For his own interest, he may create quarrel there. So, he should always be under the guidance of Sanātan. Sanātan is a sober man and knows how to deal with the people in that place. He is My trusted leader there. Jagadānanda must remain under his guidance and should not mix closely with the Vraja-vāsīs. Because of his intolerance, he may quarrel with them.” Mahāprabhu knew Jagadānanda was very sentimental, and He did not want that Jagadānanda would go there and freely display intense sentiments for Him. Still, Jagadānanda did so.
One day, while Jagadānanda Paṇḍit was cooking, Sanātan Goswāmī came to visit him just as he was placing a cooking pot on the oven. Sanātan Goswāmī was wearing a turban made of red cloth. Jagadānanda Prabhu was delighted to see the red cloth and said, “That must be Mahāprabhu’s cloth! Did He give it to you?”
Sanātan Goswāmī replied, “No, no. I received this cloth from another sannyāsī, Mukunda Saraswatī, who stays in this area.”
Jagadānanda said, “Oh! Is it? You are the leading follower of Mahāprabhu but you wear on your head the cloth of another sannyāsī!”
Jagadānanda rushed toward Sanātan to strike Sanātan with the cooking pot in his hand. “Who can tolerate this?” he exclaimed.
“Yes, Paṇḍitjī!” Sanātan Goswāmī joined his palms, “I have now found the jewel I have been searching for. I wanted to see your exclusive love for Mahāprabhu, and today, by Mahāprabhu’s grace, I have seen it. I wore this turban only with the hope that I would see your exclusive devotion to Mahāprabhu and the extreme intolerance produced by your love. Seeing the intensity of your love for Mahāprabhu, my life is fulfilled. I am very fortunate.”
Jagadānanda was nonplussed by Sanātan’s words and felt that his excitement was quite abrupt and awkward. He felt shy and fell silent. Then he said, “No, no, no. I am mistaken. But who can tolerate this? You are one of the main followers of Mahāprabhu, but you have such respect for another sannyāsī, a māyāvādī, that you wear his cloth on your head as a turban? I cannot tolerate this, but please forgive me for coming to strike you.”
On another occasion, when Sanātan Goswāmī came to Purī, he asked for Jagadānanda’s advice as to whether he should remain there with Mahāprabhu or return to Vṛndāvan. Jagadānanda advised him to return to Vṛndāvan, and later Śrīman Mahāprabhu heard that Jagadānanda had given this advice to Sanātan Goswāmī, who was his senior. Mahāprabhu chastised Jagadānanda and then praised Sanātan Goswāmī, but Sanātan Goswāmī replied to Mahāprabhu, “Oh! This is my misfortune. You are feeding me so much bitterness coated with praise. Jagadānanda’s fortune is higher. You blame him and punish him with ill words—that means that You think of him as Your own, but You keep me at a respectful distance. This shows his good fortune and my bad fortune. It is my bad fate that You praise me and keep me at a respectful distance. That You punish Jagadānanda shows that You favour him, and that he is Your own. You are actually treating him most affectionately.”
Through Sanātan’s glorification, we can understand the exalted position of Jagadānanda Paṇḍit and his intimate relationship with Mahāprabhu.
In another instance, Jagadānanda Paṇḍit carried a large clay pot full of sandalwood oil from Bengal to Purī, a distance of more than three hundred miles. He came to Govinda, Mahāprabhu’s personal servant, and modestly offered it: “With great trouble, I have carried this pot full of sandalwood oil here for Mahāprabhu. May the Lord graciously accept it. Please keep it here. You can massage Mahāprabhu’s head with this oil; it has a cooling effect. Sometimes the Lord cannot sleep, and sometimes He speaks deliriously. This oil will help Him greatly at those times. I have taken the oil from Śivānanda Sen, and it is pure. Please keep it here and use it for the Lord.”
Mahāprabhu overheard Jagadānanda saying this to Govinda. “What is this?” He asked.
“Jagadānanda Paṇḍit has brought a full pot of sandalwood oil for You, and his request is that You smear it on Your head now and then so that You will sleep soundly and remain in good health”, said Govinda.
“No, no, no. Sandalwood oil is very fragrant. What will people say about Me? I am a sannyāsī. If I smear this oil on My head and go to see Jagannāth, the public will smell it and say, ‘Such luxury for a sannyāsī? Does He also keep a woman with Him?’ I cannot use this oil at all. I will get a bad name.”
Mahāprabhu turned to Jagadānanda, “Would that please you? I advise you to take the oil to the Temple of Jagannāth. There it can be burned in the lamps, and Jagannāth will enjoy its scent. In that way, your labour of carrying the oil here will be successful. You will be greatly benefitted by offering the oil in that way.”
“Remove the oil from My room”, Mahāprabhu said to Govinda.
Hearing this, Jagadānanda took the pot of oil from Govinda, came in front of Mahāprabhu, and smashed it on the floor. The oil spilled everywhere, and Jagadānanda ran straight to his room. He locked the door from the inside and did not come out for three days. When Mahāprabhu heard that Jagadānanda had been fasting for three days, He could not contain Himself, and He personally went to Jagadānanda’s door. “O Jagadānanda! What is the matter? Arise and open the door. Today, I shall take prasādam prepared by your hands. I will not take prasādam from anyone else. I am going now, and at noon time I will return to take lunch here, prepared by you.”
Jagadānanda thought, “Oh! Mahāprabhu will accept my cooking today!” He got out of bed and began to cook. Mahāprabhu came with Govinda to take prasādam, and He remarked, “Oh! All the dishes are very, very sweet today. Perhaps your cooking with a hot temper has made them extra sweet.”
After eating, Mahāprabhu stood and said, “Now you eat. Before I leave, I want to see you eat.”
Jagadānanda replied, “Oh no, no, no. My Lord, You go and take rest. I shall take later. Certainly I will eat.”
Mahāprabhu said, “Govinda, you remain here. Once Jagadānanda has eaten, come and inform Me.” Finally, Jagadānanda took prasādam.
Jagadānanda Paṇḍit has a very sentimental character like that of Satyabhāmā. He cannot give up his tendency of being reactionary towards Mahāprabhu. He is abhimānyu, very sensitive about subtle things, and known for his prema-vivarta, the peculiar charac­teristics of the reactions produced by his divine love. They are of a peculiar type and are described in the science of divine love. Like Satyabhāmā, he has vāmya-bhāva, which is the nature of the highest class of heroines (nāyikās). They instantly refuse whatever is offered to them by their lover (nāyaka). In the science of love, we are told that this nature is the most valuable: it increases the lover’s earnestness.
Rādhārāṇī’s nature is also of that type: always in opposition (nirantara vāmya). This spirit of opposition is a peculiar thing, and the experts in rasa say that it is the highest mood because it enhances the intensity of the other side. This mood is found in Jagadānanda and Satyabhāmā.
After Kṛṣṇa went to Mathurā, His Vṛndāvan-līlā continued underground, that is, outside of ordinary vision. During that time, parts (aṁśas) of the gopīs went to Dvārakā. Satyabhāmā appeared from a portion of Rādhārāṇī’s lustre and Rukmiṇī from Chandrāvalī’s. Chandrāvalī is more judicious, Rādhārāṇī more sentimental. Senti­ment has the upper hand in Vṛndāvan: it is above judiciousness in matters of love. In Dvārakā, however, judiciousness gets the upper hand, and sentimentalism goes into the lower position. So, Satyabhāmā—Rādhārāṇī’s connection, or shadow—is considered of lower value there, and the judiciousness and cleverness of Chandrāvalī—Rukmiṇī—comes into the first rank. The mood that has its highest glory in Vṛndāvan cannot play fully in Dvārakā. It goes into a secondary position there. These are the peculiarities in the līlā.
yathā yathā gaura-padāravinde<br />vindeta bhaktiṁ kṛta-puṇya-rāśiḥ<br />tathā tathotsarpati hṛdy akasmād<br />rādhā-padāmbhoja-sudhāmburāśiḥ
(Śrī Chaitanya-chandrāmṛta: 88)
As much as one engages in the service of Gaura-līlā, automatically one finds oneself within the inner development of the service of Śrī Rādhikā in Vraja-līlā. One’s service begins here and reaches there. Automatically, spontaneously, one will be led there to the service of the highest value and quality. So, begin properly with Gaura-līlā, begin with Nityānanda and Gaura-Gadādhar, and then find yourself in the midst of Vṛndāvan-lilā. Unknowingly, you will find, “I have attained a good position in Vṛndāvan-līlā.”

শ্রীশ্রীপ্রেমবিবর্ত্ত
Śrī Śrī Prema-vivarta

Chapter One
মঙ্গলাচরণ
Maṅgalācharaṇa
Invocation of Auspiciousness
রাধাকৃষ্ণপ্রণয়বিকৃতির্হ্লাদিনী শক্তিরস্মাদ্<br />একাত্মানাবপি ভুবি পুরা দেহভেদং গতৌ তৌ<br />চৈতন্যাখ্যং প্রকটমধুনা তদ্দ্বয়ং চৈক্যমাপ্তং<br />রাধাভাবদ্যুতিসুবলিতং নৌমি কৃষ্ণস্বরূপম্
rādhā-kṛṣṇa-praṇaya-vikṛtir hlādinī-śaktir asmād<br />ekātmānāv api bhuvi purā deha-bhedaṁ gatau tau<br />chaitanyākhyaṁ prakaṭam adhunā tad-dvayaṁ chaikyam āptaṁ<br />rādhā-bhāva-dyuti-suvalitaṁ naumi kṛṣṇa-svarūpam
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Ādi-līlā, 1.5)
<span class="e2">api</span>–Although <span class="e2">tau</span>–They [are] <span class="e2">eka-ātmānau</span>–by nature one, <span class="e2">asmāt</span>–through <span class="e2">hlādinī-śaktiḥ</span>–the pleasure potency, <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa-praṇaya-vikṛtiḥ</span>–a transformation of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s love, [They] <span class="e2">purā</span>–eternally <span class="e2">gatau</span>–possess <span class="e2">deha-bhedam</span>–separate bodies <span class="e2">bhuvi</span>–within the world. <span class="e2">adhunā</span>–Now, <span class="e2">tad-dvayam</span>–these two <span class="e2">āptam</span>–have become <span class="e2">prakaṭam</span>–manifest <span class="e2">aikyam</span>–as one <span class="e2">cha</span>–and [are] <span class="e2">ākhyam</span>–known as <span class="e2">chaitanya</span>–‘Chaitanya’. <span class="e2">naumi</span>–I bow <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-svarūpam</span>–to Kṛṣṇa’s form <span class="e2">suvalitam</span>–adorned with <span class="e2">rādhā-bhāva-dyuti</span>–the heart and halo of Śrī Rādhā.
Although Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa are by nature one, through the hlādinī-śakti, a transformation of Their love, They exist eternally in separate forms. Now, They have manifested in one combined form as Śrī Chaitanya. I bow to Him, Kṛṣṇa Himself adorned with the heart and halo of Śrī Rādhā.
শ্রীরাধাকৃষ্ণতত্ত্ব
śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-tattva
The nature of Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa
অখণ্ড-অদ্বয়-জ্ঞান সর্ব্বতত্ত্বসার ।<br />সেই তত্ত্বে দণ্ড-পরণাম বার বার ॥১॥
akhaṇḍa-advaya-jñāna sarva-tattva-sāra<br />sei tattve daṇḍa-paraṇāma bāra bāra [1]
<span class="e2">daṇḍa-paraṇāma</span>–I bow <span class="e2">bāra</span> <span class="e2">bāra</span>–again and again <span class="e2">sei khaṇḍa-advaya-jñāna tattve</span>–to the indivisible, nondual Absolute, <span class="e2">sarva-tattva-sāra</span>–the essence of all truths.
I bow again and again to the indivisible, nondual Absolute, the essence of all truths.
সেই তত্ত্ব কভু দুই রাধাকৃষ্ণরূপে ।<br />কভু এক পরাৎপর চৈতন্যস্বরূপে ॥২॥
sei tattva kabhu dui rādhā-kṛṣṇa-rūpe<br />kabhu eka parātpara chaitanya-svarūpe [2]
<span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">tattva</span>–The Absolute [is] <span class="e2">kabhu</span>–sometimes <span class="e2">dui</span>–two <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa-rūpe</span>–as Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, [and] <span class="e2">kabhu</span>–sometimes <span class="e2">eka</span>–one <span class="e2">chaitanya-svarūpe</span>–as Śrī Chaitanya, <span class="e2">parātpara</span>–the Supreme Being.
The Absolute is sometimes two, as Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and sometimes one, as Śrī Chaitanya, the Supreme Being.
তত্ত্ব-বস্তু এক সদা অদ্বিতীয় ভায় ।<br />বস্তু বস্তুশক্তি মাঝে কিছু ভেদ নাই ॥৩॥
tattva-vastu eka sadā advitīya bhāya<br />vastu vastu-śakti mājhe kichhu bheda nāi [3]
<span class="e2">tattva-vastu</span>–The Absolute [is] <span class="e2">sadā</span>–eternally <span class="e2">eka</span>–one <span class="e2">advitīya bhāya</span>–without a second, [and] <span class="e2">kichhu</span> <span class="e2">nāi</span>–there is no <span class="e2">bheda</span>–difference <span class="e2">mājhe</span>–between <span class="e2">vastu</span>–the Absolute [and] <span class="e2">vastu-śakti</span>–the Absolute’s energy.
The Absolute is eternally one without a second, and there is no difference between the Absolute and the Absolute’s energy.
ভেদ নাই বটে, কিন্তু সদা ভেদ তায় ।<br />“ভেদাভেদ অবিচিন্ত্য” সর্ব্ব-বেদে গায় ॥৪॥
bheda nāi vaṭe, kintu sadā bheda tāya<br />“bhedābheda avichintya” sarva-vede gāya [4]
<span class="e2">vaṭe</span>–Truly, <span class="e2">nāi</span>–there is no <span class="e2">bheda</span>–difference [between them], <span class="e2">kintu</span>–yet [there is] <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always <span class="e2">bheda</span>–a difference <span class="e2">tāya</span>–between them. <span class="e2">sarva-vede</span>–All the Vedas <span class="e2">gāya</span>–glorify <span class="e2">“bhedābheda</span> <span class="e2">avichintya”</span>–this “inconceivable difference and nondifference”.
Truly, there is no difference between them, yet there is always a difference between them. All the Vedas glorify this “inconceivable difference and nondifference”.
বস্তুশক্তি চিৎ-স্বরূপ ভাবেতে সন্ধিনী ।<br />ক্রিয়াতে হ্লাদিনী তাই ত্রিভাবধারিণী ॥৫॥
vastu-śakti chit-svarūpa bhāvete sandhinī<br />kriyāte hlādinī tāi tribhāva-dhāriṇī [5]
<span class="e2">vastu-śakti</span>–The Absolute’s energy [is] <span class="e2">chit-svarūpa</span>–spirit by nature, <span class="e2">bhāvete</span> <span class="e2">sandhinī</span>–existence in form, [and] <span class="e2">kriyāte</span> <span class="e2">hlādinī</span>–pleasure in action, [and] <span class="e2">tāi</span>–thus <span class="e2">tribhāva-dhāriṇī</span>–possesses three aspects.
The Absolute’s energy is spirit by nature, existence in form, and pleasure in action. The Absolute’s energy thus possesses three aspects.
বস্তুশক্তিদ্বারে বস্তু দেয় পরিচয় ।<br />বস্তুশক্তি ক্রিয়াযোগে সর্ব্ব সিদ্ধ হয় ॥৬॥
vastu-śakti-dvāre vastu deya parichaya<br />vastu-śakti kriyā-yoge sarva siddha haya [6]
<span class="e2">vastu</span>–The Absolute <span class="e2">parichaya deya</span>–reveals Himself <span class="e2">vastu-śakti-dvāre</span>–through the Absolute’s energy; <span class="e2">sarva</span>–everything <span class="e2">haya</span>–is <span class="e2">siddha</span>–effected <span class="e2">kriyā-yoge</span>–by the action <span class="e2">vastu-śakti</span>–of the Absolute’s energy.
The Absolute reveals Himself through His energy; everything is effected by the action of the Absolute’s energy.
অখণ্ড বস্তুতে ভাব ক্রিয়া নিত্য হয় ।<br />শক্তি শক্তিমান্ বস্তু তবু পৃথক্ নয় ॥৭॥
akhaṇḍa vastute bhāva kriyā nitya haya<br />śakti śaktimān vastu tabu pṛthak naya [7]
<span class="e2">bhāva</span>–Feeling [and] <span class="e2">kriyā</span>–action <span class="e2">haya</span>–happen <span class="e2">nitya</span>–constantly <span class="e2">akhaṇḍa</span> <span class="e2">vastute</span>–within the indivisible Absolute. <span class="e2">vastu</span>–The Absolute [is]<span class="e2"> śakti</span>–energy [and] <span class="e2">śaktimān</span>–the possessor of all energy. <span class="e2">tabu</span>–Still, <span class="e2">naya</span>–the Absolute is not <span class="e2">pṛthak</span>–differentiated.
Feeling and action happen constantly within the indivisible Absolute. The Absolute is energy and the possessor of all energy. Still, the Absolute is not differentiated.
হ্লাদিনী বস্তুকে দিয়া দুইটী স্বরূপ ।<br />ব্রজে রাধাকৃষ্ণলীলা করায় অপরূপ ॥৮॥
hlādinī vastuke diyā duiṭī svarūpa<br />vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇa-līlā karāya aparūpa [8]
<span class="e2">hlādinī</span>–The pleasure potency <span class="e2">vastuke</span> <span class="e2">duiṭī</span> <span class="e2">svarūpa diyā</span>–separates the Absolute into two [and] <span class="e2">karāya</span>–makes <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa-līlā</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s Pastimes <span class="e2">vraje</span>–in Vraja <span class="e2">aparūpa</span>–sublime.
The hlādinī-śakti separates the Absolute into two and makes Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s Pastimes in Vraja sublime.
রাধাকৃষ্ণ-প্রণয়ের বিকৃতি হ্লাদিনী ।<br />অবিচিন্ত্য শক্তি রাধাকৃষ্ণ-উন্মাদিনী ॥৯॥
rādhā-kṛṣṇa-praṇayera vikṛti hlādinī<br />avichintya śakti rādhā-kṛṣṇa-unmādinī [9]
<span class="e2">hlādinī</span>–The pleasure potency [is] <span class="e2">vikṛti</span>–a transformation<span class="e2"> rādhā-kṛṣṇa-praṇayera</span>–of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s love, <span class="e2">avichintya śakti</span>–an inconceivable energy [that] <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa-unmādinī</span>–delights Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.
The hlādinī-śakti is a transformation of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s love, an inconceivable energy that delights Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.
অঘটন ঘটাইতে ধরে মহাশক্তি ।<br />নির্ব্বিকারে করিয়াছে বিকার অনুরক্তি ॥১০॥
aghaṭana ghaṭāite dhare mahāśakti<br />nirvikāre kariyāchhe vikāra anurakti [10]
<span class="e2">dhare</span>–She has <span class="e2">mahāśakti</span>–immense power <span class="e2">aghaṭana</span> <span class="e2">ghaṭāite</span>–to make the impossible possible: <span class="e2">kariyāchhe</span>–she has made <span class="e2">vikāra</span>–transformations <span class="e2">anurakti</span>–of love <span class="e2">nirvikāre</span>–within that which is non-transformable.
The hlādinī-śakti has immense power to make the impossible possible: she has made transformations of love within the non-transformable Absolute.
তত্ত্ববস্তু তার্কিকের অগোচর; কৃষ্ণকৃপাসাপেক্ষ
tattva-vastu tārkikera agochara; kṛṣṇa-kṛpā-sāpekṣa
The Absolute is incomprehensible to speculators; realisation is dependent on Kṛṣṇa’s grace
এবে এক উঠিল অপূর্ব্ব পূর্ব্বপক্ষ ।<br />তার্কিক না বুঝে যদি চিন্তে বর্ষ লক্ষ ॥১১॥
ebe eka uṭhila apūrva pūrva-pakṣa<br />tārkika nā bujhe yadi chinte varṣa lakṣa [11]
<span class="e2">ebe</span>–Now, <span class="e2">eka</span>–an <span class="e2">apūrva</span>–unprecedented <span class="e2">pūrva-pakṣa</span>–proposition <span class="e2">uṭhila</span>–has arisen [that] <span class="e2">tārkika</span>–speculators <span class="e2">bujhe nā</span>–do not understand [even] <span class="e2">yadi</span>–if <span class="e2">chinte</span>–they think [about it] <span class="e2">lakṣa varṣa</span>–for hundreds of thousands of years.
Now, an unprecedented proposition has arisen that speculators do not understand, even if they think about it for hundreds of thousands of years.
কৃষ্ণ যারে কৃপা করে সেই মাত্র জানে ।<br />লক্ষবর্ষ চিন্তি তাহা না বুঝিবে আনে ॥১২॥
kṛṣṇa yāre kṛpā kare sei mātra jāne<br />lakṣa-varṣa chinti’ tāhā nā bujhibe āne [12]
<span class="e2">mātra</span>–Only <span class="e2">sei</span>–those <span class="e2">yāre</span>–whom <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–Kṛṣṇa <span class="e2">kṛpā kare</span>–blesses <span class="e2">jāne</span>–understand [it]. <span class="e2">āne</span>–Others <span class="e2">bujhibe nā</span>–will not understand <span class="e2">tāhā</span>–it [even] <span class="e2">chinti’</span>–after thinking [about it] <span class="e2">lakṣa-varṣa</span>–for hundreds of thousands of years.
Only those whom Kṛṣṇa blesses understand it. Others will not understand it, even after thinking about it for hundreds of thousands of years.
রাধাকৃষ্ণ-প্রণয়ের বিকার হ্লাদিনী ।<br />প্রণয়ের পরে জন্মে চিত্ত-উন্মাদিনী ॥১৩॥
rādhā-kṛṣṇa-praṇayera vikāra hlādinī<br />praṇayera pare janme chitta-unmādinī [13]
<span class="e2">hlādinī</span>–The pleasure potency, <span class="e2">vikāra</span>–a transformation<span class="e2"> rādhā-kṛṣṇa-praṇayera</span>–of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s love, <span class="e2">janme</span>–manifests <span class="e2">pare</span>–after [Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s] <span class="e2">praṇayera</span>–love [and] <span class="e2">chitta-unmādinī</span>–delights [Their] hearts.
The hlādinī-śakti, a transformation of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s love, manifests after Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s love and delights Their hearts.
রাধা-কৃষ্ণ দুই হলে হয় ত প্রণয় ।<br />প্রণয় হৈলে তবে বিকার ঘটয় ॥১৪॥
rādhā-kṛṣṇa dui hale haya ta’ praṇaya<br />praṇaya ha-ile tabe vikāra ghaṭaya [14]
[When] <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa <span class="e2">hale</span>–become <span class="e2">dui</span>–two, <span class="e2">praṇaya</span>–love <span class="e2">ta’ haya</span>–manifests, [and when] <span class="e2">praṇaya</span>–love <span class="e2">ha-ile</span>–manifests, <span class="e2">tabe</span>–then <span class="e2">vikāra</span>–transformations <span class="e2">ghaṭaya</span>–occur.
When Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa become two, love manifests, and when love manifests, transformations occur.
দুই দেহ হবার আগে বিকার না ছিল ।<br />তবে এক রূপ দুই কেমনে হৈল ॥১৫॥
dui deha habāra āge vikāra nā chhila<br />tabe eka-rūpa dui kemane ha-ila [15]
<span class="e2">āge</span>–Before <span class="e2">habāra</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa assumed <span class="e2">dui</span>–two <span class="e2">deha</span>–bodies, <span class="e2">chhila nā</span>–there were no <span class="e2">vikāra</span>–transformations. <span class="e2">tabe</span>–So, <span class="e2">kemane</span>–how [did] <span class="e2">eka-rūpa</span>–one form <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–become <span class="e2">dui</span>–two?
Before Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa assumed two bodies, there were no transformations. So, how did one form become two?
হ্লাদিনী হইতে হয় দুই দেহ ভেদ ।<br />কোথা বা হ্লাদিনী ছিল হইল প্রভেদ ॥১৬॥
hlādinī ha-ite haya dui deha bheda<br />kothā vā hlādinī chhila ha-ila prabheda [16]
<span class="e2">bheda haya</span>–One form separated [into] <span class="e2">dui</span>–two <span class="e2">deha</span>–bodies <span class="e2">ha-ite</span>–because of <span class="e2">hlādinī</span>–the hlādinī-śakti. [But] <span class="e2">kothā</span> <span class="e2">vā</span>–where <span class="e2">chhila</span>–was <span class="e2">hlādinī</span>–the hlādinī-śakti [when] <span class="e2">prabheda ha-ila</span>–they separated?
One form separated into two because of the hlādinī-śakti. But where was the hlādinī-śakti when they separated?
এই প্রশ্নের এক মাত্র আছে ত’ উত্তর ।<br />দেশকালাতীত কৃষ্ণতত্ত্ব নিরন্তর ॥১৭॥
ei praśnera eka-mātra āchhe ta’ uttara<br />deśa-kālātīta kṛṣṇa-tattva nirantara [17]
<span class="e2">eka-mātra</span>–The only <span class="e2">uttara</span>–answer <span class="e2">ta’ āchhe</span>–there is <span class="e2">ei</span> <span class="e2">praśnera</span>–to this question [is that] <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-tattva</span>–Kṛṣṇa, by nature, [is] <span class="e2">nirantara</span>–eternally <span class="e2">deśa-kālātīta</span>–beyond time and space.
The only answer to this question is that Kṛṣṇa, by nature, is eternally transcendental to time and space.
অপ্রাকৃত-তত্ত্বে দেশকালাদির বিচার নাই
aprākṛta-tattve deśa-kālādira vichāra nāi
There is no consideration of time and space in divinity
প্রকৃতির মধ্যে দেখ কালের প্রভাব ।<br />ভূত-ভবিষ্যতের বুদ্ধি তাহার স্বভাব ॥১৮॥
prakṛtira madhye dekha kālera prabhāva<br />bhūta-bhaviṣyatera buddhi tāhāra svabhāva [18]
<span class="e2">prakṛtira</span> <span class="e2">madhye</span>–Within material existence, <span class="e2">dekha</span>–you see <span class="e2">prabhāva</span>–the influence <span class="e2">kālera</span>–of time; <span class="e2">buddhi</span>–awareness <span class="e2">bhūta-bhaviṣyatera</span>–of past and future [is part of] <span class="e2">tāhāra</span>–its <span class="e2">svabhāva</span>–nature.
Within material existence, you see the influence of time; awareness of past and future are natural within material existence.
অপ্রাকৃত-তত্ত্বে ভূত ভবিষ্যৎ নাই ।<br />নিত্য-বর্ত্তমান তথা বলিহারি যাই ॥১৯॥
aprākṛta-tattve bhūta bhaviṣyat nāi<br />nitya-vartamāna tathā balihāri yāi [19]
<span class="e2">aprākṛta-tattve</span>–In divinity, [however,] <span class="e2">nāi</span>–there is no <span class="e2">bhūta</span>–past [or] <span class="e2">bhaviṣyat</span>–future. <span class="e2">tathā</span>–There, [there is] <span class="e2">nitya-vartamāna</span>–the eternal present, [which] <span class="e2">balihāri</span> <span class="e2">yāi</span>–
is indescribable.
In divinity, however, there is no past or future; there is only the eternal present, which is indescribable.
বাঙ্মনের অগোচর অপ্রাকৃত-তত্ত্ব ।<br />বর্ণিতে আইসে দোষ এই মাত্র সত্য ॥২০॥
vāṅmanera agochara aprākṛta-tattva<br />varṇite āise doṣa ei mātra satya [20]
<span class="e2">aprākṛta-tattva</span>–Divinity [is] <span class="e2">vāṅmanera</span> <span class="e2">agochara</span>–beyond the mind and words. <span class="e2">varṇite</span>–Describing [it] <span class="e2">āise</span>–brings about <span class="e2">doṣa</span>–error. <span class="e2">ei</span>–This <span class="e2">mātra</span>–alone [is] <span class="e2">satya</span>–true.
Divinity is beyond thought and description. Describing it leads to error. This alone is the truth.
অপ্রাকৃত-তত্ত্বে কভু দোষ নাহি পাই ।<br />অচিন্ত্য-শক্তিতে সব সমাধান ভাই ॥২১॥
aprākṛta-tattve kabhu doṣa nāhi pāi<br />achintya-śaktite saba samādhāna bhāi [21]
<span class="e2">kabhu</span> <span class="e2">nāhi</span> <span class="e2">pāi</span>–We never find <span class="e2">doṣa</span>–faults <span class="e2">aprākṛta-tattve</span>–in divinity. <span class="e2">bhāi</span>–Brother, <span class="e2">saba</span>–everything [is] <span class="e2">samādhāna</span>–harmonised <span class="e2">achintya-śaktite</span>–by [the Absolute’s] inconceivable energy.
We never find faults in divinity. Brother, everything is harmonised by the Absolute’s inconceivable energy.
পূর্ব্বাপর হেন কথা কভু নাহি তায় ।<br />সর্ব্বদা নূতন সব আনন্দে মাতায় ॥২২॥
pūrvāpara hena kathā kabhu nāhi tāya<br />sarvadā nūtana saba ānande mātāya [22]
<span class="e2">kabhu</span> <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–There is never <span class="e2">hena</span> <span class="e2">kathā</span>–such notion <span class="e2">pūrvāpara</span>–of before and after <span class="e2">tāya</span>–there. <span class="e2">saba</span>–Everything [is] <span class="e2">sarvadā</span> <span class="e2">nūtana</span>–ever-new [and] <span class="e2">mātāya</span>–overflows <span class="e2">ānande</span>–with joy.
There is never any sense of before and after in the Absolute. Everything is ever-new and overflows with joy.
অতএব তত্ত্বে যে অখণ্ড-খণ্ড-ভাব ।<br />সমকালে দেখি সেও তত্ত্বের স্বভাব ॥২৩॥
ataeva tattve ye akhaṇḍa-khaṇḍa-bhāva<br />sama-kāle dekhi seo tattvera svabhāva [23]
<span class="e2">ataeva</span>–Thus, <span class="e2">seo ye</span> <span class="e2">akhaṇḍa-khaṇḍa-bhāva</span>–the states of being divided and undivided, [which] <span class="e2">dekhi</span>–we see <span class="e2">tattve</span>–in the Absolute <span class="e2">sama-kāle</span>–simultaneously, [are both part of] <span class="e2">tattvera</span>–the Absolute’s <span class="e2">svabhāva</span>–nature.
Thus, the states of being divided and undivided, which we see within the Absolute simultaneously, are both part of the Absolute’s nature.
বিরুদ্ধ-ধর্ম্মাশ্রয় তত্ত্ব আশ্চর্য তার গুণ ।<br />জন্মে নাই হ্লাদিনী তবু ক্রিয়াতে নিপুণ ॥২৪॥
viruddha-dharmāśraya tattva āścharya tāra guṇa<br />janme nāi hlādinī tabu kriyāte nipuṇa [24]
<span class="e2">tattva</span>–The Absolute [is] <span class="e2">viruddha-dharmāśraya</span>–the shelter of contradictory natures. [This is] <span class="e2">tāra</span>–His <span class="e2">āścharya</span>–astonishing <span class="e2">guṇa</span>–quality: <span class="e2">janme</span> <span class="e2">nāi</span>–without having manifest, <span class="e2">hlādinī</span>–the hlādinī-śaktī [is] <span class="e2">tabu</span>–still <span class="e2">nipuṇa</span>–adept <span class="e2">kriyāte</span>–in action.
The Absolute has contradictory natures. This is one of the Absolute’s astonishing qualities: without having manifest, the hlādinī-śakti still acts expertly.
জন্মিবার পূর্ব্বে রাধা-কৃষ্ণে দুই করে ।<br />দুঁহে প্রেমের বিকার হয়ে নিজে জন্ম ধরে ॥২৫॥
janmibāra pūrve rādhā-kṛṣṇe dui kare<br />du̐he premera vikāra haye nije janma dhare [25]
<span class="e2">pūrve</span>–Prior <span class="e2">janmibāra</span>–to [her] manifestation, <span class="e2">kare</span>–she makes <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇe</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa <span class="e2">dui</span>–two [and then] <span class="e2">janma</span> <span class="e2">dhare</span>–she manifests <span class="e2">nije</span>–herself <span class="e2">haye</span>–as <span class="e2">vikāra</span>–the transformations <span class="e2">premera</span>–of love <span class="e2">du̐he</span>–between Them.
Prior to her manifestation, she makes Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa two, and then manifests herself as the transformations of love between Them.
নিত্য-বর্ত্তমান তত্ত্ব কালদোষহীন ।<br />কালদোষ-বিচার প্রাকৃতে সমীচীন ॥২৬॥
nitya-vartamāna tattva kāla-doṣa-hīna<br />kāla-doṣa-vichāra prākṛte samīchīna [26]
<span class="e2">tattva</span>–The Absolute, <span class="e2">nitya-vartamāna</span>–eternally present, [is] <span class="e2">kāla-doṣa-hīna</span>–free from the fault of time. <span class="e2">kāla-doṣa-vichāra</span>–Consideration of the fault of time [is] <span class="e2">samīchīna</span>–appropriate <span class="e2">prākṛte</span>–for material existence.
The eternally present Absolute is free from the fault of time. Consideration of time applies only to material existence.
শ্রীঅদ্বয়তত্ত্ব আর রাধাকৃষ্ণতত্ত্ব ।<br />সমকাল সত্য নিত্য আর শুদ্ধ সত্ত্ব ॥২৭॥
śrī-advaya-tattva āra rādhā-kṛṣṇa-tattva<br />sama-kāla satya nitya āra śuddha sattva [27]
<span class="e2">śrī-advaya-tattva</span>–The nondual Absolute <span class="e2">āra</span>–and <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa-tattva</span>–Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa [are] <span class="e2">sama-kāla</span>–simultaneously <span class="e2">satya</span>–true, <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternal, <span class="e2">āra</span>–and <span class="e2">śuddha</span> <span class="e2">sattva</span>–pure in nature.
The nondual Absolute and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are simultaneously existent, eternal, and spiritual.
শ্রীরাধাকৃষ্ণই শ্রীচৈতন্য
śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-i śrī-chaitanya
Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa are Śrī Chaitanya
অতএব রাধাকৃষ্ণ দুই এক হঞা ।<br />অধুনা প্রকট মোর চৈতন্য গোসাঞাঁ ॥২৮॥
ataeva rādhā-kṛṣṇa dui eka hañā<br />adhunā prakaṭa mora chaitanya gosāñā̐ [28]
<span class="e2">ataeva</span>–Thus, <span class="e2">dui</span>–the two, <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, <span class="e2">hañā</span>–have become <span class="e2">eka</span>–one <span class="e2">adhunā</span>–now [and] <span class="e2">prakaṭa</span>–manifest [as] <span class="e2">mora</span>–my <span class="e2">gosāñā̐</span>–Lord, <span class="e2">chaitanya</span>–Śrī Chaitanya.
Thus, the two, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, have now become one and manifest as my Lord, Śrī Chaitanya.
“অধুনা” বলিতে কালভেদ নাহি কর ।<br />অপ্রাকৃতে কালভেদ নাহি তাহা স্মর ॥২৯॥
“adhunā” balite kāla-bheda nāhi kara<br />aprākṛte kāla-bheda nāhi tāhā smara [29]
<span class="e2">balite</span>–As I say, <span class="e2">“adhunā”</span>–“now”, <span class="e2">kara nāhi</span>–do not make <span class="e2">kāla-bheda</span>–a temporal distinction. <span class="e2">smara</span>–Remember <span class="e2">tāhā</span>–that <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–there are no <span class="e2">kāla-bheda</span>–temporal distinctions <span class="e2">aprākṛte</span>–in divinity.
I said, “now”, but do not make a temporal distinction. Remember that there are no such distinctions in divinity.
“রাধাকৃষ্ণ ছিল, ভেল চৈতন্য গোসাঞি” ।<br />এ বলিলে কালদোষ সত্যবস্তু হারাই ॥৩০॥
“rādhā-kṛṣṇa chhila, bhela chaitanya gosāñi”<br />e balile kāla-doṣa satya-vastu hārāi [30]
<span class="e2">“rādhā-kṛṣṇa</span>–“Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa <span class="e2">chhila</span>–existed, [and then] <span class="e2">bhela</span>–became <span class="e2">chaitanya</span> <span class="e2">gosāñi</span>–Lord Chaitanya”— <span class="e2">e</span> <span class="e2">balile</span>–if you say this, <span class="e2">kāla-doṣa</span>–the fault of time [occurs, and] <span class="e2">hārāi</span>–you misunderstand <span class="e2">satya-vastu</span>–the true Absolute.
“Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa existed, and then became Lord Chaitanya”—if you say this, you make a temporal distinction and misunderstand the Absolute.
‘একাত্মা’ শব্দেতে যদি শ্রীচৈতন্য মান ।<br />রাধাকৃষ্ণে হবে ভাই আধুনিক জ্ঞান ॥৩১॥
‘ekātmā’ śabdete yadi śrī-chaitanya māna<br />rādhā-kṛṣṇe habe bhāi ādhunika jñāna [31]
<span class="e2">bhāi</span>–Brother, <span class="e2">yadi</span>–if <span class="e2">māna</span>–you consider <span class="e2">‘ekātmā’ śabdete</span>–the word <span class="e33">ekātmā</span> [means] <span class="e2">śrī-chaitanya</span>–Śrī Chaitanya, [and that] <span class="e2">habe</span>–He will become <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇe</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, [then] <span class="e2">ādhunika</span> <span class="e2">jñāna</span>–a temporal distinction [is made].
Brother, if you consider that the word <span class="e3">ekātmā</span> means Śrī Chaitanya and that He will become Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, then you make a temporal distinction between Them.
“অগ্রে রাধাকৃষ্ণ কিবা শচীর নন্দন” ।<br />এ বিচারে বৃথা কাল না কর কর্ত্তন ॥৩২॥
“agre rādhā-kṛṣṇa kibā śachīra nandana”<br />e vichāre vṛthā kāla nā kara kartana [32]
<span class="e2">“kibā</span>–“Who [was] <span class="e2">agre</span>–first: <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa [or] <span class="e2">śachīra</span> <span class="e2">nandana”</span>–the son of Śachī?” <span class="e2">kāla</span> <span class="e2">kartana kara nā</span>–Do not spend [your] time <span class="e2">vṛthā</span>–uselessly <span class="e2">e</span> <span class="e2">vichāre</span>–with such analysis.
“Who was first: Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa or Śrī Chaitanya?” Do not waste your time analysing this.
বলিয়াছি অপ্রাকৃতে সব বর্ত্তমান ।<br />চৈতন্য কৃষ্ণেতে তর্কে হও সাবধান ॥৩৩॥
baliyāchhi aprākṛte saba vartamāna<br />chaitanye kṛṣṇete tarke hao sāvadhāna [33]
<span class="e2">baliyāchhi</span>–I have said [that] <span class="e2">saba</span>–everything <span class="e2">aprākṛte</span>–within divinity [exists] <span class="e2">vartamāna</span>–in the present. <span class="e2">sāvadhāna hao</span>–Be cautious <span class="e2">tarke</span>–in arguing [over] <span class="e2">chaitanye</span> <span class="e2">kṛṣṇete</span>–Chaitanya and Kṛṣṇa.
I have already said that everything within divinity exists in the present, so be cautious about arguing over Śrī Chaitanya and Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
সমকাল নিত্যকাল দুই তত্ত্ব সত্য ।<br />অখণ্ড অদ্বয় লীলা তত্ত্বের মহত্ত্ব ॥৩৪॥
sama-kāla nitya-kāla dui tattva satya<br />akhaṇḍa advaya līlā tattvera mahattva [34]
<span class="e2">dui</span> <span class="e2">tattva</span>–The two of Them <span class="e2">satya</span>–exist <span class="e2">sama-kāla</span>–simultaneously [and] <span class="e2">nitya-kāla</span>–eternally, [and Their] <span class="e2">akhaṇḍa</span>–indivisible, <span class="e2">advaya</span>–nondual <span class="e2">līlā</span>–Pastimes [are] <span class="e2">mahattva</span>–the glory <span class="e2">tattvera</span>–of the Absolute.
Śrī Chaitanya and Śrī Kṛṣṇa exist simultaneously and eternally, and Their indivisible, nondual Pastimes are Their glory.
প্রণয়-বিকার-শক্তি সেই আহ্লাদিনী ।<br />দুই তত্ত্বে সমকাল রাখে এই জানি ॥৩৫॥
praṇaya-vikāra-śakti sei āhlādinī<br />dui tattve sama-kāla rākhe ei jāni [35]
<span class="e2">jāni</span>–We understand <span class="e2">ei</span>–that <span class="e2">praṇaya-vikāra-śakti</span>–this energy, the transformation of [Their] love, <span class="e2">sei āhlādinī</span>–the hlādinī-śakti, <span class="e2">sama-kāla</span>–simultaneously <span class="e2">rākhe</span>–maintains <span class="e2">dui</span> <span class="e2">tattve</span>–the two of Them.
We understand that the transformation of Their love, the hlādinī-śakti, simultaneously maintains Them both.
সেই ত’ চৈতন্য এবে প্রপঞ্চ-প্রকটে ।<br />সঙ্কীর্ত্তন করি’ বুলে গঙ্গাসিন্ধুতটে ॥৩৬॥
sei ta’ chaitanya ebe prapañcha-prakaṭe<br />saṅkīrtana kari’ bule gaṅgā-sindhu-taṭe [36]
<span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">ta’</span> <span class="e2">chaitanya</span>–This Śrī Chaitanya [is] <span class="e2">ebe</span>–now <span class="e2">prapañcha-prakaṭe</span>–manifest in the material world. <span class="e2">bule</span>–He walks <span class="e2">gaṅgā-sindhu-taṭe</span>–along the shore of the Gaṅgā and the ocean <span class="e2">saṅkīrtana kari’</span>–chanting [His Name].
Śrī Chaitanya is now manifest in the material world. He walks along the shore of the Gaṅgā and the ocean performing saṅkīrtan.
কৃষ্ণলীলার অধিক এই শ্রীচৈতন্যলীলা ।<br />প্রণয়-বিকার যাতে উৎকট হইলা ॥৩৭॥
kṛṣṇa-līlāra adhika ei śrī-chaitanya-līlā<br />praṇaya-vikāra yāte utkaṭa ha-ilā [37]
<span class="e2">ei</span> <span class="e2">śrī-chaitanya-līlā</span>–Śrī Chaitanya’s Pastimes [are] <span class="e2">adhika</span>–more <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-līlāra</span>–than Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s Pastimes: <span class="e2">praṇaya-vikāra</span>–the transformations of love <span class="e2">yāte</span>–within them <span class="e2">ha-ilā</span>–have become <span class="e2">utkaṭa</span>–extreme.
Śrī Chaitanya’s Pastimes are more than Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s Pastimes: the transformations of love within them are the most intense.
উৎকট হইয়া কৃষ্ণে রাধাভাবদ্যুতি ।<br />মাখাইল প্রেমভরে আহ্লাদিনী সতী ॥৩৮॥
utkaṭa ha-iyā kṛṣṇe rādhā-bhāva-dyuti<br />mākhāila prema-bhare āhlādinī satī [38]
<span class="e2">utkaṭa</span> <span class="e2">ha-iyā</span>–Intensifying, <span class="e2">satī āhlādinī</span>–the chaste pleasure potency <span class="e2">prema-bhare</span>–lovingly <span class="e2">mākhāila</span>–enveloped <span class="e2">kṛṣṇe</span>–Kṛṣṇa <span class="e2">rādhā-bhāva-dyuti</span>–with the heart and halo of Rādhā.
Intensifying, the chaste hlādinī-śakti lovingly enveloped Kṛṣṇa with the heart and halo of Rādhā.
ব্রজের অধিক সুখ নবদ্বীপধামে ।<br />পাইল পুরট কৃষ্ণ আসি’ নিজ কামে ॥৩৯॥
vrajera adhika sukha navadvīpa-dhāme<br />pāila puraṭa kṛṣṇa āsi’ nija kāme [39]
<span class="e2">puraṭa</span>–Golden <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–Kṛṣṇa <span class="e2">āsi’</span>–came <span class="e2">nija</span> <span class="e2">kāme</span>–to fulfil His desires, [and] <span class="e2">pāila</span>–felt <span class="e2">adhika</span>–more <span class="e2">sukha</span>–joy <span class="e2">navadvīpa-dhāme</span>–in Nabadwīp Dhām <span class="e2">vrajera</span>–than [in] Vraja.
Then Golden Kṛṣṇa appeared to fulfil His desires, and felt more joy in Nabadwīp Dhām than He does in Vraja.
শ্রীচৈতন্যের স্বরূপ
śrī-chaitanyera svarūpa
Śrī Chaitanya’s nature
চৈতন্যমুরতি কৃষ্ণের অপূর্ব্বস্বরূপ ।<br />কৃষ্ণমূর্ত্তি চৈতন্যের স্বরূপ অপরূপ ॥৪০॥
chaitanya-murati kṛṣṇera apūrva-svarūpa<br />kṛṣṇa-mūrti chaitanyera svarūpa aparūpa [40]
<span class="e2">chaitanya-murati</span>–The form of Śrī Chaitanya [is] <span class="e2">apūrva-svarūpa</span>–an extraordinary form <span class="e2">kṛṣṇera</span>–of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, [and] <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-mūrti</span>–the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa [is] <span class="e2">aparūpa svarūpa</span>–a wonderful form <span class="e2">chaitanyera</span>–of Śrī Chaitanya.
Śrī Chaitanya is an extraordinary form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and Śrī Kṛṣṇa is a wonderful form of Śrī Chaitanya.
হ্লাদিনীর দুই সাজ পরম মধুর ।<br />মধু হৈতে মধু, তাহা হৈতে সুমধুর ॥৪১॥
hlādinīra dui sāja parama madhura<br />madhu haite madhu, tāhā haite sumadhura [41]
<span class="e2">dui</span>–These two <span class="e2">sāja</span>–arrangements <span class="e2">hlādinīra</span>–of the pleasure potency [are] <span class="e2">parama</span>–supremely <span class="e2">madhura</span>–sweet. [They are] <span class="e2">madhu</span>–sweeter <span class="e2">haite</span>–than <span class="e2">madhu</span>–sweetness, [and] <span class="e2">sumadhura</span>–even sweeter <span class="e2">haite</span>–than <span class="e2">tāhā</span>–that.
Both of these arrangements of the hlādinī-śakti are supremely sweet. They are sweeter than sweetness, and even sweeter still.
সুমধুর স্বরূপ কৃষ্ণের চৈতন্য মুরতি ।<br />নিরন্তর করি তাঁতে দণ্ডবন্নতি ॥৪২॥
sumadhura svarūpa kṛṣṇera chaitanya-murati<br />nirantara kari tā̐te daṇḍavan-nati [42]
<span class="e2">nirantara</span>–Eternally, <span class="e2">daṇḍavan-nati kari</span>–I bow <span class="e2">tā̐te</span>–to Him, <span class="e2">svarūpa</span>–the embodiment <span class="e2">sumadhura</span>–of the supreme sweetness, <span class="e2">kṛṣṇera</span> <span class="e2">chaitanya-murati</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s form as Śrī Chaitanya.
Eternally, I bow to the embodiment of the supreme sweetness, Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s form as Śrī Chaitanya.
যদি বল ‘একাত্মা’ শব্দে ব্রহ্ম নির্ব্বিকার ।<br />যাহা হৈতে রাধাকৃষ্ণস্বরূপ সাকার ॥৪৩॥
yadi bala ‘ekātmā’ śabde brahma nirvikāra<br />yāhā haite rādhā-kṛṣṇa-svarūpa sākāra [43]
<span class="e2">yadi</span> <span class="e2">bala</span>–You may say <span class="e2">‘ekātmā’ śabde</span>–the word <span class="e33">ekātmā</span> [means] <span class="e2">nirvikāra brahma</span>–nondifferentiated Brahma, <span class="e2">haite</span>–from <span class="e2">yāhā</span>–which <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa-svarūpa</span>–Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa [became] <span class="e2">sākāra</span>–embodied.
You may say that <span class="e3">ekātmā</span> means nondifferentiated Brahma, from which Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa assumed forms.
এ সিদ্ধান্ত হৈতে নারে শ্লোকের আভাসে ।<br />সেই দুই এক আত্মা চৈতন্যপ্রকাশে ॥৪৪॥
e siddhānta haite nāre ślokera ābhāse<br />sei dui eka ātmā chaitanya-prakāśe [44]
<span class="e2">e</span> <span class="e2">siddhānta</span>–This conclusion <span class="e2">haite</span> <span class="e2">nāre</span>–cannot be <span class="e2">ābhāse</span>–the intention <span class="e2">ślokera</span>–of the verse. <span class="e2">sei</span> <span class="e2">dui</span>–The two [are] <span class="e2">eka</span>–one <span class="e2">ātmā</span>–entity <span class="e2">chaitanya-prakāśe</span>–in the form of Śrī Chaitanya.
Such a conclusion, however, cannot be the intended meaning of the verse. The two, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, are one entity (ātmā) as Śrī Chaitanya.
ব্রহ্ম শ্রীচৈতন্যের অঙ্গকান্তি
brahma śrī-chaitanyera aṅga-kānti
Brahma is Śrī Chaitanya’s bodily lustre
চৈতন্য নহেন কভু ব্রহ্ম নির্ব্বিকার ।<br />আনন্দবিকারপূর্ণ বিশুদ্ধ সাকার ॥৪৫॥
chaitanya nahena kabhu brahma nirvikāra<br />ānanda-vikāra-pūrṇa viśuddha sākāra [45]
<span class="e2">chaitanya</span>–Śrī Chaitanya <span class="e2">kabhu nahena</span>–is never <span class="e2">nirvikāra brahma</span>–nondifferentiated Brahma. [He has] <span class="e2">viśuddha</span>–a pure <span class="e2">sākāra</span>–form <span class="e2">ānanda-vikāra-pūrṇa</span>–filled with transformations of ecstasy.
Śrī Chaitanya is never nondifferentiated Brahma. He has a spiritual form and is filled with transformations of ecstasy.
ব্রহ্ম তাঁর শ্রীঅঙ্গের জ্যোতি নির্ব্বিশেষ ।<br />ব্রহ্মের প্রতিষ্ঠা কৃষ্ণচৈতন্যবিশেষ ॥৪৬॥
brahma tā̐ra śrī-aṅgera jyoti nirviśeṣa<br />brahmera pratiṣṭhā kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-viśeṣa [46]
